declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.pointsMap_injective_of_fullyFaithful
declarations.doc: A monomorphism of algebraic stacks induces an injective map on points.
declarations.statement:
public theorem pointsMap_injective_of_fullyFaithful
    (B : BigFppfSite.{u}) (S : Scheme.{u}) (hS : B.Contains S)
    {𝒳 𝒴 : AlgebraicStacks.{u, w} B S hS}
    (f : 𝒳 ⟶ 𝒴)
    [Functor.Full (CatFiberedInGroupoids.homFunctor f.hom)]
    [Functor.Faithful (CatFiberedInGroupoids.homFunctor f.hom)] :
    Function.Injective
      (pointsMap B S hS 𝒳.val.val

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.AlgebraicStacks.isImmersion_snd_of_isTwoFibreProduct
declarations.doc:
Base change of an immersion of algebraic stacks. If `g : 𝒵 ⟶ 𝒴` is an immersion of
algebraic stacks over `S` and `P` is a 2-fibre product of the cospan `(g, f)` in the 2-category of
algebraic stacks, then `P.snd : P.pt ⟶ 𝒳` is an immersion of algebraic stacks.

Both halves are base-change statements: representability by algebraic spaces is Stacks 0302 and
the immersion property of Stacks 04XB is Stacks 045C. The attribute records the latter, at the
level of algebraic stacks. It deliberately does **not** record Stacks 04YL: that tag is a
definition — its three parts define open immersions, closed immersions and immersions in terms
of Section 04XB — and says nothing about stability under base change, so a theorem must not
carry it. The definition itself is carried by `AlgebraicStacks.IsImmersion`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isImmersion_snd_of_isTwoFibreProduct
    (P : Bicategory.TwoCommSq g f) (hP : Bicategory.IsTwoFibreProduct P)
    (hg : IsImmersion B S hS g) :
    IsImmersion B S hS P.snd
declarations.comment: immersions

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.AlgebraicStacks.isClosedImmersion_baseChange_snd
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0501 for closed immersions.** Let `f : 𝒳 ⟶ 𝒴` be a 1-morphism of algebraic stacks
over `S` and let `g : 𝒵 ⟶ 𝒴` be a closed immersion of algebraic stacks. Then the projection
`𝒵 ×_𝒴 𝒳 ⟶ 𝒳` is a closed immersion of algebraic stacks.

Stated at an arbitrary 2-fibre product square `P` of the cospan `(g, f)` in the 2-category of
algebraic stacks; the source's `𝒵 ×_𝒴 𝒳` is the canonical such square.
declarations.statement:
theorem isClosedImmersion_baseChange_snd
    (P : Bicategory.TwoCommSq g f) (hP : Bicategory.IsTwoFibreProduct P)
    (hg : IsClosedImmersion B S hS g) :
    IsClosedImmersion B S hS P.snd
declarations.comment: closed immersions

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.AlgebraicStacks.isOpenImmersion_baseChange_snd
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0501 for open immersions.** Let `f : 𝒳 ⟶ 𝒴` be a 1-morphism of algebraic stacks

`𝒵 ×_𝒴 𝒳 ⟶ 𝒳` is an open immersion of algebraic stacks.

Stated at an arbitrary 2-fibre product square `P` of the cospan `(g, f)` in the 2-category of
algebraic stacks; the source's `𝒵 ×_𝒴 𝒳` is the canonical such square.
declarations.statement:
theorem isOpenImmersion_baseChange_snd

    (hg : IsOpenImmersion B S hS g) :
    IsOpenImmersion B S hS P.snd
declarations.comment: open immersions

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.AlgebraicStacks.isImmersion_iff_exists_isImmersion_representingMap
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0503 for immersions.** Let `f : 𝒳 ⟶ 𝒴` be a 1-morphism of algebraic stacks over
`S`, let `W` be an algebraic space over `S` and let `g : W ⟶ 𝒴` be surjective, flat and locally
of finite presentation. Then `f` is an immersion of algebraic stacks (Stacks 04YL, part (3))
exactly when `V = W ×_𝒴 𝒳` is an algebraic space and `V ⟶ W` is an immersion of algebraic
spaces.

The forward implication reads representability by algebraic spaces off clause (1); the backward
one obtains it from Stacks 04ZP. The content of both is Stacks 04XD at the immersion property.
declarations.statement:
theorem isImmersion_iff_exists_isImmersion_representingMap :
    IsImmersion B S hS f ↔
      ∃ (V : (BigFppfOver B S hS)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u) (_hV : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS V)
        (eV : StacksRepresentableCFG.EquivalenceOver
          Q.pt.val.p (presheafOfCategories (V ⋙ typeToCat)).p),
        Space.IsImmersion B S hS (representingMap B S hS Q.pt 𝒲 V W eV eW Q.fst)
declarations.comment: immersions

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.AlgebraicStacks.isClosedImmersion_iff_exists_isClosedImmersion_representingMap
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0503 for closed immersions.** In the situation of
`AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.AlgebraicStacks.isImmersion_iff_exists_isImmersion_representingMap`,
`f` is a closed immersion of algebraic stacks (Stacks 04YL, part (2)) exactly when
`V = W ×_𝒴 𝒳` is an algebraic space and `V ⟶ W` is a closed immersion of algebraic spaces.
declarations.statement:
theorem isClosedImmersion_iff_exists_isClosedImmersion_representingMap :
    IsClosedImmersion B S hS f ↔
      ∃ (V : (BigFppfOver B S hS)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u) (_hV : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS V)
        (eV : StacksRepresentableCFG.EquivalenceOver
          Q.pt.val.p (presheafOfCategories (V ⋙ typeToCat)).p),
        Space.IsClosedImmersion B S hS (representingMap B S hS Q.pt 𝒲 V W eV eW Q.fst)
declarations.comment: closed immersions

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.AlgebraicStacks.isOpenImmersion_iff_exists_isOpenImmersion_representingMap
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0503 for open immersions.** In the situation of
`AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.AlgebraicStacks.isImmersion_iff_exists_isImmersion_representingMap`,
`f` is an open immersion of algebraic stacks (Stacks 04YL, part (1)) exactly when
`V = W ×_𝒴 𝒳` is an algebraic space and `V ⟶ W` is an open immersion of algebraic spaces.
declarations.statement:
theorem isOpenImmersion_iff_exists_isOpenImmersion_representingMap :
    IsOpenImmersion B S hS f ↔
      ∃ (V : (BigFppfOver B S hS)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u) (_hV : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS V)
        (eV : StacksRepresentableCFG.EquivalenceOver
          Q.pt.val.p (presheafOfCategories (V ⋙ typeToCat)).p),
        Space.IsOpenImmersion B S hS (representingMap B S hS Q.pt 𝒲 V W eV eW Q.fst)
declarations.comment: open immersions

    IsMonomorphism B S hS f

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.exists_isInvariantLocallyClosed_groupoidPresentation_of_isImmersion
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0505.** Let `G = (U, R, s, t, c)` be a smooth groupoid in algebraic spaces over a
scheme `S` of a big fppf site, and let `i : 𝒵 ⟶ [U/R]` be an immersion — a 1-morphism
representable by algebraic spaces with the relative immersion property of Stacks 04XB, that is
part (3) of Stacks 04YL — whose source satisfies descent. Then there are an `R`-invariant locally
closed subspace `Z ⊆ U` in the sense of Stacks 044F, part (2), a *presentation*
`[Z/R_Z] ⟶ 𝒵` of `𝒵` in the sense of Stacks 04TI by the restriction `R_Z` of `G` to `Z`
(Stacks 044B), and a 2-isomorphism making the triangle

    [Z/R_Z] ⟶ 𝒵 ⟶ [U/R]        [Z/R_Z] ⟶ [U/R]

2-commutative, the second leg being the 1-morphism of Stacks 046Q induced by the canonical
morphism of groupoids from the restriction. If `i` is a closed, respectively open, immersion then
`Z` is a closed, respectively open, subspace of `U`.

`Z` is pinned down by the conclusion: it is, pointwise, the locus of `U` whose image in `[U/R]`
lies in the essential image of `i`, which is the `𝒵 ×_{[U/R]} U` of Stacks 04Y6 read as a
subspace of `U`.

The subspace and its invariance are
`AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.exists_isInvariantLocallyClosed_range_of_isImmersion_quotientStack`;
smoothness of the restricted groupoid, the one place smoothness of `G` is used, is
`AlgebraicGeometry.GroupoidInAlgebraicSpaces.isSmoothGroupoid_restrict_invariant`; and the
equivalence together with the 2-commutative triangle is
`AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.exists_equivalenceOver_quotientStack_restrict`, whose two inputs are
full faithfulness of `i` (**Stacks 05UK** at the monomorphism **Stacks 042R** supplies, which is
**Stacks 0504**) and the pointwise description of `Z`.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_isInvariantLocallyClosed_groupoidPresentation_of_isImmersion
    (G : GroupoidInAlgebraicSpaces C S hS (baseSpace C S hS))
    (hG : GroupoidInAlgebraicSpaces.IsSmooth C S hS G)
    (h𝒵 : 𝒵.val.p.IsStack (BigFppfOver.topology C S hS))
    (i : 𝒵 ⟶ CatFiberedInGroupoids.mk (quotientStack G) (isFiberedInGroupoids_quotientStack G))
    (hi : IsRepresentableByAlgebraicSpaces C S hS i.hom)
    (himm : IsImmersion C S hS i) :
    ∃ (Z : Subfunctor G.objects.obj) (hZ : IsInvariantLocallyClosed G Z)
      (hsm : GroupoidInAlgebraicSpaces.IsSmooth C S hS
        (G.restrict (subspaceInclusion G Z hZ.1.1)).groupoid)
      (e : StacksRepresentableCFG.EquivalenceOver
        (quotientStack (G.restrict (subspaceInclusion G Z hZ.1.1)).groupoid).p 𝒵.val.p),
      Nonempty ((GroupoidPresentation.basedFunctor
            (⟨(G.restrict (subspaceInclusion G Z hZ.1.1)).groupoid, hsm, e⟩ :
              GroupoidPresentation C S hS 𝒵.val)).comp i.hom ≅
          quotientStackMap (G.restrict (subspaceInclusion G Z hZ.1.1)).hom) ∧
        (∀ (W : (BigFppfOver C S hS)ᵒᵖ) (u : G.objects.obj.obj W),
          u ∈ Z.obj W ↔ (CatFiberedInGroupoids.homFunctor i).essImage
            ((quotientStackProjection G).obj ⟨W.unop, Discrete.mk u⟩)) ∧
        (IsClosedImmersion C S hS i → Space.IsClosedSubspace C S hS Z) ∧
        (IsOpenImmersion C S hS i → Space.IsOpenSubspace C S hS Z)
declarations.comment: for i an immersion (representable by algebraic spaces with the 04XB immersion property, Stacks 04YL part (3)) out of a stack, a 1-morphism into the quotient stack of a smooth groupoid: the R-invariant locally closed Z, the presentation [Z/R_Z] ≃ 𝒵 with its 2-commutative triangle over [U/R], and Z closed (resp. open) when i is a closed (resp. open) immersion

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.AlgebraicStacks.isLocallyClosedSubstack_essImage
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0506**, the image is a locally closed substack. The essential image of an immersion
of algebraic stacks over `S` cuts out a locally closed substack of its target.

It is closed under isomorphism because an essential image always is; its full subcategory is an
algebraic stack by Stacks 03YQ; and the inclusion of that full subcategory is an immersion because
the immersion `i` factors through it by an equivalence, so Stacks 0457 transports both
representability by algebraic spaces and the Stacks 04XB immersion condition.
declarations.statement:
theorem isLocallyClosedSubstack_essImage (i : 𝒵 ⟶ 𝒳) (hi : IsImmersion B S hS i) :
    IsLocallyClosedSubstack 𝒳 (CatFiberedInGroupoids.homFunctor i.hom).essImage
declarations.comment: the image is a locally closed substack

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.AlgebraicStacks.exists_isEquivalence_to_essImage
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0506**, the factorization. An immersion of algebraic stacks over `S` factors as a
1-morphism onto the full subcategory cut out by its essential image whose underlying functor is an
equivalence of categories, followed by the inclusion of that full subcategory.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_isEquivalence_to_essImage (i : 𝒵 ⟶ 𝒳) (hi : IsImmersion B S hS i)
    (hP : IsAlgebraicStack.{u, w} B S hS
      (fullSubcategoryBased 𝒳 (CatFiberedInGroupoids.homFunctor i.hom).essImage)) :
    ∃ f : 𝒵 ⟶ fullSubcategoryAlgebraicStack 𝒳
        (CatFiberedInGroupoids.homFunctor i.hom).essImage hP,
      Functor.IsEquivalence (CatFiberedInGroupoids.homFunctor f.hom) ∧
        Nonempty (f ≫ fullSubcategoryInclusion 𝒳
          (CatFiberedInGroupoids.homFunctor i.hom).essImage hP ≅ i)
declarations.comment: the factorization through the image

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.AlgebraicStacks.eq_essImage_of_isEquivalence_factorization
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0506**, uniqueness. A strictly full subcategory of an algebraic stack which is an
algebraic stack and through which an immersion factors by a 1-morphism whose underlying functor is
an equivalence of categories is cut out by the essential image of the immersion.

The essential image of the inclusion of a strictly full subcategory is the property cutting it
out, and precomposing with an essentially surjective functor does not change an essential image,
so the essential image of the immersion is that property.
declarations.statement:
theorem eq_essImage_of_isEquivalence_factorization (i : 𝒵 ⟶ 𝒳)
    (P : ObjectProperty 𝒳.val.val.obj) (hstrict : P.IsClosedUnderIsomorphisms)
    (hP : IsAlgebraicStack.{u, w} B S hS (fullSubcategoryBased 𝒳 P))
    (f : 𝒵 ⟶ fullSubcategoryAlgebraicStack 𝒳 P hP)
    (hf : Functor.IsEquivalence (CatFiberedInGroupoids.homFunctor f.hom))
    (α : f ≫ fullSubcategoryInclusion 𝒳 P hP ≅ i) :
    P = (CatFiberedInGroupoids.homFunctor i.hom).essImage
declarations.comment: uniqueness of the substack

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.AlgebraicStacks.existsUnique_locallyClosedSubstack_of_isImmersion
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0506.** For an immersion `i : 𝒵 ⟶ 𝒳` of algebraic stacks over `S` there is a
*unique* locally closed substack of `𝒳` through which `i` factors as a 1-morphism whose underlying
functor is an equivalence of categories followed by the inclusion of the substack.

That substack is cut out by the essential image of the functor underlying `i`.
declarations.statement:
theorem existsUnique_locallyClosedSubstack_of_isImmersion (i : 𝒵 ⟶ 𝒳)
    (hi : IsImmersion B S hS i) :
    ∃! P : ObjectProperty 𝒳.val.val.obj,
      IsLocallyClosedSubstack 𝒳 P ∧
        ∃ (hP : IsAlgebraicStack.{u, w} B S hS (fullSubcategoryBased 𝒳 P))
          (f : 𝒵 ⟶ fullSubcategoryAlgebraicStack 𝒳 P hP),
          Functor.IsEquivalence (CatFiberedInGroupoids.homFunctor f.hom) ∧
            Nonempty (f ≫ fullSubcategoryInclusion 𝒳 P hP ≅ i)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.AlgebraicStacks.isClosedSubstack_essImage
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0506**, the closed case. The essential image of a closed immersion of algebraic
stacks over `S` cuts out a closed substack of its target.

A closed immersion is an immersion, so the essential image cuts out a locally closed substack; the
closed-immersion condition on the inclusion is the condition on `i` transported across the
equivalence by Stacks 0457.
declarations.statement:
theorem isClosedSubstack_essImage (i : 𝒵 ⟶ 𝒳) (hi : IsClosedImmersion B S hS i) :
    IsClosedSubstack 𝒳 (CatFiberedInGroupoids.homFunctor i.hom).essImage
declarations.comment: the image of a closed immersion is a closed substack

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.AlgebraicStacks.exists_openSubstack_essImage
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0506**, the open case. The essential image of an open immersion of algebraic stacks
over `S` is the object property of an open substack of its target.

An open immersion is an immersion, so the essential image cuts out a locally closed substack; the
open-immersion condition on the inclusion is the condition on `i` transported across the
equivalence by Stacks 0457.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_openSubstack_essImage (i : 𝒵 ⟶ 𝒳) (hi : IsOpenImmersion B S hS i) :
    ∃ U : OpenSubstack 𝒳,
      U.property = (CatFiberedInGroupoids.homFunctor i.hom).essImage
declarations.comment: the image of an open immersion is an open substack

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.factorsThroughSubstack_iff_presentation
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0507**, the factorization criterion. Let `𝒳` be an algebraic stack over `S`
presented by a smooth groupoid in algebraic spaces `G` through an equivalence `E` over the big
fppf site, let `P` cut out an open, closed or locally closed substack of `𝒳`, and let
`f : 𝒴 ⟶ 𝒳` be a 1-morphism of algebraic stacks. Then `f` factors through the substack, over
the big fppf site and up to a 2-isomorphism, if and only if the base change of `f` along the
presentation `S_U ⟶ 𝒳` factors through the base change of the substack.

The proof is pointwise on both sides, and the content is that membership of the substack is
local on the site; see the module documentation.
declarations.statement:
theorem factorsThroughSubstack_iff_presentation
    (𝒳 𝒴 : AlgebraicStacks.{u, w} B S hS)
    (G : GroupoidInAlgebraicSpaces B S hS (baseSpace B S hS))
    (_hG : GroupoidInAlgebraicSpaces.IsSmooth B S hS G)
    (E : (quotientStack G).obj ⥤ 𝒳.val.val.obj)
    [E.IsEquivalence]
    (hE : E ⋙ 𝒳.val.val.p = (quotientStack G).p)
    (P : ObjectProperty 𝒳.val.val.obj)
    (hP : (IsLocallyClosedSubstack 𝒳 P ∨ IsClosedSubstack 𝒳 P) ∨
      ∃ V : OpenSubstack 𝒳, V.property = P)
    (f : 𝒴 ⟶ 𝒳) :
    let U := (fibredCategory B S hS G.objects.obj).val
    let p := (quotientStackProjection G).comp
      (⟨E, hE⟩ : (quotientStack G) ⥤ᵇ 𝒳.val.val)
    let F := TwoFibreProductOver.structureFunctor U.p 𝒴.val.val.p 𝒳.val.val.p
      p.toFunctor f.hom.hom.toFunctor
    let D := BasedCategory.ofFunctor F
    let q : D ⥤ᵇ U :=
      { toFunctor := TwoFibreProductOver.fst U.p 𝒴.val.val.p 𝒳.val.val.p
          p.toFunctor f.hom.hom.toFunctor
        w := TwoFibreProductOver.fst_comp_eq }
    let i := fullSubcategoryBasedInclusion 𝒳 P
    let Z := BasedCategory.ofFunctor
      (TwoFibreProductOver.structureFunctor U.p
        (fullSubcategoryBased 𝒳 P).p
        𝒳.val.val.p p.toFunctor i.toFunctor)
    let z : Z ⥤ᵇ U :=
      { toFunctor := TwoFibreProductOver.fst U.p
          (fullSubcategoryBased 𝒳 P).p
          𝒳.val.val.p p.toFunctor i.toFunctor
        w := TwoFibreProductOver.fst_comp_eq }
    (∃ g : 𝒴.val.val ⥤ᵇ fullSubcategoryBased 𝒳 P,
      Nonempty (g.comp i ≅ f.hom.hom)) ↔
      (∃ g : D ⥤ᵇ Z, Nonempty (g.comp z ≅ q))
declarations.comment: factorization_criterion

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.exists_equiv_isInvariantLocallyClosed_presentation
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0507**, locally closed substacks. Let `[U/R] ⟶ 𝒳` be a presentation of an algebraic
stack. There is a canonical bijection from the locally closed substacks `𝒵` of `𝒳` to the
`R`-invariant locally closed subspaces of `U`, sending `𝒵` to `U ×_𝒳 𝒵`. Moreover, a 1-morphism
`f : 𝒴 ⟶ 𝒳` of algebraic stacks factors through `𝒵` if and only if `𝒴 ×_𝒳 U ⟶ U` factors through
`U ×_𝒳 𝒵`.

Here `[U/R] ⟶ 𝒳` is a presentation of the algebraic stack `𝒳` (Stacks 04TI), and `π : U ⟶ 𝒳`
is the canonical projection followed by the equivalence. The bijection `e` sends `𝒵` to the
subspace of `U` that is the image of the projection `U ×_𝒳 𝒵 ⟶ U` from the 2-fibre product
(first conjunct). For every 1-morphism `f : 𝒴 ⟶ 𝒳` of algebraic stacks, `f` factors through `𝒵`
over the site and up to a 2-isomorphism exactly when the projection `𝒴 ×_𝒳 U ⟶ U` factors
through `U ×_𝒳 𝒵` (second conjunct), and exactly when the `U`-component of every object of
`𝒴 ×_𝒳 U` lies in `e 𝒵` (third conjunct), which is to say that `𝒴 ×_𝒳 U ⟶ U` factors through
the subspace `e 𝒵`.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_equiv_isInvariantLocallyClosed_presentation :
    ∃ e : {P : ObjectProperty 𝒳.val.val.obj // IsLocallyClosedSubstack 𝒳 P} ≃
        {Z : Subfunctor Pr.groupoid.objects.obj // IsInvariantLocallyClosed Pr.groupoid Z},
      ∀ P : {P : ObjectProperty 𝒳.val.val.obj // IsLocallyClosedSubstack 𝒳 P},
        (∀ (T : BigFppfOver B S hS) (u : Pr.groupoid.objects.obj.obj (op T)),
          u ∈ (e P).1.obj (op T) ↔
            ∃ d : TwoFibreProductOver (fibredCategory B S hS Pr.groupoid.objects.obj).val.p
                (fullSubcategoryBased 𝒳 P.1).p 𝒳.val.val.p
                (presentationProjection Pr.groupoid Pr.basedFunctor.toFunctor
                  Pr.basedFunctor.w).toFunctor
                (fullSubcategoryBasedInclusion 𝒳 P.1).toFunctor,
              d.x = ⟨T, Discrete.mk u⟩) ∧
        ∀ (𝒴 : AlgebraicStacks.{u, w} B S hS) (f : 𝒴 ⟶ 𝒳),
          ((∃ g : 𝒴.val.val ⥤ᵇ fullSubcategoryBased 𝒳 P.1,
              Nonempty (g.comp (fullSubcategoryBasedInclusion 𝒳 P.1) ≅ f.hom.hom)) ↔
            ∃ g : BasedCategory.ofFunctor (TwoFibreProductOver.structureFunctor
                  (fibredCategory B S hS Pr.groupoid.objects.obj).val.p 𝒴.val.val.p 𝒳.val.val.p
                  (presentationProjection Pr.groupoid Pr.basedFunctor.toFunctor
                    Pr.basedFunctor.w).toFunctor f.hom.hom.toFunctor) ⥤ᵇ
                BasedCategory.ofFunctor (TwoFibreProductOver.structureFunctor
                  (fibredCategory B S hS Pr.groupoid.objects.obj).val.p
                  (fullSubcategoryBased 𝒳 P.1).p 𝒳.val.val.p
                  (presentationProjection Pr.groupoid Pr.basedFunctor.toFunctor
                    Pr.basedFunctor.w).toFunctor
                  (fullSubcategoryBasedInclusion 𝒳 P.1).toFunctor),
              Nonempty (g.comp (TwoFibreProductOver.fstBased (fullSubcategoryBased 𝒳 P.1).p
                  𝒳.val.val.p (presentationProjection Pr.groupoid Pr.basedFunctor.toFunctor
                    Pr.basedFunctor.w).toFunctor
                  (fullSubcategoryBasedInclusion 𝒳 P.1).toFunctor) ≅
                TwoFibreProductOver.fstBased 𝒴.val.val.p 𝒳.val.val.p
                  (presentationProjection Pr.groupoid Pr.basedFunctor.toFunctor
                    Pr.basedFunctor.w).toFunctor f.hom.hom.toFunctor)) ∧
          ((∃ g : 𝒴.val.val ⥤ᵇ fullSubcategoryBased 𝒳 P.1,
              Nonempty (g.comp (fullSubcategoryBasedInclusion 𝒳 P.1) ≅ f.hom.hom)) ↔
            ∀ d : TwoFibreProductOver (fibredCategory B S hS Pr.groupoid.objects.obj).val.p
                𝒴.val.val.p 𝒳.val.val.p
                (presentationProjection Pr.groupoid Pr.basedFunctor.toFunctor
                  Pr.basedFunctor.w).toFunctor f.hom.hom.toFunctor,
              d.x.fiber.as ∈ (e P).1.obj (op d.x.base))
declarations.comment: locally closed

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.exists_equiv_isInvariantClosed_presentation
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0507**, closed substacks. Let `[U/R] ⟶ 𝒳` be a presentation of an algebraic stack.
There is a canonical bijection from the closed substacks `𝒵` of `𝒳` to the `R`-invariant closed
subspaces of `U`, sending `𝒵` to `U ×_𝒳 𝒵`. Moreover, a 1-morphism `f : 𝒴 ⟶ 𝒳` of algebraic
stacks factors through `𝒵` if and only if `𝒴 ×_𝒳 U ⟶ U` factors through `U ×_𝒳 𝒵`.

Here `[U/R] ⟶ 𝒳` is a presentation of the algebraic stack `𝒳` (Stacks 04TI), and `π : U ⟶ 𝒳`
is the canonical projection followed by the equivalence. The bijection `e` sends `𝒵` to the
subspace of `U` that is the image of the projection `U ×_𝒳 𝒵 ⟶ U` from the 2-fibre product
(first conjunct). For every 1-morphism `f : 𝒴 ⟶ 𝒳` of algebraic stacks, `f` factors through `𝒵`
over the site and up to a 2-isomorphism exactly when the projection `𝒴 ×_𝒳 U ⟶ U` factors
through `U ×_𝒳 𝒵` (second conjunct), and exactly when the `U`-component of every object of
`𝒴 ×_𝒳 U` lies in `e 𝒵` (third conjunct), which is to say that `𝒴 ×_𝒳 U ⟶ U` factors through
the subspace `e 𝒵`.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_equiv_isInvariantClosed_presentation :
    ∃ e : {P : ObjectProperty 𝒳.val.val.obj // IsClosedSubstack 𝒳 P} ≃
        {Z : Subfunctor Pr.groupoid.objects.obj // IsInvariantClosed Pr.groupoid Z},
      ∀ P : {P : ObjectProperty 𝒳.val.val.obj // IsClosedSubstack 𝒳 P},
        (∀ (T : BigFppfOver B S hS) (u : Pr.groupoid.objects.obj.obj (op T)),
          u ∈ (e P).1.obj (op T) ↔
            ∃ d : TwoFibreProductOver (fibredCategory B S hS Pr.groupoid.objects.obj).val.p
                (fullSubcategoryBased 𝒳 P.1).p 𝒳.val.val.p
                (presentationProjection Pr.groupoid Pr.basedFunctor.toFunctor
                  Pr.basedFunctor.w).toFunctor
                (fullSubcategoryBasedInclusion 𝒳 P.1).toFunctor,
              d.x = ⟨T, Discrete.mk u⟩) ∧
        ∀ (𝒴 : AlgebraicStacks.{u, w} B S hS) (f : 𝒴 ⟶ 𝒳),
          ((∃ g : 𝒴.val.val ⥤ᵇ fullSubcategoryBased 𝒳 P.1,
              Nonempty (g.comp (fullSubcategoryBasedInclusion 𝒳 P.1) ≅ f.hom.hom)) ↔
            ∃ g : BasedCategory.ofFunctor (TwoFibreProductOver.structureFunctor
                  (fibredCategory B S hS Pr.groupoid.objects.obj).val.p 𝒴.val.val.p 𝒳.val.val.p
                  (presentationProjection Pr.groupoid Pr.basedFunctor.toFunctor
                    Pr.basedFunctor.w).toFunctor f.hom.hom.toFunctor) ⥤ᵇ
                BasedCategory.ofFunctor (TwoFibreProductOver.structureFunctor
                  (fibredCategory B S hS Pr.groupoid.objects.obj).val.p
                  (fullSubcategoryBased 𝒳 P.1).p 𝒳.val.val.p
                  (presentationProjection Pr.groupoid Pr.basedFunctor.toFunctor
                    Pr.basedFunctor.w).toFunctor
                  (fullSubcategoryBasedInclusion 𝒳 P.1).toFunctor),
              Nonempty (g.comp (TwoFibreProductOver.fstBased (fullSubcategoryBased 𝒳 P.1).p
                  𝒳.val.val.p (presentationProjection Pr.groupoid Pr.basedFunctor.toFunctor
                    Pr.basedFunctor.w).toFunctor
                  (fullSubcategoryBasedInclusion 𝒳 P.1).toFunctor) ≅
                TwoFibreProductOver.fstBased 𝒴.val.val.p 𝒳.val.val.p
                  (presentationProjection Pr.groupoid Pr.basedFunctor.toFunctor
                    Pr.basedFunctor.w).toFunctor f.hom.hom.toFunctor)) ∧
          ((∃ g : 𝒴.val.val ⥤ᵇ fullSubcategoryBased 𝒳 P.1,
              Nonempty (g.comp (fullSubcategoryBasedInclusion 𝒳 P.1) ≅ f.hom.hom)) ↔
            ∀ d : TwoFibreProductOver (fibredCategory B S hS Pr.groupoid.objects.obj).val.p
                𝒴.val.val.p 𝒳.val.val.p
                (presentationProjection Pr.groupoid Pr.basedFunctor.toFunctor
                  Pr.basedFunctor.w).toFunctor f.hom.hom.toFunctor,
              d.x.fiber.as ∈ (e P).1.obj (op d.x.base))
declarations.comment: closed

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.exists_equiv_isInvariantOpen_presentation
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0507**, open substacks. Let `[U/R] ⟶ 𝒳` be a presentation of an algebraic stack.
There is a canonical bijection from the open substacks `𝒵` of `𝒳` to the `R`-invariant open
subspaces of `U`, sending `𝒵` to `U ×_𝒳 𝒵`. Moreover, a 1-morphism `f : 𝒴 ⟶ 𝒳` of algebraic
stacks factors through `𝒵` if and only if `𝒴 ×_𝒳 U ⟶ U` factors through `U ×_𝒳 𝒵`.

Here `[U/R] ⟶ 𝒳` is a presentation of the algebraic stack `𝒳` (Stacks 04TI), and `π : U ⟶ 𝒳`
is the canonical projection followed by the equivalence. The bijection `e` sends `𝒵` to the
subspace of `U` that is the image of the projection `U ×_𝒳 𝒵 ⟶ U` from the 2-fibre product
(first conjunct). For every 1-morphism `f : 𝒴 ⟶ 𝒳` of algebraic stacks, `f` factors through `𝒵`
over the site and up to a 2-isomorphism exactly when the projection `𝒴 ×_𝒳 U ⟶ U` factors
through `U ×_𝒳 𝒵` (second conjunct), and exactly when the `U`-component of every object of
`𝒴 ×_𝒳 U` lies in `e 𝒵` (third conjunct), which is to say that `𝒴 ×_𝒳 U ⟶ U` factors through
the subspace `e 𝒵`. An `R`-invariant open subspace is one whose inverse image under the source
map is contained in its inverse image under the target map (Stacks 044F, part (1)).
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_equiv_isInvariantOpen_presentation :
    ∃ e : OpenSubstack 𝒳 ≃
        {Z : Subfunctor Pr.groupoid.objects.obj // IsInvariantOpen Pr.groupoid Z},
      ∀ P : OpenSubstack 𝒳,
        (∀ (T : BigFppfOver B S hS) (u : Pr.groupoid.objects.obj.obj (op T)),
          u ∈ (e P).1.obj (op T) ↔
            ∃ d : TwoFibreProductOver (fibredCategory B S hS Pr.groupoid.objects.obj).val.p
                (fullSubcategoryBased 𝒳 P.property).p 𝒳.val.val.p
                (presentationProjection Pr.groupoid Pr.basedFunctor.toFunctor
                  Pr.basedFunctor.w).toFunctor
                (fullSubcategoryBasedInclusion 𝒳 P.property).toFunctor,
              d.x = ⟨T, Discrete.mk u⟩) ∧
        ∀ (𝒴 : AlgebraicStacks.{u, w} B S hS) (f : 𝒴 ⟶ 𝒳),
          ((∃ g : 𝒴.val.val ⥤ᵇ fullSubcategoryBased 𝒳 P.property,
              Nonempty (g.comp (fullSubcategoryBasedInclusion 𝒳 P.property) ≅ f.hom.hom)) ↔
            ∃ g : BasedCategory.ofFunctor (TwoFibreProductOver.structureFunctor
                  (fibredCategory B S hS Pr.groupoid.objects.obj).val.p 𝒴.val.val.p 𝒳.val.val.p
                  (presentationProjection Pr.groupoid Pr.basedFunctor.toFunctor
                    Pr.basedFunctor.w).toFunctor f.hom.hom.toFunctor) ⥤ᵇ
                BasedCategory.ofFunctor (TwoFibreProductOver.structureFunctor
                  (fibredCategory B S hS Pr.groupoid.objects.obj).val.p
                  (fullSubcategoryBased 𝒳 P.property).p 𝒳.val.val.p
                  (presentationProjection Pr.groupoid Pr.basedFunctor.toFunctor
                    Pr.basedFunctor.w).toFunctor
                  (fullSubcategoryBasedInclusion 𝒳 P.property).toFunctor),
              Nonempty (g.comp (TwoFibreProductOver.fstBased (fullSubcategoryBased 𝒳 P.property).p
                  𝒳.val.val.p (presentationProjection Pr.groupoid Pr.basedFunctor.toFunctor
                    Pr.basedFunctor.w).toFunctor
                  (fullSubcategoryBasedInclusion 𝒳 P.property).toFunctor) ≅
                TwoFibreProductOver.fstBased 𝒴.val.val.p 𝒳.val.val.p
                  (presentationProjection Pr.groupoid Pr.basedFunctor.toFunctor
                    Pr.basedFunctor.w).toFunctor f.hom.hom.toFunctor)) ∧
          ((∃ g : 𝒴.val.val ⥤ᵇ fullSubcategoryBased 𝒳 P.property,
              Nonempty (g.comp (fullSubcategoryBasedInclusion 𝒳 P.property) ≅ f.hom.hom)) ↔
            ∀ d : TwoFibreProductOver (fibredCategory B S hS Pr.groupoid.objects.obj).val.p
                𝒴.val.val.p 𝒳.val.val.p
                (presentationProjection Pr.groupoid Pr.basedFunctor.toFunctor
                  Pr.basedFunctor.w).toFunctor f.hom.hom.toFunctor,
              d.x.fiber.as ∈ (e P).1.obj (op d.x.base))
declarations.comment: open

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.eq_of_isReducedStack_of_range_pointsMap_eq
declarations.doc:
**The uniqueness assertion of Stacks 0509.** Two reduced closed substacks
of an algebraic stack `𝒳` over `S`
with the same set of points are equal: each is contained in the other by
`AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.le_of_isReducedStack_of_range_pointsMap_subset`.
declarations.statement:
theorem eq_of_isReducedStack_of_range_pointsMap_eq {𝒳 : AlgebraicStacks.{u, w} B S hS}
    {P Q : ObjectProperty 𝒳.val.val.obj}
    (hP : IsClosedSubstack 𝒳 P) (hQ : IsClosedSubstack 𝒳 Q)
    (hAP : IsAlgebraicStack.{u, w} B S hS (fullSubcategoryBased 𝒳 P))
    (hAQ : IsAlgebraicStack.{u, w} B S hS (fullSubcategoryBased 𝒳 Q))
    (hPred : IsReducedStack B S hS (fullSubcategoryAlgebraicStack 𝒳 P hAP))
    (hQred : IsReducedStack B S hS (fullSubcategoryAlgebraicStack 𝒳 Q hAQ))
    (hpoints :
      Set.range (AlgebraicStacks.pointsMap B S hS (fullSubcategoryInclusion 𝒳 P hAP)) =
        Set.range (AlgebraicStacks.pointsMap B S hS (fullSubcategoryInclusion 𝒳 Q hAQ))) :
    P = Q
declarations.comment: uniqueness

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.existsUnique_reducedClosedSubstack
declarations.doc:
Let `𝒳` be an algebraic stack over `S` and let `T` be a closed subset of its space of points
`|𝒳|`. There exists a unique closed substack `𝒵 ⊆ 𝒳` such that (a) `|𝒵| = T` and (b) `𝒵` is
reduced.

A closed substack is a property of the objects of `𝒳` cutting out a strictly full subcategory
which is an algebraic stack with closed immersion inclusion
(`AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.IsClosedSubstack`); its set of points is the image of the map on points
of its inclusion. Both clauses are stated for every proof that the full subcategory is an
algebraic stack.
declarations.statement:
theorem existsUnique_reducedClosedSubstack :
    ∃! P : ObjectProperty 𝒳.val.val.obj, IsClosedSubstack 𝒳 P ∧
      (∀ hP : IsAlgebraicStack.{u, w} B S hS (fullSubcategoryBased 𝒳 P),
        Set.range (AlgebraicStacks.pointsMap B S hS (fullSubcategoryInclusion 𝒳 P hP)) = T) ∧
      ∀ hP : IsAlgebraicStack.{u, w} B S hS (fullSubcategoryBased 𝒳 P),
        IsReducedStack B S hS (fullSubcategoryAlgebraicStack 𝒳 P hP)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.eq_top_of_isClosedSubstack_of_isReducedStack
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 050A.** Let `𝒳` be an algebraic stack over `S` and let `P` cut out a closed substack
of `𝒳`. If `𝒳` is reduced and the inclusion of the substack is surjective on points, then the
substack is the whole of `𝒳`.

Every scheme chart of a reduced algebraic stack is reduced, and the chart supplied by the
algebraic-stack condition is locally essentially surjective; so
`AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.prop_of_isReduced_fiber` puts the image of the tautological object of
that chart in the substack, `AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.prop_of_isHomLift` puts the image of every
object of the chart there, and membership of a substack being local on the big fppf site puts
every object of `𝒳` there.
declarations.statement:
theorem eq_top_of_isClosedSubstack_of_isReducedStack {𝒳 : AlgebraicStacks.{u, w} B S hS}
    (P : ObjectProperty 𝒳.val.val.obj) (hclosed : IsClosedSubstack 𝒳 P)
    (hpoints : IsSurjective B S hS (fullSubcategoryInclusion 𝒳 P hclosed.2.choose))
    (hred : IsReducedStack B S hS 𝒳) :
    P = ⊤

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.factorsThroughSubstack_iff_range_pointsMap_subset
declarations.doc:
Let `𝒳` and `𝒴` be algebraic stacks over `S`, let `P` cut out a closed
substack of `𝒳` and let `𝒴` be reduced. A 1-morphism `f : 𝒴 ⟶ 𝒳` factors through the substack
if and only if the image of the induced map on points is contained in the points of the
substack.
declarations.statement:
theorem factorsThroughSubstack_iff_range_pointsMap_subset
    {𝒳 𝒴 : AlgebraicStacks.{u, w} B S hS} (f : 𝒴 ⟶ 𝒳)
    {P : ObjectProperty 𝒳.val.val.obj} (hP : IsClosedSubstack 𝒳 P)
    (hA : IsAlgebraicStack.{u, w} B S hS (fullSubcategoryBased 𝒳 P))
    (hred : IsReducedStack B S hS 𝒴) :
    FactorsThroughSubstack f P ↔
      Set.range (AlgebraicStacks.pointsMap B S hS f) ⊆
        Set.range (AlgebraicStacks.pointsMap B S hS (fullSubcategoryInclusion 𝒳 P hA))

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.IsAlgebraicStackStructure
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 050C, an algebraic stack structure on a closed set of points.** Let `𝒳` be an
algebraic stack over `S` and let `Z` be a set of points of `𝒳`. An *algebraic stack structure* on
`Z` is a closed substack of `𝒳` whose set of points is `Z`, that is, a property `P` of the
objects of `𝒳` cutting out a closed substack the canonical inclusion of which has range `Z` on
points.
declarations.statement:
def IsAlgebraicStackStructure {𝒳 : AlgebraicStacks.{u, w} B S hS}
    (Z : Set (AlgebraicStacks.points B S hS 𝒳)) (P : ObjectProperty 𝒳.val.val.obj) : Prop
declarations.comment: algebraic stack structure on a closed set of points

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.IsReducedInducedStackStructure
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 050C, the reduced induced algebraic stack structure.** The *reduced induced
algebraic stack structure* on a set `Z` of points of `𝒳` is the algebraic stack structure on `Z`
which is reduced. There is at most one,
`AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.IsReducedInducedStackStructure.unique`, which is the content of the
uniqueness half of **Stacks 0509**.
declarations.statement:
def IsReducedInducedStackStructure {𝒳 : AlgebraicStacks.{u, w} B S hS}
    (Z : Set (AlgebraicStacks.points B S hS 𝒳)) (P : ObjectProperty 𝒳.val.val.obj) : Prop
declarations.comment: the reduced induced algebraic stack structure

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.IsReducedInducedStackStructure.unique
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 050C, uniqueness of the reduced induced structure.** Two reduced induced algebraic
stack structures on the same set of points are equal. This is the uniqueness half of
**Stacks 0509**, and it is what makes the definite article of the source legitimate.
declarations.comment: uniqueness of the reduced induced structure

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.IsReduction
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 050C, the reduction.** The *reduction* `𝒳_red` of an algebraic stack `𝒳` over `S` is
the reduced induced algebraic stack structure on the whole of its space of points. It is unique,
`AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.IsReduction.unique`.
declarations.statement: def IsReduction {𝒳 : AlgebraicStacks.{u, w} B S hS} (P : ObjectProperty 𝒳.val.val.obj) : Prop
declarations.comment: the reduction

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.isUnramified_relativeDiagonal_of_isRepresentableByAlgebraicSpaces
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 050E, part (3).** A 1-morphism of algebraic stacks which is representable by
algebraic spaces is Deligne–Mumford: its relative diagonal is representable by algebraic spaces
(Stacks 04XS, part (1)), a monomorphism by part (3) of Stacks 04YQ and locally of finite type by
part (2) of that tag, so Stacks 05W6 makes it unramified — which is the Deligne–Mumford
condition of Stacks 04YW.

**No part key of Stacks 04YQ is claimed**: that tag's five parts are representability, local
finite type, monomorphy, separatedness and local quasi-finiteness, and unramifiedness is none of
them.
declarations.statement: theorem isUnramified_relativeDiagonal_of_isRepresentableByAlgebraicSpaces : IsDM B S hS f
declarations.comment: representable_implies_dm

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.AlgebraicStacks.isQuasiDMWithRepresentableDiagonal_of_isDM
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 050E.** A DM 1-morphism of algebraic stacks over `S` is quasi-DM.

Both conditions quantify over the same represented base changes of the relative diagonal and
differ only in the property tested of the resulting morphism of algebraic spaces, so the
implication is Stacks 05W0 — an unramified morphism of algebraic spaces is locally quasi-finite —
applied at each of them.
declarations.statement:
theorem isQuasiDMWithRepresentableDiagonal_of_isDM
    {𝒳 𝒴 : Stack.AlgebraicStacks.{u, w} B S hS} (f : 𝒳 ⟶ 𝒴)
    (hf : Stack.IsDM B S hS f) : IsQuasiDMWithRepresentableDiagonal B S hS f
declarations.comment: dm_implies_quasi_dm

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.AlgebraicStacks.isQuasiSeparated_of_isSeparated
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 050E, part (1).** A separated 1-morphism of algebraic stacks over `S` is
quasi-separated: its relative diagonal is proper, hence separated and of finite type, hence
quasi-separated and quasi-compact.
declarations.statement:
theorem isQuasiSeparated_of_isSeparated {f : 𝒳 ⟶ 𝒴} (hf : IsSeparated B S hS f) :
    IsQuasiSeparated B S hS f
declarations.comment: part (1): separated implies quasi-separated

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.AlgebraicStacks.isQuasiDM_of_isDM
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 050E, part (2).** A Deligne–Mumford 1-morphism of algebraic stacks over `S` is
quasi-DM: its relative diagonal is unramified, hence locally quasi-finite.
declarations.statement:
theorem isQuasiDM_of_isDM {f : 𝒳 ⟶ 𝒴} (hf : Stack.IsDM B S hS f) :
    IsQuasiDM B S hS f
declarations.comment: part (2): DM implies quasi-DM

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.AlgebraicStacks.isDM_baseChange
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 050F, DM.** The base change `q : 𝒳 ×_𝒴 𝒵 ⟶ 𝒵` of a Deligne–Mumford 1-morphism of
algebraic stacks over `S` is Deligne–Mumford: its relative diagonal is representable by algebraic
spaces (**Stacks 04XS**, part (1)) and unramified in the sense of Stacks 04XB, the latter because
`Δ_q` is a base change of `Δ_f`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isDM_baseChange (hf : Stack.IsDM B S hS f) :
    Stack.IsDM B S hS (twoFibreProductSquare B S hS f g).snd
declarations.comment: dm

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.AlgebraicStacks.isQuasiDM_baseChange
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 050F, quasi-DM.** The base change `q : 𝒳 ×_𝒴 𝒵 ⟶ 𝒵` of a quasi-DM 1-morphism of
algebraic stacks over `S` is quasi-DM: `Δ_q` is a base change of `Δ_f`, which is locally
quasi-finite in the sense of Stacks 04XB.
declarations.statement:
theorem isQuasiDM_baseChange (hf : IsQuasiDM B S hS f) :
    IsQuasiDM B S hS (twoFibreProductSquare B S hS f g).snd
declarations.comment: quasi_dm

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.AlgebraicStacks.isSeparated_baseChange
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 050F, separated.** The base change `q : 𝒳 ×_𝒴 𝒵 ⟶ 𝒵` of a separated 1-morphism of
algebraic stacks over `S` is separated: `Δ_q` is a base change of `Δ_f`, which is proper in the
sense of Stacks 04XB.
declarations.statement:
theorem isSeparated_baseChange (hf : IsSeparated B S hS f) :
    IsSeparated B S hS (twoFibreProductSquare B S hS f g).snd
declarations.comment: separated

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.AlgebraicStacks.isQuasiSeparated_baseChange
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 050F, quasi-separated.** The base change `q : 𝒳 ×_𝒴 𝒵 ⟶ 𝒵` of a quasi-separated
1-morphism of algebraic stacks over `S` is quasi-separated: `Δ_q` is a base change of `Δ_f`,
which is quasi-compact and quasi-separated in the sense of Stacks 04XB.
declarations.statement:
theorem isQuasiSeparated_baseChange (hf : IsQuasiSeparated B S hS f) :
    IsQuasiSeparated B S hS (twoFibreProductSquare B S hS f g).snd
declarations.comment: quasi_separated

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.AlgebraicStacks.isQuasiDMOver_changeOfBase
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 050G, the quasi-DM key.** Being quasi-DM over the base is stable under change of
base scheme.
declarations.statement:
theorem isQuasiDMOver_changeOfBase (𝒳' : AlgebraicStacks.{u, w} B S' hS')
    (h𝒳' : Stack.IsQuasiDMOver B S' hS' 𝒳') :
    Stack.IsQuasiDMOver B S hS (Stack.changeOfBase B S S' hS hS' g 𝒳')
declarations.comment: quasi-DM over the base

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.AlgebraicStacks.isQuasiSeparatedOver_changeOfBase
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 050G, the quasi-separated key.** Being quasi-separated over the base is stable under
change of base scheme.
declarations.statement:
theorem isQuasiSeparatedOver_changeOfBase (𝒳' : AlgebraicStacks.{u, w} B S' hS')
    (h𝒳' : Stack.IsQuasiSeparatedOver B S' hS' 𝒳') :
    Stack.IsQuasiSeparatedOver B S hS (Stack.changeOfBase B S S' hS hS' g 𝒳')
declarations.comment: quasi-separated over the base

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.AlgebraicStacks.isSeparatedOver_changeOfBase
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 050G, the separated key.** Being separated over the base is stable under change of
base scheme.
declarations.statement:
theorem isSeparatedOver_changeOfBase (𝒳' : AlgebraicStacks.{u, w} B S' hS')
    (h𝒳' : Stack.IsSeparatedOver B S' hS' 𝒳') :
    Stack.IsSeparatedOver B S hS (Stack.changeOfBase B S S' hS hS' g 𝒳')
declarations.comment: separated over the base

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.isRepresentableByAlgebraicSpaces_comparison
declarations.doc: The comparison 1-morphism `i : 𝒳 ×_𝒵 𝒴 ⟶ 𝒳 ×_𝒯 𝒴` is representable by algebraic spaces.
declarations.statement:
theorem isRepresentableByAlgebraicSpaces_comparison
    (f : 𝒳 ⟶ 𝒵) (g : 𝒴 ⟶ 𝒵) (h : 𝒵 ⟶ 𝒯) :
    IsRepresentableByAlgebraicSpaces B S hS (comparison B S hS f g h).hom.hom
declarations.comment: part (1): representable by algebraic spaces

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.isUnramified_comparison
declarations.doc:
If `h : 𝒵 ⟶ 𝒯` is Deligne–Mumford then the comparison 1-morphism
`i : 𝒳 ×_𝒵 𝒴 ⟶ 𝒳 ×_𝒯 𝒴` is unramified, in the sense of `HasRelativeProperty`. The statement
supplies, as local instances, the stability of unramifiedness of morphisms of algebraic spaces
under base change and its locality on the target for the fppf precoverage.
declarations.statement:
theorem isUnramified_comparison (f : 𝒳 ⟶ 𝒵) (g : 𝒴 ⟶ 𝒵) (h : 𝒵 ⟶ 𝒯)
    (hh : IsDM B S hS h) :
    letI : MorphismProperty.IsStableUnderBaseChange
      (fun ⦃X Y : AlgebraicSpaces B S hS⦄ (k : X ⟶ Y) =>
        Space.IsUnramified B S hS k.hom) :=
      Space.isUnramified_isStableUnderBaseChange B S hS
    letI : MorphismProperty.IsLocalAtTarget
      (fun ⦃X Y : AlgebraicSpaces B S hS⦄ (k : X ⟶ Y) =>
        Space.IsUnramified B S hS k.hom)
      (Space.Topology.fppf.precoverage.{u, u} B S hS) :=
      (Space.isUnramified_isLocalAtTarget_fpqc B S hS).of_le
        (Space.fppfPrecoverage_le_fpqcPrecoverage.{u, u} B S hS)
    HasRelativeProperty B S hS
      (fun _ _ k => Space.IsUnramified B S hS k.hom)
      (comparison B S hS f g h).hom
      (isRepresentableByAlgebraicSpaces_comparison B S hS f g h)
declarations.comment: dm_unramified

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.isLocallyOfFiniteType_comparison
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 050H, part (1), locally-of-finite-type half.** The comparison 1-morphism
`i : 𝒳 ×_𝒵 𝒴 ⟶ 𝒳 ×_𝒯 𝒴` is locally of finite type, in the sense of Properties of Stacks,
Section 04XB.

By Stacks 04Z1 the comparison is the base change of the relative diagonal `Δ_{𝒵/𝒯}` along the
right-hand leg of `AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.comparisonSquare`; that diagonal is locally of finite
type by part (2) of Stacks 04XS, with no hypothesis on `h`, and Stacks 045C carries the property
across. Together with `AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.isRepresentableByAlgebraicSpaces_comparison` this
is the whole of part (1).
declarations.statement:
theorem isLocallyOfFiniteType_comparison (f : 𝒳 ⟶ 𝒵) (g : 𝒴 ⟶ 𝒵) (h : 𝒵 ⟶ 𝒯) :
    IsLocallyOfFiniteType B S hS (comparison B S hS f g h).hom
declarations.comment: part (1): locally of finite type

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.isQuasiSeparated_comparison_of_diagonal
declarations.doc:
If the relative diagonal `Δ_{𝒵/𝒯}` is quasi-separated, then so is the comparison 1-morphism
`i : 𝒳 ×_𝒵 𝒴 ⟶ 𝒳 ×_𝒯 𝒴`, both in the sense of Properties of Stacks, Section 04XB.
declarations.statement:
theorem isQuasiSeparated_comparison_of_diagonal (f : 𝒳 ⟶ 𝒵) (g : 𝒴 ⟶ 𝒵) (h : 𝒵 ⟶ 𝒯)
    (hΔ : IsQuasiSeparated B S hS (relativeDiagonalAlgebraicStacks B S hS h).hom) :
    IsQuasiSeparated B S hS (comparison B S hS f g h).hom
declarations.comment: quasi_separated_diagonal

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.isSeparated_comparison_of_diagonal
declarations.doc:
If the relative diagonal `Δ_{𝒵/𝒯}` is separated, then so is the comparison 1-morphism
`i : 𝒳 ×_𝒵 𝒴 ⟶ 𝒳 ×_𝒯 𝒴`, both in the sense of Properties of Stacks, Section 04XB.
declarations.statement:
theorem isSeparated_comparison_of_diagonal (f : 𝒳 ⟶ 𝒵) (g : 𝒴 ⟶ 𝒵) (h : 𝒵 ⟶ 𝒯)
    (hΔ : IsSeparated B S hS (relativeDiagonalAlgebraicStacks B S hS h).hom) :
    IsSeparated B S hS (comparison B S hS f g h).hom
declarations.comment: separated_diagonal

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.isLocallyQuasiFinite_comparison
declarations.doc:
If `h : 𝒵 ⟶ 𝒯` is quasi-DM then the comparison 1-morphism `i : 𝒳 ×_𝒵 𝒴 ⟶ 𝒳 ×_𝒯 𝒴` is
locally quasi-finite, in the sense of Properties of Stacks, Section 04XB.
declarations.statement:
theorem isLocallyQuasiFinite_comparison (f : 𝒳 ⟶ 𝒵) (g : 𝒴 ⟶ 𝒵) (h : 𝒵 ⟶ 𝒯)
    (hh : AlgebraicStacks.IsQuasiDM B S hS h) :
    IsLocallyQuasiFinite B S hS (comparison B S hS f g h).hom
declarations.comment: quasi_dm_lqf

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.isProper_comparison
declarations.doc:
If `h : 𝒵 ⟶ 𝒯` is separated then the comparison 1-morphism `i : 𝒳 ×_𝒵 𝒴 ⟶ 𝒳 ×_𝒯 𝒴` is
proper, in the sense of Properties of Stacks, Section 04XB.
declarations.statement:
theorem isProper_comparison (f : 𝒳 ⟶ 𝒵) (g : 𝒴 ⟶ 𝒵) (h : 𝒵 ⟶ 𝒯)
    (hh : AlgebraicStacks.IsSeparated B S hS h) :
    IsProper B S hS (comparison B S hS f g h).hom
declarations.comment: separated_proper

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.isQuasiCompact_comparison
declarations.doc:
If `h : 𝒵 ⟶ 𝒯` is quasi-separated as a 1-morphism of algebraic stacks, then the comparison
1-morphism `i : 𝒳 ×_𝒵 𝒴 ⟶ 𝒳 ×_𝒯 𝒴` is quasi-compact, in the sense of Properties of Stacks,
Section 04XB.
declarations.statement:
theorem isQuasiCompact_comparison (f : 𝒳 ⟶ 𝒵) (g : 𝒴 ⟶ 𝒵) (h : 𝒵 ⟶ 𝒯)
    (hh : AlgebraicStacks.IsQuasiSeparated B S hS h) :
    IsQuasiCompact B S hS (comparison B S hS f g h).hom
declarations.comment: part (7), the quasi-compactness half

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.isQuasiSeparated_comparison
declarations.doc:
If `h : 𝒵 ⟶ 𝒯` is quasi-separated as a 1-morphism of algebraic stacks, then the comparison
1-morphism `i : 𝒳 ×_𝒵 𝒴 ⟶ 𝒳 ×_𝒯 𝒴` is quasi-separated, in the sense of Properties of Stacks,
Section 04XB.
declarations.statement:
theorem isQuasiSeparated_comparison (f : 𝒳 ⟶ 𝒵) (g : 𝒴 ⟶ 𝒵) (h : 𝒵 ⟶ 𝒯)
    (hh : AlgebraicStacks.IsQuasiSeparated B S hS h) :
    IsQuasiSeparated B S hS (comparison B S hS f g h).hom
declarations.comment: part (7), the quasi-separatedness half

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.AlgebraicStacks.isQuasiSeparated_mapBase
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 050H, part (2).** If the relative diagonal `Δ_{𝒵/𝒯}` is quasi-separated in the sense
of Stacks 04XB, then so is the comparison 1-morphism `i : 𝒳 ×_𝒵 𝒴 ⟶ 𝒳 ×_𝒯 𝒴`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isQuasiSeparated_mapBase
    (hΔ : Stack.IsQuasiSeparated.{u, u, u + 1} B S hS
      (relativeDiagonal.{u, u, u + 1} B S hS 𝒵.val 𝒯.val h.hom)) :
    Stack.IsQuasiSeparated.{u, u, u + 1} B S hS (mapBase B S hS f g h).hom
declarations.comment: part (2): quasi-separated

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.AlgebraicStacks.isSeparated_mapBase
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 050H, part (3).** If the relative diagonal `Δ_{𝒵/𝒯}` is separated in the sense of
Stacks 04XB, then so is the comparison 1-morphism `i : 𝒳 ×_𝒵 𝒴 ⟶ 𝒳 ×_𝒯 𝒴`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isSeparated_mapBase
    (hΔ : Stack.IsSeparated.{u, u, u + 1} B S hS
      (relativeDiagonal.{u, u, u + 1} B S hS 𝒵.val 𝒯.val h.hom)) :
    Stack.IsSeparated.{u, u, u + 1} B S hS (mapBase B S hS f g h).hom
declarations.comment: part (3): separated

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.AlgebraicStacks.isUnramified_mapBase_of_isDM
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 050H, part (4).** If `h : 𝒵 ⟶ 𝒯` is Deligne–Mumford, then the comparison 1-morphism
`i : 𝒳 ×_𝒵 𝒴 ⟶ 𝒳 ×_𝒯 𝒴` is unramified in the sense of Stacks 04XB: `i` is a base change of
`Δ_{𝒵/𝒯}`, which is unramified by the definition of Stacks 04YW.
declarations.statement:
theorem isUnramified_mapBase_of_isDM (hh : Stack.IsDM B S hS h) :
    ∀ (U : BigFppfOver B S hS)
      (z : BigFppfOver B U.left.1 U.left.2 ⥤
        (twoFibreProduct B S hS (f ≫ h) (g ≫ h)).val.val.obj)
      (_hz : z ⋙ (twoFibreProduct B S hS (f ≫ h) (g ≫ h)).val.val.p = Over.map U.hom)
      (F : (BigFppfOver B U.left.1 U.left.2)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u)
      (hF : IsAlgebraicSpace B U.left.1 U.left.2 F),
        Nonempty (StacksRepresentableCFG.EquivalenceOver
          (TwoFibreProductOver.fst (Over.map U.hom)
            (twoFibreProduct B S hS f g).val.val.p
            (twoFibreProduct B S hS (f ≫ h) (g ≫ h)).val.val.p z
            (CatFiberedInGroupoids.homFunctor (mapBase B S hS f g h).hom))
          (presheafOfCategories (F ⋙ typeToCat)).p) →
        Space.IsUnramified B S hS
          (algebraicSpaceMap B S hS U
            ((spacesOverSmallerBaseFunctor B U.left.1 S U.left.2 hS U.hom).obj ⟨F, hF⟩)).hom
declarations.comment: part (4): unramified

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.AlgebraicStacks.isLocallyQuasiFinite_mapBase_of_isQuasiDM
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 050H, part (5).** If `h : 𝒵 ⟶ 𝒯` is quasi-DM, then the comparison 1-morphism
`i : 𝒳 ×_𝒵 𝒴 ⟶ 𝒳 ×_𝒯 𝒴` is locally quasi-finite in the sense of Stacks 04XB.
declarations.statement:
theorem isLocallyQuasiFinite_mapBase_of_isQuasiDM (hh : IsQuasiDM B S hS h) :
    Stack.IsLocallyQuasiFinite.{u, u, u + 1} B S hS (mapBase B S hS f g h).hom
declarations.comment: part (5): locally quasi-finite

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.AlgebraicStacks.isProper_mapBase_of_isSeparated
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 050H, part (6).** If `h : 𝒵 ⟶ 𝒯` is separated, then the comparison 1-morphism
`i : 𝒳 ×_𝒵 𝒴 ⟶ 𝒳 ×_𝒯 𝒴` is proper in the sense of Stacks 04XB.
declarations.statement:
theorem isProper_mapBase_of_isSeparated (hh : IsSeparated B S hS h) :
    Stack.IsProper.{u, u, u + 1} B S hS (mapBase B S hS f g h).hom
declarations.comment: part (6): proper

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.AlgebraicStacks.isQuasiCompactAndQuasiSeparated_mapBase
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 050H, part (7).** If `h : 𝒵 ⟶ 𝒯` is quasi-separated, then the comparison 1-morphism
`i : 𝒳 ×_𝒵 𝒴 ⟶ 𝒳 ×_𝒯 𝒴` is quasi-compact and quasi-separated in the sense of Stacks 04XB.
declarations.statement:
theorem isQuasiCompactAndQuasiSeparated_mapBase
    (hh : IsQuasiSeparated B S hS h) :
    Stack.IsQuasiCompact.{u, u, u + 1} B S hS (mapBase B S hS f g h).hom ∧
      Stack.IsQuasiSeparated.{u, u, u + 1} B S hS (mapBase B S hS f g h).hom
declarations.comment: part (7): quasi-compact and quasi-separated

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.isRepresentableByAlgebraicSpaces_graph
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 050I, part (1), representability half.** The graph of a 1-morphism of algebraic
stacks over a base algebraic stack is representable by algebraic spaces.

The graph is 2-isomorphic to the comparison 1-morphism of Stacks 050H precomposed and
postcomposed with equivalences, and representability by algebraic spaces is invariant under such
a square by Stacks 0457.
declarations.statement:
theorem isRepresentableByAlgebraicSpaces_graph (g : 𝒳 ⟶ 𝒴) (p : 𝒳 ⟶ 𝒯) (q : 𝒴 ⟶ 𝒯)
    (η : p ≅ g ≫ q) :
    IsRepresentableByAlgebraicSpaces B S hS (graph B S hS g p q η).hom.hom
declarations.comment: part (1): representable by algebraic spaces

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.isUnramified_graph
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 050I, part (2).** If `q : 𝒴 ⟶ 𝒯` is Deligne–Mumford then the graph of `g : 𝒳 ⟶ 𝒴`
over `𝒯` is unramified, in the relative sense of Stacks 03YK.

By Stacks 050H part (4) the comparison 1-morphism `𝒳 ×_𝒴 𝒴 ⟶ 𝒳 ×_𝒯 𝒴` is unramified, and
`AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.hasRelativeProperty_graph_of_comparison` carries that to the graph. The
two instance arguments of Stacks 03YK are Stacks 03ZJ and Stacks 042A composed with the
comparison of the fppf and fpqc precoverages.
declarations.statement:
theorem isUnramified_graph (g : 𝒳 ⟶ 𝒴) (p : 𝒳 ⟶ 𝒯) (q : 𝒴 ⟶ 𝒯) (η : p ≅ g ≫ q)
    (hq : IsDM B S hS q) :
    letI : MorphismProperty.IsStableUnderBaseChange
      (fun ⦃X Y : AlgebraicSpaces B S hS⦄ (k : X ⟶ Y) =>
        Space.IsUnramified B S hS k.hom) :=
      Space.isUnramified_isStableUnderBaseChange B S hS
    letI : MorphismProperty.IsLocalAtTarget
      (fun ⦃X Y : AlgebraicSpaces B S hS⦄ (k : X ⟶ Y) =>
        Space.IsUnramified B S hS k.hom)
      (Space.Topology.fppf.precoverage.{u, u} B S hS) :=
      (Space.isUnramified_isLocalAtTarget_fpqc B S hS).of_le
        (Space.fppfPrecoverage_le_fpqcPrecoverage.{u, u} B S hS)
    HasRelativeProperty B S hS
      (fun _ _ k => Space.IsUnramified B S hS k.hom)
      (graph B S hS g p q η).hom
      (isRepresentableByAlgebraicSpaces_graph B S hS g p q η)
declarations.comment: part (2)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.isLocallyOfFiniteType_graph
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 050I, part (1), locally-of-finite-type half.** The graph of a 1-morphism of
algebraic stacks over a base algebraic stack is locally of finite type, in the sense of
Properties of Stacks, Section 04XB.

By the locally-of-finite-type half of Stacks 050H part (1) the comparison 1-morphism
`𝒳 ×_𝒴 𝒴 ⟶ 𝒳 ×_𝒯 𝒴` is locally of finite type, and
`AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.relativeProperty_graph_of_comparison` carries that to the graph. No
hypothesis on `q` is needed, exactly as in Stacks 050H. Together with
`AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.isRepresentableByAlgebraicSpaces_graph` this is the whole of part (1).
declarations.statement:
theorem isLocallyOfFiniteType_graph (g : 𝒳 ⟶ 𝒴) (p : 𝒳 ⟶ 𝒯) (q : 𝒴 ⟶ 𝒯) (η : p ≅ g ≫ q) :
    IsLocallyOfFiniteType B S hS (graph B S hS g p q η).hom
declarations.comment: part (1): locally of finite type

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.isLocallyQuasiFinite_graph
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 050I, part (3).** If `q : 𝒴 ⟶ 𝒯` is quasi-DM then the graph of `g : 𝒳 ⟶ 𝒴` over `𝒯`
is locally quasi-finite, in the sense of Properties of Stacks, Section 04XB.

By Stacks 050H part (5) the comparison 1-morphism `𝒳 ×_𝒴 𝒴 ⟶ 𝒳 ×_𝒯 𝒴` is locally quasi-finite,
and `AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.relativeProperty_graph_of_comparison` carries that to the graph.
One statement suffices: Stacks 050H takes the quasi-DM condition of Stacks 04YW apart, so the
input is local quasi-finiteness alone.
declarations.statement:
theorem isLocallyQuasiFinite_graph (g : 𝒳 ⟶ 𝒴) (p : 𝒳 ⟶ 𝒯) (q : 𝒴 ⟶ 𝒯) (η : p ≅ g ≫ q)
    (hq : AlgebraicStacks.IsQuasiDM B S hS q) :
    IsLocallyQuasiFinite B S hS (graph B S hS g p q η).hom
declarations.comment: part (3)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.isProper_graph
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 050I, part (4).** If `q : 𝒴 ⟶ 𝒯` is separated then the graph of `g : 𝒳 ⟶ 𝒴` over
`𝒯` is proper, in the sense of Properties of Stacks, Section 04XB.

By Stacks 050H part (6) the comparison 1-morphism `𝒳 ×_𝒴 𝒴 ⟶ 𝒳 ×_𝒯 𝒴` is proper, and
`AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.relativeProperty_graph_of_comparison` carries that to the graph. The
separatedness condition of Stacks 04YW is a single property of the relative diagonal, so there
is no conjunction to project here.
declarations.statement:
theorem isProper_graph (g : 𝒳 ⟶ 𝒴) (p : 𝒳 ⟶ 𝒯) (q : 𝒴 ⟶ 𝒯) (η : p ≅ g ≫ q)
    (hq : AlgebraicStacks.IsSeparated B S hS q) :
    IsProper B S hS (graph B S hS g p q η).hom
declarations.comment: part (4)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.isQuasiCompact_graph
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 050I, part (5), the quasi-compactness half.** If `q : 𝒴 ⟶ 𝒯` is quasi-separated
then the graph of `g : 𝒳 ⟶ 𝒴` over `𝒯` is quasi-compact, in the sense of Properties of Stacks,
Section 04XB.

By Stacks 050H part (7) the comparison 1-morphism `𝒳 ×_𝒴 𝒴 ⟶ 𝒳 ×_𝒯 𝒴` is quasi-compact, and
`AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.relativeProperty_graph_of_comparison` carries that to the graph. A
single statement suffices here, because Stacks 050H already projects the conjunction of
Stacks 04YW quasi-separatedness: the input is quasi-compactness alone. The property is the
longhand lambda rather than `AlgebraicGeometry.Space.quasiCompactProperty`, so neither
Stacks 03HF nor Stacks 041L is needed even though both are available.
declarations.statement:
theorem isQuasiCompact_graph (g : 𝒳 ⟶ 𝒴) (p : 𝒳 ⟶ 𝒯) (q : 𝒴 ⟶ 𝒯) (η : p ≅ g ≫ q)
    (hq : AlgebraicStacks.IsQuasiSeparated B S hS q) :
    IsQuasiCompact B S hS (graph B S hS g p q η).hom
declarations.comment: part (5): quasi-compact

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.isQuasiSeparated_graph
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 050I, part (5), the quasi-separatedness half.** If `q : 𝒴 ⟶ 𝒯` is quasi-separated
then the graph of `g : 𝒳 ⟶ 𝒴` over `𝒯` is quasi-separated, in the sense of Properties of Stacks,
Section 04XB.

As for the quasi-compactness half, over the second conjunct: Stacks 050H part (7) is stated
twice, once for each conjunct of the quasi-separatedness condition of Stacks 04YW, so the input
here is quasi-separatedness of the comparison 1-morphism alone.
declarations.statement:
theorem isQuasiSeparated_graph (g : 𝒳 ⟶ 𝒴) (p : 𝒳 ⟶ 𝒯) (q : 𝒴 ⟶ 𝒯) (η : p ≅ g ≫ q)
    (hq : AlgebraicStacks.IsQuasiSeparated B S hS q) :
    IsQuasiSeparated B S hS (graph B S hS g p q η).hom
declarations.comment: part (5): quasi-separated

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.isRepresentableByAlgebraicSpaces_section
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 050J, part (1), representability half.** A section of a 1-morphism of algebraic
stacks is representable by algebraic spaces.

The graph of `s` over `𝒯`, taken for the cospan `(𝟙 𝒯, f)`, is representable by algebraic spaces
by Stacks 050I, and `s` is 2-isomorphic to its composite with the second projection, which is an
equivalence by `AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.sectionSecondProjection_isEquivalence`. Stacks 0457
carries representability across that square.
declarations.statement:
theorem isRepresentableByAlgebraicSpaces_section (f : 𝒳 ⟶ 𝒯) (s : 𝒯 ⟶ 𝒳)
    (hs : Nonempty (s ≫ f ≅ 𝟙 𝒯)) :
    IsRepresentableByAlgebraicSpaces B S hS s.hom.hom
declarations.comment: part (1): representable by algebraic spaces

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.isLocallyOfFiniteType_section
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 050J, part (1), locally-of-finite-type half.** A section of a 1-morphism of
algebraic stacks is locally of finite type, in the sense of Properties of Stacks, Section 04XB.

By the locally-of-finite-type half of Stacks 050I part (1) the graph
`Γ_s : 𝒯 ⟶ 𝒯 ×_{𝟙 𝒯, 𝒯, f} 𝒳` is locally of finite type, and
`AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.relativeProperty_section_of_graph` carries that to `s`. No hypothesis on
`f` is needed, exactly as in Stacks 050I and Stacks 050H. Together with
`AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.isRepresentableByAlgebraicSpaces_section` this is the whole of
part (1).
declarations.statement:
theorem isLocallyOfFiniteType_section (f : 𝒳 ⟶ 𝒯) (s : 𝒯 ⟶ 𝒳)
    (hs : Nonempty (s ≫ f ≅ 𝟙 𝒯)) :
    IsLocallyOfFiniteType B S hS s.hom
declarations.comment: part (1): locally of finite type

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.isUnramified_section
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 050J, part (2).** If `f : 𝒳 ⟶ 𝒯` is Deligne–Mumford then a section of `f` is
unramified, in the relative sense of Stacks 03YK.

By Stacks 050I part (2) the graph `Γ_s : 𝒯 ⟶ 𝒯 ×_{𝟙 𝒯, 𝒯, f} 𝒳` is unramified, and
`AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.hasRelativeProperty_section_of_graph` carries that to `s`. The two
instance arguments of Stacks 03YK are Stacks 03ZJ and Stacks 042A composed with the comparison
of the fppf and fpqc precoverages.
declarations.statement:
theorem isUnramified_section (f : 𝒳 ⟶ 𝒯) (s : 𝒯 ⟶ 𝒳) (hs : Nonempty (s ≫ f ≅ 𝟙 𝒯))
    (hf : IsDM B S hS f) :
    letI : MorphismProperty.IsStableUnderBaseChange
      (fun ⦃X Y : AlgebraicSpaces B S hS⦄ (k : X ⟶ Y) =>
        Space.IsUnramified B S hS k.hom) :=
      Space.isUnramified_isStableUnderBaseChange B S hS
    letI : MorphismProperty.IsLocalAtTarget
      (fun ⦃X Y : AlgebraicSpaces B S hS⦄ (k : X ⟶ Y) =>
        Space.IsUnramified B S hS k.hom)
      (Space.Topology.fppf.precoverage.{u, u} B S hS) :=
      (Space.isUnramified_isLocalAtTarget_fpqc B S hS).of_le
        (Space.fppfPrecoverage_le_fpqcPrecoverage.{u, u} B S hS)
    HasRelativeProperty B S hS
      (fun _ _ k => Space.IsUnramified B S hS k.hom)
      s.hom (isRepresentableByAlgebraicSpaces_section B S hS f s hs)
declarations.comment: part (2): unramified

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.isLocallyQuasiFinite_section
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 050J, part (3).** If `f : 𝒳 ⟶ 𝒯` is quasi-DM then a section of `f` is locally
quasi-finite, in the sense of Properties of Stacks, Section 04XB.

By Stacks 050I part (3) the graph `Γ_s : 𝒯 ⟶ 𝒯 ×_{𝟙 𝒯, 𝒯, f} 𝒳` is locally quasi-finite, and
`AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.relativeProperty_section_of_graph` carries that to `s`. One statement
suffices: Stacks 050I already takes the quasi-DM condition of Stacks 04YW apart, so the input is
local quasi-finiteness alone. The property is the longhand lambda rather than the packaged local
quasi-finiteness of Stacks 06MF, so no instance of Stacks 03YK is needed.
declarations.statement:
theorem isLocallyQuasiFinite_section (f : 𝒳 ⟶ 𝒯) (s : 𝒯 ⟶ 𝒳) (hs : Nonempty (s ≫ f ≅ 𝟙 𝒯))
    (hf : AlgebraicStacks.IsQuasiDM B S hS f) :
    IsLocallyQuasiFinite B S hS s.hom
declarations.comment: part (3): locally quasi-finite

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.isRelativelyProper_section
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 050J, part (4).** If `f : 𝒳 ⟶ 𝒯` is separated then a section of `f` is proper in
the sense of Properties of Stacks, Section 04XB.

By Stacks 050I part (4) the graph `Γ_s : 𝒯 ⟶ 𝒯 ×_{𝟙 𝒯, 𝒯, f} 𝒳` is proper, and
`AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.relativeProperty_section_of_graph` carries that to `s`. The separatedness
condition of Stacks 04YW is a single property of the relative diagonal, so there is no
conjunction to project here. The property is the longhand lambda rather than
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.properProperty`, so the fppf
`CategoryTheory.MorphismProperty.IsLocalAtTarget` instance of Stacks 0422 is not needed — which
matters here, because this library does not have it.

Properness is read in the sense of Section 04XB, as it is in Stacks 050I part (4)
(`AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.isProper_graph`) and in Stacks 050H part (6)
(`AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.isProper_comparison`). That is the reading the source's own proof
forces: Stacks 050J is a special case of Stacks 050I, so its conclusions are the conclusions of
Stacks 050I, and `s` carries the Section 04XB notions because part (1) makes it representable by
algebraic spaces. Reading part (4) at Stacks 0CL5 instead would assert properness of `s` as a
1-morphism of algebraic stacks, which is a different statement from the one Stacks 050I
supplies.
declarations.statement:
theorem isRelativelyProper_section (f : 𝒳 ⟶ 𝒯) (s : 𝒯 ⟶ 𝒳) (hs : Nonempty (s ≫ f ≅ 𝟙 𝒯))
    (hf : AlgebraicStacks.IsSeparated B S hS f) :
    IsProper B S hS s.hom
declarations.comment: part (4): proper

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.isQuasiCompact_section
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 050J, part (5), quasi-compactness half.** If `f : 𝒳 ⟶ 𝒯` is quasi-separated then a
section of `f` is quasi-compact in the sense of Stacks 050U: every base change of it by a
quasi-compact algebraic stack is again a quasi-compact algebraic stack.

The section is representable by algebraic spaces by part (1), and quasi-compact in the relative
sense of Properties of Stacks, Section 04XB by
`AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.isRelativelyQuasiCompact_section`. Stacks 050T identifies the two
notions for a 1-morphism representable by algebraic spaces, and that is the whole step.
declarations.statement:
theorem isQuasiCompact_section (f : 𝒳 ⟶ 𝒯) (s : 𝒯 ⟶ 𝒳) (hs : Nonempty (s ≫ f ≅ 𝟙 𝒯))
    (hf : AlgebraicStacks.IsQuasiSeparated B S hS f) :
    IsQuasiCompactMorphism B S hS s
declarations.comment: part (5): quasi-compact

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.isQuasiSeparated_section
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 050J, part (5), quasi-separatedness half.** If `f : 𝒳 ⟶ 𝒯` is quasi-separated then
a section of `f` is quasi-separated, in the sense of Properties of Stacks, Section 04XB.

By Stacks 050I part (5) the graph `Γ_s : 𝒯 ⟶ 𝒯 ×_{𝟙 𝒯, 𝒯, f} 𝒳` is quasi-separated, and
`AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.relativeProperty_section_of_graph` carries that to `s`. A single
statement suffices, because Stacks 050I already projects the conjunction of Stacks 04YW
quasi-separatedness: the input is quasi-separatedness alone. The quasi-compactness half of
part (5) is `AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.isQuasiCompact_section`, which reads the Section 04XB
assertion `AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.isRelativelyQuasiCompact_section` across Stacks 050T into the
notion of Stacks 050U.
declarations.statement:
theorem isQuasiSeparated_section (f : 𝒳 ⟶ 𝒯) (s : 𝒯 ⟶ 𝒳) (hs : Nonempty (s ≫ f ≅ 𝟙 𝒯))
    (hf : AlgebraicStacks.IsQuasiSeparated B S hS f) :
    IsQuasiSeparated B S hS s.hom
declarations.comment: part (5): quasi-separated

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.AlgebraicStacks.isDM_comp
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 050K, DM.** The composite of two Deligne–Mumford 1-morphisms of algebraic stacks over
`S` is Deligne–Mumford: its relative diagonal is `Δ_f` followed by the comparison 1-morphism `i`,
`Δ_f` is unramified in the sense of Stacks 04XB because `f` is DM, `i` is unramified because `g`
is DM (**Stacks 050H**, part (4)), and a condition of Stacks 04XB at a property stable under
composition which descends along a surjective étale scheme chart of the target is stable under
composition (**Stacks 045B**).
declarations.statement:
theorem isDM_comp (f : 𝒳 ⟶ 𝒴) (g : 𝒴 ⟶ 𝒵) (hf : Stack.IsDM B S hS f)
    (hg : Stack.IsDM B S hS g) : Stack.IsDM B S hS (f ≫ g)
declarations.comment: dm

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.AlgebraicStacks.isQuasiDM_comp
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 050K, quasi-DM.** The composite of two quasi-DM 1-morphisms of algebraic stacks over
`S` is quasi-DM: `Δ_{f ≫ g}` is `Δ_f` followed by the comparison 1-morphism `i`, `Δ_f` is locally
quasi-finite in the sense of Stacks 04XB because `f` is quasi-DM, `i` is locally quasi-finite
because `g` is quasi-DM (**Stacks 050H**, part (5)), and local quasi-finiteness of morphisms of
algebraic spaces over `S` composes (**Stacks 03XK**) and is fpqc local on the base
(**Stacks 0427**).
declarations.statement:
theorem isQuasiDM_comp (f : 𝒳 ⟶ 𝒴) (g : 𝒴 ⟶ 𝒵) (hf : IsQuasiDM B S hS f)
    (hg : IsQuasiDM B S hS g) : IsQuasiDM B S hS (f ≫ g)
declarations.comment: quasi-DM

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.AlgebraicStacks.isSeparated_comp
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 050K, separated.** The composite of two separated 1-morphisms of algebraic stacks
over `S` is separated: `Δ_{f ≫ g}` is `Δ_f` followed by the comparison 1-morphism `i`, `Δ_f` is
proper in the sense of Stacks 04XB because `f` is separated, `i` is proper because `g` is
separated (**Stacks 050H**, part (6)), and properness of morphisms of algebraic spaces over `S`
composes (**Stacks 04XY**) and descends along a surjective étale scheme chart of the target
(`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.properMorphismProperty_of_pullbackSnd_atlas`).
declarations.statement:
theorem isSeparated_comp (f : 𝒳 ⟶ 𝒴) (g : 𝒴 ⟶ 𝒵) (hf : IsSeparated B S hS f)
    (hg : IsSeparated B S hS g) : IsSeparated B S hS (f ≫ g)
declarations.comment: separated

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.AlgebraicStacks.isQuasiSeparated_comp
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 050K, quasi-separated.** The composite of two quasi-separated 1-morphisms of
algebraic stacks over `S` is quasi-separated. Quasi-separatedness of Stacks 04YW is the
conjunction of two conditions of Stacks 04XB on `Δ_f` — quasi-compactness and
quasi-separatedness — and each half is the same composition argument at its own property:
`Δ_{f ≫ g} = Δ_f ≫ i`, the half for `Δ_f` is the axiom for `f`, the half for `i` comes from the
axiom for `g` by **Stacks 050H**, part (7), and quasi-compactness and quasi-separatedness of
morphisms of algebraic spaces over `S` compose (**Stacks 03HG**, **Stacks 03KQ**) and are fpqc
local on the base (**Stacks 041L**, **Stacks 041N**).
declarations.statement:
theorem isQuasiSeparated_comp (f : 𝒳 ⟶ 𝒴) (g : 𝒴 ⟶ 𝒵) (hf : IsQuasiSeparated B S hS f)
    (hg : IsQuasiSeparated B S hS g) : IsQuasiSeparated B S hS (f ≫ g)
declarations.comment: quasi-separated

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.AlgebraicStacks.isAbsolutelyQuasiSeparated_of_isQuasiSeparated
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 050L, part (8).** If `f : 𝒳 ⟶ 𝒴` is quasi-separated and `𝒴` is quasi-separated, then
`𝒳` is quasi-separated.

Both absolute properties are quasi-separatedness over the terminal scheme of the views
`AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.AlgebraicStacks.viewOverIntegers` of `𝒳` and `𝒴` there, and that view is
`AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.changeBaseAlgebraicStack` along `terminal.from S` on the nose. So this is
part (4) at the terminal scheme, applied to the 1-morphism of views that the hom-bijection of
Stacks 04X5 assigns to `f`, which is quasi-separated by
`AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.AlgebraicStacks.isQuasiSeparated_changeBase`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isAbsolutelyQuasiSeparated_of_isQuasiSeparated (f : 𝒳 ⟶ 𝒴)
    (hY : IsAbsolutelyQuasiSeparated B S hS hZ 𝒴) (hf : IsQuasiSeparated B S hS f) :
    IsAbsolutelyQuasiSeparated B S hS hZ 𝒳
declarations.comment: quasi_separated_absolute

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.isSeparatedOver_of_isSeparated
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 050L, part (3).** If `𝒴` is separated over `S` and the 1-morphism `f : 𝒳 ⟶ 𝒴` is
separated, then `𝒳` is separated over `S`.

Being separated over `S` is being separated as a structure morphism (**Stacks 050D**, part (3)),
the structure morphism of `𝒳` is `f` followed by that of `𝒴`
(`AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.comp_structureMorphism`), and separated 1-morphisms compose
(**Stacks 050K**).
declarations.statement:
theorem isSeparatedOver_of_isSeparated (f : 𝒳 ⟶ 𝒴) (h𝒴 : IsSeparatedOver B S hS 𝒴)
    (hf : AlgebraicStacks.IsSeparated B S hS f) : IsSeparatedOver B S hS 𝒳
declarations.comment: part (3): separated over the base

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.isDMAbs_of_isDM
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 050L, part (5).** If `𝒴` is DM and the 1-morphism `f : 𝒳 ⟶ 𝒴` is DM, then `𝒳` is
DM — the two conditions on objects in the absolute sense of **Stacks 050D**, part (5).

Being DM is being DM over `Spec(ℤ)` after viewing (**Stacks 050D**, part (5)); the structure
morphism over `Spec(ℤ)` of `𝒳` viewed is `f` viewed followed by that of `𝒴` viewed
(`AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.comp_structureMorphism` at the terminal base); the DM axiom for `f`
survives the viewing (`AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.isDM_changeBaseHomAlgebraicStacks`); and DM
1-morphisms compose (**Stacks 050K**). So this is part (1) of Stacks 050L read at the base
`Spec(ℤ)`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isDMAbs_of_isDM (f : 𝒳 ⟶ 𝒴) (h𝒴 : IsDMAbs.{u, w, w'} B S hS 𝒴)
    (hf : IsDM B S hS f) : IsDMAbs.{u, w, w'} B S hS 𝒳
declarations.comment: part (5): DM

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.isQuasiDMAbs_of_isQuasiDM
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 050L, part (6).** If `𝒴` is quasi-DM and the 1-morphism `f : 𝒳 ⟶ 𝒴` is quasi-DM,
then `𝒳` is quasi-DM — the two conditions on objects in the absolute sense of **Stacks 050D**,
part (6).

This is part (2) of Stacks 050L read at the base `Spec(ℤ)`, with
`AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.isQuasiDM_changeBaseHomAlgebraicStacks` supplying the axiom for the
viewed 1-morphism.
declarations.statement:
theorem isQuasiDMAbs_of_isQuasiDM (f : 𝒳 ⟶ 𝒴) (h𝒴 : IsQuasiDMAbs.{u, w, w'} B S hS 𝒴)
    (hf : AlgebraicStacks.IsQuasiDM B S hS f) : IsQuasiDMAbs.{u, w, w'} B S hS 𝒳
declarations.comment: part (6): quasi-DM

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.isSeparatedAbs_of_isSeparated
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 050L, part (7).** If `𝒴` is separated and the 1-morphism `f : 𝒳 ⟶ 𝒴` is separated,
then `𝒳` is separated — the two conditions on objects in the absolute sense of **Stacks 050D**,
part (7).

This is part (3) of Stacks 050L read at the base `Spec(ℤ)`. The hypothesis on `f` is the
Stacks 04YW separatedness axiom for `f` **viewed over `Spec(ℤ)`**, which is the base the absolute
statement lives at; it is not the axiom over `S`. Unlike the DM axiom of part (5), the
separatedness axiom is not known in this library to survive the viewing: it is the Stacks 04XB
condition at properness, which is not an every-étale-chart condition. See the implementation
notes of this file.
declarations.statement:
theorem isSeparatedAbs_of_isSeparated (f : 𝒳 ⟶ 𝒴) (h𝒴 : IsSeparatedAbs.{u, w, w'} B S hS 𝒴)
    (hf : AlgebraicStacks.IsSeparated B _ (contains_specULiftZ B)
      (viewOverIntHom.{u, w, w'} B S hS f)) :
    IsSeparatedAbs.{u, w, w'} B S hS 𝒳
declarations.comment: part (7): separated, f's axiom read over Spec(Z) not over S

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.isQuasiSeparatedAbs_of_isQuasiSeparated
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 050L, part (8).** If `𝒴` is quasi-separated and the 1-morphism `f : 𝒳 ⟶ 𝒴` is
quasi-separated, then `𝒳` is quasi-separated — the two conditions on objects in the absolute
sense of **Stacks 050D**, part (8), and so each the conjunction of quasi-compactness and
quasi-separatedness of a relative diagonal. Both conjuncts of the conclusion are proved, through
`AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.AlgebraicStacks.isQuasiSeparated_comp`.

This is part (4) of Stacks 050L read at the base `Spec(ℤ)`. As in part (7) the hypothesis on `f`
is the Stacks 04YW axiom for `f` **viewed over `Spec(ℤ)`**: quasi-separatedness is the Stacks
04XB condition at quasi-compactness together with quasi-separatedness of morphisms of algebraic
spaces, neither of which is an every-étale-chart condition.
declarations.statement:
theorem isQuasiSeparatedAbs_of_isQuasiSeparated (f : 𝒳 ⟶ 𝒴)
    (h𝒴 : IsQuasiSeparatedAbs.{u, w, w'} B S hS 𝒴)
    (hf : AlgebraicStacks.IsQuasiSeparated B _ (contains_specULiftZ B)
      (viewOverIntHom.{u, w, w'} B S hS f)) :
    IsQuasiSeparatedAbs.{u, w, w'} B S hS 𝒳
declarations.comment: part (8): quasi-separated, f's axiom read over Spec(Z) not over S

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.AlgebraicStacks.isDMOver_of_isDM
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 050L, part (1).** If `f : 𝒳 ⟶ 𝒴` is Deligne–Mumford and `𝒴` is Deligne–Mumford over
the base scheme `S`, then `𝒳` is Deligne–Mumford over `S`.

The structure morphism of `𝒳` is `f` followed by the structure morphism of `𝒴`
(`AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.comp_structureMorphism`), so this is the Deligne–Mumford case of
Stacks 050K.
declarations.statement:
theorem isDMOver_of_isDM (f : 𝒳 ⟶ 𝒴) (hY : Stack.IsDMOver B S hS 𝒴) (hf : Stack.IsDM B S hS f) :
    Stack.IsDMOver B S hS 𝒳
declarations.comment: dm_over_s

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.AlgebraicStacks.isQuasiDMOver_of_isQuasiDM
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 050L, part (2).** If `f : 𝒳 ⟶ 𝒴` is quasi-DM and `𝒴` is quasi-DM over the base
scheme `S`, then `𝒳` is quasi-DM over `S`.

The structure morphism of `𝒳` is `f` followed by the structure morphism of `𝒴`
(`AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.comp_structureMorphism`), so this is the quasi-DM case of
Stacks 050K.
declarations.statement:
theorem isQuasiDMOver_of_isQuasiDM (f : 𝒳 ⟶ 𝒴) (hY : Stack.IsQuasiDMOver B S hS 𝒴)
    (hf : IsQuasiDM B S hS f) :
    Stack.IsQuasiDMOver B S hS 𝒳
declarations.comment: quasi_dm_over_s

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.AlgebraicStacks.isQuasiSeparatedOver_of_isQuasiSeparated
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 050L, part (4).** If `f : 𝒳 ⟶ 𝒴` is quasi-separated and `𝒴` is quasi-separated over
the base scheme `S`, then `𝒳` is quasi-separated over `S`.

The structure morphism of `𝒳` is `f` followed by the structure morphism of `𝒴`
(`AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.comp_structureMorphism`), so this is the quasi-separated case of
Stacks 050K.
declarations.statement:
theorem isQuasiSeparatedOver_of_isQuasiSeparated (f : 𝒳 ⟶ 𝒴)
    (hY : Stack.IsQuasiSeparatedOver B S hS 𝒴) (hf : IsQuasiSeparated B S hS f) :
    Stack.IsQuasiSeparatedOver B S hS 𝒳
declarations.comment: quasi_separated_over_s

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.AlgebraicStacks.isAbsolutelyDM_of_isDM
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 050L, part (5).** If `f : 𝒳 ⟶ 𝒴` is Deligne–Mumford and `𝒴` is Deligne–Mumford,
then `𝒳` is Deligne–Mumford.

Both absolute properties are the corresponding properties over the terminal scheme of the views
`AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.AlgebraicStacks.viewOverIntegers` of `𝒳` and `𝒴` there, and that view is
`AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.changeBaseAlgebraicStack` along `terminal.from S` on the nose. So this is
part (1) at the terminal scheme, applied to the 1-morphism of views that the hom-bijection of
Stacks 04X5 assigns to `f`, which is Deligne–Mumford by
`AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.isDM_changeBase_iff`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isAbsolutelyDM_of_isDM (f : 𝒳 ⟶ 𝒴) (hY : IsAbsolutelyDM B S hS hZ 𝒴)
    (hf : Stack.IsDM B S hS f) :
    IsAbsolutelyDM B S hS hZ 𝒳
declarations.comment: dm_absolute

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.AlgebraicStacks.isAbsolutelyQuasiDM_of_isQuasiDM
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 050L, part (6).** If `f : 𝒳 ⟶ 𝒴` is quasi-DM and `𝒴` is quasi-DM, then `𝒳` is
quasi-DM.

Part (2) at the terminal scheme, applied to the 1-morphism of views that the hom-bijection of
Stacks 04X5 assigns to `f`, which is quasi-DM by
`AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.AlgebraicStacks.isQuasiDM_changeBase_iff`. That comparison is stated at
`AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.AlgebraicStacks.IsQuasiDMWithRepresentableDiagonal`, the reading which
carries the representability witness of the relative diagonal, so the hypothesis and the
conclusion are passed across
`AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.AlgebraicStacks.isQuasiDMWithRepresentableDiagonal_iff_isQuasiDM`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isAbsolutelyQuasiDM_of_isQuasiDM (f : 𝒳 ⟶ 𝒴) (hY : IsAbsolutelyQuasiDM B S hS hZ 𝒴)
    (hf : IsQuasiDM B S hS f) :
    IsAbsolutelyQuasiDM B S hS hZ 𝒳
declarations.comment: quasi_dm_absolute

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.AlgebraicStacks.isAbsolutelySeparated_of_isSeparated
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 050L, part (7).** If `f : 𝒳 ⟶ 𝒴` is separated and `𝒴` is separated, then `𝒳` is
separated.

Both absolute properties are separatedness over the terminal scheme of the views
`AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.AlgebraicStacks.viewOverIntegers` of `𝒳` and `𝒴` there, and that view is
`AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.changeBaseAlgebraicStack` along `terminal.from S` on the nose. So this is
part (3) at the terminal scheme, applied to the 1-morphism of views that the hom-bijection of
Stacks 04X5 assigns to `f`, which is separated by
`AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.isProper_relativeDiagonal_changeBase`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isAbsolutelySeparated_of_isSeparated (f : 𝒳 ⟶ 𝒴)
    (hY : IsAbsolutelySeparated B S hS hZ 𝒴) (hf : IsSeparated B S hS f) :
