    IsAbsolutelySeparated B S hS hZ 𝒳
declarations.comment: separated_absolute

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.AlgebraicStacks.isQuasiSeparated_of_isQuasiSeparated_comp
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 050M, part (4).** If a composite `f ≫ g` of 1-morphisms of algebraic stacks over `S`
is quasi-separated and the relative diagonal of `g` is quasi-separated, then `f` is
quasi-separated.

The comparison 1-morphism `i : 𝒴 ×_𝒴 𝒳 ⟶ 𝒴 ×_𝒵 𝒳` of Stacks 050H, taken at the identity of `𝒴`,
composes with the second projection of `𝒴 ×_𝒵 𝒳` to give the second projection of `𝒴 ×_𝒴 𝒳` on
the nose. The projection out of `𝒴 ×_𝒵 𝒳` is the base change of `f ≫ g` along `𝟙 𝒴 ≫ g` and is
quasi-separated by Stacks 050F; `i` is quasi-separated by Stacks 050H part (2) from the
hypothesis on `Δ_g`, upgraded from the Section 04XB predicate to the Definition 04YW condition by
the two forms of Stacks 04YT condition (1); and Stacks 050K composes them. The projection out of
`𝒴 ×_𝒴 𝒳` is the base change of `f` along an identity, which is `f` itself by
`CategoryTheory.Bicategory.isTwoFibreProduct_trivialBaseChangeSquare`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isQuasiSeparated_of_isQuasiSeparated_comp
    {𝒳 𝒴 𝒵 : Stack.AlgebraicStacks.{u, w} B S hS} (f : 𝒳 ⟶ 𝒴) (g : 𝒴 ⟶ 𝒵)
    (hfg : IsQuasiSeparated B S hS (f ≫ g))
    (hΔg : Stack.IsQuasiSeparated B S hS
      (Stack.relativeDiagonalAlgebraicStacks B S hS g).hom) :
    IsQuasiSeparated B S hS f
declarations.comment: quasi_separated_first

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.AlgebraicStacks.isQuasiDM_of_comp
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 050M, part (2).** If a composite `f ≫ g` of 1-morphisms of algebraic stacks over `S`
is quasi-DM, then `f` is quasi-DM.

`f` is 2-isomorphic to the graph of `f` over `𝒵` followed by the second projection of the
canonical 2-fibre product of the cospan `(f ≫ g, g)`
(`AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.graph_snd_iso`). That projection is the base change of `f ≫ g` along
`g`, so it is quasi-DM by Stacks 050F; the graph is representable by algebraic spaces by
Stacks 050I part (1), and the relative diagonal of such a 1-morphism is locally quasi-finite by
Stacks 04YQ part (5), which is the quasi-DM condition on the nose. Stacks 050K composes them.
declarations.comment: quasi_dm_first

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.AlgebraicStacks.isDM_of_comp
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 050M, part (1).** If a composite `f ≫ g` of 1-morphisms of algebraic stacks over `S`
is Deligne–Mumford, then `f` is Deligne–Mumford.

`f` is 2-isomorphic to the graph of `f` over `𝒵` followed by the second projection of the
canonical 2-fibre product of the cospan `(f ≫ g, g)`
(`AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.graph_snd_iso`). That projection is the base change of `f ≫ g` along
`g`, so it is Deligne–Mumford by Stacks 050F; the graph is representable by algebraic spaces by
Stacks 050I part (1), and a 1-morphism representable by algebraic spaces is Deligne–Mumford
because its relative diagonal is a monomorphism which is locally of finite type, hence unramified
by Stacks 05W6. Stacks 050K composes them.
declarations.comment: dm_first

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.AlgebraicStacks.isSeparated_of_comp_of_isSeparated_diagonal
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 050M, part (3).** If a composite of 1-morphisms of algebraic stacks over `S` is
separated and the relative diagonal `Δ_g` of its second factor is separated in the sense of
Stacks 04XB, then its first factor is separated.

The relative diagonal `Δ_{f ≫ g}` is `Δ_f` followed by the comparison 1-morphism `i`, it is
proper in the sense of Stacks 04XB because `f ≫ g` is separated, `i` is separated because `Δ_g`
is (**Stacks 050H**, part (3)), and properness of morphisms of algebraic spaces over `S` is
inherited by the first factor of a composite that has it whose second factor is separated
(**Stacks 04NX**, part (2)).
declarations.statement:
theorem isSeparated_of_comp_of_isSeparated_diagonal (f : 𝒳 ⟶ 𝒴) (g : 𝒴 ⟶ 𝒵)
    (hfg : IsSeparated B S hS (f ≫ g))
    (hΔ : Stack.IsSeparated.{u, u, u + 1} B S hS
      (_root_.AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.relativeDiagonal.{u, u, u + 1} B S hS 𝒴.val 𝒵.val g.hom)) :
    IsSeparated B S hS f
declarations.comment: part (3): a separated composite whose second factor has separated relative diagonal has separated first factor

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.AlgebraicStacks.isQuasiSeparated_of_comp_of_isQuasiSeparated_diagonal
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 050M, part (4).** If a composite of 1-morphisms of algebraic stacks over `S` is
quasi-separated and the relative diagonal `Δ_g` of its second factor is quasi-separated in the
sense of Stacks 04XB, then its first factor is quasi-separated.

Quasi-separatedness of Stacks 04YW is the conjunction of two conditions of Stacks 04XB on the
relative diagonal — quasi-compactness and quasi-separatedness — and each half cancels the
comparison 1-morphism `i` at its own property. The hypothesis on `i` comes from the one on `Δ_g`
by **Stacks 050H**, part (2), and it is needed only by the quasi-compact half: quasi-compactness
of morphisms of algebraic spaces over `S` cancels against a quasi-separated second factor
(**Stacks 03KS**), while quasi-separatedness cancels outright (**Stacks 03KR**).
declarations.statement:
theorem isQuasiSeparated_of_comp_of_isQuasiSeparated_diagonal (f : 𝒳 ⟶ 𝒴) (g : 𝒴 ⟶ 𝒵)
    (hfg : IsQuasiSeparated B S hS (f ≫ g))
    (hΔ : Stack.IsQuasiSeparated.{u, u, u + 1} B S hS
      (_root_.AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.relativeDiagonal.{u, u, u + 1} B S hS 𝒴.val 𝒵.val g.hom)) :
    IsQuasiSeparated B S hS f
declarations.comment: part (4): a quasi-separated composite whose second factor has quasi-separated relative diagonal has quasi-separated first factor

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.AlgebraicStacks.isQuasiSeparated_of_isQuasiSeparatedOver
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 050N, part (8).** A 1-morphism `f : 𝒳 ⟶ 𝒴` of algebraic stacks over `S` whose source
is quasi-separated over `S` and whose target has quasi-separated relative diagonal over `S` is
quasi-separated.

The structure morphism of `𝒳` is `f` followed by the structure morphism of `𝒴`
(`AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.comp_structureMorphism`, an equality of 1-morphisms on the nose), so
the hypothesis on `𝒳` says that that composite is quasi-separated, and Stacks 050M part (4)
cancels the second factor. That is the source's own proof: *"Parts (5), (6), (7), and (8) follow
immediately from Lemma 050M"*.
declarations.statement:
theorem isQuasiSeparated_of_isQuasiSeparatedOver
    {𝒳 𝒴 : Stack.AlgebraicStacks.{u, w} B S hS} (f : 𝒳 ⟶ 𝒴)
    (h𝒳 : Stack.IsQuasiSeparatedOver B S hS 𝒳)
    (hΔ : Stack.IsQuasiSeparated B S hS
      (Stack.relativeDiagonalAlgebraicStacks B S hS
        (Stack.structureMorphism B S hS 𝒴)).hom) :
    IsQuasiSeparated B S hS f
declarations.comment: quasi_separated_source

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.AlgebraicStacks.isAbsolutelyDM_iff_isDMOver
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 050N, part (1).** An algebraic stack over `S` is Deligne–Mumford exactly when it is
Deligne–Mumford over `S`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isAbsolutelyDM_iff_isDMOver (𝒳 : Stack.AlgebraicStacks.{u, w} B S hS) :
    IsAbsolutelyDM.{u, w} B S hS hZ 𝒳 ↔ Stack.IsDMOver B S hS 𝒳
declarations.comment: dm_equiv

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.AlgebraicStacks.isAbsolutelyQuasiDM_iff_isQuasiDMOver
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 050N, part (2).** An algebraic stack over `S` is quasi-DM exactly when it is
quasi-DM over `S`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isAbsolutelyQuasiDM_iff_isQuasiDMOver (𝒳 : Stack.AlgebraicStacks.{u, w} B S hS) :
    IsAbsolutelyQuasiDM.{u, w} B S hS hZ 𝒳 ↔ Stack.IsQuasiDMOver B S hS 𝒳
declarations.comment: quasi_dm_equiv

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.AlgebraicStacks.isQuasiSeparatedOver_of_isAbsolutelyQuasiSeparated
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 050N, part (4): a quasi-separated algebraic stack is quasi-separated over its
base.** This is part (8) of Stacks 050D implying part (4): absolute quasi-separatedness is
quasi-separatedness over the terminal scheme `Spec ℤ` after `𝒳` has been viewed over it by
Construction A, so this is
`AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.AlgebraicStacks.isQuasiSeparatedOver_of_isQuasiSeparatedOver_changeBase`
at `S' = Spec ℤ`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isQuasiSeparatedOver_of_isAbsolutelyQuasiSeparated
    (hZ : B.Contains (⊤_ Scheme.{u})) (𝒳 : Stack.AlgebraicStacks.{u, w} B S hS)
    (h𝒳 : IsAbsolutelyQuasiSeparated B S hS hZ 𝒳) :
    Stack.IsQuasiSeparatedOver B S hS 𝒳
declarations.comment: quasi_separated_base

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.AlgebraicStacks.isSeparatedOver_of_isAbsolutelySeparated
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 050N, the separated assertion: a separated algebraic stack is separated over its
base.** This is part (7) of Stacks 050D implying part (3): absolute separatedness is
separatedness over the terminal scheme `Spec ℤ` after `𝒳` has been viewed over it by
Construction A, so this is
`AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.AlgebraicStacks.isSeparatedOver_of_isSeparatedOver_changeBase` at
`S' = Spec ℤ`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isSeparatedOver_of_isAbsolutelySeparated
    (hZ : B.Contains (⊤_ Scheme.{u})) (𝒳 : Stack.AlgebraicStacks.{u, w} B S hS)
    (h𝒳 : IsAbsolutelySeparated B S hS hZ 𝒳) :
    Stack.IsSeparatedOver B S hS 𝒳
declarations.comment: separated_base

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.isDMAbs_iff_isDMOver
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 050N, part (1).** An algebraic stack `𝒳` over `S` is DM **if and only if** it is DM
over `S`.

The implication from the absolute axiom is `AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.isDMOver_of_isDMAbs` above,
which cancels the second factor of the factorisation `𝒳 ⟶ S ⟶ Spec(ℤ)` by part (1) of
**Stacks 050M** and carries the resulting condition on the relative diagonal back from the base
`Spec(ℤ)` to the base `S`. The converse is
`AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.isDMAbs_of_isDMOver`, which composes along the same factorisation by
part (5) of **Stacks 050L**, using that the second factor is DM
(`AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.isDMOver_viewOverInt_schemeStack`, i.e. that `Δ_{S/ℤ}` is unramified).
Neither direction carries a hypothesis the source does not have.
declarations.statement:
theorem isDMAbs_iff_isDMOver (𝒵 : AlgebraicStacks.{u, w} B S hS) :
    IsDMAbs.{u, w, w'} B S hS 𝒵 ↔ IsDMOver B S hS 𝒵
declarations.comment: part (1)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.isQuasiDMAbs_iff_isQuasiDMOver
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 050N, part (2).** An algebraic stack `𝒳` over `S` is quasi-DM **if and only if** it
is quasi-DM over `S`.

The same two halves as part (1), with local quasi-finiteness in place of unramifiedness:
`AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.isQuasiDMOver_of_isQuasiDMAbs` above runs part (2) of **Stacks 050M**,
and `AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.isQuasiDMAbs_of_isQuasiDMOver` runs part (6) of **Stacks 050L**
against `AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.isQuasiDMOver_viewOverInt_schemeStack`. Neither direction
carries a hypothesis the source does not have.
declarations.statement:
theorem isQuasiDMAbs_iff_isQuasiDMOver (𝒵 : AlgebraicStacks.{u, w} B S hS) :
    IsQuasiDMAbs.{u, w, w'} B S hS 𝒵 ↔ IsQuasiDMOver B S hS 𝒵
declarations.comment: part (2)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.isDM_of_isDMOver
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 050N, part (5).** If `𝒳` is DM over `S`, then every 1-morphism `f : 𝒳 ⟶ 𝒴` of
algebraic stacks over `S` is DM.

Being DM over `S` is DM-ness of the structure morphism of `𝒳` (**Stacks 050D**, part (1)), and
that structure morphism is `f` followed by the structure morphism of `𝒴`
(`AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.comp_structureMorphism`), so part (1) of **Stacks 050M**
(`AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.AlgebraicStacks.isDM_of_comp`), which cancels the second factor of a
DM composite with no hypothesis on it, gives the conclusion.
declarations.statement: theorem isDM_of_isDMOver (f : 𝒳 ⟶ 𝒴) (h𝒳 : IsDMOver B S hS 𝒳) : IsDM B S hS f
declarations.comment: part (5)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.isQuasiDM_of_isQuasiDMOver
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 050N, part (6).** If `𝒳` is quasi-DM over `S`, then every 1-morphism `f : 𝒳 ⟶ 𝒴`
of algebraic stacks over `S` is quasi-DM.

The same argument as part (5), with part (2) of **Stacks 050M**
(`AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.AlgebraicStacks.isQuasiDM_of_comp`) in place of part (1); it too needs
no hypothesis on the second factor.
declarations.statement:
theorem isQuasiDM_of_isQuasiDMOver (f : 𝒳 ⟶ 𝒴) (h𝒳 : IsQuasiDMOver B S hS 𝒳) :
    AlgebraicStacks.IsQuasiDM B S hS f
declarations.comment: part (6)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.isSeparated_of_isSeparatedOver_of_isSeparated_diagonal
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 050N, part (7).** If `𝒳` is separated over `S` and the relative diagonal `Δ_{𝒴/S}`
is separated in the sense of Stacks 04XB, then every 1-morphism `f : 𝒳 ⟶ 𝒴` of algebraic stacks
over `S` is separated.

The same argument as part (5), with part (3) of **Stacks 050M**
(`AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.AlgebraicStacks.isSeparated_of_comp_of_isSeparated_diagonal`) in place
of part (1). That part cancels the second factor of a separated composite provided the second
factor has separated relative diagonal, and here the second factor is the structure morphism of
`𝒴`, so the proviso is exactly the hypothesis `hΔ` that the source's part (7) carries too.
declarations.statement:
theorem isSeparated_of_isSeparatedOver_of_isSeparated_diagonal (f : 𝒳 ⟶ 𝒴)
    (h𝒳 : IsSeparatedOver B S hS 𝒳)
    (hΔ : IsSeparated.{u, u, u + 1} B S hS
      (relativeDiagonal.{u, u, u + 1} B S hS 𝒴.val
        (schemeStack.{u, w} B S hS (Over.mk (𝟙 (B.obj hS)))).val
        (structureMorphism B S hS 𝒴).hom)) :
    AlgebraicStacks.IsSeparated B S hS f
declarations.comment: part (7)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.isQuasiSeparated_of_isQuasiSeparatedOver_of_isQuasiSeparated_diagonal
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 050N, part (8).** If `𝒳` is quasi-separated over `S` and the relative diagonal
`Δ_{𝒴/S}` is quasi-separated in the sense of Stacks 04XB, then every 1-morphism `f : 𝒳 ⟶ 𝒴` of
algebraic stacks over `S` is quasi-separated.

The same argument as part (7), with part (4) of **Stacks 050M**
(`AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.AlgebraicStacks.isQuasiSeparated_of_comp_of_isQuasiSeparated_diagonal`)
in place of part (3); the hypothesis `hΔ` is again what that part needs of the second factor,
which here is the structure morphism of `𝒴`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isQuasiSeparated_of_isQuasiSeparatedOver_of_isQuasiSeparated_diagonal (f : 𝒳 ⟶ 𝒴)
    (h𝒳 : IsQuasiSeparatedOver B S hS 𝒳)
    (hΔ : IsQuasiSeparated.{u, u, u + 1} B S hS
      (relativeDiagonal.{u, u, u + 1} B S hS 𝒴.val
        (schemeStack.{u, w} B S hS (Over.mk (𝟙 (B.obj hS)))).val
        (structureMorphism B S hS 𝒴).hom)) :
    AlgebraicStacks.IsQuasiSeparated B S hS f
declarations.comment: part (8)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.isAlgebraicStack_inertia
declarations.doc: The inertia `I_𝒳` of an algebraic stack `𝒳` over `S` is an algebraic stack over `S`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isAlgebraicStack_inertia
    (𝒳 : CatFiberedInGroupoids.{u, u, u + 1, u + 1} (BigFppfOver B S hS))
    (h𝒳 : IsAlgebraicStack.{u, w} B S hS 𝒳.val) :
    IsAlgebraicStack.{u, w} B S hS (inertia B S hS 𝒳).val
declarations.comment: absolute inertia is algebraic

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.isAlgebraicStack_relativeInertia
declarations.doc:
The relative inertia `I_{𝒳/𝒴}` of a 1-morphism `f : 𝒳 ⟶ 𝒴` of algebraic stacks over `S` is
an algebraic stack over `S`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isAlgebraicStack_relativeInertia
    (𝒳 𝒴 : CatFiberedInGroupoids.{u, u, u + 1, u + 1} (BigFppfOver B S hS))
    (f : 𝒳 ⟶ 𝒴)
    (h𝒳 : IsAlgebraicStack.{u, w} B S hS 𝒳.val)
    (h𝒴 : IsAlgebraicStack.{u, w} B S hS 𝒴.val) :
    IsAlgebraicStack.{u, w} B S hS (RelativeInertia.basedCategory f.hom)
declarations.comment: relative inertia is algebraic

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.AlgebraicStacks.isLocallyOfFiniteType_inertiaProjection
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 050Q, local finite type of the inertia projection, in the sense of Stacks 06FS
part (1).** The forgetful 1-morphism `I_𝒳 ⟶ 𝒳` of the inertia of an algebraic stack `𝒳` over `S`
is locally of finite type as a 1-morphism of algebraic stacks.

`AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.isLocallyOfFiniteType_inertiaProjection` is the same statement in the
relative sense of Properties of Stacks, Section 04XB; the inertia projection is representable by
algebraic spaces by Stacks 050Q, so **Stacks 06FM** for a representable 1-morphism converts the
relative property into the existential smooth-diagram test, and the universal one follows because
local finite type is smooth local on the source-and-target.
declarations.statement:
theorem isLocallyOfFiniteType_inertiaProjection (𝒳 : Stack.AlgebraicStacks.{u, w} B S hS) :
    IsLocallyOfFiniteType B S hS (Stack.inertiaProjectionAlgebraicStacks B S hS 𝒳)
declarations.comment: local finite type of the inertia projection in the sense of Stacks 06FS part (1)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.isLocallyOfFiniteType_inertiaProjection
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 050Q, local finite type of the inertia projection.** The forgetful 1-morphism
`π : I_𝒳 ⟶ 𝒳` of the inertia of an algebraic stack `𝒳` over `S` is locally of finite type, in
the sense of Properties of Stacks, Section 04XB.

By Stacks 034H (1) the inertia is the 2-fibre product `𝒳 ×_{Δ, 𝒳 × 𝒳, Δ} 𝒳`, and under that
identification `π` is the first projection of the canonical 2-fibre product square over the
cospan `(Δ, Δ)`, hence a base change of `Δ`. So this is Stacks 045C applied to
`AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.isLocallyOfFiniteType_diagonal_of_isAlgebraicStack` and transported
along that equivalence of sources by Stacks 0457.
declarations.statement:
theorem isLocallyOfFiniteType_inertiaProjection (𝒳 : AlgebraicStacks.{u, w} B S hS) :
    IsLocallyOfFiniteType B S hS (inertiaProjectionAlgebraicStacks.{u, w} B S hS 𝒳).hom
declarations.comment: local finite type of the absolute inertia projection

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.isLocallyOfFiniteType_relativeInertiaProjection
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 050Q, local finite type of the relative inertia projection.** The forgetful
1-morphism `π : I_{𝒳/𝒴} ⟶ 𝒳` of the relative inertia of a 1-morphism `f : 𝒳 ⟶ 𝒴` of algebraic
stacks over `S` is locally of finite type, in the sense of Properties of Stacks, Section 04XB.

By Stacks 034H (1) the relative inertia is the 2-fibre product `𝒳 ×_{Δ_f, 𝒳 ×_𝒴 𝒳, Δ_f} 𝒳`, and
under that identification `π` is the first projection of the canonical 2-fibre product square
over the cospan `(Δ_f, Δ_f)`, hence a base change of the relative diagonal. So this is Stacks
045C applied to part (2) of Stacks 04XS, transported along that equivalence of sources by
Stacks 0457.
declarations.statement:
theorem isLocallyOfFiniteType_relativeInertiaProjection
    {𝒳 𝒴 : AlgebraicStacks.{u, w} B S hS} (f : 𝒳 ⟶ 𝒴) :
    IsLocallyOfFiniteType B S hS (relativeInertiaProjection B S hS f).hom
declarations.comment: local finite type of the relative inertia projection

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.isRepresentableByAlgebraicSpaces_inertiaProjection
declarations.doc:
If the diagonal of a category fibred in groupoids `𝒳` over the big fppf site of `S` is
representable by algebraic spaces, then so is the forgetful 1-morphism `π : I_𝒳 ⟶ 𝒳` of its
inertia.
declarations.statement:
theorem isRepresentableByAlgebraicSpaces_inertiaProjection
    (B : BigFppfSite.{u}) (S : Scheme.{u}) (hS : B.Contains S)
    (𝒳 : CatFiberedInGroupoids.{u, max u v, u + 1, max (u + 1) v w} (BigFppfOver B S hS))
    (hΔ : IsRepresentableByAlgebraicSpaces B S hS (diagonalBasedFunctor B S hS 𝒳)) :
    IsRepresentableByAlgebraicSpaces B S hS
      (RelativeInertia.basedProjection
        (𝒴 := BasedCategory.ofFunctor (𝟭 (BigFppfOver B S hS)))
        ⟨𝒳.val.p, rfl⟩)
declarations.comment: representability by algebraic spaces of the absolute inertia projection

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.isRepresentableByAlgebraicSpaces_inertiaProjection_of_isAlgebraicStack
declarations.doc:
The forgetful 1-morphism `π : I_𝒳 ⟶ 𝒳` of the inertia of an algebraic stack `𝒳` is
representable by algebraic spaces.
declarations.statement:
theorem isRepresentableByAlgebraicSpaces_inertiaProjection_of_isAlgebraicStack
    (B : BigFppfSite.{u}) (S : Scheme.{u}) (hS : B.Contains S)
    (𝒳 : CatFiberedInGroupoids.{u, max u v, u + 1, max (u + 1) v w} (BigFppfOver B S hS))
    (h𝒳 : IsAlgebraicStack.{u, t} B S hS 𝒳.val) :
    IsRepresentableByAlgebraicSpaces B S hS
      (RelativeInertia.basedProjection
        (𝒴 := BasedCategory.ofFunctor (𝟭 (BigFppfOver B S hS)))
        ⟨𝒳.val.p, rfl⟩)
declarations.comment: the inertia projection of an algebraic stack is representable by spaces

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.isRepresentableByAlgebraicSpaces_relativeInertiaProjection_of_isAlgebraicStack
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 050Q for the relative inertia of a morphism of algebraic stacks.** The forgetful
1-morphism `π : I_{𝒳/𝒴} ⟶ 𝒳` of the relative inertia of a 1-morphism of algebraic stacks is
representable by algebraic spaces. Only the representability of the two diagonals — the second
clause of `AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.IsAlgebraicStack` — is used.

The source's statement also asserts that `I_{𝒳/𝒴}` is an algebraic stack and that `π` is
locally of finite type; neither is proved here.
declarations.statement:
theorem isRepresentableByAlgebraicSpaces_relativeInertiaProjection_of_isAlgebraicStack
    (𝒳 𝒴 : CatFiberedInGroupoids.{u, max u v, u + 1, max (max (u + 1) w) v}
      (BigFppfOver B S hS))
    (f : 𝒳 ⟶ 𝒴)
    (h𝒳 : IsAlgebraicStack.{u, t} B S hS 𝒳.val)
    (h𝒴 : IsAlgebraicStack.{u, t} B S hS 𝒴.val) :
    IsRepresentableByAlgebraicSpaces B S hS (RelativeInertia.basedProjection f.hom)
declarations.comment: representability by algebraic spaces of the relative inertia projection

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.RelativeInertia.inverse
declarations.doc:
The inverse of the group law: the 1-morphism `i : I_{S/S'} ⟶ I_{S/S'}`,
`(x, α) ↦ (x, α⁻¹)`, acting on morphisms by the identity.
declarations.statement: def inverse (F : S ⥤ S') : RelativeInertia F ⥤ RelativeInertia F
declarations.comment: the inverse

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.RelativeInertia.inverse_comp_π
declarations.doc:
**The inverse is a morphism over the source**: followed by the projection to `S` it is that
projection again.
declarations.statement:
theorem inverse_comp_π (F : S ⥤ S') :
    inverse F ⋙ RelativeInertia.π F = RelativeInertia.π F
declarations.comment: the inverse is a morphism over the source

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.RelativeInertia.composition_pairIdNeutral
declarations.doc: The right unit axiom: `c ∘ ⟨id, e ∘ π⟩ = id`.
declarations.statement:
theorem composition_pairIdNeutral :
    pairIdNeutral F p ⋙ composition F p = 𝟭 (RelativeInertia F)
declarations.comment: the right unit axiom

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.RelativeInertia.composition_pairNeutralId
declarations.doc: The left unit axiom: `c ∘ ⟨e ∘ π, id⟩ = id`.
declarations.statement:
theorem composition_pairNeutralId :
    pairNeutralId F p ⋙ composition F p = 𝟭 (RelativeInertia F)
declarations.comment: the left unit axiom

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.RelativeInertia.composition_pairIdInverse
declarations.doc: The right inverse axiom: `c ∘ ⟨id, i⟩ = e ∘ π`.
declarations.statement:
theorem composition_pairIdInverse :
    pairIdInverse F p ⋙ composition F p =
      RelativeInertia.π F ⋙ RelativeInertia.neutralSection F
declarations.comment: the right inverse axiom

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.RelativeInertia.composition_pairInverseId
declarations.doc: The left inverse axiom: `c ∘ ⟨i, id⟩ = e ∘ π`.
declarations.statement:
theorem composition_pairInverseId :
    pairInverseId F p ⋙ composition F p =
      RelativeInertia.π F ⋙ RelativeInertia.neutralSection F
declarations.comment: the left inverse axiom

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.RelativeInertia.composition_assoc
declarations.doc:
The associativity axiom: `c ∘ (c × id) = c ∘ (id × c) ∘ assoc` as
1-morphisms `(I_{S/S'} ×_S I_{S/S'}) ×_S I_{S/S'} ⟶ I_{S/S'}` over `S`: both send
`(((x, α), (x', α'), β), (x'', α''), δ)` to `(x, α ∘ β⁻¹ ∘ α' ∘ β ∘ δ⁻¹ ∘ α'' ∘ δ)`.
declarations.statement:
theorem composition_assoc :
    compFstPair F p ⋙ composition F p = idCompPair F p ⋙ composition F p
declarations.comment: the associativity axiom

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.relativeInertiaPairOverStack
declarations.doc:
`I_{𝒳/𝒴} ×_𝒳 I_{𝒳/𝒴}` as an object of `Spaces/𝒳`: the 2-fibre product of the projection
with itself, with structure 1-morphism to `𝒳` the first projection followed by `π`.
declarations.statement: noncomputable def relativeInertiaPairOverStack (f : 𝒳 ⟶ 𝒴) : SpacesOverStack B S hS 𝒳
declarations.comment:
the twofold product of the relative inertia in the 2-category of morphisms to the
  source representable by algebraic spaces

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.relativeInertiaCompositionHom
declarations.doc:
The composition law as a 1-morphism of `Spaces/𝒳`: the functor
`c : I_{𝒳/𝒴} ×_𝒳 I_{𝒳/𝒴} ⟶ I_{𝒳/𝒴}`, `((x, α), (x', α'), β) ↦ (x, α ∘ β⁻¹ ∘ α' ∘ β)`, with
the identity as comparison 2-morphism.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def relativeInertiaCompositionHom (f : 𝒳 ⟶ 𝒴) :
    relativeInertiaPairOverStack B S hS f ⟶ relativeInertiaOverStack B S hS f
declarations.comment:
the composition law as a 1-morphism of the 2-category of morphisms to the source
  representable by algebraic spaces

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.relativeInertiaInverseHom
declarations.doc:
The inverse as a 1-morphism of `Spaces/𝒳`: the functor `i : I_{𝒳/𝒴} ⟶ I_{𝒳/𝒴}`,
`(x, α) ↦ (x, α⁻¹)`, with the identity as comparison 2-morphism.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def relativeInertiaInverseHom (f : 𝒳 ⟶ 𝒴) :
    relativeInertiaOverStack B S hS f ⟶ relativeInertiaOverStack B S hS f
declarations.comment:
the inverse as a 1-morphism of the 2-category of morphisms to the source
  representable by algebraic spaces

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.relativeInertiaNeutralHom
declarations.doc:
The neutral element as a 1-morphism of algebraic stacks: `e : 𝒳 ⟶ I_{𝒳/𝒴}`,
`x ↦ (x, id_x)`.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def relativeInertiaNeutralHom (f : 𝒳 ⟶ 𝒴) :
    𝒳 ⟶ (relativeInertiaOverStack B S hS f).source
declarations.comment: the neutral element as a 1-morphism of algebraic stacks

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.relativeInertiaNeutralHom_comp_map
declarations.doc:
The neutral element is a section of the projection: `e ≫ π = 𝟙 𝒳`, an equality of
1-morphisms of algebraic stacks.
declarations.statement:
theorem relativeInertiaNeutralHom_comp_map (f : 𝒳 ⟶ 𝒴) :
    relativeInertiaNeutralHom B S hS f ≫ (relativeInertiaOverStack B S hS f).map = 𝟙 𝒳
declarations.comment: the neutral element is a section of the projection

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.RelativeInertia.composition
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 050R, the composition law of the relative inertia.** On the 2-fibre product
`I_{S/S'} ×_S I_{S/S'}`, whose objects are the triples `((x, α), (x', α'), β)` with
`β : x ≅ x'` a vertical isomorphism, it is the functor
`((x, α), (x', α'), β) ↦ (x, α ∘ β⁻¹ ∘ α' ∘ β)`, acting on morphisms by their first component.
declarations.comment: the composition law

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.RelativeInertia.composition_comp_π
declarations.doc:
**The composition law is a morphism over the source**: followed by the projection to `S` it
is the first projection of the 2-fibre product followed by that projection.
declarations.statement:
theorem composition_comp_π (F : S ⥤ S') (p : S ⥤ C) :
    composition F p ⋙ RelativeInertia.π F =
      TwoFibreProductOver.fst (RelativeInertia.π F ⋙ p) (RelativeInertia.π F ⋙ p) p
        (RelativeInertia.π F) (RelativeInertia.π F) ⋙ RelativeInertia.π F
declarations.comment: the composition law is a morphism over the source

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.relativeInertiaOverStack
declarations.doc:
**The relative inertia as an object of `Spaces/𝒳`.** For a 1-morphism `f : 𝒳 ⟶ 𝒴` of
algebraic stacks, the relative inertia `I_{𝒳/𝒴}` is an algebraic stack and its projection to
`𝒳` is representable by algebraic spaces, so the pair is an object of the 2-category of
Stacks 04ZQ. This is the ambient object of which Stacks 050R asserts that it is a group
object.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def relativeInertiaOverStack
    {𝒳 𝒴 : AlgebraicStacks.{u, w} B S hS} (f : 𝒳 ⟶ 𝒴) : SpacesOverStack B S hS 𝒳
declarations.comment:
the relative inertia as an object of the 2-category of morphisms to the source
  representable by algebraic spaces

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.relativeInertiaGrpObj
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 050R.** For a 1-morphism `f : 𝒳 ⟶ 𝒴` of algebraic stacks, the relative inertia
`I_{𝒳/𝒴}` is a *group object* of the category of 1-morphisms to `𝒳` representable by algebraic
spaces (Stacks 04ZQ): its multiplication is the composition law
`c : I_{𝒳/𝒴} ×_𝒳 I_{𝒳/𝒴} ⟶ I_{𝒳/𝒴}`, `((x, α), (x', α'), β) ↦ (x, α ∘ β⁻¹ ∘ α' ∘ β)`, its unit
is the neutral element `e : 𝒳 ⟶ I_{𝒳/𝒴}`, `x ↦ (x, id_x)`, and its inverse is
`i : (x, α) ↦ (x, α⁻¹)`.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def relativeInertiaGrpObj (f : 𝒳 ⟶ 𝒴) : GrpObj (IsoClassCategory.mk
  (relativeInertiaOverStack B S hS f))

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.relativeInertiaGrpObj_mul
declarations.doc: **Stacks 050R.** The multiplication of the group object is the composition law `c`.
declarations.statement:
theorem relativeInertiaGrpObj_mul (f : 𝒳 ⟶ 𝒴) :
    letI := relativeInertiaGrpObj B S hS f
    MonObj.mul (X := IsoClassCategory.mk (relativeInertiaOverStack B S hS f)) =
      IsoClassCategory.homMk (C := SpacesOverStack B S hS 𝒳) (relativeInertiaMulHom B S hS f)
declarations.comment: the multiplication of the group object is the composition law

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.relativeInertiaGrpObj_one
declarations.doc: **Stacks 050R.** The unit of the group object is the neutral element `e`.
declarations.statement:
theorem relativeInertiaGrpObj_one (f : 𝒳 ⟶ 𝒴) :
    letI := relativeInertiaGrpObj B S hS f
    MonObj.one (X := IsoClassCategory.mk (relativeInertiaOverStack B S hS f)) =
      IsoClassCategory.homMk (C := SpacesOverStack B S hS 𝒳) (relativeInertiaOneHom B S hS f)
declarations.comment: the unit of the group object is the neutral element

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.relativeInertiaGrpObj_inv
declarations.doc: **Stacks 050R.** The inverse of the group object is `i`.
declarations.statement:
theorem relativeInertiaGrpObj_inv (f : 𝒳 ⟶ 𝒴) :
    GrpObj.inv (X := IsoClassCategory.mk (relativeInertiaOverStack B S hS f)) (self :=
      relativeInertiaGrpObj B S hS f) =
      IsoClassCategory.homMk (C := SpacesOverStack B S hS 𝒳) (relativeInertiaInvHom B S hS f)
declarations.comment: the inverse of the group object

registrations.name: CategoryTheory.RelativeInertia.neutralSection
registrations.comment: the neutral element

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.isQuasiCompact_iff_baseChange_quasiCompact
declarations.doc:
For a 1-morphism of algebraic stacks over `S` representable by algebraic
spaces, quasi-compactness in the sense of Properties of Stacks, Section 04XB — every algebraic
space representing a base change along a scheme-valued point of the target is quasi-compact over
its base — is equivalent to quasi-compactness in the sense of Stacks 050U: every base change by a
quasi-compact algebraic stack is a quasi-compact algebraic stack.
declarations.statement:
public theorem isQuasiCompact_iff_baseChange_quasiCompact
    (B : BigFppfSite.{u}) (S : Scheme.{u}) (hS : B.Contains S)
    {𝒳 𝒴 : AlgebraicStacks.{u, w} B S hS}
    (f : 𝒳 ⟶ 𝒴)
    (hf : IsRepresentableByAlgebraicSpaces B S hS f.hom.hom) :
    IsQuasiCompact B S hS f.hom ↔ IsQuasiCompactMorphism.{u, w} B S hS f

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.IsQuasiCompactMorphism
declarations.doc:
A 1-morphism of algebraic stacks over `S` is *quasi-compact* when every base change of it by
a quasi-compact algebraic stack is again a quasi-compact algebraic stack, the fibre product being
the canonical 2-fibre product of algebraic stacks and quasi-compactness being
`AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.IsQuasiCompactStack`.
declarations.statement: abbrev IsQuasiCompactMorphism {𝒳 𝒴 : AlgebraicStacks.{u, w} B S hS} (f : 𝒳 ⟶ 𝒴) : Prop

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.isQuasiCompactMorphism_baseChange
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 050V.** A base change of a quasi-compact 1-morphism of algebraic stacks over `S` is
quasi-compact: if `P` is a 2-fibre product of the cospan `(g, f)` and `f` is quasi-compact, then
the projection `P.fst` is quasi-compact.

The base change of `P.fst` by a test 1-morphism `k` is `𝒵 ×_{𝒴'} P.pt`, and Stacks 02XD at the
recognised 2-fibre product `P` identifies it with a 2-fibre product of the cospan `(f, k ≫ g)`;
the base change of `f` along `k ≫ g` is another, and it is quasi-compact by hypothesis.
declarations.statement:
theorem isQuasiCompactMorphism_baseChange {𝒳 𝒴 𝒴' : AlgebraicStacks.{u, w} B S hS}
    (f : 𝒳 ⟶ 𝒴) (g : 𝒴' ⟶ 𝒴) (P : Bicategory.TwoCommSq g f)
    (hP : Bicategory.IsTwoFibreProduct P) (hf : IsQuasiCompactMorphism B S hS f) :
    IsQuasiCompactMorphism B S hS P.fst

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.isQuasiCompactMorphism_comp
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 050W.** The composite of two quasi-compact 1-morphisms of algebraic stacks over `S`
is quasi-compact.

A base change of `f ≫ g` by a quasi-compact algebraic stack is the iterated 2-fibre product
`(𝒲 ×_𝒵 𝒴) ×_𝒴 𝒳`; the inner apex is quasi-compact because `g` is, the outer one because `f` is,
and Stacks 02XD identifies the outer apex with a 2-fibre product of the cospan of `f ≫ g`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isQuasiCompactMorphism_comp {𝒳 𝒴 𝒵 : AlgebraicStacks.{u, w} B S hS}
    (f : 𝒳 ⟶ 𝒴) (g : 𝒴 ⟶ 𝒵)
    (hf : IsQuasiCompactMorphism B S hS f) (hg : IsQuasiCompactMorphism B S hS g) :
    IsQuasiCompactMorphism B S hS (f ≫ g)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.isQuasiCompactMorphism_of_comp_of_isSurjective
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 050X.** Let `f : 𝒳 ⟶ 𝒴`, `p : 𝒳 ⟶ 𝒵` and `q : 𝒴 ⟶ 𝒵` be a 2-commutative triangle
of 1-morphisms of algebraic stacks over `S`. If `f` is surjective and `p` is quasi-compact, then
`q` is quasi-compact.

A base change `𝒯 ×_𝒵 𝒴` of `q` by a quasi-compact algebraic stack receives the iterated product
`(𝒯 ×_𝒵 𝒴) ×_𝒴 𝒳`, which is a base change of the surjective `f` and hence surjects onto it
(Stacks 04ZU); Stacks 02XD identifies that iterated apex with a 2-fibre product of the cospan
`(k, p)`, quasi-compact by the hypothesis on `p`, and quasi-compactness of an algebraic stack
passes along a surjection.
declarations.statement:
theorem isQuasiCompactMorphism_of_comp_of_isSurjective
    {𝒳 𝒴 𝒵 : AlgebraicStacks.{u, w} B S hS}
    (f : 𝒳 ⟶ 𝒴) (p : 𝒳 ⟶ 𝒵) (q : 𝒴 ⟶ 𝒵) (e : f ≫ q ≅ p)
    (hf : IsSurjective B S hS f) (hp : IsQuasiCompactMorphism B S hS p) :
    IsQuasiCompactMorphism B S hS q

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.isQuasiCompactMorphism_of_comp_of_isQuasiSeparated
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 050Y.** If a composite of 1-morphisms of algebraic stacks over `S` is quasi-compact
and its second factor is quasi-separated, then its first factor is quasi-compact.

`f` is the composite of its graph section with the projection of `𝒴 ×_𝒵 𝒳` to `𝒴`. The projection
to `𝒳` is a base change of `g`, hence quasi-separated (Stacks 050F), so the graph section is
quasi-compact by Stacks 050J part (5); the projection to `𝒴` is a base change of `f ≫ g`, hence
quasi-compact by Stacks 050V; and Stacks 050W composes the two.
declarations.statement:
theorem isQuasiCompactMorphism_of_comp_of_isQuasiSeparated (f : 𝒳 ⟶ 𝒴) (g : 𝒴 ⟶ 𝒵)
    (hgf : IsQuasiCompactMorphism B S hS (f ≫ g))
    (hg : AlgebraicStacks.IsQuasiSeparated B S hS g) :
    IsQuasiCompactMorphism B S hS f

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.IsNoetherianStack
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0510**, verbatim: *"Let `𝒳` be an algebraic stack. We say `𝒳` is Noetherian if `𝒳`
is quasi-compact, quasi-separated and locally Noetherian."*

Quasi-compactness is `AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.IsQuasiCompactStack` (**Stacks 04YB**),
quasi-separatedness is the absolute axiom `AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.IsQuasiSeparatedAbs`
(**Stacks 050D**, part (8)) and local Noetherianity is the smooth-scheme-atlas criterion
`AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.HasPropertyOnSomeSchemeAtlas` of **Stacks 04YG** at
`AlgebraicGeometry.IsLocallyNoetherian`.
declarations.statement: noncomputable abbrev IsNoetherianStack (𝒳 : AlgebraicStacks.{u, w} B S hS) : Prop

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.representable_universallyClosed_iff_closedMap_baseChange
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0512.** A 1-morphism of algebraic stacks over `S` which is representable by
algebraic spaces is universally closed — the relative property of Tag 04XB at universal
closedness of morphisms of algebraic spaces — exactly when, for every algebraic stack `𝒵` over
`𝒴`, the first projection of the canonical 2-fibre product of Tag 04T2 is a closed map on the
points of Tag 04XL.
declarations.statement:
theorem representable_universallyClosed_iff_closedMap_baseChange
    {𝒳 𝒴 : AlgebraicStacks.{u, w} B S hS} (f : 𝒳 ⟶ 𝒴)
    (hf : IsRepresentableByAlgebraicSpaces B S hS f.hom.hom) :
    UniversallyClosed B S hS f.hom ↔
      ∀ (𝒵 : AlgebraicStacks.{u, w} B S hS) (g : 𝒵 ⟶ 𝒴),
        let P := twoFibreProductSquareAlgebraicStacks B S hS g f
        @IsClosedMap
          (points B S hS P.pt.val.val (Classical.choose P.pt.property))
          (points B S hS 𝒵.val.val (Classical.choose 𝒵.property))
          (pointTopology B S hS P.pt.val)
          (pointTopology B S hS 𝒵.val)
          (pointsMap B S hS P.pt.val.val
            (Classical.choose P.pt.property) (Classical.choose 𝒵.property)
            P.fst.hom.hom)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.AlgebraicStacks.IsClosed
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0513, part (1).** A 1-morphism of algebraic stacks over `S` *is closed* when the
map `|𝒳| → |𝒴|` it induces on the topological spaces of points of Stacks 04XG and 04XL is a
closed map.
declarations.statement: abbrev IsClosed {𝒳 𝒴 : Stack.AlgebraicStacks.{u, w} B S hS} (f : 𝒳 ⟶ 𝒴) : Prop
declarations.comment: closed

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.AlgebraicStacks.UniversallyClosed
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0513, part (2).** A 1-morphism `f : 𝒳 ⟶ 𝒴` of algebraic stacks over `S` *is
universally closed* when, for every 1-morphism `g : 𝒵 ⟶ 𝒴` of algebraic stacks over `S`, the
base change `𝒵 ×_{g, 𝒴, f} 𝒳 ⟶ 𝒵` of `f` by `g` is closed in the sense of
`AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.AlgebraicStacks.IsClosed`.
declarations.statement: abbrev UniversallyClosed {𝒳 𝒴 : Stack.AlgebraicStacks.{u, w} B S hS} (f : 𝒳 ⟶ 𝒴) : Prop
declarations.comment: universally closed

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.AlgebraicStacks.universallyClosed_baseChange_of_isTwoFibreProduct
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0514.** Universal closedness is stable under base change: let `f : 𝒳 ⟶ 𝒴` be a
universally closed 1-morphism of algebraic stacks over `S` and let `R` be a 2-fibre product
square of the cospan `(g, f)` for some `g : 𝒴' ⟶ 𝒴`. Then the base change `R.fst : R.pt ⟶ 𝒴'`
of `f` along `g` is universally closed.

The square is arbitrary, so this applies to any square a consumer has already exhibited as a
2-fibre product rather than only to the canonical one of Stacks 04T2.
declarations.statement:
theorem universallyClosed_baseChange_of_isTwoFibreProduct
    {𝒳 𝒴 𝒴' : AlgebraicStacks.{u, w} B S hS} {f : 𝒳 ⟶ 𝒴} {g : 𝒴' ⟶ 𝒴}
    (R : Bicategory.TwoCommSq g f) (hR : Bicategory.IsTwoFibreProduct R)
    (hf : UniversallyClosed B S hS f) :
    UniversallyClosed B S hS R.fst

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.AlgebraicStacks.isClosed_comp
declarations.doc: The composite of two closed 1-morphisms of algebraic stacks over `S` is closed.
declarations.comment: closed

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.AlgebraicStacks.universallyClosed_comp
declarations.doc:
The composite of two universally closed 1-morphisms of algebraic stacks over `S` is
universally closed.
declarations.statement:
theorem universallyClosed_comp {𝒳 𝒴 𝒵 : Stack.AlgebraicStacks.{u, w} B S hS}
    (f : 𝒳 ⟶ 𝒴) (g : 𝒴 ⟶ 𝒵)
    (hf : UniversallyClosed B S hS f) (hg : UniversallyClosed B S hS g) :
    UniversallyClosed B S hS (f ≫ g)
declarations.comment: universally closed
