declarations.name: isClosed_support_and_isCompact_compl_support
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 051B.** The support of a finitely presented module is a closed subset of `Spec R`
whose complement is quasi-compact. The support is the zero locus of the zeroth Fitting ideal,
the ideal of maximal minors of a presentation matrix, and that ideal is finitely generated for
a finitely presented module.
declarations.statement:
theorem isClosed_support_and_isCompact_compl_support {R : Type*} [CommRing R]
    (M : Type*) [AddCommGroup M] [Module R M] [Module.FinitePresentation R M] :
    IsClosed (Module.support R M) ∧ IsCompact (Module.support R M)ᶜ
declarations.comment: Supp(M) = V(Fit_0(M)) with Fit_0(M) finitely generated, as in the source proof

declarations.name: tor1_vanishes_of_annihilated
declarations.doc:
If `M/IM` is flat over `R/I` and `Tor₁^R(R/I, M) = 0`, then `Tor₁^R(N, M) = 0` for every
`R`-module `N` annihilated by `Iᵐ` for some `m`.
declarations.statement:
theorem tor1_vanishes_of_annihilated
    (H1 : Module.Flat (R ⧸ I) (M ⧸ (I • (⊤ : Submodule R M))))
    (H2 : Tor1Vanishes R (R ⧸ I) M)
    (N : Type u) [AddCommGroup N] [Module R N]
    (m : ℕ) (hN : (I ^ m) • (⊤ : Submodule R N) = ⊥) :
    Tor1Vanishes R N M

declarations.name: flat_quotient_pow
declarations.doc:
If `M/IM` is flat over `R/I` and `Tor₁^R(R/I, M) = 0`, then for every `n ≥ 1` the
`R/Iⁿ`-module `M/IⁿM` is flat over `R/Iⁿ`.
declarations.statement:
theorem flat_quotient_pow
    (H1 : Module.Flat (R ⧸ I) (M ⧸ (I • (⊤ : Submodule R M))))
    (H2 : Tor1Vanishes R (R ⧸ I) M) :
    ∀ n : ℕ, 1 ≤ n →
      Module.Flat (R ⧸ I ^ n) (M ⧸ ((I ^ n) • (⊤ : Submodule R M)))

declarations.name: flat_of_nilpotent
declarations.doc:
If `M/IM` is flat over `R/I`, `Tor₁^R(R/I, M) = 0` and `I` is nilpotent, then `M` is flat
over `R`.
declarations.statement:
theorem flat_of_nilpotent
    (H1 : Module.Flat (R ⧸ I) (M ⧸ (I • (⊤ : Submodule R M))))
    (H2 : Tor1Vanishes R (R ⧸ I) M)
    (hI : ∃ n : ℕ, 1 ≤ n ∧ I ^ n = ⊥) :
    Module.Flat R M
declarations.comment: in particular

declarations.name: Module.Flat.linearIndependent_and_span_eq_top_mkQ_comp_iff_of_isNilpotent
declarations.doc:
Let `R` be a commutative ring, let `I ⊆ R` be a nilpotent ideal and let `M` be a flat
`R`-module. A family `x : ι → M`, indexed by an arbitrary type, is an `R`-basis of `M` if and only
if the family of its reductions is an `R/I`-basis of `M/IM`. "Is a basis" is read as
`LinearIndependent … ∧ Submodule.span … = ⊤`, the hypotheses of `Module.Basis.mk`.
declarations.statement:
theorem linearIndependent_and_span_eq_top_mkQ_comp_iff_of_isNilpotent {R : Type*}
    [CommRing R] {M : Type*} [AddCommGroup M] [Module R M] [Module.Flat R M] (I : Ideal R)
    (hI : IsNilpotent I) {ι : Type*} (x : ι → M) :
    (LinearIndependent (R ⧸ I) ((I • (⊤ : Submodule R M)).mkQ ∘ x) ∧
        Submodule.span (R ⧸ I) (Set.range ((I • (⊤ : Submodule R M)).mkQ ∘ x)) = ⊤) ↔
      (LinearIndependent R x ∧ Submodule.span R (Set.range x) = ⊤)
declarations.comment:
Stated for an arbitrary nilpotent ideal `I` of an arbitrary commutative ring, the
source's local ring being the case `I = IsLocalRing.maximalIdeal R`; `M/IM` is `M ⧸ I • ⊤` over
`R ⧸ I` with reduction map `Submodule.mkQ`, and `forms a basis` is
`LinearIndependent … ∧ Submodule.span … = ⊤`. See the module docstring.

declarations.name: Module.tfae_flat_free_projective_of_isNilpotent_maximalIdeal
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 051G**: let `(R, 𝔪)` be a local ring whose maximal ideal is nilpotent — an Artinian
local ring, for instance — and let `M` be an `R`-module. Then `M` is flat over `R` if and only if
`M` is a free `R`-module if and only if `M` is a projective `R`-module. No finiteness hypothesis on
`M` is needed; compare `Module.free_of_flat_of_isLocalRing`, which assumes `Module.Finite R M` over
an arbitrary local ring, and `Module.Flat.projective_of_finitePresentation`. The proof is the
source's: a family of elements of `M` whose reductions form a basis of `M/𝔪M` over `R/𝔪` is a basis
of `M` over `R`, by Lemma 051F.
declarations.statement:
public theorem tfae_flat_free_projective_of_isNilpotent_maximalIdeal {R : Type*} [CommRing R]
    [IsLocalRing R] {M : Type*} [AddCommGroup M] [Module R M]
    (hR : IsNilpotent (IsLocalRing.maximalIdeal R)) :
    List.TFAE [Module.Flat R M, Module.Free R M, Module.Projective R M]
declarations.comment:
The equivalence is a `List.TFAE` in the source's order (flat, free, projective);
nilpotence of the maximal ideal is `IsNilpotent (IsLocalRing.maximalIdeal R)`.

declarations.name: Stacks.FreeOfNilpotentIdeal.free_of_nilpotent_of_basis_mod_of_tor
declarations.doc:
**Theorem (Stacks Project, Tag 051H; Lemma 10.101.3).**

Let `R` be a ring, `I ⊆ R` an ideal, `M` an `R`-module, `A` a set, and
`x : A → M` a family of elements of `M`. Assume:

1. `I` is nilpotent;
2. the family of reductions `(reduction I (x α))_{α}` forms a basis of the
   `R/I`-module `M/IM`, witnessed by a basis `b` with `b α = reduction I (x α)`;
3. `Tor₁^R(R/I, M) = 0`, expressed as injectivity of the multiplication map
   `torMul I : I ⊗_R M → M`.

Then `x` is a basis of `M` as an `R`-module: it is linearly independent and
spans `M`.
declarations.statement:
theorem free_of_nilpotent_of_basis_mod_of_tor
    {A : Type*} (x : A → M) (I : Ideal R)
    (hI : IsNilpotent I)
    (b : Module.Basis A (R ⧸ I) (M ⧸ smul (M := M) I))
    (hb : ∀ α, b α = reduction I (x α))
    (hTor : Function.Injective (torMul (M := M) I)) :
    LinearIndependent R x ∧ ⊤ ≤ Submodule.span R (Set.range x)

declarations.name: flat_quot_idealTwo_smul_top_of_flat_quot_and_flat_baseChange
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Tag 051I, Lemma 10.101.4.** Wires the square-zero local criterion
(`flat_of_sq_zero_local_criterion`) to the two base-change inputs
(`hquot_from_h1`, `htor_from_base_change`), using that the image of `I` in
`R ⧸ I₂` is square-zero (`image_I_sq_eq_bot`).
declarations.statement:
theorem flat_quot_idealTwo_smul_top_of_flat_quot_and_flat_baseChange
    {R R' : Type*} [CommRing R] [CommRing R'] [Algebra R R']
    {M : Type*} [AddCommGroup M] [Module R M]
    (I : Ideal R)
    (h1 : Module.Flat (R ⧸ I) (M ⧸ I • (⊤ : Submodule R M)))
    (h2 : Module.Flat R' (R' ⊗[R] M)) :
    Module.Flat (R ⧸ idealTwo I R')
      (M ⧸ (idealTwo I R') • (⊤ : Submodule R M))

declarations.name: Module.Flat.of_flat_quotient_of_flat_tensorProduct_of_isNilpotent_of_injective
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 051J**: the local criterion for flatness along an injective ring map. Let
`φ : R → R'` be a map of commutative rings, `I ⊆ R` a nilpotent ideal and `M` an `R`-module. If
`φ = algebraMap R R'` is injective, `M/IM` is flat over `R ⧸ I` and the base change `R' ⊗[R] M`
is flat over `R'`, then `M` is flat over `R`. Compare `Module.Flat.of_flat_tensorProduct`, which
descends flatness along a faithfully flat ring map with no nilpotent ideal in sight, and
`Module.Flat.of_flat_baseChange_of_injective` (Stacks 051L), the case where `R` is Artinian and
`I` is its Jacobson radical, so that flatness of the reduction is automatic. The proof is the
source's: the tower `I₁ = I`, `I_{n+1} = φ⁻¹(φ(I_n) ^ 2 R')` reaches `0` because `I` is nilpotent
and `φ` is injective, and each step preserves flatness of the reduction by the square-zero
criterion (Stacks 051I).
declarations.statement:
public theorem of_flat_quotient_of_flat_tensorProduct_of_isNilpotent_of_injective
    {R R' : Type*} [CommRing R] [CommRing R'] [Algebra R R']
    {M : Type*} [AddCommGroup M] [Module R M] (I : Ideal R)
    (hI : IsNilpotent I) (hφ : Function.Injective (algebraMap R R'))
    (hMI : Module.Flat (R ⧸ I) (M ⧸ I • (⊤ : Submodule R M)))
    (hM' : Module.Flat R' (R' ⊗[R] M)) :
    Module.Flat R M
declarations.comment:
The ring map is `algebraMap R R'`; `M/IM` is `M ⧸ I • ⊤` with its canonical
`R ⧸ I`-action and the base change is `R' ⊗[R] M`, acted on by `R'` through the left factor. See
the module docstring.

declarations.name: Module.Flat.iff_flat_quotient_and_isZero_Tor'_one
declarations.doc:
The local criterion for flatness over a local ring with nilpotent maximal ideal (an Artinian
local ring, for instance). Let `R` be such a ring, let `M` be an `R`-module and
let `I ⊆ R` be a proper ideal. Then `M` is flat over `R` if and only if `M/IM` is flat over `R/I`
and `Tor₁^R(R/I, M) = 0`. Here `Tor₁^R(R/I, M)` is
`((Tor' (ModuleCat R) 1).obj (ModuleCat.of R (R ⧸ I))).obj (ModuleCat.of R M)`, the first left
derived functor of `- ⊗ M` evaluated at `R ⧸ I`.
declarations.statement:
theorem iff_flat_quotient_and_isZero_Tor'_one {R : Type u} [CommRing R] [IsLocalRing R]
    (M : Type u) [AddCommGroup M] [Module R M] (I : Ideal R)
    (hR : IsNilpotent (IsLocalRing.maximalIdeal R)) (hI : I ≠ ⊤) :
    Module.Flat R M ↔
      Module.Flat (R ⧸ I) (M ⧸ (I • ⊤ : Submodule R M)) ∧
        IsZero (((Tor' (ModuleCat.{u} R) 1).obj (ModuleCat.of R (R ⧸ I))).obj
          (ModuleCat.of R M))
declarations.comment:
The source's Artinian local `R` is weakened to `R` local with nilpotent maximal
ideal, the hypothesis of 051G; `Tor_1^R(R/I, M)` is `Tor'`, which derives the first variable, as
in 00MJ and 00M5. See the module docstring.

declarations.name: Module.Flat.of_flat_baseChange_of_injective
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 051L**: flatness descends along an injective ring map whose source is Artinian. Let
`R → S` be a map of commutative rings with `R` Artinian and `algebraMap R S` injective, let `M` be
an `R`-module and let `f : M →ₗ[R] N` exhibit `N` as the base change of `M` to `S`, for instance
`N = S ⊗[R] M` with `f = TensorProduct.mk R S M 1`. If `N` is flat over `S`, then `M` is flat over
`R`. Compare `Module.Flat.of_flat_tensorProduct`, where `R → S` is faithfully flat instead.
declarations.statement:
public theorem of_flat_baseChange_of_injective {R : Type*} [CommRing R] [IsArtinianRing R]
    (S : Type*) [CommRing S] [Algebra R S] {M : Type*} [AddCommGroup M] [Module R M]
    (N : Type*) [AddCommGroup N] [Module R N] [Module S N] [IsScalarTower R S N]
    [Module.Flat S N] {f : M →ₗ[R] N} (hf : IsBaseChange S f)
    (hRS : Function.Injective (algebraMap R S)) :
    Module.Flat R M
declarations.comment:
The source's `M ⊗_R S` is an arbitrary base change `f : M →ₗ[R] N` with
`IsBaseChange S f`, which specialises to it by `TensorProduct.isBaseChange`; injectivity of the
ring map is injectivity of `algebraMap R S`. See the module docstring.

declarations.name: eventuallyRapidlyDecreasing_snoc_dotProduct_eq_iff
declarations.doc:
Stacks 051M with an arbitrary positive last exponent: for a finite set `N` of
multi-indices in `ℕ^{n+1}` and any `c > 0`, for `e_1 ≫ ⋯ ≫ e_n ≫ e_{n+1} = c` the dot
product with `e = (e_1, …, e_n, c)` separates `N`.
declarations.statement:
theorem eventuallyRapidlyDecreasing_snoc_dotProduct_eq_iff {n : ℕ}
    (N : Finset (Fin (n + 1) → ℕ)) {c : ℕ} (hc : 0 < c) :
    EventuallyRapidlyDecreasing n fun e => ∀ ν ∈ N, ∀ ν' ∈ N,
      ((Fin.snoc e c : Fin (n + 1) → ℕ) ⬝ᵥ ν = (Fin.snoc e c : Fin (n + 1) → ℕ) ⬝ᵥ ν' ↔
        ν = ν')
declarations.comment: the last exponent `e_n` may be any positive integer; `N` need not be nonempty

declarations.name: eventuallyRapidlyDecreasing_dotProduct_eq_iff
declarations.doc:
Stacks 051M: for a finite set `N` of multi-indices in `ℕ^n`, for all exponent vectors
`e = (e_1, …, e_n)` with `e_1 ≫ e_2 ≫ ⋯ ≫ e_n` (in the nested sense of
`EventuallyRapidlyDecreasing`) we have `e · ν = e · ν' ↔ ν = ν'` for all `ν, ν' ∈ N`.
declarations.statement:
theorem eventuallyRapidlyDecreasing_dotProduct_eq_iff {n : ℕ} (N : Finset (Fin n → ℕ)) :
    EventuallyRapidlyDecreasing n fun e => ∀ ν ∈ N, ∀ ν' ∈ N, (e ⬝ᵥ ν = e ⬝ᵥ ν' ↔ ν = ν')
declarations.comment: nested quantifier `e_1 ≫ ⋯ ≫ e_n` as `EventuallyRapidlyDecreasing`; `N` need not be nonempty

declarations.name: eventuallyRapid_subst_constant_leadingCoeff_of_nonconstant
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 051N.** Let `g ∈ R[x_1, …, x_N]` be nonconstant (here `N = n + 1`, the
variable `X 0` plays the role of the distinguished variable `x_N`, and `X i` for `1 ≤ i ≤ n`
plays the role of `x_{N-i}`). Then for all exponents `e_1 ≫ e_2 ≫ ⋯ ≫ e_{N-1} ≫ e_N = 1`,
in the nested sense of `EventuallyRapid` (the tuple `e' : Fin n → ℕ` lists
`e_{N-1}, …, e_1`, and the full exponent vector is `Fin.cons 1 e'`), the substituted
polynomial `g(x_1 + x_N^{e_1}, …, x_{N-1} + x_N^{e_{N-1}}, x_N)`, viewed via `finSuccEquiv`
as a polynomial in `x_N`, equals `a x_N^d + (lower order terms in x_N)` with `d > 0` and
`a ∈ R` one of the nonzero coefficients of `g`: its degree is `d` and its leading
coefficient is the constant `MvPolynomial.C a`.
declarations.statement:
theorem eventuallyRapid_subst_constant_leadingCoeff_of_nonconstant
    (n : ℕ) (g : MvPolynomial (Fin (n + 1)) R)
    (hg : ¬ ∃ r : R, g = MvPolynomial.C r) :
    EventuallyRapid n fun e' => ∃ (d : ℕ) (a : R),
      (∃ ν ∈ g.support, a = g.coeff ν) ∧
      0 < d ∧
      (finSuccEquiv R n (subst n (Fin.cons 1 e') g)).natDegree = d ∧
      (finSuccEquiv R n (subst n (Fin.cons 1 e') g)).leadingCoeff = MvPolynomial.C a
declarations.comment: for all exponents e₁ ≫ ⋯ ≫ e_{N-1} ≫ e_N = 1 in the nested sense of `EventuallyRapid`; X 0 is the distinguished variable x_N

declarations.name: MvPolynomial.exists_finite_comap_eq_span_X_image_of_trdeg_eq
declarations.doc:
Let `k` be a field, let `q ⊆ k[x_1, …, x_n]` be a prime ideal, and let `r` be the
transcendence degree of the residue field `κ(q)` over `k`. Then there is a finite `k`-algebra map
`φ : k[y_1, …, y_n] → k[x_1, …, x_n]` whose preimage of `q` is the ideal `(y_{r + 1}, …, y_n)`
generated by the last `n - r` variables.
declarations.statement:
public theorem exists_finite_comap_eq_span_X_image_of_trdeg_eq {k : Type u} [Field k]
    {n : ℕ} (q : Ideal (MvPolynomial (Fin n) k)) [q.IsPrime] {r : ℕ}
    (hr : Algebra.trdeg k q.ResidueField = r) :
    ∃ φ : MvPolynomial (Fin n) k →ₐ[k] MvPolynomial (Fin n) k,
      φ.toRingHom.Finite ∧ q.comap φ = Ideal.span (X '' {i : Fin n | r ≤ (i : ℕ)})
declarations.comment:
The two polynomial rings are the one type `MvPolynomial (Fin n) k`, with
`(y_{r + 1}, …, y_n)` spelled `Ideal.span (X '' {i | r ≤ (i : ℕ)})`; `φ` is a `k`-algebra
map, as the source's construction gives, and `κ(q)` is the canonical
`Ideal.ResidueField`. See the module docstring.

declarations.name: Module.exists_ne_zero_free_localizedModule_away
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 051R** (generic freeness). Let `R` be a Noetherian domain, let `S` be an `R`-algebra
of finite type and let `M` be a finite `S`-module. Then there is a nonzero `f ∈ R` such that the
localization `M_f` is a free `R_f`-module.

The proof is not the source's induction on `dim (K ⊗_R S)`: it reduces to `M = A ⧸ I` over a
polynomial ring `A = R[y_1, …, y_d]` and settles that case by division with remainder, so
`IsNoetherianRing R` is not used. See the module docstring.
declarations.statement:
public theorem exists_ne_zero_free_localizedModule_away
    {R S M : Type*} [CommRing R] [IsNoetherianRing R] [IsDomain R] [CommRing S] [Algebra R S]
    [Algebra.FiniteType R S] [AddCommGroup M] [Module R M] [Module S M] [IsScalarTower R S M]
    [Module.Finite S M] :
    ∃ f : R, f ≠ 0 ∧ ∀ (Rf : Type*) [CommRing Rf] [Algebra R Rf] [IsLocalization.Away f Rf]
      (Mf : Type*) [AddCommGroup Mf] [Module R Mf] [Module Rf Mf] [IsScalarTower R Rf Mf]
      (g : M →ₗ[R] Mf) [IsLocalizedModule (Submonoid.powers f) g],
      Module.Free Rf Mf
declarations.comment:
The localizations are abstract: the conclusion asserts
freeness over every model `Rf` of `R_f` and `Mf` of `M_f`, pinned by `IsLocalization.Away` and
`IsLocalizedModule`. The `R`-module structure on `M` is the one induced by `R → S`. See the module
docstring.

declarations.name: Module.FinitePresentation.exists_ne_zero_free_localizedModule_away
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 051S** (generic freeness). Let `R` be a domain, let `S` be an `R`-algebra of finite
presentation and let `M` be an `S`-module of finite presentation. Then there is a nonzero `f ∈ R`
such that the localization `M_f` is a free `R_f`-module.

Write `S = P/I` with `P = R[x_1, …, x_n]`, so that `M ≅ P^t/K` with `K` finitely generated, and let
`R₀ ⊆ R` be the `ℤ`-subalgebra generated by the coefficients of generators of `K`. Then `R₀` is a
domain of finite type over `ℤ`, hence Noetherian, and `M` is the base change along `R₀ → R` of the
finite `R₀[x]`-module `M₀` defined by the descended generators, so 051R applies over `R₀`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem exists_ne_zero_free_localizedModule_away
    {R S M : Type*} [CommRing R] [IsDomain R] [CommRing S] [Algebra R S]
    [Algebra.FinitePresentation R S] [AddCommGroup M] [Module R M] [Module S M]
    [IsScalarTower R S M] [Module.FinitePresentation S M] :
    ∃ f : R, f ≠ 0 ∧ ∀ (Rf : Type*) [CommRing Rf] [Algebra R Rf] [IsLocalization.Away f Rf]
      (Mf : Type*) [AddCommGroup Mf] [Module R Mf] [Module Rf Mf] [IsScalarTower R Rf Mf]
      (g : M →ₗ[R] Mf) [IsLocalizedModule (Submonoid.powers f) g],
      Module.Free Rf Mf
declarations.comment:
The localizations are abstract: the conclusion asserts freeness over every model
`Rf` of `R_f` and `Mf` of `M_f`, pinned by `IsLocalization.Away` and `IsLocalizedModule`. The
`R`-module structure on `M` is the one induced by `R → S`. See the module docstring.

declarations.name: Algebra.exists_ne_zero_isFinitePresentationFreeAway
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 051T** (generic freeness and generic finite presentation). Let `R` be a domain, let
`S` be an `R`-algebra of finite type and let `M` be a finite `S`-module. Then some nonzero `f ∈ R`
satisfies the condition `Algebra.IsFinitePresentationFreeAway R S M f` of Equation 051U: the
localizations `S_f` and `M_f` are free `R_f`-modules, `S_f` is a finitely presented `R_f`-algebra
and `M_f` is a finitely presented `S_f`-module.
declarations.statement:
public theorem exists_ne_zero_isFinitePresentationFreeAway
    {R S M : Type*} [CommRing R] [IsDomain R] [CommRing S] [Algebra R S] [Algebra.FiniteType R S]
    [AddCommGroup M] [Module S M] [Module.Finite S M] :
    ∃ f : R, f ≠ 0 ∧ Algebra.IsFinitePresentationFreeAway R S M f
declarations.comment:
The four conclusions are the condition of Equation 051U, so they are cited as
`Algebra.IsFinitePresentationFreeAway` rather than written out; that definition fixes the models
of `R_f`, `S_f` and `M_f`, and `Algebra.isFinitePresentationFreeAway_iff` moves the conclusion to
any other models. See the module docstring.

declarations.name: Algebra.IsFinitePresentationFreeAway
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 051U**. Let `R → S` be a ring map, let `M` be an `S`-module and let `f : R`. The
condition `Algebra.IsFinitePresentationFreeAway R S M f` says that, after inverting `f`, the ring
`S_f` is of finite presentation as an `R_f`-algebra, the module `M_f` is of finite presentation as
an `S_f`-module, and `S_f` and `M_f` are free as `R_f`-modules. The localizations are the
canonical ones: `R_f = Localization.Away f`, `S_f` is the localization of `S` at the image of the
powers of `f`, and `M_f = S_f ⊗[S] M`; by `Algebra.isFinitePresentationFreeAway_iff` the four
properties may be tested on any other models.
declarations.statement:
public def IsFinitePresentationFreeAway (R S M : Type*) [CommRing R] [CommRing S] [Algebra R S]
    [AddCommGroup M] [Module S M] (f : R) : Prop
declarations.comment:
The condition of the source's display, as a predicate on `f`, with the canonical
models of the localizations; `M_f` is the base change `S_f ⊗[S] M`. See the module docstring.

declarations.name: Algebra.iUnion_basicOpen_isFinitePresentationFreeAway_inter_subset_of_shortExact
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 051W**. Let `R → S` be a ring map and let `0 → M₁ → M₂ → M₃ → 0` be a short exact
sequence of `S`-modules. Writing `U(R → S, M) = ⋃ {D(f) | Algebra.IsFinitePresentationFreeAway R S
M f}` for the locus of Equation 051V, one has
`U(R → S, M₁) ∩ U(R → S, M₃) ⊆ U(R → S, M₂)`: an extension of free modules is free and an
extension of finitely presented modules is finitely presented, so if `f₁` and `f₃` satisfy
Equation 051U for `M₁` and `M₃` then `f₁f₃` satisfies it for `M₂`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem iUnion_basicOpen_isFinitePresentationFreeAway_inter_subset_of_shortExact
    {R S : Type*} [CommRing R] [CommRing S] [Algebra R S]
    {M₁ M₂ M₃ : Type*} [AddCommGroup M₁] [Module S M₁] [AddCommGroup M₂] [Module S M₂]
    [AddCommGroup M₃] [Module S M₃] (i : M₁ →ₗ[S] M₂) (q : M₂ →ₗ[S] M₃)
    (hi : Function.Injective i) (hq : Function.Surjective q) (hiq : Function.Exact i q) :
    (⋃ f ∈ {f : R | IsFinitePresentationFreeAway R S M₁ f},
          (basicOpen f : Set (PrimeSpectrum R))) ∩
        (⋃ f ∈ {f : R | IsFinitePresentationFreeAway R S M₃ f},
          (basicOpen f : Set (PrimeSpectrum R))) ⊆
      ⋃ f ∈ {f : R | IsFinitePresentationFreeAway R S M₂ f},
        (basicOpen f : Set (PrimeSpectrum R))
declarations.comment:
The locus `U(R → S, M)` of Equation 051V, which has no separate definition here, is
written out as the union of the standard opens `D(f)` over the `f` satisfying Equation 051U, i.e.
over `Algebra.IsFinitePresentationFreeAway R S M f`. See the module docstring.

declarations.name: Algebra.image_comap_iUnion_basicOpen_isFinitePresentationFreeAway
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 051X**. Let `R → S` be a ring map, let `M` be an `S`-module and let `f : R`. Call
`g` good for a module when it satisfies the condition `Algebra.IsFinitePresentationFreeAway` of
Equation 051U, and let `U(R → S, M) ⊆ Spec R` be the union of the standard opens `D(g)` over the
good `g` (Equation 051V). Then, under the identification of `Spec(R_f)` with `D(f)` given by
`PrimeSpectrum.comap (algebraMap R R_f)`, one has
`U(R_f → S_f, M_f) = D(f) ∩ U(R → S, M)`. Here `R_f`, `S_f` and `M_f` are arbitrary models of the
localizations at the powers of `f`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem image_comap_iUnion_basicOpen_isFinitePresentationFreeAway
    {R S M : Type*} [CommRing R] [CommRing S] [Algebra R S] [AddCommGroup M] [Module S M] (f : R)
    (Rf : Type*) [CommRing Rf] [Algebra R Rf] [IsLocalization.Away f Rf]
    (Sf : Type*) [CommRing Sf] [Algebra R Sf] [Algebra S Sf] [Algebra Rf Sf]
      [IsScalarTower R S Sf] [IsScalarTower R Rf Sf]
      [IsLocalization.Away (algebraMap R S f) Sf]
    (Mf : Type*) [AddCommGroup Mf] [Module S Mf] [Module Sf Mf] [IsScalarTower S Sf Mf]
    (l : M →ₗ[S] Mf) [IsLocalizedModule.Away (algebraMap R S f) l] :
    comap (algebraMap R Rf) ''
        (⋃ g ∈ {g : Rf | Algebra.IsFinitePresentationFreeAway Rf Sf Mf g},
          (basicOpen g : Set (PrimeSpectrum Rf))) =
      (basicOpen f : Set (PrimeSpectrum R)) ∩
        ⋃ g ∈ {g : R | Algebra.IsFinitePresentationFreeAway R S M g},
          (basicOpen g : Set (PrimeSpectrum R))
declarations.comment:
The locus `U(R → S, M)` of Equation 051V is written out as the union of the standard
opens `D(g)` over the `g` satisfying 051U, cited as `Algebra.IsFinitePresentationFreeAway`; the
identification `Spec(R_f) = D(f)` is the open embedding `PrimeSpectrum.comap (algebraMap R R_f)`,
along which the left-hand side is pushed forward. See the module docstring.

declarations.name: Algebra.dense_iUnion_basicOpen_isFinitePresentationFreeAway_of_localizationAway
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 051Y**. Let `R → S` be a ring map and let `M` be an `S`-module. Call `f ∈ R` good when
`S_f` is of finite presentation over `R_f`, `M_f` is of finite presentation over `S_f` and `S_f`,
`M_f` are free over `R_f` (Equation 051U), and let `U(R → S, M) ⊆ Spec R` be the union of the
standard opens `D(f)` over the good `f` (Equation 051V). If the opens `D(f)`, `f ∈ s`, have dense
union in `Spec R` — that is, they cover a dense open — and if for each `f ∈ s` the locus
`U(R_f → S_f, M_f)` is dense in `Spec(R_f) = D(f)`, then `U(R → S, M)` is dense in `Spec R`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem dense_iUnion_basicOpen_isFinitePresentationFreeAway_of_localizationAway
    {R S M : Type*} [CommRing R] [CommRing S] [Algebra R S] [AddCommGroup M] [Module S M]
    (s : Set R) (hs : Dense (⋃ f ∈ s, (basicOpen f : Set (PrimeSpectrum R))))
    (H : ∀ f ∈ s, Dense (⋃ g ∈ {g : Localization.Away f |
          IsFinitePresentationFreeAway (Localization.Away f)
            (Localization (algebraMapSubmonoid S (.powers f)))
            (Localization (algebraMapSubmonoid S (.powers f)) ⊗[S] M) g},
        (basicOpen g : Set (PrimeSpectrum (Localization.Away f))))) :
    Dense (⋃ f ∈ {f : R | IsFinitePresentationFreeAway R S M f},
      (basicOpen f : Set (PrimeSpectrum R)))
declarations.comment:
The dense open `U` of the source is the union of the `D(f)`, `f ∈ s`, so it is not
a separate variable; the locus of Equation 051V is written out as the union of the `D(f)` over the
`f` satisfying 051U, and density in `D(f)` is stated in
`Spec(R_f)`. See the module docstring.

declarations.name: Algebra.exists_isOpen_dense_isFinitePresentationFreeAway
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 051Z** (generic flatness over a reduced base). Let `R → S` be a ring map of finite
type with `R` reduced, and let `M` be a finite `S`-module. Then there is an open dense subset
`U ⊆ Spec R` such that every `u ∈ U` lies in a standard open `D(f) ⊆ U` for which `M_f` and `S_f`
are free over `R_f`, `S_f` is a finitely presented `R_f`-algebra and `M_f` is a finitely presented
`S_f`-module.
declarations.statement:
public theorem exists_isOpen_dense_isFinitePresentationFreeAway {R S M : Type*} [CommRing R]
    [IsReduced R] [CommRing S] [Algebra R S] [Algebra.FiniteType R S] [AddCommGroup M]
    [Module S M] [Module.Finite S M] :
    ∃ U : Set (PrimeSpectrum R), IsOpen U ∧ Dense U ∧
      ∀ u ∈ U, ∃ f : R, u ∈ basicOpen f ∧ (basicOpen f : Set (PrimeSpectrum R)) ⊆ U ∧
        IsFinitePresentationFreeAway R S M f
declarations.comment:
The four conditions on `f` are the condition of Equation 051U, cited as
`Algebra.IsFinitePresentationFreeAway`; that definition fixes the models of `R_f`, `S_f` and `M_f`,
and `Algebra.isFinitePresentationFreeAway_iff` moves the conclusion to any other models.

declarations.name: Algebra.exists_quasiFinite_mvPolynomial_away_comap_map_eq
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0520.** Let `R → S` be a ring map of finite type and let `𝔮 ⊂ S` be a prime lying
over `𝔭 ⊂ R` with `dim_𝔮(S/R) = n` and `trdeg_{κ(𝔭)} κ(𝔮) = r`. Then there are `f ∈ R`,
`f ∉ 𝔭`, `g ∈ S`, `g ∉ 𝔮` and a quasi-finite `R`-algebra map `φ : R_f[x_1, …, x_n] → S_g`
with `φ⁻¹(𝔮S_g) = (𝔭, x_{r+1}, …, x_n)`.
declarations.statement:
theorem Algebra.exists_quasiFinite_mvPolynomial_away_comap_map_eq
    {R S : Type*} [CommRing R] [CommRing S] [Algebra R S] [Algebra.FiniteType R S]
    (p : Ideal R) [p.IsPrime] (q : Ideal S) [q.IsPrime] [q.LiesOver p]
    [Algebra p.ResidueField q.ResidueField] [IsScalarTower R p.ResidueField q.ResidueField]
    {n r : ℕ} (hn : Algebra.relativeDimensionAt R q = n)
    (hr : Algebra.trdeg p.ResidueField q.ResidueField = r) :
    ∃ f ∉ p, ∃ g ∉ q, ∃ φ : MvPolynomial (Fin n) (Localization.Away f) →+* Localization.Away g,
      φ.comp (C.comp (algebraMap R (Localization.Away f))) =
        algebraMap R (Localization.Away g) ∧
      φ.FiniteType ∧ φ.QuasiFinite ∧
      (q.map (algebraMap S (Localization.Away g))).comap φ =
        Ideal.map C (p.map (algebraMap R (Localization.Away f))) ⊔
          Ideal.span (X '' {i : Fin n | r ≤ (i : ℕ)})
declarations.comment:
`R_f[x_1, …, x_n]` is `MvPolynomial (Fin n) (Localization.Away f)`, with
`x_{i+1}` indexed by `i : Fin n`; the ideal `(𝔭, x_{r+1}, …, x_n)` is the sum of the extension of
`𝔭` along the constants and the ideal generated by the variables indexed by `{i | r ≤ i}`.
Quasi-finite is `RingHom.QuasiFinite` together with `RingHom.FiniteType`, and `φ` is recorded to
be an `R`-algebra map. The algebra `κ(𝔭) → κ(𝔮)` is any one compatible with `R`.

declarations.name: Module.Flat.quotient_inf
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0522**.
If `M ⧸ I₁ • ⊤` is flat over `R ⧸ I₁` and `M ⧸ I₂ • ⊤` is flat over `R ⧸ I₂`, then
`M ⧸ (I₁ ⊓ I₂) • ⊤` is flat over `R ⧸ (I₁ ⊓ I₂)`.
declarations.statement:
theorem Module.Flat.quotient_inf {R : Type*} [CommRing R] {M : Type*} [AddCommGroup M]
    [Module R M] (I₁ I₂ : Ideal R)
    (h₁ : Module.Flat (R ⧸ I₁) (M ⧸ (I₁ • (⊤ : Submodule R M))))
    (h₂ : Module.Flat (R ⧸ I₂) (M ⧸ (I₂ • (⊤ : Submodule R M)))) :
    Module.Flat (R ⧸ (I₁ ⊓ I₂)) (M ⧸ ((I₁ ⊓ I₂) • (⊤ : Submodule R M)))

declarations.name: Module.Flat.of_flat_quotient_pow
declarations.doc:
Let `R → S` be a ring map with `R` and `S` Noetherian, let `I ⊆ R` be an ideal and let `M` be a
finite `S`-module. If `M/IⁿM` is flat over `R/Iⁿ` for every `n ≥ 1`, then for every prime `q` of
`S` containing `IS` the localization `M_q` is flat over `R`.

The localization is taken abstractly: `Mq` is any `S`-module with a map `f : M →ₗ[S] Mq` exhibiting
it as the localization of `M` at `q`. Taking `S` local with maximal ideal `q`, `Mq = M` and
`f = LinearMap.id` shows that `M` is flat over `R` when `IS` is contained in the maximal ideal of a
local `S`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem of_flat_quotient_pow {R S : Type*} [CommRing R] [CommRing S] [Algebra R S]
    [IsNoetherianRing R] [IsNoetherianRing S] (I : Ideal R)
    (M : Type*) [AddCommGroup M] [Module R M] [Module S M] [IsScalarTower R S M]
    [Module.Finite S M]
    (hflat : ∀ n : ℕ,
      Module.Flat (R ⧸ I ^ (n + 1)) (M ⧸ (I ^ (n + 1) • (⊤ : Submodule R M))))
    (q : Ideal S) [q.IsPrime] (hq : I.map (algebraMap R S) ≤ q)
    (Mq : Type*) [AddCommGroup Mq] [Module R Mq] [Module S Mq] [IsScalarTower R S Mq]
    (f : M →ₗ[S] Mq) [IsLocalizedModule.AtPrime q f] :
    Module.Flat R Mq
declarations.comment:
Both statements: the second is the case where `S` is local, `q` is its maximal
ideal and the localization is taken to be `M` itself. `M/IⁿM` is
`M ⧸ (I ^ n • ⊤ : Submodule R M)` and `M_q` is given by `IsLocalizedModule.AtPrime q f`; see the
module docstring.

declarations.name: exists_least_flat_quotient_ideal
declarations.doc:
Over an Artinian ring `R`, there is a smallest ideal `I` such that `M ⧸ I • M` is flat over
`R ⧸ I`.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_least_flat_quotient_ideal {R M : Type*} [CommRing R]
    [IsArtinianRing R] [AddCommGroup M] [Module R M] :
    ∃ I : Ideal R,
      Module.Flat (R ⧸ I) (M ⧸ (I • (⊤ : Submodule R M))) ∧
        ∀ J : Ideal R,
          Module.Flat (R ⧸ J) (M ⧸ (J • (⊤ : Submodule R M))) → I ≤ J

declarations.name: flat_tensorProduct_iff_map_least_flat_quotient_ideal_eq_bot
declarations.doc:
The least ideal making the corresponding quotient of a module flat maps
to zero under precisely those ring maps along which the module becomes flat.
declarations.statement:
theorem flat_tensorProduct_iff_map_least_flat_quotient_ideal_eq_bot
    {R M : Type*} [CommRing R] [IsArtinianRing R] [AddCommGroup M] [Module R M]
    (I : Ideal R)
    (hI : Module.Flat (R ⧸ I) (M ⧸ (I • (⊤ : Submodule R M))))
    (hmin : ∀ J : Ideal R,
      Module.Flat (R ⧸ J) (M ⧸ (J • (⊤ : Submodule R M))) → I ≤ J) :
    ∀ {S : Type*} [CommRing S] (φ : R →+* S),
      let _ := φ.toAlgebra;
      Module.Flat S (S ⊗[R] M) ↔ I.map φ = ⊥

declarations.name: Module.FlatAfterQuotientAlong
declarations.doc:
Flatness along the inverse image of `V(m)` after quotienting `R`, `S` and `M` by the ideal
`I` of `R`. Here `(S / IS) ⊗[S] M` is the canonical model of `M / IM`.
declarations.statement:
abbrev Module.FlatAfterQuotientAlong
    (R : Type u) (S : Type v) [CommRing R] [CommRing S] [Algebra R S]
    (M : Type w) [AddCommGroup M] [Module S M] (m I : Ideal R) : Prop
declarations.comment: the property (15.20.1) quantified over in the statement

declarations.name: Module.exists_least_flattening_ideal
declarations.doc:
Over a complete Noetherian local ring, there is a least ideal contained in the maximal ideal
such that the quotient module is flat at every prime lying over the maximal ideal.
declarations.statement:
theorem Module.exists_least_flattening_ideal
    (R : Type u) (S : Type v) [CommRing R] [CommRing S] [Algebra R S]
    [IsLocalRing R] [IsNoetherianRing R]
    [IsAdicComplete (IsLocalRing.maximalIdeal R) R]
    (M : Type w) [AddCommGroup M] [Module S M] [Module.Finite S M]
    [IsNoetherianRing S] :
    ∃ I : Ideal R,
      I ≤ IsLocalRing.maximalIdeal R ∧
        Module.FlatAfterQuotientAlong R S M (IsLocalRing.maximalIdeal R) I ∧
          ∀ J : Ideal R,
            Module.FlatAfterQuotientAlong R S M (IsLocalRing.maximalIdeal R) J → I ≤ J

declarations.name: Module.flatAlongZeroLocus_baseChange_iff_map_eq_bot
declarations.doc:
For the least ideal making the indicated quotient of `M` flat along the closed point, a local
map from `R` to a Noetherian local ring `R'` annihilates that ideal exactly when the base change
of `M` is flat along the closed point of `R'`.
declarations.statement:
lemma Module.flatAlongZeroLocus_baseChange_iff_map_eq_bot
    (R : Type u) (S : Type v) [CommRing R] [CommRing S] [Algebra R S]
    [IsLocalRing R] [IsNoetherianRing R]
    (M : Type w) [AddCommGroup M] [Module S M]
    (I : Ideal R)
    (hI_flat : Module.FlatAfterQuotientAlong
      R S M (IsLocalRing.maximalIdeal R) I)
    (hI_min : ∀ J : Ideal R,
      Module.FlatAfterQuotientAlong R S M (IsLocalRing.maximalIdeal R) J → I ≤ J)
    (R' : Type x) [CommRing R'] [IsLocalRing R'] [IsNoetherianRing R']
    [Algebra R R'] [IsLocalHom (algebraMap R R')] :
    Module.FlatAlongZeroLocus R' (S ⊗[R] R')
        (IsLocalRing.maximalIdeal R') ((S ⊗[R] R') ⊗[S] M) ↔
      I.map (algebraMap R R') = ⊥

declarations.name: Module.flatAlongZeroLocus_baseChange_iff_map_eq_bot_of_finiteType
declarations.doc:
For the least ideal making the indicated quotient of `M` flat along the closed point, a local
map from `R` to an arbitrary local ring `R'` annihilates that ideal exactly when the base change
of `M` is flat along the closed point, provided `S` is of finite type over the Noetherian local
ring `R` and `M` is finite over `S`. No Noetherian hypothesis is imposed on `R'`.
declarations.statement:
lemma Module.flatAlongZeroLocus_baseChange_iff_map_eq_bot_of_finiteType
    (R : Type u) (S : Type v) [CommRing R] [CommRing S] [Algebra R S]
    [IsLocalRing R] [IsNoetherianRing R] [Algebra.FiniteType R S]
    (M : Type w) [AddCommGroup M] [Module S M] [Module.Finite S M]
    (I : Ideal R)
    (hI_flat : Module.FlatAfterQuotientAlong
      R S M (IsLocalRing.maximalIdeal R) I)
    (hI_min : ∀ J : Ideal R,
      Module.FlatAfterQuotientAlong R S M (IsLocalRing.maximalIdeal R) J → I ≤ J)
    (R' : Type x) [CommRing R'] [IsLocalRing R']
    [Algebra R R'] [IsLocalHom (algebraMap R R')] :
    Module.FlatAlongZeroLocus R' (S ⊗[R] R')
        (IsLocalRing.maximalIdeal R') ((S ⊗[R] R') ⊗[S] M) ↔
      I.map (algebraMap R R') = ⊥

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.exists_dense_open_flat_finitePresentation_of_isIntegral
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 052A.** For a finite type morphism `f : X ⟶ S` to an integral scheme and a finite
type quasi-coherent module `F` on `X`, there is a dense open `U ⊆ S` such that `X_U → U` is flat
and of finite presentation and `F|_{X_U}` is flat over `U` and of finite presentation over
`𝒪_{X_U}`. An integral scheme is reduced, so this is a case of generic flatness over a reduced
base.
declarations.statement:
public theorem exists_dense_open_flat_finitePresentation_of_isIntegral
    {X S : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ S) [IsIntegral S]
    [LocallyOfFiniteType f] [QuasiCompact f]
    (F : X.Modules) [F.IsQuasicoherent] [F.IsFiniteType] :
    ∃ U : S.Opens,
      Dense (U : Set S) ∧
        Flat (f.resLE U (f ⁻¹ᵁ U) le_rfl) ∧
        AlgebraicGeometry.FinitePresentation (f.resLE U (f ⁻¹ᵁ U) le_rfl) ∧
        AlgebraicGeometry.IsFlatOver
          (f.resLE U (f ⁻¹ᵁ U) le_rfl).toLRSHom.toShHom
          (F.restrict (f ⁻¹ᵁ U).ι) ∧
        (F.restrict (f ⁻¹ᵁ U).ι).IsFinitePresentation
declarations.comment:
Deduced from the reduced-base Proposition 052B, which the Stacks Project notes
supersedes this one, using that an integral scheme is reduced (01ON).

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.exists_dense_open_flat_finitePresentation
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 052B.** A finite type morphism and a finite type
quasi-coherent module become flat and finitely presented over a common dense
open of a reduced base.
declarations.statement:
public theorem exists_dense_open_flat_finitePresentation
    {X S : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ S) [IsReduced S]
    [LocallyOfFiniteType f] [QuasiCompact f]
    (F : X.Modules) [F.IsQuasicoherent] [F.IsFiniteType] :
    ∃ U : S.Opens,
      Dense (U : Set S) ∧
        Flat (f.resLE U (f ⁻¹ᵁ U) le_rfl) ∧
        AlgebraicGeometry.FinitePresentation (f.resLE U (f ⁻¹ᵁ U) le_rfl) ∧
        AlgebraicGeometry.IsFlatOver
          (f.resLE U (f ⁻¹ᵁ U) le_rfl).toLRSHom.toShHom
          (F.restrict (f ⁻¹ᵁ U).ι) ∧
        (F.restrict (f ⁻¹ᵁ U).ι).IsFinitePresentation

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.exists_finite_over_smooth_of_locallyOfFiniteType
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 052E.** Let `f : X ⟶ S` be locally of finite type, let `x ∈ X` and set `s = f x`.
If the fibre `X_s` has local dimension `n` at `x`, then there is a commutative square
`g ≫ f = π ≫ h` in which `h : Y ⟶ S` is smooth of relative dimension `n`,
`g : (X', x') ⟶ (X, x)` is an elementary étale neighbourhood, `π : X' ⟶ Y` is finite, and the
fibre of `π` over `y = π x'` is the single point `x'`; moreover `κ(y)` is a purely
transcendental extension of `κ(s)`, and if `f` is locally of finite presentation then `π` is of
finite presentation.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_finite_over_smooth_of_locallyOfFiniteType
    {X S : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ S) [LocallyOfFiniteType f] (x : X) (n : ℕ)
    (hdim : topologicalKrullDimAt (f.fiber (f x)) (f.asFiber x) = n) :
    ∃ (Y : Scheme.{u}) (h : Y ⟶ S) (N : EtaleNeighborhood X x) (π : N.scheme ⟶ Y),
      SmoothOfRelativeDimension n h ∧ N.IsElementary ∧ IsFinite π ∧
      {z : N.scheme | π z = π N.point} = {N.point} ∧
      N.toBase ≫ f = π ≫ h ∧
      (∃ hy : h (π N.point) = f x,
        letI : Algebra (S.residueField (f x)) (Y.residueField (π N.point)) :=
          (((S.residueFieldCongr hy).inv ≫ h.residueFieldMap (π N.point)).hom).toAlgebra
        PurelyTranscendental (S.residueField (f x)) (Y.residueField (π N.point))) ∧
      (LocallyOfFinitePresentation f → FinitePresentation π)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.exists_idealSheafData_forall_isFlatOverAt_iff_of_isAdicComplete
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 052G.** Let `S = Spec A` be the spectrum of a Noetherian complete local
ring with closed point `s`, let `f : X ⟶ S` be of finite type and let `F` be a quasi-coherent
`𝒪_X`-module of finite type. Then the closed subscheme `Z ⊆ S` of Lemma 05PI for `E = X_s`
exists: for every morphism of pointed schemes `(T, t) ⟶ (S, s)`, the pulled back module `F_T` is
flat over `T` at every point of the fibre `X_t` if and only if `Spec(𝒪_{T,t}) ⟶ S` factors
through `Z`. As the remark explains, the proof is elementary: a finite affine open cover reduces
to `X` affine, where `Z` is cut out by the least flattening ideal of More on Algebra, Lemma 0526,
whose universal property is Lemma 0528.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_idealSheafData_forall_isFlatOverAt_iff_of_isAdicComplete
    (A : Type u) [CommRing A] [IsLocalRing A] [IsNoetherianRing A]
    [IsAdicComplete (IsLocalRing.maximalIdeal A) A]
    {X : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ Spec (.of A)) [LocallyOfFiniteType f] [QuasiCompact f]
    (F : X.Modules) [F.IsFiniteType] [F.IsQuasicoherent] :
    ∃ Z : (Spec (.of A)).IdealSheafData,
      ∀ (T : Scheme.{u}) (g : T ⟶ Spec (.of A)) (t : T),
        g t = IsLocalRing.closedPoint A →
        ((∀ y : (pullback f g : Scheme.{u}), pullback.snd f g y = t →
            IsFlatOverAt (pullback.snd f g).toLRSHom.toShHom
              ((Scheme.Modules.pullback (pullback.fst f g)).obj F) y) ↔
          ∃ h : Spec (T.presheaf.stalk t) ⟶ Z.subscheme,
            h ≫ Z.subschemeι = T.fromSpecStalk t ≫ g)
declarations.comment:
the closed subscheme of Lemma 05PI for E = X_s over a Noetherian complete local
base, constructed from finite affine charts and Lemma 0528

declarations.name: isIntegral_of_fg_stable
declarations.doc:
General determinant-trick lemma: if `M` is a finitely-generated `R`-submodule
of an `R`-algebra `B` that contains `1` and is stable under multiplication by `α`,
then `α` is integral over `R`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isIntegral_of_fg_stable
    {R B : Type*} [CommRing R] [Ring B] [Algebra R B]
    (M : Submodule R B) (hMfg : M.FG) (h1 : (1 : B) ∈ M)
    (α : B) (hstable : ∀ z ∈ M, α * z ∈ M) :
    IsIntegral R α

declarations.name: shortExact_fmap_gmap
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Tag 052J.** Under the hypothesis that `R` is integrally closed in
`R_x` or in `R_y`, the sequence
`0 → R → R[x/y] ⊕ R[y/x] → R[x/y, y/x] → 0`
is a short exact sequence of `R`-modules:
1. `f` is injective;
2. `im f = ker g`;
3. `g` is surjective.
declarations.statement:
theorem shortExact_fmap_gmap
    (hx : x ∈ R⁰) (hy : y ∈ R⁰)
    (hint : (∀ α : Localization.Away x, IsIntegral R α → α ∈ (⊥ : Subalgebra R (Localization.Away
        x))) ∨
            (∀ α : Localization.Away y, IsIntegral R α → α ∈ (⊥ : Subalgebra R (Localization.Away
                y)))) :
    Function.Injective (fmap x y) ∧
    LinearMap.range (fmap x y) = LinearMap.ker (gmap x y) ∧
    Function.Surjective (gmap x y)

declarations.name: Stacks.AffineBlowup.stacks052M_main
declarations.doc:
**Theorem 1 (Stacks Tag 052M, main case `𝔪 ≠ 0`).**
Let `(R, 𝔪)` be a local domain with fraction field `K`, and assume `𝔪 ≠ 0`.
Let `A` be a valuation ring of `K` which dominates `R`. Then the family `𝒮` of
admissible affine blowup algebras of Definition 7:

1. is **nonempty** and **directed** under inclusion, and moreover for any two
   *admissible pairs* `(I, a)`, `(J, b)` (Definition 7'), the explicit displayed
   product pair `(I*J, a*b)` is again an admissible pair, and its associated
   subring `affineBlowupImage (I*J) (a*b)` contains both
   `affineBlowupImage I a` and `affineBlowupImage J b`; and
2. has **directed union equal to `A`**: an element `x ∈ K` lies in `A` iff it
   lies in some member of `𝒮`.

Assembled from the four conjunct lemmas `stacks052M_C1_nonempty`,
`stacks052M_C2_directed`, `stacks052M_C3_refinement`, `stacks052M_C4_union`.
declarations.statement:
theorem stacks052M_main
    [IsDomain R] [IsLocalRing R]
    (hm : IsLocalRing.maximalIdeal R ≠ ⊥)
    (A : ValuationSubring K) (hdom : Dominates R A) :
    -- (1a) nonemptiness
    (∃ B, IsAdmissibleBlowup R A B) ∧
    -- (1b) abstract directedness under inclusion
    DirectedOn (· ≤ ·) {B | IsAdmissibleBlowup R A B} ∧
    -- (1c) the explicit common refinement `R[IJ/(ab)]` of two admissible pairs:
    -- the displayed product pair `(I*J, a*b)` is itself an admissible pair, and
    -- its subring contains both factors.
    (∀ (I J : Ideal R) (a b : R) (ha : a ∈ I) (hb : b ∈ J),
        IsAdmissiblePair R A I a ha →
        IsAdmissiblePair R A J b hb →
        ∃ (hab : a * b ∈ I * J),
          IsAdmissiblePair R A (I * J) (a * b) hab ∧
          (affineBlowupImage I a ha : Subring K) ≤ affineBlowupImage (I * J) (a * b) hab ∧
          (affineBlowupImage J b hb : Subring K) ≤ affineBlowupImage (I * J) (a * b) hab) ∧
    -- (2) the directed union equals A
    (∀ x : K, x ∈ A ↔ ∃ B, IsAdmissibleBlowup R A B ∧ x ∈ B)

declarations.name: exists_gradedAlgebra_degZeroPart_equiv
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Tag 052N (Lemma 10.57.10).**
Let `R` be a ring, `R'` a finite type `R`-algebra, and `M` a finite `R'`-module.
Then there exist a graded `R`-algebra `S`, a graded `S`-module `N`, and a
degree-`1` element `f ∈ S₁` such that `R' ≅ S_(f)` as `R`-algebras, `M ≅ N_(f)`
as modules (compatibly), `S₀ = R`, `S` is generated by finitely many degree-`1`
elements over `R`, and `N` is a finite `S`-module.  Here `S_(f)` is
`HomogeneousLocalization.Away 𝒜 f` and `N_(f)` is `degZeroPart f N ℬ`, the
degree-`0` part of the localization induced from the grading `ℬ`.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_gradedAlgebra_degZeroPart_equiv
    (R : Type uR) [CommRing R]
    (R' : Type uB) [CommRing R'] [Algebra R R'] [Algebra.FiniteType R R']
    (M : Type uM) [AddCommGroup M] [Module R' M] [Module.Finite R' M] :
    ∃ (S : Type (max uR uB)) (_ : CommRing S) (_ : Algebra R S)
      -- `𝒜` is the family of homogeneous pieces; `GradedAlgebra 𝒜` makes `S` a
      -- graded `R`-algebra graded by `ℕ = ℤ_{≥0}`.
      (𝒜 : ℕ → Submodule R S) (_ : GradedAlgebra 𝒜)
      -- `N` is an `S`-module with `ℤ`-graded homogeneous pieces `ℬ`.
      (N : Type uM) (_ : AddCommGroup N) (_ : Module S N)
      (ℬ : ℤ → AddSubgroup N) (_ : SetLike.GradedSMul 𝒜 ℬ) (_ : DirectSum.Decomposition ℬ)
      -- `f` is homogeneous of degree `1`.
      (f : S) (_ : f ∈ 𝒜 1),
      -- (2) `S₀ = R`: the structure map `R → S` is injective with range `𝒜 0`;
      -- and `S` is generated over `R` by finitely many degree-`1` elements.
      (Function.Injective (algebraMap R S) ∧
        Set.range (algebraMap R S) = (𝒜 0 : Set S)) ∧
      (∃ (gs : Finset S), (∀ g ∈ gs, g ∈ 𝒜 1) ∧
        Algebra.adjoin R (gs : Set S) = ⊤) ∧
      -- (3) `N` is a finite `S`-module.
      Module.Finite S N ∧
      -- (1) `R' ≅ S_(f)` as `R`-algebras and `M ≅ N_(f)` as modules.
      --
      -- `eR` is a ring isomorphism `R' ≃+* S_(f)`; it is an `R`-algebra
      -- isomorphism because it is compatible with the structure maps: the image
      -- of `r : R` in `R'` is sent to the image of `r` in `S_f` (which lies in the
      -- degree-`0` part `S_(f)`).  Since `S₀ = R` by (2), this is exactly the
      -- `R`-algebra compatibility `eR ∘ (R → R') = (R → S_(f))`.
      --
      -- `eM` is an additive isomorphism `M ≃+ N_(f)` to the faithfully-defined
      -- degree-`0` part `N_(f) = degZeroPart f N ℬ`.  It is semilinear over `eR`:
      -- `eM (r • m) = (eR r).val • eM m` inside `N_f`, where `S_(f)` acts via the
      -- embedding `HomogeneousLocalization.val : S_(f) → S_f`.  Together with the
      -- `R`-compatibility of `eR`, this expresses `M ≅ N_(f)` as `R' ≅ S_(f)`-modules.
      (∃ (eR : R' ≃+* HomogeneousLocalization.Away 𝒜 f)
         (eM : M ≃+ (degZeroPart f N ℬ)),
         (∀ r : R, (eR (algebraMap R R' r)).val
            = algebraMap S (Localization (Submonoid.powers f)) (algebraMap R S r)) ∧
         (∀ (r : R') (m : M),
           (eM (r • m) : LocalizedModule (Submonoid.powers f) N)
             = (eR r).val • (eM m : LocalizedModule (Submonoid.powers f) N)))

declarations.name: Stacks.Blowup.instGradedAlgebraReesGrading
declarations.doc:
**The Rees algebra is a graded algebra.** The ideal powers `Iⁿ`, placed in degree `n`,
decompose `R[It]`. This is the blowup algebra `Bl_I(R) = ⨁_{n ≥ 0} Iⁿ` of Stacks 052Q (1): the
`R`-algebra `reesAlgebra I` with this grading, whose degree-`n` part is `Iⁿ` by
`reesGradingEquivPow`.
declarations.statement: instance instGradedAlgebraReesGrading : GradedAlgebra (reesGrading I)
declarations.comment: (1) the blowup (Rees) algebra Bl_I(R) = ⨁ₙ Iⁿ as a graded R-algebra: `reesAlgebra I` graded by `reesGrading I`, degree n part ≅ Iⁿ (`reesGradingEquivPow`)

declarations.name: affineBlowupAlgebra
declarations.doc:
The affine blowup algebra `R[I/a]` of an ideal `I` of a ring `R` and an element `a : R`,
defined as the `R`-subalgebra of a localization `S` of `R` away from `a` generated by the
fractions `y/a` with `y ∈ I`. For `a ∈ I` its elements are exactly the fractions `x/aⁿ` with
`x ∈ Iⁿ`. For `a ∈ I` this is Stacks' `(Bl_I(R))_{(a⁽¹⁾)}`: the degree-zero part of the
localization of the graded Rees algebra at `a⁽¹⁾` is identified with it by
`Stacks.Blowup.reesAwayEquivAffineBlowup` and
`Stacks.AffineBlowup.affineBlowup_eq_affineBlowupAlgebra`. The graded Rees algebra itself, part
(1) of the definition, is `Stacks.Blowup.instGradedAlgebraReesGrading`.
declarations.statement:
public def affineBlowupAlgebra (I : Ideal R) (a : R) (S : Type*) [CommRing S] [Algebra R S]
    [IsLocalization.Away a S] : Subalgebra R S
declarations.comment: (2) the affine blowup algebra R[I/a], realized as the subalgebra of R_a generated by the y/a, y ∈ I; for a ∈ I identified with (Bl_I R)_(a^(1)) by `Stacks.Blowup.reesAwayEquivAffineBlowup`

declarations.name: affineBlowup_isDomain
declarations.doc:
If `R` is a domain, `I ⊆ R` an ideal, and `a ∈ I` is a nonzero element, then the affine
blowup algebra `R[I/a]` is a domain.
declarations.statement:
theorem affineBlowup_isDomain [IsDomain R] (ha : a ≠ 0) :
    IsDomain (affineBlowup I a)

declarations.name: isReduced_affineBlowup
declarations.doc: If `R` is reduced and `a ∈ I`, then the affine blowup algebra `R[I/a]` is reduced.
declarations.statement:
theorem isReduced_affineBlowup [IsReduced R] (ha : a ∈ I) :
    IsReduced (affineBlowupAlgebraAway I a)

declarations.name: PrimeSpectrum.denseRange_comap_of_notMem_minimalPrimes
declarations.doc:
**Blowing up is dominant.** Let `f : R →+* S` be a ring map and `a : R` an element such that
every element of the kernel of `f` is annihilated by a power of `a`. If `a` is contained in no
minimal prime of `R`, then `Spec S → Spec R` has dense image.

Applied to the affine blowup algebra `S = R[I/a]` of an ideal `I ∋ a` — whose structure map kills
exactly the `a`-power torsion of `R` — this is Stacks Tag 052T; see
`PrimeSpectrum.denseRange_comap_algebraMap_affineBlowupAlgebra`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem denseRange_comap_of_notMem_minimalPrimes {R S : Type*} [CommSemiring R]
    [CommSemiring S] (f : R →+* S) (a : R)
    (hker : ∀ x : R, f x = 0 → ∃ n : ℕ, a ^ n * x = 0)
    (ha : ∀ p ∈ minimalPrimes R, a ∉ p) :
    DenseRange (comap f)

declarations.name: PrimeSpectrum.denseRange_comap_algebraMap_affineBlowupAlgebra
declarations.doc:
**Blowing up is dominant.** Let `R` be a ring, `I ⊆ R` an ideal and `a : R`. If `a` is
contained in no minimal prime of `R`, then `Spec (R[I/a]) → Spec R` has dense image, where
`R[I/a] = affineBlowupAlgebra I a S` is the affine blowup algebra of `(R, I)` at `a`, realized
inside a localization `S` of `R` away from `a`.

The source assumes `a ∈ I`; the statement holds without it, since for arbitrary `a` the algebra
`affineBlowupAlgebra I a S` is the affine blowup algebra of `I + (a)` at `a`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem denseRange_comap_algebraMap_affineBlowupAlgebra {R : Type*} [CommRing R]
    (I : Ideal R) (a : R) (S : Type*) [CommRing S] [Algebra R S] [IsLocalization.Away a S]
    (ha : ∀ p ∈ minimalPrimes R, a ∉ p) :
    DenseRange (comap (algebraMap R (affineBlowupAlgebra I a S)))

declarations.name: PrimeSpectrum.forall_isOpen_of_isClosed_of_stableUnderGeneralization_iff_forall_projective
declarations.doc:
Let `R` be a commutative ring. Every closed subset of `Spec(R)` that is stable under
generalization is open if and only if every finite flat `R`-module is finite locally free, the
latter being spelled "finite projective" (Stacks 00NX (2) `⇔` (7)).
declarations.statement:
public theorem forall_isOpen_of_isClosed_of_stableUnderGeneralization_iff_forall_projective
    (R : Type u) [CommRing R] :
    (∀ Z : Set (PrimeSpectrum R), IsClosed Z → StableUnderGeneralization Z → IsOpen Z) ↔
      ∀ (M : Type u) [AddCommGroup M] [Module R M] [Module.Finite R M] [Module.Flat R M],
        Module.Projective R M
declarations.comment: Finite local freeness is spelled `Module.Projective`; see the module docstring.

declarations.name: Stacks.LocalizationOfFiniteAlgebra.essFiniteType_localization_finite
declarations.doc:
Let `f : (R, m_R) → (S, m_S)` be a local homomorphism of local rings. Assume `f` is
essentially of finite type, the residue field extension `κ(m_R) ⊆ κ(m_S)` is finite, and the
closed fiber `S / m_R S` has Krull dimension `0`. Then `S` is a localization of a finite
`R`-algebra: there exist a ring `S''`, a finite ring map `g : R →+* S''`, a submonoid `T ≤ S''`,
and a ring map `h : S'' →+* S` exhibiting `S` as the localization of `S''` at `T`, with
`h ∘ g = f` as `R`-algebra maps.
declarations.statement:
theorem essFiniteType_localization_finite {R S : Type u} [CommRing R] [CommRing S]
    [IsLocalRing R] [IsLocalRing S] (f : R →+* S) [IsLocalHom f]
    (hft : f.EssFiniteType)
    (hres : @Module.Finite (IsLocalRing.ResidueField R) (IsLocalRing.ResidueField S)
      _ _ (residueAlgebra f).toModule)
    (hdim : ringKrullDim (closedFiber f) = 0) :
    ∃ (S'' : Type u) (_ : CommRing S'') (g : R →+* S'') (h : S'' →+* S)
      (T : Submonoid S''),
      g.Finite ∧ h.comp g = f ∧ @IsLocalization S'' _ T S _ h.toAlgebra

declarations.name: Module.FlatAlongZeroLocus
declarations.doc:
An `S`-module `M` is flat over `R` along the inverse image of the zero
locus of an ideal `I` of `R` if the localization `M_q` is flat over `R` for every prime ideal `q`
of `S` containing the extension of `I`.
declarations.statement:
def Module.FlatAlongZeroLocus
    (R : Type u) (S : Type v) [CommRing R] [CommRing S] [Algebra R S]
    (I : Ideal R) (M : Type w) [AddCommGroup M] [Module R M] [Module S M]
    [IsScalarTower R S M] : Prop

declarations.name: Module.FlatAlongZeroLocus.baseChange
declarations.doc:
Let `T` be a pushout of maps of commutative rings `R → S` and `R → R'`.
If an `S`-module `M` is flat over `R` along the inverse image of the zero locus of `I`, and the
extension of `I` to `R'` is contained in `I'`, then `T ⊗[S] M` is flat over `R'` along the
inverse image of the zero locus of `I'`.
declarations.statement:
lemma Module.FlatAlongZeroLocus.baseChange
    (R : Type u) (S : Type v) (R' : Type w) (T : Type x)
    [CommRing R] [CommRing S] [CommRing R'] [CommRing T]
    [Algebra R S] [Algebra R R'] [Algebra R T] [Algebra S T] [Algebra R' T]
    [IsScalarTower R S T] [IsScalarTower R R' T] [Algebra.IsPushout R R' S T]
    (I : Ideal R) (I' : Ideal R')
    (M : Type*) [AddCommGroup M] [Module R M] [Module S M] [IsScalarTower R S M]
    (hI : I.map (algebraMap R R') ≤ I')
    (hM : Module.FlatAlongZeroLocus R S I M) :
    Module.FlatAlongZeroLocus R' T I' (TensorProduct S T M)

declarations.name: exists_monic_eq_X_sub_C_mul_of_isRoot
declarations.doc:
If `a` is a root of a monic polynomial `P`, then `P = (X - C a) * Q` for some monic
polynomial `Q`.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_monic_eq_X_sub_C_mul_of_isRoot {R : Type*} [CommRing R]
    {P : Polynomial R} (hP : P.Monic) {a : R} (ha : P.IsRoot a) :
    ∃ Q : Polynomial R, Q.Monic ∧ P = (Polynomial.X - Polynomial.C a) * Q

declarations.name: exists_finite_free_algebra_factor
declarations.doc:
For a monic polynomial `P` over `R` there is a finite free `R`-algebra `R'` over which the
image of `P` factors as `(X - C α) * Q`, with `Q` monic.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_finite_free_algebra_factor {R : Type u} [CommRing R]
    {P : Polynomial R} (hP : P.Monic) :
    ∃ (R' : Type u) (_ : CommRing R') (_ : Algebra R R')
      (_ : Module.Finite R R') (_ : Module.Free R R'),
      ∃ (α : R') (Q : Polynomial R'),
        Q.Monic ∧ P.map (algebraMap R R') = (Polynomial.X - Polynomial.C α) * Q

declarations.name: exists_finite_free_extension_quotient_split_polynomials
declarations.doc:
A finite algebra becomes a quotient by split univariate polynomials after an injective
finite free extension of its base ring.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_finite_free_extension_quotient_split_polynomials
    {R : Type u} [CommRing R] {S : Type v} [CommRing S]
    [Algebra R S] [Module.Finite R S] :
    ∃ (R' : Type u) (_ : CommRing R') (_ : Algebra R R')
      (_ : Module.Finite R R') (_ : Module.Free R R'),
      Function.Injective (algebraMap R R') ∧
        letI : Algebra R' (S ⊗[R] R') := Algebra.TensorProduct.rightAlgebra
        ∃ (n : ℕ) (d : Fin n → ℕ) (α : ∀ i, Fin (d i) → R')
          (f : (MvPolynomial (Fin n) R' ⧸
            Ideal.span (Set.range fun i : Fin n ↦
              ∏ j : Fin (d i), (MvPolynomial.X i - MvPolynomial.C (α i j))))
              →ₐ[R'] S ⊗[R] R'),
          Function.Surjective f

declarations.name: Stacks.Spectrum.PolynomialQuotientImage.range_comap_eq_zeroLocus_iInf_imageIdeal
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Tag 0532.** The image of the map `Spec(S) → Spec(R)` induced by the
structure map `R → S = R[T_1, …, T_n] / J` equals the closed set `V(⋂_{k ∈ K} J_k)`
cut out by the intersection of the image ideals.
declarations.statement:
theorem range_comap_eq_zeroLocus_iInf_imageIdeal
    (J : Ideal (MvPolynomial (Fin n) R))
    (hJ : ∀ i, factoredPoly d α i ∈ J) :
    Set.range (PrimeSpectrum.comap (structMap J)) =
      PrimeSpectrum.zeroLocus (R := R)
        ((⨅ k : (i : Fin n) → Fin (d i), imageIdeal d α k J) : Ideal R)

declarations.name: Module.finitePresentation_of_flat_of_localized
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Tag 053A.** Let `S = R[x₁, …, x_n]` and let `M` be a finite `S`-module which is flat
over `R`.  If finitely many prime localizations jointly detect elements of `R` and `M` is
finitely presented over `S` after localizing at every prime of `R`, then `M` is finitely
presented over `S`.
declarations.statement:
theorem Module.finitePresentation_of_flat_of_localized
    {R : Type u} [CommRing R] {n : ℕ} {M : Type v} [AddCommGroup M]
    [Module (MvPolynomial (Fin n) R) M] [Module R M]
    [IsScalarTower R (MvPolynomial (Fin n) R) M]
    (hprimes : HasFiniteDetectingPrimes R)
    [Module.Finite (MvPolynomial (Fin n) R) M] [Module.Flat R M]
    (hlocal : ∀ p : PrimeSpectrum R,
      Module.FinitePresentation
        (Localization (Algebra.algebraMapSubmonoid (MvPolynomial (Fin n) R)
          p.asIdeal.primeCompl))
        (LocalizedModule (Algebra.algebraMapSubmonoid (MvPolynomial (Fin n) R)
          p.asIdeal.primeCompl) M)) :
    Module.FinitePresentation (MvPolynomial (Fin n) R) M

declarations.name: Algebra.FinitePresentation.of_flat_of_localized
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Tag 053B.** Let `R → S` be a flat ring map of finite type.  Suppose finitely many
prime localizations jointly detect elements of `R`, and that for every prime `p` of `R` the
localization of `S` at `p` is finitely presented over `R` localized at `p`.  Then `S` is
finitely presented over `R`.
declarations.statement:
theorem Algebra.FinitePresentation.of_flat_of_localized
    {R : Type u} [CommRing R] {S : Type v} [CommRing S] [Algebra R S]
    (hprimes : HasFiniteDetectingPrimes R)
    [Algebra.FiniteType R S] [Module.Flat R S]
    (hlocal : ∀ p : PrimeSpectrum R,
      Algebra.FinitePresentation (Localization.AtPrime p.asIdeal)
        (Localization (Algebra.algebraMapSubmonoid S p.asIdeal.primeCompl))) :
    Algebra.FinitePresentation R S

declarations.name: finitePresentation_of_finite_flat_of_isLocalRing
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Tag 053C.** Let `R` be a local ring and let
`S = MvPolynomial (Fin n) R = R[x_1, ..., x_n]` be the graded polynomial algebra
with positive weights `w_i = deg(x_i) > 0`, graded by
`weightedHomogeneousSubmodule R w`.  Let `M` be a graded `S`-module, encoded by a
family of `R`-submodules `𝓜 : ℤ → Submodule R M` together with a compatible
graded scalar multiplication and a direct-sum decomposition.  If `M` is finite as
an `S`-module and flat as an `R`-module, then `M` is finitely presented as an
`S`-module.
declarations.statement:
theorem finitePresentation_of_finite_flat_of_isLocalRing
    (R : Type*) [CommRing R] [IsLocalRing R]
    (n : ℕ) (w : Fin n → ℤ) (hw : ∀ i, 0 < w i)
    (M : Type*) [AddCommGroup M] [Module (MvPolynomial (Fin n) R) M]
    -- `R` acts on `M` through the structure map `R → S` compatibly
    [Module R M] [IsScalarTower R (MvPolynomial (Fin n) R) M]
    -- the grading on `M` over `ℤ`, as a family of `R`-submodules
    (𝓜 : ℤ → Submodule R M)
    [SetLike.GradedSMul (weightedHomogeneousSubmodule R w) 𝓜]
    [DirectSum.Decomposition 𝓜]
    -- `M` is finite as an `S`-module
    [Module.Finite (MvPolynomial (Fin n) R) M]
    -- `M` is flat as an `R`-module
    [Module.Flat R M] :
    Module.FinitePresentation (MvPolynomial (Fin n) R) M

declarations.name: finitePresentation_of_flat_of_finiteType_of_finite_degreeZero
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Tag 053D.** Let `S = ⨁_d 𝒜 d` be a nonnegatively graded `R`-algebra of finite type
whose degree-zero part is finite over `R`, and suppose a finite family of prime localizations
jointly detects elements of `R`.  Then an `R`-flat `S` is finitely presented as an `R`-algebra,
and every finite graded `S`-module which is flat over `R` is finitely presented as an
`S`-module.
declarations.statement:
theorem finitePresentation_of_flat_of_finiteType_of_finite_degreeZero
    {R : Type u} {S : Type v} {M : Type w} [CommRing R] [CommRing S]
    [AddCommGroup M] [Algebra R S] [Module S M] [Module R M] [IsScalarTower R S M]
    (𝒜 : ℕ → Submodule R S) [GradedAlgebra 𝒜]
    (ℳ : ℤ → Submodule R M) [SetLike.GradedSMul 𝒜 ℳ] [DirectSum.Decomposition ℳ]
    [Algebra.FiniteType R S] [Module.Finite R (𝒜 0)]
    (hprimes : HasFiniteDetectingPrimes R) :
    (Module.Flat R S → Algebra.FinitePresentation R S) ∧
      (Module.Flat R M → Module.Finite S M → Module.FinitePresentation S M)

declarations.name: finitePresentation_of_flat_of_finiteType_of_valuationRing
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Tag 053E (Nagata).** Let `A` be a valuation ring, `B` an `A`-algebra of finite type,
and `M` a `B`-module.  If `B` is flat over `A`, then `B` is finitely presented as an
`A`-algebra.  If `M` is finite over `B` and flat over `A`, then `M` is finitely presented as a
`B`-module.
declarations.statement:
theorem finitePresentation_of_flat_of_finiteType_of_valuationRing
    {A : Type u} {B : Type v} {M : Type w} [CommRing A] [IsDomain A] [ValuationRing A]
    [CommRing B] [Algebra A B] [Algebra.FiniteType A B] [AddCommGroup M] [Module B M]
    [Module A M] [IsScalarTower A B M] :
    (Module.Flat A B → Algebra.FinitePresentation A B) ∧
      (Module.Flat A M → Module.Finite B M → Module.FinitePresentation B M)

declarations.name: strictTransform
declarations.doc:
The strict transform of an `R`-module `M` along the affine blowup algebra `R → R[I/a]`:
the scalar extension `R[I/a] ⊗[R] M`, modulo the elements annihilated by some power of the
image of `a`.

noncomputable def strictTransform (I : Ideal R) (a : R) [Fact (a ∈ I)]
    (M : Type v) [AddCommGroup M] [Module R M]

declarations.name: Stacks.Flatness.BlowupFlattening.stacks053I
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Tag 053I: flattening by blowing up.** Let `(R, 𝔪)` be a local domain with fraction
field `K` and `𝔪 ≠ 0`, let `S` be a finite type `R`-algebra, let `M` be a finite `S`-module and
let `A ⊆ K` be a valuation ring dominating `R`.  Then there is an admissible affine blowup chart
`R[I/a]` — so `I ⊆ 𝔪` is finitely generated, the fibre ring of `R → R[I/a]` at `𝔪` is nonzero and
`A` has center on `R[I/a]` — on which the strict transform of `S` is flat and of finite
presentation over `R[I/a]` and the strict transform of `M` is flat over `R[I/a]` and finitely
presented over the strict transform of `S`.

The polynomial case is `Stacks.Flatness.BlowupFlattening.exists_admissiblePair_mvPolynomial`.  The
  reduction to it is
the source's first step: write `S` as a quotient of `P = R[x_1, …, x_n]` and apply the polynomial
case to the `P`-module `N = S ⊕ M`.  The strict transform of `N` is the product of the strict
transforms of `S` and of `M` (`Stacks.Flatness.BlowupFlattening.prodLinearEquiv`, the version of
`strictTransform.prodEquiv` that is linear over the strict transform of `P`), so flatness and
finite presentation of each summand follow from `Module.Flat.prod_iff` and
`Module.FinitePresentation.prod_iff`.  Finite presentation of the strict transform of `S` as an
`R[I/a]`-*algebra* is then
`Algebra.FinitePresentation.of_surjective_of_module_finitePresentation`, and finite presentation
of the strict transform of `M` over the strict transform of `S` is Stacks Tag 0561,
`Module.FinitePresentation.of_restrictScalars_of_finiteType`.

The statement deviates from the source in two ways: the
hypothesis `𝔪 ≠ 0`, without which the conclusion is unsatisfiable, and clause (4) being read over
`R[I/a]` rather than over `R`.
declarations.statement:
theorem stacks053I (hdom : Dominates R A) (hm : IsLocalRing.maximalIdeal R ≠ ⊥) (S : Type w)
    [CommRing S] [Algebra R S] [Algebra.FiniteType R S] (M : Type uM) [AddCommGroup M]
    [Module S M] [Module R M] [IsScalarTower R S M] [Module.Finite S M] :
    Stacks053IConclusion R A S M

declarations.name: IsLocalRing.exists_finite_faithfullyFlat_forall_isMaximal_isLocalHom_comp_eq
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 053K.** Let `(R, m_R) → (S, m_S)` be a local homomorphism of local rings such that
`S` is the localization of an étale `R`-algebra `T` at a prime `q`. Then there is a finite,
finitely presented, faithfully flat `R`-algebra `S'` such that for every maximal ideal `m'` of
`S'` the canonical map `R → S'_{m'}` factors as `R → S → S'_{m'}`, with `S → S'_{m'}` a local
homomorphism.
declarations.statement:
public theorem IsLocalRing.exists_finite_faithfullyFlat_forall_isMaximal_isLocalHom_comp_eq
    (R : Type u) [CommRing R] [IsLocalRing R] (S : Type v) [CommRing S] [IsLocalRing S]
    [Algebra R S] [IsLocalHom (algebraMap R S)] (T : Type w) [CommRing T] [Algebra R T]
    [Algebra.Etale R T] [Algebra T S] [IsScalarTower R T S] (q : Ideal T) [q.IsPrime]
    [IsLocalization.AtPrime S q] :
    ∃ (S' : Type u) (_ : CommRing S') (_ : Algebra R S') (_ : Module.Finite R S')
      (_ : Algebra.FinitePresentation R S') (_ : Module.FaithfullyFlat R S'),
      ∀ (m' : Ideal S') (_ : m'.IsMaximal) (A : Type x) (_ : CommRing A) (_ : Algebra S' A)
        (_ : IsLocalization.AtPrime A m'), ∃ (ψ : S →+* A) (_ : IsLocalHom ψ),
          ψ.comp (algebraMap R S) = (algebraMap S' A).comp (algebraMap R S')
declarations.comment:
The étale algebra `T` and the prime `q` presenting `S` are hypotheses rather than an
existential, as in Lemma 0GSD. `R → S'` is `Module.Finite`, `Algebra.FinitePresentation` and
`Module.FaithfullyFlat`; `S'_{m'}` is an arbitrary localization of `S'` at `m'`; the factorization
is pinned by an equation with the canonical map `R → S'_{m'}`, and the factoring map is required to
be local, as in the source's proof. See the module docstring.

declarations.name: ColimCategory.objEquiv
declarations.doc:
The type of *objects* of `I^u_V` is exactly the comprehension
`{(U, φ) | U : Ob C, φ : V ⟶ u U}`, formalized as the dependent pair type
`Σ U : C, (V ⟶ u U)`.
declarations.statement: def objEquiv : I u V ≃ Σ U : C, (V ⟶ u.obj U)
declarations.comment: Ob

declarations.name: ColimCategory.homEquiv
declarations.doc:
The type of *morphisms* in `I^u_V` from `(U, φ)` to `(U', φ')` is exactly the comprehension
`{f : U ⟶ U' | u f ∘ φ = φ'}`, formalized as the subtype of morphisms `f : U ⟶ U'` satisfying
`φ ≫ u f = φ'` (note the diagrammatic-order composition in Mathlib).
declarations.statement:
def homEquiv (X Y : I u V) :
    (X ⟶ Y) ≃ { f : X.right ⟶ Y.right // X.hom ≫ u.map f = Y.hom }
declarations.comment: Mor

declarations.doc:
A point above a point closed in its fibre remains closed in its fibre after

public theorem isClosed_asFiber_of_isPullback

    {f' : X' ⟶ S'} {g' : X' ⟶ X} [LocallyOfFiniteType f]

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.Modules.forall_isFiniteLocallyFree_iff_forall_isOpen
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 053N.** For a scheme `X` the following are equivalent: every
quasi-coherent `𝒪_X`-module of finite type which is flat is finite locally free; every closed
subset of `X` stable under generalization is open.
declarations.statement:
theorem forall_isFiniteLocallyFree_iff_forall_isOpen (X : Scheme.{u}) :
    (∀ F : X.Modules, _root_.SheafOfModules.IsFiniteType.{u, u, u} F → F.IsQuasicoherent →
        AlgebraicGeometry.SheafOfModules.IsFlat
            (C := TopologicalSpace.Opens X.toTopCat)
            (J := Opens.grothendieckTopology X.toTopCat) (O := X.sheaf) F →
          AlgebraicGeometry.SheafOfModules.IsFiniteLocallyFree.{u, u, u}
            (R := X.ringCatSheaf) F) ↔
      ∀ Z : Set X, IsClosed Z → StableUnderGeneralization Z → IsOpen Z

declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 053P.** The inverse image of a locally principal closed subscheme is
locally principal.
