    (I : Y.IdealSheafData)
    (hI : IsLocallyPrincipal I) :
    IsLocallyPrincipal (I.comap f)

declarations.name: Stacks.Divisors.fiber_support_eq_union_irreducibleComponents_general
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 053R.** Let `f : X ⟶ S` be a dominant morphism locally of finite type between
irreducible schemes, let `I` be a locally principal ideal sheaf on `X` whose closed subscheme
misses the generic fibre of `f`, and let `s` be a point of `S` whose fibre has dimension at most
that of the generic fibre. Then the support of the closed subscheme inside the fibre `X_s` is
set-theoretically the union of the irreducible components of `X_s` that it contains.

No Noetherian hypothesis: the Noetherian case
`Stacks.Divisors.fiber_support_eq_union_irreducibleComponents` is applied not to `f` but to a
finitely generated `ℤ`-algebra that the affine situation descends to, in
`Stacks.Divisors.fiber_preimage_zeroLocus_eq_sUnion_irreducibleComponents`. The two reductions in
front of that are
`Stacks.Divisors.fiber_support_eq_union_irreducibleComponents_of_isIntegral`, which passes to the
reductions of `X` and `S` and so makes both integral, and
`Stacks.Divisors.fiber_support_eq_union_irreducibleComponents_integral`, which localises to an
affine chart on which `I` is principal.
declarations.statement:
public theorem fiber_support_eq_union_irreducibleComponents_general {X S : Scheme.{u}}
    (f : X ⟶ S) [IrreducibleSpace S] [IrreducibleSpace X] [IsDominant f] [LocallyOfFiniteType f]
    (I : X.IdealSheafData) (hI : IsLocallyPrincipal I)
    (hgeneric : IsEmpty ((I.subschemeι ≫ f).fiber (genericPoint S))) (s : S)
    (hdim : topologicalKrullDim (f.fiber s) ≤ topologicalKrullDim (f.fiber (genericPoint S))) :
    (f.fiberι s) ⁻¹' (I.support : Set X) =
      ⋃₀ {C : Set (f.fiber s) | C ∈ irreducibleComponents (f.fiber s) ∧
        C ⊆ (f.fiberι s) ⁻¹' (I.support : Set X)}

declarations.name: Stacks.Divisors.fiber_support_eq_union_irreducibleComponents
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 053R, the Noetherian case.** Let `f : X ⟶ S` be a dominant morphism locally of
finite type between irreducible schemes with `X` locally Noetherian, let `I` be a locally
principal ideal sheaf on `X` whose closed subscheme misses the generic fibre, and let `s ∈ S` be
a point whose fibre has dimension at most that of the generic fibre. Then the support of the
closed subscheme inside `f.fiber s` is set-theoretically the union of the irreducible components
of `f.fiber s` that it contains.
declarations.statement:
public theorem fiber_support_eq_union_irreducibleComponents {X S : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ S)
    [IrreducibleSpace S] [IrreducibleSpace X] [IsDominant f] [LocallyOfFiniteType f]
    [IsLocallyNoetherian X] (I : X.IdealSheafData) (hI : IsLocallyPrincipal I)
    (hgeneric : IsEmpty ((I.subschemeι ≫ f).fiber (genericPoint S))) (s : S)
    (hdim : topologicalKrullDim (f.fiber s) ≤
      topologicalKrullDim (f.fiber (genericPoint S))) :
    (f.fiberι s) ⁻¹' (I.support : Set X) =
      ⋃₀ {C : Set (f.fiber s) | C ∈ irreducibleComponents (f.fiber s) ∧
        C ⊆ (f.fiberι s) ⁻¹' (I.support : Set X)}
declarations.comment:
the locally Noetherian case, the form in which Krull's principal ideal theorem
applies to `f` directly. The statement without `[IsLocallyNoetherian X]`, which is the source's
own, is `Stacks.Divisors.fiber_support_eq_union_irreducibleComponents_general` in
`StacksFrontier/AlgebraicGeometry/FibreDimension/GeneralCase.lean:352`; it applies this one to a
finitely generated ℤ-algebra that the affine situation descends to, by
`StacksFrontier.AlgebraicGeometry.FibreDimension.AffineGeneralCase`.

declarations.name: IsLocalRing.injective_quotient_of_dimension_add_trdeg_eq
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 053S.** Let `A ⊆ B` be an injective local homomorphism of local domains with `B`
essentially of finite type over `A`, and let `g ∈ 𝔪_B` lie in no minimal prime over `𝔪_A B`. If
`dim (B/𝔪_A B) + trdeg_{κ(𝔪_A)} κ(𝔪_B) = trdeg_A B`, then `A → B/gB` is injective, i.e. the
generic point of `Spec A` is in the image of `Spec (B/gB) → Spec A`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem injective_quotient_of_dimension_add_trdeg_eq
    {A B : Type u} [CommRing A] [CommRing B] [IsDomain A] [IsDomain B]
    [IsLocalRing A] [IsLocalRing B] [Algebra A B]
    [IsLocalHom (algebraMap A B)]
    (hinj : Function.Injective (algebraMap A B))
    (hB : IsEssentiallyOfFiniteType A B (algebraMap A B))
    (g : B) (hg : g ∈ maximalIdeal B)
    (hnot : ∀ q ∈ (Ideal.map (algebraMap A B) (maximalIdeal A)).minimalPrimes, g ∉ q)
    (hdim : letI := (ResidueField.map (algebraMap A B)).toAlgebra;
      ringKrullDim (B ⧸ Ideal.map (algebraMap A B) (maximalIdeal A)) +
        (Cardinal.toENat (Algebra.trdeg (ResidueField A) (ResidueField B)) :
          WithBot ℕ∞) =
      (Cardinal.toENat (Algebra.trdeg A B) : WithBot ℕ∞)) :
    Function.Injective ((Ideal.Quotient.mk (Ideal.span {g})).comp (algebraMap A B))

declarations.name: IsLocalRing.ringKrullDim_closedFiber_add_trdeg_eq_trdeg
declarations.doc:
The dimension of the closed fibre of an injective flat essentially finite type local
extension of domains, plus the residue-field transcendence degree, is the transcendence
degree of the extension.
declarations.statement:
public theorem ringKrullDim_closedFiber_add_trdeg_eq_trdeg
    {A B : Type u} [CommRing A] [CommRing B] [IsDomain A] [IsDomain B]
    [IsLocalRing A] [IsLocalRing B] [Algebra A B]
    [IsLocalHom (algebraMap A B)]
    (hinj : Function.Injective (algebraMap A B))
    (hfinite : IsEssentiallyOfFiniteType A B (algebraMap A B))
    [Module.Flat A B] :
    letI := (IsLocalRing.ResidueField.map (algebraMap A B)).toAlgebra
    ringKrullDim (B ⧸ (IsLocalRing.maximalIdeal A).map (algebraMap A B)) +
      (Cardinal.toENat (Algebra.trdeg (IsLocalRing.ResidueField A)
        (IsLocalRing.ResidueField B)) : WithBot ℕ∞) =
      (Cardinal.toENat (Algebra.trdeg A B) : WithBot ℕ∞)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.closure_closedPoints_between_fiber_eq_iff
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 053U**, under the hypotheses of the tag and no others. Let `f : X ⟶ S` be locally
of finite type, let `x ⤳ x'` be a specialization in `X` with `x'` closed in its fibre
`X_{f x'}`, and set `s = f x`. Then the points of `X_s` which are closed in `X_s` and lie
between `x` and `x'` are dense in the closure of `x` in `X_s` if and only if `x = x'` or
`f x ≠ f x'`.

The reverse implication is the assertion of the tag and carries its mathematical content: it is
`AlgebraicGeometry.closure_closedPoints_between_fiber_eq`, proved by the argument of the source.

The forward implication settles the one remaining situation, a nontrivial specialization inside
one fibre, where the density fails: a point of `X_s` closed in `X_s` which specializes to `x'`
*is* `x'`, so the set of the tag is `{x'}`, whose closure is `{x'}`, while the closure of `x` in
`X_s` is larger whenever `x ≠ x'` — for `X = 𝔸¹` over a field with `x` its generic point and
`x'` a closed point it is all of `𝔸¹`. The implication is exactly that computation, through
`AlgebraicGeometry.closure_closedPoints_between_fiber_subset_singleton_of_eq_base`. Since the
source relates `f x` and `f x'` by no hypothesis, its statement overreaches there; its proof
does not, drawing the same line at the prime-avoidance step (see the module docstring).
declarations.statement:
public theorem closure_closedPoints_between_fiber_eq_iff
    {X S : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ S) [LocallyOfFiniteType f]
    (x x' : X) (hxx' : x ⤳ x')
    (hx' : IsClosed ({f.asFiber x'} : Set (f.fiber (f x')))) :
    closure {y : f.fiber (f x) |
          IsClosed ({y} : Set (f.fiber (f x))) ∧
            x ⤳ ((f.fiberι (f x)) y) ∧
              ((f.fiberι (f x)) y) ⤳ x'} =
        closure ({f.asFiber x} : Set (f.fiber (f x))) ↔
      x = x' ∨ f x ≠ f x'
declarations.comment: the density conclusion of the tag, under the tag's own hypotheses — `f` locally of finite type, `x ⤳ x'`, `x'` closed in `X_{f x'}` — together with its exact range of validity: the points of `X_s` closed in `X_s` and lying between `x` and `x'` are dense in the closure of `x` in `X_s` if and only if `x = x'` or `f x ≠ f x'`. The reverse implication is the tag itself, proved by the argument of the source in `closure_closedPoints_between_fiber_eq`; the forward implication disposes of the only remaining situation, a nontrivial specialization inside one fibre, where the tag's set is the single closed point `x'` and the density is false — a gap in the source's statement, computed in `closure_closedPoints_between_fiber_subset_singleton_of_eq_base` and respected by the source's own proof.

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.exists_chain_isImmediateSpecialization_isClosed_fiber
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 053V**, the chain of immediate specializations inside the fibre, together with the
avoidance clause. For `f` locally of finite type and `W` a closed subset of the fibre `X_{f x}`
not containing `x`, there is a chain

`x = c 0 ⤳ c 1 ⤳ ⋯ ⤳ c d`

of `d = natTrdegFiber f x` immediate specializations inside `X_{f x}`, avoiding `W`, whose last
term is a closed point of `X_{f x}`.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_chain_isImmediateSpecialization_isClosed_fiber
    (f : X ⟶ S) [LocallyOfFiniteType f] (x : X)
    {W : Set (f.fiber (f x))} (hW : IsClosed W) (hxW : f.asFiber x ∉ W) :
    ∃ c : Fin (natTrdegFiber f x + 1) → f.fiber (f x),
      c 0 = f.asFiber x ∧
      (∀ i : Fin (natTrdegFiber f x),
        IsImmediateSpecialization (c i.castSucc) (c i.succ)) ∧
      IsClosed ({c (Fin.last (natTrdegFiber f x))} : Set (f.fiber (f x))) ∧
      ∀ i, c i ∉ W
declarations.comment:
the chain of immediate specializations inside the fibre, of length `d`, ending in
a closed point of the fibre, together with the avoidance clause, and with nothing assumed about
a prescribed `x'`. The final link `x_d ⤳ x'` to a prescribed `x'` with `x ⤳ x'` closed in its
own fibre is not in this file, which never mentions `x'`; it is
`AlgebraicGeometry.exists_chain_isImmediateSpecialization_specializes_fiber_of_isClosed` in
`StacksFrontier.AlgebraicGeometry.Morphisms.Fibres.SpecializationChainToClosedSpecialization`,
where `AlgebraicGeometry.exists_chain_isImmediateSpecialization_specializes_fiber_iff` states
every assertion of the remark at once, at the hypotheses of the tag, together with the exact
range of validity of the remark.

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.natTrdegFiber_eq_topologicalKrullDim_closure
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 053V**, the identity `d = dim(closure of {x})`, the closure being taken in the
fibre `X_{f x}`.
declarations.statement:
theorem natTrdegFiber_eq_topologicalKrullDim_closure (f : X ⟶ S) [LocallyOfFiniteType f]
    (x : X) :
    ((natTrdegFiber f x : ℕ∞) : WithBot ℕ∞) =
      topologicalKrullDim (closure ({f.asFiber x} : Set (f.fiber (f x))))
declarations.comment: the equality of `d` with the dimension of the closure of `x` in the fibre

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.natTrdegFiber_eq_toNat_trdeg_residueField
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 053V**, the identity `d = trdeg_{κ(s)}(κ(x))`: the integer produced by
`AlgebraicGeometry.natTrdegFiber` is the transcendence degree of the residue field of `X` at `x`
over the residue field of `S` at `s = f x`.
declarations.statement:
theorem natTrdegFiber_eq_toNat_trdeg_residueField (f : X ⟶ S) (x : X) :
    letI := (f.residueFieldMap x).hom.toAlgebra
    natTrdegFiber f x =
      Cardinal.toNat (Algebra.trdeg (S.residueField (f x)) (X.residueField x))
declarations.comment:
the equality of the length `d` of the chain with the transcendence degree
`trdeg_{κ(s)}(κ(x))`

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.exists_chain_isImmediateSpecialization_specializes_fiber_of_isClosed
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 053V without its avoidance clause**, and with no hypothesis added to the tag. For
`f` locally of finite type and `x ⤳ x'` with `x'` closed in its own fibre there is a chain

`x = c 0 ⤳ c 1 ⤳ ⋯ ⤳ c d`

of `d = natTrdegFiber f x` immediate specializations inside `X_{f x}` whose last term is a closed
point of `X_{f x}` specializing to `x'`.

This needs no non-degeneracy hypothesis because the point to walk down to can be produced without
Stacks 053U when `x'` already lies in the fibre of `x`: it is then `x'` itself. It is the
avoidance clause that fails in that case, which is why the remark as a whole is registered on
the equivalence
`AlgebraicGeometry.exists_chain_isImmediateSpecialization_specializes_fiber_iff` above.
declarations.statement:
public theorem exists_chain_isImmediateSpecialization_specializes_fiber_of_isClosed
    (f : X ⟶ S) [LocallyOfFiniteType f] (x x' : X) (hxx' : x ⤳ x')
    (hx' : IsClosed ({f.asFiber x'} : Set (f.fiber (f x')))) :
    ∃ c : Fin (natTrdegFiber f x + 1) → f.fiber (f x),
      c 0 = f.asFiber x ∧
      (∀ i : Fin (natTrdegFiber f x),
        IsImmediateSpecialization (c i.castSucc) (c i.succ)) ∧
      IsClosed ({c (Fin.last (natTrdegFiber f x))} : Set (f.fiber (f x))) ∧
      f.fiberι (f x) (c (Fin.last (natTrdegFiber f x))) ⤳ x'
declarations.comment: the chain of immediate specializations inside the fibre, of length `d`, ending in a closed point of the fibre which specializes to the prescribed `x'` — unconditionally, the avoidance clause aside. The remark as a whole, avoidance clause included, is `AlgebraicGeometry.exists_chain_isImmediateSpecialization_specializes_fiber_iff` above, which states it at the hypotheses of the tag together with its exact range of validity

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.exists_chain_isImmediateSpecialization_specializes_fiber_iff
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 053V, under the hypotheses of the tag and no others.** Let `f : X ⟶ S` be locally
of finite type, let `x ⤳ x'` be a specialization in `X` with `x'` closed in its own fibre
`X_{f x'}`, and write `d = natTrdegFiber f x`. Then the remark holds — for *every* closed subset
`W` of the fibre `X_{f x}` not containing `x` there is a chain

`x = c 0 ⤳ c 1 ⤳ ⋯ ⤳ c d ⤳ x'`

whose first `d` steps are immediate specializations inside `X_{f x}`, which avoids `W`, and whose
last term `c d` is a closed point of `X_{f x}` — if and only if `x = x'` or `f x ≠ f x'`.

The reverse implication is the assertion of the remark and carries its mathematical content: it
is `AlgebraicGeometry.exists_chain_isImmediateSpecialization_specializes_fiber`, which runs the
argument of the source.

The forward implication settles the one remaining situation, a nontrivial specialization inside
one fibre, where the remark fails. If `f x = f x'` then `x'` is a point `z` of `X_{f x}`, closed
there, so `{z}` is a closed subset of `X_{f x}`; were `x ≠ x'` it would not contain `x`, hence
would be a legitimate set to avoid, and the chain avoiding it would end in a point of `X_{f x}`,
closed there, specializing to `x'` and different from `z`. But a point of a fibre closed in that
fibre is the only point of the fibre it specializes to
(`AlgebraicGeometry.eq_of_fiberι_specializes_of_isClosed`), so that last term is `z` after all.
For `X = 𝔸¹` over a field, `x` its generic point and `x'` a closed point, every hypothesis of
the remark holds and its conclusion is therefore false. This is the gap inherited from
Stacks 053U, whose density conclusion supplies the point to walk down to and which is stated
with the same range of validity in
`AlgebraicGeometry.closure_closedPoints_between_fiber_eq_iff`; the source's own proof draws the
same line, at the prime-avoidance step (see the module docstring).

The closed set to be avoided is quantified inside the existence statement because that is where
the source puts it: the points `x_i` can be chosen to avoid *any* closed subset of `X_s` not
containing `x`. Fixing a single `W` instead would make the equivalence false, `W = ∅` being
avoided by a chain in every configuration.
declarations.statement:
public theorem exists_chain_isImmediateSpecialization_specializes_fiber_iff
    (f : X ⟶ S) [LocallyOfFiniteType f] (x x' : X) (hxx' : x ⤳ x')
    (hx' : IsClosed ({f.asFiber x'} : Set (f.fiber (f x')))) :
    (∀ W : Set (f.fiber (f x)), IsClosed W → f.asFiber x ∉ W →
        ∃ c : Fin (natTrdegFiber f x + 1) → f.fiber (f x),
          c 0 = f.asFiber x ∧
          (∀ i : Fin (natTrdegFiber f x),
            IsImmediateSpecialization (c i.castSucc) (c i.succ)) ∧
          IsClosed ({c (Fin.last (natTrdegFiber f x))} : Set (f.fiber (f x))) ∧
          f.fiberι (f x) (c (Fin.last (natTrdegFiber f x))) ⤳ x' ∧
          ∀ i, c i ∉ W) ↔
      x = x' ∨ f x ≠ f x'
declarations.comment: EVERY assertion of the remark at once — the chain of `d` immediate specializations inside the fibre, its last term closed in the fibre, the final link `x_d ⤳ x'`, the avoidance of any closed subset of the fibre which misses `x`, and `d = natTrdegFiber f x` — under the tag's own hypotheses, namely `f` locally of finite type, `x ⤳ x'` and `x'` closed in `X_{f x'}`, together with its exact range of validity: all of that holds if and only if `x = x'` or `f x ≠ f x'`. The reverse implication is the remark itself, by the argument of the source in `exists_chain_isImmediateSpecialization_specializes_fiber`; the forward implication disposes of the one remaining situation, a nontrivial specialization inside a single fibre, where `{x'}` is a closed subset of the fibre missing `x` which the last term of the chain cannot avoid, since a closed point specializing to `x'` is `x'`. That is the gap inherited from Stacks 053U, recorded there in `closure_closedPoints_between_fiber_eq_iff`, and respected by the source's own proof.

declarations.name: main_theorem053W
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 053W**.
For a finite covering `V : Fin m → Set X` of `X` by retrocompact open subsets, a subset
`E ⊆ X` is constructible in `X` if and only if `E ∩ V j` is constructible in `V j` for
every `j`.
declarations.statement:
theorem main_theorem053W
    {X : Type*} [TopologicalSpace X]
    {m : ℕ} (V : Fin m → Set X)
    (hVopen : ∀ j, IsOpen (V j))
    (hVretro : ∀ j, IsRetrocompact (V j))
    (hVcover : ⋃ j, V j = Set.univ)
    (E : Set X) :
    IsConstructibleIn E ↔ ∀ j, IsConstructibleInSubspace E (V j)

declarations.name: isConstructibleSet_preimage
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 053Y.** Let `f : X → Y` be a continuous map from a Noetherian topological space. If
`E ⊆ Y` is constructible in `Y`, then `f ⁻¹' E` is constructible in `X`: preimages preserve opens,
and retrocompactness is automatic in a Noetherian space.
declarations.statement:
theorem isConstructibleSet_preimage
    {X Y : Type*} [TopologicalSpace X] [TopologicalSpace Y]
    [TopologicalSpace.NoetherianSpace X]
    {f : X → Y} (hf : Continuous f) {E : Set Y}
    (hE : Topology.IsConstructible E) :
    Topology.IsConstructible (f ⁻¹' E)

declarations.name: constructible_iff_dichotomy_irreducible_closed
declarations.doc:
Let `X` be a Noetherian topological space and let `E ⊆ X`. Then `E` is
constructible if and only if for every irreducible closed `Z ⊆ X` the intersection `E ∩ Z` either
contains a nonempty open of `Z` or fails to be dense in `Z`.
declarations.statement:
theorem constructible_iff_dichotomy_irreducible_closed
    [TopologicalSpace.NoetherianSpace X] (E : Set X) :
    IsConstructibleSet E ↔
      ∀ Z : Set X, IsIrreducible Z → IsClosed Z →
        ContainsNonemptyOpenOf E Z ∨ ¬ IsDenseIn E Z

declarations.name: Topology.IsConstructible.mem_nhds_iff_forall_subset_closure_inter
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0540.** In a Noetherian topological space, a constructible subset `E` is a
neighbourhood of a point `x` if and only if `E ∩ Y` is dense in `Y` for every irreducible closed
subset `Y` containing `x`.

declarations.name: Topology.isOpen_iff_inter_irreducible_closed
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0541.** A subset `E` of a Noetherian topological space is open if and only if, for
every irreducible closed subset `Y`, the intersection `E ∩ Y` is empty or contains a nonempty
open subset of `Y`, that is, a set `V ∩ Y` with `V` open in `X` and `V ∩ Y` nonempty.
declarations.statement:
theorem isOpen_iff_inter_irreducible_closed [NoetherianSpace X] (E : Set X) :
    IsOpen E ↔ ∀ Y : Set X, IsClosed Y → IsIrreducible Y →
      E ∩ Y = ∅ ∨ ∃ V : Set X, IsOpen V ∧ (V ∩ Y).Nonempty ∧ V ∩ Y ⊆ E

declarations.name: isOpen_of_stableUnderGeneralization_of_isConstructible
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0542** (2).
In a Noetherian sober topological space, every constructible subset that is stable under
generalization is open.
declarations.statement:
theorem isOpen_of_stableUnderGeneralization_of_isConstructible
    (X : Type u) [TopologicalSpace X] [NoetherianSpace X] [QuasiSober X] [T0Space X]
    (E : Set X) (hcon : Topology.IsConstructible E) (hgen : StableUnderGeneralization E) :
    IsOpen E

declarations.name: isClosed_of_stableUnderSpecialization_of_isConstructible
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0542** (1).
In a Noetherian sober topological space, every constructible subset that is stable under
specialization is closed.
declarations.statement:
theorem isClosed_of_stableUnderSpecialization_of_isConstructible
    (X : Type u) [TopologicalSpace X] [NoetherianSpace X] [QuasiSober X] [T0Space X]
    (E : Set X) (hcon : Topology.IsConstructible E) (hspec : StableUnderSpecialization E) :
    IsClosed E

declarations.name: Ideal.IsLocallyNilpotent0544.map
declarations.doc:
If `R → R'` is a ring map and `I ⊂ R` is a locally nilpotent ideal, then
the extended ideal `IR' = I.map f` is locally nilpotent in `R'`.
declarations.statement:
theorem Ideal.IsLocallyNilpotent0544.map
    {R R' : Type*} [CommRing R] [CommRing R']
    (f : R →+* R') (I : Ideal R)
    (hI : Ideal.IsLocallyNilpotent0544 I) :
    Ideal.IsLocallyNilpotent0544 (I.map f)

declarations.name: Stacks.UniversalHomeomorphism.FrobeniusPowerSubring.exists_pow_mem
declarations.doc:
Let `p` be a prime number and `n, m > 0`. Then there is an `a` such that both
`(x + y) ^ p ^ a` and `p ^ a (x + y)` lie in `R = ℤ[x ^ p ^ n, p ^ n x, y ^ p ^ m, p ^ m y]`,
where `x = X 0` and `y = X 1`.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_pow_mem (p : ℕ) (hp : p.Prime) (n m : ℕ) (hn : 0 < n) (hm : 0 < m) :
    ∃ a : ℕ, (X 0 + X 1 : MvPolynomial (Fin 2) ℤ) ^ p ^ a ∈ subringR p n m ∧
      (p ^ a : ℤ) • (X 0 + X 1 : MvPolynomial (Fin 2) ℤ) ∈ subringR p n m

declarations.name: IsWeaklyAssociatedPrime
declarations.doc:
A prime ideal `I` of `R` is *weakly associated* to the `R`-module `M` if `I` is minimal among
the prime ideals containing the annihilator `(R ∙ m).annihilator` of some element `m ∈ M`.
declarations.statement: def IsWeaklyAssociatedPrime (I : Ideal R) : Prop
declarations.comment: predicate

declarations.name: weaklyAssociatedPrimes
declarations.doc: The set of weakly associated primes of `M` (over `R`).
declarations.statement: def weaklyAssociatedPrimes : Set (Ideal R)
declarations.comment: set

declarations.name: Module.weaklyAssociatedPrimes_subset_of_injective
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0548**, first inclusion. Let `R` be a ring and let `f : M →ₗ[R] M'` be an injective
map of `R`-modules. Then `WeakAss(M) ⊆ WeakAss(M')`, where `WeakAss(N)` is the set of primes of `R`
minimal over the annihilator of an element of `N`.

declarations.name: Module.weaklyAssociatedPrimes_subset_union_of_exact
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0548**, second inclusion. Let `R` be a ring and let `0 → M → M' → M''` be an exact
sequence of `R`-modules, i.e. `f : M →ₗ[R] M'` is injective with image the kernel of
`g : M' →ₗ[R] M''`. Then `WeakAss(M') ⊆ WeakAss(M) ∪ WeakAss(M'')`, where `WeakAss(N)` is the set
of primes of `R` minimal over the annihilator of an element of `N`.

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.isLocallyConstructible_iff_forall_affineOpens
declarations.doc:
A subset of a scheme is locally constructible if and only if
its restriction to every affine open subscheme is constructible.
declarations.statement:
public theorem isLocallyConstructible_iff_forall_affineOpens
    {X : Scheme.{u}} (E : Set X) :
    Topology.IsLocallyConstructible E ↔
      ∀ U : X.affineOpens, Topology.IsConstructible ((U.1 : Set X) ↓∩ E)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.isCompact_inter_of_quasiSeparated
declarations.doc:
Let `X` be a quasi-separated scheme, i.e. `X ⟶ Spec ℤ` (the morphism to the terminal
scheme) is quasi-separated. The intersection of any two quasi-compact opens `U`, `V` of `X` is a
quasi-compact open of `X`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isCompact_inter_of_quasiSeparated (X : Scheme) [QuasiSeparated (terminal.from X)]
    {U V : Set X} (hU : IsOpen U) (hU' : IsCompact U) (hV : IsOpen V) (hV' : IsCompact V) :
    IsOpen (U ∩ V) ∧ IsCompact (U ∩ V)
declarations.comment: first assertion; Stacks' quasi-separated scheme is a quasi-separated morphism to the terminal scheme

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.isRetrocompact_of_quasiSeparated
declarations.doc:
Let `X` be a quasi-separated scheme, i.e. `X ⟶ Spec ℤ` (the morphism to the terminal
scheme) is quasi-separated. Every quasi-compact open `U` of `X` is retrocompact in `X`: its
intersection with every quasi-compact open of `X` is quasi-compact.
declarations.statement:
theorem isRetrocompact_of_quasiSeparated (X : Scheme) [QuasiSeparated (terminal.from X)]
    {U : Set X} (hU : IsOpen U) (hU' : IsCompact U) : IsRetrocompact U
declarations.comment: second assertion; Stacks' quasi-separated scheme is a quasi-separated morphism to the terminal scheme

registrations.name: Topology.IsLocallyConstructible.isConstructible
registrations.comment: stated for any topological space; on a qcqs scheme its hypotheses are instances

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.exists_dvr_morphism_of_specializes_with_residueField_equiv
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 054F, part (2).** For a strict specialization and a
finitely generated extension `K` of the residue field at the generic point,
the realizing discrete valuation ring can be chosen so that its generic
residue field is isomorphic to `K` over that residue field.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_dvr_morphism_of_specializes_with_residueField_equiv
    (X : Scheme.{u}) [IsLocallyNoetherian X] {x' x : X}
    (h : x' ⤳ x) (hne : x ≠ x')
    (K : Type u) [Field K] [Algebra (X.residueField x') K]
    [Algebra.EssFiniteType (X.residueField x') K] :
    ∃ (R : Type u) (_ : CommRing R) (_ : IsDomain R)
      (_ : IsDiscreteValuationRing R) (f : Spec (.of R) ⟶ X)
      (hη : f (genericPoint (Spec (.of R))) = x'),
      f (IsLocalRing.closedPoint R) = x ∧
        ∃ e : (Spec (.of R)).residueField (genericPoint (Spec (.of R))) ≃+* K,
          ∀ a : X.residueField x',
            e (f.residueFieldMap (genericPoint (Spec (.of R)))
              ((X.residueFieldCongr hη.symm).hom a)) =
              algebraMap (X.residueField x') K a
declarations.comment: part (2)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.exists_dvr_morphism_of_specializes
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 054F, part (1).** A specialization of points on a
locally Noetherian scheme is the image of the generic-to-closed specialization
on the spectrum of a discrete valuation ring.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_dvr_morphism_of_specializes (X : Scheme.{u}) [IsLocallyNoetherian X]
    {x' x : X} (h : x' ⤳ x) :
    ∃ (R : Type u) (_ : CommRing R) (_ : IsDomain R)
      (_ : IsDiscreteValuationRing R) (f : Spec (.of R) ⟶ X),
      f (genericPoint (Spec (.of R))) = x' ∧
        f (IsLocalRing.closedPoint R) = x
declarations.comment: part (1)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.isQuasiAffineHom_of_isQuasiAffine_of_quasiSeparatedSpace
declarations.doc: Every morphism from a quasi-affine scheme to a quasi-separated scheme is quasi-affine.
declarations.statement:
instance isQuasiAffineHom_of_isQuasiAffine_of_quasiSeparatedSpace
    {X S : Scheme.{u}} [Scheme.IsQuasiAffine X] [QuasiSeparatedSpace S]
    (f : X ⟶ S) : IsQuasiAffineHom f
declarations.comment: absolute corollary

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.IsQuasiAffineHom.of_comp
declarations.doc:
A morphism `g : X ⟶ Y` to a scheme quasi-separated over a base `S` via `h : Y ⟶ S` is
quasi-affine as soon as the structure morphism `g ≫ h` of `X` over `S` is quasi-affine.
declarations.statement:
theorem IsQuasiAffineHom.of_comp {X Y S : Scheme.{u}} (g : X ⟶ Y) (h : Y ⟶ S)
    [IsQuasiAffineHom (g ≫ h)] [QuasiSeparated h] : IsQuasiAffineHom g
declarations.comment: relative statement

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.isLocallyConstructible_preimage
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 054I.** The inverse image of a locally constructible
subset under a morphism of schemes is locally constructible.
declarations.comment: locally constructible case

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.exists_affine_open_etale_affineSpace
declarations.doc:
A morphism of schemes which is smooth at a point is, over any affine open neighbourhood `V`
of the image of that point, étale-locally an affine space over `V`: there is an affine open
neighbourhood `U` of the point mapping into `V` and an étale morphism from `U` to an affine
space over `V` commuting with the morphism.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_affine_open_etale_affineSpace {X Y : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ Y) (x : X)
    (V : Y.Opens) (hV : IsAffineOpen V) (hxV : x ∈ f ⁻¹ᵁ V)
    (hf : InfinitesimalLifting.SmoothAt f x) :
    ∃ (d : ℕ) (U : X.Opens) (_ : IsAffineOpen U) (_ : x ∈ U) (hUV : U ≤ f ⁻¹ᵁ V)
      (π : U.toScheme ⟶ AffineSpace (ULift.{u} (Fin d)) V.toScheme),
      Etale π ∧
        π ≫ (AffineSpace (ULift.{u} (Fin d)) V.toScheme ↘ V.toScheme) =
          f.resLE V U hUV

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.universalHomeomorphism_nilradical_subschemeι
declarations.doc:
The reduction of a scheme is universally homeomorphic to the scheme through its canonical
closed immersion.
declarations.statement:
instance universalHomeomorphism_nilradical_subschemeι (X : Scheme.{u}) :
    UniversalHomeomorphism X.nilradical.subschemeι

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.geometricallyConnected_iff_baseChange_fieldExtension
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 054N.** A scheme over a field is geometrically connected if and only if
its base change along a field extension is geometrically connected.
declarations.statement:
public theorem geometricallyConnected_iff_baseChange_fieldExtension
    {X : Scheme.{u}} (k k' : Type u) [Field k] [Field k'] [Algebra k k']
    (f : X ⟶ Spec (.of k)) :
    GeometricallyConnected f ↔
      GeometricallyConnected
        (pullback.snd f (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap k k'))))

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.geometricallyIrreducible_iff_baseChange_fieldExtension
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 054P.** A scheme over a field is geometrically irreducible if and only
if its base change along any field extension is geometrically irreducible.
declarations.statement:
public theorem geometricallyIrreducible_iff_baseChange_fieldExtension
    (k k' : Type u) [Field k] [Field k'] [Algebra k k'] {X : Scheme.{u}}
    (f : X ⟶ Spec (of k)) :
    GeometricallyIrreducible f ↔
      GeometricallyIrreducible
        (pullback.snd f (Spec.map (ofHom (algebraMap k k'))))

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.geometricallyIrreducible_fiber_iff_isGeometricallyIrreducible_residueField
declarations.doc:
**The generic fibre is geometrically irreducible exactly when the residue field at the
generic point is.** Let `R` be a domain and let `f : X ⟶ Spec R` carry the generic point of an
irreducible `X` to the generic point `η` of `Spec R`. Then the generic fibre of `f` is
geometrically irreducible over `κ(η)` if and only if the residue field of `X` at its generic
point is geometrically irreducible over `κ(η)`.

This is [Stacks, Tag 054Q] applied to the generic fibre, which is irreducible by
`AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.Hom.irreducibleSpace_fiber_of_genericPoint`, followed by the
identification `AlgebraicGeometry.genericFiberResidueFieldMap` of its residue field at its
generic point with that of `X`. `X` is not assumed reduced.
declarations.statement:
theorem geometricallyIrreducible_fiber_iff_isGeometricallyIrreducible_residueField :
    letI := residueFieldAlgebraOfEq f hgen
    GeometricallyIrreducible (f.fiberToSpecResidueField (genericPoint (Spec R))) ↔
      Algebra.IsGeometricallyIrreducible
        ↥((Spec R).residueField (genericPoint (Spec R))) ↥(X.residueField (genericPoint X))
declarations.comment: the generic fibre, read on the residue field of the source

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.geometricallyIrreducible_fiber_genericPoint_iff_residueField_of_isAffine
declarations.doc:
**The generic fibre over an integral affine base is geometrically irreducible exactly when
the residue field at the generic point is.** The criterion
`AlgebraicGeometry.geometricallyIrreducible_fiber_iff_isGeometricallyIrreducible_residueField`
for a base presented as an integral affine scheme rather than literally as the spectrum of a
domain; the residue field of the base is then written at the generic point of
`Spec Γ(Y, ⊤)`, which is where a fraction-field presentation of it is available.
declarations.statement:
theorem geometricallyIrreducible_fiber_genericPoint_iff_residueField_of_isAffine
    (hgen : f (genericPoint X) = genericPoint Y) :
    letI := residueFieldAlgebraOfEq (f ≫ Y.isoSpec.hom) (comp_isoSpec_genericPoint_eq f hgen)
    GeometricallyIrreducible (f.fiberToSpecResidueField (genericPoint Y)) ↔
      Algebra.IsGeometricallyIrreducible
        ↥((Spec Γ(Y, ⊤)).residueField (genericPoint (Spec Γ(Y, ⊤))))
        ↥(X.residueField (genericPoint X))
declarations.comment: the generic fibre over an affine base, read on the residue field of the source

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.geometricallyIrreducible_tfae_functionField
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 054Q.** For an irreducible scheme `X` over a field `k`, the following
are equivalent: `X` is geometrically irreducible over `k`; the residue field at a generic point
is geometrically irreducible over `k`; and the separable closure of `k` in that residue field is
trivial.
declarations.statement:
public theorem geometricallyIrreducible_tfae_functionField
    (k : Type u) [Field k] (X : Scheme.{u}) (f : X ⟶ Spec (.of k))
    [IrreducibleSpace X] (ξ : X) (hξ : IsGenericPoint ξ Set.univ) :
    letI : Algebra k (X.residueField ξ) :=
      ((Scheme.ΓSpecIso (.of k)).inv ≫ f.appTop ≫ X.Γevaluation ξ).hom.toAlgebra
    List.TFAE [
      GeometricallyIrreducible f,
      Algebra.IsGeometricallyIrreducible k (X.residueField ξ),
      separableClosure k (X.residueField ξ) = ⊥]

declarations.name: Algebra.isGeometricallyIrreducible_tfae_residueField
declarations.statement:
theorem isGeometricallyIrreducible_tfae_residueField (k A : Type u) [Field k] [CommRing A]
    [Algebra k A] (I : Ideal A) [I.IsPrime] (hI : I = nilradical A) :
    List.TFAE [IsGeometricallyIrreducible k A, IsGeometricallyIrreducible k I.ResidueField,
      separableClosure k I.ResidueField = ⊥]
declarations.comment:
The affine case. The source states this for an irreducible scheme `X` over `k` and
  the residue field at its generic point; here `X = Spec A`, and that the spectrum is irreducible
  is expressed by the hypothesis that the nilradical of `A` is the prime `I`. The scheme-level
  statement is NOT proved here: deducing it needs in addition the reduction of geometric
  irreducibility to affine opens (Stacks 038G, formalized as
  `AlgebraicGeometry.geometricallyIrreducible_tfae_local`) and the identification of the residue
  field at the generic point with the generic residue field of an affine open's ring of
  sections.

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.exists_finite_separable_extension_geometricallyIrreducible_components
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 054R.** After a finite separable extension of the ground field, every
irreducible component of a scheme locally of finite type over a field is geometrically
irreducible, provided that the original scheme has only finitely many irreducible components.
declarations.statement:
public theorem exists_finite_separable_extension_geometricallyIrreducible_components
    (k : Type u) [Field k] (X : Scheme.{u}) (f : X ⟶ Spec (.of k))
    [LocallyOfFiniteType f] (hX : (irreducibleComponents X).Finite) :
    ∃ (k' : Type u) (_ : Field k') (_ : Algebra k k')
      (_ : FiniteDimensional k k') (_ : Algebra.IsSeparable k k'),
      let X' := pullback (C := Scheme.{u}) f (Spec.map (ofHom (algebraMap k k')))
      ∀ Z : irreducibleComponents X',
        GeometricallyIrreducible
          ((Scheme.IdealSheafData.vanishingIdeal (X := X')
              ⟨Z.1, isClosed_of_mem_irreducibleComponents Z.1 Z.2⟩).subschemeι ≫
            pullback.snd f (Spec.map (ofHom (algebraMap k k'))))

declarations.name: TopologicalSpace.finite_connectedComponents_of_finite_irreducibleComponents
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 054S.** Finitely many irreducible components imply finitely many
connected components.
declarations.statement:
public theorem finite_connectedComponents_of_finite_irreducibleComponents
    {X : Type*} [TopologicalSpace X] (hX : (irreducibleComponents X).Finite) :
    Finite (ConnectedComponents X)
declarations.comment: finiteness of connected components

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.geometricallyConnected_connectedComponent
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 054S.** If each of the finitely many irreducible components of a
scheme over a field is geometrically irreducible, each connected component has an open
subscheme structure that is geometrically connected over that field.
declarations.statement:
public theorem geometricallyConnected_connectedComponent
    (k : Type u) [Field k] (X : Scheme.{u}) (f : X ⟶ Spec (.of k))
    (hX : (irreducibleComponents X).Finite)
    (hgeom : ∀ Z : irreducibleComponents X,
      GeometricallyIrreducible
        ((Scheme.IdealSheafData.vanishingIdeal (X := X)
            ⟨Z.1, isClosed_of_mem_irreducibleComponents Z.1 Z.2⟩).subschemeι ≫ f))
    (c : ConnectedComponents X) :
    ∃ U : X.Opens,
      (U : Set X) = (ConnectedComponents.mk : X → ConnectedComponents X) ⁻¹' {c} ∧
        GeometricallyConnected (U.ι ≫ f)
declarations.comment: geometric connectedness of connected components

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.exists_open_relativeDimension_fiberwise_dense
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 054T.** A flat morphism locally of finite presentation admits open
pieces of every nonnegative relative dimension whose union is dense in every fibre.
declarations.statement:
public theorem exists_open_relativeDimension_fiberwise_dense
    {X S : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ S) [Flat f] [LocallyOfFinitePresentation f] :
    ∃ U : ℕ → X.Opens,
      (∀ s : S, Dense ((f.fiberι s) ⁻¹' (((iSup U : X.Opens) : Set X)))) ∧
        (∀ d : ℕ, RelativeDimension ((U d).ι ≫ f) d)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.topologicalKrullDimAt_fiber_eq_of_specialization_of_mem_genericPoints
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 054U.** For a flat morphism locally of finite presentation, local
dimension in the fibres is constant along a specialization whose endpoint is generic in an
irreducible component of its fibre.
declarations.statement:
public theorem topologicalKrullDimAt_fiber_eq_of_specialization_of_mem_genericPoints
    {X S : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ S) [Flat f] [LocallyOfFinitePresentation f]
    {x' x : X} (hxx : x' ⤳ x)
    (hx : f.asFiber x ∈ genericPoints (f.fiber (f x))) :
    topologicalKrullDimAt (f.fiber (f x')) (f.asFiber x') =
      topologicalKrullDimAt (f.fiber (f x)) (f.asFiber x)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.exists_open_preimage_eq_bot_of_isEmpty_generic_fiber
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 054W.** Let `f : X ⟶ Y` be a finite type morphism with `Y`
irreducible with generic point `η`. If the fibre over `η` is empty, then the base change of `f`
to some nonempty open subset `V` of `Y` is empty, that is, `f ⁻¹ᵁ V = ⊥`.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_open_preimage_eq_bot_of_isEmpty_generic_fiber
    {X Y : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ Y)
    [LocallyOfFiniteType f] [QuasiCompact f]
    (η : Y) (hη : IsGenericPoint η Set.univ) (hempty : IsEmpty (f.fiber η)) :
    ∃ V : Y.Opens, Nonempty V ∧ f ⁻¹ᵁ V = ⊥

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.exists_open_isNowhereDense_fiber
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 054X.** A closed subset that is nowhere dense in the generic fibre of a
finite type morphism remains nowhere dense in all fibres over a nonempty open subset of the
irreducible base.

The base is replaced by its reduction, which is a universal homeomorphism onto it (Stacks 054M),
so the base change of `f` is a homeomorphism onto `X`; nowhere density in fibres is invariant
under that, and the reduced base is handled by
`AlgebraicGeometry.exists_open_isNowhereDense_fiber_of_isReduced`.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_open_isNowhereDense_fiber {X Y : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ Y) [IrreducibleSpace Y]
    [LocallyOfFiniteType f] [QuasiCompact f] (Z : Set X) (hZ : IsClosed Z) (η : Y)
    (hη : IsGenericPoint η Set.univ) (hηZ : IsNowhereDense ((f.fiberι η) ⁻¹' Z)) :
    ∃ V : Set Y, IsOpen V ∧ V.Nonempty ∧
      ∀ y ∈ V, IsNowhereDense ((f.fiberι y) ⁻¹' Z)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.exists_open_fiber_covered_by_closures
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 054Y.** Let `f : X ⟶ Y` be a finite type morphism with `Y`
irreducible with generic point `η`. If the subsets `Z i` cover the generic fibre, then over
some nonempty open subset of `Y` the closures in `X` of their images cover every fibre.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_open_fiber_covered_by_closures
    {X Y : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ Y)
    [LocallyOfFiniteType f] [QuasiCompact f]
    (η : Y) (hη : IsGenericPoint η Set.univ)
    {ι : Type v}
    (Z : ι → Set (f.fiber η))
    (hcover : ∀ x : f.fiber η, ∃ i, x ∈ Z i) :
    ∃ V : Set Y, IsOpen V ∧ V.Nonempty ∧
      ∀ y ∈ V, ∀ x : f.fiber y,
        ∃ i, f.fiberι y x ∈ closure (f.fiberι η '' Z i)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.comap_nilradical_fiberι
declarations.doc:
The reduction of the fibre over a generic point of an irreducible component is the
base change of the reduction of the source.
declarations.statement:
theorem comap_nilradical_fiberι {X Y : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ Y)
    (η : Y) (hη : η ∈ genericPoints Y) :
    X.nilradical.comap (f.fiberι η) = (f.fiber η).nilradical

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.exists_finiteUniversalHomeomorphism_geometricallyReduced_genericFiber
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0550.** A finite type morphism over an irreducible
base admits, locally on the base, a finite universal homeomorphic cover whose
reduced pullback is flat and finitely presented with geometrically reduced
generic fibre.
declarations.statement:
public theorem exists_finiteUniversalHomeomorphism_geometricallyReduced_genericFiber
    {X Y : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ Y) [IrreducibleSpace Y]
    [LocallyOfFiniteType f] [QuasiCompact f] :
    ∃ (V : Y.Opens) (_ : V.1.Nonempty)
      (Y' : Scheme.{u}) (g : Y' ⟶ V.toScheme)
      (_ : IsFinite g) (_ : UniversalHomeomorphism g)
      (_ : IsIntegral Y') (_ : IsAffine Y'),
      let X_V := pullback V.ι f
      let P := pullback (g ≫ V.ι) f
      let X' := P.nilradical.subscheme
      let r : X' ⟶ P := P.nilradical.subschemeι
      let f' : X' ⟶ Y' := r ≫ pullback.fst (g ≫ V.ι) f
      let g' : X' ⟶ X_V := pullback.lift
        (f' ≫ g) (r ≫ pullback.snd (g ≫ V.ι) f) (by
          dsimp [f']
          rw [Category.assoc, Category.assoc, pullback.condition]
          rfl)
      IsFinite g' ∧ UniversalHomeomorphism g' ∧ Flat f' ∧
        AlgebraicGeometry.FinitePresentation f' ∧
        ∀ η : Y', IsGenericPoint η Set.univ →
          GeometricallyReduced (f'.fiberToSpecResidueField η)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.exists_nonemptyOpen_finiteEtale_cover_geometricallyIrreducible_genericFiber
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0551.** After passing to a nonempty open of an irreducible base, a
finite type morphism has a finite etale surjective base change from an irreducible affine
scheme whose generic fibre has geometrically irreducible irreducible components.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_nonemptyOpen_finiteEtale_cover_geometricallyIrreducible_genericFiber
    {X Y : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ Y) [IrreducibleSpace Y]
    [LocallyOfFiniteType f] [QuasiCompact f] :
    ∃ (V : Y.Opens) (_ : V.1.Nonempty)
      (Y' : Scheme.{u}) (g : Y' ⟶ V.toScheme)
      (_ : Surjective g) (_ : IsFinite g) (_ : Etale g)
      (_ : IrreducibleSpace Y') (_ : IsAffine Y'),
      let X_V := pullback V.ι f
      let fV : X_V ⟶ V.toScheme := pullback.fst V.ι f
      let X' := pullback (g ≫ V.ι) f
      let f' : X' ⟶ Y' := pullback.fst (g ≫ V.ι) f
      let g' : X' ⟶ X_V := pullback.lift
        (pullback.fst (g ≫ V.ι) f ≫ g)
        (pullback.snd (g ≫ V.ι) f) (by
          rw [Category.assoc]
          exact pullback.condition)
      IsPullback g' f' fV g ∧
        Surjective g' ∧ IsFinite g' ∧ Etale g' ∧
        ∀ (η : Y'), IsGenericPoint η Set.univ →
          ∀ Z : irreducibleComponents (f'.fiber η),
            GeometricallyIrreducible
              ((Scheme.IdealSheafData.vanishingIdeal (X := f'.fiber η)
                  ⟨Z.1, isClosed_of_mem_irreducibleComponents Z.1 Z.2⟩).subschemeι ≫
                f'.fiberToSpecResidueField η)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.tfae_dominantBirationalOver_residueField_genericPoint
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0552.** Let `X` and `Y` be integral schemes locally of finite type over `S`, with
generic points `x` and `y`. The following are equivalent: (1) `X` and `Y` are `S`-birational,
that is, isomorphic in the category of irreducible schemes over `S` and dominant `S`-rational
maps; (2) there are nonempty opens of `X` and `Y` which are `S`-isomorphic; (3) `x` and `y` map
to the same point `s` of `S` and `κ(x) ≅ κ(y)` as extensions of `κ(s)`.
declarations.statement:
theorem tfae_dominantBirationalOver_residueField_genericPoint
    {S X Y : Scheme.{u}} [X.Over S] [Y.Over S]
    [IsIntegral X] [IsIntegral Y]
    [LocallyOfFiniteType (X ↘ S)] [LocallyOfFiniteType (Y ↘ S)] :
    List.TFAE
      [Scheme.DominantBirationalOver S X Y,
        ∃ (U : X.Opens) (V : Y.Opens),
          (U : Set X).Nonempty ∧ (V : Set Y).Nonempty ∧
            ∃ e : U.toScheme ≅ V.toScheme, e.hom ≫ V.ι ≫ Y ↘ S = U.ι ≫ X ↘ S,
        ∃ (h : (X ↘ S) (genericPoint X) = (Y ↘ S) (genericPoint Y))
          (e : X.residueField (genericPoint X) ≅ Y.residueField (genericPoint Y)),
          h ▸ ((X ↘ S).residueFieldMap (genericPoint X) ≫ e.hom) =
            (Y ↘ S).residueFieldMap (genericPoint Y)]

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.exists_open_ncard_irreducibleComponents_fiber_ge
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0554.** For a finite type morphism to a scheme with a chosen dense
generic point, the number of irreducible components of the fibres is at least the number for
the generic fibre over a nonempty open subset of the base.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_open_ncard_irreducibleComponents_fiber_ge {X Y : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ Y)
    [LocallyOfFiniteType f] [QuasiCompact f] (η : Y) (hη : IsGenericPoint η Set.univ)
    (n : ℕ) (hcomp : (irreducibleComponents (f.fiber η)).ncard = n) :
    ∃ V : Set Y, IsOpen V ∧ V.Nonempty ∧
      ∀ y ∈ V, n ≤ (irreducibleComponents (f.fiber y)).ncard

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.geometricallyIrreducibleFiberLocus_baseChange
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0555.** The points with geometrically irreducible fibre pull back
exactly under an arbitrary base change.
declarations.statement:
theorem geometricallyIrreducibleFiberLocus_baseChange
    {X Y Y' : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ Y) (g : Y' ⟶ Y) :
    {y' : Y' | GeometricallyIrreducible
      ((pullback.snd f g).fiberToSpecResidueField y')} =
      g ⁻¹' {y : Y | GeometricallyIrreducible (f.fiberToSpecResidueField y)}
declarations.comment: the locus pulls back under the chosen fibre product

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.geometricallyIrreducibleFiberLocus_eq_preimage_of_isPullback
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0555.** The points with geometrically irreducible fibre pull back
exactly under an arbitrary cartesian square, not only under the chosen fibre product.
declarations.statement:
theorem geometricallyIrreducibleFiberLocus_eq_preimage_of_isPullback
    {X Y X' Y' : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ Y) (f' : X' ⟶ Y') (i : X' ⟶ X) (g : Y' ⟶ Y)
    (h : IsPullback i f' f g) :
    {y' : Y' | GeometricallyIrreducible (f'.fiberToSpecResidueField y')} =
      g ⁻¹' {y : Y | GeometricallyIrreducible (f.fiberToSpecResidueField y)}
declarations.comment: the locus pulls back under an arbitrary cartesian square

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.geometricIrreducibleComponentCount
declarations.doc:
The number, as an extended natural number, of geometrically irreducible components of each
fibre of a morphism of schemes.
declarations.statement: def geometricIrreducibleComponentCount {X Y : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ Y) : Y → ℕ∞
declarations.comment: the function

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.encard_irreducibleComponents_geometricFiber
declarations.doc:
The number of irreducible components of the geometric fibre can be computed after extension
to any separably closed field containing the residue field.
declarations.statement:
theorem encard_irreducibleComponents_geometricFiber {X Y : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ Y)
    (y : Y) (K : Type u) [Field K] [Algebra (Y.residueField y) K] [IsSepClosed K] :
    (irreducibleComponents (geometricFiber f y K)).encard =
      geometricIrreducibleComponentCount f y
declarations.comment: well-definedness

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.geometricIrreducibleComponentCount_pullback
declarations.doc:
Formation of the function counting geometrically irreducible components of fibres commutes
with arbitrary base change.
declarations.statement:
theorem geometricIrreducibleComponentCount_pullback {X Y Y' : Scheme.{u}}
    (f : X ⟶ Y) (g : Y' ⟶ Y) :
    geometricIrreducibleComponentCount (pullback.snd f g) =
      geometricIrreducibleComponentCount f ∘ g
declarations.comment: base change

declarations.name: MvPolynomial.exists_away_irreducible_map
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0557.** An absolutely irreducible polynomial over a domain
remains irreducible under every specialization to a field after restricting to a
nonempty principal open subset.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_away_irreducible_map
    (A : Type u) [CommRing A] [IsDomain A]
    (K : Type v) [Field K] [Algebra A K] [IsFractionRing A K]
    (Kbar : Type w) [Field Kbar] [Algebra K Kbar] [IsAlgClosed Kbar]
    (ι : Type x) [Finite ι] (P : MvPolynomial ι A)
    (hP : Irreducible (P.map ((algebraMap K Kbar).comp (algebraMap A K)))) :
    ∃ f : A, f ≠ 0 ∧
      ∀ (κ : Type y) [Field κ] (φ : Localization.Away f →+* κ),
        Irreducible (P.map (φ.comp (algebraMap A (Localization.Away f))))

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.geometricallyIrreducibleAfterShrinking
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0559.** A morphism of finite type onto an irreducible base whose
fibre over the generic point is geometrically irreducible has geometrically irreducible fibres
over a nonempty open subscheme of the base.
declarations.statement:
theorem geometricallyIrreducibleAfterShrinking :
    GeometricallyIrreducibleAfterShrinking.{u}

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.exists_open_geometricIrreducibleComponentCount_constant
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 055A.** The number of geometrically irreducible components of the
fibres of a finite type morphism is constant on a nonempty open subset of the closure of any
point of the target.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_open_geometricIrreducibleComponentCount_constant {X Y : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ Y)
    [LocallyOfFiniteType f] [QuasiCompact f] (y : Y) :
    ∃ V : Opens (↑(closure ({y} : Set Y))), Nonempty V ∧
      ∃ n : ℕ∞, ∀ z : V, geometricIrreducibleComponentCount f z.1.1 = n

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.isLocallyConstructible_level_geometricIrreducibleComponentCount
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 055B.** Every level set of the number of geometrically irreducible
components of the fibres of a morphism of finite presentation is locally constructible.

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.exists_open_natCard_connectedComponents_fiber_ge
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 055D.** For a finite type morphism to a scheme with a chosen dense
generic point, the number of connected components of the fibres is at least the number for the
generic fibre on a nonempty open subset of the base.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_open_natCard_connectedComponents_fiber_ge {X Y : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ Y)
    [LocallyOfFiniteType f] [QuasiCompact f] (η : Y) (hη : IsGenericPoint η Set.univ) (n : ℕ)
    (hcomp : Nat.card (ConnectedComponents (f.fiber η)) = n) :
    ∃ V : Set Y, IsOpen V ∧ V.Nonempty ∧
      ∀ y ∈ V, n ≤ Nat.card (ConnectedComponents (f.fiber y))

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.geometricallyConnected_fiber_locus_pullback
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 055E.** Formation of the locus where the fibres of a scheme morphism
are geometrically connected commutes with arbitrary base change.
declarations.statement:
theorem geometricallyConnected_fiber_locus_pullback
    {X Y Y' : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ Y) (g : Y' ⟶ Y) :
    {y' : Y' |
        GeometricallyConnected ((pullback.snd f g).fiberToSpecResidueField y')} =
      g ⁻¹' {y : Y | GeometricallyConnected (f.fiberToSpecResidueField y)}

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.numGeometricConnectedComponents
declarations.doc: The number of geometric connected components of each fibre of a morphism of schemes.
declarations.statement: def numGeometricConnectedComponents (f : X ⟶ Y) : Y → ℕ∞
declarations.comment: the function

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.enatCard_connectedComponents_fiberBaseChange
declarations.doc:
Computing the number of connected components after extending a fibre to any separably closed
extension gives the canonical number of geometric connected components.
declarations.statement:
theorem enatCard_connectedComponents_fiberBaseChange (f : X ⟶ Y) (y : Y)
    (K : Type u) [Field K] [Algebra (Y.residueField y) K] [IsSepClosed K] :
    ENat.card (ConnectedComponents (geometricFiber f y K)) =
      numGeometricConnectedComponents f y
declarations.comment: well-definedness

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.numGeometricConnectedComponents_eq_of_isPullback
declarations.doc:
The number of geometric connected components of fibres is preserved by arbitrary base
change.
declarations.statement:
theorem numGeometricConnectedComponents_eq_of_isPullback
    {X' Y' : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ Y) (f' : X' ⟶ Y') (i : X' ⟶ X) (g : Y' ⟶ Y)
    (h : IsPullback i f' f g) :
    numGeometricConnectedComponents f' = numGeometricConnectedComponents f ∘ g
declarations.comment: base change

registrations.name: geometricFiber
registrations.comment: geometric fibre

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.geometricallyConnectedAfterShrinking
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 055G.** A finite type morphism onto an irreducible base whose fibre
over the generic point is geometrically connected has geometrically connected fibres over a
nonempty open subscheme of the base.
declarations.statement: theorem geometricallyConnectedAfterShrinking : GeometricallyConnectedAfterShrinking.{u}

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.exists_open_numGeometricConnectedComponents_eq
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 055H.** For a finite type morphism of schemes, the number of
geometric connected components of the fibres is constant on some nonempty open subset of the
closure of any prescribed point of the base.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_open_numGeometricConnectedComponents_eq {X Y : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ Y)
    [LocallyOfFiniteType f] [QuasiCompact f] (y : Y) :
    ∃ V : TopologicalSpace.Opens (↑(closure ({y} : Set Y))), Nonempty V ∧
      ∃ n : ℕ∞, ∀ z : V, numGeometricConnectedComponents f z.1.1 = n

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.isLocallyConstructible_numGeometricConnectedComponents
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 055I.** Every level set of the number of geometrically connected
components of the fibres of a morphism of finite presentation is locally constructible.

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.connectedSpace_fiber_bot_of_isReduced_fiber_closedPoint
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 055J.** A flat degeneration of a disconnected scheme
is either disconnected or nonreduced: if a flat scheme over a discrete
valuation ring is connected and its closed fibre is reduced, then its generic
fibre is connected.
declarations.statement:
theorem connectedSpace_fiber_bot_of_isReduced_fiber_closedPoint
    {R : Type u} [CommRing R] [IsDomain R] [IsDiscreteValuationRing R]
    {X : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ Spec (.of R)) [Flat f] [ConnectedSpace X]
    [IsReduced (f.fiber (IsLocalRing.closedPoint R))] :
    ConnectedSpace (f.fiber (⟨⊥, inferInstance⟩ : PrimeSpectrum R))

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.ConnectedAlongSection.mem_locus_iff_asFiber_mem
declarations.doc:
For a morphism `f : X ⟶ Y` with a section `s`, the subset `X⁰ = ⋃_y X⁰_y` of `X` consists of
the points `x` which, viewed as points of their own fibre `X_{f(x)}`, lie in the connected
component `X⁰_{f(x)}` of that fibre containing `s(f(x))`.
declarations.statement:
theorem mem_locus_iff_asFiber_mem (D : ConnectedAlongSection.{u}) (x : D.X) :
    x ∈ D.locus ↔ D.f.asFiber x ∈ D.fiberComponent (D.f x)
declarations.comment: Situation 055L: X⁰ = ⋃_y X⁰_y, pointwise

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.ConnectedAlongSection.ofGrpObj
declarations.doc:
A group scheme `G ⟶ S` together with its neutral section `e : S ⟶ G`, as a morphism of
schemes with a section. The neutral section is the morphism of schemes underlying the unit
`η[G] : 𝟙_ (Over S) ⟶ G` of the group object `G`.
declarations.statement: noncomputable def ofGrpObj : ConnectedAlongSection.{u}
declarations.comment: a group scheme G → S with its neutral section e : S → G

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.GroupScheme.neutralLocus
declarations.doc:
For a group scheme `G ⟶ S` with neutral section `e`, the subset `G⁰ ⊆ G`: the union over
`s : S` of the connected components `G⁰_s` of the fibres `G_s` containing `e(s)`, that is, the
locus `X⁰` for `f = (G ⟶ S)` and the section `e`.
declarations.statement: noncomputable def neutralLocus : Set G.left
declarations.comment: G⁰ = ⋃_s G⁰_s for the neutral section

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.GroupScheme.fiberι_preimage_neutralLocus
declarations.doc:
For a group scheme `G ⟶ S` with neutral section `e` and a point `s : S`, the trace of `G⁰` on
the fibre `G_s` is the connected component of `G_s` containing the point `e(s)`.
declarations.statement:
theorem fiberι_preimage_neutralLocus (s : S) (z : G.hom.fiber s)
    (hz : G.hom.fiberι s z = η[G].left s) :
    (G.hom.fiberι s) ⁻¹' neutralLocus G = connectedComponent z
declarations.comment: the trace of G⁰ on G_s is the component of G_s containing e(s)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.ConnectedAlongSection
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 055L (standing data).** A morphism of schemes together with a
specified section.
declarations.statement: structure ConnectedAlongSection
declarations.comment: the sectioned morphism

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.ConnectedAlongSection.fiberComponent
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 055L (the fibrewise component).** The connected component of the
fibre over `y` which contains the point supplied by the section.
declarations.statement: noncomputable def fiberComponent (D : ConnectedAlongSection) (y : D.Y) : Set (D.f.fiber y)
declarations.comment: the component X⁰_y

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.ConnectedAlongSection.locus
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 055L (the union).** The subset `X⁰ ⊆ X` obtained by taking, for
every `y : Y`, the image in `X` of the connected component `X⁰_y`.
declarations.statement: noncomputable def locus (D : ConnectedAlongSection) : Set D.X
declarations.comment: the union X⁰

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.ConnectedAlongSection.locus_eq_preimage_of_isPullback
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 055M.** In a cartesian square of sectioned morphisms, where the
sections are compatible with the horizontal maps, the union of the connected components of
the fibres containing the section pulls back to the corresponding union upstairs.
declarations.statement:
theorem locus_eq_preimage_of_isPullback
    (D D' : ConnectedAlongSection.{u})
    (g' : D'.X ⟶ D.X) (g : D'.Y ⟶ D.Y)
    (h : IsPullback g' D'.f D.f g)
    (hs : D'.s ≫ g' = g ≫ D.s) :
    D'.locus = g' ⁻¹' D.locus

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.ConnectedAlongSection.clopenLocusAfterShrinking
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 055N.** For a finite type morphism with a section and a point `y` of
the target, the locus `X⁰` is open and closed in the inverse image of a nonempty open subset of
the closure of `y`.
declarations.statement: theorem clopenLocusAfterShrinking : ClopenLocusAfterShrinking.{u}

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.ConnectedAlongSection.isLocallyConstructible_locus
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 055P.** For a morphism of finite presentation with a section, the
locus `X⁰` is locally constructible in the source.
declarations.statement: theorem isLocallyConstructible_locus : Statement055P.{u}

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.locus_mem_nhds_of_isDiscreteValuationRing
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 055Q over a discrete valuation ring base.** The locus `X⁰` is a neighbourhood of
every point of the connected component of the closed fibre containing the section.
declarations.statement:
theorem locus_mem_nhds_of_isDiscreteValuationRing
    {X : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ Spec (.of R)) (sec : Spec (.of R) ⟶ X)
    (hsec : sec ≫ f = 𝟙 _) [Flat f] [LocallyOfFiniteType f]
    [IsReduced (f.fiber (IsLocalRing.closedPoint R))]
    {x : X} (hx : x ∈ connectedComponentIn (f ⁻¹' {IsLocalRing.closedPoint R} : Set X)
      (sec (IsLocalRing.closedPoint R))) :
    ConnectedAlongSection.locus ⟨X, Spec (.of R), f, sec, hsec⟩ ∈ nhds x
declarations.comment:
the case of a discrete valuation ring base; the source's reduction to this case,
and hence the statement for a general base, is not proved here

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.ConnectedAlongSection.locus_mem_nhds_of_isConstructible
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 055Q for a Noetherian source.** If `X` is a Noetherian scheme, `f` is flat and
locally of finite type and the fibre of `f` through `x ∈ X⁰` is geometrically reduced, then `X⁰`
is a neighbourhood of `x`.

Quantified over the points `x` of `X⁰` lying over a point `y` of `Y`, this is the conclusion of
the source: `X⁰` is a neighbourhood of `X⁰_y`.
declarations.statement:
theorem locus_mem_nhds_of_isConstructible (D : ConnectedAlongSection.{u})
    [AlgebraicGeometry.IsNoetherian D.X] [Flat D.f] [LocallyOfFiniteType D.f]
    {x : D.X} (hx : x ∈ D.locus)
    (hred : GeometricallyReduced (D.f.fiberToSpecResidueField (D.f x))) :
    D.locus ∈ nhds x
declarations.comment:
the topological reduction to the discrete valuation ring case, for a Noetherian
source

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.ConnectedAlongSection.locus_mem_nhdsSet_fiberComponent
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 055Q.** For a flat morphism of finite presentation with a section
whose fibre over `y` is geometrically reduced, the locus `X⁰` is a neighbourhood of the
connected component of that fibre meeting the section.
declarations.statement:
theorem locus_mem_nhdsSet_fiberComponent (D : ConnectedAlongSection.{u})
    (hfp : FinitePresentation D.f) [Flat D.f] (y : D.Y)
    (hgr : GeometricallyReduced (D.f.fiberToSpecResidueField y)) :
    D.locus ∈ nhdsSet (D.f.fiberι y '' D.fiberComponent y)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.isOpen_locus_of_isDiscreteValuationRing
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 055R over a discrete valuation ring base.** The locus `X⁰` of connected components
of fibres meeting the section is open. Only reducedness of the closed fibre is needed; the
source's hypothesis that all fibres be geometrically reduced is not used, and the two reductions
of the source that pass from a general base to this one are not proved here.
declarations.statement:
theorem isOpen_locus_of_isDiscreteValuationRing
    {X : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ Spec (.of R)) (sec : Spec (.of R) ⟶ X)
    (hsec : sec ≫ f = 𝟙 _) [Flat f] [LocallyOfFiniteType f]
    [IsReduced (f.fiber (IsLocalRing.closedPoint R))] :
    IsOpen (ConnectedAlongSection.locus ⟨X, Spec (.of R), f, sec, hsec⟩)
declarations.comment:
the case of a discrete valuation ring base; the source's reduction to this case,
and hence the statement for a general base, is not proved here

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.ConnectedAlongSection.isOpen_locus_of_isConstructible
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 055R for a Noetherian source.** If `X` is a Noetherian scheme and `f` is flat and
locally of finite type with geometrically reduced fibres, then `X⁰` is open.
declarations.statement:
theorem isOpen_locus_of_isConstructible (D : ConnectedAlongSection.{u})
    [AlgebraicGeometry.IsNoetherian D.X] [Flat D.f] [LocallyOfFiniteType D.f]
    [GeometricallyReduced D.f] :
    IsOpen D.locus
declarations.comment:
the topological reduction to the discrete valuation ring case, for a Noetherian
source

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.ConnectedAlongSection.isOpen_locus
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 055R.** For a flat morphism of finite presentation with a section and
geometrically reduced fibres, the locus `X⁰` is open in the source.
declarations.statement: theorem isOpen_locus : Statement055R.{u}

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.exists_closedPoint_finite_separable_residueField
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 055T.** A nonempty open subset of affine space over a field contains
a closed point whose residue field is a finite separable extension of the field.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_closedPoint_finite_separable_residueField
    {k : Type u} [Field k] {d : ℕ}
    (W : Set (AffineSpace (ULift.{u} (Fin d)) (Spec (.of k))))
    (hWopen : IsOpen W) (hWnonempty : W.Nonempty) :
    ∃ w : AffineSpace (ULift.{u} (Fin d)) (Spec (.of k)),
      w ∈ W ∧ w ∈ closedPoints (AffineSpace (ULift.{u} (Fin d)) (Spec (.of k))) ∧
        let X := AffineSpace (ULift.{u} (Fin d)) (Spec (.of k))
        let f := X ↘ Spec (.of k)
        letI := ((Scheme.ΓSpecIso (.of k)).inv ≫ f.appTop ≫ X.Γevaluation w).hom.toAlgebra
        Module.Finite k (X.residueField w) ∧
          Algebra.IsSeparable k (X.residueField w)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.exists_etaleNeighborhood_lift_of_smooth
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 055U.** A smooth morphism admits an étale local section through any
point of its image.

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.exists_etale_cover_refining_smooth_cover
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 055V.** Every smooth covering of a scheme is refined by an étale
covering.
declarations.statement:
public theorem exists_etale_cover_refining_smooth_cover {S : Scheme.{u}}
    (𝒰 : S.Cover.{v} (Scheme.precoverage (@Smooth.{u}))) :
    ∃ 𝒱 : S.Cover.{u} (Scheme.precoverage (@Etale.{u})),
      Nonempty (𝒱.toPreZeroHypercover.Hom 𝒰.toPreZeroHypercover)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.exists_etaleNeighborhood_geometricallyConnected
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 055W.** A geometrically connected open in a fibre of a flat, finitely
presented morphism with geometrically reduced fibres spreads, after an affine elementary étale
base change, to a quasi-compact open with geometrically connected fibres.
declarations.statement: theorem exists_etaleNeighborhood_geometricallyConnected : Statement055W.{u}

declarations.name: Module.FinitePresentation.of_restrictScalars_of_finiteType
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0561.** Let `R → S` be a ring map of finite type and let `M` be an `S`-module which
is finitely presented as an `R`-module. Then `M` is finitely presented as an `S`-module.

Mathlib's `Module.FinitePresentation.trans` is the converse implication: it deduces finite
presentation over `R` from finite presentation over `S` together with finite presentation of `S`
over `R`. Mathlib's own declaration carrying the tag `0561`,
`Algebra.FinitePresentation.of_restrict_scalars_finitePresentation`, is not this lemma but the
analogue for algebras in place of modules.
declarations.statement:
theorem Module.FinitePresentation.of_restrictScalars_of_finiteType (R S M : Type*) [CommRing R]
    [CommRing S] [Algebra R S] [AddCommGroup M] [Module R M] [Module S M] [IsScalarTower R S M]
    [Algebra.FiniteType R S] [Module.FinitePresentation R M] : Module.FinitePresentation S M
declarations.comment: the module statement, not the analogue for algebras

declarations.name: Module.FinitePresentation.restrictScalars_iff
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0564.** Let `R → S` be a finite and finitely presented ring map and let `M` be an
`S`-module, regarded as an `R`-module by restriction of scalars. Then `M` is finitely presented
as an `R`-module if and only if `M` is finitely presented as an `S`-module.
declarations.statement:
public theorem restrictScalars_iff (R S M : Type*) [CommRing R] [CommRing S] [Algebra R S]
    [AddCommGroup M] [Module R M] [Module S M] [IsScalarTower R S M]
    [Module.Finite R S] [Algebra.FinitePresentation R S] :
    Module.FinitePresentation R M ↔ Module.FinitePresentation S M

declarations.name: bigLambda_injective_iff_bigPhi_injective
declarations.doc:
The map `Λ : M → ⨁_i M_{f_i}`, `m ↦ (m/1, ..., m/1)`,
is injective if and only if the map `Φ : M → ⨁_i M`, `m ↦ (f_1 m, ..., f_n m)`, is
injective.
declarations.statement:
theorem bigLambda_injective_iff_bigPhi_injective
    (n : ℕ) (f : Fin n → R) :
    Function.Injective (bigLambda (M := M) n f) ↔ Function.Injective (bigPhi (M := M) n f)

declarations.name: weaklyAssociated_iff_localization_and_exists_radical_eq
declarations.statement:
theorem weaklyAssociated_iff_localization_and_exists_radical_eq
    (p : Ideal R) [p.IsPrime] :
    (WeaklyAssociated p M ↔
      WeaklyAssociated (IsLocalRing.maximalIdeal (Localization.AtPrime p))
        (LocalizedModule.AtPrime p M))
    ∧ (WeaklyAssociated (IsLocalRing.maximalIdeal (Localization.AtPrime p))
        (LocalizedModule.AtPrime p M) ↔
      ∃ t : LocalizedModule.AtPrime p M,
        (annihilatorOfElem_semiring (R := Localization.AtPrime p) t).radical
          = IsLocalRing.maximalIdeal (Localization.AtPrime p))

declarations.name: main_theorem0567
declarations.doc: **A regular ring is normal.**
declarations.statement:
theorem main_theorem0567 (R : Type*) [CommRing R] [IsRegularRing R] :

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.isNormal_of_isRegular
declarations.doc: **Stacks Project, Tag 0569.** Every regular scheme is normal.
declarations.statement:
public theorem isNormal_of_isRegular (X : Scheme.{u}) (hX : IsRegular X) :
    IsNormal X
declarations.comment:
a regular scheme is normal; the sole hypothesis is `IsRegular` of Tag 02IS, whose
  `IsRegularRing` already carries Noetherianness, so nothing beyond the source is assumed

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.ker_SpecMap_eq_ker_SpecMap_quotientMk
declarations.doc:
The scheme-theoretic image of `Spec B ⟶ Spec A` and the closed subscheme
`Spec (A ⧸ ker φ)` of `Spec A` are cut out by the same ideal sheaf.
declarations.statement:
theorem ker_SpecMap_eq_ker_SpecMap_quotientMk :
    (Spec.map φ).ker =
      (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (Ideal.Quotient.mk (RingHom.ker φ.hom)))).ker
declarations.comment: equal closed subschemes

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.imageSpecMapIso
declarations.doc: The scheme-theoretic image of `Spec B ⟶ Spec A` is `Spec (A ⧸ ker φ)`.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def imageSpecMapIso :
    (Spec.map φ).image ≅ Spec (.of (A ⧸ RingHom.ker φ.hom))

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.imageSpecMapIso_hom_comp
declarations.doc: The isomorphism `imageSpecMapIso` lies over `Spec A`.
declarations.statement:
theorem imageSpecMapIso_hom_comp :
    (imageSpecMapIso φ).hom ≫
        Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (Ideal.Quotient.mk (RingHom.ker φ.hom))) =
      (Spec.map φ).imageι
declarations.comment: over Spec A

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.Hom.ker_eq_vanishingIdeal_closure_range
declarations.doc:
The scheme-theoretic image of a morphism `f : X ⟶ Y` with `X` reduced is the reduced induced
closed subscheme structure on the closure of `Set.range f`, that is, the closed subscheme cut out
by the vanishing ideal sheaf of that closure.
declarations.statement:
theorem ker_eq_vanishingIdeal_closure_range [IsReduced X] (f : X ⟶ Y) :
    f.ker = IdealSheafData.vanishingIdeal (.closure (Set.range f))

declarations.name: Stacks.Morphisms.schemeTheoreticImage_iso_quotient
declarations.doc:
The scheme-theoretic closure of the finite union of standard opens is the
closed subscheme `Spec (A/I)`, with its canonical map to `Spec A`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem schemeTheoreticImage_iso_quotient [Finite ι] (f : ι → A) :
    ∃ e : (standardOpenUnion f).ι.image ≅ Spec (.of (A ⧸ localizationKernel f)),
      (standardOpenUnion f).ι.imageι =
        e.hom ≫ Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (Ideal.Quotient.mk (localizationKernel f)))
declarations.comment: scheme-theoretic closure

declarations.name: Stacks.Morphisms.quasiCompact_standardOpenUnion
declarations.doc: The inclusion of a finite union of standard opens is quasi-compact.
declarations.statement:
public theorem quasiCompact_standardOpenUnion [Finite ι] (f : ι → A) :
    QuasiCompact (standardOpenUnion f).ι
declarations.comment: quasi-compactness

declarations.name: Stacks.Morphisms.schemeTheoreticallyDense_iff_localizationKernel_eq_bot
declarations.doc:
A finite union of standard opens is scheme-theoretically dense precisely
when the canonical map to the product of localizations is injective.
declarations.statement:
public theorem schemeTheoreticallyDense_iff_localizationKernel_eq_bot [Finite ι]
    (f : ι → A) :
    AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.Opens.IsSchemeTheoreticallyDense (standardOpenUnion f) ↔
      localizationKernel f = ⊥
declarations.comment: scheme-theoretic density

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.dense_open_tfae
declarations.doc:
For an open subscheme of a reduced scheme, topological density, having the whole scheme as
scheme-theoretic closure, and scheme-theoretic density are equivalent.
declarations.statement:
theorem dense_open_tfae {X : Scheme.{u}} [IsReduced X]
    (U : X.Opens) :
    List.TFAE [
      Dense (U : Set X),
      IsIso U.ι.imageι,
      Scheme.Opens.IsSchemeTheoreticallyDense U]

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.isSchemeTheoreticallyDominant_iff_isSchemeTheoreticallyDense
declarations.doc:
For a reduced open subscheme, having scheme-theoretic closure equal to the ambient scheme is
equivalent to being scheme-theoretically dense.
declarations.statement:
lemma isSchemeTheoreticallyDominant_iff_isSchemeTheoreticallyDense
    {X : Scheme.{u}} (U : X.Opens) [IsReduced U] :
    IsSchemeTheoreticallyDominant U.ι ↔ Scheme.Opens.IsSchemeTheoreticallyDense U
declarations.comment: equivalence

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.isReduced_of_isSchemeTheoreticallyDense
declarations.doc: A scheme with a reduced scheme-theoretically dense open subscheme is reduced.
declarations.statement:
lemma isReduced_of_isSchemeTheoreticallyDense
    {X : Scheme.{u}} (U : X.Opens) [IsReduced U]
    (hU : Scheme.Opens.IsSchemeTheoreticallyDense U) : IsReduced X
declarations.comment: reducedness

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.universallyOpen_of_syntomic

declarations.statement:

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.Modules.fromSpec_preimage_supp
declarations.doc:
**The sheaf-theoretic and module-theoretic supports agree.** The inverse image of the
support of a quasi-coherent module `F` under the inclusion `Spec Γ(X, U) → X` of an affine open
`U` is the support of the `Γ(X, U)`-module `Γ(F, U)`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem fromSpec_preimage_supp {X : Scheme.{u}} (F : X.Modules) [F.IsQuasicoherent]
    (U : X.affineOpens) :
    ⇑U.2.fromSpec ⁻¹' SheafOfModules.supp F = Module.support Γ(X, U.1) Γ(F, U.1)
declarations.comment: the sheaf-theoretic and module-theoretic supports agree

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.Modules.mem_support_sections_iff_mem_supp
declarations.doc:
On an affine open, support of the sections module agrees with support of the
quasi-coherent sheaf.
declarations.statement:
public lemma mem_support_sections_iff_mem_supp {X : Scheme.{u}} (F : X.Modules)
    [F.IsQuasicoherent] (U : X.affineOpens) (x : X) (hx : x ∈ U.1) :
    U.2.primeIdealOf ⟨x, hx⟩ ∈ Module.support Γ(X, U.1) Γ(F, U.1) ↔
      x ∈ SheafOfModules.supp F

declarations.name: SheafOfModules.isClosed_supp
declarations.doc: The support of a sheaf of modules of finite type on a topological space is closed.
declarations.comment: closed_support

declarations.name: SheafOfModules.mem_supp_iff_nontrivial_stalk
declarations.doc: A point is in the support of a sheaf of modules if and only if its stalk is nonzero.
declarations.statement:
lemma mem_supp_iff_nontrivial_stalk {X : TopCat.{u}}
    {R : TopCat.Sheaf RingCat.{u} X} (F : SheafOfModules.{u} R) (x : X) :
    x ∈ supp F ↔
      Nontrivial ((show TopCat.Presheaf Ab.{u} X from F.val.presheaf).stalk x)
declarations.comment: support_by_stalk

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.Modules.nontrivial_stalk_iff_nontrivial_fibre
declarations.doc:
A finite type quasi-coherent module has nonzero stalk at `x` exactly when its fibre over
the residue field at `x` is nonzero.
declarations.statement:
lemma nontrivial_stalk_iff_nontrivial_fibre
    {X : Scheme.{u}} (F : X.Modules) [F.IsFiniteType] [F.IsQuasicoherent] (x : X) :
    letI : Module (X.presheaf.stalk x) (F.presheaf.stalk x) :=
      PresheafOfModules.instModuleCarrierStalkCommRingCatCarrierAbPresheafOpensCarrier
        F.val x
    letI : Algebra (X.presheaf.stalk x) (X.residueField x) :=
      (X.residue x).hom.toAlgebra
    Nontrivial (F.presheaf.stalk x) ↔
      Nontrivial (TensorProduct (X.presheaf.stalk x)
        (F.presheaf.stalk x) (X.residueField x))
declarations.comment: support_by_fibre

declarations.name: SheafOfModules.supp_pullback
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 056J.** The support of the pullback of a module of finite type
along a morphism of schemes is the inverse image of its support.
declarations.statement:
theorem supp_pullback {X Y : Scheme.{u}} (f : Y ⟶ X) (F : X.Modules) [F.IsFiniteType] :
    supp ((Scheme.Modules.pullback f).obj F) = f ⁻¹' supp F
declarations.comment: pullback_support
