registrations.comment: pullback_finite_type

declarations.name: Stacks.Divisors.IsWeaklyAssociatedPoint
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 056L, part (1).** A point `x` is *weakly associated* to an `𝒪_X`-module `F` when
the maximal ideal of the local ring `𝒪_{X, x}` is a weakly associated prime of the stalk
`F_x`, that is, when it is minimal among the primes containing the annihilator of some element
of `F_x`.
declarations.statement: abbrev IsWeaklyAssociatedPoint (F : X.Modules) (x : X) : Prop
declarations.comment: part (1)

declarations.name: Stacks.Divisors.weaklyAssociatedPoints
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 056L, part (2).** The set `WeakAss(F)` of points weakly associated to an
`𝒪_X`-module `F`.
declarations.statement: abbrev weaklyAssociatedPoints (F : X.Modules) : Set X
declarations.comment: part (2)

declarations.name: Stacks.Divisors.schemeWeaklyAssociatedPoints
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 056L, part (3).** The weakly associated points `WeakAss(X)` of a scheme `X` are
the weakly associated points of its structure sheaf.
declarations.statement: abbrev schemeWeaklyAssociatedPoints (X : Scheme.{u}) : Set X
declarations.comment: part (3)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.isWeaklyAssociatedPrime_iff_isWeaklyAssociatedPoint
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 056M.** On an affine open, a point is weakly associated to a
quasi-coherent sheaf if and only if its corresponding prime ideal is weakly associated to the
module of sections.
declarations.statement:
theorem isWeaklyAssociatedPrime_iff_isWeaklyAssociatedPoint {X : Scheme.{u}} (F : X.Modules)
    [F.IsQuasicoherent] (U : X.Opens) (hU : IsAffineOpen U) (x : X) (hx : x ∈ U) :
    IsWeaklyAssociatedPrime Γ(X, U) Γ(F, U) (hU.primeIdealOf ⟨x, hx⟩).asIdeal ↔
      Stacks.Divisors.IsWeaklyAssociatedPoint F x

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.topologicalKrullDimAt_subscheme_lt
declarations.doc:
An effective Cartier divisor has smaller local dimension at every point where the ambient
local dimension is finite.
declarations.statement:
theorem topologicalKrullDimAt_subscheme_lt {X : Scheme.{u}}
    (I : X.IdealSheafData) (hI : IsEffectiveCartierDivisor I)
    (x : I.subscheme)
    (hfin : topologicalKrullDimAt X (I.subschemeι x) < ⊤) :
    topologicalKrullDimAt I.subscheme x <
      topologicalKrullDimAt X (I.subschemeι x)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.isEffectiveCartierDivisor_comap_pullback
declarations.doc:
A relative effective Cartier divisor stays effective Cartier under arbitrary base
change.
declarations.statement:
theorem isEffectiveCartierDivisor_comap_pullback {X S S' : Scheme.{u}}
    (f : X ⟶ S) (g : S' ⟶ S) (I : X.IdealSheafData)
    (hI : IsEffectiveCartierDivisor I)
    [Flat (I.subschemeι ≫ f)] :
    IsEffectiveCartierDivisor
      (I.comap (pullback.snd g f))

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.geometricallyConnected_of_comp_of_connectedSpace
declarations.doc:
If a connected scheme over a field admits a morphism over that field from a geometrically
connected scheme, then it is geometrically connected.
declarations.statement:
public lemma geometricallyConnected_of_comp_of_connectedSpace
    (k : Type u) [Field k] {T X : Scheme.{u}} (f : T ⟶ X)
    (p : X ⟶ Spec (.of k)) [GeometricallyConnected (f ≫ p)] [ConnectedSpace X] :
    GeometricallyConnected p

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.isRegular_of_smooth_over_field
declarations.doc: **Stacks Project, Tag 056S.** A scheme smooth over a field is regular.
declarations.statement:
public theorem isRegular_of_smooth_over_field
    {k : Type u} [Field k] {X : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ Spec (.of k)) [Smooth f] :
    IsRegular X

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.isGeometricallyRegular_of_smooth
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 056T**, the geometric-regularity conclusion: a scheme smooth over a
field `k` is geometrically regular over `k`.

Proved at every point of the base change, not only at the points lying over the given point.
declarations.statement:
public theorem isGeometricallyRegular_of_smooth {k : Type u} [Field k] {X : Scheme.{u}}
    (f : X ⟶ Spec (.of k)) [Smooth f] : IsGeometricallyRegular f
declarations.comment: geometrically regular

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.isGeometricallyNormal_of_smooth
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 056T**, the geometric-normality conclusion: a scheme smooth over a
field `k` is geometrically normal over `k`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem isGeometricallyNormal_of_smooth {k : Type u} [Field k] {X : Scheme.{u}}
    (f : X ⟶ Spec (.of k)) [Smooth f] : IsGeometricallyNormal f
declarations.comment: geometrically normal

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.geometricallyReduced_of_smooth
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 056T**, the geometric-reducedness conclusion: a smooth morphism of
schemes is geometrically reduced, that is, its base change to every field-valued point of the
target is a reduced scheme.

The source fixes a field `k` as the base; no base field is needed, a morphism `Spec K ⟶ Spec k`
being the same thing as a field extension of `k`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem geometricallyReduced_of_smooth {X Y : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ Y) [Smooth f] :
    GeometricallyReduced f
declarations.comment: geometrically reduced

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.dense_closedPoints_with_finite_separable_residueField_of_smooth
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 056U.** If `X` is smooth over a field `k`, then the closed points of
`X` whose residue fields are finite separable extensions of `k` are dense in `X`.
declarations.statement:
theorem dense_closedPoints_with_finite_separable_residueField_of_smooth
    {k : Type u} [Field k] {X : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ Spec (.of k)) [Smooth f] :
    Dense {x : X | x ∈ closedPoints X ∧
      letI := ((Scheme.ΓSpecIso (.of k)).inv ≫ f.appTop ≫ X.Γevaluation x).hom.toAlgebra
      Module.Finite k (X.residueField x) ∧
        Algebra.IsSeparable k (X.residueField x)}

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.geometricallyReduced_iff_exists_dense_open_smooth
declarations.doc:
A reduced scheme locally of finite type over a field is geometrically reduced if and only if
it contains a dense open subscheme smooth over that field.
declarations.statement:
public theorem geometricallyReduced_iff_exists_dense_open_smooth
    {k : Type u} [Field k] {X : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ Spec (.of k))
    [IsReduced X] [LocallyOfFiniteType f] :
    GeometricallyReduced f ↔
      ∃ U : X.Opens, Dense (U : Set X) ∧ Smooth (U.ι ≫ f)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.Hom.isNormal_of_smooth
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 056W.** A smooth morphism of schemes is normal: it is flat at every
point and all of its fibres are geometrically normal.
declarations.statement: public theorem isNormal_of_smooth {X Y : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ Y) [Smooth f] : f.IsNormal

declarations.name: Stacks.AlgebraicGeometry.exists_affineOpen_effectiveCartierDivisor_of_isRegular_fiber
declarations.doc:
Let `f : X ⟶ S` be locally of finite presentation and flat at `x : X`, and let `h` be an
element of the maximal ideal of `𝒪_{X, x}` whose image in the local ring of the fibre `X_{f x}`
at `x` is a nonzerodivisor.  Then there is an affine open `U ∋ x` and a global section `a` of `U`
whose germ at `x` is `h`, such that the zero scheme `V(a) ⊆ U` is an effective Cartier divisor
containing `x` which is flat and locally of finite presentation over `S`.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_affineOpen_effectiveCartierDivisor_of_isRegular_fiber (f : X ⟶ S)
    [LocallyOfFinitePresentation f] (x : X) (h : X.presheaf.stalk x)
    (hh : h ∈ IsLocalRing.maximalIdeal (X.presheaf.stalk x))
    (hflat : IsFlatAt f.toLRSHom.toShHom x)
    (hregular : IsRegular (((f.fiberι (f x)).stalkMap (f.asFiber x)).hom
      ((f.fiberι_asFiber x).symm ▸ h))) :
    ∃ (U : X.affineOpens) (hx : x ∈ U.1) (a : Γ(U.1.toScheme, ⊤)),
      let y : U.1.toScheme := ⟨x, hx⟩
      let I : U.1.toScheme.IdealSheafData :=
        Scheme.IdealSheafData.ofIdealTop (Ideal.span {a})
      (U.1.ι.stalkMap y).hom ((show U.1.ι y = x by rfl).symm ▸ h) =
          U.1.toScheme.presheaf.germ ⊤ y (by trivial) a ∧
        y ∈ I.support ∧
        Stacks.Divisors.IsEffectiveCartierDivisor I ∧
        Flat (I.subschemeι ≫ U.1.ι ≫ f) ∧
        LocallyOfFinitePresentation (I.subschemeι ≫ U.1.ι ≫ f)

declarations.name: Stacks.AlgebraicGeometry.exists_affineOpen_effectiveCartierDivisor_of_one_le_depth
declarations.doc:
Let `f : X ⟶ S` be locally of finite presentation and flat at `x : X`, and assume the local
ring of the fibre `X_{f x}` at `x` has depth at least one.  Then some affine open neighbourhood
of `x` carries an effective Cartier divisor through `x` which is flat and locally of finite
presentation over `S`.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_affineOpen_effectiveCartierDivisor_of_one_le_depth (f : X ⟶ S)
    [LocallyOfFinitePresentation f] (x : X) (hflat : IsFlatAt f.toLRSHom.toShHom x)
    (hdepth : (1 : ℕ∞) ≤
      Module.depth ((f.fiber (f x)).presheaf.stalk (f.asFiber x))
        (IsLocalRing.maximalIdeal ((f.fiber (f x)).presheaf.stalk (f.asFiber x)))
        ((f.fiber (f x)).presheaf.stalk (f.asFiber x))) :
    ∃ (U : X.affineOpens) (I : U.1.toScheme.IdealSheafData),
      x ∈ Set.range (I.subschemeι ≫ U.1.ι) ∧
        Stacks.Divisors.IsEffectiveCartierDivisor I ∧
        Flat (I.subschemeι ≫ U.1.ι ≫ f) ∧
        LocallyOfFinitePresentation (I.subschemeι ≫ U.1.ι ≫ f)

declarations.name: Stacks.AlgebraicGeometry.exists_regularImmersion_flat_locallyQuasiFinite_singleton_fiber_of_isCohenMacaulayAt
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Lemma 37.23.4 (Tag 0570).**  Let `f : X ⟶ S` be locally of finite
presentation, let `x : X` be a point at which `f` is Cohen–Macaulay, and assume `x` is closed in
its fibre `X_{f x}`.  Then there is a regular immersion `i : Z ⟶ X` through `x` such that `Z` is
flat, locally of finite presentation and locally quasi-finite over `S`, and such that the fibre
of `Z` over `f x` is set-theoretically the single point of `Z` above `x`.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_regularImmersion_flat_locallyQuasiFinite_singleton_fiber_of_isCohenMacaulayAt
    {X S : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ S) [LocallyOfFinitePresentation f] (x : X)
    (hCM : ∃ hf : ∀ y : S, IsLocallyNoetherian (f.fiber y),
      Scheme.Hom.IsCohenMacaulayAt f hf x)
    (hclosed : IsClosed ({f.asFiber x} : Set (f.fiber (f x)))) :
    ∃ (Z : Scheme.{u}) (i : Z ⟶ X) (z : Z) (hi : IsImmersion i),
      letI := hi
      i z = x ∧ IsRegularImmersion i ∧
        Flat (i ≫ f) ∧ LocallyOfFinitePresentation (i ≫ f) ∧
        LocallyQuasiFinite (i ≫ f) ∧
        {z' : Z | (i ≫ f) z' = f x} = {z}

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.exists_flat_locallyQuasiFinite_factorization_through
declarations.doc:
A point in the image of a flat morphism `f : X ⟶ S` locally of
finite presentation lies in the image of some `g : S' ⟶ S` which factors as `h ≫ f` through `f`
and is flat, locally of finite presentation and locally quasi-finite.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_flat_locallyQuasiFinite_factorization_through
    {X S : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ S) [Flat f] [LocallyOfFinitePresentation f]
    (s : S) (hs : s ∈ Set.range f) :
    ∃ (S' : Scheme.{u}) (g : S' ⟶ S) (h : S' ⟶ X),
      h ≫ f = g ∧ Flat g ∧ LocallyOfFinitePresentation g ∧
        LocallyOfFiniteType g ∧ LocallyQuasiFinite g ∧ s ∈ Set.range g

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.hasLocallyQuasiFiniteRefinement
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0572.** An fppf covering `𝒰` of a scheme `S` is refined by an fppf
covering `{T_j ⟶ S}`, indexed by the points of `S`, each member of which is locally
quasi-finite over `S`.

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.exists_open_isSchemeTheoreticallyDense_fiber
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0573.** Let `f : X ⟶ Y` be a finite type morphism of schemes with `Y`
irreducible with generic point `η`, and let `U ⊆ X` be an open subscheme whose trace on the fibre
over `η` is scheme-theoretically dense there. Then there is a nonempty open `V ⊆ Y` such that the
trace of `U` on the fibre over `y` is scheme-theoretically dense for every `y ∈ V`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem exists_open_isSchemeTheoreticallyDense_fiber {X Y : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ Y)
    [IrreducibleSpace Y] [LocallyOfFiniteType f] [QuasiCompact f] (U : X.Opens) (η : Y)
    (hη : IsGenericPoint η Set.univ)
    (hηU : Scheme.Opens.IsSchemeTheoreticallyDense (f.fiberι η ⁻¹ᵁ U)) :
    ∃ V : Y.Opens, (V : Set Y).Nonempty ∧ ∀ y ∈ V,
      Scheme.Opens.IsSchemeTheoreticallyDense (f.fiberι y ⁻¹ᵁ U)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.exists_open_forall_not_isReduced_fiber
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0575.** If the generic fibre of a finite type morphism to an
irreducible scheme is nonreduced, then every fibre over a suitable nonempty open subset of
the target is nonreduced.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_open_forall_not_isReduced_fiber
    {X Y : AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ Y)
    [IrreducibleSpace Y] [AlgebraicGeometry.LocallyOfFiniteType f]
    [AlgebraicGeometry.QuasiCompact f] (η : Y) (hη : IsGenericPoint η Set.univ)
    (h : ¬ AlgebraicGeometry.IsReduced (f.fiber η)) :
    ∃ V : Set Y, IsOpen V ∧ V.Nonempty ∧
      ∀ y ∈ V, ¬ AlgebraicGeometry.IsReduced (f.fiber y)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.geometricallyReduced_fiber_set_eq_preimage_of_isPullback
declarations.doc: The locus of geometrically reduced fibres commutes with arbitrary base change.
declarations.statement:
theorem geometricallyReduced_fiber_set_eq_preimage_of_isPullback
    {X Y X' Y' : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ Y) (f' : X' ⟶ Y') (i : X' ⟶ X) (g : Y' ⟶ Y)
    (h : IsPullback i f' f g) :
    {y' : Y' | GeometricallyReduced (f'.fiberToSpecResidueField y')} =
      g ⁻¹' {y : Y | GeometricallyReduced (f.fiberToSpecResidueField y)}

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.exists_open_forall_not_geometricallyReduced_fiber
declarations.doc:
If the generic fibre of a finite type morphism to an irreducible scheme is not geometrically
reduced, then every fibre over a suitable nonempty open subset of the target is not geometrically
reduced.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_open_forall_not_geometricallyReduced_fiber
    {X Y : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ Y)
    [IrreducibleSpace Y] [LocallyOfFiniteType f]
    [QuasiCompact f] (η : Y) (hη : IsGenericPoint η Set.univ)
    (h : ¬ GeometricallyReduced (f.fiberToSpecResidueField η)) :
    ∃ V : Set Y, IsOpen V ∧ V.Nonempty ∧
      ∀ y ∈ V, ¬ GeometricallyReduced (f.fiberToSpecResidueField y)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.exists_opens_nonempty_geometricallyReduced_morphismRestrict_of_finiteType
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0578.** Let `f : X ⟶ Y` be a morphism of finite type onto an
irreducible scheme with generic point `η`. If the fibre of `f` over `η` is geometrically reduced,
then there is a nonempty open subscheme `V ⊆ Y` such that `X_V ⟶ V` has geometrically reduced
fibres.

Finite presentation is reached by the source's own bridge, Stacks 052A. The base is replaced by
its reduction `r : Y_red ⟶ Y`, which is a universal homeomorphism, so it carries opens and
generic points across and, by Stacks 0576, carries the geometrically reduced fibre locus of the
base change back to that of `f`. Over the reduced base generic flatness
`AlgebraicGeometry.exists_dense_open_flat_finitePresentation_structureSheaf` supplies a dense
open `U ⊆ Y_red` over which the base change is of finite presentation; the generic point lies in
`U` because `U` is dense, so the finite presentation case applies over `U` and produces an open
subset of `U` inside the locus and containing the generic point. Its image in `Y` under the open
immersion of `U` followed by the homeomorphism `r` is open, nonempty and inside the locus of
`f`.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_opens_nonempty_geometricallyReduced_morphismRestrict_of_finiteType
    {X Y : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ Y) [IrreducibleSpace Y]
    [LocallyOfFiniteType f] [QuasiCompact f] (η : Y)
    (hη : IsGenericPoint η (Set.univ : Set Y))
    [GeometricallyReduced (f.fiberToSpecResidueField η)] :
    ∃ V : Y.Opens, Nonempty V ∧ GeometricallyReduced (f ∣_ V)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.isLocallyConstructible_geometricallyReduced_fiber_of_isAffine
declarations.doc:
**The affine Noetherian case of Stacks 0579.** For a morphism `g : X ⟶ S` of finite
presentation between affine schemes with `S` locally Noetherian, the set of points of `S` whose
fibre is geometrically reduced is locally constructible.

Comparing `g` with `Spec Γ(X, ⊤) ⟶ Spec Γ(S, ⊤)` gives a cartesian square with isomorphisms along
the top and bottom, so Stacks 0576 identifies the locus with the inverse image of the locus of the
latter; that locus is `Algebra.geometricallyReducedFibreLocus Γ(S, ⊤) Γ(X, ⊤)` by
`AlgebraicGeometry.geometricallyReduced_fiberToSpecResidueField_specMap_iff`, which is
constructible by `Algebra.isConstructible_geometricallyReducedFibreLocus'`; and Stacks 054I takes
local constructibility back along the isomorphism.
declarations.comment:
affine Noetherian case: `X` and `S` affine with `S` locally Noetherian. The source
states the lemma for an arbitrary quasi-compact morphism locally of finite presentation.

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.isLocallyConstructible_geometricallyReduced_fiber
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0579.** Let `f : X ⟶ Y` be a quasi-compact morphism of schemes which
is locally of finite presentation. Then the set of points of `Y` whose fibre is geometrically
reduced is locally constructible in `Y`.

Local constructibility is tested on the affine opens of `Y`
(`AlgebraicGeometry.isLocallyConstructible_iff_forall_affineOpens`). Over an affine open `U` the
restriction `f ∣_ U` is again quasi-compact and locally of finite presentation, and its
geometrically reduced fibre locus is the inverse image of that of `f` by Stacks 0576, so
`AlgebraicGeometry.isConstructible_geometricallyReduced_fiber_of_isAffine_target` applies.

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.exists_common_refinement
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 057A, part (1).** Two étale neighborhoods of a point
admit a common refinement.
declarations.comment: part (1)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.exists_equalizing_refinement
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 057A, part (2).** Two neighborhood maps which induce
the same map on residue fields become equal after a refinement.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_equalizing_refinement (f g : U ⟶ V)
    (hκ : (V.scheme.residueFieldCongr f.map_point).inv ≫
        f.hom.residueFieldMap U.point =
      (V.scheme.residueFieldCongr g.map_point).inv ≫
        g.hom.residueFieldMap U.point) :
    ∃ W : EtaleNeighborhood S s, ∃ h : W ⟶ U, h ≫ f = h ≫ g
declarations.comment: part (2)

declarations.name: Stacks.EtaleCohomology.isCofiltered_elementaryEtaleNeighborhood
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 057B.** The category of elementary étale neighbourhoods of a point of a scheme is
cofiltered: two neighbourhoods are dominated by their fibre product and two morphisms of
elementary neighbourhoods are equalized after a refinement, both by Tag 057A.
declarations.statement:
public instance isCofiltered_elementaryEtaleNeighborhood (X : Scheme.{u}) (x : X) :
    IsCofiltered (ElementaryEtaleNeighborhood X x)

declarations.name: Stacks.AlgebraicGeometry.exists_smooth_effectiveCartierDivisor_of_nonzero_differential
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 057C.** A local equation with nonzero relative
differential cuts out a smooth effective Cartier divisor near the point.
declarations.statement:
public theorem exists_smooth_effectiveCartierDivisor_of_nonzero_differential
    {X S : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ S) (x : X)
    (h : X.presheaf.stalk x)
    (hh : h ∈ IsLocalRing.maximalIdeal (X.presheaf.stalk x))
    (hf : InfinitesimalLifting.SmoothAt f x)
    (hdh : HasNonzeroRelativeDifferential f x h) :
    ∃ (U : X.Opens) (_hU : IsAffineOpen U) (hxU : x ∈ U)
      (a : Γ(X, U)) (I : U.toScheme.IdealSheafData),
      ((TopCat.Presheaf.germ X.presheaf U x hxU).hom a = h) ∧
      (∀ V : U.toScheme.affineOpens,
        I.ideal V = Ideal.span
          {((U.toScheme.presheaf.map (homOfLE le_top).op).hom
            (U.topIso.inv.hom a))}) ∧
      Stacks.Divisors.IsEffectiveCartierDivisor I ∧
      (⟨x, hxU⟩ : U.toScheme) ∈ I.support ∧
      Smooth (I.subschemeι ≫ U.ι ≫ f)

declarations.name: Stacks.AlgebraicGeometry.exists_smooth_divisor_of_nonzero_differential_kernel
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 057D.**  Let `f : X ⟶ S` be smooth at `x`, with image `s = f x`.  If
the map `Ω_{X_s/s,x} ⊗_{𝒪_{X_s,x}} κ(x) ⟶ Ω_{κ(x)/κ(s)}` has a nonzero kernel, then there is an
affine open neighbourhood `U` of `x` and an effective Cartier divisor `D ⊆ U` containing `x`
with `D ⟶ S` smooth.
declarations.statement:
public theorem exists_smooth_divisor_of_nonzero_differential_kernel
    (hf : InfinitesimalLifting.SmoothAt f x)
    (hker :
      letI := algebraResidueFiber f x
      letI := algebraFiberResidue f x
      letI := algebraTargetResidueResidueField f x
      letI := isScalarTower_targetResidue_fiberStalk_residueField f x
      ¬ Function.Injective (KaehlerDifferential.mapBaseChange (targetResidue f x)
        (ToType ((f.fiber (f x)).sheaf.presheaf.stalk (fiberPoint f x)))
        (ToType (X.residueField x)))) :
    ∃ (U : X.Opens) (_hU : IsAffineOpen U) (hxU : x ∈ U)
      (I : U.toScheme.IdealSheafData),
      Stacks.Divisors.IsEffectiveCartierDivisor I ∧
      (⟨x, hxU⟩ : U.toScheme) ∈ I.support ∧
      Smooth (I.subschemeι ≫ U.ι ≫ f)

declarations.name: Stacks.AlgebraicGeometry.not_exists_etale_lift_through_inseparableClosedPoint
declarations.doc:
**No étale lift through an inseparable closed point.**  Let `k` be a field of characteristic
`p > 0` and let `a ∈ k` not be a `p`-th power, so that `k` is imperfect.  For the closed point `w`
of `X = 𝐀²_k` given by the maximal ideal `(x, y^p - a)` and the projection `f : X ⟶ S = 𝐀¹_k`,
there is no commutative diagram `h : S' ⟶ X`, `g : S' ⟶ S` with `h ≫ f = g`, `g` étale, and `w`
in the image of `h`.
declarations.statement:
theorem not_exists_etale_lift_through_inseparableClosedPoint {k : Type u} [Field k] {p : ℕ}
    [Fact p.Prime] [CharP k p] (a : k) (ha : ∀ b : k, b ^ p ≠ a) :
    ¬ ∃ (S' : Scheme.{u}) (g : S' ⟶ affineLine k) (h : S' ⟶ affinePlane k),
        Etale g ∧ h ≫ projection k = g ∧ closedPoint a ha ∈ Set.range h.base

declarations.name: Stacks.AlgebraicGeometry.exists_smooth_divisor_of_separable_residueField
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 057F.**  Let `f : X ⟶ S` be smooth at `x`, with image `s = f x`.  If
the residue field extension `κ(x)/κ(s)` is separable and `x` is not a generic point of the fibre
`X_s`, then there is an affine open neighbourhood `U` of `x` and an effective Cartier divisor
`D ⊆ U` containing `x` with `D ⟶ S` smooth.
declarations.statement:
public theorem exists_smooth_divisor_of_separable_residueField
    (hf : InfinitesimalLifting.SmoothAt f x)
    (hsep : letI := (f.residueFieldMap x).hom.toAlgebra
      Algebra.IsSeparableExtension (ToType (S.residueField (f x)))
        (ToType (X.residueField x)))
    (hngen : f.asFiber x ∉ genericPoints (f.fiber (f x))) :
    ∃ (U : X.Opens) (_hU : IsAffineOpen U) (hxU : x ∈ U)
      (I : U.toScheme.IdealSheafData),
      Stacks.Divisors.IsEffectiveCartierDivisor I ∧
      (⟨x, hxU⟩ : U.toScheme) ∈ I.support ∧
      Smooth (I.subschemeι ≫ U.ι ≫ f)

declarations.name: Stacks.AlgebraicGeometry.exists_etale_immersion_with_singleton_fiber
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 057G.**  Let `f : X ⟶ S` be a morphism of schemes, `x : X` a point with
image `s = f x`.  If `f` is smooth at `x`, if `x` is a closed point of the fibre `X_s`, and if the
residue field extension `κ(x)/κ(s)` is separable, then there is an immersion `i : Z ⟶ X` whose
image contains `x` such that `Z ⟶ S` is étale and `Z_s = {x}` set theoretically.
declarations.statement:
public theorem exists_etale_immersion_with_singleton_fiber
    {X S : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ S) (x : X)
    (hsmooth : InfinitesimalLifting.SmoothAt f x)
    (hclosed : IsClosed ({f.asFiber x} : Set (f.fiber (f x))))
    (hsep : letI := (f.residueFieldMap x).hom.toAlgebra
      Algebra.IsSeparableExtension (S.residueField (f x)) (X.residueField x)) :
    ∃ (Z : Scheme.{u}) (i : Z ⟶ X) (z : Z),
      IsImmersion i ∧ i z = x ∧ Etale (i ≫ f) ∧
        {z' : Z | (i ≫ f) z' = f x} = {z}

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.exists_compactOpen_geometricallyConnected_fibers
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 057I.** A geometrically connected fibre in a flat, finitely presented
family with geometrically reduced fibres and a nonempty finite locally free multisection has a
quasi-compact open neighbourhood in the source whose nonempty fibres are geometrically
connected.
declarations.statement: theorem exists_compactOpen_geometricallyConnected_fibers : Statement057I.{u}

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.exists_etaleNeighborhood_geometricallyIntegral
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 057J.** A geometrically irreducible open in a fibre of a normal,
finitely presented morphism spreads, after an affine elementary étale base change, to a
quasi-compact open with geometrically integral fibres.
declarations.statement: theorem exists_etaleNeighborhood_geometricallyIntegral : Statement057J.{u}

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.exists_finite_over_smooth
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 057K.** A morphism locally of finite type is, in elementary étale
neighbourhoods of a point and of its image, finite over a smooth morphism of relative dimension
the dimension of the fibre at that point, with geometrically integral fibres and purely
transcendental residue field extension; and the finite morphism is of finite presentation as
soon as the original one is.
declarations.statement: theorem exists_finite_over_smooth : Statement057K.{u}

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.exists_finite_over_smooth_affine
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 057L.** The finite-over-smooth local structure of a locally
finite-type morphism can be obtained with all three new schemes affine.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_finite_over_smooth_affine {X S : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ S) [LocallyOfFiniteType f]
    (x : X) :
    ∃ (n : ℕ) (_ : topologicalKrullDimAt (f.fiber (f x)) (f.asFiber x) = n)
      (U : EtaleNeighborhood X x) (V : EtaleNeighborhood S (f x))
      (Y : Scheme.{u}) (h : Y ⟶ V.scheme) (π : U.scheme ⟶ Y),
      U.IsElementary ∧ V.IsElementary ∧ (U.toBase ≫ f = π ≫ h ≫ V.toBase) ∧
        SmoothOfRelativeDimension n h ∧
        (∀ s' : V.scheme, GeometricallyIntegral (h.fiberToSpecResidueField s')) ∧
        IsFinite π ∧ (∀ z : U.scheme, π z = π U.point ↔ z = U.point) ∧
        (∃ heq : h (π U.point) = V.point,
          letI : Algebra (V.scheme.residueField V.point) (Y.residueField (π U.point)) :=
            ((V.scheme.residueFieldCongr heq).inv ≫ h.residueFieldMap (π U.point)).hom.toAlgebra
          PurelyTranscendental (V.scheme.residueField V.point)
            (Y.residueField (π U.point))) ∧
        (LocallyOfFinitePresentation f → FinitePresentation π) ∧
        IsAffine V.scheme ∧ IsAffine Y ∧ IsAffine U.scheme

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.exists_finitePresentation_closedSubscheme_fiber_eq_supp
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 057Q].** Let `f : X ⟶ S` be a finite type morphism of affine schemes and let
`F` be a quasi-coherent `𝒪_X`-module of finite type. For every point `s` of `S` there is a closed
immersion `i : Z ⟶ X` of finite presentation and a quasi-coherent finite type `𝒪_Z`-module `G`
with `i_* G ≅ F` whose fibre over `s` is the support of the restriction of `F` to the fibre of
`X` over `s`.

The equality of the fibre with the support is an equality of subsets of `X`: the image of the
fibre of `Z` is the image of the support of the pullback of `F` to the fibre of `X`.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_finitePresentation_closedSubscheme_fiber_eq_supp {S : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ S)
    [IsAffine X] [IsAffine S] [LocallyOfFiniteType f] [QuasiCompact f] (F : X.Modules)
    [F.IsFiniteType] [F.IsQuasicoherent] (s : S) :
    ∃ (Z : Scheme.{u}) (i : Z ⟶ X) (G : Z.Modules)
      (_ : (Scheme.Modules.pushforward i).obj G ≅ F),
      IsClosedImmersion i ∧ FinitePresentation i ∧ G.IsQuasicoherent ∧ G.IsFiniteType ∧
        Set.range (fun z : (i ≫ f).fiber s => i ((i ≫ f).fiberι s z)) =
          f.fiberι s '' SheafOfModules.supp ((Scheme.Modules.pullback (f.fiberι s)).obj F)

declarations.name: Stacks.Etale.exists_etale_lift_of_isClosedImmersion
declarations.doc:
Let `Z → X` be a closed immersion of affine schemes and let `Z' → Z` be an
étale morphism with affine source. Then it is the pullback of an étale morphism
`X' → X` with affine source.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_etale_lift_of_isClosedImmersion
    {Z X Z' : AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.{u}} (i : Z ⟶ X) (p : Z' ⟶ Z)
    [AlgebraicGeometry.IsAffine Z] [AlgebraicGeometry.IsAffine X]
    [AlgebraicGeometry.IsAffine Z'] [AlgebraicGeometry.IsClosedImmersion i]
    [AlgebraicGeometry.Etale p] :
    ∃ (X' : AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.{u}) (f : X' ⟶ X),
      AlgebraicGeometry.IsAffine X' ∧ AlgebraicGeometry.Etale f ∧
        ∃ e : Z' ≅ pullback i f, e.hom ≫ pullback.fst i f = p

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.exists_elementaryDevissage
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 057S.** A finite-type quasi-coherent module admits an elementary
dévissage at any point of the support of its fibre.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_elementaryDevissage {X S : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ S) [LocallyOfFiniteType f]
    (F : X.Modules) [F.IsFiniteType] [F.IsQuasicoherent] (x : X)
    (hx : f.asFiber x ∈
      SheafOfModules.supp ((Scheme.Modules.pullback (f.fiberι (f x))).obj F)) :
    Nonempty (ElementaryDevissage f F x hx)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.ElementaryDevissage.finitePresentation_π
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 057T.** The finite morphism `π` of an elementary dévissage of a
morphism locally of finite presentation is of finite presentation.

The composite `Z ⟶ Y ⟶ V` equals `Z ⟶ U ⟶ X ⟶ S`, which is locally of finite presentation
because the closed immersion `i` is, `U ⟶ X` is étale and `f` is; the structure morphism
`V ⟶ S` is locally of finite type, so Stacks 02FV strips it off twice and leaves `π` locally of
finite presentation. A finite morphism is quasi-compact and quasi-separated, so `π` is of finite
presentation.
declarations.statement:
theorem finitePresentation_π [LocallyOfFinitePresentation f] (D : ElementaryDevissage f F x hx) :
    FinitePresentation D.π
declarations.comment: finite presentation of π

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.ElementaryDevissage.isFinitePresentationNear_iff_closed
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 057T**, the equivalence of conditions (1) and (2). In an elementary
dévissage, `F` is of finite presentation near `x` exactly when the module `G` on the closed
subscheme is of finite presentation near `z`.

Finite presentation near `x` passes to the étale neighbourhood `U` and back by Stacks 01BQ and
Stacks 05B0; on `U` the module is `i_* G` by the dévissage isomorphism, and the closed immersion
`i` is finite with singleton fibre, so Stacks 05B4 and Stacks 05B8 exchange `i_* G` and `G`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isFinitePresentationNear_iff_closed [F.IsQuasicoherent]
    (D : ElementaryDevissage f F x hx) :
    IsFinitePresentationNear F x ↔ IsFinitePresentationNear D.G D.z
declarations.comment: equivalence of (1), (2) and (3)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.ElementaryDevissage.isFinitePresentationNear_iff_pushforward
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 057T**, the equivalence of conditions (2) and (3). In an elementary
dévissage of a morphism locally of finite presentation, the module `G` is of finite presentation
near `z` exactly when its direct image `π_* G` is of finite presentation near `π z`.

The morphism `π` is finite, of finite presentation by
`AlgebraicGeometry.ElementaryDevissage.finitePresentation_π`, and its fibre over `π z` is `{z}`,
so this is the transfer across a finite morphism with a singleton fibre.
declarations.statement:
theorem isFinitePresentationNear_iff_pushforward [LocallyOfFinitePresentation f]
    (D : ElementaryDevissage f F x hx) :
    IsFinitePresentationNear D.G D.z ↔
      IsFinitePresentationNear ((Scheme.Modules.pushforward D.π).obj D.G) (D.π D.z)
declarations.comment: equivalence of (1), (2) and (3)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.ElementaryDevissage.finitePresentation_stalk_iff_closed
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 057T**, the equivalence of conditions (a) and (b). In an elementary
dévissage the stalk `F_x` is a finitely presented `𝒪_{X,x}`-module exactly when the stalk `G_z`
is a finitely presented `𝒪_{Z,z}`-module.

The étale morphism `U ⟶ X` is flat, so the stalk map `𝒪_{X,x} → 𝒪_{U,i z}` is a flat local
homomorphism and finite presentation of the stalk is unchanged by the pullback; the pullback of
`F` to `U` is `i_* G`; and the closed immersion `i` is finite, of finite presentation and has
singleton fibre, so Stacks 05B8 and Stacks 0564 exchange `(i_* G)_{i z}` and `G_z`.
declarations.statement:
theorem finitePresentation_stalk_iff_closed (D : ElementaryDevissage f F x hx) :
    Module.FinitePresentation (ToType (X.presheaf.stalk x))
        (ToType (TopCat.Presheaf.stalk F.val.presheaf x)) ↔
      Module.FinitePresentation (ToType (D.Z.presheaf.stalk D.z))
        (ToType (TopCat.Presheaf.stalk D.G.val.presheaf D.z))
declarations.comment: equivalence of (a), (b) and (c)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.ElementaryDevissage.finitePresentation_stalk_iff_pushforward
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 057T**, the equivalence of conditions (b) and (c). In an elementary
dévissage of a morphism locally of finite presentation the stalk `G_z` is a finitely presented
`𝒪_{Z,z}`-module exactly when the stalk `(π_* G)_{π z}` is a finitely presented
`𝒪_{Y,π z}`-module.

The morphism `π` is finite, of finite presentation by
`AlgebraicGeometry.ElementaryDevissage.finitePresentation_π`, and its fibre over `π z` is `{z}`,
so this is the transfer of finite presentation of a stalk across a finite morphism with a
singleton fibre.
declarations.statement:
theorem finitePresentation_stalk_iff_pushforward [LocallyOfFinitePresentation f]
    (D : ElementaryDevissage f F x hx) :
    Module.FinitePresentation (ToType (D.Z.presheaf.stalk D.z))
        (ToType (TopCat.Presheaf.stalk D.G.val.presheaf D.z)) ↔
      Module.FinitePresentation (ToType (D.Y.presheaf.stalk (D.π D.z)))
        (ToType (TopCat.Presheaf.stalk
          ((Scheme.Modules.pushforward D.π).obj D.G).val.presheaf (D.π D.z)))
declarations.comment: equivalence of (a), (b) and (c)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.ElementaryDevissage.isFlatOverAt_iff_closed
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 057U**, the equivalence of conditions (a) and (b). In an elementary
dévissage the stalk `F_x` is flat over `𝒪_{S,f x}` exactly when the stalk `G_z` is flat over
`𝒪_{V,h (π z)}`.

The étale morphism `U ⟶ X` is flat, so Stacks 02JZ replaces `F` at `x` by its pullback to `U` at
the distinguished point; Stacks 05B9 replaces flatness over `S` by flatness over `V`; the
pullback of `F` to `U` is `i_* G`; and the closed immersion `i` is finite with singleton fibre,
so Stacks 05B8 exchanges the stalk of `i_* G` for the stalk of `G`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isFlatOverAt_iff_closed [F.IsQuasicoherent] (D : ElementaryDevissage f F x hx) :
    IsFlatOverAt f.toLRSHom.toShHom F x ↔
      IsFlatOverAt (D.π ≫ D.h).toLRSHom.toShHom D.G D.z
declarations.comment: equivalence of (a), (b) and (c)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.ElementaryDevissage.isFlatOverAt_iff_pushforward
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 057U**, the equivalence of conditions (b) and (c). In an elementary
dévissage the stalk `G_z` is flat over `𝒪_{V,h (π z)}` exactly when the stalk `(π_* G)_{π z}`
is.

The morphism `π` is finite and its fibre over `π z` is `{z}`, so this is the transfer of
flatness over the base at a point across a finite morphism with a singleton fibre.
declarations.statement:
theorem isFlatOverAt_iff_pushforward (D : ElementaryDevissage f F x hx) :
    IsFlatOverAt (D.π ≫ D.h).toLRSHom.toShHom D.G D.z ↔
      IsFlatOverAt D.h.toLRSHom.toShHom
        ((Scheme.Modules.pushforward D.π).obj D.G) (D.π D.z)
declarations.comment: equivalence of (a), (b) and (c)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.ElementaryDevissage.isFlatOverNear_iff_closed
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 057U**, the equivalence of conditions (1) and (2). In an elementary
dévissage, `F` is flat over `S` near `x` exactly when `G` is flat over `V` near `z`.

The étale morphism `U ⟶ X` is flat and open, so Stacks 02JZ transfers flatness over the base
near `x` to flatness of the pullback near the distinguished point of `U`; Stacks 05B9 interchanges
flatness over `S` and over `V`; the pullback is `i_* G`; and the closed immersion `i` is finite
with singleton fibre, so Stacks 0FLM and Stacks 05B8 exchange `i_* G` and `G`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isFlatOverNear_iff_closed [F.IsQuasicoherent] (D : ElementaryDevissage f F x hx) :
    IsFlatOverNear f F x ↔ IsFlatOverNear (D.π ≫ D.h) D.G D.z
declarations.comment: equivalence of (1), (2) and (3)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.ElementaryDevissage.isFlatOverNear_iff_pushforward
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 057U**, the equivalence of conditions (2) and (3). In an elementary
dévissage, `G` is flat over `V` near `z` exactly when `π_* G` is flat over `V` near `π z`.

The morphism `π` is finite and its fibre over `π z` is `{z}`, so this is the transfer of
flatness over the base near a point across a finite morphism with a singleton fibre.
declarations.statement:
theorem isFlatOverNear_iff_pushforward (D : ElementaryDevissage f F x hx) :
    IsFlatOverNear (D.π ≫ D.h) D.G D.z ↔
      IsFlatOverNear D.h ((Scheme.Modules.pushforward D.π).obj D.G) (D.π D.z)
declarations.comment: equivalence of (1), (2) and (3)

declarations.name: Module.Flat.tensorProduct_of_flat
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0584 (1)**: if `S → S'` is a flat map of `R`-algebras and `M` is an `S`-module that
is flat over `R`, then `S' ⊗_S M` is flat over `R`.

theorem tensorProduct_of_flat [Module.Flat S S'] [Module.Flat R M] :
    Module.Flat R (S' ⊗[S] M)

declarations.name: Module.Flat.tensorProduct_iff_of_faithfullyFlat
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0584 (2)**: if `S → S'` is a faithfully flat map of `R`-algebras, then an `S`-module
`M` is flat over `R` if and only if `S' ⊗_S M` is flat over `R`.
declarations.statement:
theorem tensorProduct_iff_of_faithfullyFlat {R S S' M : Type*} [CommRing R] [CommRing S]
    [CommRing S'] [Algebra R S] [Algebra R S'] [Algebra S S'] [IsScalarTower R S S']
    [AddCommGroup M] [Module R M] [Module S M] [IsScalarTower R S M]
    [Module.FaithfullyFlat S S'] :
    Module.Flat R (S' ⊗[S] M) ↔ Module.Flat R M

declarations.name: assPrimes_subset_support

the localization `M_p` is nonzero.
declarations.statement:
theorem assPrimes_subset_support (R M : Type*) [CommRing R] [AddCommGroup M] [Module R M] :
    assAssociatedPrimes R M ⊆ Module.support R M
