declarations.name: weakAss_empty_iff_zero
declarations.doc:
Stacks Tag 0588 (Lemma 10.66.5): an `R`-module `M` is the zero module if and
only if it has no weakly associated primes.
declarations.statement:
theorem weakAss_empty_iff_zero {R : Type*} [CommRing R] {M : Type*} [AddCommGroup M]
    [Module R M] :
    (∀ m : M, m = 0) ↔ weaklyAssociatedPrimes R M = ∅

declarations.name: StacksProblem.ass_subset_weakAss_subset_supp
declarations.doc: Stacks tag 0589 (Lemma 10.66.6): `Ass(M) ⊆ WeakAss(M) ⊆ Supp(M)`.
declarations.statement:
theorem ass_subset_weakAss_subset_supp (R : Type*) [CommRing R] (M : Type*)
    [AddCommGroup M] [Module R M] :
    Ass R M ⊆ WeakAss R M ∧ WeakAss R M ⊆ Supp R M

declarations.name: isAssociatedPrime_tfae_of_fg
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 058A.** Let `R` be a ring, `M` an `R`-module and `p` a finitely generated ideal of
`R`. Then `p ∈ Ass(M)`, i.e. `p` is prime and is the annihilator of an element of `M`, iff `p` is
an associated prime of `M` in Mathlib's sense (the radical of the annihilator of an element), iff
`p ∈ WeakAss(M)`, i.e. `p` is minimal among the primes containing the annihilator of an element of
`M`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem isAssociatedPrime_tfae_of_fg {R : Type*} [CommSemiring R] {M : Type*}
    [AddCommMonoid M] [Module R M] {p : Ideal R} (hp : p.FG) :
    List.TFAE [(p.IsPrime ∧ ∃ m : M, p = (R ∙ m).annihilator),
      IsAssociatedPrime p M,
      ∃ m : M, p ∈ (R ∙ m).annihilator.minimalPrimes]

declarations.name: associatedPrimes_eq_setOf_exists_mem_minimalPrimes_annihilator
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 058A**, the Noetherian case. Let `R` be a Noetherian ring and `M` an `R`-module. Then
`Ass(M) = WeakAss(M)`: a prime of `R` is the radical of the annihilator of an element of `M` if and
only if it is minimal among the primes containing the annihilator of an element of `M`.

declarations.name: Module.Flat.iff_exists_factorization_of_finitePresentation
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 058E.** An `R`-module `M` is flat if and only if every `R`-linear map to `M` from a
finitely presented `R`-module `P` factors through a free finite `R`-module: there are `k : ℕ` and
maps `h : P → (Fin k →₀ R)` and `g : (Fin k →₀ R) → M` with `f = g ∘ h`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem Module.Flat.iff_exists_factorization_of_finitePresentation {R : Type u} {M : Type v}
    [CommRing R] [AddCommGroup M] [Module R M] :
    Module.Flat R M ↔ ∀ ⦃P : Type u⦄ [AddCommGroup P] [Module R P]
      [Module.FinitePresentation R P] (f : P →ₗ[R] M),
      ∃ (k : ℕ) (h : P →ₗ[R] (Fin k →₀ R)) (g : (Fin k →₀ R) →ₗ[R] M), f = g ∘ₗ h

declarations.name: Module.Flat.iff_surjective_compRight_of_finitePresentation
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 058F.** An `R`-module `M` is flat if and only if for every finitely presented
`R`-module `P` and every surjection `φ : N → M` of `R`-modules the induced map
`Hom_R(P, N) → Hom_R(P, M)`, postcomposition with `φ`, is surjective.
declarations.statement:
public theorem Module.Flat.iff_surjective_compRight_of_finitePresentation {R : Type u} [CommRing R]
    [Small.{v} R] {M : Type v} [AddCommGroup M] [Module R M] :
    Module.Flat R M ↔
      ∀ (P : Type v) [AddCommGroup P] [Module R P] [Module.FinitePresentation R P]
        ⦃N : Type v⦄ [AddCommGroup N] [Module R N] (φ : N →ₗ[R] M), Function.Surjective φ →
        Function.Surjective (LinearMap.compRight (M := P) R φ)

declarations.name: flat_iff_directLimit_free_finite
declarations.doc:
**Lazard's theorem.**
An `R`-module `M` over a commutative ring `R` is flat if and only if `M` is the
colimit of a directed system of free finite `R`-modules: there exists a directed
(nonempty, filtered) preorder `ι`, a family of `R`-modules `G : ι → Type` with
`R`-linear transition maps `f` forming a `DirectedSystem`, such that every `G i`
is free and finite, together with an `R`-linear isomorphism between the direct
limit `Module.DirectLimit G f` and `M`.
declarations.statement:
theorem flat_iff_directLimit_free_finite {R : Type u} [CommRing R] (M : Type u)
    [AddCommGroup M] [Module R M] :
    Module.Flat R M ↔
      ∃ (ι : Type u) (_ : Preorder ι) (_ : IsDirected ι (· ≤ ·)) (_ : Nonempty ι)
        (_ : DecidableEq ι) (G : ι → Type u) (_ : (i : ι) → AddCommGroup (G i))
        (_ : (i : ι) → Module R (G i)) (f : (i j : ι) → i ≤ j → G i →ₗ[R] G j)
        (_ : DirectedSystem G fun i j h => f i j h),
        (∀ i, Module.Free R (G i)) ∧ (∀ i, Module.Finite R (G i)) ∧
          Nonempty (Module.DirectLimit G f ≃ₗ[R] M)

declarations.name: UniversallyExact
declarations.doc:
The short exact sequence `0 -> M_1 ->[u] M_2 ->[v] M_3 -> 0` is *universally exact* if it
is a short exact sequence (`u` injective, `v` surjective, exact at `M_2`) and the map `u`
is universally injective. This is the second of the two notions of Stacks 058I; the first,
universally injective maps, is `UniversallyInjective`.
declarations.statement:
structure UniversallyExact
    {M₁ M₂ M₃ : Type u} [AddCommGroup M₁] [AddCommGroup M₂] [AddCommGroup M₃]
    [Module R M₁] [Module R M₂] [Module R M₃]
    (u : M₁ →ₗ[R] M₂) (v : M₂ →ₗ[R] M₃) : Prop
declarations.comment: universally exact

declarations.name: UniversallyInjective
declarations.doc:
**Universally injective module map.**
A homomorphism of `R`-modules `f : M →ₗ[R] N` is *universally injective* if for every
`R`-module `Q`, the induced map `f ⊗ id_Q : M ⊗_R Q → N ⊗_R Q` (i.e. `f.rTensor Q`) is
injective. This is the first of the two notions of Stacks 058I; the second, universally exact
short exact sequences, is `UniversallyExact`.
declarations.statement:
def UniversallyInjective {M N : Type v} [AddCommGroup M] [AddCommGroup N]
    [Module R M] [Module R N] (f : M →ₗ[R] N) : Prop
declarations.comment: universally injective

declarations.name: split_universallyExact
declarations.doc:
A split short exact sequence is universally exact; equivalently its first map `f₁`
is universally injective.
declarations.statement:
theorem split_universallyExact
    {M₁ M₂ M₃ : Type v} [AddCommGroup M₁] [Module R M₁]
    [AddCommGroup M₂] [Module R M₂] [AddCommGroup M₃] [Module R M₃]
    (S : ShortExact (R := R) M₁ M₂ M₃) (hS : S.IsSplit) :
    S.UniversallyExact

declarations.name: colim_universallyExact
declarations.doc: Filtered colimits preserve universally exact short exact sequences.
declarations.statement:
theorem colim_universallyExact
    {ι : Type v} [Preorder ι] [IsDirected ι (· ≤ ·)] [Nonempty ι] [DecidableEq ι]
    {M₁ M₂ M₃ : ι → Type v}
    [∀ i, AddCommGroup (M₁ i)] [∀ i, Module R (M₁ i)]
    [∀ i, AddCommGroup (M₂ i)] [∀ i, Module R (M₂ i)]
    [∀ i, AddCommGroup (M₃ i)] [∀ i, Module R (M₃ i)]
    (D : DirectedSES (R := R) ι M₁ M₂ M₃)
    (hD : ∀ i, (D.seq i).UniversallyExact) :
    Function.Injective D.colimF₁ ∧
      Function.Surjective D.colimF₂ ∧
      LinearMap.range D.colimF₁ = LinearMap.ker D.colimF₂ ∧
      UniversallyInjective D.colimF₁

declarations.name: Function.Exact.universallyExact_tfae
declarations.statement:
public theorem Function.Exact.universallyExact_tfae {R : Type u} [CommRing R] [Small.{v} R]
    {M₁ M₂ M₃ : Type v} [AddCommGroup M₁] [Module R M₁] [AddCommGroup M₂] [Module R M₂]
    [AddCommGroup M₃] [Module R M₃] {f₁ : M₁ →ₗ[R] M₂} {f₂ : M₂ →ₗ[R] M₃}
    (h : Function.Exact f₁ f₂) (h₁ : Function.Injective f₁) (h₂ : Function.Surjective f₂) :
    List.TFAE
      [ ∀ (Q : Type v) [AddCommGroup Q] [Module R Q], Function.Injective (f₁.rTensor Q),
        ∀ (Q : Type v) [AddCommGroup Q] [Module R Q] [Module.FinitePresentation R Q],
          Function.Injective (f₁.rTensor Q) ∧ Function.Exact (f₁.rTensor Q) (f₂.rTensor Q) ∧
            Function.Surjective (f₂.rTensor Q),
        ∀ (n m : ℕ) (x : Fin n → M₁) (y : Fin m → M₂) (a : Fin n → Fin m → R),
          (∀ i, f₁ (x i) = ∑ j, a i j • y j) → ∃ z : Fin m → M₁, ∀ i, x i = ∑ j, a i j • z j,
        ∀ (n m : ℕ) (α : (Fin n →₀ R) →ₗ[R] (Fin m →₀ R)) (β : (Fin n →₀ R) →ₗ[R] M₁)
          (γ : (Fin m →₀ R) →ₗ[R] M₂), f₁ ∘ₗ β = γ ∘ₗ α →
            ∃ δ : (Fin m →₀ R) →ₗ[R] M₁, δ ∘ₗ α = β,
        ∀ (P : Type v) [AddCommGroup P] [Module R P] [Module.FinitePresentation R P],
          Function.Surjective (LinearMap.compRight (M := P) R f₂),
        ∃ (J : Type v) (_ : Preorder J) (_ : IsDirected J (· ≤ ·)) (_ : Nonempty J)
            (F : J ⥤ ShortComplex (ModuleCat.{v} R)) (c : Cocone F) (_ : IsColimit c)
            (_ : c.pt ≅ ModuleCat.shortComplexOfCompEqZero f₁ f₂ h.linearMap_comp_eq_zero),
          ∀ j, Nonempty (F.obj j).Splitting ∧ Module.FinitePresentation R (F.obj j).X₃ ∧
            IsIso ((c.ι.app j).τ₁) ]
declarations.comment: Items (1)-(6), in the source's order, as a `List.TFAE`.

declarations.name: Function.Exact.split_iff_forall_rTensor_injective
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 058L.** Let `0 → M₁ →[f₁] M₂ →[f₂] M₃ → 0` be a short exact sequence of `R`-modules
with `M₃` of finite presentation. Then `f₂` admits an `R`-linear section — equivalently, the
sequence is split — if and only if the sequence is universally exact, that is, if and only if
`f₁ ⊗ id_Q : M₁ ⊗ Q → M₂ ⊗ Q` is injective for every `R`-module `Q`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem Function.Exact.split_iff_forall_rTensor_injective {R : Type u} [CommRing R]
    [Small.{v} R] {M₁ M₂ M₃ : Type v} [AddCommGroup M₁] [Module R M₁] [AddCommGroup M₂]
    [Module R M₂] [AddCommGroup M₃] [Module R M₃] [Module.FinitePresentation R M₃]
    {f₁ : M₁ →ₗ[R] M₂} {f₂ : M₂ →ₗ[R] M₃} (h : Function.Exact f₁ f₂)
    (h₁ : Function.Injective f₁) (h₂ : Function.Surjective f₂) :
    (∃ l : M₃ →ₗ[R] M₂, f₂ ∘ₗ l = LinearMap.id) ↔
      ∀ (Q : Type v) [AddCommGroup Q] [Module R Q],
        Function.Injective (f₁.rTensor Q)
declarations.comment: Exactness is hypothesised; splitness is the existence of a section of `f₂`.

declarations.name: Module.Flat.iff_forall_rTensor_injective_of_exact
declarations.doc:
An `R`-module `M` is flat if and only if every short exact sequence
`0 → M₁ →[f₁] M₂ →[f₂] M → 0` of `R`-modules is universally exact, that is, if and only if
`f₁ ⊗ id_Q : M₁ ⊗ Q → M₂ ⊗ Q` is injective for every such sequence and every `R`-module `Q`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem Module.Flat.iff_forall_rTensor_injective_of_exact {R : Type u} [CommRing R]
    [Small.{v} R] {M : Type v} [AddCommGroup M] [Module R M] :
    Module.Flat R M ↔
      ∀ ⦃M₁ M₂ : Type v⦄ [AddCommGroup M₁] [Module R M₁] [AddCommGroup M₂] [Module R M₂]
        (f₁ : M₁ →ₗ[R] M₂) (f₂ : M₂ →ₗ[R] M), Function.Injective f₁ →
        Function.Exact f₁ f₂ → Function.Surjective f₂ →
          ∀ (Q : Type v) [AddCommGroup Q] [Module R Q],
            Function.Injective (f₁.rTensor Q)
declarations.comment: Exactness is hypothesised; universal injectivity of `f₁` is spelled out.

declarations.name: UniversallyExact.flat_of_middle_flat
declarations.doc:
**Theorem (Stacks Tag 058P, Lemma 10.82.7).**
Let `0 -> M_1 ->[u] M_2 ->[v] M_3 -> 0` be a universally exact sequence of `R`-modules
with `M_2` flat. Then `M_1` is flat and `M_3` is flat.
declarations.statement:
theorem UniversallyExact.flat_of_middle_flat
    {M₁ M₂ M₃ : Type u} [AddCommGroup M₁] [AddCommGroup M₂] [AddCommGroup M₃]
    [Module R M₁] [Module R M₂] [Module R M₃]
    (u : M₁ →ₗ[R] M₂) (v : M₂ →ₗ[R] M₃)
    (hue : UniversallyExact u v) (hM₂ : Module.Flat R M₂) :
    Module.Flat R M₁ ∧ Module.Flat R M₃

registrations.name: Module.finitePresentation_of_projective
registrations.comment: (⇒) finitely presented

registrations.name: Module.Flat.of_projective
registrations.comment: (⇒) flat: projective modules are flat

registrations.name: Module.Flat.projective_of_finitePresentation
registrations.comment: (⇐) projective; finiteness comes from `FinitePresentation` (instance)

declarations.name: Module.Projective.of_finite_of_isBaseChange_of_faithfullyFlat
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 058S** (the projectivity half). Let `R → S` be a faithfully flat ring map, let `M` be
an `R`-module and let `f : M →ₗ[R] N` exhibit the `S`-module `N` as the base change of `M` along
`R → S`. If `N` is a finite projective `S`-module, then `M` is a projective `R`-module. Together
with `Module.Finite.of_finite_tensorProduct_of_faithfullyFlat` this says that being a finite
projective module descends along a faithfully flat ring map.
declarations.statement:
theorem Projective.of_finite_of_isBaseChange_of_faithfullyFlat {R : Type*} [CommRing R]
    {S : Type*} [CommRing S] [Algebra R S] [Module.FaithfullyFlat R S]
    {M : Type*} [AddCommGroup M] [Module R M]
    {N : Type*} [AddCommGroup N] [Module R N] [Module S N] [IsScalarTower R S N]
    (f : M →ₗ[R] N) (h : IsBaseChange S f)
    [Module.Finite S N] [Module.Projective S N] :
    Module.Projective R M
declarations.comment:
The projectivity half of the conclusion; the finiteness half is Mathlib's
`Module.Finite.of_finite_tensorProduct_of_faithfullyFlat`.

declarations.name: Submodule.IsDirectSumDevissage
declarations.doc:
A *direct sum dévissage* of an `R`-module `M` is an increasing family `N` of submodules of `M`,
indexed by the ordinals `α < s`, with `N 0 = 0`, with union `M`, continuous at limit ordinals, and
with `N α` a direct summand of `N (α + 1)` whenever `α + 1 < s`.
declarations.statement:
public structure IsDirectSumDevissage (s : Ordinal.{w}) (N : Ordinal.{w} → Submodule R M) :
    Prop
declarations.comment: direct sum devissage

declarations.name: Submodule.IsKaplanskyDevissage
declarations.doc:
A *Kaplansky dévissage* of an `R`-module `M` is a direct sum dévissage all of whose quotients
`N (α + 1) / N α` are countably generated, which is to say that `N (α + 1)` is generated over `N α`
by countably many elements of `M`.
declarations.statement:
public structure IsKaplanskyDevissage (s : Ordinal.{w}) (N : Ordinal.{w} → Submodule R M) : Prop
    extends IsDirectSumDevissage s N
declarations.comment: Kaplansky devissage

declarations.name: devissage_iso
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Tag 058V (Lemma 10.84.2).** Given a direct sum dévissage of `N`,
the module `N` is isomorphic to the direct sum of the successive quotients
`M_{α+1} / M_α` over all ordinals `α` with `α + 1 < S`.

Here the `α`-th summand `M_{α+1}/M_α` is realized as the quotient of the
submodule `M (Order.succ α)` of `N` by the image of `M α` inside it
(`(M α).submoduleOf (M (Order.succ α))`, which is `M α ⊓ M (succ α) = M α`
viewed as a submodule of `↥(M (succ α))`).

declarations.name: Submodule.exists_sSupIndep_countable_span_iff_exists_isKaplanskyDevissage
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 058W.** Let `M` be a module over a ring `R`. Then `M` is a direct sum of countably
generated `R`-modules — that is, `M` is the internal direct sum of an independent set of countably
generated submodules — if and only if `M` admits a Kaplansky dévissage.
declarations.statement:
public theorem exists_sSupIndep_countable_span_iff_exists_isKaplanskyDevissage
    (R : Type v) (M : Type u) [Ring R] [AddCommGroup M] [Module R M] :
    (∃ S : Set (Submodule R M), sSupIndep S ∧ sSup S = ⊤ ∧
        ∀ N ∈ S, ∃ t : Set M, t.Countable ∧ span R t = N) ↔
      ∃ (s : Ordinal.{u}) (N : Ordinal.{u} → Submodule R M),
        IsKaplanskyDevissage s N
declarations.comment:
Countable generation written as a countable spanning set, and the direct sum
  decomposition internally, as an independent set of submodules of `M` with supremum `⊤`.

declarations.name: Submodule.exists_sSupIndep_countable_span_of_isCompl
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 058X.** Let `M` be a module over a ring `R` which is a direct sum of countably
generated `R`-modules — that is, `M` is the internal direct sum of an independent set of countably
generated submodules. If `P` is a direct summand of `M`, with complement `Q`, then `P` is also a
direct sum of countably generated `R`-modules.
declarations.statement:
public theorem exists_sSupIndep_countable_span_of_isCompl {R : Type*} {M : Type*} [Ring R]
    [AddCommGroup M] [Module R M]
    (hM : ∃ S : Set (Submodule R M), sSupIndep S ∧ sSup S = ⊤ ∧
      ∀ N ∈ S, ∃ t : Set M, t.Countable ∧ span R t = N)
    (P Q : Submodule R M) (hPQ : IsCompl P Q) :
    ∃ S : Set (Submodule R ↥P), sSupIndep S ∧ sSup S = ⊤ ∧
      ∀ N ∈ S, ∃ t : Set ↥P, t.Countable ∧ span R t = N
declarations.comment:
Being a direct sum of countably generated modules written internally, as in 058W:
  an independent set of submodules with supremum `⊤`, each spanned by a countable set. `P` is a
  direct summand of `M` in the sense of a complement in the submodule lattice of `M`.

declarations.name: Submodule.exists_sSupIndep_countable_span_projective_of_projective
declarations.doc:
Let `M` be a projective module over a ring `R`. Then `M` is a direct sum of countably generated
projective `R`-modules: there is an independent set of submodules of `M` with supremum `⊤`, each
spanned by a countable set and each projective over `R`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem exists_sSupIndep_countable_span_projective_of_projective {R : Type*} {M : Type*}
    [Ring R] [AddCommGroup M] [Module R M] [Module.Projective R M] :
    ∃ S : Set (Submodule R M), sSupIndep S ∧ sSup S = ⊤ ∧
      ∀ N ∈ S, (∃ t : Set M, t.Countable ∧ span R t = N) ∧ Module.Projective R ↥N
declarations.comment:
Being a direct sum of countably generated projective modules is written internally,
  as in 058W and 058X: an independent set of submodules with supremum `⊤`, each spanned by a
  countable set and each projective. Countable generation is a countable spanning set.

declarations.name: Module.forall_free_of_projective_iff_forall_free_of_projective_of_countable_span
declarations.doc:
Let `R` be a ring. Every projective `R`-module is free if and only if every projective
`R`-module admitting a countable generating set is free.
declarations.statement:
public theorem Module.forall_free_of_projective_iff_forall_free_of_projective_of_countable_span
    (R : Type u) [Ring R] :
    (∀ (M : Type v) [AddCommGroup M] [Module R M], Module.Projective R M → Module.Free R M) ↔
      ∀ (M : Type v) [AddCommGroup M] [Module R M], Module.Projective R M →
        (∃ s : Set M, s.Countable ∧ Submodule.span R s = ⊤) → Module.Free R M
declarations.comment: The equivalence, with countable generation written as a countable spanning set.

declarations.name: countablyGenerated_propertyP_free
declarations.doc:
Stacks Tag 0591 / Lemma 10.85.2: a countably generated module satisfying
property (P) is free.
declarations.statement:
theorem countablyGenerated_propertyP_free
    (hcg : CountablyGenerated R M) (hP : PropertyP R M) :
    Module.Free R M

declarations.name: projective_local_free_summand
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Tag 0592, Lemma 10.85.3.** Any element of a projective module over a
(commutative) local ring is contained in a free direct summand. Concretely, for
every `x` in a projective module `P` over a local ring `R`, there is a submodule
`N` of `P` with `x ∈ N`, with `N` free as an `R`-module, and with `N` a direct
summand of `P` (witnessed by a complementary submodule `N'`, `IsCompl N N'`).
declarations.statement:
theorem projective_local_free_summand {R : Type*} [CommRing R] [IsLocalRing R]
    {P : Type*} [AddCommGroup P] [Module R P] [Module.Projective R P] (x : P) :
    ∃ N : Submodule R P, x ∈ N ∧ Module.Free R N ∧ ∃ N' : Submodule R P, IsCompl N N'

declarations.name: Module.free_of_projective_of_isLocalRing
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0593** (Kaplansky). If `P` is a projective module over a commutative local ring `R`,
then `P` is free. No finiteness hypothesis on `P` is needed.
declarations.statement:
public theorem Module.free_of_projective_of_isLocalRing {R : Type u} {P : Type v} [CommRing R]
    [AddCommGroup P] [Module R P] [IsLocalRing R] [Module.Projective R P] : Module.Free R P
declarations.comment: Projective modules over local rings are free, with no finiteness hypothesis.

declarations.name: MittagLeffler.IsMittagLefflerSet
declarations.doc:
A directed inverse system of sets `(F_i, φ_{ji})` is *Mittag-Leffler*
if for every index `i`, there exists some `j ≥ i` such that for all
`k ≥ j`, the image of `F_k` in `F_i` (via the transition map) equals
the image of `F_j` in `F_i`.
declarations.statement:
def IsMittagLefflerSet {ι : Type*} [Preorder ι] [IsDirected ι (· ≤ ·)] {F : ι → Type*}
    (φ : ⦃i j : ι⦄ → i ≤ j → F j → F i) [InverseSystem φ] : Prop

declarations.name: MittagLeffler.IsMittagLefflerModule
declarations.doc:
A directed inverse system of `R`-modules `(M_i, φ_{ji})` is
*Mittag-Leffler* if the underlying directed inverse system of sets is
Mittag-Leffler.
declarations.statement:
def IsMittagLefflerModule {R : Type*} [Ring R] {ι : Type*} [Preorder ι]
    [IsDirected ι (· ≤ ·)] {M : ι → Type*} [∀ i, AddCommGroup (M i)] [∀ i, Module R (M i)]
    (φ : ⦃i j : ι⦄ → i ≤ j → M j →ₗ[R] M i)
    [InverseSystem (fun _ _ h => (φ h : M _ → M _))] : Prop

declarations.name: DirInvSystem.nonempty_limit_of_isMittagLeffler
declarations.doc:
Let `(A_i, φ_{ji})` be a directed inverse system of sets over a directed set `I`.
If `I` is countable, the system is Mittag-Leffler, and each `A_i` is nonempty,
then the limit `lim A_i` is nonempty.
declarations.statement:
theorem DirInvSystem.nonempty_limit_of_isMittagLeffler
    [Countable I] [Nonempty I] [IsDirected I (· ≤ ·)]
    {A : I → Type*} (S : DirInvSystem A)
    (hML : S.IsMittagLeffler) (hne : ∀ i, Nonempty (A i)) :
    S.limit.Nonempty

declarations.name: invLimit_exact
declarations.doc:
Let `I` be a countable directed set and let
`0 → A →[f] B →[g] C → 0` be an exact sequence of directed inverse systems of abelian
groups over `I`.  If the system `(A, φ)` is Mittag-Leffler, then the induced sequence of
inverse limits
`0 → lim A →[lim f] lim B →[lim g] lim C → 0`
is exact:

1. `lim f` is injective;
2. `range (lim f) = ker (lim g)`;
3. `lim g` is surjective.

Left-exactness (parts 1 and 2) holds for any exact sequence of inverse systems; the
Mittag-Leffler hypothesis and countability are used for part 3, the surjectivity of
`lim g`.
declarations.statement:
theorem invLimit_exact
    {I : Type*} [Preorder I] [IsDirected I (· ≤ ·)] [Nonempty I] [Countable I]
    {A : I → Type*} [∀ i, AddCommGroup (A i)]
    {φ : ⦃i j : I⦄ → i ≤ j → (A j →+ A i)}
    (hφ : InverseSystem (fun _ _ h => (φ h : _ → _)))
    {B : I → Type*} [∀ i, AddCommGroup (B i)]
    {ψ : ⦃i j : I⦄ → i ≤ j → (B j →+ B i)}
    (hψ : InverseSystem (fun _ _ h => (ψ h : _ → _)))
    {C : I → Type*} [∀ i, AddCommGroup (C i)]
    {χ : ⦃i j : I⦄ → i ≤ j → (C j →+ C i)}
    (hχ : InverseSystem (fun _ _ h => (χ h : _ → _)))
    {f : ⦃i : I⦄ → (A i →+ B i)} {g : ⦃i : I⦄ → (B i →+ C i)}
    (hexact : IsExactSeq (φ := φ) (ψ := ψ) (χ := χ) f g)
    (hML : IsMittagLefflerSystem A φ) :
    Function.Injective (addInvLimit.map A φ B ψ f hexact.hf_mor) ∧
      (addInvLimit.map A φ B ψ f hexact.hf_mor).range =
        (addInvLimit.map B ψ C χ g hexact.hg_mor).ker ∧
      Function.Surjective (addInvLimit.map B ψ C χ g hexact.hg_mor)

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.Functor.IsMittagLefflerSystem
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 059A.** A diagram `F : J ⥤ ModuleCat R` of `R`-modules, thought of as a directed
system `(M i, f i j)`, is a *Mittag-Leffler system* if every `M i` is an `R`-module of finite
presentation and if for every `R`-module `N` the inverse system of dual modules
`(Hom_R(M i, N), Hom_R(f i j, N))`, that is `F.op ⋙ yoneda.obj N`, satisfies the Mittag-Leffler
condition.
declarations.statement:
public def IsMittagLefflerSystem {R : Type u} [Ring R] {J : Type w} [Category.{w'} J]
    (F : J ⥤ ModuleCat.{v} R) : Prop

declarations.name: LinearMap.Dominates
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 059B.** Let `f : M → N` and `g : M → M'` be maps of `R`-modules with common source.
We say `g` *dominates* `f` if for every `R`-module `Q` we have
`Ker(f ⊗_R id_Q) ⊆ Ker(g ⊗_R id_Q)` as submodules of `M ⊗_R Q`.
declarations.comment:
Domination is spelled out as containment of the kernels of the two maps
  tensored with the identity of the test module.

declarations.name: LinearMap.dominates_iff_forall_finitePresentation
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 059C.** Let `f : M → N` and `g : M → M'` be maps of `R`-modules. Then `g` dominates
`f`, that is `Ker(f ⊗_R id_Q) ⊆ Ker(g ⊗_R id_Q)` for every `R`-module `Q`, if and only if
`Ker(f ⊗_R id_Q) ⊆ Ker(g ⊗_R id_Q)` for every finitely presented `R`-module `Q`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem LinearMap.dominates_iff_forall_finitePresentation {R : Type u} [CommRing R]
    [Small.{v} R] {M : Type v} {N : Type w} {M' : Type w'} [AddCommGroup M] [Module R M]
    [AddCommGroup N] [Module R N] [AddCommGroup M'] [Module R M'] (g : M →ₗ[R] M')
    (f : M →ₗ[R] N) :
    g.Dominates f ↔
      ∀ (Q : Type v) [AddCommGroup Q] [Module R Q] [Module.FinitePresentation R Q],
        LinearMap.ker (f.rTensor Q) ≤ LinearMap.ker (g.rTensor Q)
declarations.comment:
Domination is the project's `LinearMap.Dominates`; the containment of kernels is
  the containment of the kernels of the maps tensored with the identity of the test module.

declarations.name: LinearMap.forall_ker_rTensor_le_iff_exists_eq_comp
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 059D.** Let `f : M → N` and `g : M → M'` be maps of `R`-modules and suppose that
`Coker(f) = N ⧸ Im(f)` is of finite presentation. Then `g` dominates `f`, that is
`Ker(f ⊗ id_Q) ⊆ Ker(g ⊗ id_Q)` for every `R`-module `Q`, if and only if `g` factors through `f`,
that is `g = h ∘ f` for some module map `h : N → M'`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem LinearMap.forall_ker_rTensor_le_iff_exists_eq_comp {R : Type u} [CommRing R]
    [Small.{v} R] {M N M' : Type v} [AddCommGroup M] [Module R M] [AddCommGroup N] [Module R N]
    [AddCommGroup M'] [Module R M'] (f : M →ₗ[R] N) (g : M →ₗ[R] M')
    [Module.FinitePresentation R (N ⧸ LinearMap.range f)] :
    (∀ (Q : Type v) [AddCommGroup Q] [Module R Q],
        LinearMap.ker (f.rTensor Q) ≤ LinearMap.ker (g.rTensor Q)) ↔
      ∃ h : N →ₗ[R] M', g = h ∘ₗ f
declarations.comment: Domination is spelled out as containment of the kernels of the tensored maps.

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.Functor.tfae_isMittagLefflerSystem
declarations.statement:
public theorem tfae_isMittagLefflerSystem {R : Type u} [CommRing R] [Small.{w} R] {J : Type w}
    [Preorder J] [IsDirectedOrder J] [Nonempty J] (F : J ⥤ ModuleCat.{w} R)
    [∀ i, Module.FinitePresentation R (F.obj i)] {c : Cocone F} (hc : IsColimit c) :
    List.TFAE
      [∀ (P : ModuleCat.{w} R) [Module.FinitePresentation R P] (f : P ⟶ c.pt),
          ∃ (Q : ModuleCat.{w} R) (_ : Module.FinitePresentation R Q) (g : P ⟶ Q),
            ∀ T : ModuleCat.{w} R,
              LinearMap.ker (f.hom.rTensor T) = LinearMap.ker (g.hom.rTensor T),
        ∀ i : J, ∃ (j : J) (u : i ⟶ j), ∀ T : ModuleCat.{w} R,
          LinearMap.ker ((c.ι.app i).hom.rTensor T) ≤ LinearMap.ker ((F.map u).hom.rTensor T),
        ∀ i : J, ∃ (j : J) (u : i ⟶ j), ∀ (k : J) (v : i ⟶ k),
          ∃ h : F.obj k ⟶ F.obj j, F.map u = F.map v ≫ h,
        F.IsMittagLefflerSystem,
        (F.op ⋙ yoneda.obj (ModuleCat.of R (∀ s : J, F.obj s))).IsMittagLeffler]
declarations.comment:
Domination is spelled out as containment of the kernels of the tensored maps;
condition (4) is 059A's `IsMittagLefflerSystem`.

declarations.name: IsMittagLeffler
declarations.doc:
(Stacks 10.88.7, tag 059F.) An `R`-module `M` is *Mittag-Leffler* if for
every finitely presented `R`-module `P` and every `R`-linear map `f : P → M`,
there exists a finitely presented `R`-module `Q` and an `R`-linear map
`g : P → Q` such that `f` and `g` dominate each other.

This is condition (1) of Stacks Proposition 10.88.6 (tag 059E), which is
equivalent to the other four conditions in that proposition. We choose this
condition because it is intrinsic to `M` and does not depend on any auxiliary
choice of a directed system writing `M` as a colimit of finitely presented
modules.

The universe parameters `uP`, `uQ`, `uN` are independent of `uR`, `uM`, so
"for every finitely presented `R`-module `P`", "there exists ... `Q`", and
"for every test module `N`" each range over their own arbitrary universe,
matching the Stacks quantifications.
declarations.statement:
def IsMittagLeffler (R : Type uR) [CommRing R] (M : Type uM)
    [AddCommGroup M] [Module R M] : Prop

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.Functor.isMittagLefflerSystem_iff_isMittagLeffler_dual
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 059G.** Let `R` be a commutative ring and let `F : J ⥤ ModuleCat R` be a diagram
`(M i, f i j)` of finitely generated projective `R`-modules. Then `F` is a Mittag-Leffler system
— that is, the inverse system of duals `(Hom_R(M i, N), Hom_R(f i j, N))` is Mittag-Leffler for
every `R`-module `N`, and the `M i` are of finite presentation — if and only if the single
inverse system of `R`-duals `(Hom_R(M i, R), Hom_R(f i j, R))` is Mittag-Leffler.

Combined with criterion (4) of Proposition 059E, this says that for a flat module `M` written by
Lazard's theorem (Theorem 058G) as the colimit of a directed system of finite free modules
`M = colim M i`, it is enough for `(Hom_R(M i, R), Hom_R(f i j, R))` to be Mittag-Leffler for `M`
to be a Mittag-Leffler module.
declarations.statement:
public theorem isMittagLefflerSystem_iff_isMittagLeffler_dual {R : Type u} [CommRing R]
    [Small.{v} R] {J : Type w} [Category.{w'} J] (F : J ⥤ ModuleCat.{v} R)
    [∀ i, Module.Finite R (F.obj i)] [∀ i, Module.Projective R (F.obj i)] :
    F.IsMittagLefflerSystem ↔
      (F.op ⋙ yoneda.obj (ModuleCat.of R (Shrink.{v} R))).IsMittagLeffler
declarations.comment:
The content is the reduction of criterion (4) of 059E to the single test module
`R`, stated for finitely generated projective members and an arbitrary index category, and as an
iff; the passage to the colimit is 059E and the system comes from 058G. See the module
docstring.

declarations.name: comparisonMap_not_injective
declarations.doc:
**Statement 1 (the comparison map need not be injective).**
With `Q_n = Z/(n+1)Z`, the canonical map
`c : Q ⊗_Z (∏_n Z/(n+1)Z) → ∏_n (Q ⊗_Z Z/(n+1)Z)` is not injective.
declarations.statement:
theorem comparisonMap_not_injective :
    ¬ Function.Injective (tensorPiComparison (fun n : ℕ => ZMod (n + 1)))

declarations.name: comparisonMap_not_surjective
declarations.doc:
**Statement 2 (the comparison map need not be surjective).**
With `Q_n = Z` and the identification `Q ⊗_Z Z ≅ Q`, the canonical map
`c : Q ⊗_Z (∏_n Z) → ∏_n Q` is not surjective.
declarations.statement:
theorem comparisonMap_not_surjective :
    ¬ Function.Surjective comparisonMapQ

declarations.name: Module.Finite.tfae_piRightHom_surjective
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 059J.** Let `R` be a commutative ring and `M` an `R`-module. The following are
equivalent: (1) `M` is finitely generated; (2) for every family `Q` of `R`-modules the canonical
map `M ⊗[R] (∀ α, Q α) → ∀ α, M ⊗[R] Q α` is surjective; (3) for every `R`-module `Q` and every
set `A` the canonical map `M ⊗[R] Q^A → (M ⊗[R] Q)^A` is surjective; (4) for every set `A` the
canonical map `M ⊗[R] R^A → M^A` is surjective.
declarations.statement:
public theorem Module.Finite.tfae_piRightHom_surjective (R : Type u) [CommRing R] (M : Type v)
    [AddCommGroup M] [Module R M] :
    List.TFAE
      [Module.Finite R M,
        ∀ (A : Type v) (Q : A → Type v) [∀ α, AddCommGroup (Q α)] [∀ α, Module R (Q α)],
          Function.Surjective (TensorProduct.piRightHom R R M Q),
        ∀ (A : Type v) (Q : Type v) [AddCommGroup Q] [Module R Q],
          Function.Surjective (TensorProduct.piRightHom R R M fun _ : A ↦ Q),
        ∀ A : Type v, Function.Surjective (TensorProduct.piScalarRightHom R R M A)]

declarations.name: Module.FinitePresentation.tfae_piRightHom_bijective
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 059K.** Let `R` be a commutative ring and `M` an `R`-module. The following are
equivalent: (1) `M` is finitely presented; (2) for every family `Q` of `R`-modules the canonical
map `M ⊗[R] (∀ α, Q α) → ∀ α, M ⊗[R] Q α` is bijective; (3) for every `R`-module `Q` and every
set `A` the canonical map `M ⊗[R] Q^A → (M ⊗[R] Q)^A` is bijective; (4) for every set `A` the
canonical map `M ⊗[R] R^A → M^A` is bijective.
declarations.statement:
public theorem Module.FinitePresentation.tfae_piRightHom_bijective (R : Type u) [CommRing R]
    [Small.{v} R] (M : Type v) [AddCommGroup M] [Module R M] :
    List.TFAE
      [Module.FinitePresentation R M,
        ∀ (A : Type v) (Q : A → Type v) [∀ α, AddCommGroup (Q α)] [∀ α, Module R (Q α)],
          Function.Bijective (TensorProduct.piRightHom R R M Q),
        ∀ (A : Type v) (Q : Type v) [AddCommGroup Q] [Module R Q],
          Function.Bijective (TensorProduct.piRightHom R R M fun _ : A ↦ Q),
        ∀ A : Type v, Function.Bijective (TensorProduct.piScalarRightHom R R M A)]
declarations.comment: Test data in the universe of `M`, as in 059J; hence `Small.{v} R`. See the module docstring.

declarations.name: LinearMap.exists_finitePresentation_factorization_of_rTensor_apply_eq_zero
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 059L.** Let `R` be a commutative ring, `P` a finitely presented `R`-module,
`f : P → M` a map of `R`-modules and `Q` an `R`-module, and let `x ∈ P ⊗ Q` be killed by
`f ⊗ id_Q`. Then there are a finitely presented `R`-module `P'` and maps `f' : P → P'`,
`g : P' → M` with `f = g ∘ f'` such that `x` is killed by `f' ⊗ id_Q`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem LinearMap.exists_finitePresentation_factorization_of_rTensor_apply_eq_zero
    {R : Type u} [CommRing R] [Small.{v} R] {P M : Type v} {Q : Type w} [AddCommGroup P]
    [Module R P] [AddCommGroup M] [Module R M] [AddCommGroup Q] [Module R Q]
    [Module.FinitePresentation R P] (f : P →ₗ[R] M) {x : P ⊗[R] Q}
    (hx : f.rTensor Q x = 0) :
    ∃ (P' : Type v) (_ : AddCommGroup P') (_ : Module R P')
      (_ : Module.FinitePresentation R P') (f' : P →ₗ[R] P') (g : P' →ₗ[R] M),
      f = g ∘ₗ f' ∧ f'.rTensor Q x = 0
declarations.comment:
The kernel conditions are elementwise, `x` being a single element; `f` factors
through `f'` by the pinned equation `f = g ∘ₗ f'`.

declarations.name: Module.mittagLeffler_iff_piRightHom_injective
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 059M.** Let `R` be a commutative ring and `M` an `R`-module. Then `M` is
Mittag-Leffler — every map `f : P → M` from a finitely presented `R`-module dominates and is
dominated by a map `g : P → Q` into a finitely presented `R`-module, that is
`Ker(f ⊗ id_N) = Ker(g ⊗ id_N)` for every `R`-module `N`, which is condition (1) of
Proposition 059E — if and only if for every family `(Q α)` of `R`-modules the canonical map
`M ⊗[R] (∀ α, Q α) → ∀ α, M ⊗[R] Q α` is injective.
declarations.statement:
public theorem Module.mittagLeffler_iff_piRightHom_injective (R : Type u) [CommRing R]
    [Small.{v} R] (M : Type v) [AddCommGroup M] [Module R M] :
    (∀ (P : Type v) [AddCommGroup P] [Module R P] [Module.FinitePresentation R P]
        (f : P →ₗ[R] M), ∃ (Q : Type v) (_ : AddCommGroup Q) (_ : Module R Q)
          (_ : Module.FinitePresentation R Q) (g : P →ₗ[R] Q), ∀ (N : Type v) [AddCommGroup N]
            [Module R N], LinearMap.ker (f.rTensor N) = LinearMap.ker (g.rTensor N)) ↔
      ∀ (A : Type v) (Q : A → Type v) [∀ α, AddCommGroup (Q α)] [∀ α, Module R (Q α)],
        Function.Injective (TensorProduct.piRightHom R R M Q)
declarations.comment:
Mittag-Leffler is spelled out inline as condition (1) of 059E; test data in the
universe of `M`, as in 059J and 059K, whence `Small.{v} R`. See the module docstring.

declarations.name: Function.Exact.mittagLeffler_M₁_and_mittagLeffler_M₂_of_forall_rTensor_injective
declarations.doc:
Let `0 → M₁ →[f₁] M₂ →[f₂] M₃ → 0` be a universally exact sequence of `R`-modules, that is, a
short exact sequence for which `f₁ ⊗ id_T : M₁ ⊗ T → M₂ ⊗ T` is injective for every `R`-module `T`.
Then (1) if `M₂` is Mittag-Leffler, so is `M₁`, and (2) if `M₁` and `M₃` are Mittag-Leffler, so is
`M₂`. Being Mittag-Leffler is spelled out in the intrinsic form 059E (1): every map `f : P → M`
from a finitely presented module dominates and is dominated by a map `g : P → Q` into a finitely
presented module, domination meaning `Ker(f ⊗ id_N) = Ker(g ⊗ id_N)` for every `R`-module `N`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem Function.Exact.mittagLeffler_M₁_and_mittagLeffler_M₂_of_forall_rTensor_injective
    {R : Type u} [CommRing R] [Small.{v} R] {M₁ M₂ M₃ : Type v} [AddCommGroup M₁] [Module R M₁]
    [AddCommGroup M₂] [Module R M₂] [AddCommGroup M₃] [Module R M₃] {f₁ : M₁ →ₗ[R] M₂}
    {f₂ : M₂ →ₗ[R] M₃} (h : Function.Exact f₁ f₂) (h₂ : Function.Surjective f₂)
    (hf₁ : ∀ (T : Type v) [AddCommGroup T] [Module R T], Function.Injective (f₁.rTensor T)) :
    ((∀ (P : Type v) [AddCommGroup P] [Module R P] [Module.FinitePresentation R P]
          (f : P →ₗ[R] M₂), ∃ (Q : Type v) (_ : AddCommGroup Q) (_ : Module R Q)
            (_ : Module.FinitePresentation R Q) (g : P →ₗ[R] Q), ∀ (N : Type v) [AddCommGroup N]
              [Module R N], LinearMap.ker (f.rTensor N) = LinearMap.ker (g.rTensor N)) →
        ∀ (P : Type v) [AddCommGroup P] [Module R P] [Module.FinitePresentation R P]
          (f : P →ₗ[R] M₁), ∃ (Q : Type v) (_ : AddCommGroup Q) (_ : Module R Q)
            (_ : Module.FinitePresentation R Q) (g : P →ₗ[R] Q), ∀ (N : Type v) [AddCommGroup N]
              [Module R N], LinearMap.ker (f.rTensor N) = LinearMap.ker (g.rTensor N)) ∧
      ((∀ (P : Type v) [AddCommGroup P] [Module R P] [Module.FinitePresentation R P]
            (f : P →ₗ[R] M₁), ∃ (Q : Type v) (_ : AddCommGroup Q) (_ : Module R Q)
              (_ : Module.FinitePresentation R Q) (g : P →ₗ[R] Q), ∀ (N : Type v) [AddCommGroup N]
                [Module R N], LinearMap.ker (f.rTensor N) = LinearMap.ker (g.rTensor N)) →
        (∀ (P : Type v) [AddCommGroup P] [Module R P] [Module.FinitePresentation R P]
            (f : P →ₗ[R] M₃), ∃ (Q : Type v) (_ : AddCommGroup Q) (_ : Module R Q)
              (_ : Module.FinitePresentation R Q) (g : P →ₗ[R] Q), ∀ (N : Type v) [AddCommGroup N]
                [Module R N], LinearMap.ker (f.rTensor N) = LinearMap.ker (g.rTensor N)) →
        ∀ (P : Type v) [AddCommGroup P] [Module R P] [Module.FinitePresentation R P]
          (f : P →ₗ[R] M₂), ∃ (Q : Type v) (_ : AddCommGroup Q) (_ : Module R Q)
            (_ : Module.FinitePresentation R Q) (g : P →ₗ[R] Q), ∀ (N : Type v) [AddCommGroup N]
              [Module R N], LinearMap.ker (f.rTensor N) = LinearMap.ker (g.rTensor N))
declarations.comment:
Mittag-Leffler is spelled out inline as condition (1) of 059E, as in 059M and
05CQ; universal exactness is `h`, `h₂` and injectivity of `f₁ ⊗ id_T` for every `T`, as in
058K (1). The two items are the two conjuncts.

declarations.name: Module.mittagLeffler_directSum_iff
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 059P.** Let `R` be a commutative ring and `(M i)` a family of `R`-modules indexed by a
type `ι`. Then the direct sum `⨁ i, M i` is Mittag-Leffler if and only if each `M i` is. Being
Mittag-Leffler is spelled out in the intrinsic form 059E (1): every map `f : P → M` from a finitely
presented module dominates and is dominated by a map `g : P → Q` into a finitely presented module,
domination meaning `Ker(f ⊗ id_N) = Ker(g ⊗ id_N)` for every `R`-module `N`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem Module.mittagLeffler_directSum_iff (R : Type u) [CommRing R] {ι : Type v}
    (M : ι → Type v) [∀ i, AddCommGroup (M i)] [∀ i, Module R (M i)] :
    (∀ (P : Type v) [AddCommGroup P] [Module R P] [Module.FinitePresentation R P]
        (f : P →ₗ[R] (⨁ i, M i)), ∃ (Q : Type v) (_ : AddCommGroup Q) (_ : Module R Q)
          (_ : Module.FinitePresentation R Q) (g : P →ₗ[R] Q), ∀ (N : Type v) [AddCommGroup N]
            [Module R N], LinearMap.ker (f.rTensor N) = LinearMap.ker (g.rTensor N)) ↔
      ∀ i, ∀ (P : Type v) [AddCommGroup P] [Module R P] [Module.FinitePresentation R P]
        (f : P →ₗ[R] M i), ∃ (Q : Type v) (_ : AddCommGroup Q) (_ : Module R Q)
          (_ : Module.FinitePresentation R Q) (g : P →ₗ[R] Q), ∀ (N : Type v) [AddCommGroup N]
            [Module R N], LinearMap.ker (f.rTensor N) = LinearMap.ker (g.rTensor N)
declarations.comment:
Mittag-Leffler is spelled out inline as condition (1) of 059E, as in 059M, 059N and
05CQ; the module is `Mathlib`'s `DirectSum`, as in `Module.Flat.directSum_iff`. No smallness of `R`
is assumed, neither direction using it. See the module docstring.

declarations.name: Module.mittagLeffler_iff_finitePresentation_and_mittagLeffler_of_projective
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 059R.** Let `R` be a commutative ring and `M` an `R`-module. Then (1) if `M` is
finitely generated, `M` is Mittag-Leffler if and only if `M` is finitely presented — in particular
every finitely presented module is Mittag-Leffler — and (2) if `M` is projective, in particular if
`M` is free, then `M` is Mittag-Leffler. Being Mittag-Leffler is spelled out in the intrinsic form
059E (1): every map `f : P → M` from a finitely presented module dominates and is dominated by a
map `g : P → Q` into a finitely presented module, domination meaning
`Ker(f ⊗ id_N) = Ker(g ⊗ id_N)` for every `R`-module `N`.

This is the example as the source states it, over one module. The two items are independent of
each other and each is stated separately, over its own hypothesis alone, as
`Module.mittagLeffler_iff_finitePresentation` and `Module.mittagLeffler_of_projective`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem Module.mittagLeffler_iff_finitePresentation_and_mittagLeffler_of_projective
    (R : Type u) [CommRing R] [Small.{v} R] (M : Type v) [AddCommGroup M] [Module R M] :
    (Module.Finite R M →
        ((∀ (P : Type v) [AddCommGroup P] [Module R P] [Module.FinitePresentation R P]
            (f : P →ₗ[R] M), ∃ (Q : Type v) (_ : AddCommGroup Q) (_ : Module R Q)
              (_ : Module.FinitePresentation R Q) (g : P →ₗ[R] Q), ∀ (N : Type v) [AddCommGroup N]
                [Module R N], LinearMap.ker (f.rTensor N) = LinearMap.ker (g.rTensor N)) ↔
          Module.FinitePresentation R M)) ∧
      (Module.Projective R M →
        ∀ (P : Type v) [AddCommGroup P] [Module R P] [Module.FinitePresentation R P]
          (f : P →ₗ[R] M), ∃ (Q : Type v) (_ : AddCommGroup Q) (_ : Module R Q)
            (_ : Module.FinitePresentation R Q) (g : P →ₗ[R] Q), ∀ (N : Type v) [AddCommGroup N]
              [Module R N], LinearMap.ker (f.rTensor N) = LinearMap.ker (g.rTensor N))
declarations.comment:
Items (1) and (3) together, over one module and with the two hypotheses as
antecedents; the forms to cite are the two halves. Mittag-Leffler is spelled out inline as
condition (1) of 059E, as in 059M, 059N and 059P. Test data in the universe of `M`, whence
`Small.{v} R`. See the module docstring.

declarations.name: Module.mittagLeffler_iff_finitePresentation
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 059R, item (1).** Let `R` be a commutative ring and `M` a finitely generated
`R`-module. Then `M` is Mittag-Leffler if and only if `M` is finitely presented; in particular
every finitely presented module is Mittag-Leffler, finite presentation implying finite generation.
Being Mittag-Leffler is spelled out in the intrinsic form
059E (1): every map `f : P → M` from a finitely presented module dominates and is dominated by a
map `g : P → Q` into a finitely presented module, domination meaning
`Ker(f ⊗ id_N) = Ker(g ⊗ id_N)` for every `R`-module `N`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem Module.mittagLeffler_iff_finitePresentation (R : Type u) [CommRing R] [Small.{v} R]
    (M : Type v) [AddCommGroup M] [Module R M] [Module.Finite R M] :
    (∀ (P : Type v) [AddCommGroup P] [Module R P] [Module.FinitePresentation R P]
        (f : P →ₗ[R] M), ∃ (Q : Type v) (_ : AddCommGroup Q) (_ : Module R Q)
          (_ : Module.FinitePresentation R Q) (g : P →ₗ[R] Q), ∀ (N : Type v) [AddCommGroup N]
            [Module R N], LinearMap.ker (f.rTensor N) = LinearMap.ker (g.rTensor N)) ↔
      Module.FinitePresentation R M
declarations.comment:
Item (1), with the finite generation an instance hypothesis; `finitely presented
implies Mittag-Leffler` is the direction `←`, via `instFiniteOfFinitePresentation`.

declarations.name: Module.mittagLeffler_of_projective
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 059R, items (2) and (3).** Let `R` be a commutative ring and `M` a projective
`R`-module, in particular a free one, `Module.Projective.of_free` being an instance. Then `M` is
Mittag-Leffler, spelled out in the intrinsic form 059E (1): every map `f : P → M` from a finitely
presented module dominates and is dominated by a map `g : P → Q` into a finitely presented module,
domination meaning `Ker(f ⊗ id_N) = Ker(g ⊗ id_N)` for every `R`-module `N`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem Module.mittagLeffler_of_projective (R : Type u) [CommRing R] [Small.{v} R]
    (M : Type v) [AddCommGroup M] [Module R M] [Module.Projective R M] :
    ∀ (P : Type v) [AddCommGroup P] [Module R P] [Module.FinitePresentation R P]
        (f : P →ₗ[R] M), ∃ (Q : Type v) (_ : AddCommGroup Q) (_ : Module R Q)
          (_ : Module.FinitePresentation R Q) (g : P →ₗ[R] Q), ∀ (N : Type v) [AddCommGroup N]
            [Module R N], LinearMap.ker (f.rTensor N) = LinearMap.ker (g.rTensor N)
declarations.comment:
Items (2) and (3), with the projectivity an instance hypothesis; item (2), a free
module, is this statement via `Module.Projective.of_free`.

declarations.name: Module.mittagLeffler_iff_exists_isLeast_mem_range_rTensor_subtype
declarations.doc:
Let `R` be a commutative ring and let `M` be a flat `R`-module. Then `M` is Mittag-Leffler if
and only if for every finite free `R`-module `F` and every `x ∈ F ⊗[R] M` there is a smallest
submodule `F'` of `F` with `x ∈ F' ⊗[R] M` — that is, with `x` in the range of
`F' ⊗[R] M → F ⊗[R] M`.

Being Mittag-Leffler is spelled out inline as condition (1) of Proposition 059E: every map
`f : P → M` from a finitely presented `R`-module dominates and is dominated by a map `g : P → Q`
into a finitely presented `R`-module, that is `Ker(f ⊗ id_N) = Ker(g ⊗ id_N)` for every
`R`-module `N`. This is Definition 059F, `IsMittagLeffler`, by `isMittagLeffler_def_iff`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem Module.mittagLeffler_iff_exists_isLeast_mem_range_rTensor_subtype (R : Type u)
    [CommRing R] [Small.{v} R] (M : Type v) [AddCommGroup M] [Module R M] [Module.Flat R M] :
    (∀ (P : Type v) [AddCommGroup P] [Module R P] [Module.FinitePresentation R P]
        (f : P →ₗ[R] M), ∃ (Q : Type v) (_ : AddCommGroup Q) (_ : Module R Q)
          (_ : Module.FinitePresentation R Q) (g : P →ₗ[R] Q), ∀ (N : Type v) [AddCommGroup N]
            [Module R N], LinearMap.ker (f.rTensor N) = LinearMap.ker (g.rTensor N)) ↔
      ∀ (F : Type v) [AddCommGroup F] [Module R F] [Module.Free R F] [Module.Finite R F]
        (x : F ⊗[R] M), ∃ F' : Submodule R F,
          IsLeast {N : Submodule R F | x ∈ LinearMap.range (N.subtype.rTensor M)} F'
declarations.comment:
Mittag-Leffler is spelled out inline as condition (1) of 059E, as in 059M and
0AS6; `finite free` is `Module.Free` and `Module.Finite`, `x ∈ F' ⊗_R M` is membership in the
range of `F'.subtype.rTensor M`, and `smallest` is `IsLeast`. Test data in the universe of `M`,
whence `Small.{v} R`. See the module docstring.

declarations.name: Module.flat_and_mittagLeffler_mvPowerSeries
declarations.doc:
Let `R` be a Noetherian ring and let `n : ℕ`. Then the power series module
`M = R[[t_1, …, t_n]]`, regarded as an `R`-module, is flat and Mittag-Leffler.

Being Mittag-Leffler is spelled out inline as condition (1) of Proposition 059E: every map
`f : P → M` from a finitely presented `R`-module dominates and is dominated by a map `g : P → Q`
into a finitely presented `R`-module, that is `Ker(f ⊗ id_N) = Ker(g ⊗ id_N)` for every
`R`-module `N`.
declarations.statement:
theorem Module.flat_and_mittagLeffler_mvPowerSeries (R : Type u) [CommRing R]
    [IsNoetherianRing R] (n : ℕ) :
    Module.Flat R (MvPowerSeries (Fin n) R) ∧
      ∀ (P : Type u) [AddCommGroup P] [Module R P] [Module.FinitePresentation R P]
        (f : P →ₗ[R] MvPowerSeries (Fin n) R), ∃ (Q : Type u) (_ : AddCommGroup Q)
          (_ : Module R Q) (_ : Module.FinitePresentation R Q) (g : P →ₗ[R] Q),
            ∀ (N : Type u) [AddCommGroup N] [Module R N],
              LinearMap.ker (f.rTensor N) = LinearMap.ker (g.rTensor N)
declarations.comment:
The source's `0 < n` is dropped as unused: at `n = 0` the module is free of rank
one, hence flat and Mittag-Leffler. Mittag-Leffler is spelled out inline as condition (1) of 059E,
as in 05D0, 059M, 059S and 0AS6; `R[[t_1, …, t_n]]` is `MvPowerSeries (Fin n) R`, the product over
the monomials with its coefficientwise `R`-module structure, and the two conclusions are one
conjunction, as in the source. Test data in the universe of `R`. See the module docstring.

declarations.name: ModuleCat.exists_countable_directedOn_isColimit_whisker
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 059W.** Let `R` be a ring, `w`-small relative to the universe of the modules below,
let `F : J ⥤ ModuleCat R` be a directed system of `R`-modules over a nonempty directed preorder
`J`, and let `c` be a colimit cocone on `F`, so that `M = c.pt` is `colim_{i ∈ J} M i`. Assume that
for every `i` there is a `j ≥ i` such that the transition map `M i → M j` factors through
`M i → M k` for every `k ≥ i` — condition (3) of Stacks 059E, which for a system of finitely
presented modules says exactly that `M` is Mittag-Leffler — and that `M` is spanned by a countable
set. Then there is a nonempty countable directed subset `J' ⊆ J` such that `M`, with the canonical
maps `M i → M` for `i ∈ J'`, is a colimit of the restricted system: `M = colim_{i ∈ J'} M i`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem ModuleCat.exists_countable_directedOn_isColimit_whisker
    {R : Type u} [Ring R] [Small.{w} R] {J : Type v} [Preorder J] [IsDirectedOrder J] [Nonempty J]
    {F : J ⥤ ModuleCat.{w} R}
    (hfac : ∀ i : J, ∃ (j : J) (u : i ⟶ j), ∀ (k : J) (v : i ⟶ k),
      ∃ h : F.obj k ⟶ F.obj j, F.map u = F.map v ≫ h)
    {c : Cocone F} (hc : IsColimit c)
    (hcg : ∃ t : Set c.pt, t.Countable ∧ Submodule.span R t = ⊤) :
    ∃ s : Set J, s.Nonempty ∧ s.Countable ∧ DirectedOn (· ≤ ·) s ∧
      Nonempty (IsColimit (c.whisker (Set.mono_coe s).functor))
declarations.comment: Mittag-Leffler as 059E (3); finite presentation of the members is unused

declarations.name: Module.Flat.projective_of_isMittagLeffler_of_countablyGenerated
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 059X.** A flat, Mittag-Leffler, countably generated module over a commutative ring is
projective. The Mittag-Leffler condition is `IsMittagLeffler` (Definition 059F), with its finitely
presented modules and test modules taken in the universe of `M`; countable generation is
`Module.CountablyGenerated`, the existence of a countable spanning set.
declarations.statement:
public theorem Module.Flat.projective_of_isMittagLeffler_of_countablyGenerated
    (R : Type u) [CommRing R] [Small.{v} R] (M : Type v) [AddCommGroup M] [Module R M]
    [Module.Flat R M] (hML : IsMittagLeffler.{u, v, v, v, v} R M)
    (hcg : Module.CountablyGenerated R M) :
    Module.Projective R M
declarations.comment:
Mittag-Leffler is `IsMittagLeffler` (059F) and countable generation is
`Module.CountablyGenerated` (from Tag 0GVD), both cited by name; the companion statements write them
out inline, `isMittagLeffler_def_iff` identifying the two forms. Test data in the universe of `M`,
whence `Small.{v} R`. See the module docstring.

declarations.name: Module.projective_iff_flat_and_mittagLeffler_and_exists_sSupIndep_countable_span
declarations.doc:
Let `R` be a commutative ring and `M` an `R`-module. Then `M` is projective if and only if (1)
`M` is flat, (2) `M` is Mittag-Leffler, and (3) `M` is a direct sum of countably generated
`R`-modules. Being Mittag-Leffler is spelled out in the intrinsic form 059E (1): every map
`f : P → M` from a finitely presented module dominates and is dominated by a map `g : P → Q` into a
finitely presented module, domination meaning `Ker(f ⊗ id_T) = Ker(g ⊗ id_T)` for every `R`-module
`T`. Being a direct sum of countably generated modules is spelled internally, as in 058W and 058Y:
an independent set of submodules of `M` with supremum `⊤`, each spanned by a countable set.
declarations.statement:
public theorem Module.projective_iff_flat_and_mittagLeffler_and_exists_sSupIndep_countable_span
    (R : Type u) [CommRing R] [Small.{v} R] (M : Type v) [AddCommGroup M] [Module R M] :
    Module.Projective R M ↔
      Module.Flat R M ∧
        (∀ (P : Type v) [AddCommGroup P] [Module R P] [Module.FinitePresentation R P]
            (f : P →ₗ[R] M), ∃ (Q : Type v) (_ : AddCommGroup Q) (_ : Module R Q)
              (_ : Module.FinitePresentation R Q) (g : P →ₗ[R] Q), ∀ (T : Type v) [AddCommGroup T]
                [Module R T], LinearMap.ker (f.rTensor T) = LinearMap.ker (g.rTensor T)) ∧
        (∃ S : Set (Submodule R M), sSupIndep S ∧ sSup S = ⊤ ∧
          ∀ N ∈ S, ∃ t : Set M, t.Countable ∧ Submodule.span R t = N)
declarations.comment:
Mittag-Leffler is spelled out inline as condition (1) of 059E, as in 059M, 059N,
059P, 059R, 05CQ, 05D6 and 059X; the direct sum decomposition internally, as an independent set of
submodules of `M` with supremum `⊤`, as in 058W and 058Y, with countable generation as a countable
spanning set, as in 0590. Test data in the universe of `M`, whence `Small.{v} R`. See the module
docstring.

declarations.name: Module.projective_of_forall_rTensor_injective_of_exists_sSupIndep_countable_span
declarations.doc:
Let `f : M → N` be a universally injective map of `R`-modules, that is, one for which
`f ⊗ id_T` is injective for every `R`-module `T`. Suppose `M` is a direct sum of countably
generated `R`-modules and suppose `N` is flat and Mittag-Leffler. Then `M` is projective. Being a
direct sum of countably generated modules is spelled internally, as in 058W and 058Y: an
independent set of submodules of `M` with supremum `⊤`, each spanned by a countable set. Being
Mittag-Leffler is spelled out in the intrinsic form 059E (1): every map `g : P → N` from a finitely
presented module dominates and is dominated by a map `h : P → Q` into a finitely presented module,
domination meaning `Ker(g ⊗ id_T) = Ker(h ⊗ id_T)` for every `R`-module `T`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem Module.projective_of_forall_rTensor_injective_of_exists_sSupIndep_countable_span
    (R : Type u) [CommRing R] [Small.{v} R] (M : Type v) [AddCommGroup M] [Module R M]
    (N : Type v) [AddCommGroup N] [Module R N] [Module.Flat R N] (f : M →ₗ[R] N)
    (hf : ∀ (T : Type v) [AddCommGroup T] [Module R T], Function.Injective (f.rTensor T))
    (hM : ∃ S : Set (Submodule R M), sSupIndep S ∧ sSup S = ⊤ ∧
      ∀ K ∈ S, ∃ t : Set M, t.Countable ∧ Submodule.span R t = K)
    (hML : ∀ (P : Type v) [AddCommGroup P] [Module R P] [Module.FinitePresentation R P]
      (g : P →ₗ[R] N), ∃ (Q : Type v) (_ : AddCommGroup Q) (_ : Module R Q)
        (_ : Module.FinitePresentation R Q) (h : P →ₗ[R] Q), ∀ (T : Type v) [AddCommGroup T]
          [Module R T], LinearMap.ker (g.rTensor T) = LinearMap.ker (h.rTensor T)) :
    Module.Projective R M
declarations.comment:
Universal injectivity of `f` is injectivity of `f ⊗ id_T` for every `T`, as in
058K (1) and 059N; Mittag-Leffler is spelled out inline as condition (1) of 059E, as in 059N, 059X
and 059Z; the direct sum decomposition internally, as an independent set of submodules of `M` with
supremum `⊤`, as in 058W and 058Y, with countable generation as a countable spanning set, as in
0590. Test data in the universe of `M` and `N`, whence `Small.{v} R`. See the module docstring.

declarations.name: Module.projective_of_forall_rTensor_injective_mvPowerSeries_of_exists_sSupIndep_countable_span
declarations.doc:
Let `R` be a Noetherian ring and let `M` be an `R`-module. Suppose `M` is a direct sum of
countably generated `R`-modules, and suppose there is a universally injective map
`f : M → R[[t_1, …, t_n]]` for some `n`, that is, one for which `f ⊗ id_T` is injective for every
`R`-module `T`. Then `M` is projective. Being a direct sum of countably generated modules is
spelled internally, as in 058W, 058Y and 05A0: an independent set of submodules of `M` with
supremum `⊤`, each spanned by a countable set.
declarations.statement:
public theorem
    Module.projective_of_forall_rTensor_injective_mvPowerSeries_of_exists_sSupIndep_countable_span
    (R : Type u) [CommRing R] [IsNoetherianRing R] (M : Type u) [AddCommGroup M] [Module R M]
    (n : ℕ) (f : M →ₗ[R] MvPowerSeries (Fin n) R)
    (hf : ∀ (T : Type u) [AddCommGroup T] [Module R T], Function.Injective (f.rTensor T))
    (hM : ∃ S : Set (Submodule R M), sSupIndep S ∧ sSup S = ⊤ ∧
      ∀ K ∈ S, ∃ t : Set M, t.Countable ∧ Submodule.span R t = K) :
    Module.Projective R M
declarations.comment:
`R[[t_1, …, t_n]]` is `MvPowerSeries (Fin n) R` with its coefficientwise `R`-module
structure, as in 059T; universal injectivity of `f` is injectivity of `f ⊗ id_T` for every `T`, as
in 058K (1), 059N and 05A0; the direct sum decomposition internally, as an independent set of
submodules of `M` with supremum `⊤` each spanned by a countable set, as in 058W, 058Y and 05A0.
`n` and `f` are parameters rather than existentially bound, the conclusion mentioning neither, and
no positivity of `n` is assumed, as none is in the source. See the module docstring.

declarations.name: Module.baseChange_flat_and_mittagLeffler_and_exists_sSupIndep_countable_span_and_projective
declarations.doc:
Base change along a ring map `R → S` preserves flatness, the Mittag-Leffler condition, being
a direct sum of countably generated modules, and projectivity.
declarations.statement:
theorem baseChange_flat_and_mittagLeffler_and_exists_sSupIndep_countable_span_and_projective
    [Small.{v} R] :
    (Module.Flat R M → Module.Flat S (S ⊗[R] M)) ∧
    ((∀ (P : Type v) [AddCommGroup P] [Module R P] [Module.FinitePresentation R P]
      (f : P →ₗ[R] M), ∃ (Q : Type v) (_ : AddCommGroup Q) (_ : Module R Q)
        (_ : Module.FinitePresentation R Q) (g : P →ₗ[R] Q), ∀ (N : Type v) [AddCommGroup N]
          [Module R N], LinearMap.ker (f.rTensor N) = LinearMap.ker (g.rTensor N)) →
      ∀ (P : Type v) [AddCommGroup P] [Module S P] [Module.FinitePresentation S P]
      (f : P →ₗ[S] S ⊗[R] M), ∃ (Q : Type v) (_ : AddCommGroup Q) (_ : Module S Q)
        (_ : Module.FinitePresentation S Q) (g : P →ₗ[S] Q), ∀ (N : Type v) [AddCommGroup N]
          [Module S N], LinearMap.ker (f.rTensor N) = LinearMap.ker (g.rTensor N)) ∧
    ((∃ 𝒮 : Set (Submodule R M), sSupIndep 𝒮 ∧ sSup 𝒮 = ⊤ ∧
        ∀ N ∈ 𝒮, ∃ t : Set M, t.Countable ∧ Submodule.span R t = N) →
      ∃ 𝒮 : Set (Submodule S (S ⊗[R] M)), sSupIndep 𝒮 ∧ sSup 𝒮 = ⊤ ∧
        ∀ N ∈ 𝒮, ∃ t : Set (S ⊗[R] M), t.Countable ∧ Submodule.span S t = N) ∧
    (Module.Projective R M → Module.Projective S (S ⊗[R] M))
declarations.comment:
Mittag-Leffler is spelled out inline as condition (1) of 059E and "direct sum of
countably generated modules" as an independent set of countably spanned submodules with supremum
`⊤`, as in 059M, 05A5 and 058W. The source's `M ⊗_R S` is written `S ⊗[R] M`.

declarations.name: Module.mittagLeffler_of_mittagLeffler_tensorProduct
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 05A5.** Let `R → S` be a faithfully flat ring map and let `M` be an `R`-module. If the
`S`-module `S ⊗_R M` is Mittag-Leffler, then `M` is Mittag-Leffler. The Mittag-Leffler condition is
spelled out in the intrinsic form 059E (1): every map `f` from a finitely presented module into the
module in question dominates and is dominated by a map `g` into a finitely presented module,
domination meaning equality of the kernels of the maps `· ⊗ id_T`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem Module.mittagLeffler_of_mittagLeffler_tensorProduct {R : Type u} [CommRing R]
    [Small.{v} R] {S : Type v} [CommRing S] [Algebra R S] [Module.FaithfullyFlat R S]
    {M : Type v} [AddCommGroup M] [Module R M]
    (hM : ∀ (P : Type v) [AddCommGroup P] [Module S P] [Module.FinitePresentation S P]
      (f : P →ₗ[S] S ⊗[R] M), ∃ (Q : Type v) (_ : AddCommGroup Q) (_ : Module S Q)
        (_ : Module.FinitePresentation S Q) (g : P →ₗ[S] Q), ∀ (T : Type v) [AddCommGroup T]
          [Module S T], LinearMap.ker (f.rTensor T) = LinearMap.ker (g.rTensor T)) :
    ∀ (P : Type v) [AddCommGroup P] [Module R P] [Module.FinitePresentation R P]
      (f : P →ₗ[R] M), ∃ (Q : Type v) (_ : AddCommGroup Q) (_ : Module R Q)
        (_ : Module.FinitePresentation R Q) (g : P →ₗ[R] Q), ∀ (T : Type v) [AddCommGroup T]
          [Module R T], LinearMap.ker (f.rTensor T) = LinearMap.ker (g.rTensor T)
declarations.comment:
Mittag-Leffler is spelled out inline as condition (1) of 059E, as in 05A3, 05CN and
  05CQ. The base change is written `S ⊗[R] M`, Mathlib's order, the source writing `M ⊗_R S`.

declarations.name: Module.countablyGenerated_and_projective_of_faithfullyFlat_baseChange
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 05A6.** Let `R → S` be a faithfully flat ring map and let `M` be an `R`-module. If the
`S`-module `S ⊗_R M` is countably generated and projective, then `M` is countably generated and
projective.
declarations.comment: Countable generation is `Module.CountablyGenerated`, the predicate introduced with 0GVD. The base change is written `S ⊗[R] M`, Mathlib's order, the source writing `M ⊗_R S`.

declarations.name: exists_countablyGenerated_submodule_le_baseChange_range
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Tag 05A7, Lemma 10.95.4.**
Let `R → S` be a ring map, `M` an `R`-module, and `Q` a countably generated
`S`-submodule of `S ⊗[R] M`. Then there exists a countably generated
`R`-submodule `P` of `M` such that `Q ⊆ Im(S ⊗[R] P → S ⊗[R] M)`, where the map
is induced by the inclusion `P ↪ M`.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_countablyGenerated_submodule_le_baseChange_range
    {R S : Type*} [CommRing R] [CommRing S] [Algebra R S]
    {M : Type*} [AddCommGroup M] [Module R M]
    (Q : Submodule S (S ⊗[R] M)) (hQ : Q.IsCountablyGenerated) :
    ∃ P : Submodule R M, P.IsCountablyGenerated ∧
      Q ≤ LinearMap.range (LinearMap.baseChange S P.subtype)

declarations.name: exists_countablyGenerated_baseChange_eq_iSup_of_internal_directSum
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Tag 05A8 / Lemma 10.95.5.**  If `M ⊗_R S` decomposes as an internal
direct sum of countably generated `S`-submodules `Q_i`, then any countably
generated `R`-submodule `N` of `M` is contained in a countably generated
`R`-submodule `N'` whose image `Im(N' ⊗_R S → M ⊗_R S) = N'.baseChange S` equals
the partial direct sum `⨁_{i ∈ I'} Q_i` over some subset `I' ⊆ I`.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_countablyGenerated_baseChange_eq_iSup_of_internal_directSum
    (Q : I → Submodule S (TensorProduct R S M))
    (hQ : DirectSum.IsInternal Q)
    (hQcg : ∀ i, (Q i).IsCountablyGenerated)
    (N : Submodule R M) (hN : N.IsCountablyGenerated) :
    ∃ (N' : Submodule R M) (I' : Set I),
      N'.IsCountablyGenerated ∧ N ≤ N' ∧
      N'.baseChange S = ⨆ i : I', Q i

declarations.name: Module.Projective.of_projective_tensorProduct
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 05A9.** Let `R → S` be a faithfully flat ring map and let `M` be an `R`-module. If
the `S`-module `S ⊗_R M` is projective, then `M` is projective. This is the projective analogue of
`Module.Flat.of_flat_tensorProduct`, and it assumes no finiteness of `M`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem Projective.of_projective_tensorProduct {R : Type*} [CommRing R] {M : Type*}
    [AddCommGroup M] [Module R M] (S : Type*) [CommRing S] [Algebra R S]
    [Module.FaithfullyFlat R S] [Module.Projective S (S ⊗[R] M)] :
    Module.Projective R M
declarations.comment:
The source's `M ⊗_R S` is written `S ⊗[R] M`, Mathlib's order for a base change and
  the one used by `Module.Flat.of_flat_tensorProduct`. The finite case is 058S and the countably
  generated case is 05A6; neither hypothesis appears here.

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.associatedPoints_subset_support

support.

lemma associatedPoints_subset_support {X : Scheme.{u}} (F : X.Modules) :

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.associatedPoints_subset_of_mono
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 05AE.** The associated points of a subsheaf are associated points of
the ambient sheaf.
declarations.statement:
theorem associatedPoints_subset_of_mono {X : Scheme.{u}} {F₁ F₂ : X.Modules} (f : F₁ ⟶ F₂)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.associatedPoints_subset_union_of_shortExact
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 05AE.** The associated points of the middle term of a short exact
sequence lie in the union of those of its outer terms.
declarations.statement:
theorem associatedPoints_subset_union_of_shortExact {X : Scheme.{u}}

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.associatedPoints_inter_finite
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 05AF.** A coherent module on a locally Noetherian scheme has only
finitely many associated points in a quasi-compact open subset.

theorem associatedPoints_inter_finite {X : Scheme.{u}} [IsLocallyNoetherian X] (F : X.Modules)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.isZero_iff_associatedPoints_eq_empty
declarations.doc:
A quasi-coherent module on a locally Noetherian scheme is zero if and only if its set of
associated points is empty.
declarations.statement:
theorem isZero_iff_associatedPoints_eq_empty (X : Scheme.{u}) [IsLocallyNoetherian X]
    (F : X.Modules) [F.IsQuasicoherent] :
    IsZero F ↔ Stacks.Divisors.associatedPoints F = ∅

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.mem_associatedPoints_of_mem_supp_of_specialization
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 05AH.** A point of the support of a quasi-coherent module on a locally
Noetherian scheme which is not a specialization of another point of the support is associated to
the module.
declarations.statement:
theorem mem_associatedPoints_of_mem_supp_of_specialization (X : Scheme.{u})

    (hx : x ∈ SheafOfModules.supp F)

    x ∈ Stacks.Divisors.associatedPoints F

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.mem_schemeAssociatedPoints_of_isGenericPoint_irreducibleComponent
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 05AH.** Every generic point of an irreducible component of a locally
Noetherian scheme is an associated point of the scheme.
declarations.statement:
theorem mem_schemeAssociatedPoints_of_isGenericPoint_irreducibleComponent (X : Scheme.{u})

declarations.comment: generic points of irreducible components

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.maximalIdeal_locallyNilpotent

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.spectrum_associatedPoints_eq_empty

**Stacks 05AI.** The spectrum of the square-zero-variable quotient has no associated

theorem spectrum_associatedPoints_eq_empty (k : Type u) [Field k] :
