declarations.name: exists_isIdempotentElem_add_sq_sub_mul_sum
declarations.doc:
Let `A` be a possibly noncommutative ring and let `e ∈ A` be such that `x = e ^ 2 - e` is
nilpotent. Then there is an idempotent of the form `e + x * (∑ a i j • (e ^ i * x ^ j))` with
integer coefficients `a i j`.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_isIdempotentElem_add_sq_sub_mul_sum {e : A} (he : IsNilpotent (e ^ 2 - e)) :
    ∃ (N : ℕ) (a : ℕ → ℕ → ℤ), IsIdempotentElem (e + (e ^ 2 - e) *
      ∑ i ∈ Finset.range N, ∑ j ∈ Finset.range N, a i j • (e ^ i * (e ^ 2 - e) ^ j))

declarations.name: Module.mem_associatedPrimes_of_minimal_mem_support
declarations.doc:
Let `R` be a Noetherian ring and let `M` be an `R`-module. Any prime `𝔭` which is minimal among
the elements of the support of `M` is an associated prime of `M`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem Module.mem_associatedPrimes_of_minimal_mem_support {R : Type*} [CommRing R]
    [IsNoetherianRing R] {M : Type*} [AddCommGroup M] [Module R M] {p : PrimeSpectrum R}
    (hp : Minimal (· ∈ Module.support R M) p) :
    p.asIdeal ∈ associatedPrimes R M

declarations.name: spec_image_ass_subset
declarations.doc:
Stacks Tag 05BW (Lemma 10.63.11): for a ring map `φ : R → S` and an
`S`-module `M` viewed as an `R`-module via restriction of scalars along `φ`
(encoded by `hcompat : ∀ r m, r • m = φ r • m`), the image of `Ass_S(M)` under
the contraction map `Spec(φ) = Ideal.comap φ` is contained in `Ass_R(M)`.
declarations.statement:
theorem spec_image_ass_subset
    {R S M : Type*} [CommSemiring R] [CommSemiring S]
    [AddCommMonoid M] [Module R M] [Module S M] (φ : R →+* S)
    (hcompat : ∀ (r : R) (m : M), r • m = φ r • m) :
    (Ideal.comap φ) '' (assOf S (M := M)) ⊆ assOf R (M := M)

declarations.name: assExact_not_functorial
declarations.doc:
Together, the two statements above witness the failure of functoriality of
associated primes along `algebraMap k (S k)`: `Ass_k(S) ≠ ∅` while `Ass_S(S) = ∅`.
declarations.statement:
theorem assExact_not_functorial (k : Type*) [Field k] :
    (assExact k (S k)).Nonempty ∧ assExact (S k) (S k) = ∅

declarations.name: Stacks.AssociatedPrimes.main_theorem_05by
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Tag 05BY.** Contraction along `π : R → R ⧸ I` carries the associated primes
of `M` over `R ⧸ I` onto the associated primes of `M` over `R`.
declarations.statement:
theorem main_theorem_05by :
    (fun p : Ideal (R ⧸ I) => p.comap (Ideal.Quotient.mk I)) '' assPrimes (R ⧸ I) M =
      assPrimes R M

declarations.name: Stacks.AssociatedPrimes.assPrimes_eq_image_comap_assPrimes
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 05BZ (1).** For `R'` a localization `S⁻¹R` and any `R'`-module `M'` (in particular
`M' = S⁻¹M`), the associated primes of `M'` over `R` are the contractions along
`Spec(S⁻¹R) → Spec(R)` of its associated primes over `R'`:
`Ass_R(M') = Ass_{S⁻¹R}(M')`.
declarations.statement:
theorem assPrimes_eq_image_comap_assPrimes :
    assPrimes R M' = Ideal.comap (algebraMap R R') '' assPrimes R' M'

declarations.name: Stacks.AssociatedPrimes.assPrimes_inter_image_comap_subset
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 05BZ (2).** Via the canonical injection `Spec(S⁻¹R) → Spec(R)`, whose image is
`Ideal.comap (algebraMap R R') '' {J | J.IsPrime}`, we have
`Ass_R(M) ∩ Spec(S⁻¹R) ⊆ Ass_R(S⁻¹M)`.
declarations.statement:
theorem assPrimes_inter_image_comap_subset :
    assPrimes R M ∩ Ideal.comap (algebraMap R R') '' {J | J.IsPrime} ⊆ assPrimes R M'

declarations.name: Stacks.AssociatedPrimes.assPrimes_inter_image_comap_eq
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 05BZ (3).** If `R` is Noetherian, the inclusion of Stacks 05BZ (2) is an equality:
`Ass_R(M) ∩ Spec(S⁻¹R) = Ass_R(S⁻¹M)`.
declarations.statement:
theorem assPrimes_inter_image_comap_eq [IsNoetherianRing R] :
    assPrimes R M ∩ Ideal.comap (algebraMap R R') '' {J | J.IsPrime} = assPrimes R M'

declarations.name: AssLocalization.assPrimes_localizedModule_eq
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Tag 05C0 / Lemma 10.63.17.**
If every element of the multiplicative subset `S` is a nonzerodivisor on the
`R`-module `M`, then the (exact-annihilator) associated primes of `M` and of its
localization `S⁻¹M = LocalizedModule S M` (both as `R`-modules) coincide.
declarations.statement:
theorem assPrimes_localizedModule_eq (S : Submonoid R) (hS : AllNonZeroDivisorsOn S M) :
    Stacks.AssociatedPrimes.assPrimes R M
      = Stacks.AssociatedPrimes.assPrimes R (LocalizedModule S M)

declarations.name: Stacks.AssociatedPrimes.Localization.assPrimes_chain
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 05C1 / Lemma 10.65.4.**  Let `R → S` be a ring map, `N` an `S`-module that is flat
over `R`, and `K` the fraction field of `R` (more generally, its total ring of fractions).
Then `Ass_S(N) = Ass_S(N ⊗_R K) = Ass_{S ⊗_R K}(N ⊗_R K)` via the canonical inclusion
`Spec(S ⊗_R K) ⊆ Spec(S)`: the first equality holds as sets of ideals of `S`, and contraction
along `algebraMap S (S ⊗_R K)` is injective on ideals and maps `Ass_{S ⊗_R K}(N ⊗_R K)` onto
`Ass_S(N ⊗_R K)`.  Here `Ass` is the exact-annihilator notion `assPrimes` of Stacks 00LA,
`S ⊗_R K` is modelled as the localization `SK` of `S` at the image of `R⁰`, and `N ⊗_R K` as
the localization `NK` of `N` at `R⁰` (over `R`) and at the image of `R⁰` (over `S`), the two
localization maps agreeing.
declarations.statement:
theorem assPrimes_chain [Module.Flat R N] (μN : N →ₗ[R] NK) (μNₛ : N →ₗ[S] NK)
    (hSK : IsLocalization (Algebra.algebraMapSubmonoid S (nonZeroDivisors R)) SK)
    (hμN : IsLocalizedModule (nonZeroDivisors R) μN)
    (hμNₛ : IsLocalizedModule (Algebra.algebraMapSubmonoid S (nonZeroDivisors R)) μNₛ)
    (hμ : ∀ n, μNₛ n = μN n) :
    assPrimes S N = assPrimes S NK ∧
      Function.Injective (Ideal.comap (algebraMap S SK)) ∧
      Ideal.comap (algebraMap S SK) '' assPrimes SK NK = assPrimes S NK
declarations.comment: Exact-annihilator Ass (00LA); S ⊗_R K and N ⊗_R K modelled by their localization universal properties; R generalized from a domain to any ring with K its total ring of fractions.

declarations.name: assStacks_tensorProduct_of_flat_fiberRing
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Tag 05C2.** Let `R → S` be a ring map, let `M` be an `R`-module and let `N` be an
`S`-module which is flat as an `R`-module. Viewing `Spec(S ⊗_R κ(𝔭))` as a subset of `Spec(S)`
(Remark 00E6), we have
`Ass_S(N ⊗_R M) ⊇ ⋃_{𝔭 ∈ Ass_R(M)} Ass_{S ⊗_R κ(𝔭)}(N ⊗_R κ(𝔭))`,
and this inclusion is an equality if `R` is Noetherian. Every `Ass` is that of Definition 00LA,
`IsAssociatedPrimeStacks`: the primes that are the annihilator of an element, over `R`, over `S`
and over the fibre rings, with no Noetherian hypothesis on `S` or on the fibre rings.

The source writes `M ⊗_R N`; it is `N ⊗[R] M` here, the `S`-module structure being carried by the
left factor, and the two are the same `S`-module by `TensorProduct.comm`. The fibre module
`N ⊗_R κ(𝔭)` is spelled as the base change `(S ⊗[R] κ(𝔭)) ⊗[S] N`, which carries the action of
the fibre ring and is `S`-isomorphic to `N ⊗[R] κ(𝔭)` by
`TensorProduct.AlgebraTensorModule.cancelBaseChange`. The inclusion
`Spec(S ⊗_R κ(𝔭)) ⊆ Spec(S)` is the image under `PrimeSpectrum.comap` of the canonical map
`S → S ⊗_R κ(𝔭)`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem assStacks_tensorProduct_of_flat_fiberRing {R S M N : Type*} [CommRing R]
    [CommRing S] [Algebra R S] [AddCommGroup M] [Module R M] [AddCommGroup N] [Module S N]
    [Module R N] [IsScalarTower R S N] [Module.Flat R N] :
    (⋃ p ∈ {p : PrimeSpectrum R | IsAssociatedPrimeStacks R M p.asIdeal},
        PrimeSpectrum.comap (algebraMap S (S ⊗[R] p.asIdeal.ResidueField)) ''
          {Q | IsAssociatedPrimeStacks (S ⊗[R] p.asIdeal.ResidueField)
            ((S ⊗[R] p.asIdeal.ResidueField) ⊗[S] N) Q.asIdeal}) ⊆
      {q : PrimeSpectrum S | IsAssociatedPrimeStacks S (N ⊗[R] M) q.asIdeal} ∧
    (IsNoetherianRing R →
      {q : PrimeSpectrum S | IsAssociatedPrimeStacks S (N ⊗[R] M) q.asIdeal} =
        ⋃ p ∈ {p : PrimeSpectrum R | IsAssociatedPrimeStacks R M p.asIdeal},
          PrimeSpectrum.comap (algebraMap S (S ⊗[R] p.asIdeal.ResidueField)) ''
            {Q | IsAssociatedPrimeStacks (S ⊗[R] p.asIdeal.ResidueField)
              ((S ⊗[R] p.asIdeal.ResidueField) ⊗[S] N) Q.asIdeal})
declarations.comment: Every `Ass` is that of Definition 00LA (`IsAssociatedPrimeStacks`), over `R`, over `S` and over the fibre rings; the fibre module `N ⊗_R κ(𝔭)` is written `(S ⊗[R] κ(𝔭)) ⊗[S] N`.

declarations.name: iUnion_weaklyAssociatedPrimes_eq_zeroDivisorsOn
declarations.doc:
Let `R` be a commutative ring and `M` an `R`-module. The union of the weakly associated primes
of `M` is the set of zerodivisors on `M`.
declarations.statement:
theorem iUnion_weaklyAssociatedPrimes_eq_zeroDivisorsOn
    (R : Type*) [CommRing R] (M : Type*) [AddCommGroup M] [Module R M] :
    (⋃ q ∈ weaklyAssociatedPrimes05C3 R M, (q : Set R)) = zeroDivisorsOn05C3 R M

declarations.name: Module.exists_mem_minimalPrimes_annihilator_span_singleton_of_minimal_mem_support
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 05C4.** Let `R` be a ring and `M` an `R`-module. Any prime `𝔭` which is minimal among
the elements of the support of `M` is weakly associated to `M`, i.e. `𝔭` is minimal over the
annihilator of some element of `M`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem Module.exists_mem_minimalPrimes_annihilator_span_singleton_of_minimal_mem_support
    {R : Type*} [CommRing R] {M : Type*} [AddCommGroup M] [Module R M] {p : PrimeSpectrum R}
    (hp : Minimal (· ∈ Module.support R M) p) :
    ∃ m : M, p.asIdeal ∈ (R ∙ m).annihilator.minimalPrimes

declarations.name: weakAss_subset_image_comap
declarations.doc:
Stacks tag 05C6 (Lemma 10.66.11): for a ring map `φ : R → S` and an `S`-module `M`
regarded as an `R`-module by restriction of scalars along `φ`, every prime of `R` weakly
associated to `M` is the contraction along `φ` of a prime of `S` weakly associated
to `M`.
declarations.statement:
theorem weakAss_subset_image_comap
    {R S : Type*} [CommRing R] [CommRing S] (φ : R →+* S)
    {M : Type*} [AddCommGroup M] [Module S M] :
    letI : Module R M := Module.compHom M φ
    weaklyAssociatedPrimes R M ⊆ (Ideal.comap φ) '' (weaklyAssociatedPrimes S M)

declarations.name: weaklyAssociatedPrimes_comap_quotient
declarations.doc:
For a commutative ring `R`, an ideal `I`, and an `R/I`-module `M` (viewed as an `R`-module by
restriction of scalars), the canonical injection `π* = Ideal.comap (R → R/I)` carries the weakly
associated primes computed over `R/I` onto those computed over `R`.
declarations.statement:
theorem weaklyAssociatedPrimes_comap_quotient :
    Ideal.comap (Ideal.Quotient.mk I) '' weaklyAssociatedPrimes (R ⧸ I) M
      = weaklyAssociatedPrimes R M

declarations.name: weakAss_localizedModule_eq_image
declarations.doc:
`WeakAss_R(S⁻¹M) = ι(WeakAss_{S⁻¹R}(S⁻¹M))`: the `R`-module weakly associated primes of `S⁻¹M`
are the image under `ι` of the `S⁻¹R`-module weakly associated primes of `S⁻¹M`.
declarations.statement:
theorem weakAss_localizedModule_eq_image :
    weakAss R (LocalizedModule S M) =
      localizationComap S '' (weakAss (Localization S) (LocalizedModule S M))

declarations.name: weakAss_inter_image_eq_weakAss_localizedModule
declarations.doc:
`{ p ∈ WeakAss_R(M) | p ∈ ι(Spec(S⁻¹R)) } = WeakAss_R(S⁻¹M)`: the primes weakly associated to
`M` and lying in the image of `ι` (i.e. disjoint from `S`) are exactly the primes weakly associated
to `S⁻¹M`.
declarations.statement:
theorem weakAss_inter_image_eq_weakAss_localizedModule :
    {p ∈ weakAss R M | p ∈ Set.range (localizationComap S)} =
      weakAss R (LocalizedModule S M)

declarations.name: Module.weaklyAssociatedPrimes_eq_of_isSMulRegular_of_isLocalizedModule
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 05CA.** Let `R` be a ring, `M` an `R`-module and `S ⊆ R` a multiplicative subset such
that every `s ∈ S` is a nonzerodivisor on `M`. Then `M` and its localization `S⁻¹M` have the same
weakly associated primes: `WeakAss(M) = WeakAss(S⁻¹M)`, where `WeakAss(N)` is the set of primes of
`R` minimal over the annihilator of an element of `N`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem Module.weaklyAssociatedPrimes_eq_of_isSMulRegular_of_isLocalizedModule
    {R : Type*} [CommSemiring R] {M M' : Type*}
    [AddCommMonoid M] [Module R M] [AddCommMonoid M'] [Module R M']
    (S : Submonoid R) (f : M →ₗ[R] M') [IsLocalizedModule S f]
    (hS : ∀ s ∈ S, IsSMulRegular M s) :
    {p : Ideal R | ∃ m : M, p ∈ (R ∙ m).annihilator.minimalPrimes} =
      {p : Ideal R | ∃ m : M', p ∈ (R ∙ m).annihilator.minimalPrimes}

declarations.name: Module.injective_pi_localization_weaklyAssociatedPrimes
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 05CB.** Let `R` be a ring and `M` an `R`-module. The canonical map
`M → ∏_{𝔭 ∈ WeakAss(M)} M_𝔭` from `M` to the product of its localizations at the weakly
associated primes of `M` — the primes minimal over the annihilator of an element of `M` — is
injective.
declarations.statement:
public theorem Module.injective_pi_localization_weaklyAssociatedPrimes
    {R : Type*} [CommRing R] {M : Type*} [AddCommGroup M] [Module R M]
    {Mₚ : {p : PrimeSpectrum R // ∃ m : M, p.asIdeal ∈ (R ∙ m).annihilator.minimalPrimes} → Type*}
    [∀ p, AddCommMonoid (Mₚ p)] [∀ p, Module R (Mₚ p)] (f : ∀ p, M →ₗ[R] Mₚ p)
    [∀ p, IsLocalizedModule.AtPrime p.1.asIdeal (f p)] :
    Function.Injective (LinearMap.pi f)

declarations.name: Stacks.WeaklyAssociatedPrimes.BaseChange.weakAss_eq_of_flat_domain
declarations.doc:
Stacks tag 05CC (Lemma 10.66.18): let `R → S` be a ring map and `N` an `S`-module that
is flat over the domain `R` (with `Module R N` compatible with the `S`-action via
`IsScalarTower R S N`). Identifying `S ⊗_R K` with `A = Localization T_S`, `N ⊗_R K` with
`M = LocalizedModule T_S N`, and `Spec(S ⊗_R K)` with its image in `Spec(S)` under
`PrimeSpectrum.comap (algebraMap S A)`, the weakly associated primes of `N` over `S` are
exactly the images of the weakly associated primes of `N ⊗_R K` over `S ⊗_R K`: a prime `q`
of `S` is weakly associated to `N` if and only if there is a prime `q'` of `A` that is
weakly associated to `M` and whose contraction along `S → A` equals `q`.
declarations.statement:
theorem weakAss_eq_of_flat_domain
    [Module.Flat R N] (q : PrimeSpectrum S) :
    IsWeaklyAssociatedPrime S N q.asIdeal ↔
      ∃ q' : PrimeSpectrum (Localization (baseChangeSubmonoid R S)),
        IsWeaklyAssociatedPrime (Localization (baseChangeSubmonoid R S))
          (LocalizedModule (baseChangeSubmonoid R S) N) q'.asIdeal ∧
        PrimeSpectrum.comap (algebraMap S (Localization (baseChangeSubmonoid R S))) q' = q

declarations.name: Module.projective_iff_homLeft_shortExact
declarations.doc:
An `R`-module `P` is projective if and only if `Hom_R(P, -)` carries every short exact
sequence `0 → N₁ → N₂ → N₃ → 0` to a short exact sequence
`0 → Hom(P, N₁) → Hom(P, N₂) → Hom(P, N₃) → 0`.
declarations.statement:
theorem projective_iff_homLeft_shortExact :
    Module.Projective R P ↔ ∀ (N₁ N₂ N₃ : Type (max u v)) [AddCommGroup N₁] [Module R N₁]
      [AddCommGroup N₂] [Module R N₂] [AddCommGroup N₃] [Module R N₃]
      (f : N₁ →ₗ[R] N₂) (g : N₂ →ₗ[R] N₃), Function.Injective f → Function.Exact f g →
        Function.Surjective g →
        Function.Injective (LinearMap.compRight (M := P) ℕ f) ∧
        Function.Exact (LinearMap.compRight (M := P) ℕ f) (LinearMap.compRight (M := P) ℕ g) ∧
        Function.Surjective (LinearMap.compRight (M := P) ℕ g)
declarations.comment: elementwise form, any ring

declarations.name: Module.projective_iff_shortExact_map_linearCoyoneda
declarations.doc:
An `R`-module `P` is projective if and only if the functor
`Hom_R(P, -) : ModuleCat R ⥤ ModuleCat R` sends short exact sequences to short exact
sequences.
declarations.statement:
theorem projective_iff_shortExact_map_linearCoyoneda :
    Module.Projective R P ↔ ∀ S : ShortComplex (ModuleCat.{max u v} R), S.ShortExact →
      (S.map ((linearCoyoneda R (ModuleCat.{max u v} R)).obj
        (op (ModuleCat.of R P)))).ShortExact

declarations.name: Module.projective_iff_preservesFiniteLimits_and_preservesFiniteColimits_linearCoyoneda
declarations.doc:
An `R`-module `P` is projective if and only if the functor
`Hom_R(P, -) : ModuleCat R ⥤ ModuleCat R` is exact, in the sense that it preserves finite
limits and finite colimits.
declarations.statement:
theorem projective_iff_preservesFiniteLimits_and_preservesFiniteColimits_linearCoyoneda :
    Module.Projective R P ↔
      PreservesFiniteLimits ((linearCoyoneda R (ModuleCat.{max u v} R)).obj
        (op (ModuleCat.of R P))) ∧
      PreservesFiniteColimits ((linearCoyoneda R (ModuleCat.{max u v} R)).obj
        (op (ModuleCat.of R P)))
declarations.comment: exact functor as preserving finite limits and finite colimits

declarations.name: characterize_projective
declarations.doc:
Theorem (Stacks Tag 05CF). For an `R`-module `P`, the three conditions
"`P` is projective (lifting property)", "`P` is a direct summand of a free
module", and "`Ext^1_R(P, M) = 0` for all `M`" are equivalent.
declarations.statement:
theorem characterize_projective (P : Type u) [AddCommGroup P] [Module R P] :
    List.TFAE
      [IsProjectiveLifting R P, IsDirectSummandOfFree R P, ExtOneVanishes R P]

declarations.name: Module.Flat.projective_of_isNilpotent_of_projective_quotient_smul_top
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 05CG.** Let `R` be a ring, let `I ⊆ R` be a nilpotent ideal and let `M` be a flat
`R`-module such that `M/IM` is a projective `R ⧸ I`-module. Then `M` is a projective
`R`-module.
declarations.statement:
public theorem Module.Flat.projective_of_isNilpotent_of_projective_quotient_smul_top
    {R : Type u} [CommRing R] {I : Ideal R} {M : Type v} [AddCommGroup M] [Module R M]
    [Module.Flat R M] (hI : IsNilpotent I)
    (hM : Module.Projective (R ⧸ I) (M ⧸ I • (⊤ : Submodule R M))) :
    Module.Projective R M

declarations.name: UniversallyInjective.rTensor
declarations.doc:
If `u : M →ₗ[R] M'` is universally injective, then for any `R`-module `N` the induced map
`u ⊗ id_N : M ⊗_R N → M' ⊗_R N` (i.e. `LinearMap.rTensor N u`) is again universally
injective. The ring lives in any universe `u` and the modules in any universe `v`.
declarations.statement:
theorem UniversallyInjective.rTensor {R : Type u} [CommRing R]
    {M : Type v} [AddCommGroup M] [Module R M]
    {M' : Type v} [AddCommGroup M'] [Module R M']
    {u : M →ₗ[R] M'} (hu : UniversallyInjective u)
    (N : Type v) [AddCommGroup N] [Module R N] :
    UniversallyInjective (LinearMap.rTensor N u)

declarations.name: comp_universallyInjective
declarations.doc: A composition of universally injective `R`-module maps is universally injective.
declarations.statement:
theorem comp_universallyInjective {R : Type u} [CommRing R] {M N P : Type*}
    [AddCommGroup M] [AddCommGroup N] [AddCommGroup P]
    [Module R M] [Module R N] [Module R P]
    (f : M →ₗ[R] N) (g : N →ₗ[R] P)
    (hf : IsPureMono.{u, v} f) (hg : IsPureMono.{u, v} g) :
    IsPureMono.{u, v} (g ∘ₗ f)

declarations.name: Function.Injective.of_rTensor_comp
declarations.doc:
Let `f : M →ₗ[R] M'` and `g : M' →ₗ[R] M''` be `R`-module maps and let `Q` be an `R`-module.
If `(g ∘ₗ f) ⊗ id_Q` is injective, then so is `f ⊗ id_Q`. Quantifying over `Q`: if the
composition `g ∘ₗ f` is universally injective, then `f` is universally injective.
declarations.comment: Stated for one test module `Q`; the source's form is its closure over `Q`.

declarations.name: faithfullyFlat_universallyInjective
declarations.doc:
For a faithfully flat ring map `φ : R → S`, the structure map `R → S` viewed as an
`R`-linear map (`Algebra.linearMap R S`, where `S` is given its `R`-module structure
via `φ`) is universally injective: for every `R`-module `Q`, the induced map
`R ⊗_R Q → S ⊗_R Q` is injective.
declarations.statement:
theorem faithfullyFlat_universallyInjective
    {R S : Type*} [CommRing R] [CommRing S] (φ : R →+* S) (hφ : φ.FaithfullyFlat) :
    haveI := φ.toAlgebra
    UniversallyInjectivePoly (Algebra.linearMap R S)

declarations.name: faithfullyFlat_comap_map_eq
declarations.doc:
For a faithfully flat ring map `φ : R → S` and every ideal `I ⊆ R`, the contraction
of the extended ideal `I S` back to `R` equals `I`, i.e. `φ⁻¹(I S) = I`.

This is Mathlib's `Ideal.comap_map_eq_self_of_faithfullyFlat`, restated for a bare ring map.
declarations.statement:
theorem faithfullyFlat_comap_map_eq
    {R S : Type*} [CommRing R] [CommRing S] (φ : R →+* S) (hφ : φ.FaithfullyFlat)
    (I : Ideal R) :
    Ideal.comap φ (Ideal.map φ I) = I
declarations.comment: in particular

declarations.name: Stacks.UniversalInjectivity.LocalizationCriteria.universally_injective_check_stalks
declarations.doc:
For a ring map `R → S` and a map `f : M → M'` of `S`-modules, universal injectivity of `f` as
a map of `R`-modules can be checked on localizations: the following are equivalent: `f` is
universally injective over `R`; `f_q` is, for every prime `q` of `S`; `f_m` is, for every maximal
ideal `m` of `S`; and the corresponding statements over the localizations `R_p`.
declarations.statement:
theorem universally_injective_check_stalks
    {R : Type u} {S : Type v} [CommRing R] [CommRing S] [Algebra R S]
    {M : Type w} {M' : Type w'}
    [AddCommGroup M] [Module S M] [Module R M] [IsScalarTower R S M]
    [AddCommGroup M'] [Module S M'] [Module R M'] [IsScalarTower R S M']
    (f : M →ₗ[S] M') :
    [ -- (1) f is universally injective as a map of R-modules
      UniversallyInjective.{max u t} (f.restrictScalars R),
      -- (2) for every prime q of S, f_q is universally injective as a map of R-modules
      ∀ (q : Ideal S) [q.IsPrime], UniversallyInjective.{max u t} (A := R) (localizedMapR f q),
      -- (3) for every maximal m of S, f_m is universally injective as a map of R-modules
      ∀ (m : Ideal S) [m.IsMaximal], UniversallyInjective.{max u t} (A := R) (localizedMapR f m),
      -- (4) for every prime q of S, f_q is universally injective as a map of R_p-modules
      ∀ (q : Ideal S) [q.IsPrime],
        UniversallyInjective.{max u t} (A := Localization.AtPrime (q.under R)) (localizedMapRp f q),
      -- (5) for every maximal m of S, f_m is universally injective as a map of R_p-modules
      ∀ (m : Ideal S) [m.IsMaximal],
        UniversallyInjective.{max u t} (A := Localization.AtPrime (m.under R)) (localizedMapRp f m)
    ].TFAE

declarations.name: IsLocalizedModule.rTensor_injective_of_rTensor_injective_and_iff_extendScalars
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 05CM.** Let `A → B` be a ring map, let `S ⊆ A` and `S' ⊆ B` be multiplicative
subsets, let `f : M → M'` be a map of `B`-modules and let `fₛ : N → N'` be its localization at
`S'`, pinned by the square `fₛ ∘ₗ g = g' ∘ₗ f`. Let `Q` be an `A`-module with localization
`S⁻¹Q` at `S`. Then:

1. if `f ⊗ id_Q` is injective, so is `fₛ ⊗ id_Q`, both tensor products taken over `A`;
2. `fₛ ⊗_A id_Q` is injective if and only if `fₛ ⊗_{S⁻¹A} id_{S⁻¹Q}` is injective.

This is the source's own sentence, about one localized map. The two items are independent of each
other and each is stated separately, over its own data alone, as
`IsLocalizedModule.rTensor_injective_of_rTensor_injective` and
`LinearMap.rTensor_injective_iff_extendScalarsOfIsLocalization`; those are the forms to cite.
declarations.statement:
public theorem IsLocalizedModule.rTensor_injective_of_rTensor_injective_and_iff_extendScalars
    {A B : Type*} [CommRing A] [CommRing B] [Algebra A B] (S : Submonoid A) (S' : Submonoid B)
    (Aₛ : Type*) [CommRing Aₛ] [Algebra A Aₛ] [IsLocalization S Aₛ] {M M' N N' Q Qₛ : Type*}
    [AddCommGroup M] [Module A M] [Module B M] [IsScalarTower A B M]
    [AddCommGroup M'] [Module A M'] [Module B M'] [IsScalarTower A B M']
    [AddCommGroup N] [Module A N] [Module B N] [IsScalarTower A B N]
    [Module Aₛ N] [IsScalarTower A Aₛ N]
    [AddCommGroup N'] [Module A N'] [Module B N'] [IsScalarTower A B N']
    [Module Aₛ N'] [IsScalarTower A Aₛ N']
    [AddCommGroup Q] [Module A Q] [AddCommGroup Qₛ] [Module A Qₛ] [Module Aₛ Qₛ]
    [IsScalarTower A Aₛ Qₛ] (g : M →ₗ[B] N) (g' : M' →ₗ[B] N') [IsLocalizedModule S' g]
    [IsLocalizedModule S' g'] (q : Q →ₗ[A] Qₛ) [IsLocalizedModule S q] (f : M →ₗ[B] M')
    (fₛ : N →ₗ[B] N') (hf : fₛ ∘ₗ g = g' ∘ₗ f) :
    (Function.Injective ((f.restrictScalars A).rTensor Q) →
        Function.Injective ((fₛ.restrictScalars A).rTensor Q)) ∧
      (Function.Injective ((fₛ.restrictScalars A).rTensor Q) ↔
        Function.Injective ((LinearMap.extendScalarsOfIsLocalization S Aₛ
          (fₛ.restrictScalars A)).rTensor Qₛ))
declarations.comment:
Items (1) and (2) together, for one test module `Q`; the source's form is the
closure over `Q`.

declarations.name: IsLocalizedModule.rTensor_injective_of_rTensor_injective
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 05CM, item (1).** Let `A → B` be a ring map, let `S' ⊆ B` be a multiplicative subset,
let `f : M → M'` be a map of `B`-modules and let `fₛ : N → N'` be its localization at `S'`, pinned
by the square `fₛ ∘ₗ g = g' ∘ₗ f`. Let `Q` be an `A`-module. If `f ⊗ id_Q` is injective, so is
`fₛ ⊗ id_Q`, both tensor products taken over `A`.

Quantifying over `Q`: if `f` is universally injective as a map of `A`-modules, then so is its
localization at `S'`. Composed with
`LinearMap.rTensor_injective_iff_extendScalarsOfIsLocalization` this gives the universal
injectivity of the localization as a map of `S⁻¹A`-modules as well, for any `S ⊆ A` with
`φ(S) ⊆ S'`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem IsLocalizedModule.rTensor_injective_of_rTensor_injective
    {A B : Type*} [CommRing A] [CommRing B] [Algebra A B] (S' : Submonoid B)
    {M M' N N' : Type*}
    [AddCommGroup M] [Module A M] [Module B M] [IsScalarTower A B M]
    [AddCommGroup M'] [Module A M'] [Module B M'] [IsScalarTower A B M']
    [AddCommGroup N] [Module A N] [Module B N] [IsScalarTower A B N]
    [AddCommGroup N'] [Module A N'] [Module B N'] [IsScalarTower A B N']
    (g : M →ₗ[B] N) (g' : M' →ₗ[B] N') [IsLocalizedModule S' g] [IsLocalizedModule S' g']
    (f : M →ₗ[B] M') (fₛ : N →ₗ[B] N') (hf : fₛ ∘ₗ g = g' ∘ₗ f) (Q : Type*) [AddCommGroup Q]
    [Module A Q] (h : Function.Injective ((f.restrictScalars A).rTensor Q)) :
    Function.Injective ((fₛ.restrictScalars A).rTensor Q)
declarations.comment: Item (1), for one test module `Q`; the source's form is the closure over `Q`.

declarations.name: LinearMap.rTensor_injective_iff_extendScalarsOfIsLocalization
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 05CM, item (2).** Let `S ⊆ A` be a multiplicative subset, let `fₛ : N → N'` be a map
of `A`-modules between two `S⁻¹A`-modules and let `Q` be an `A`-module with localization `S⁻¹Q` at
`S`. Then `fₛ ⊗_A id_Q` is injective if and only if `fₛ ⊗_{S⁻¹A} id_{S⁻¹Q}` is injective.

Quantifying over `Q`: for a map between `S⁻¹A`-modules — in particular between `(S')⁻¹B`-modules,
for a multiplicative `S' ⊆ B` with `φ(S) ⊆ S'`, which is the case the source states — universal
injectivity as a map of `A`-modules and universal injectivity as a map of `S⁻¹A`-modules are the
same condition.
declarations.statement:
public theorem LinearMap.rTensor_injective_iff_extendScalarsOfIsLocalization
    {A : Type*} [CommRing A] (S : Submonoid A) (Aₛ : Type*) [CommRing Aₛ] [Algebra A Aₛ]
    [IsLocalization S Aₛ] {N N' Q Qₛ : Type*}
    [AddCommGroup N] [Module A N] [Module Aₛ N] [IsScalarTower A Aₛ N]
    [AddCommGroup N'] [Module A N'] [Module Aₛ N'] [IsScalarTower A Aₛ N']
    [AddCommGroup Q] [Module A Q] [AddCommGroup Qₛ] [Module A Qₛ] [Module Aₛ Qₛ]
    [IsScalarTower A Aₛ Qₛ] (q : Q →ₗ[A] Qₛ) [IsLocalizedModule S q] (fₛ : N →ₗ[A] N') :
    Function.Injective (fₛ.rTensor Q) ↔
      Function.Injective ((LinearMap.extendScalarsOfIsLocalization S Aₛ fₛ).rTensor Qₛ)
declarations.comment:
Item (2), for one test module `Q` and one localization `S⁻¹Q` of it; stated for an
`A`-linear map between `S⁻¹A`-modules, of which the source's `B`-linear map between
`(S')⁻¹B`-modules is a case.

declarations.name: Module.mittagLeffler_tensorProduct
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 05CN.** If `R` is a ring and `M`, `N` are Mittag-Leffler modules over `R`, then
`M ⊗_R N` is a Mittag-Leffler module. The Mittag-Leffler condition is spelled out in the
intrinsic form 059E (1): every map `f` from a finitely presented module into the module in
question dominates and is dominated by a map `g` into a finitely presented module, domination
meaning containment of the kernels of the maps `· ⊗ id_T`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem Module.mittagLeffler_tensorProduct {R : Type u} [CommRing R] [Small.{v} R]
    {M N : Type v} [AddCommGroup M] [Module R M] [AddCommGroup N] [Module R N]
    (hM : ∀ (P : Type v) [AddCommGroup P] [Module R P] [Module.FinitePresentation R P]
      (f : P →ₗ[R] M), ∃ (Q : Type v) (_ : AddCommGroup Q) (_ : Module R Q)
        (_ : Module.FinitePresentation R Q) (g : P →ₗ[R] Q), ∀ (T : Type v) [AddCommGroup T]
          [Module R T], LinearMap.ker (f.rTensor T) = LinearMap.ker (g.rTensor T))
    (hN : ∀ (P : Type v) [AddCommGroup P] [Module R P] [Module.FinitePresentation R P]
      (f : P →ₗ[R] N), ∃ (Q : Type v) (_ : AddCommGroup Q) (_ : Module R Q)
        (_ : Module.FinitePresentation R Q) (g : P →ₗ[R] Q), ∀ (T : Type v) [AddCommGroup T]
          [Module R T], LinearMap.ker (f.rTensor T) = LinearMap.ker (g.rTensor T)) :
    ∀ (P : Type v) [AddCommGroup P] [Module R P] [Module.FinitePresentation R P]
      (f : P →ₗ[R] M ⊗[R] N), ∃ (Q : Type v) (_ : AddCommGroup Q) (_ : Module R Q)
        (_ : Module.FinitePresentation R Q) (g : P →ₗ[R] Q), ∀ (T : Type v) [AddCommGroup T]
          [Module R T], LinearMap.ker (f.rTensor T) = LinearMap.ker (g.rTensor T)
declarations.comment: Mittag-Leffler is spelled out inline as condition (1) of 059E.

declarations.name: Module.mittagLeffler_iff_forall_finite_free
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 05CP.** Let `R` be a ring and `M` an `R`-module. Then `M` is Mittag-Leffler if and
only if for every finite free `R`-module `F` and every module map `f : F → M` there are a finitely
presented `R`-module `Q` and a module map `g : F → Q` such that `f` and `g` dominate each other,
that is `Ker(f ⊗ id_N) = Ker(g ⊗ id_N)` for every `R`-module `N`. Being Mittag-Leffler is spelled
out in the intrinsic form 059E (1): the same condition with `F` ranging over all finitely
presented modules.
declarations.statement:
public theorem Module.mittagLeffler_iff_forall_finite_free {R : Type u} [CommRing R] [Small.{v} R]
    {M : Type v} [AddCommGroup M] [Module R M] :
    (∀ (P : Type v) [AddCommGroup P] [Module R P] [Module.FinitePresentation R P]
        (f : P →ₗ[R] M), ∃ (Q : Type v) (_ : AddCommGroup Q) (_ : Module R Q)
          (_ : Module.FinitePresentation R Q) (g : P →ₗ[R] Q), ∀ (N : Type v) [AddCommGroup N]
            [Module R N], LinearMap.ker (f.rTensor N) = LinearMap.ker (g.rTensor N)) ↔
      ∀ (F : Type v) [AddCommGroup F] [Module R F] [Module.Free R F] [Module.Finite R F]
        (f : F →ₗ[R] M), ∃ (Q : Type v) (_ : AddCommGroup Q) (_ : Module R Q)
          (_ : Module.FinitePresentation R Q) (g : F →ₗ[R] Q), ∀ (N : Type v) [AddCommGroup N]
            [Module R N], LinearMap.ker (f.rTensor N) = LinearMap.ker (g.rTensor N)
declarations.comment:
Mittag-Leffler is spelled out inline as condition (1) of 059E; domination as
equality of the kernels of the tensored maps.

declarations.name: Module.mittagLeffler_trans
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 05CQ.** Let `R → S` be a ring map with `S` finitely presented as an `R`-module (for
instance a finite and finitely presented ring map) and let `M` be an `S`-module. If `M` is
Mittag-Leffler over `S` then `M` is Mittag-Leffler over `R`. The Mittag-Leffler condition is
spelled out in the intrinsic form 059E (1): every map `f` from a finitely presented module into
`M` dominates and is dominated by a map `g` into a finitely presented module, domination meaning
containment of the kernels of the maps `· ⊗ id_N`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem Module.mittagLeffler_trans {R : Type u} {S : Type w} {M : Type v} [CommRing R]
    [CommRing S] [Algebra R S] [Small.{v} R] [Module.FinitePresentation R S] [AddCommGroup M]
    [Module R M] [Module S M] [IsScalarTower R S M]
    (hM : ∀ (P : Type v) [AddCommGroup P] [Module S P] [Module.FinitePresentation S P]
      (f : P →ₗ[S] M), ∃ (Q : Type v) (_ : AddCommGroup Q) (_ : Module S Q)
        (_ : Module.FinitePresentation S Q) (g : P →ₗ[S] Q), ∀ (N : Type v) [AddCommGroup N]
          [Module S N], LinearMap.ker (f.rTensor N) = LinearMap.ker (g.rTensor N)) :
    ∀ (P : Type v) [AddCommGroup P] [Module R P] [Module.FinitePresentation R P]
      (f : P →ₗ[R] M), ∃ (Q : Type v) (_ : AddCommGroup Q) (_ : Module R Q)
        (_ : Module.FinitePresentation R Q) (g : P →ₗ[R] Q), ∀ (N : Type v) [AddCommGroup N]
          [Module R N], LinearMap.ker (f.rTensor N) = LinearMap.ker (g.rTensor N)
declarations.comment: Mittag-Leffler is spelled out inline as condition (1) of 059E.

declarations.name: Module.mittagLeffler_restrictScalars_iff_of_surjective
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 05CR.** Let `R` be a ring and let `S = R/I` for a finitely generated ideal `I`,
presented here as an `R`-algebra with surjective structure map which is finitely presented as an
`R`-module. Let `M` be an `S`-module. Then `M` is a Mittag-Leffler module over `R` if and only if
`M` is a Mittag-Leffler module over `S`. The Mittag-Leffler condition is spelled out in the
intrinsic form 059E (1): every map `f` from a finitely presented module into `M` dominates and is
dominated by a map `g` into a finitely presented module, domination meaning equality of the kernels
of the maps `· ⊗ id_N`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem Module.mittagLeffler_restrictScalars_iff_of_surjective {R : Type u} {S : Type w}
    {M : Type v} [CommRing R] [CommRing S] [Algebra R S] [Small.{v} R]
    [Module.FinitePresentation R S] [AddCommGroup M] [Module R M] [Module S M]
    [IsScalarTower R S M] (hRS : Function.Surjective (algebraMap R S)) :
    (∀ (P : Type v) [AddCommGroup P] [Module R P] [Module.FinitePresentation R P]
      (f : P →ₗ[R] M), ∃ (Q : Type v) (_ : AddCommGroup Q) (_ : Module R Q)
        (_ : Module.FinitePresentation R Q) (g : P →ₗ[R] Q), ∀ (N : Type v) [AddCommGroup N]
          [Module R N], LinearMap.ker (f.rTensor N) = LinearMap.ker (g.rTensor N)) ↔
      ∀ (P : Type v) [AddCommGroup P] [Module S P] [Module.FinitePresentation S P]
        (f : P →ₗ[S] M), ∃ (Q : Type v) (_ : AddCommGroup Q) (_ : Module S Q)
          (_ : Module.FinitePresentation S Q) (g : P →ₗ[S] Q), ∀ (N : Type v) [AddCommGroup N]
            [Module S N], LinearMap.ker (f.rTensor N) = LinearMap.ker (g.rTensor N)
declarations.comment:
Mittag-Leffler is spelled out inline as condition (1) of 059E; `S = R/I` with `I`
finitely generated is spelled abstractly as a surjective `algebraMap R S` with `S` finitely
presented as an `R`-module.

declarations.name: Module.mittagLeffler_trans_of_flat
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 05CT.** Let `R → S` be a ring map and let `M` be an `S`-module. If `S` is
Mittag-Leffler as an `R`-module, and `M` is flat and Mittag-Leffler as an `S`-module, then `M` is
Mittag-Leffler as an `R`-module. Being Mittag-Leffler is spelled out in the intrinsic form
059E (1): every map `f : P → M` from a finitely presented module dominates and is dominated by a
map `g : P → Q` into a finitely presented module, domination meaning
`Ker(f ⊗ id_N) = Ker(g ⊗ id_N)` for every test module `N`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem Module.mittagLeffler_trans_of_flat {R : Type u} {S M : Type v} [CommRing R]
    [CommRing S] [Algebra R S] [Small.{v} R] [AddCommGroup M] [Module R M] [Module S M]
    [IsScalarTower R S M] [Module.Flat S M]
    (hS : ∀ (P : Type v) [AddCommGroup P] [Module R P] [Module.FinitePresentation R P]
      (f : P →ₗ[R] S), ∃ (Q : Type v) (_ : AddCommGroup Q) (_ : Module R Q)
        (_ : Module.FinitePresentation R Q) (g : P →ₗ[R] Q), ∀ (N : Type v) [AddCommGroup N]
          [Module R N], LinearMap.ker (f.rTensor N) = LinearMap.ker (g.rTensor N))
    (hM : ∀ (P : Type v) [AddCommGroup P] [Module S P] [Module.FinitePresentation S P]
      (f : P →ₗ[S] M), ∃ (Q : Type v) (_ : AddCommGroup Q) (_ : Module S Q)
        (_ : Module.FinitePresentation S Q) (g : P →ₗ[S] Q), ∀ (N : Type v) [AddCommGroup N]
          [Module S N], LinearMap.ker (f.rTensor N) = LinearMap.ker (g.rTensor N)) :
    ∀ (P : Type v) [AddCommGroup P] [Module R P] [Module.FinitePresentation R P]
      (f : P →ₗ[R] M), ∃ (Q : Type v) (_ : AddCommGroup Q) (_ : Module R Q)
        (_ : Module.FinitePresentation R Q) (g : P →ₗ[R] Q), ∀ (N : Type v) [AddCommGroup N]
          [Module R N], LinearMap.ker (f.rTensor N) = LinearMap.ker (g.rTensor N)
declarations.comment:
Mittag-Leffler is spelled out inline as condition (1) of 059E, as in 059M, 059N,
059P and 05CQ; flatness is `Module.Flat S M`. `S` and `M` share the universe of the test data,
whence the single `Small.{v} R`. See the module docstring.

declarations.name: Module.IsCoherent
declarations.doc:
An `R`-module `M` is *coherent* if it is finitely generated and every
finitely generated submodule of `M` is finitely presented over `R`.
declarations.statement:
class Module.IsCoherent (R : Type*) (M : Type*) [Ring R] [AddCommGroup M] [Module R M] :
    Prop
declarations.comment: (1) coherent module: finite, every f.g. submodule finitely presented

declarations.name: IsCoherentRing
declarations.doc: A ring `R` is a *coherent ring* if it is coherent as a module over itself.
declarations.statement: class IsCoherentRing (R : Type*) [Ring R] : Prop
declarations.comment: (2) coherent ring: coherent as a module over itself

declarations.name: isCoherent_of_fg_submodule
declarations.doc: A finitely generated submodule of a coherent module is coherent.
declarations.statement:
theorem isCoherent_of_fg_submodule
    {R M : Type*} [Ring R] [AddCommGroup M] [Module R M] [Module.IsCoherent R M]
    (N : Submodule R M) (hN : N.FG) :
    Module.IsCoherent R N

declarations.name: finite_ker_and_coherent_range_coker
declarations.doc:
If `φ : N → M` with `N` finite and `M` coherent, then the kernel of
`φ` is finite, the range of `φ` is coherent, and the cokernel `M ⧸ range φ` is
coherent.
declarations.statement:
theorem finite_ker_and_coherent_range_coker
    {R N M : Type*} [Ring R] [AddCommGroup N] [Module R N]
    [AddCommGroup M] [Module R M] [Module.Finite R N] [Module.IsCoherent R M]
    (φ : N →ₗ[R] M) :
    Module.Finite R (LinearMap.ker φ) ∧
      Module.IsCoherent R (LinearMap.range φ) ∧
      Module.IsCoherent R (M ⧸ LinearMap.range φ)

declarations.name: coherent_ker_and_coker_of_coherent
declarations.doc:
If `φ : N → M` is a homomorphism of coherent modules, then its kernel
and cokernel are coherent.
declarations.statement:
theorem coherent_ker_and_coker_of_coherent
    {R N M : Type*} [Ring R] [AddCommGroup N] [Module R N]
    [AddCommGroup M] [Module R M] [Module.IsCoherent R N] [Module.IsCoherent R M]
    (φ : N →ₗ[R] M) :
    Module.IsCoherent R (LinearMap.ker φ) ∧
      Module.IsCoherent R (M ⧸ LinearMap.range φ)

declarations.name: isCoherent_two_out_of_three
declarations.doc:
Two-out-of-three for coherence in a short exact sequence `0 → M₁ → M₂ → M₃ → 0`, where `i` is
injective, `p` is surjective and `range i = ker p`: any two of `M₁`, `M₂`, `M₃` coherent imply
the third is coherent.
declarations.statement:
theorem isCoherent_two_out_of_three
    {R M₁ M₂ M₃ : Type*} [Ring R]
    [AddCommGroup M₁] [Module R M₁] [AddCommGroup M₂] [Module R M₂]
    [AddCommGroup M₃] [Module R M₃]
    (i : M₁ →ₗ[R] M₂) (p : M₂ →ₗ[R] M₃)
    (hi : Function.Injective i) (hp : Function.Surjective p)
    (hexact : LinearMap.range i = LinearMap.ker p) :
    (Module.IsCoherent R M₁ → Module.IsCoherent R M₂ → Module.IsCoherent R M₃) ∧
    (Module.IsCoherent R M₁ → Module.IsCoherent R M₃ → Module.IsCoherent R M₂) ∧
    (Module.IsCoherent R M₂ → Module.IsCoherent R M₃ → Module.IsCoherent R M₁)

declarations.name: coherent_iff_finitePresentation_of_coherentRing
declarations.doc:
If `R` is a coherent ring, then an `R`-module `M` is coherent if and only if
it is finitely presented.
declarations.statement:
theorem coherent_iff_finitePresentation_of_coherentRing
    (hR : Module.IsCoherent R R)
    (M : Type*) [AddCommGroup M] [Module R M] :
    Module.IsCoherent R M ↔ Module.FinitePresentation R M

declarations.name: isCoherentRing_of_isNoetherianRing
declarations.doc: Every left Noetherian ring is a coherent ring.
declarations.statement:
theorem isCoherentRing_of_isNoetherianRing (R : Type*) [Ring R] [IsNoetherianRing R] :
    IsCoherentRing R

declarations.name: IsCoherentRing.tfae_flat_pi
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 05CZ** (Chase's theorem). Let `R` be a commutative ring. The following are
equivalent: (1) `R` is coherent; (2) any product of flat `R`-modules is flat; (3) for every set
`A` the module `R^A` is flat.
declarations.statement:
theorem IsCoherentRing.tfae_flat_pi (R : Type u) [CommRing R] :
    List.TFAE
      [IsCoherentRing R,
        ∀ (A : Type u) (Q : A → Type u) [∀ α, AddCommGroup (Q α)] [∀ α, Module R (Q α)],
          (∀ α, Module.Flat R (Q α)) → Module.Flat R (∀ α, Q α),
        ∀ A : Type u, Module.Flat R (A → R)]
declarations.comment: Test data in the universe of `R`. See the module docstring.

declarations.name: Module.flat_and_mittagLeffler_pi
declarations.doc:
Let `R` be a Noetherian ring and `A` a set. Then `M = R^A`, the `R`-module of functions
`A → R`, is a flat and Mittag-Leffler `R`-module.

Being Mittag-Leffler is spelled out inline as condition (1) of Proposition 059E: every map
`f : P → M` from a finitely presented `R`-module dominates and is dominated by a map `g : P → Q`
into a finitely presented `R`-module, that is `Ker(f ⊗ id_N) = Ker(g ⊗ id_N)` for every
`R`-module `N`.
declarations.statement:
theorem Module.flat_and_mittagLeffler_pi (R : Type u) [CommRing R] [IsNoetherianRing R]
    (A : Type u) :
    Module.Flat R (A → R) ∧
      ∀ (P : Type u) [AddCommGroup P] [Module R P] [Module.FinitePresentation R P]
        (f : P →ₗ[R] (A → R)), ∃ (Q : Type u) (_ : AddCommGroup Q) (_ : Module R Q)
          (_ : Module.FinitePresentation R Q) (g : P →ₗ[R] Q), ∀ (N : Type u) [AddCommGroup N]
            [Module R N], LinearMap.ker (f.rTensor N) = LinearMap.ker (g.rTensor N)
declarations.comment:
Mittag-Leffler is spelled out inline as condition (1) of 059E, as in 059M, 059S and
0AS6; `R^A` is the `Pi` module `A → R`, as in item (3) of 05CZ, and the two conclusions are one
conjunction, as in the source. Test data in the universe of `R` and `A`. See the module
docstring.

declarations.name: Module.exists_end_factorization_finitePresentation_of_countable_span_of_mittagLeffler
declarations.doc:
Let `R` be a commutative ring and let `M` be an `R`-module which is countably generated — it
admits a countable spanning set — and Mittag-Leffler, the latter in the intrinsic form 059E (1):
every map `f : P → M` from a finitely presented module dominates and is dominated by a map
`g : P → Q` into a finitely presented module, domination meaning `Ker (f ⊗ id_T) = Ker (g ⊗ id_T)`
for every `R`-module `T`. Then for every `R`-module map `f : P → M` with `P` finitely generated
there is an endomorphism `α : M → M` such that (1) `α` factors through a finitely presented
`R`-module, that is `α = v ∘ₗ u` for some `u : M → Q` and `v : Q → M` with `Q` finitely presented,
and (2) `α ∘ f = f`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem Module.exists_end_factorization_finitePresentation_of_countable_span_of_mittagLeffler
    (R : Type u) [CommRing R] [Small.{v} R] (M : Type v) [AddCommGroup M] [Module R M]
    (hcg : ∃ s : Set M, s.Countable ∧ Submodule.span R s = ⊤)
    (hML : ∀ (P : Type v) [AddCommGroup P] [Module R P] [Module.FinitePresentation R P]
      (f : P →ₗ[R] M), ∃ (Q : Type v) (_ : AddCommGroup Q) (_ : Module R Q)
        (_ : Module.FinitePresentation R Q) (g : P →ₗ[R] Q), ∀ (T : Type v) [AddCommGroup T]
          [Module R T], LinearMap.ker (f.rTensor T) = LinearMap.ker (g.rTensor T))
    {P : Type w} [AddCommGroup P] [Module R P] [Module.Finite R P] (f : P →ₗ[R] M) :
    ∃ α : M →ₗ[R] M,
      (∃ (Q : Type v) (_ : AddCommGroup Q) (_ : Module R Q) (_ : Module.FinitePresentation R Q)
        (u : M →ₗ[R] Q) (v : Q →ₗ[R] M), α = v ∘ₗ u) ∧ α ∘ₗ f = f
declarations.comment:
Mittag-Leffler is spelled out inline as condition (1) of 059E, as in 059M, 059N,
059P, 059R, 05CQ, 059X and 05D6; countable generation as a countable spanning set, as in 0590.
Test data in the universe of `M`, whence `Small.{v} R`; the source's `P` keeps its own universe.
Factoring through a finitely presented module is the equation `α = v ∘ₗ u`, as in
`Module.Flat.exists_factorization_of_finitePresentation`. See the module docstring.

declarations.name: AdicCompletion.map_splitExact_of_projective_quotient_smul_top
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 05D3.** Let `R` be a ring, let `I ⊆ R` be an ideal and let `0 → K → P → M → 0` be a
short exact sequence of `R`-modules, given by `f : K →ₗ[R] P` injective, `g : P →ₗ[R] M`
surjective and `Function.Exact f g`. If `M` is flat over `R` and `M/IM` is a projective
`R ⧸ I`-module, then the sequence of `I`-adic completions `0 → K^∧ → P^∧ → M^∧ → 0` is split
exact: `map I f` is injective, `map I f` and `map I g` are exact, and `map I g` has an
`R^∧`-linear right inverse.
declarations.statement:
public theorem map_splitExact_of_projective_quotient_smul_top {R : Type u} [CommRing R]
    (I : Ideal R) {K : Type v} {P : Type w} {M : Type t} [AddCommGroup K] [Module R K]
    [AddCommGroup P] [Module R P] [AddCommGroup M] [Module R M] [Module.Flat R M]
    {f : K →ₗ[R] P} {g : P →ₗ[R] M} (hf : Function.Injective f) (hfg : Function.Exact f g)
    (hg : Function.Surjective g)
    (hM : Module.Projective (R ⧸ I) (M ⧸ I • (⊤ : Submodule R M))) :
    Function.Injective (map I f) ∧ Function.Exact (map I f) (map I g) ∧
      ∃ s : AdicCompletion I M →ₗ[AdicCompletion I R] AdicCompletion I P,
        map I g ∘ₗ s = LinearMap.id

declarations.name: conormal_finite_projective
declarations.doc:
Part (1) of Stacks tag 05D5: the conormal module is finite locally free.
If `S` is a smooth `R`-algebra and `σ : S →ₐ[R] R`, then the conormal module `I/I²` of
`I = Ker(σ)` is a finitely generated projective `R`-module.
declarations.statement:
theorem conormal_finite_projective (h : Algebra.Smooth R S) :
    Module.Finite R (RingHom.ker σ).Cotangent ∧
      Module.Projective R (RingHom.ker σ).Cotangent

declarations.name: adicCompletion_algEquiv_mvPowerSeries
declarations.doc:
Part (2) of Stacks tag 05D5: the completion is a power series ring when the conormal
module is free. If `S` is a smooth `R`-algebra, `σ : S →ₐ[R] R`, and the conormal module `I/I²` of
`I = Ker(σ)` is free (necessarily of finite rank `d := Module.finrank R (I/I²)` by (1)),
then the `I`-adic completion `S^∧` is isomorphic, as an `R`-algebra, to the formal power
series `R`-algebra in `d` variables `R[[t_1, …, t_d]]`.
declarations.statement:
theorem adicCompletion_algEquiv_mvPowerSeries (h : Algebra.Smooth R S)
    (hfree : Module.Free R (RingHom.ker σ).Cotangent) :
    Nonempty (AdicCompletion (RingHom.ker σ) S ≃ₐ[R]
      MvPowerSeries (Fin (Module.finrank R (RingHom.ker σ).Cotangent)) R)

declarations.name: Module.exists_sSupIndep_finitePresentation_of_countable_span_of_mittagLeffler
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 05D6.** Let `R` be a henselian local ring and let `M` be an `R`-module which is
countably generated — it admits a countable spanning set — and Mittag-Leffler, the latter in the
intrinsic form 059E (1): every map `f : P → M` from a finitely presented module dominates and is
dominated by a map `g : P → Q` into a finitely presented module, domination meaning
`Ker(f ⊗ id_T) = Ker(g ⊗ id_T)` for every `R`-module `T`. Then `M` is a direct sum of finitely
presented `R`-modules, in the internal form: there is an independent set of finitely presented
submodules of `M` whose supremum is `⊤`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem Module.exists_sSupIndep_finitePresentation_of_countable_span_of_mittagLeffler
    (R : Type u) [CommRing R] [HenselianLocalRing R] [Small.{v} R]
    (M : Type v) [AddCommGroup M] [Module R M]
    (hcg : ∃ s : Set M, s.Countable ∧ Submodule.span R s = ⊤)
    (hML : ∀ (P : Type v) [AddCommGroup P] [Module R P] [Module.FinitePresentation R P]
      (f : P →ₗ[R] M), ∃ (Q : Type v) (_ : AddCommGroup Q) (_ : Module R Q)
        (_ : Module.FinitePresentation R Q) (g : P →ₗ[R] Q), ∀ (T : Type v) [AddCommGroup T]
          [Module R T], LinearMap.ker (f.rTensor T) = LinearMap.ker (g.rTensor T)) :
    ∃ S : Set (Submodule R M), sSupIndep S ∧ sSup S = ⊤ ∧
      ∀ N ∈ S, Module.FinitePresentation R N
declarations.comment:
Mittag-Leffler is spelled out inline as condition (1) of 059E, as in 059M, 059N,
059P, 059R, 05CQ and 0AS7; countable generation as a countable spanning set, as in 0590; and the
direct sum decomposition internally, as an independent set of submodules of `M` with supremum `⊤`,
as in 058W. Test data in the universe of `M`, whence `Small.{v} R`. See the module docstring.

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.RingedSite.oneIsNeverZero
declarations.doc:
The canonical morphism from the empty sheaf to the equalizer of the zero and one sections
of the structure sheaf.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def oneIsNeverZero (X : RingedSite.{u, v, w}) :
    ⊥_ (Sheaf X.J (Type w)) ⟶ equalizer (zeroSection X) (oneSection X)

declarations.name: Stacks.Sheaves.LocallyRingedSite.oneIsNeverZero
declarations.doc:
The canonical morphism of sheaves of sets

  `∅^# ⟶ Equalizer(0, 1 : * ⟶ O)`

from the initial sheaf to the equalizer of the zero and one sections of the structure sheaf.
The first condition in the definition of a locally ringed site (Tag 04EU) is that it be an
isomorphism.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def oneIsNeverZero (O : Sheaf J CommRingCat.{w}) :
    ⊥_ (Sheaf J (Type w)) ⟶ equalizer (zeroSection J O) (oneSection J O)
declarations.comment: the displayed morphism from the empty sheaf to the equalizer of 0 and 1

declarations.name: Stacks.Sheaves.LocallyRingedSite.isIso_oneIsNeverZero_iff
declarations.doc:
The canonical morphism `∅^# ⟶ Equalizer(0, 1)` is an isomorphism exactly when, for every
object `U` that is not sheaf-theoretically empty, the sections `0` and `1` of `O(U)` are
distinct.
declarations.statement:
theorem isIso_oneIsNeverZero_iff (O : Sheaf J CommRingCat.{w}) :
    IsIso (oneIsNeverZero J O) ↔
      ∀ U : C, (⊥ : Sieve U) ∉ J U → (0 : O.obj.obj (op U)) ≠ 1
declarations.comment:
the equivalent sections-level form: 0 ≠ 1 over every object the empty sieve
  does not cover

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.RingedSite.nontrivial_stalk_of_isIso_oneIsNeverZero
declarations.doc:
If zero and one are nowhere equal, then the stalk of the structure sheaf at every point is a
nonzero ring.
declarations.statement:
lemma nontrivial_stalk_of_isIso_oneIsNeverZero (X : RingedSite.{v, u, u})
    [IsIso (oneIsNeverZero X)] (p : X.J.Point.{u}) :
    Nontrivial ((p.presheafFiber (A := CommRingCat.{u})).obj X.O.obj)
declarations.comment: the implication (1) ⇒ (2)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.RingedSite.isIso_oneIsNeverZero_iff_forall_nontrivial_stalk
declarations.doc:
On a site with a conservative family of points, zero and one are nowhere equal if and only if
every stalk of the structure sheaf is a nonzero ring.
declarations.statement:
lemma isIso_oneIsNeverZero_iff_forall_nontrivial_stalk (X : RingedSite.{v, u, u})
    (hX : X.J.HasConservativeFamily.{u}) :
    IsIso (oneIsNeverZero X) ↔
      ∀ p : X.J.Point.{u}, Nontrivial ((p.presheafFiber (A := CommRingCat.{u})).obj X.O.obj)
declarations.comment: the equivalence (1) ⇔ (2) when the site has enough points

declarations.name: Stacks.Sheaves.LocallyRingedSite.nontrivial_stalkRingObj
declarations.doc:
If the morphism of Tag 05D7 is an isomorphism then for every point `p` of the site the stalk
`O_p` is not the zero ring.
declarations.statement:
theorem nontrivial_stalkRingObj (h : IsIso (oneIsNeverZero X.J X.O))
    (p : Stacks.Sheaves.LocallyRingedTopos.Point X) : Nontrivial p.stalkRingObj
declarations.comment:
(1) implies (2): if the morphism of 05D7 is an isomorphism then no stalk of
  the structure sheaf is the zero ring

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.exists_affineOpens_free_conormal_powerSeries
declarations.doc:
At a smooth point of a section, there are compatible affine open neighbourhoods on which the
conormal module is free and the completion is a formal power series algebra over the base.
declarations.statement:
public theorem exists_affineOpens_free_conormal_powerSeries
    {X S : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ S) (σ : S ⟶ X)
    (hσ : σ ≫ f = 𝟙 S) (s : S)
    (hsmooth : InfinitesimalLifting.SmoothAt f (σ s)) :
    ∃ (U : S.Opens) (V : X.Opens) (_ : IsAffineOpen U)
      (_ : IsAffineOpen V) (_ : s ∈ U) (_ : σ s ∈ V)
      (hVU : V ≤ f ⁻¹ᵁ U) (hUV : U ≤ σ ⁻¹ᵁ V),
      let A := Γ(S, U)
      let B := Γ(X, V)
      letI : Algebra A B := (f.appLE U V hVU).hom.toAlgebra
      ∃ (sectionHom : B →ₐ[A] A),
        sectionHom.toRingHom = (σ.appLE V U hUV).hom ∧
        (letI : Algebra B A := sectionHom.toAlgebra
         Module.Free A (RingHom.ker sectionHom.toRingHom).Cotangent) ∧
        (letI : Algebra B A := sectionHom.toAlgebra
         Nonempty (AdicCompletion (RingHom.ker sectionHom.toRingHom) B ≃ₐ[A]
           MvPowerSeries (Fin (Module.finrank A
             (RingHom.ker sectionHom.toRingHom).Cotangent)) A))

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.relativeAssassin_subset_associatedPoints_tensor_pullback
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 05DB, inclusion.** The associated points of the tensor
product with a pulled-back module contain the images of the associated points
of `F` on scheme-theoretic fibres over associated points of `G`.
declarations.statement:
theorem relativeAssassin_subset_associatedPoints_tensor_pullback
    {X S : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ S) (F : X.Modules) (G : S.Modules)
    [F.IsQuasicoherent] [G.IsQuasicoherent]
    (hF : IsFlatOver f.toLRSHom.toShHom F) :
    (⋃ s ∈ Stacks.Divisors.associatedPoints G,
      f.fiberι s ''
        Stacks.Divisors.associatedPoints
          ((Scheme.Modules.pullback (f.fiberι s)).obj F)) ⊆
    Stacks.Divisors.associatedPoints
        ((((Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.sheafTensor
          ⟨((X.toLocallyRingedSpace.toRingedSpace)).presheaf,
            ((X.toLocallyRingedSpace.toRingedSpace)).IsSheaf⟩).obj (F)).obj
              (((Scheme.Modules.pullback f).obj G))))
declarations.comment: the inclusion

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.associatedPoints_tensor_pullback_eq_relativeAssassin
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 05DB, equality.** Over a locally Noetherian base, the
associated points of the tensor product are exactly the images of the
associated points of `F` on fibres over associated points of `G`.
declarations.statement:
theorem associatedPoints_tensor_pullback_eq_relativeAssassin
    {X S : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ S) (F : X.Modules) (G : S.Modules)
    [F.IsQuasicoherent] [G.IsQuasicoherent]
    (hF : IsFlatOver f.toLRSHom.toShHom F)
    [IsLocallyNoetherian S] :
    Stacks.Divisors.associatedPoints
        ((((Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.sheafTensor
          ⟨((X.toLocallyRingedSpace.toRingedSpace)).presheaf,
            ((X.toLocallyRingedSpace.toRingedSpace)).IsSheaf⟩).obj (F)).obj
              (((Scheme.Modules.pullback f).obj G)))) =
      ⋃ s ∈ Stacks.Divisors.associatedPoints G,
        f.fiberι s ''
          Stacks.Divisors.associatedPoints
            ((Scheme.Modules.pullback (f.fiberι s)).obj F)
declarations.comment: equality for a locally Noetherian base

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.mem_relativeAssassin_pullback_iff
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 05DC.** Under arbitrary base change, a point is in
the relative assassin of the pulled-back quasi-coherent module exactly when
its image is in the original relative assassin and its residue-field tensor
product point is generic in an irreducible component.
declarations.statement:
theorem mem_relativeAssassin_pullback_iff
    {X S S' : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ S) (g : S' ⟶ S) (F : X.Modules)
    [F.IsQuasicoherent] [LocallyOfFiniteType f]
    (x' : pullback (C := Scheme.{u}) f g) :
    x' ∈ Stacks.Divisors.relativeAssassin (pullback.snd (C := Scheme.{u}) f g)
        ((Scheme.Modules.pullback (pullback.fst (C := Scheme.{u}) f g)).obj F) ↔
      (pullback.fst (C := Scheme.{u}) f g x' ∈ Stacks.Divisors.relativeAssassin f F ∧
        ∃ Z ∈ irreducibleComponents
            (Spec (Scheme.Pullback.Triplet.ofPoint x').tensor),
          IsGenericPoint (Scheme.Pullback.SpecOfPoint x') Z)

declarations.name: Stacks.UniversalInjectivity.finite_maximalSpectrum_localization_nonZeroSMulDivisors
declarations.doc:
Localizing at the elements regular on a finite module over the Noetherian closed fibre of a
local base produces a semilocal ring.
declarations.statement: theorem finite_maximalSpectrum_localization_nonZeroSMulDivisors : Finite (MaximalSpectrum T)
declarations.comment: semilocality; the multiplicative subset is `nonZeroSMulDivisors`

declarations.name: Stacks.UniversalInjectivity.range_under_localization_nonZeroSMulDivisors
declarations.doc:
The contractions of the primes of the localization are exactly the primes of `S` contained
in an associated prime of the closed-fibre module.
declarations.statement:
theorem range_under_localization_nonZeroSMulDivisors :
    Set.range (fun q : PrimeSpectrum T ↦ q.asIdeal.under S) =
      {q : Ideal S | q.IsPrime ∧
        ∃ p ∈ assStacks S
          (N ⧸ (Ideal.map (algebraMap R S) (maximalIdeal R) • (⊤ : Submodule S N))), q ≤ p}
declarations.comment: the prime spectrum

declarations.name: Stacks.UniversalInjectivity.exists_assStacks_closedFibre_of_isMaximal_localization
declarations.doc:
Every maximal ideal of the localization corresponds to an associated prime of the
closed-fibre module over the closed-fibre ring, whose contraction to `S` is the maximal ideal's.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_assStacks_closedFibre_of_isMaximal_localization (q : MaximalSpectrum T) :
    ∃ p ∈ assStacks (S ⧸ Ideal.map (algebraMap R S) (maximalIdeal R))
      (N ⧸ (Ideal.map (algebraMap R S) (maximalIdeal R) • (⊤ : Submodule S N))),
      p.comap (Ideal.Quotient.mk (Ideal.map (algebraMap R S) (maximalIdeal R))) =
        q.asIdeal.under S
declarations.comment: the maximal ideals

declarations.name: Stacks.UniversalInjectivity.universallyInjectivePoly_lsmul_of_nonZeroSMulDivisors
declarations.doc:
Every element acting injectively on the closed fibre defines a universally injective
`R`-linear homothety of `N`.
declarations.statement:
lemma universallyInjectivePoly_lsmul_of_nonZeroSMulDivisors
    (hS : (algebraMap R S).EssentiallyOfFinitePresentation)
    (s : nonZeroSMulDivisors S
      (N ⧸ (Ideal.map (algebraMap R S) (maximalIdeal R) • (⊤ : Submodule S N)))) :
    UniversallyInjectivePoly (((LinearMap.lsmul S N) s.1).restrictScalars R)
declarations.comment: the homotheties

declarations.name: Stacks.UniversalInjectivity.universallyInjectivePoly_mkLinearMap_nonZeroSMulDivisors
declarations.doc:
The canonical map from `N` to its localization at the elements acting injectively on the
closed fibre is universally injective over `R`.
declarations.statement:
lemma universallyInjectivePoly_mkLinearMap_nonZeroSMulDivisors
    (hS : (algebraMap R S).EssentiallyOfFinitePresentation) :
    UniversallyInjectivePoly
      ((LocalizedModule.mkLinearMap
        (nonZeroSMulDivisors S
          (N ⧸ (Ideal.map (algebraMap R S) (maximalIdeal R) •
            (⊤ : Submodule S N)))) N).restrictScalars R)
declarations.comment: the localization map

declarations.name: Stacks.UniversalInjectivity.universallyInjectivePoly_tensorUnit_of_flat
declarations.doc:
Let `R → S` be a local homomorphism of local rings, essentially of finite presentation, let
`N` be a finitely presented `S`-module which is flat over `R`, and let `S → S'` be flat. If the
image of `Spec(S') → Spec(S)` contains every prime of `S` lying over the maximal ideal of `R`
which is an associated prime of the closed fibre `N / 𝔪_R N`, then the canonical map
`N → N ⊗[S] S'` is universally injective over `R`.
declarations.statement:
theorem universallyInjectivePoly_tensorUnit_of_flat {R : Type u} {S : Type v} {S' : Type w}
    {N : Type x} [CommRing R] [CommRing S] [CommRing S'] [IsLocalRing R] [IsLocalRing S]
    [Algebra R S] [IsLocalHom (algebraMap R S)] [Algebra S S']
    [AddCommGroup N] [Module S N] [Module R N] [IsScalarTower R S N]
    [Module.FinitePresentation S N] [Module.Flat R N] [Module.Flat S S']
    (hS : (algebraMap R S).EssentiallyOfFinitePresentation)
    (hspec : ∀ q : Ideal S, Ideal.comap (algebraMap R S) q = maximalIdeal R →
      IsAssociatedPrimeStacks S
        (N ⧸ (Ideal.map (algebraMap R S) (maximalIdeal R) • (⊤ : Submodule S N))) q →
      ∃ q' : Ideal S', q'.IsPrime ∧ Ideal.comap (algebraMap S S') q' = q) :
    UniversallyInjectivePoly (((TensorProduct.mk S N S').flip 1).restrictScalars R)

declarations.name: Stacks.UniversalInjectivity.universallyInjective_baseChange_of_flat
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 05DH.** Under the stated finite-presentation and flatness hypotheses, if every
associated prime of each fibre of `N` lifts to `S'`, then the canonical base-change map
`N → N ⊗[S] S'` is universally injective over `R`.
declarations.statement:
theorem universallyInjective_baseChange_of_flat
    {R : Type u} {S : Type v} {S' N : Type w}
    [CommRing R] [CommRing S] [CommRing S']
    [AddCommGroup N] [Module S N] [Algebra R S] [Algebra S S']
    [Module R N] [IsScalarTower R S N] [Algebra R S'] [IsScalarTower R S S']
    [Algebra.FinitePresentation R S] [Module.FinitePresentation S N]
    [Module.Flat R N] [Module.Flat S S']
    (himage : ∀ (q : Ideal S) [q.IsPrime],
      IsAssociatedPrimeStacks S (N ⊗[R] (q.under R).ResidueField) q →
        ∃ q' : Ideal S', q'.IsPrime ∧ q'.under S = q) :
    UniversallyInjective
      (((TensorProduct.mk S N S').flip 1).restrictScalars R)

declarations.name: AdicCompletion.isMittagLeffler_finsupp
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 05DJ.** If `R` is Noetherian and `I`-adically complete, then the
`I`-adic completion of the direct sum of an `A`-indexed family of copies of `R` is a
Mittag-Leffler `R`-module.
declarations.statement:
theorem isMittagLeffler_finsupp {R : Type uR} [CommRing R] (I : Ideal R) [IsNoetherianRing R]
    [IsAdicComplete I R] (A : Type uA) :
    IsMittagLeffler.{uR, uP, max uR uA, max uR uP, uN} R (AdicCompletion I (A →₀ R))
declarations.comment:
the Mittag-Leffler property; the direct sum `⊕_{α ∈ A} R` is spelled `A →₀ R`.
Mittag-Leffler is `IsMittagLeffler`, condition (1) of 059E, as in 059N and 059X.

registrations.name: AdicCompletion.flat_directSum
registrations.comment:
flatness; neither `IsAdicComplete` nor the shape of the direct sum is needed,
so the library statement is the more general Tag 06LE

declarations.name: AdicCompletion.flat_of_projective_quotient_smul_top
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 05DK.** If `R` is Noetherian, `M` is flat and `M/IM` is projective over
`R/I`, then the `I`-adic completion of `M` is flat over `R`. The source's hypothesis that `R` be
`I`-adically complete is not needed for this half.
declarations.statement:
theorem flat_of_projective_quotient_smul_top [IsNoetherianRing R]
    [Module.Flat R M] (hM : Module.Projective (R ⧸ I) (M ⧸ I • (⊤ : Submodule R M))) :
    Module.Flat R (AdicCompletion I M)
declarations.comment:
flatness; `M/IM` is `M ⧸ I • ⊤`. The source's hypothesis that `R` be `I`-adically
complete is dropped: it is unused, neither Tag 05D3 nor Tag 06LE needing it, so this is strictly
more general than the source's statement.

declarations.name: AdicCompletion.isMittagLeffler_of_projective_quotient_smul_top
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 05DK.** If `R` is Noetherian and `I`-adically complete, `M` is flat and
`M/IM` is projective over `R/I`, then the `I`-adic completion of `M` is a Mittag-Leffler
`R`-module.
declarations.statement:
theorem isMittagLeffler_of_projective_quotient_smul_top [IsNoetherianRing R] [IsAdicComplete I R]
    [Module.Flat R M] (hM : Module.Projective (R ⧸ I) (M ⧸ I • (⊤ : Submodule R M))) :
    IsMittagLeffler.{u, uP, v, max u uP, uN} R (AdicCompletion I M)
declarations.comment:
the Mittag-Leffler property; `M/IM` is `M ⧸ I • ⊤`, and Mittag-Leffler is
`IsMittagLeffler`, condition (1) of 059E, as in 059N and 05DJ.

declarations.name: AdicCompletion.universallyInjective_of_associatedPrimes
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 05DL.** Let `R → S` be a map of Noetherian rings, let `I ⊆ R` be an
ideal and let `N` be a finite `S`-module. If for every finite `R`-module `Q` and every associated
prime `q` of `N ⊗[R] Q` the ideal `IS + q` is proper, then the canonical map from `N` to its
`I`-adic completion is universally injective as a map of `R`-modules.
declarations.statement:
theorem universallyInjective_of_associatedPrimes {R : Type u} [CommRing R] (I : Ideal R)
    {S : Type v} [CommRing S] [Algebra R S] {N : Type w} [AddCommGroup N] [Module R N]
    [Module S N] [IsScalarTower R S N] [IsNoetherianRing S] [Module.Finite S N]
    (h : ∀ (Q : Type w) [AddCommGroup Q] [Module R Q] [Module.Finite R Q] (q : Ideal S),
      IsAssociatedPrimeStacks S (N ⊗[R] Q) q → I.map (algebraMap R S) ⊔ q ≠ ⊤) :
    UniversallyInjective (AdicCompletion.of I N)
declarations.comment:
`IS` is `I.map (algebraMap R S)` and `IS + 𝔮` is a supremum of ideals; associatedness
is `IsAssociatedPrimeStacks`, the source's definition; the tensor product is written `N ⊗[R] Q`,
with `N` on the left, so that it carries its standard `S`-module structure. The source's
hypothesis that `R` be Noetherian is dropped: the argument runs entirely over `S`, using Tag 00IQ
and Tag 0311 there, so this is strictly more general than the source's statement.

declarations.name: AdicCompletion.universallyInjective_of_flat_of_fibre_associatedPrimes
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 05DM.** Let `R → S` be a map of Noetherian rings, let `I ⊆ R` be an
ideal and let `N` be a finite `S`-module which is flat over `R`. If for every prime `𝔮` of `S`
which is an associated prime of the fibre `N ⊗[R] κ(𝔭)`, where `𝔭 = R ∩ 𝔮`, the ideal `IS + 𝔮` is
proper, then the canonical map from `N` to its `I`-adic completion is universally injective as a
map of `R`-modules.
declarations.statement:
theorem universallyInjective_of_flat_of_fibre_associatedPrimes {R : Type u} {S : Type v}
    [CommRing R] [CommRing S] [Algebra R S] (I : Ideal R) (N : Type w) [AddCommGroup N]
    [Module S N] [Module R N] [IsScalarTower R S N] [IsNoetherianRing R] [IsNoetherianRing S]
    [Module.Finite S N] [Module.Flat R N]
    (h : ∀ q : PrimeSpectrum S, q.asIdeal ∈ associatedPrimes S
        (N ⊗[R] (PrimeSpectrum.comap (algebraMap R S) q).asIdeal.ResidueField) →
      I.map (algebraMap R S) ⊔ q.asIdeal ≠ ⊤) :
    UniversallyInjective (AdicCompletion.of I N)
declarations.comment:
`IS` is `I.map (algebraMap R S)` and `IS + 𝔮` is a supremum of ideals; the
contraction `𝔭 = R ∩ 𝔮` is `PrimeSpectrum.comap (algebraMap R S) 𝔮`, and `κ(𝔭)` is its
`ResidueField`; the tensor product is written `N ⊗[R] κ(𝔭)`, with `N` on the left, so that it
carries its standard `S`-module structure.

declarations.name: Module.projective_of_flat_of_projective_quotient_of_associatedPrimes
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 05DP.** Let `R` be a Noetherian ring, `I`-adically complete, let `S` be
a finite type `R`-algebra and let `N` be a finite `S`-module which is flat over `R`. If `N/IN` is
projective over `R/I` and `IS + 𝔮 ≠ S` for every prime `𝔮` of `S` which is an associated prime of
the fibre `N ⊗[R] κ(𝔭)` with `𝔭 = R ∩ 𝔮`, then `N` is projective as an `R`-module.
declarations.statement:
theorem projective_of_flat_of_projective_quotient_of_associatedPrimes (R : Type u) (S : Type v)
    [CommRing R] [CommRing S] [Algebra R S] (I : Ideal R) (N : Type w) [AddCommGroup N]
    [Module S N] [Module R N] [IsScalarTower R S N] [IsNoetherianRing R] [IsAdicComplete I R]
    [Algebra.FiniteType R S] [Module.Finite S N] [Module.Flat R N]
    (hprojective : Module.Projective (R ⧸ I) (N ⧸ I • (⊤ : Submodule R N)))
    (hassociated : ∀ q : PrimeSpectrum S, q.asIdeal ∈ associatedPrimes S
        (N ⊗[R] (PrimeSpectrum.comap (algebraMap R S) q).asIdeal.ResidueField) →
      I.map (algebraMap R S) ⊔ q.asIdeal ≠ ⊤) :
    Module.Projective R N
declarations.comment:
`N/IN` is `N ⧸ I • ⊤`; the contraction `𝔭 = R ∩ 𝔮` is
`PrimeSpectrum.comap (algebraMap R S) 𝔮` and `κ(𝔭)` its `ResidueField`; the condition `IS + 𝔮 ≠ S`
is the join of ideals being different from `⊤`.
