    (f : X ⟶ S) [LocallyOfFiniteType f] [IsLocallyNoetherian S] (x x' : X) (hxx' : x ⤳ x')
    (hx' : IsClosed ({f.asFiber x'} : Set (f.fiber (f x'))))
    (hs : f x ≠ f x' ∨ x = x') :
    closure {y : f.fiber (f x) | IsClosed ({y} : Set (f.fiber (f x))) ∧
        x ⤳ f.fiberι (f x) y ∧ f.fiberι (f x) y ⤳ x'} =
      closure ({f.asFiber x} : Set (f.fiber (f x)))
declarations.comment: the theorem the remark asserts, by the route it sketches; the hypothesis `f x ≠ f x'` (or `x = x'`) is added, Stacks 053U being false without it

declarations.name: Stacks.ClosedPointsFibre.exists_closedSubscheme_quasiFiniteAt_meeting_open_of_mem_closure
declarations.doc:
Let `f : X ⟶ S` be locally of finite type with `S` locally Noetherian, and let `x` be closed
in its fibre. If `x` lies in the closure of an open `U` no point of which lies over `f x`, then
there are a closed immersion `i : Z ⟶ X` and a point `xZ` of `Z` over `x` at which `i ≫ f` is
quasi-finite, together with a generalization `zZ` of `xZ` mapping into `U` and lying over a point
other than `f x`.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_closedSubscheme_quasiFiniteAt_meeting_open_of_mem_closure
    {X S : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ S) [LocallyOfFiniteType f]
    [IsLocallyNoetherian S] (x : X) (U : X.Opens)
    (hx : IsClosed ({f.asFiber x} : Set (f.fiber (f x))))
    (hU : ∀ y : X, y ∈ U.1 → f y ≠ f x)
    (hclosure : x ∈ closure (U.1 : Set X)) :
    ∃ (Z : Scheme.{u}) (i : Z ⟶ X), IsClosedImmersion i ∧
      ∃ xZ : Z, i xZ = x ∧ quasiFiniteAt (i ≫ f) xZ ∧
        ∃ zZ : Z, i zZ ∈ U.1 ∧ zZ ⤳ xZ ∧ f (i zZ) ≠ f x

declarations.name: Module.finitePresentationRel_tfae
declarations.doc:
Stacks 05GY: for an `A`-module `M` over a finite type ring map `R → A`, the three
conditions "some presentation", "all presentations" and "all finitely presented covers" are
equivalent.
declarations.statement:
theorem Module.finitePresentationRel_tfae [Algebra.FiniteType R A] :
    [Module.FinitePresentationRel R A M,
     Module.FinitePresentationRel.AllPresentations R A M,
     Module.FinitePresentationRel.AllFPCovers.{u} R A M].TFAE

declarations.name: Module.FinitePresentationRel.finitePresentation
declarations.doc: A module finitely presented relative to `R` is a finitely presented `A`-module.
declarations.statement:
theorem Module.FinitePresentationRel.finitePresentation
    (h : Module.FinitePresentationRel R A M) : Module.FinitePresentation A M
declarations.comment: the final conclusion, that a module finitely presented relative to R is a finitely presented A-module

declarations.name: Module.FinitePresentationRel
declarations.doc:
`M` is *finitely presented relative to `R`*: for some surjective `R`-algebra map
`α : R[x_1, …, x_n] → A`, the module `M` viewed over `R[x_1, …, x_n]` via `α` is finitely
presented.
declarations.statement:
def Module.FinitePresentationRel (R A : Type*) [CommRing R] [CommRing A] [Algebra R A]
    (M : Type*) [AddCommGroup M] [Module A M] : Prop

declarations.name: Module.finitePresentationRel_iff_of_finite
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Tag 05H0 (Lemma 15.82.3).** Let `R` be a ring, `φ : A → B` a finite
map of `R`-algebras with both `R → A` and `R → B` of finite type, and `M` a
`B`-module (hence an `A`-module via `φ`). Then `M` is finitely presented
relative to `R` as an `A`-module iff it is finitely presented relative to `R`
as a `B`-module.

The hypothesis `[IsScalarTower R A B]` encodes that `A → B` is a map of
`R`-algebras; `[IsScalarTower A B M]` encodes that the `A`-module structure on
`M` is the one obtained by restriction of scalars along `φ : A → B`.
declarations.statement:
theorem Module.finitePresentationRel_iff_of_finite
    (R A B : Type*) [CommRing R] [CommRing A] [CommRing B]
    [Algebra R A] [Algebra R B] [Algebra A B] [IsScalarTower R A B]
    [Algebra.FiniteType R A] [Algebra.FiniteType R B] [Module.Finite A B]
    (M : Type*) [AddCommGroup M] [Module A M] [Module B M] [IsScalarTower A B M] :
    Module.FinitePresentationRel R A M ↔ Module.FinitePresentationRel R B M

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.IsFinitelyPresentedRelative
declarations.doc:
A sheaf of modules `M` on `X` is finitely presented relative to `S` if there is an affine
open cover of `S` and, over each member, an affine open cover of its inverse image such that
the corresponding module of sections of `M` is finitely presented relative to the ring of
functions on the base open.
declarations.statement: abbrev IsFinitelyPresentedRelative {X S : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ S) (M : X.Modules) : Prop

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.etale_stalkBaseChangeMap
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 05H2.** The morphism between the base changes to the spectrum of a
local ring, induced by a commutative square with étale horizontal morphisms, is étale.
declarations.statement:
lemma etale_stalkBaseChangeMap (f' : X' ⟶ S') (g' : X' ⟶ X)
    (g : S' ⟶ S) (f : X ⟶ S) (h : g' ≫ f = f' ≫ g) (s' : S')
    [Etale g'] [Etale g] : Etale (stalkBaseChangeMap f' g' g f h s')

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.OneStepDevissage
declarations.doc: A one-step dévissage of `F/X/S` over `s`.
declarations.statement:
structure OneStepDevissage {X S : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ S) (F : X.Modules) (s : S)
    [LocallyOfFiniteType f] [F.IsQuasicoherent] [F.IsFiniteType]

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.OneStepDevissageAt
declarations.doc: A one-step dévissage of `F/X/S` at `x`.
declarations.statement:
structure OneStepDevissageAt {X S : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ S) (F : X.Modules) (x : X)
    [LocallyOfFiniteType f] [F.IsQuasicoherent] [F.IsFiniteType]

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.exists_etaleNeighborhood_oneStepDevissageAt
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 05H6.** A finite-type quasi-coherent module supported at a point of a
fibre admits a one-step dévissage there after elementary étale neighbourhoods of the point and
of its image.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_etaleNeighborhood_oneStepDevissageAt {X S : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ S)
    [LocallyOfFiniteType f] (F : X.Modules) [F.IsFiniteType] [F.IsQuasicoherent] (x : X)
    (hx : f.asFiber x ∈
      SheafOfModules.supp ((Scheme.Modules.pullback (f.fiberι (f x))).obj F)) :
    ∃ (U : EtaleNeighborhood X x) (V : EtaleNeighborhood S (f x)) (h : U.scheme ⟶ V.scheme),
      U.IsElementary ∧ V.IsElementary ∧ (U.toBase ≫ f = h ≫ V.toBase) ∧
        (h U.point = V.point) ∧
        ∃ (hft : LocallyOfFiniteType h)
          (hq : ((Scheme.Modules.pullback U.toBase).obj F).IsQuasicoherent)
          (hf : ((Scheme.Modules.pullback U.toBase).obj F).IsFiniteType),
          letI : LocallyOfFiniteType h := hft
          letI : ((Scheme.Modules.pullback U.toBase).obj F).IsQuasicoherent := hq
          letI : ((Scheme.Modules.pullback U.toBase).obj F).IsFiniteType := hf
          Nonempty (OneStepDevissageAt h
            ((Scheme.Modules.pullback U.toBase).obj F) U.point)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.exists_etaleNeighborhood_oneStepDevissageAt_iff_mem_fiber_supp
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 05H6**, in sharp form. The elementary étale neighbourhoods of `(X, x)`
and of `(S, f x)` over which the pullback of `F` acquires a one-step dévissage at the
distinguished point exist exactly when `x` lies in the support of the restriction of `F` to the
fibre of `f` through `x`.

The forward implication is the converse of the source's lemma; it holds because a one-step
dévissage at a point records that the point lies in the support of the module on its fibre
(`AlgebraicGeometry.OneStepDevissageAt.mem_supp`), and the support of the pullback of `F` to an
étale neighbourhood is the inverse image of the support of `F`.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_etaleNeighborhood_oneStepDevissageAt_iff_mem_fiber_supp {X S : Scheme.{u}}
    (f : X ⟶ S) [LocallyOfFiniteType f] (F : X.Modules) [F.IsFiniteType] [F.IsQuasicoherent]
    (x : X) :
    (∃ (U : EtaleNeighborhood X x) (V : EtaleNeighborhood S (f x)) (h : U.scheme ⟶ V.scheme),
      U.IsElementary ∧ V.IsElementary ∧ (U.toBase ≫ f = h ≫ V.toBase) ∧
        (h U.point = V.point) ∧
        ∃ (hft : LocallyOfFiniteType h)
          (hq : ((Scheme.Modules.pullback U.toBase).obj F).IsQuasicoherent)
          (hf : ((Scheme.Modules.pullback U.toBase).obj F).IsFiniteType),
          letI : LocallyOfFiniteType h := hft
          letI : ((Scheme.Modules.pullback U.toBase).obj F).IsQuasicoherent := hq
          letI : ((Scheme.Modules.pullback U.toBase).obj F).IsFiniteType := hf
          Nonempty (OneStepDevissageAt h
            ((Scheme.Modules.pullback U.toBase).obj F) U.point)) ↔
      f.asFiber x ∈
        SheafOfModules.supp ((Scheme.Modules.pullback (f.fiberι (f x))).obj F)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.OneStepDevissage.baseChange
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 05H7.** A one-step dévissage and all its presenting data persist
under base change to a pointed affine scheme.
declarations.statement:
def baseChange {X S S' : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ S) (F : X.Modules)
    (s : S) (s' : S') (h : S' ⟶ S) (hs : h s' = s)
    [LocallyOfFiniteType f] [F.IsQuasicoherent] [F.IsFiniteType] [IsAffine S']
    (D : OneStepDevissage f F s) :
    BaseChangeData f F s s' h hs D

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.OneStepDevissageAt.exists_baseChange
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 05H8.** A one-step dévissage at a point survives an affine pointed
base change which induces an isomorphism of residue fields: for the unique points `x'`, `z'`,
`y'` of the base-changed schemes lying over the original distinguished points and over the new
base point, the base-changed dévissage is a one-step dévissage at `x'` with distinguished
points `z'` and `y'`.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_baseChange {X S S' : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ S) (F : X.Modules) (x : X)
    [LocallyOfFiniteType f] [F.IsQuasicoherent] [F.IsFiniteType]
    (D : OneStepDevissageAt f F x)
    (s' : S') (h : S' ⟶ S) (hs : h s' = f x) [IsAffine S']
    [IsIso ((S.residueFieldCongr hs).inv ≫ h.residueFieldMap s')]
    (B : OneStepDevissage.BaseChangeData f F (f x) s' h hs D.toOneStepDevissage) :
    letI := B.locallyOfFiniteType
    letI := B.quasicoherent
    letI := B.finiteType
    ∀ (x' : ↥(pullback f h)) (_ : pullback.fst f h x' = x)
      (_ : pullback.snd f h x' = s') (z' : B.devissage.Z) (_ : B.pZ z' = D.z)
      (_ : (B.devissage.π ≫ B.devissage.g) z' = s') (y' : B.devissage.Y)
      (_ : B.pY y' = D.y) (_ : B.devissage.g y' = s'),
      ∃ E : OneStepDevissageAt (pullback.snd f h)
          ((Scheme.Modules.pullback (pullback.fst f h)).obj F) x',
        HEq E.toOneStepDevissage B.devissage ∧ HEq E.z z' ∧ HEq E.y y'

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.OneStepDevissageAt.exists_baseChange_of_affine
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 05H8.** A one-step dévissage at a point survives an affine pointed
base change which induces an isomorphism of residue fields: the base change of the dévissage
constructed in `AlgebraicGeometry.OneStepDevissage.baseChange` is a one-step dévissage at the
unique point `x'` of the base-changed source lying over `x` and over the new base point, with
distinguished points the unique points `z'` and `y'` of the base-changed closed subscheme and
smooth scheme lying over `z` and `y` and over the new base point.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_baseChange_of_affine {X S S' : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ S) (F : X.Modules) (x : X)
    [LocallyOfFiniteType f] [F.IsQuasicoherent] [F.IsFiniteType]
    (D : OneStepDevissageAt f F x)
    (s' : S') (h : S' ⟶ S) (hs : h s' = f x) [IsAffine S']
    [IsIso ((S.residueFieldCongr hs).inv ≫ h.residueFieldMap s')] :
    let B := OneStepDevissage.baseChange f F (f x) s' h hs D.toOneStepDevissage
    letI := B.locallyOfFiniteType
    letI := B.quasicoherent
    letI := B.finiteType
    ∃ (x' : ↥(pullback f h)) (z' : B.devissage.Z) (y' : B.devissage.Y)
      (E : OneStepDevissageAt (pullback.snd f h)
        ((Scheme.Modules.pullback (pullback.fst f h)).obj F) x'),
      ((pullback.fst f h x' = x ∧ pullback.snd f h x' = s') ∧
        ∀ w : ↥(pullback f h), pullback.fst f h w = x → pullback.snd f h w = s' → w = x') ∧
      ((B.pZ z' = D.z ∧ (B.devissage.π ≫ B.devissage.g) z' = s') ∧
        ∀ w : B.devissage.Z, B.pZ w = D.z →
          (B.devissage.π ≫ B.devissage.g) w = s' → w = z') ∧
      ((B.pY y' = D.y ∧ B.devissage.g y' = s') ∧
        ∀ w : B.devissage.Y, B.pY w = D.y → B.devissage.g w = s' → w = y') ∧
      HEq E.toOneStepDevissage B.devissage ∧ HEq E.z z' ∧ HEq E.y y'

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.OneStepDevissageAt.StandardShrinking
declarations.doc: A standard shrinking of a one-step dévissage at `x`.
declarations.statement:
structure StandardShrinking {X S : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ S)
    (F : X.Modules) (x : X) [LocallyOfFiniteType f]
    [F.IsQuasicoherent] [F.IsFiniteType]
    (D : OneStepDevissageAt f F x)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.exists_standardShrinking_base
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Tag 05HA, part (1).** Restricting a one-step dévissage at `x` to a principal open
neighbourhood `V` of `f x` in the base is a standard shrinking, whose other three opens are the
inverse images of `V`.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_standardShrinking_base {X S : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ S) (F : X.Modules) (x : X)
    [LocallyOfFiniteType f] [F.IsQuasicoherent] [F.IsFiniteType] (D : OneStepDevissageAt f F x)
    (V : S.Opens) (a : Γ(S, ⊤)) (hV : V = S.basicOpen a) (hs : f x ∈ V) :
    ∃ E : D.StandardShrinking, E.S' = V ∧ E.X' = f ⁻¹ᵁ V ∧
      E.Z' = (D.toOneStepDevissage.i ≫ f) ⁻¹ᵁ V ∧ E.Y' = D.toOneStepDevissage.g ⁻¹ᵁ V
declarations.comment: part (1)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.exists_standardShrinking_smooth
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Tag 05HA, part (2).** Given a principal open neighbourhood `W` of the distinguished
point `y` of the smooth scheme, there is a standard shrinking whose smooth open is `W` cut down
to the inverse image of the new base.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_standardShrinking_smooth {X S : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ S) (F : X.Modules) (x : X)
    [LocallyOfFiniteType f] [F.IsQuasicoherent] [F.IsFiniteType] (D : OneStepDevissageAt f F x)
    (W : D.toOneStepDevissage.Y.Opens) (a : Γ(D.toOneStepDevissage.Y, ⊤))
    (hW : W = D.toOneStepDevissage.Y.basicOpen a) (hy : D.y ∈ W) :
    ∃ E : D.StandardShrinking, E.Y' = W ⊓ (D.toOneStepDevissage.g ⁻¹ᵁ E.S')
declarations.comment: part (2)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.exists_standardShrinking_source
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Tag 05HA, part (3).** Given any open neighbourhood `U` of `x`, there is a standard
shrinking whose source open lies inside `U`.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_standardShrinking_source {X S : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ S) (F : X.Modules) (x : X)
    [LocallyOfFiniteType f] [F.IsQuasicoherent] [F.IsFiniteType] (D : OneStepDevissageAt f F x)
    (U : X.Opens) (hx : x ∈ U) : ∃ E : D.StandardShrinking, E.X' ≤ U
declarations.comment: part (3)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.exists_oneStepDevissageAt_of_etaleNeighborhood
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 05HE.** A one-step dévissage at a point can be pulled through a
compatible pair of elementary étale neighbourhoods of the base and of the smooth scheme, after a
further elementary étale localization of the base: the new smooth scheme is an open subscheme of
the base change of the given neighbourhood, the new closed subscheme is the base change of the
old one, and the new module is the pullback of the old one.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_oneStepDevissageAt_of_etaleNeighborhood
    {X S : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ S) (F : X.Modules) (x : X)
    [LocallyOfFiniteType f] [F.IsQuasicoherent] [F.IsFiniteType]
    (D : OneStepDevissageAt f F x)
    (U : EtaleNeighborhood S (f x)) (hU : U.IsElementary)
    (V : EtaleNeighborhood D.toOneStepDevissage.Y D.y)
    (hV : V.IsElementary) (h : V.scheme ⟶ U.scheme)
    (hcomm : V.toBase ≫ D.toOneStepDevissage.g = h ≫ U.toBase)
    (hpoint : h V.point = U.point) :
    ∃ (W : EtaleNeighborhood U.scheme U.point)
      (_ : W.IsElementary)
      (A : EtaleNeighborhood X x) (_ : A.IsElementary)
      (b : A.scheme ⟶ W.scheme),
      b A.point = W.point ∧
      A.toBase ≫ f = b ≫ W.toBase ≫ U.toBase ∧
      ∃ (hl : LocallyOfFiniteType b)
        (hq : ((Scheme.Modules.pullback A.toBase).obj F).IsQuasicoherent)
        (ht : ((Scheme.Modules.pullback A.toBase).obj F).IsFiniteType),
        letI := hl
        letI := hq
        letI := ht
        ∃ (D' : OneStepDevissageAt b ((Scheme.Modules.pullback A.toBase).obj F) A.point)
          (j : D'.toOneStepDevissage.Y ⟶ pullback h W.toBase)
          (p : D'.toOneStepDevissage.Z ⟶ D.toOneStepDevissage.Z),
          IsOpenImmersion j ∧
          D'.toOneStepDevissage.g = j ≫ pullback.snd h W.toBase ∧
          (j ≫ pullback.fst h W.toBase) D'.y = V.point ∧
          p D'.z = D.z ∧
          D'.toOneStepDevissage.i ≫ A.toBase =
            p ≫ D.toOneStepDevissage.i ∧
          IsPullback p D'.toOneStepDevissage.i D.toOneStepDevissage.i
            A.toBase ∧
          IsPullback p D'.toOneStepDevissage.π D.toOneStepDevissage.π
            (j ≫ pullback.fst h W.toBase ≫ V.toBase) ∧
          Nonempty (D'.toOneStepDevissage.G ≅
            (Scheme.Modules.pullback p).obj D.toOneStepDevissage.G)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.exists_freeMap_isIso_genericFiber
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 05HF**, first assertion. For a one-step dévissage, a free `𝒪_Y`-module of positive
finite rank maps to the direct image `π_* G` by a map that becomes an isomorphism over the
residue field of the image in `Y` of a point of the fibre of `g` over `s`.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_freeMap_isIso_genericFiber :
    ∃ (r : ℕ) (_ : 0 < r)
      (α : SheafOfModules.free (R := D.Y.ringCatSheaf) (ULift.{u} (Fin r)) ⟶
        (Scheme.Modules.pushforward D.π).obj D.G),
      IsIso ((Scheme.Modules.pullback
        (D.Y.fromSpecResidueField (D.g.fiberι s ξ))).map α)
declarations.comment: existence of the generically invertible map

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.dim_support_cokernel_fiber_lt
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 05HF**, second assertion. If a map into the direct image `π_* G` of a one-step
dévissage becomes an isomorphism over the residue field of the image in `Y` of a point of the
fibre of `g` over `s`, then the fibre over `s` of the support of its cokernel has strictly
smaller dimension than the fibre over `s` of the support of `F`.
declarations.statement:
theorem dim_support_cokernel_fiber_lt {P : D.Y.Modules}
    (α : P ⟶ (Scheme.Modules.pushforward D.π).obj D.G)
    (hα : IsIso ((Scheme.Modules.pullback
      (D.Y.fromSpecResidueField (D.g.fiberι s ξ))).map α)) :
    topologicalKrullDim
        (SheafOfModules.supp ((Scheme.Modules.pullback (D.g.fiberι s)).obj (cokernel α))) <
      topologicalKrullDim
        (SheafOfModules.supp ((Scheme.Modules.pullback (f.fiberι s)).obj F))
declarations.comment: dimension of the cokernel support

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.NonemptyCompleteDevissage
declarations.doc:
A complete dévissage of `F/X/S` over `s`: a finite chain of stages
`(Z_k, Y_k, i_k, π_k, G_k, α_k)_{k = 1, …, n}`, with `n ≥ 1`, whose first stage is a one-step
dévissage of `F/X/S` over `s`, whose `k`-th stage for `k ≥ 2` is a one-step dévissage of
`Coker(α_{k-1})/Y_{k-1}/S` over `s`, each `α_k` inducing an isomorphism over the residue field
of the generic point of `(Y_k)_s`, and with `Coker(α_n) = 0`.
declarations.statement:
structure NonemptyCompleteDevissage {X S : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ S) (F : X.Modules) (s : S)
    [hl : LocallyOfFiniteType f] [hq : F.IsQuasicoherent] [ht : F.IsFiniteType]

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.NonemptyCompleteDevissageAt
declarations.doc:
A complete dévissage of `F/X/S` at `x`, as in the source: a nonempty complete dévissage
over the image of `x` whose first stage is a one-step dévissage at `x` and each later stage a
one-step dévissage at the distinguished point of the preceding smooth scheme. Its first stage
places `x` in the support of the fibre module
(`AlgebraicGeometry.NonemptyCompleteDevissageAt.mem_fiber_support`), so the zero module has
none.
declarations.statement:
structure NonemptyCompleteDevissageAt {X S : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ S) (F : X.Modules) (x : X)
    [hl : LocallyOfFiniteType f] [hq : F.IsQuasicoherent] [ht : F.IsFiniteType]

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.exists_completeDevissage_baseChange
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 05HJ.** A complete dévissage of `F/X/S` over `s` base-changes, stage by stage, to
a complete dévissage of the base-changed module over `s'`, for any cartesian square whose
new base is affine.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_completeDevissage_baseChange {X X' : Scheme.{u}} {f : X ⟶ S} {f' : X' ⟶ S'}
    {F : X.Modules} {F' : X'.Modules} (hs : h s' = s) [IsAffine S'] [LocallyOfFiniteType f]
    [F.IsQuasicoherent] [F.IsFiniteType] [LocallyOfFiniteType f'] [F'.IsQuasicoherent]
    [F'.IsFiniteType] (D : NonemptyCompleteDevissage f F s) (pX : X' ⟶ X)
    (hX : IsPullback pX f' f h) (eF : (Scheme.Modules.pullback pX).obj F ≅ F') :
    ∃ D' : NonemptyCompleteDevissage f' F' s', ChainIsBaseChange h pX D.chain D'.chain

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.CompleteDevissageAt.exists_isBaseChange
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 05HK.** Let `(S', s') → (S, s)` be a morphism of pointed schemes inducing an
isomorphism of residue fields, with `S'` affine, let `X'` be the base change of `X` and `F'`
the pullback of `F`, and let `x' ∈ X'` lie over `x ∈ X` and `s'` (so `s = f x`, `s' = f' x'`).
Then every complete dévissage of `F/X/S` at `x` base-changes, stage by stage as in Stacks 05HJ,
to a complete dévissage of `F'/X'/S'` at `x'` whose distinguished points lie over the original
ones. The finiteness properties of `f'` and `F'` are derived from the base change, not
assumed.
declarations.statement:
theorem CompleteDevissageAt.exists_isBaseChange {h : S' ⟶ S} [IsAffine S']
    [LocallyOfFiniteType f] [F.IsQuasicoherent] [F.IsFiniteType]
    (hres : IsIso (h.residueFieldMap (f' x'))) (pX : X' ⟶ X) (hX : IsPullback pX f' f h)
    (eF : (Scheme.Modules.pullback pX).obj F ≅ F') (hx : pX x' = x)
    (D : CompleteDevissageAt f F x) :
    haveI := locallyOfFiniteType_of_isPullback hX
    haveI := isQuasicoherent_of_iso_pullback eF
    haveI := isFiniteType_of_iso_pullback eF
    ∃ D' : CompleteDevissageAt f' F' x', D.IsBaseChange h pX D'

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.NonemptyCompleteDevissageAt.StandardShrinking
declarations.doc:
A standard shrinking of a complete dévissage of `F/X/S` at `x`: standard opens of the
base and of the source, and standard opens in every stage, containing the distinguished
points, whose restricted system is again a complete dévissage at `x`.
declarations.statement:
structure StandardShrinking {X S : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ S) (F : X.Modules) (x : X)
    [LocallyOfFiniteType f] [F.IsQuasicoherent] [F.IsFiniteType]
    (D : NonemptyCompleteDevissageAt f F x)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.exists_standardShrinking_finalTarget
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 05HM, final target shrinking.** Let `W` be a principal open neighbourhood of the
distinguished point of the smooth scheme of the last stage of a complete dévissage of `F/X/S` at
`x`. Then there is a standard shrinking of the dévissage whose last smooth open is `W` cut down
to the inverse image of the new base.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_standardShrinking_finalTarget {X S : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ S) (F : X.Modules)
    (x : X) [LocallyOfFiniteType f] [F.IsQuasicoherent] [F.IsFiniteType]
    (D : NonemptyCompleteDevissageAt f F x) (W : (finalTargetScheme D.pointed).Opens)
    (a : Γ(finalTargetScheme D.pointed, ⊤))
    (hW : W = (finalTargetScheme D.pointed).basicOpen a)
    (hy : finalTargetPoint D.pointed ∈ W) :
    ∃ E : NonemptyCompleteDevissageAt.StandardShrinking f F x D,
      letI := E.locally_finite_type
      letI := E.quasi_coherent
      letI := E.finite_type
      FinalTargetIsBaseRestriction E.S'.ι E.S' D.pointed E.restricted_devissage.pointed
        E.restricted_stages W
declarations.comment: final_target_shrinking

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.NonemptyCompleteDevissageAt.exists_standardShrinking_base
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 05HM, base shrinking.** Restricting a complete dévissage at `x` over a standard
open neighbourhood of `f x` gives a standard shrinking whose base and source are that open
and its inverse image, and all of whose stages are the corresponding base changes.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_standardShrinking_base {X S : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ S) (F : X.Modules) (x : X)
    [LocallyOfFiniteType f] [F.IsQuasicoherent] [F.IsFiniteType]
    (D : NonemptyCompleteDevissageAt f F x)
    (V : S.Opens) (a : Γ(S, ⊤)) (hV : V = S.basicOpen a) (hs : f x ∈ V) :
    ∃ E : NonemptyCompleteDevissageAt.StandardShrinking f F x D,
      E.S' = V ∧ E.X' = f ⁻¹ᵁ V ∧
        (letI := E.locally_finite_type
         letI := E.quasi_coherent
         letI := E.finite_type
         PointedChainIsBaseChange E.S'.ι E.X'.ι D.pointed E.restricted_devissage.pointed)
declarations.comment: base_shrinking

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.NonemptyCompleteDevissageAt.exists_standardShrinking_source
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 05HM, source shrinking.** A complete dévissage of `F/X/S` at `x` admits a standard
shrinking whose source open lies inside any prescribed open neighbourhood of `x`.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_standardShrinking_source {X S : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ S) (F : X.Modules) (x : X)
    [LocallyOfFiniteType f] [F.IsQuasicoherent] [F.IsFiniteType]
    (D : NonemptyCompleteDevissageAt f F x) (U : X.Opens) (hx : x ∈ U) :
    ∃ E : NonemptyCompleteDevissageAt.StandardShrinking f F x D, E.X' ≤ U
declarations.comment: source_shrinking

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.hasEtaleNeighborhoodCompleteDevissageAt
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 05HR.** A finite-type quasi-coherent module on a scheme locally of
finite type over `S` acquires a complete dévissage at any chosen point after elementary étale
neighbourhoods of that point and of its image.

The induction is a well-founded recursion on `AlgebraicGeometry.fiberSupportDim`, which takes
values in the well-founded order `WithBot ℕ∞`.
declarations.statement:
theorem hasEtaleNeighborhoodCompleteDevissageAt {X S : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ S)
    [LocallyOfFiniteType f] (F : X.Modules) [F.IsQuasicoherent] [F.IsFiniteType] (x : X) :
    HasEtaleNeighborhoodCompleteDevissageAt f F x

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.exists_etaleNeighborhood_completeDevissage_cover
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 05HU.** Let `X ⟶ S` be a finite-type morphism of schemes and `F` a
finite-type quasi-coherent module on `X`. For every point `s` of `S` there is an elementary étale
neighbourhood `(S', s') ⟶ (S, s)` and finitely many étale morphisms `hᵢ : Yᵢ ⟶ X ×_S S'` whose
images cover the fibre `(X ×_S S')_{s'} = X_s`, such that the pullback of `F` to each `Yᵢ` has a
complete dévissage along `Yᵢ ⟶ S'` over `s'`.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_etaleNeighborhood_completeDevissage_cover {X S : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ S)
    [LocallyOfFiniteType f] [QuasiCompact f] (F : X.Modules) [F.IsQuasicoherent]
    [F.IsFiniteType] (s : S) :
    ∃ (S' : EtaleNeighborhood S s) (_ : S'.IsElementary) (n : ℕ) (Y : Fin n → Scheme.{u})
      (h : ∀ i, Y i ⟶ pullback f S'.toBase) (_ : ∀ i, Etale (h i))
      (hl : ∀ i, LocallyOfFiniteType (h i ≫ pullback.snd f S'.toBase))
      (hq : ∀ i, ((Scheme.Modules.pullback
        (h i ≫ pullback.fst f S'.toBase)).obj F).IsQuasicoherent)
      (ht : ∀ i, ((Scheme.Modules.pullback
        (h i ≫ pullback.fst f S'.toBase)).obj F).IsFiniteType),
      (∀ i, Nonempty (@CompleteDevissage _ _ (h i ≫ pullback.snd f S'.toBase)
        ((Scheme.Modules.pullback (h i ≫ pullback.fst f S'.toBase)).obj F) S'.point
        (hl i) (hq i) (ht i))) ∧
        pullback.snd f S'.toBase ⁻¹' {S'.point} ⊆ ⋃ i, Set.range (h i)

declarations.name: Algebra.ElementaryEtaleLocalization
declarations.doc:
An **elementary étale localization** of `R → S` at a prime `q` lying over `p`.

The rings `R'` and `S'`, their structure maps, and `commutes` form the square of the definition.
The primes `p'` and `q'` lie over the indicated primes, and the canonical residue-field maps are
isomorphisms.

declarations.name: Module.CompleteDevissage
declarations.doc:
A **complete dévissage** of a finite `S`-module `N` over a prime ideal `r` of `R`.

There are `stepCount + 1` stages. At stage `i`, `A i` and `B i` are `R`-algebras,
`M i` is a finite `A i`-module, and `alpha i` maps a finite free `B i`-module to `M i`
viewed as a `B i`-module through `toLeft i`. The maps `toRight` connect consecutive stages.
declarations.statement:
public structure CompleteDevissage (R : Type u) (S : Type v) (N : Type w) [CommRing R]
    [CommRing S] [Algebra R S] [Algebra.FiniteType R S] [AddCommGroup N] [Module S N]
    [Module.Finite S N] (r : Ideal R) [r.IsPrime]

declarations.name: Ideal.isPrime_map_of_smooth_of_geometricallyIrreducible
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 05HX.** If `R → B` is smooth and the fibres of `Spec B → Spec R` are
geometrically irreducible, then the ideal generated by a prime `r` of `R` in `B` is prime. It is
the generic point of the fibre over `r`.
declarations.statement:
theorem Ideal.isPrime_map_of_smooth_of_geometricallyIrreducible
    (R B : Type u) [CommRing R] [CommRing B] [Algebra R B] [Algebra.Smooth R B]
    [GeometricallyIrreducible (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap R B)))]
    (r : Ideal R) [r.IsPrime] : (Ideal.map (algebraMap R B) r).IsPrime
declarations.comment: the prime of the lower algebra

declarations.name: Module.CompleteDevissage.upperAlgebra_finitePresentation
declarations.doc:
Except for the first one, every upper algebra in a complete dévissage is finitely
presented over the base.
declarations.comment: finite presentation of the upper algebras after the first

declarations.name: Module.CompleteDevissage.initialUpperAlgebra_finitePresentation
declarations.doc:
If the original algebra is finitely presented over the base, so is the first upper
algebra in a complete dévissage.
declarations.statement:
public theorem initialUpperAlgebra_finitePresentation [Algebra.FinitePresentation R S]
    (D : CompleteDevissage R S N r) :
    Algebra.FinitePresentation R (D.A 0)
declarations.comment: finite presentation of the first upper algebra

declarations.name: Module.CompleteDevissage.left_finitePresentation
declarations.doc:
When the original algebra is finitely presented over the base, every same-stage map
`B i → A i` in a complete dévissage is finitely presented.
declarations.statement:
public theorem left_finitePresentation [Algebra.FinitePresentation R S]
    (D : CompleteDevissage R S N r) (i : Fin (D.stepCount + 1)) :
    (D.toLeft i).toRingHom.FinitePresentation
declarations.comment: finite presentation of the maps in the dévissage

declarations.name: Module.CompleteDevissage.finitePresentation_iff_initial_over_upper
declarations.doc:
Condition (1) of Tag 05HY is equivalent to condition (2): finite presentation of the
original module is equivalent to finite presentation of the first stage over its upper
algebra.
declarations.statement:
public theorem finitePresentation_iff_initial_over_upper [Algebra.FinitePresentation R S]
    (D : CompleteDevissage R S N r) :
    Module.FinitePresentation S N ↔ Module.FinitePresentation (D.A 0) (D.M 0)
declarations.comment: equivalence of conditions (1) and (2)

declarations.name: Module.CompleteDevissage.finitePresentation_iff_initial_over_lower
declarations.doc:
Conditions (2) and (3) of Tag 05HY are equivalent: at the first stage, finite
presentation over the upper algebra is equivalent to finite presentation after restriction
of scalars to the lower algebra.
declarations.statement:
public theorem finitePresentation_iff_initial_over_lower [Algebra.FinitePresentation R S]
    (D : CompleteDevissage R S N r) :
    letI : Module (D.B 0) (D.M 0) :=
      Module.compHom (D.M 0) (D.toLeft 0).toRingHom
    Module.FinitePresentation (D.A 0) (D.M 0) ↔
      Module.FinitePresentation (D.B 0) (D.M 0)
declarations.comment: equivalence of conditions (2) and (3)

declarations.name: Module.CompleteDevissage.finitePresentation_iff_all_stages
declarations.doc:
Condition (3) of Tag 05HY is equivalent to condition (4): finite presentation at the
first lower algebra propagates precisely to finite presentation over both algebras at every
stage.
declarations.statement:
public theorem finitePresentation_iff_all_stages [Algebra.FinitePresentation R S]
    (D : CompleteDevissage R S N r) :
    letI : Module (D.B 0) (D.M 0) :=
      Module.compHom (D.M 0) (D.toLeft 0).toRingHom
    Module.FinitePresentation (D.B 0) (D.M 0) ↔
      ∀ i : Fin (D.stepCount + 1),
        Module.FinitePresentation (D.A i) (D.M i) ∧
          letI : Module (D.B i) (D.M i) :=
            Module.compHom (D.M i) (D.toLeft i).toRingHom
          Module.FinitePresentation (D.B i) (D.M i)
declarations.comment: equivalence of conditions (3) and (4)

registrations.name: Module.CompleteDevissage.initial_finitePresentation
registrations.comment: finite presentation of the initial map

registrations.name: Module.CompleteDevissage.transition_finitePresentation
registrations.comment: finite presentation of the transition maps

registrations.name: Algebra.Smooth.finitePresentation
registrations.comment: finite presentation of the lower algebras

declarations.name: Module.CompleteDevissageAt
declarations.doc:
A **complete dévissage at `q`** is either the empty dévissage of the zero module,
or a nonempty dévissage with the prime and dimension conditions of Stacks 05HZ.  The empty case
is the repository's convention for `N = 0`; Stacks 05HZ as printed has no empty case.
declarations.statement:
public inductive CompleteDevissageAt (R : Type u) (S : Type v) (N : Type w)
    [CommRing R] [CommRing S] [Algebra R S] [Algebra.FiniteType R S]
    [AddCommGroup N] [Module S N] [Module.Finite S N]
    (q : Ideal S) [q.IsPrime]
declarations.comment: the empty dévissage of N = 0 is added as the repository's convention; the nonempty case is the printed definition

declarations.name: Module.nonempty_completeDevissage_of_completeDevissage
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 05I0, item (1).**

Let `f : X ⟶ S` be locally of finite type between affine schemes, let `ℱ` be a quasi-coherent
`𝒪_X`-module of finite type and let `s : S` correspond to the prime `r` of `Γ(S, ⊤)`. If there
exists a complete dévissage of `ℱ/X/S` over `s`, then there exists a complete dévissage of
`Γ(ℱ, ⊤)/Γ(X, ⊤)/Γ(S, ⊤)` over `r`.

Taking `X = Spec B`, `S = Spec A` and `ℱ = Ñ` recovers the statement of the source, whose `N` is
`Γ(ℱ, ⊤)`. Remark 05I0 states this item as an implication and nothing more, and says why: the
definition of a complete dévissage of `N/B/A` over `r`, Stacks 05HX, omits the condition on the
relative dimension that Stacks 05H4 (5) puts on the smooth scheme of a one-step dévissage, so
the algebraic notion over `r` is the weaker of the two. The zero module separates them. It has
the one-stage dévissage `Module.CompleteDevissage.ofSubsingleton`, while the zero sheaf has only
the empty dévissage of Stacks 05HH: a smooth morphism with geometrically irreducible fibres has
fibres of dimension at least `0`, and `dim (Supp(ℱ_s)) = -∞`. Item (2) of the source, for the
notions *at a point*, is an equivalence, because Stacks 05HZ (4) restores that condition.

Both cases of `AlgebraicGeometry.CompleteDevissage` are covered. A chain of stages is translated
stage by stage by `AlgebraicGeometry.DevissageChain.toCompleteDevissage`. The empty dévissage,
which `AlgebraicGeometry.CompleteDevissage.empty` allows for the zero sheaf, is sent to
`Module.CompleteDevissage.ofSubsingleton`: the sections of a zero sheaf vanish, and the zero
module has a one-stage algebraic dévissage — with the zero ring upstairs and `Γ(S, ⊤)` itself as
the smooth algebra — because Stacks 05HX imposes no condition on the dimensions of the fibres,
which is the same omission that makes this item one-directional.
declarations.statement:
public theorem nonempty_completeDevissage_of_completeDevissage {X S : Scheme.{u}}
    [IsAffine X] [IsAffine S] {f : X ⟶ S} {F : X.Modules} {s : S} [hl : LocallyOfFiniteType f]
    [hq : F.IsQuasicoherent] [ht : F.IsFiniteType] (r : Ideal Γ(S, ⊤)) [r.IsPrime]
    (hr : (S.isoSpec.hom s).asIdeal = r)
    (D : AlgebraicGeometry.CompleteDevissage f F s) :
    letI := f.appTop.hom.toAlgebra
    letI : Algebra.FiniteType Γ(S, ⊤) Γ(X, ⊤) :=
      HasRingHomProperty.appTop (P := @LocallyOfFiniteType) f hl
    letI : Module.Finite Γ(X, ⊤) Γ(F, (⊤ : X.Opens)) :=
      Stacks.AlgebraicGeometry.CoherentFinite.finite_sections F (isAffineOpen_top X)
    Nonempty (Module.CompleteDevissage Γ(S, ⊤) Γ(X, ⊤) Γ(F, (⊤ : X.Opens)) r)
declarations.comment: (1): a geometric complete dévissage over a point gives an algebraic one

declarations.name: Module.nonempty_completeDevissage_of_nonemptyCompleteDevissage
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 05I0, item (1).**

Let `f : X ⟶ S` be locally of finite type between affine schemes, let `ℱ` be a quasi-coherent
`𝒪_X`-module of finite type and let `s : S` correspond to the prime `r` of `Γ(S, ⊤)`. If there
exists a nonempty complete dévissage of `ℱ/X/S` over `s`, then there exists a complete dévissage
of `Γ(ℱ, ⊤)/Γ(X, ⊤)/Γ(S, ⊤)` over `r`.

Taking `X = Spec B`, `S = Spec A` and `ℱ = Ñ` recovers the statement of the source, whose `N` is
`Γ(ℱ, ⊤)`. The implication goes only in this direction: the source omits the condition on the
relative dimension from the definition of a complete dévissage of `N/B/A` over `r`, so an
algebraic dévissage carries strictly less information than a geometric one. The hypothesis is the
*nonempty* notion because `Module.CompleteDevissage`, like the zigzag of Stacks 05HX, always has
at least one stage, while `AlgebraicGeometry.CompleteDevissage` also allows the empty
dévissage of the zero sheaf.
declarations.statement:
public theorem nonempty_completeDevissage_of_nonemptyCompleteDevissage {X S : Scheme.{u}}
    [IsAffine X] [IsAffine S] {f : X ⟶ S} {F : X.Modules} {s : S} [hl : LocallyOfFiniteType f]
    [hq : F.IsQuasicoherent] [ht : F.IsFiniteType] (r : Ideal Γ(S, ⊤)) [r.IsPrime]
    (hr : (S.isoSpec.hom s).asIdeal = r)
    (D : AlgebraicGeometry.NonemptyCompleteDevissage f F s) :
    letI := f.appTop.hom.toAlgebra
    letI : Algebra.FiniteType Γ(S, ⊤) Γ(X, ⊤) :=
      HasRingHomProperty.appTop (P := @LocallyOfFiniteType) f hl
    letI : Module.Finite Γ(X, ⊤) Γ(F, (⊤ : X.Opens)) :=
      Stacks.AlgebraicGeometry.CoherentFinite.finite_sections F (isAffineOpen_top X)
    Nonempty (Module.CompleteDevissage Γ(S, ⊤) Γ(X, ⊤) Γ(F, (⊤ : X.Opens)) r)
declarations.comment: (1): a geometric complete dévissage over a point gives an algebraic one

declarations.name: Module.nonempty_completeDevissageAt_of_completeDevissageAt
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 05I0, item (2).**

Let `f : X ⟶ S` be locally of finite type between affine schemes, let `ℱ` be a quasi-coherent
`𝒪_X`-module of finite type and let `x : X` correspond to the prime `q` of `Γ(X, ⊤)`. If `ℱ/X/S`
has a complete dévissage at `x` then `Γ(ℱ, ⊤)/Γ(X, ⊤)/Γ(S, ⊤)` has a complete dévissage at `q`.

Taking `X = Spec B`, `S = Spec A` and `ℱ = Ñ` recovers the statement of the source, whose `N` is
`Γ(ℱ, ⊤)`, after composing `Module.nonempty_completeDevissageAt_ofRingEquiv` with the three
comparison isomorphisms `Γ(Spec A, ⊤) ≅ A`, `Γ(Spec B, ⊤) ≅ B` and `Γ(Ñ, ⊤) ≅ N`.

The source states item (2) as an equivalence and uses only this direction; the equivalence is
`Module.nonempty_completeDevissageAt_iff` in
`StacksFrontier/AlgebraicGeometry/Flatness/Devissage/Complete/SpecCompleteDevissageAt.lean`, whose
converse half builds the scheme-theoretic dévissage out of the algebraic one on `Spec`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem nonempty_completeDevissageAt_of_completeDevissageAt {X S : Scheme.{u}}
    [IsAffine X] [IsAffine S] {f : X ⟶ S} {F : X.Modules} {x : X}
    [hl : LocallyOfFiniteType f] [hq : F.IsQuasicoherent] [ht : F.IsFiniteType]
    (q : Ideal Γ(X, ⊤)) (hqp : q.IsPrime) (hqx : (X.isoSpec.hom x).asIdeal = q)
    (D : AlgebraicGeometry.CompleteDevissageAt f F x) :
    letI := f.appTop.hom.toAlgebra
    letI : Algebra.FiniteType Γ(S, ⊤) Γ(X, ⊤) :=
      HasRingHomProperty.appTop (P := @LocallyOfFiniteType) f hl
    letI : Module.Finite Γ(X, ⊤) Γ(F, (⊤ : X.Opens)) :=
      Stacks.AlgebraicGeometry.CoherentFinite.finite_sections F (isAffineOpen_top X)
    letI := hqp
    Nonempty (Module.CompleteDevissageAt Γ(S, ⊤) Γ(X, ⊤) Γ(F, (⊤ : X.Opens)) q)
declarations.comment: (2): a geometric complete dévissage at a point gives an algebraic one

declarations.name: Module.nonempty_completeDevissageAt_iff
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 05I0 (2)**, as an equivalence. For a ring map `A → B` of finite type,
a finite `B`-module `N` and a prime `q` of `B`, a complete dévissage of `Ñ/Spec B/Spec A` at the
point of `q` exists if and only if a complete dévissage of `N/B/A` at `q` exists.

The relative dimension condition of Stacks 05HZ (4) is read fibre by fibre, as Stacks 05I0
describes it: every fibre of `Spec Bᵢ → Spec A` has the dimension
`dim_{qᵢ}(Supp(Mᵢ ⊗ κ(r)))`. That is the supremum condition
`Module.NonemptyCompleteDevissageAt.relativeDimension_eq_support` of the dévissage together with
`Module.CompleteDevissageAt.FibresHaveRelativeDimension`.

The direction from sheaves to modules is
`AlgebraicGeometry.exists_completeDevissageAt_fibresHaveRelativeDimension_of_spec`; the converse
is `nonempty_completeDevissageAt_of_algebraic`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem Module.nonempty_completeDevissageAt_iff (A B : Type u) [CommRing A] [CommRing B]
    [Algebra A B] [Algebra.FiniteType A B] (N : Type u) [AddCommGroup N] [Module B N]
    [Module.Finite B N] (q : PrimeSpectrum B) :
    Nonempty (@AlgebraicGeometry.CompleteDevissageAt (Spec (.of B)) (Spec (.of A))
        (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap A B)))
        (tilde (R := .of B) (ModuleCat.of B N)) q
        (AlgebraicGeometry.locallyOfFiniteType_specMap_algebraMap A B) inferInstance
        ((AlgebraicGeometry.tilde_isFiniteType_iff (R := .of B) (ModuleCat.of B N)).2
          inferInstance)) ↔
      ∃ D : @Module.CompleteDevissageAt A B N _ _ _ _ _ _ _ q.asIdeal q.isPrime,
        D.FibresHaveRelativeDimension
declarations.comment: (2): a complete dévissage at a point exists for the sheaf exactly when it exists for the module

declarations.name: Module.exists_elementaryEtaleLocalization_completeDevissageAt
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 05I1.** Let `R → S` be a ring map of finite type, let `M` be a finite
`S`-module and let `q` be a prime of `S`. There is an elementary étale localization of `R → S`
at `q` — rings `R'` and `S'`, primes `p'` and `q'` — such that `(M ⊗_S S')/S'/R'` has a complete
dévissage at `q'`.

The localized ring map `R' → S'` is again of finite type, which the definition of a complete
dévissage at a prime requires; it is returned with the dévissage because no consumer can state
it in advance of the localization.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_elementaryEtaleLocalization_completeDevissageAt (R S M : Type u) [CommRing R]
    [CommRing S] [Algebra R S] [Algebra.FiniteType R S] [AddCommGroup M] [Module S M]
    [Module.Finite S M] (q : Ideal S) [q.IsPrime] :
    ∃ E : Algebra.ElementaryEtaleLocalization.{u, u, u, u} R S (q.under R) q,
      ∃ hFiniteType : Algebra.FiniteType E.R' E.S',
        letI := hFiniteType
        Nonempty (Module.CompleteDevissageAt E.R' E.S' (TensorProduct S E.S' M) E.q')

declarations.name: Algebra.closedFiberIdeal_isPrime
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 05I3, the generic point of the closed fibre.** If the fibres of
`Spec S ⟶ Spec R` are geometrically integral, the ideal extending the maximal ideal of the
local ring `R` is prime.
declarations.statement:
public theorem Algebra.closedFiberIdeal_isPrime
    (R : Type u) (S : Type u) [CommRing R] [CommRing S] [IsLocalRing R] [Algebra R S]
    [GeometricallyIntegral (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap R S)))] :
    (Algebra.closedFiberIdeal R S).IsPrime
declarations.comment: the generic point of the closed fibre

declarations.name: Module.freeMapAtResidueField
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 05I3, construction of the free map.** For a finite module and a prime
ideal `p`, some map from a finite free module becomes an isomorphism after tensoring with the
residue field at `p`.
declarations.statement:
public noncomputable def Module.freeMapAtResidueField
    (S : Type u) [CommRing S] (p : Ideal S) [p.IsPrime]
    (N : Type v) [AddCommGroup N] [Module S N] [Module.Finite S N] :
    Σ r : ℕ, { alpha : (Fin r → S) →ₗ[S] N //
      Function.Bijective (alpha.rTensor p.ResidueField) }
declarations.comment: construction of the free map

declarations.name: Module.flat_localizedModule_tfae
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 05I3, the five equivalent conditions**, with the universe of the module
independent of that of the base ring and the algebra.

Every hypothesis of the source is present and no others: `R` is local, `R → S` is flat of finite
presentation with geometrically integral fibres, `q` lies over the maximal ideal, `N` is a finite
`S`-module and `alpha` becomes an isomorphism over the residue field of `𝔪S`. Projectivity of
`S` over `R`, which the source invokes to run the argument, is Stacks 05FT
(`Algebra.projective_of_geometricallyIntegral_fibres`) applied to the geometrically integral
fibres.
declarations.statement:
public theorem flat_localizedModule_tfae
    (R : Type u) (S : Type u) [CommRing R] [CommRing S] [IsLocalRing R] [Algebra R S]
    [Algebra.FinitePresentation R S] [Module.Flat R S]
    [AlgebraicGeometry.GeometricallyIntegral
      (AlgebraicGeometry.Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap R S)))]
    [(Algebra.closedFiberIdeal R S).IsPrime]
    (q : Ideal S) [q.IsPrime]
    (hq : q.comap (algebraMap R S) = IsLocalRing.maximalIdeal R)
    (N : Type w) [AddCommGroup N] [Module S N] [Module R N] [IsScalarTower R S N]
    [Module.Finite S N]
    (r : ℕ) (alpha : (Fin r → S) →ₗ[S] N)
    (halpha : Function.Bijective (alpha.rTensor (Algebra.closedFiberIdeal R S).ResidueField)) :
    List.TFAE [
      Module.Flat R (LocalizedModule q.primeCompl N),
      Stacks.UniversalInjectivity.LocalizationCriteria.UniversallyInjective.{max u w}
        (alpha.restrictScalars R) ∧
        Module.Flat R (LocalizedModule q.primeCompl (N ⧸ LinearMap.range alpha)),
      Function.Injective alpha ∧
        Module.Flat R (LocalizedModule q.primeCompl (N ⧸ LinearMap.range alpha)),
      Function.Bijective
          (LocalizedModule.map (Algebra.closedFiberIdeal R S).primeCompl alpha) ∧
        Module.Flat R (LocalizedModule q.primeCompl (N ⧸ LinearMap.range alpha)),
      Function.Injective (LocalizedModule.map q.primeCompl alpha) ∧
        Module.Flat R (LocalizedModule q.primeCompl (N ⧸ LinearMap.range alpha))]
declarations.comment: the five equivalent conditions

declarations.name: Module.CompleteDevissageAt.finitePresentation_free_linearEquiv_directSum_of_flat
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 05I4.** Let `(R, 𝔪)` be a local ring, let `R → S` be a ring map of
finite presentation, let `N` be a finite `S`-module and let `q` be a prime of `S` lying over `𝔪`.
Assume that `N_q` is flat over `R` and that `D` is a complete dévissage of `N/S/R` at `q`. Then `N`
is a finitely presented `S`-module, free as an `R`-module, and there is an isomorphism of
`R`-modules `N ≅ B₁^{⊕ r₁} ⊕ … ⊕ Bₙ^{⊕ rₙ}`, where `B₁, …, Bₙ` are the lower algebras of `D` and
each `Bᵢ` is a smooth `R`-algebra with geometrically irreducible fibres.
declarations.statement:
public theorem finitePresentation_free_linearEquiv_directSum_of_flat [IsLocalRing R] [Module R N]
    [IsScalarTower R S N] [Algebra.FinitePresentation R S]
    (D : CompleteDevissageAt R S N q) (hq : q.under R = IsLocalRing.maximalIdeal R)
    (hflat : Module.Flat R (LocalizedModule q.primeCompl N)) :
    Module.FinitePresentation S N ∧ Module.Free R N ∧
      (∀ i : Fin D.length, Algebra.Smooth R (D.lowerAlgebra i) ∧
        GeometricallyIrreducible
          (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap R (D.lowerAlgebra i))))) ∧
      Nonempty (N ≃ₗ[R] ⨁ i : Fin D.length, (Fin (D.multiplicity i) →₀ D.lowerAlgebra i))

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.existsElementaryEtaleNeighborhoodFinitePresentationFlatOver
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 05I5.** For `f` locally of finite presentation and `F` quasi-coherent of
finite type and flat over `S` at `x`, there is an elementary étale neighbourhood `(S', s')` of
`(S, f x)` and an open subscheme of `X ×_S Spec 𝒪_{S', s'}` containing the unique point over `x`
on which the pullback of `F` is of finite presentation and flat over `𝒪_{S', s'}`.

Here `U` is the elementary étale neighbourhood `(S', s')`, the base change is along the composite
`Spec 𝒪_{S', s'} ⟶ S' ⟶ S`, `V` is the open subscheme and `v` the point of `V` over `x`; the
first clause says that `v` is the only point of `X ×_S Spec 𝒪_{S', s'}` over `x`. Its type is
the body of `AlgebraicGeometry.ExistsElementaryEtaleNeighborhoodFinitePresentationFlatOver`,
written out.

The pointwise form above composed with
`AlgebraicGeometry.ExistsElementaryEtaleNeighborhoodFinitePresentationFlatOver.of_mem`, which
supplies the uniqueness of the point over `x`.
declarations.statement:
theorem existsElementaryEtaleNeighborhoodFinitePresentationFlatOver
    {X S : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ S) [LocallyOfFinitePresentation f] (F : X.Modules)
    [F.IsQuasicoherent] [F.IsFiniteType] (x : X)
    (hflat : IsFlatOverAt f.toLRSHom.toShHom F x) :
    ∃ (U : EtaleNeighborhood S (f x)) (_ : U.IsElementary)
      (V : (pullback f (U.scheme.fromSpecStalk U.point ≫ U.toBase)).Opens) (v : V),
      (pullback.fst f (U.scheme.fromSpecStalk U.point ≫ U.toBase) ⁻¹' {x} = {V.ι v}) ∧
      ((Scheme.Modules.pullback
        (V.ι ≫ pullback.fst f (U.scheme.fromSpecStalk U.point ≫ U.toBase))).obj
          F).IsFinitePresentation ∧
      IsFlatOver
        (LocallyRingedSpace.forgetToSheafedSpace.map
          (V.ι ≫ pullback.snd f (U.scheme.fromSpecStalk U.point ≫ U.toBase)).toLRSHom)
        ((Scheme.Modules.pullback
          (V.ι ≫ pullback.fst f (U.scheme.fromSpecStalk U.point ≫ U.toBase))).obj F)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.exists_elementaryEtaleNeighborhood_flat_finitePresentation
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 05I6.** Let `X` be locally of finite type over `S` and let `x ∈ X` be a
point at which `X` is flat over `S`. Then there is an elementary étale neighbourhood `(S', s')`
of `(S, f x)` and an open subscheme of `X ×_S Spec 𝒪_{S', s'}` containing the unique point over
`x` which is flat and of finite presentation over `Spec 𝒪_{S', s'}`.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_elementaryEtaleNeighborhood_flat_finitePresentation {X S : Scheme.{u}}
    (f : X ⟶ S) [LocallyOfFiniteType f] (x : X) (hflat : IsFlatAt f.toLRSHom.toShHom x) :
    ∃ (U : EtaleNeighborhood S (f x)) (_ : U.IsElementary),
      let b : Spec (U.scheme.presheaf.stalk U.point) ⟶ S :=
        U.scheme.fromSpecStalk U.point ≫ U.toBase
      ∃ (V : (pullback f b).Opens) (v : V),
        (pullback.fst f b ⁻¹' {x} = {V.ι v}) ∧
        Flat (V.ι ≫ pullback.snd f b) ∧
        FinitePresentation (V.ι ≫ pullback.snd f b)

declarations.name: Stacks.Flatness.finitePresentation_stalk_of_isFlatOverAt
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 05I7, from Stacks Project, Tag 05I5.** Let `f : X ⟶ S` be locally of
finite presentation and let `F` be a finite type quasi-coherent `𝒪_X`-module. If `F` is flat over
`S` at `x`, then the stalk `F_x` is a finitely presented `𝒪_{X,x}`-module.

Stacks 05I5 is `AlgebraicGeometry.existsElementaryEtaleNeighborhoodFinitePresentationFlatOver`.
The neighbourhood it produces maps to `X` by a flat morphism, the pullback of `F` to it is
finitely presented, so its stalk is finitely presented
(`Stacks.StalkFiniteType.finitePresentation_stalk`), and finite presentation descends along the
flat local homomorphism of local rings that the stalk map is
(`Stacks.StalkFiniteType.finitePresentation_stalk_of_flat`).
declarations.statement:
theorem finitePresentation_stalk_of_isFlatOverAt
    {X S : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ S) [LocallyOfFinitePresentation f] (F : X.Modules)
    [F.IsQuasicoherent] [F.IsFiniteType] (x : X)
    (hflat : IsFlatOverAt f.toLRSHom.toShHom F x) :
    Module.FinitePresentation (ToType (X.presheaf.stalk x))
      (ToType (TopCat.Presheaf.stalk F.val.presheaf x))

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.isEssentiallyOfFinitePresentation_stalkMap_of_flatAt
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 05I8.** If `f : X ⟶ S` is locally of finite type and flat at `x`, then
the local ring `𝒪_{X,x}` is essentially of finite presentation over `𝒪_{S,f x}`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isEssentiallyOfFinitePresentation_stalkMap_of_flatAt
    {X S : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ S) [LocallyOfFiniteType f]
    (x : X) (hflat : AlgebraicGeometry.IsFlatAt f.toLRSHom.toShHom x) :
    IsEssentiallyOfFinitePresentation
      (S.presheaf.stalk (f x)) (X.presheaf.stalk x) (f.stalkMap x).hom

declarations.name: Module.exists_freeMap_bijective_residueField
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 05IA, the existence assertion.** Let `R → S` be flat with a
geometrically integral fibre over the prime `r`, and let `N` be a finite `S`-module. Then the
extension `𝔭 = rS` is prime and some map from a finite free `S`-module to `N` becomes an
isomorphism after base change to the residue field `κ(𝔭)`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem Module.exists_freeMap_bijective_residueField {R S N : Type u} [CommRing R]
    [CommRing S] [Algebra R S] [Module.Flat R S] {r : Ideal R} [r.IsPrime] [AddCommGroup N]
    [Module S N] [Module.Finite S N]
    (hgeom : Algebra.IsGeometricallyIntegral r.ResidueField (r.Fiber S)) :
    ∃ (n : ℕ) (a : (Fin n → S) →ₗ[S] N),
      ∃ hp : (r.map (algebraMap R S)).IsPrime,
        Function.Bijective
          (a.rTensor (@Ideal.ResidueField S _ (r.map (algebraMap R S)) hp))
declarations.comment: existence

declarations.name: Module.universallyInjective_localizedMap_of_flat_localizedModule
declarations.doc:
Let `R → S` be a flat ring map of finite presentation with geometrically integral fibres,
let `q ⊆ S` be a prime lying over `r = q ∩ R`, write `p = rS` for the generic point of the fibre
over `r`, let `N` be a finite `S`-module and let `alpha : S^{⊕ n} → N` become injective over
`κ(p)`. If `N_q` is flat over `R` then `alpha_r : S_r^{⊕ n} → N_r` is universally injective as a
map of `R`-modules.
declarations.statement:
public theorem Module.universallyInjective_localizedMap_of_flat_localizedModule
    (R S : Type u) [CommRing R] [CommRing S] [Algebra R S]
    [Algebra.FinitePresentation R S] [Module.Flat R S]
    [GeometricallyIntegral (Spec.map (ofHom (algebraMap R S)))]
    (q : Ideal S) [q.IsPrime]
    (N : Type w) [AddCommGroup N] [Module S N] [Module R N] [IsScalarTower R S N]
    [Module.Finite S N] (n : ℕ) (alpha : (Fin n → S) →ₗ[S] N)
    (halpha : letI := Ideal.isPrime_map_of_geometricallyIntegral R S (q.under R)
      Function.Injective (alpha.rTensor
        (Ideal.map (algebraMap R S) (q.under R)).ResidueField))
    (hflat : Module.Flat R (LocalizedModule q.primeCompl N))
    (Q : Type (max u w)) [AddCommGroup Q] [Module R Q] :
    Function.Injective (((LocalizedModule.map (q.under R).primeCompl
      (alpha.restrictScalars R)).restrictScalars R).rTensor Q)
declarations.comment: the implication (1) ⟹ (3), the universal injectivity of `α_𝔯` over `R_𝔯`

declarations.name: Module.exists_universallyInjective_localizedModule_away_of_flat_localizedModule
declarations.doc:
In the situation of `Module.universallyInjective_localizedMap_of_flat_localizedModule`, with
`N` finitely presented and `alpha` an isomorphism over `κ(p)`, there is an `f ∈ R`, `f ∉ r`, such
that `alpha_f : S_f^{⊕ n} → N_f` is universally injective as a map of `R`-modules.
declarations.statement:
public theorem Module.exists_universallyInjective_localizedModule_away_of_flat_localizedModule
    (R S : Type u) [CommRing R] [CommRing S] [Algebra R S]
    [Algebra.FinitePresentation R S] [Module.Flat R S]
    [GeometricallyIntegral (Spec.map (ofHom (algebraMap R S)))]
    (r : Ideal R) [r.IsPrime] (q : Ideal S) [q.IsPrime] (hq : q.under R = r)
    (N : Type u) [AddCommGroup N] [Module S N] [Module R N] [IsScalarTower R S N]
    [Module.FinitePresentation S N] (n : ℕ) (alpha : (Fin n → S) →ₗ[S] N)
    (halpha : letI := Ideal.isPrime_map_of_geometricallyIntegral R S r
      Function.Bijective (alpha.rTensor (Ideal.map (algebraMap R S) r).ResidueField))
    (hflat : Module.Flat R (LocalizedModule q.primeCompl N)) :
    ∃ f ∈ r.primeCompl, ∀ (Q : Type u) [AddCommGroup Q] [Module R Q],
        Function.Injective (((LocalizedModule.map (Submonoid.powers f)
          (alpha.restrictScalars R)).restrictScalars R).rTensor Q)
declarations.comment: the first half of the implication (1) ⟹ (2), the universal injectivity of `α_f`

declarations.name: Module.flat_localizedModule_coker_of_flat_localizedModule
declarations.doc:
In the situation of `Module.universallyInjective_localizedMap_of_flat_localizedModule` the
localization of `Coker(alpha)` at `q` is flat over `R`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem Module.flat_localizedModule_coker_of_flat_localizedModule
    (R S : Type u) [CommRing R] [CommRing S] [Algebra R S]
    [Algebra.FinitePresentation R S] [Module.Flat R S]
    [GeometricallyIntegral (Spec.map (ofHom (algebraMap R S)))]
    (q : Ideal S) [q.IsPrime]
    (N : Type u) [AddCommGroup N] [Module S N] [Module R N] [IsScalarTower R S N]
    [Module.Finite S N] (n : ℕ) (alpha : (Fin n → S) →ₗ[S] N)
    (halpha : letI := Ideal.isPrime_map_of_geometricallyIntegral R S (q.under R)
      Function.Injective (alpha.rTensor
        (Ideal.map (algebraMap R S) (q.under R)).ResidueField))
    (hflat : Module.Flat R (LocalizedModule q.primeCompl N)) :
    Module.Flat R (LocalizedModule q.primeCompl (N ⧸ LinearMap.range alpha))
declarations.comment: the flatness of `Coker(α)_𝔮`, the second half of conditions (3) to (6)

declarations.name: Module.exists_universallyInjective_and_flat_coker_of_flat_localizedModule
declarations.doc:
Let `R → S` be a flat ring map of finite presentation with geometrically integral fibres,
let `q ⊆ S` be a prime lying over `r = q ∩ R`, write `p = rS`, let `N` be a finitely presented
`S`-module and let `alpha : S^{⊕ n} → N` be an isomorphism over `κ(p)`. If `N_q` is flat over `R`
then there are an `f ∈ R`, `f ∉ r`, such that `alpha_f` is universally injective as a map of
`R`-modules, and a `g ∈ S`, `g ∉ q`, such that `Coker(alpha)_g` is flat over `R`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem Module.exists_universallyInjective_and_flat_coker_of_flat_localizedModule
    (R S : Type u) [CommRing R] [CommRing S] [Algebra R S]
    [Algebra.FinitePresentation R S] [Module.Flat R S]
    [GeometricallyIntegral (Spec.map (ofHom (algebraMap R S)))]
    (q : Ideal S) [q.IsPrime]
    (N : Type u) [AddCommGroup N] [Module S N] [Module R N] [IsScalarTower R S N]
    [Module.FinitePresentation S N] (n : ℕ) (alpha : (Fin n → S) →ₗ[S] N)
    (halpha : letI := Ideal.isPrime_map_of_geometricallyIntegral R S (q.under R)
      Function.Bijective (alpha.rTensor
        (Ideal.map (algebraMap R S) (q.under R)).ResidueField))
    (hflat : Module.Flat R (LocalizedModule q.primeCompl N)) :
    (∃ f ∈ (q.under R).primeCompl, ∀ (Q : Type u) [AddCommGroup Q] [Module R Q],
        Function.Injective (((LocalizedModule.map (Submonoid.powers f)
          (alpha.restrictScalars R)).restrictScalars R).rTensor Q)) ∧
      ∃ g ∈ q.primeCompl, Module.Flat R (LocalizedModule.Away g (N ⧸ LinearMap.range alpha))
declarations.comment: the implication (1) ⟹ (2)

declarations.name: Module.universallyInjective_localizedMap_and_flat_coker_of_exists_away
declarations.doc:
If `alpha_f` is universally injective as a map of `R`-modules for some `f ∈ R`, `f ∉ r`, and
`Coker(alpha)_g` is `R`-flat for some `g ∈ S`, `g ∉ q`, then `alpha_r` is universally injective
as a map of `R`-modules and `Coker(alpha)_q` is `R`-flat. The prime `q` need not lie over `r`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem Module.universallyInjective_localizedMap_and_flat_coker_of_exists_away
    (R S : Type u) [CommRing R] [CommRing S] [Algebra R S] (r : Ideal R) [r.IsPrime]
    (q : Ideal S) [q.IsPrime]
    (N : Type w) [AddCommGroup N] [Module S N] [Module R N] [IsScalarTower R S N] (n : ℕ)
    (alpha : (Fin n → S) →ₗ[S] N)
    (h : (∃ f ∈ r.primeCompl, UniversallyInjective.{max u w} (A := R)
            ((LocalizedModule.map (Submonoid.powers f)
              (alpha.restrictScalars R)).restrictScalars R)) ∧
      ∃ g ∈ q.primeCompl,
        Module.Flat R (LocalizedModule.Away g (N ⧸ LinearMap.range alpha))) :
    UniversallyInjective.{max u w} (A := R)
        ((LocalizedModule.map r.primeCompl (alpha.restrictScalars R)).restrictScalars R) ∧
      Module.Flat R (LocalizedModule q.primeCompl (N ⧸ LinearMap.range alpha))
declarations.comment: the implication (2) ⟹ (3)

declarations.name: Module.injective_localizedMap_of_universallyInjective_localizedMap
declarations.doc: If `alpha_r` is universally injective as a map of `R`-modules then it is injective.
declarations.statement:
public theorem Module.injective_localizedMap_of_universallyInjective_localizedMap
    (R S : Type u) [CommRing R] [CommRing S] [Algebra R S] (r : Ideal R) [r.IsPrime]
    (N : Type w) [AddCommGroup N] [Module S N] [Module R N] [IsScalarTower R S N] (n : ℕ)
    (alpha : (Fin n → S) →ₗ[S] N)
    (h : UniversallyInjective.{max u w} (A := R)
      ((LocalizedModule.map r.primeCompl (alpha.restrictScalars R)).restrictScalars R)) :
    Function.Injective (LocalizedModule.map r.primeCompl (alpha.restrictScalars R))
declarations.comment: the implication (3) ⟹ (4), the injectivity of `α_𝔯`

declarations.name: Module.bijective_localizedMap_map_of_injective_localizedMap
declarations.doc:
If `alpha` is surjective over `κ(p)` and `alpha_r` is injective, then `alpha_p` is an
isomorphism at the generic point `p = rS` of the fibre over `r`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem Module.bijective_localizedMap_map_of_injective_localizedMap (R S : Type u)
    [CommRing R] [CommRing S] [Algebra R S] [Algebra.FinitePresentation R S] [Module.Flat R S]
    [GeometricallyIntegral (Spec.map (ofHom (algebraMap R S)))] (r : Ideal R) [r.IsPrime]
    (N : Type w) [AddCommGroup N] [Module S N] [Module R N] [IsScalarTower R S N]
    [Module.Finite S N] (n : ℕ) (alpha : (Fin n → S) →ₗ[S] N)
    (halpha : letI := Ideal.isPrime_map_of_geometricallyIntegral R S r
      Function.Surjective (alpha.rTensor (Ideal.map (algebraMap R S) r).ResidueField))
    (hinj : Function.Injective (LocalizedModule.map r.primeCompl (alpha.restrictScalars R))) :
    letI := Ideal.isPrime_map_of_geometricallyIntegral R S r
    Function.Bijective
      (LocalizedModule.map (Ideal.map (algebraMap R S) r).primeCompl alpha)
declarations.comment: the implication (4) ⟹ (5), the isomorphism `α_𝔭`

declarations.name: Module.injective_localizedMap_atPrime_of_bijective_localizedMap_map
declarations.doc:
If `alpha_p` is an isomorphism at the generic point `p = rS` of the fibre over `r` then
`alpha_q` is injective at every prime `q` of `S` lying over `r`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem Module.injective_localizedMap_atPrime_of_bijective_localizedMap_map (R S : Type u)
    [CommRing R] [CommRing S] [Algebra R S] [Algebra.FinitePresentation R S] [Module.Flat R S]
    [GeometricallyIntegral (Spec.map (ofHom (algebraMap R S)))] (r : Ideal R) [r.IsPrime]
    (q : Ideal S) [q.IsPrime] (hq : q.under R = r)
    (N : Type w) [AddCommGroup N] [Module S N] (n : ℕ) (alpha : (Fin n → S) →ₗ[S] N)
    (hbij : letI := Ideal.isPrime_map_of_geometricallyIntegral R S r
      Function.Bijective (LocalizedModule.map (Ideal.map (algebraMap R S) r).primeCompl alpha)) :
    Function.Injective (LocalizedModule.map q.primeCompl alpha)
declarations.comment: the implication (5) ⟹ (6), the injectivity of `α_𝔮`

declarations.name: Module.flat_localizedModule_of_injective_localizedMap_of_flat_coker
declarations.doc:
For `S` flat over `R`, if `alpha_q` is injective and `Coker(alpha)_q` is `R`-flat then `N_q`
is `R`-flat.
declarations.statement:
public theorem Module.flat_localizedModule_of_injective_localizedMap_of_flat_coker (R S : Type u)
    [CommRing R] [CommRing S] [Algebra R S] [Module.Flat R S] (q : Ideal S) [q.IsPrime]
    (N : Type w) [AddCommGroup N] [Module S N] [Module R N] [IsScalarTower R S N] (n : ℕ)
    (alpha : (Fin n → S) →ₗ[S] N)
    (hinj : Function.Injective (LocalizedModule.map q.primeCompl alpha))
    (hC : Module.Flat R (LocalizedModule q.primeCompl (N ⧸ LinearMap.range alpha))) :
    Module.Flat R (LocalizedModule q.primeCompl N)
declarations.comment: the implication (6) ⟹ (1)

declarations.name: Module.flat_localizedModule_freeMap_tfae
declarations.statement:
public theorem Module.flat_localizedModule_freeMap_tfae (R S : Type u) [CommRing R] [CommRing S]
    [Algebra R S] [Algebra.FinitePresentation R S] [Module.Flat R S]
    [GeometricallyIntegral (Spec.map (ofHom (algebraMap R S)))] (r : Ideal R) [r.IsPrime]
    (q : Ideal S) [q.IsPrime] (hq : q.under R = r)
    (N : Type u) [AddCommGroup N] [Module S N] [Module R N] [IsScalarTower R S N]
    [Module.FinitePresentation S N] (n : ℕ) (alpha : (Fin n → S) →ₗ[S] N)
    (halpha : letI := Ideal.isPrime_map_of_geometricallyIntegral R S r
      Function.Bijective (alpha.rTensor (Ideal.map (algebraMap R S) r).ResidueField)) :
    letI := Ideal.isPrime_map_of_geometricallyIntegral R S r
    List.TFAE [
      Module.Flat R (LocalizedModule q.primeCompl N),
      (∃ f ∈ r.primeCompl, UniversallyInjective.{u} (A := R)
            ((LocalizedModule.map (Submonoid.powers f)
              (alpha.restrictScalars R)).restrictScalars R)) ∧
        ∃ g ∈ q.primeCompl,
          Module.Flat R (LocalizedModule.Away g (N ⧸ LinearMap.range alpha)),
      UniversallyInjective.{u} (A := R)
          ((LocalizedModule.map r.primeCompl (alpha.restrictScalars R)).restrictScalars R) ∧
        Module.Flat R (LocalizedModule q.primeCompl (N ⧸ LinearMap.range alpha)),
      Function.Injective (LocalizedModule.map r.primeCompl (alpha.restrictScalars R)) ∧
        Module.Flat R (LocalizedModule q.primeCompl (N ⧸ LinearMap.range alpha)),
      Function.Bijective (LocalizedModule.map (Ideal.map (algebraMap R S) r).primeCompl alpha) ∧
        Module.Flat R (LocalizedModule q.primeCompl (N ⧸ LinearMap.range alpha)),
      Function.Injective (LocalizedModule.map q.primeCompl alpha) ∧
        Module.Flat R (LocalizedModule q.primeCompl (N ⧸ LinearMap.range alpha))]
declarations.comment: the equivalence of the six conditions

declarations.name: Module.CompleteDevissage.exists_away_decomposition_projective
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 05IB.** Let `N` be a finitely presented module over a finitely
presented `R`-algebra `S` which is flat over `R`, and let `N/S/R` admit a complete dévissage over
a prime `r` of `R`. Then there is an `a ∈ R` outside `r` such that, over `R_a`, the stage algebras
of the dévissage stay smooth with geometrically irreducible fibres, the module `N_a` is the direct
sum of the finite free modules `(Bᵢ)_a^{⊕ rᵢ}` over them, and `N_a` is projective.

One and the same `a` does all of this: it is the element of
`Module.CompleteDevissage.exists_away_injective_alpha`, after inverting which the away-localized
dévissage (`Module.CompleteDevissage.localizeAwayCanonical`) has injective stage maps, so that
`Module.CompleteDevissage.nonempty_linearEquiv_directSum` gives the decomposition and
`Module.CompleteDevissage.projective_of_injective_alpha` the projectivity, the lower algebras
being projective over the new base by Stacks 05FT
(`Module.CompleteDevissage.projective_lowerAlgebra`). The smoothness and the fibres are the fields
of the away-localized dévissage.
declarations.statement:
public theorem exists_away_decomposition_projective (D : CompleteDevissage R S N r) :
    ∃ a ∈ r.primeCompl,
      (∀ i, Algebra.Smooth (Localization.Away a) (D.locAwayB a i)) ∧
      (∀ i, GeometricallyIrreducible
        (Spec.map (ofHom (algebraMap (Localization.Away a) (D.locAwayB a i))))) ∧
      Nonempty (LocalizedModule (Submonoid.powers a) N ≃ₗ[Localization.Away a]
        ⨁ i : Fin (D.stepCount + 1), (Fin (D.multiplicity i) →₀ D.locAwayB a i)) ∧
      Module.Projective (Localization.Away a) (LocalizedModule (Submonoid.powers a) N)
declarations.comment: the decomposition and projectivity, over a general base

declarations.name: Module.CompleteDevissage.nonempty_linearEquiv_directSum_of_flat
declarations.doc:
**The decomposition over a local base.** Let `R` be a local ring, let `N` be a finite
`S`-module flat over `R` and let `N/S/R` have a complete dévissage over the maximal ideal of `R`.
Then `N` is, as an `R`-module, the direct sum of the finite free modules `Bᵢ^{⊕ rᵢ}` over the
smooth stage algebras of the dévissage.
declarations.statement:
public theorem nonempty_linearEquiv_directSum_of_flat [IsLocalRing R] [Module.Flat R N]
    (D : CompleteDevissage R S N r) (hr : r = IsLocalRing.maximalIdeal R) :
    Nonempty (N ≃ₗ[R] ⨁ i : Fin (D.stepCount + 1), (Fin (D.multiplicity i) →₀ D.B i))
declarations.comment: the decomposition, over a local base

declarations.name: Module.CompleteDevissage.projective_of_flat
declarations.doc:
**Projectivity over a local base.** In the situation of
`Module.CompleteDevissage.nonempty_linearEquiv_directSum_of_flat` the module `N` is projective
over `R`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem projective_of_flat [IsLocalRing R] [Module.Flat R N]
    (D : CompleteDevissage R S N r) (hr : r = IsLocalRing.maximalIdeal R) :
    Module.Projective R N
declarations.comment: projectivity over a local base

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.exists_elementaryEtaleNeighborhood_projective_sections_of_isFlatOverAt
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 05ID.** A finitely presented quasi-coherent module which is flat over
the base at a point has projective global sections after compatible affine elementary étale
localization of the source and of the base.

Openness of the flat locus (Tag 0399) replaces `X` by the open subscheme on which `F` is flat over
`S`; Proposition 05HR and Remark 05I0 then produce an affine elementary étale square carrying a
complete dévissage of the global sections at the prime of the distinguished point, and Lemma 05IB
over a general base makes those sections projective after inverting a global function on the new
base which does not vanish at the distinguished point. Shrinking the square to the basic opens of
that function and of its pullback gives the square of the conclusion.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_elementaryEtaleNeighborhood_projective_sections_of_isFlatOverAt
    {X S : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ S) (F : X.Modules) (x : X)
    [LocallyOfFinitePresentation f] [F.IsQuasicoherent] [F.IsFinitePresentation]
    (hflat : IsFlatOverAt f.toLRSHom.toShHom F x) :
    ∃ (V : EtaleNeighborhood S (f x))
      (U : EtaleNeighborhood X x) (h : U.scheme ⟶ V.scheme),
      V.IsElementary ∧ U.IsElementary ∧
        (h ≫ V.toBase = U.toBase ≫ f) ∧ (h U.point = V.point) ∧
        IsAffine U.scheme ∧ IsAffine V.scheme ∧
        (let M := (Scheme.Modules.pullback U.toBase).obj F
         letI : Module Γ(V.scheme, ⊤) Γ(M, ⊤) :=
           Module.compHom Γ(M, ⊤) h.appTop.hom
         Module.Projective Γ(V.scheme, ⊤) Γ(M, ⊤))
declarations.comment: exactly the source's hypotheses and full conclusion, unconditional: 0399, 05HR with 05I0 and 05IB are proved in the library, not assumed

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.exists_elementaryEtaleNeighborhood_projective_structureSheafSections
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 05IE.** Let `f : X ⟶ S` be locally of finite presentation and let
`x : X`. If `f` is flat at `x` over `S`, then there is a commutative square of pointed schemes
```
  (X, x) ←ᵍ (X', x')
    ↓          ↓
  (S, s) ← (S', s')
```
whose horizontal arrows are elementary étale neighbourhoods, with `X'` and `S'` affine, such that
`Γ(X', 𝒪_{X'})` is a projective `Γ(S', 𝒪_{S'})`-module.

This is the case `ℱ = 𝒪_X` of Tag 05ID, as in the source. The flatness hypothesis is converted
from the morphism to the structure sheaf by
`AlgebraicGeometry.isFlatOverAt_unit_iff_isFlatAt`, and the conclusion is converted back from
`Γ(X', g^*𝒪_X)` to `Γ(X', 𝒪_{X'})` by
`AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.Modules.pullbackUnitSectionsLinearEquiv`; the finite presentation of
`𝒪_X` as a module, which Tag 05ID requires of `ℱ`, is
`AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.unitModule_isFinitePresentation`.

The hypothesis `hdev` is the hypothesis of the conditional reduction of Tag 05ID,
`AlgebraicGeometry.exists_elementaryEtaleNeighborhood_projective_sections`, instantiated at
the structure sheaf: Proposition 05HR composed with Remark 05I0, carrying the injectivity of the
maps `α i` of Lemma 05IA. Nothing is assumed beyond it — in particular no Noetherian hypothesis,
which Tag 05IE does not have. The form without `hdev` is
`exists_elementaryEtaleNeighborhood_projective_structureSheafSections_of_isFlatAt`.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_elementaryEtaleNeighborhood_projective_structureSheafSections
    {X S : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ S) (x : X) [LocallyOfFinitePresentation f]
    (hflat : IsFlatAt (LocallyRingedSpace.forgetToSheafedSpace.map f.toLRSHom) x)
    (hdev : IsFlatOverAt (LocallyRingedSpace.forgetToSheafedSpace.map f.toLRSHom)
        (Scheme.unitModule X) x →
      ∃ (V : EtaleNeighborhood S (f x)) (U : EtaleNeighborhood X x) (h : U.scheme ⟶ V.scheme)
        (_ : V.IsElementary) (_ : U.IsElementary)
        (hover : h ≫ V.toBase = U.toBase ≫ f) (_ : h U.point = V.point)
        (_ : IsAffine U.scheme) (_ : IsAffine V.scheme)
        (r : Ideal Γ(V.scheme, ⊤)) (_ : r.IsPrime),
        letI : (Scheme.unitModule X).IsFiniteType :=
          SheafOfModules.instIsFiniteTypeOfIsFinitePresentation (Scheme.unitModule X)
        letI : Algebra Γ(V.scheme, ⊤) Γ(U.scheme, ⊤) := h.appTop.hom.toAlgebra
        letI : Algebra.FinitePresentation Γ(V.scheme, ⊤) Γ(U.scheme, ⊤) :=
          EtaleNeighborhood.algebraFinitePresentation_globalSections f V U h hover
        letI : Module Γ(V.scheme, ⊤)
            Γ((Scheme.Modules.pullback U.toBase).obj (Scheme.unitModule X), ⊤) :=
          Module.compHom _ h.appTop.hom
        letI : Module.Finite Γ(U.scheme, ⊤)
            Γ((Scheme.Modules.pullback U.toBase).obj (Scheme.unitModule X), ⊤) :=
          EtaleNeighborhood.moduleFinite_pullback_globalSections (Scheme.unitModule X) U
        letI : IsScalarTower Γ(V.scheme, ⊤) Γ(U.scheme, ⊤)
            Γ((Scheme.Modules.pullback U.toBase).obj (Scheme.unitModule X), ⊤) :=
          IsScalarTower.of_algebraMap_smul fun _ _ => rfl
        ∃ D : Module.CompleteDevissage Γ(V.scheme, ⊤) Γ(U.scheme, ⊤)
            Γ((Scheme.Modules.pullback U.toBase).obj (Scheme.unitModule X), ⊤) r,
          ∀ i, letI : Module (D.B i) (D.M i) :=
              Module.compHom (D.M i) (D.toLeft i).toRingHom
            Function.Injective (D.alpha i)) :
    ∃ (V : EtaleNeighborhood S (f x)) (U : EtaleNeighborhood X x) (h : U.scheme ⟶ V.scheme),
      V.IsElementary ∧ U.IsElementary ∧
        (h ≫ V.toBase = U.toBase ≫ f) ∧ (h U.point = V.point) ∧
        IsAffine U.scheme ∧ IsAffine V.scheme ∧
        (letI : Module Γ(V.scheme, ⊤) Γ(U.scheme, ⊤) :=
           Module.compHom Γ(U.scheme, ⊤) h.appTop.hom
         Module.Projective Γ(V.scheme, ⊤) Γ(U.scheme, ⊤))
declarations.comment: the full conclusion; assumes only `hdev` of Tag 05ID at the structure sheaf

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.exists_elementaryEtaleNeighborhood_projective_structureSheafSections_of_isFlatAt
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 05IE.** Let `f : X ⟶ S` be locally of finite presentation and let
`x : X`. If `f` is flat at `x` over `S`, then there is a commutative square of pointed schemes
```
  (X, x) ←ᵍ (X', x')
    ↓          ↓
  (S, s) ← (S', s')
```
whose horizontal arrows are elementary étale neighbourhoods, with `X'` and `S'` affine, such that
`Γ(X', 𝒪_{X'})` is a projective `Γ(S', 𝒪_{S'})`-module.

This is the case `ℱ = 𝒪_X` of Tag 05ID, as in the source, whose proof of Tag 05IE is the single
sentence "This is a special case of Proposition 05ID". The specialisation needs the three
identifications of the module docstring: `AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.unitModule X` is quasi-coherent
and, by `AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.unitModule_isFinitePresentation`, of finite presentation, so Tag
05ID applies to it; `AlgebraicGeometry.isFlatOverAt_unit_iff_isFlatAt` turns flatness of the
morphism at `x` into flatness of the structure sheaf over the base at `x`; and
`AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.Modules.pullbackUnitSectionsLinearEquiv` identifies `Γ(X', g^*𝒪_X)` with
`Γ(X', 𝒪_{X'})`, compatibly with the restriction of scalars along
`Γ(S', 𝒪_{S'}) ⟶ Γ(X', 𝒪_{X'})` that both sides carry.

Unlike
`AlgebraicGeometry.exists_elementaryEtaleNeighborhood_projective_structureSheafSections`, this
carries no hypothesis beyond the source's: the unconditional form of Tag 05ID,
`AlgebraicGeometry.exists_elementaryEtaleNeighborhood_projective_sections_of_isFlatOverAt`, is
used in place of the conditional
`AlgebraicGeometry.exists_elementaryEtaleNeighborhood_projective_sections`, so there is nothing
left to assume.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_elementaryEtaleNeighborhood_projective_structureSheafSections_of_isFlatAt
    {X S : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ S) (x : X) [LocallyOfFinitePresentation f]
    (hflat : IsFlatAt f.toLRSHom.toShHom x) :
    ∃ (V : EtaleNeighborhood S (f x)) (U : EtaleNeighborhood X x) (h : U.scheme ⟶ V.scheme),
      V.IsElementary ∧ U.IsElementary ∧
        (h ≫ V.toBase = U.toBase ≫ f) ∧ (h U.point = V.point) ∧
        IsAffine U.scheme ∧ IsAffine V.scheme ∧
        (letI : Module Γ(V.scheme, ⊤) Γ(U.scheme, ⊤) :=
           Module.compHom Γ(U.scheme, ⊤) h.appTop.hom
         Module.Projective Γ(V.scheme, ⊤) Γ(U.scheme, ⊤))

declarations.name: Stacks.WeaklyAssociatedPrimes.isWeaklyAssociatedPrime_and_isAssociatedPrimeStacks_fibre_of_tensorProduct
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 05IG], the implication `⟹`.**  Let `R → S` be a ring map of finite
presentation, let `N` be an `S`-module of finite presentation which is flat as an `R`-module, let
`M` be an `R`-module, and let `𝔮` be a prime of `S` lying over a prime `𝔭` of `R` which is
finitely generated.  If `𝔮` is *weakly* associated to `N ⊗_R M` over `S`, then `𝔭` is *weakly*
associated to `M` over `R` and `𝔮-bar` is an *associated* prime, in the strict sense of
[Stacks, Tag 00LA], of `N-bar` over the fibre ring `S-bar`.

Finite generation of `𝔭` enters the base clause only.  It stands in for the étale-local
structure theorem [Stacks, Tag 05ID], which the source uses to make `N` projective over the base
and which this library has only in scheme-theoretic form;  see the module documentation for what
the ring-theoretic form would need.  With `N` projective over a local base the witness lands in a
finite free summand and no prime avoidance is needed, whereas the finiteness-free content
available here (`exists_smul_pow_eq_zero_localizedModule_of_tensorProduct`) only covers `𝔭 R_𝔭`
by the primes weakly associated to `M_𝔭`, and finitely many generators of `𝔭` are what turn
that covering into a single witness.  The variant
`..._of_tensorProduct_of_finite` trades it for finiteness of `WeakAss_R(M)`, and the fibre clause
`isAssociatedPrimeStacks_fibre_of_isWeaklyAssociatedPrime_tensorProduct` is free of both.

The converse implication of the tag is not proved here;  see the module documentation.
declarations.statement:
theorem isWeaklyAssociatedPrime_and_isAssociatedPrimeStacks_fibre_of_tensorProduct
    [Algebra.FinitePresentation R S] [Module.FinitePresentation S N] [Module.Flat R N]
    (q : Ideal S) [q.IsPrime] [q.LiesOver p] (hfg : p.FG)
    (hq : IsWeaklyAssociatedPrime S (N ⊗[R] M) q) :
