    IsWeaklyAssociatedPrime R M p ∧
      IsAssociatedPrimeStacks (Localization (primeComplImage S p) ⧸ fibreIdeal S p)
        ((Localization (primeComplImage S p) ⧸ fibreIdeal S p) ⊗[S] N)
        (Ideal.map (algebraMap S (Localization (primeComplImage S p) ⧸ fibreIdeal S p)) q)
declarations.comment: RESTRICTED: the implication ⟹ only, and its base clause carries the extra hypothesis that 𝔭 is finitely generated, which the tag does not have. That hypothesis stands in for the étale-local structure theorem 05ID, proved only scheme-side here

declarations.name: Stacks.WeaklyAssociatedPrimes.tensorFibreFormula05IG
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 05IG].**  Let `R → S` be a ring map of finite presentation, let `N` be a
finitely presented `S`-module which is flat as an `R`-module, let `M` be an `R`-module and let `𝔮`
be a prime of `S` lying over a prime `𝔭` of `R`.  Then `𝔮` is weakly associated to `N ⊗_R M` if and
only if `𝔭` is weakly associated to `M` and some prime of the fibre ring `S ⊗_R κ(𝔭)` associated —
in the strict sense of [Stacks, Tag 00LA] — to the fibre module contracts to `𝔮`.

Both directions are proved, and no hypothesis beyond the tag's own is used.
declarations.statement: theorem tensorFibreFormula05IG : TensorFibreFormula05IG.{u}

declarations.name: Stacks.Divisors.isWeaklyAssociatedPoint_tensorPullback_iff_of_finiteType
declarations.doc:
Let `S` be a scheme, let `f : X ⟶ S` be locally of finite type, let `x ∈ X`, let `F` be a
quasi-coherent `𝒪_X`-module of finite type and let `G` be a quasi-coherent `𝒪_S`-module. If `F` is
flat at `x` over `S`, then `x` is weakly associated to `F ⊗_{𝒪_X} f^*G` if and only if `f x` is
weakly associated to `G` and `x` is an associated point of the restriction of `F` to the fibre
`X_{f x}`, that is, `x` lies in the relative assassin `Ass_{X/S}(F)`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isWeaklyAssociatedPoint_tensorPullback_iff_of_finiteType
    {X S : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ S) [LocallyOfFiniteType f]
    (F : X.Modules) (G : S.Modules) [F.IsQuasicoherent] [F.IsFiniteType] [G.IsQuasicoherent]
    (x : X) (hF : IsFlatOverAt f.toLRSHom.toShHom F x) :
    IsWeaklyAssociatedPoint
        ((((Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.sheafTensor
                  ⟨((X.toLocallyRingedSpace.toRingedSpace)).presheaf,
                    ((X.toLocallyRingedSpace.toRingedSpace)).IsSheaf⟩).obj (F)).obj
              (((Scheme.Modules.pullback f).obj G)))) x ↔
      (IsWeaklyAssociatedPoint G (f x) ∧ x ∈ relativeAssassin f F)

declarations.name: Stacks.WeaklyAssociatedPrimes.weaklyAssociatedPrimes_tensorProduct_eq_fibrewise_assStacks_of_small
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 05II].** For `R → S` essentially of finite type, `N` a localization of a
finite `S`-module flat over `R` and `M` any `R`-module, the weakly associated primes of
`N ⊗[R] M` are the contractions of the primes of the fibre rings `S ⊗[R] κ(p)` associated to the
fibre modules, over the weakly associated primes `p` of `M`.
declarations.statement:
theorem weaklyAssociatedPrimes_tensorProduct_eq_fibrewise_assStacks_of_small
    (R S : Type u) (M : Type v) (N₀ : Type w) (N : Type x)
    [CommRing R] [CommRing S] [Algebra R S]
    [AddCommGroup M] [Module R M]
    [AddCommGroup N₀] [Module S N₀] [Module.Finite S N₀]
    [AddCommGroup N] [Module S N] [Module R N] [IsScalarTower R S N]
    [Module.Flat R N]
    (hfinite : IsEssentiallyOfFiniteType R S (algebraMap R S))
    (T : Submonoid S) (f : N₀ →ₗ[S] N) [IsLocalizedModule T f] :
    weaklyAssociatedPrimes S (N ⊗[R] M) =
      {q : Ideal S | ∃ p ∈ weaklyAssociatedPrimes R M, ∃ hp : p.IsPrime,
        letI : p.IsPrime := hp
        ∃ q' ∈ assStacks (S ⊗[R] p.ResidueField)
          ((S ⊗[R] p.ResidueField) ⊗[S] N),
          q = Ideal.comap (Algebra.TensorProduct.includeLeft (R := R)
            (S := S) (A := S) (B := p.ResidueField)).toRingHom q'}
declarations.comment: the full set equality; the two rings lie in one universe, as `IsEssentiallyOfFiniteType` requires, and the modules are in arbitrary universes

declarations.name: Stacks.WeaklyAssociatedPrimes.weaklyAssociatedPrimes_tensorProduct_eq_fibrewise_assStacks_of_small'
declarations.doc:
For `M` in the universe of the two rings, the weakly associated primes of `N ⊗[R] M` are the
contractions of the primes of the fibre rings associated to the fibre modules, over the weakly
associated primes of `M`.
declarations.statement:
theorem weaklyAssociatedPrimes_tensorProduct_eq_fibrewise_assStacks_of_small'
    (R S : Type u) (M : Type u) (N₀ : Type w) (N : Type x)
    [CommRing R] [CommRing S] [Algebra R S]
    [AddCommGroup M] [Module R M]
    [AddCommGroup N₀] [Module S N₀] [Module.Finite S N₀]
    [AddCommGroup N] [Module S N] [Module R N] [IsScalarTower R S N]
    [Module.Flat R N]
    (hfinite : IsEssentiallyOfFiniteType R S (algebraMap R S))
    (T : Submonoid S) (f : N₀ →ₗ[S] N) [IsLocalizedModule T f] :
    weaklyAssociatedPrimes S (N ⊗[R] M) =
      {q : Ideal S | ∃ p ∈ weaklyAssociatedPrimes R M, ∃ hp : p.IsPrime,
        letI : p.IsPrime := hp
        ∃ q' ∈ assStacks (S ⊗[R] p.ResidueField)
          ((S ⊗[R] p.ResidueField) ⊗[S] N),
          q = Ideal.comap (Algebra.TensorProduct.includeLeft (R := R)
            (S := S) (A := S) (B := p.ResidueField)).toRingHom q'}
declarations.comment: the full set equality, for a module in the universe of the two rings

declarations.name: Stacks.Divisors.weaklyAssociatedPoints_tensorPullback_eq
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 05IJ].** Let `f : X ⟶ S` be locally of finite type, let `F` be a
quasi-coherent `𝒪_X`-module of finite type which is flat over `S`, and let `G` be a
quasi-coherent `𝒪_S`-module. Then the weakly associated points of `F ⊗_{𝒪_X} f^*G` are exactly
the points of the fibres `X_s`, over the weakly associated points `s` of `G`, that are
associated to the restriction of `F` to `X_s`.

This is the global form of Tag 05IH, and the source's proof of it is the pointwise statement
plus the passage to sets. Both are already in
`StacksFrontier.AlgebraicGeometry.Flatness.WeaklyAssociatedTensorPullbackGlobal`, up to the same
algebraic input that Tag 05IH needed; supplying it here removes the hypothesis.
declarations.statement:
theorem weaklyAssociatedPoints_tensorPullback_eq
    {X S : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ S) [LocallyOfFiniteType f]
    (F : X.Modules) (G : S.Modules)
    [F.IsQuasicoherent] [F.IsFiniteType] [G.IsQuasicoherent]
    (hF : IsFlatOver f.toLRSHom.toShHom F) :
    weaklyAssociatedPoints
        (((Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.sheafTensor
              ⟨(X.toLocallyRingedSpace.toRingedSpace).presheaf,
                (X.toLocallyRingedSpace.toRingedSpace).IsSheaf⟩).obj F).obj
          ((Scheme.Modules.pullback f).obj G)) =
      ⋃ s ∈ weaklyAssociatedPoints G,
        f.fiberι s '' associatedPoints ((Scheme.Modules.pullback (f.fiberι s)).obj F)
declarations.comment: the set equality for f locally of finite type, F quasi-coherent of finite type and flat over S, G quasi-coherent; unconditional

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.isOpen_flatLocus
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 05IK (openness).** The locus where a quasi-coherent module of finite
type is flat over the target of a morphism locally of finite presentation is open, provided the
weakly associated points of the target are locally finite.
declarations.statement:
theorem isOpen_flatLocus
    {X S : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ S) [LocallyOfFinitePresentation f]
    (F : X.Modules) [F.IsQuasicoherent] [F.IsFiniteType]
    (hS : ∀ s : S, ∃ W : S.Opens, s ∈ W ∧
      (schemeWeaklyAssociatedPoints S ∩ (W : Set S)).Finite) :
    IsOpen (flatLocus f F)
declarations.comment: openness of the relative flat locus

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.isFinitePresentation_flatLocus
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 05IK (finite presentation on the flat locus).** For a morphism locally
of finite presentation whose target has locally finite weakly associated points, a quasi-coherent
module of finite type restricts to a module of finite presentation on the open subscheme that is
its relative flat locus.
declarations.statement:
theorem isFinitePresentation_flatLocus
    {X S : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ S) [LocallyOfFinitePresentation f]
    (F : X.Modules) [F.IsQuasicoherent] [F.IsFiniteType]
    (hS : ∀ s : S, ∃ W : S.Opens, s ∈ W ∧
      (schemeWeaklyAssociatedPoints S ∩ (W : Set S)).Finite) :
    letI U : X.Opens := ⟨flatLocus f F, isOpen_flatLocus f F hS⟩
    (F.restrict U.ι).IsFinitePresentation
declarations.comment: finite presentation on the flat locus

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.isFlatOver_flatLocus
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 05IK (flatness on the flat locus).** For a morphism locally of finite
presentation whose target has locally finite weakly associated points, a quasi-coherent module of
finite type restricts to a module flat over the base on the open subscheme that is its relative
flat locus.
declarations.statement:
theorem isFlatOver_flatLocus
    {X S : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ S) [LocallyOfFinitePresentation f]
    (F : X.Modules) [F.IsQuasicoherent] [F.IsFiniteType]
    (hS : ∀ s : S, ∃ W : S.Opens, s ∈ W ∧
      (schemeWeaklyAssociatedPoints S ∩ (W : Set S)).Finite) :
    letI U : X.Opens := ⟨flatLocus f F, isOpen_flatLocus f F hS⟩
    IsFlatOver (U.ι ≫ f).toLRSHom.toShHom (F.restrict U.ι)
declarations.comment: flatness over the base on the flat locus

declarations.name: Stacks.Flatness.isOpen_setOf_flat_localizedModule_atPrime_of_finite_weaklyAssociatedPrimes
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 05IL (openness).** For a ring map `R → S` of finite presentation and a
finite `S`-module `M`, the locus of primes `q` of `S` at which `M_q` is flat over `R` is open in
`Spec S`, provided `R` has only finitely many weakly associated primes.
declarations.comment: openness of the relative flat locus

declarations.name: Stacks.Flatness.finitePresentation_localizedModule_away_of_basicOpen_subset_flatLocus
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 05IL (finite presentation on a basic open).** For a ring map `R → S` of
finite presentation and a finite `S`-module `M`, if the basic open `D(g)` is contained in the
locus where `M` is flat over `R`, then `M_g` is a finitely presented `S_g`-module, provided `R`
has only finitely many weakly associated primes.
declarations.statement:
theorem finitePresentation_localizedModule_away_of_basicOpen_subset_flatLocus
    (hR : (weaklyAssociatedPrimes R R).Finite) (g : S)
    (hg : (↑(PrimeSpectrum.basicOpen g) : Set (PrimeSpectrum S)) ⊆
      {q : PrimeSpectrum S | Module.Flat R (LocalizedModule.AtPrime q.asIdeal M)}) :
    Module.FinitePresentation (Localization.Away g) (LocalizedModule.Away g M)
declarations.comment: finite presentation on a basic open inside the flat locus

declarations.name: Stacks.Flatness.OpenFlatLocus.flat_localizedModule_away_of_forall_flat_atPrime
declarations.doc:
**Flatness over the base spreads from the points of a basic open to the basic open itself.** If
`M_{𝔮}` is flat over `R` for every prime `𝔮` of `S` with `g ∉ 𝔮`, then `M_g` is flat over `R`.

Flatness over `R` is local on `Spec (S_g)` (`Module.flat_of_isLocalized_maximal`), and the local
ring of `M_g` at a prime `P` of `S_g` is the localization of `M` at the prime `P ∩ S` of `S`:
`(S_g)_P` is the localization of `S` at `P ∩ S`
(`IsLocalization.isLocalization_atPrime_localization_atPrime`), and a composite of two base changes
is a base change (`IsBaseChange.comp`).
declarations.statement:
theorem flat_localizedModule_away_of_forall_flat_atPrime {R S M : Type*} [CommRing R]
    [CommRing S]
    [Algebra R S] [AddCommGroup M] [Module R M] [Module S M] [IsScalarTower R S M] (g : S)
    (H : ∀ q : PrimeSpectrum S, q ∈ PrimeSpectrum.basicOpen g →
      Module.Flat R (LocalizedModule.AtPrime q.asIdeal M)) :
    Module.Flat R (LocalizedModule.Away g M)
declarations.comment: flatness over the base

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.isOpen_setOf_isFlatAt_of_locallyOfFiniteType_of_locally_finite_weakAss
declarations.doc:
**Openness of the flat locus.** For a morphism `f : X ⟶ S` locally of finite type whose base
has locally finite weakly associated points, the set of points at which `f` is flat is open.
declarations.statement:
theorem isOpen_setOf_isFlatAt_of_locallyOfFiniteType_of_locally_finite_weakAss
    {X S : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ S) [LocallyOfFiniteType f]
    (hS : ∀ s : S, ∃ V : S.Opens, s ∈ V ∧
      (schemeWeaklyAssociatedPoints S ∩ (V : Set S)).Finite) :
    IsOpen {x : X | IsFlatAt f.toLRSHom.toShHom x}
declarations.comment: openness of the locus of flatness

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.locallyOfFinitePresentation_restrict_of_subset_flatLocus
declarations.doc:
**Finite presentation on the flat locus.** For a morphism `f : X ⟶ S` locally of finite type
whose base has locally finite weakly associated points, the restriction of `f` to an open
subscheme contained in the locus of points of flatness is locally of finite presentation.
declarations.statement:
theorem locallyOfFinitePresentation_restrict_of_subset_flatLocus
    {X S : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ S) [LocallyOfFiniteType f]
    (hS : ∀ s : S, ∃ V : S.Opens, s ∈ V ∧
      (schemeWeaklyAssociatedPoints S ∩ (V : Set S)).Finite)
    (U : X.Opens) (hU : (U : Set X) ⊆ {x : X | IsFlatAt f.toLRSHom.toShHom x}) :
    LocallyOfFinitePresentation (U.ι ≫ f)
declarations.comment: the flat locus is locally of finite presentation over the base

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.flat_of_subset_setOf_isFlatAt
declarations.doc:
A morphism which is flat at every point of an open subscheme of its source is flat after
restriction to that open subscheme.
declarations.statement:
theorem flat_of_subset_setOf_isFlatAt {X S : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ S) (V : X.Opens)
    (hV : (V : Set X) ⊆ {x : X | IsFlatAt f.toLRSHom.toShHom x}) :
    Flat (V.ι ≫ f)
declarations.comment: the flat locus is flat over the base

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.locallyOfFinitePresentation_of_flat_of_isIntegral
declarations.doc:
A morphism locally of finite type and flat over an integral base is locally of finite
presentation.
declarations.statement:
theorem locallyOfFinitePresentation_of_flat_of_isIntegral
    {X S : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ S) [LocallyOfFiniteType f] [Flat f] [IsIntegral S] :
    LocallyOfFinitePresentation f

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.isOpen_flatLocus_of_locallyOfFiniteType
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 05IQ (openness).** The locus where a quasi-coherent module of finite
type is flat over the target of a morphism locally of finite type is open, provided the weakly
associated points of the target are locally finite.
declarations.statement:
theorem isOpen_flatLocus_of_locallyOfFiniteType
    {X S : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ S) [LocallyOfFiniteType f]
    (F : X.Modules) [F.IsQuasicoherent] [F.IsFiniteType]
    (hS : ∀ s : S, ∃ W : S.Opens, s ∈ W ∧
      (schemeWeaklyAssociatedPoints S ∩ (W : Set S)).Finite) :
    IsOpen (flatLocus f F)
declarations.comment: openness of the relative flat locus

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.isFlatOver_flatLocus_of_locallyOfFiniteType
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 05IQ (flatness on the flat locus).** The restriction of the module to
its relative flat locus is flat over the base.
declarations.statement:
theorem isFlatOver_flatLocus_of_locallyOfFiniteType
    {X S : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ S) [LocallyOfFiniteType f]
    (F : X.Modules) [F.IsQuasicoherent] [F.IsFiniteType]
    (hS : ∀ s : S, ∃ W : S.Opens, s ∈ W ∧
      (schemeWeaklyAssociatedPoints S ∩ (W : Set S)).Finite) :
    letI U : X.Opens := ⟨flatLocus f F, isOpen_flatLocus_of_locallyOfFiniteType f F hS⟩
    IsFlatOver (U.ι ≫ f).toLRSHom.toShHom (F.restrict U.ι)
declarations.comment: flatness over the base on the flat locus

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.isFinitelyPresentedRelative_flatLocus
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 05IQ (relative finite presentation on the flat locus).** The
restriction of the module to its relative flat locus is finitely presented relative to the
base.
declarations.statement:
theorem isFinitelyPresentedRelative_flatLocus
    {X S : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ S) [LocallyOfFiniteType f]
    (F : X.Modules) [F.IsQuasicoherent] [F.IsFiniteType]
    (hS : ∀ s : S, ∃ W : S.Opens, s ∈ W ∧
      (schemeWeaklyAssociatedPoints S ∩ (W : Set S)).Finite) :
    letI U : X.Opens := ⟨flatLocus f F, isOpen_flatLocus_of_locallyOfFiniteType f F hS⟩
    IsFinitelyPresentedRelative (U.ι ≫ f) (F.restrict U.ι)
declarations.comment: relative finite presentation on the flat locus

declarations.name: Stacks.Flatness.isOpen_setOf_flat_localizedModule_atPrime_of_finiteType
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 05IR (openness).** For a ring map `R → S` of finite type and a finite
`S`-module `M`, the locus of primes `q` of `S` at which `M_q` is flat over `R` is open in
`Spec S`, provided `R` has only finitely many weakly associated primes.
declarations.statement:
theorem isOpen_setOf_flat_localizedModule_atPrime_of_finiteType
    {R : Type u} [CommRing R] {S : Type v} [CommRing S] [Algebra R S] [Algebra.FiniteType R S]
    {M : Type w} [AddCommGroup M] [Module S M] [Module R M] [IsScalarTower R S M]
    [Module.Finite S M] (hR : (weaklyAssociatedPrimes R R).Finite) :
    IsOpen {q : PrimeSpectrum S | Module.Flat R (LocalizedModule.AtPrime q.asIdeal M)}
declarations.comment: openness of the relative flat locus

declarations.name: Stacks.Flatness.finitePresentationRel_localizedModule_away_of_basicOpen_subset_flatLocus
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 05IR (relative finite presentation on a basic open).** For a ring map
`R → S` of finite type and a finite `S`-module `M`, if the basic open `D(g)` is contained in the
locus where `M` is flat over `R`, then `M_g` is an `S_g`-module finitely presented relative to
`R`, provided `R` has only finitely many weakly associated primes.
declarations.statement:
theorem finitePresentationRel_localizedModule_away_of_basicOpen_subset_flatLocus
    {R : Type u} [CommRing R] {S : Type v} [CommRing S] [Algebra R S] [Algebra.FiniteType R S]
    {M : Type w} [AddCommGroup M] [Module S M] [Module R M] [IsScalarTower R S M]
    [Module.Finite S M] (hR : (weaklyAssociatedPrimes R R).Finite) (g : S)
    (hg : (↑(PrimeSpectrum.basicOpen g) : Set (PrimeSpectrum S)) ⊆
      {q : PrimeSpectrum S | Module.Flat R (LocalizedModule.AtPrime q.asIdeal M)}) :
    Module.FinitePresentationRel R (Localization.Away g) (LocalizedModule.Away g M)
declarations.comment: relative finite presentation on a basic open inside the flat locus

declarations.name: Stacks.Flatness.OpenFlatLocus.flat_localizedModule_away_of_forall_flat_atPrime
declarations.doc:
**Flatness over the base spreads from the points of a basic open to the basic open itself.** If
`M_{𝔮}` is flat over `R` for every prime `𝔮` of `S` with `g ∉ 𝔮`, then `M_g` is flat over `R`.

Flatness over `R` is local on `Spec (S_g)` (`Module.flat_of_isLocalized_maximal`), and the local
ring of `M_g` at a prime `P` of `S_g` is the localization of `M` at the prime `P ∩ S` of `S`:
`(S_g)_P` is the localization of `S` at `P ∩ S`
(`IsLocalization.isLocalization_atPrime_localization_atPrime`), and a composite of two base changes
is a base change (`IsBaseChange.comp`).
declarations.statement:
theorem flat_localizedModule_away_of_forall_flat_atPrime {R S M : Type*} [CommRing R]
    [CommRing S]
    [Algebra R S] [AddCommGroup M] [Module R M] [Module S M] [IsScalarTower R S M] (g : S)
    (H : ∀ q : PrimeSpectrum S, q ∈ PrimeSpectrum.basicOpen g →
      Module.Flat R (LocalizedModule.AtPrime q.asIdeal M)) :
    Module.Flat R (LocalizedModule.Away g M)
declarations.comment: flatness over the base

declarations.name: Stacks.PureModules.associatedPrime_add_map_ne_top_of_isAdicComplete
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 05IT.** An associated prime of the tensor product of an adically
complete module with any base module is not comaximal with the ideal of completion.
declarations.statement:
theorem associatedPrime_add_map_ne_top_of_isAdicComplete
    (R : Type u) (S : Type v) [CommRing R] [CommRing S] [Algebra R S]
    (I : Ideal R) (N : Type w) [AddCommGroup N] [Module R N] [Module S N]
    [IsScalarTower R S N] [IsAdicComplete I N]
    (M : Type x) [AddCommGroup M] [Module R M]
    (q : Ideal S) (hq : IsAssociatedPrimeStacks S (N ⊗[R] M) q) :
    q + I.map (algebraMap R S) ≠ ⊤

declarations.name: Stacks.PureModules.associatedPrime_add_map_maximalIdeal_ne_top_of_directSum_finite
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 05IU.** An associated prime of a tensor product of a direct sum of
finite modules cannot be comaximal with the closed fibre of a local base ring.
declarations.statement:
theorem associatedPrime_add_map_maximalIdeal_ne_top_of_directSum_finite
    (R : Type u) (S : Type v) [CommRing R] [CommRing S] [IsLocalRing R] [Algebra R S]
    (N : Type w) [AddCommGroup N] [Module R N] [Module S N] [IsScalarTower R S N]
    (ι : Type x) (F : ι → Type y)
    [∀ i, AddCommGroup (F i)] [∀ i, Module R (F i)]
    (hF : ∀ i, Module.Finite R (F i))
    (e : N ≃ₗ[R] ⨁ i, F i)
    (M : Type z) [AddCommGroup M] [Module R M]
    (q : Ideal S) (hq : IsAssociatedPrimeStacks S (N ⊗[R] M) q) :
    q + (IsLocalRing.maximalIdeal R).map (algebraMap R S) ≠ ⊤

declarations.name: Stacks.PureModules.associatedPrime_add_map_maximalIdeal_ne_top_of_countable_mittagLeffler
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 05IV.** An associated prime of a tensor product of a countably
generated Mittag-Leffler module over a henselian local ring cannot be comaximal with the
closed fibre.
declarations.statement:
theorem associatedPrime_add_map_maximalIdeal_ne_top_of_countable_mittagLeffler
    (R : Type u) (S : Type v) [CommRing R] [CommRing S] [HenselianLocalRing R]
    [Algebra R S]
    (N : Type w) [AddCommGroup N] [Module R N] [Module S N] [IsScalarTower R S N]
    [Small.{w} R]
    (hcg : ∃ t : Set N, t.Countable ∧ Submodule.span R t = ⊤)
    (hML : IsMittagLeffler.{u, w, w, w, w} R N)
    (M : Type x) [AddCommGroup M] [Module R M]
    (q : Ideal S) (hq : IsAssociatedPrimeStacks S (N ⊗[R] M) q) :
    q + (IsLocalRing.maximalIdeal R).map (algebraMap R S) ≠ ⊤

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.ImpurityDiagram
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 05IX.** A base-change diagram together with a specialization over the
chosen point of a pre-pure situation and a point above its generalization.
declarations.statement: structure ImpurityDiagram (P : PrePureSituation.{u})

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.IsImpurity
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 05IY.** An impurity diagram defines an impurity when its chosen point
belongs to the relative assassin of the pulled-back module and its closure is disjoint from the
fibre over the specialized point.
declarations.statement: abbrev IsImpurity (P : PrePureSituation.{u}) (D : ImpurityDiagram P) : Prop

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.exists_isImpurity_mapBase_of_isLimit
declarations.doc:
An impurity on a cofiltered limit of affine schemes over the base is the pullback of an
impurity at some stage.
declarations.statement:
public theorem exists_isImpurity_mapBase_of_isLimit
    {P : AlgebraicGeometry.PrePureSituation.{u}}
    {I : Type v} [Category.{w} I] [IsCofiltered I]
    (F : I ⥤ Over P.S) (c : Cone F) (hc : IsLimit c)
    (D : AlgebraicGeometry.ImpurityDiagram P) (e : Over.mk D.g ≅ c.pt)
    (hF : ∀ i, IsAffine (F.obj i).left) (hD : AlgebraicGeometry.IsImpurity P D) :
    ∃ i, AlgebraicGeometry.IsImpurity P
      (mapBase D (F.obj i).hom (e.hom ≫ c.π.app i).left (e.hom ≫ c.π.app i).w)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.exists_isImpurity_elementaryEtaleNeighborhood_of_quasiFiniteAt
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 05J0.** If a pre-pure situation admits an impurity whose test family
is quasi-finite over the base at the distinguished point, then it admits one whose test family,
pointed at the distinguished point, is an elementary étale neighbourhood of the chosen point of
the base.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_isImpurity_elementaryEtaleNeighborhood_of_quasiFiniteAt
    (P : PrePureSituation.{u})
    (h : ∃ D : ImpurityDiagram P, IsImpurity P D ∧ quasiFiniteAt D.g D.t) :
    ∃ (D : ImpurityDiagram P) (hD : Etale D.g), IsImpurity P D ∧
      EtaleNeighborhood.IsElementary
        ({ scheme := D.T
           point := D.t
           toBase := D.g
           etale_toBase := hD
           map_point := D.mapsToChosenPoint } : EtaleNeighborhood P.S P.s)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.exists_isImpurity_quasiFiniteAt
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 05J1.** Over a locally Noetherian base, an impurity of the module of a
pre-pure situation above the chosen point of the base can be witnessed by an impurity whose test
family is quasi-finite over the base at its specialized point.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_isImpurity_quasiFiniteAt (P : PrePureSituation.{u}) [IsLocallyNoetherian P.S]
    (h : ∃ D : ImpurityDiagram P, IsImpurity P D) :
    ∃ D : ImpurityDiagram P, IsImpurity P D ∧ quasiFiniteAt D.g D.t

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.exists_isImpurity_elementaryEtaleNeighborhood_of_henselization
declarations.doc:
An impurity whose test family is the spectrum of a henselization of the local ring of the base
at the distinguished point already occurs over an elementary étale neighbourhood of that point.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_isImpurity_elementaryEtaleNeighborhood_of_henselization
    (P : PrePureSituation.{u}) (Rh : Type u) [CommRing Rh] [IsLocalRing Rh]
    [Algebra (P.S.presheaf.stalk P.s) Rh]
    [IsLocalRing.IsHenselization (P.S.presheaf.stalk P.s)
      (IsLocalRing.ResidueField (P.S.presheaf.stalk P.s)) Rh]
    (h : ∃ (D : ImpurityDiagram P) (e : D.T ≅ Spec (CommRingCat.of Rh)),
      D.g = e.hom ≫ specHenselizationToBase P.s Rh ∧ IsImpurity P D) :
    ∃ (D : ImpurityDiagram P) (hD : Etale D.g), IsImpurity P D ∧
      EtaleNeighborhood.IsElementary
        ({ scheme := D.T
           point := D.t
           toBase := D.g
           etale_toBase := hD
           map_point := D.mapsToChosenPoint } : EtaleNeighborhood P.S P.s)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.exists_isImpurity_henselization_iff_elementaryEtaleNeighborhood
declarations.doc:
In a pre-pure situation, an impurity over the henselization of the base at the distinguished
point exists if and only if one exists over an elementary étale neighbourhood of that point.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_isImpurity_henselization_iff_elementaryEtaleNeighborhood
    (P : PrePureSituation.{u}) :
    (∃ (D : ImpurityDiagram P) (e : D.T ≅ henselization P.S P.s),
      D.g = e.hom ≫ henselizationToBase P.S P.s ∧ IsImpurity P D) ↔
    (∃ (D : ImpurityDiagram P) (hD : Etale D.g), IsImpurity P D ∧
      EtaleNeighborhood.IsElementary
        ({ scheme := D.T
           point := D.t
           toBase := D.g
           etale_toBase := hD
           map_point := D.mapsToChosenPoint } : EtaleNeighborhood P.S P.s))
declarations.comment: parts (1) and (2)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.exists_isImpurity_elementaryEtaleNeighborhood_iff_quasiFiniteAt
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 05J3, parts (2) and (3).** A pre-pure situation admits an impurity
whose test family, pointed at the distinguished point, is an elementary étale neighbourhood of
the chosen point of the base if and only if it admits one whose test family is quasi-finite over
the base at the distinguished point.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_isImpurity_elementaryEtaleNeighborhood_iff_quasiFiniteAt
    (P : PrePureSituation.{u}) :
    (∃ (D : ImpurityDiagram P) (hD : Etale D.g), IsImpurity P D ∧
      EtaleNeighborhood.IsElementary
        ({ scheme := D.T
           point := D.t
           toBase := D.g
           etale_toBase := hD
           map_point := D.mapsToChosenPoint } : EtaleNeighborhood P.S P.s)) ↔
    (∃ D : ImpurityDiagram P, IsImpurity P D ∧ quasiFiniteAt D.g D.t)
declarations.comment: parts (2) and (3)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.IsPureAlong
declarations.doc:
A finite type quasi-coherent module is pure along the fibre over the chosen point if no
impurity occurs over an elementary étale neighbourhood of that point.
declarations.statement: abbrev IsPureAlong (P : PrePureSituation.{u}) : Prop
declarations.comment: part (1)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.IsUniversallyPureAlong
declarations.doc:
A finite type quasi-coherent module is universally pure along the fibre over the chosen
point if no impurity occurs after any base change.
declarations.statement: abbrev IsUniversallyPureAlong (P : PrePureSituation.{u}) : Prop
declarations.comment: part (2)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.IsSchemePureAlong
declarations.doc: The scheme `X` is pure along the fibre over `s` when its structure sheaf is pure there.
declarations.statement:
abbrev IsSchemePureAlong {X S : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ S)
    [LocallyOfFiniteType f] [QuasiCompact f] (s : S) : Prop
declarations.comment: part (3)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.IsUniversallyPureRelative
declarations.doc:
A finite type quasi-coherent module is universally pure relative to the base if it is
universally pure along every fibre.
declarations.statement:
abbrev IsUniversallyPureRelative {X S : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ S)
    [LocallyOfFiniteType f] [QuasiCompact f] (F : X.Modules)
    [F.IsFiniteType] [F.IsQuasicoherent] : Prop
declarations.comment: part (4)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.IsPureRelative
declarations.doc:
A finite type quasi-coherent module is pure relative to the base if it is pure along every
fibre.
declarations.statement:
abbrev IsPureRelative {X S : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ S)
    [LocallyOfFiniteType f] [QuasiCompact f] (F : X.Modules)
    [F.IsFiniteType] [F.IsQuasicoherent] : Prop
declarations.comment: part (5)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.IsSchemePureRelative
declarations.doc:
The scheme `X` is pure relative to `S` when its structure sheaf is pure relative to the
base.
declarations.statement:
abbrev IsSchemePureRelative {X S : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ S)
    [LocallyOfFiniteType f] [QuasiCompact f] : Prop
declarations.comment: part (6)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.noElementaryEtaleImpurity_of_noQuasiFiniteImpurity
declarations.doc:
Condition (2) implies condition (1): an elementary étale neighbourhood is étale, hence
quasi-finite at its distinguished point.

This is one direction of the equivalence of conditions (1) and (2), and is unconditional. The
converse is Tag 05J0, whose proof does not use quasi-compactness but which is not available in
this library, so the equivalence itself is not claimed here.
declarations.statement:
theorem noElementaryEtaleImpurity_of_noQuasiFiniteImpurity {f : X ⟶ S} {F : X.Modules} {s : S}
    (h : NoQuasiFiniteImpurity f F s) : NoElementaryEtaleImpurity f F s
declarations.comment: condition (2) implies condition (1)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.noHenselianImpurity_iff_relativeAssassinSpecializesIntoClosedFibre
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 05J5.** For a morphism which is only locally of finite type,
conditions (3) and (4) are still equivalent: the impurities above `s` whose test family is a
model of `S^h → S` are exactly the points of `Ass_{X^h/S^h}(ℱ^h)` which fail to specialize into
the fibre of `X^h` over the closed point of `S^h`.

What makes this work is that the auxiliary data of such an impurity carry no information: its
distinguished point is forced to be the closed point of the model, because every point of
`S^h` over `s` is the closed point, and the specialization to it is automatic, because every
point of the spectrum of a local ring specializes to its closed point.
declarations.statement:
theorem noHenselianImpurity_iff_relativeAssassinSpecializesIntoClosedFibre
    [LocallyOfFiniteType f] [F.IsFiniteType] [F.IsQuasicoherent] :
    NoHenselianImpurity f F s Rh ↔ RelativeAssassinSpecializesIntoClosedFibre f F s Rh
declarations.comment: conditions (3) and (4) are equivalent

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.noElementaryEtaleImpurity_iff_noQuasiFiniteImpurity
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 05J5.** For a morphism which is only locally of finite type,
conditions (1) and (2) are still equivalent: an impurity above `s` whose test family is merely
quasi-finite at its distinguished point can be replaced by one whose test family is an
elementary étale neighbourhood of `s`.

This is the half of the remark which asserts that the proof of Tag 05J0 does not use
quasi-compactness of the morphism: that proof is run here for impurity data, which carry no
such hypothesis.
declarations.statement:
theorem noElementaryEtaleImpurity_iff_noQuasiFiniteImpurity {f : X ⟶ S} [LocallyOfFiniteType f]
    {F : X.Modules} [F.IsQuasicoherent] {s : S} :
    NoElementaryEtaleImpurity f F s ↔ NoQuasiFiniteImpurity f F s
declarations.comment: conditions (1) and (2) are equivalent

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.isUniversallyPureAlong_iff_forall_baseChange_isPureAlong
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 05J6.** Universal purity along the chosen fibre can be tested by
purity after every pointed base change.
declarations.statement:
public theorem isUniversallyPureAlong_iff_forall_baseChange_isPureAlong
    (P : PrePureSituation.{u}) :
    IsUniversallyPureAlong P ↔
      ∀ (Q : PrePureSituation.{u}) (g : Q.S ⟶ P.S)
        (_hg : g.base Q.s = P.s) (toX : Q.X ⟶ P.X)
        (_hpb : IsPullback toX Q.f P.f g)
        (_hF : Q.F ≅ (Scheme.Modules.pullback toX).obj P.F),
          IsPureAlong Q
declarations.comment: the pointed-fibre equivalence

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.isUniversallyPureRelative_iff_forall_baseChange_isPureRelative
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 05J6, in particular.** Universal purity over the base can be tested
by purity relative to every base change.
declarations.statement:
public theorem isUniversallyPureRelative_iff_forall_baseChange_isPureRelative
    {X S : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ S) [LocallyOfFiniteType f] [QuasiCompact f]
    (F : X.Modules) [F.IsFiniteType] [F.IsQuasicoherent] :
    IsUniversallyPureRelative f F ↔
      ∀ {X' S' : Scheme.{u}} (f' : X' ⟶ S')
        [LocallyOfFiniteType f'] [QuasiCompact f']
        (F' : X'.Modules) [F'.IsFiniteType] [F'.IsQuasicoherent]
        (g : S' ⟶ S) (toX : X' ⟶ X)
        (_hpb : IsPullback toX f' f g)
        (_hF : F' ≅ (Scheme.Modules.pullback toX).obj F),
          IsPureRelative f' F'
declarations.comment: the relative equivalence

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.isPureAlong_of_quasiFiniteAt_of_isPureAlong
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 05J7.** If a morphism of pointed schemes `(S', s') → (S, s)` is
quasi-finite at `s'` and a finite type quasi-coherent module is pure along the fibre over `s`,
then its pullback to the base change is pure along the fibre over `s'`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem isPureAlong_of_quasiFiniteAt_of_isPureAlong {P Q : PrePureSituation.{u}}
    (g : Q.S ⟶ P.S) (hg : g.base Q.s = P.s) (toX : Q.X ⟶ P.X)
    (hpb : IsPullback toX Q.f P.f g)
    (hF : Q.F ≅ (Scheme.Modules.pullback toX).obj P.F)
    (hqf : quasiFiniteAt g Q.s) (hP : IsPureAlong P) :
    IsPureAlong Q

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.isPureAlong_iff_isUniversallyPureAlong_of_isNoetherianRing_stalk
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 05J8.** Let `f : X ⟶ S` be of finite type, let `ℱ` be a finite type
quasi-coherent `𝒪_X`-module and let `s` be a point of `S` whose local ring `𝒪_{S, s}` is
Noetherian. Then `ℱ` is pure along the fibre `X_s` if and only if it is universally pure
along `X_s`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isPureAlong_iff_isUniversallyPureAlong_of_isNoetherianRing_stalk
    (P : PrePureSituation.{u}) [IsNoetherianRing (P.S.presheaf.stalk P.s)] :
    IsPureAlong P ↔ IsUniversallyPureAlong P

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.isPureAlong_of_flatPointedBaseChange
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 05J9.** Purity along the original fibre follows from purity along the
fibre of a pointed base change which is flat at its distinguished point.
declarations.statement:
public theorem isPureAlong_of_flatPointedBaseChange (H : FlatPointedBaseChangeSituation.{u})
    (P' : PrePureSituation.{u}) (eS : P'.S = H.S') (eX : P'.X = pullback H.f H.g)
    (hf : eqToHom eX.symm ≫ P'.f ≫ eqToHom eS = pullback.snd H.f H.g)
    (hF : HEq P'.F ((Scheme.Modules.pullback (pullback.fst H.f H.g)).obj H.F))
    (hs : eS ▸ P'.s = H.s') (hpure : IsPureAlong P') :
    IsPureAlong ({ S := H.S, X := H.X, f := H.f, F := H.F, s := H.s } :
      PrePureSituation.{u})
declarations.comment: flat_descend_pure

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.universallyPureAlong_of_flatPointedBaseChange
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 05J9.** Universal purity along a fibre descends through a pointed base
change which is flat at the new distinguished point.
declarations.statement:
public theorem universallyPureAlong_of_flatPointedBaseChange
    (H : FlatPointedBaseChangeSituation.{u})
    (h : IsUniversallyPureAlong H.baseChangedSituation) :
    IsUniversallyPureAlong ({ S := H.S, X := H.X, f := H.f, F := H.F, s := H.s } :
      PrePureSituation.{u})
declarations.comment: flat_descend_universally_pure

declarations.name: Stacks.Examples.CountableVarLocalization.exists_isLocalRing_adicCompletion_not_complete
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 05JC.** There exists a local ring `R` and a maximal ideal `m` of it such that the
`m`-adic completion `R ^∧` of `R` is local with maximal ideal different from `m R ^∧`, is not
complete for its own maximal ideal, and is not `m`-adically complete as an `R`-module.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_isLocalRing_adicCompletion_not_complete :
    ∃ (R : Type) (_ : CommRing R) (_ : IsLocalRing R) (m : Ideal R), m.IsMaximal ∧
      ∃ _ : IsLocalRing (AdicCompletion m R),
        IsLocalRing.maximalIdeal (AdicCompletion m R) ≠ m.map (AdicCompletion.of m R) ∧
        ¬ IsAdicComplete (IsLocalRing.maximalIdeal (AdicCompletion m R))
            (AdicCompletion m R) ∧
        ¬ IsAdicComplete m (AdicCompletion m R)

declarations.name: Stacks.Examples.exists_complete_principal_ideal_not_complete_quotient
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 05JE.** A quotient by a principal ideal of a ring complete for another principal
ideal need not be complete for the induced ideal.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_complete_principal_ideal_not_complete_quotient :
    ∃ (R : Type u) (_ : CommRing R) (I J : Ideal R),
      I.IsPrincipal ∧ J.IsPrincipal ∧ IsAdicComplete I R ∧
        ¬ IsAdicComplete (I.map (Ideal.Quotient.mk J)) (R ⧸ J)

declarations.name: Stacks.Examples.exists_not_left_exact_adicCompletion
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 05JG.** Adic completion need not preserve the exactness of a short exact sequence
at its middle term, so it is not left exact in general.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_not_left_exact_adicCompletion :
    ∃ (R : Type u) (_ : CommRing R) (I J : Ideal R),
      I.IsPrincipal ∧ J.IsPrincipal ∧
        Function.Exact (Submodule.subtype (J : Submodule R R))
          (Submodule.mkQ (J : Submodule R R)) ∧
        ¬ Function.Exact
          (AdicCompletion.map I (Submodule.subtype (J : Submodule R R)))
          (AdicCompletion.map I (Submodule.mkQ (J : Submodule R R)))
declarations.comment: failure of left exactness

declarations.name: Stacks.Examples.exists_not_right_exact_adicCompletion_finitePresentation
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 05JG.** Completion is not right exact even on finitely presented modules over a
ring, with a principal ideal of definition.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_not_right_exact_adicCompletion_finitePresentation :
    ∃ (R : Type u) (_ : CommRing R) (I : Ideal R) (f : R),
      I.IsPrincipal ∧
        Module.FinitePresentation R (R ⧸ (Ideal.span {f} : Submodule R R)) ∧
        Function.Exact (LinearMap.mulLeft R f)
          (Submodule.mkQ (Ideal.span {f} : Submodule R R)) ∧
        ¬ Function.Exact
          (AdicCompletion.map I (LinearMap.mulLeft R f))
          (AdicCompletion.map I (Submodule.mkQ (Ideal.span {f} : Submodule R R)))
declarations.comment: failure of right exactness on finitely presented modules

declarations.name: Stacks.Examples.exists_localHom_not_isNoetherianRing_no_quasiFinite_quotient
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 05JI.** There is a local homomorphism `f : A → B` of local domains, essentially of
finite type, with finite residue field extension, such that for every prime `q ≠ m_B` of `B`
the map `A → B/q` is not a localization of a quasi-finite ring map.

The witness is the one of Stacks: `A` is not Noetherian and some prime of `B` (namely `(0)`)
does not lie over `m_A`. So all hypotheses of Stacks 05GT except the Noetherian one hold, with
`V = Spec B`, while its conclusion fails.
declarations.statement:
public theorem exists_localHom_not_isNoetherianRing_no_quasiFinite_quotient :
    ∃ (A B : Type u) (_ : CommRing A) (_ : CommRing B)
      (_ : IsDomain A) (_ : IsDomain B) (_ : IsLocalRing A) (_ : IsLocalRing B)
      (f : A →+* B) (hf : IsLocalHom f),
      IsEssentiallyOfFiniteType A B f ∧
      (letI : IsLocalHom f := hf
       letI := (IsLocalRing.ResidueField.map f).toAlgebra
       Module.Finite (IsLocalRing.ResidueField A) (IsLocalRing.ResidueField B)) ∧
      ¬ IsNoetherianRing A ∧
      (∃ q : PrimeSpectrum B, q.asIdeal.comap f ≠ IsLocalRing.maximalIdeal A) ∧
      (∀ q : PrimeSpectrum B, q.asIdeal ≠ IsLocalRing.maximalIdeal B →
        ¬ (letI := f.toAlgebra
           ∃ (C : Type u) (_ : CommRing C) (_ : Algebra A C)
             (_ : Algebra.FiniteType A C) (_ : Algebra.QuasiFinite A C)
             (M : Submonoid C) (_ : Algebra C (B ⧸ q.asIdeal)),
             IsScalarTower A C (B ⧸ q.asIdeal) ∧ IsLocalization M (B ⧸ q.asIdeal)))

declarations.name: Stacks.Examples.exists_isPureRelative_not_isUniversallyPureRelative
declarations.doc:
There is a morphism of affine schemes of finite presentation and a module of finite
presentation on its source which is pure relative to the base, but not universally pure relative
to it.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_isPureRelative_not_isUniversallyPureRelative :
    ∃ (X S : Scheme.{u}) (_ : IsAffine X) (_ : IsAffine S) (f : X ⟶ S)
      (hf : FinitePresentation f) (F : X.Modules)
      (hF : SheafOfModules.IsFinitePresentation.{u, u, u} F)
      (hFT : SheafOfModules.IsFiniteType.{u, u, u} F)
      (hQC : SheafOfModules.IsQuasicoherent.{u, u, u} F),
      letI : LocallyOfFinitePresentation f := hf.1
      letI : LocallyOfFiniteType f := inferInstance
      letI : QuasiCompact f := hf.2.1
      letI : SheafOfModules.IsFinitePresentation.{u, u, u} F := hF
      letI : SheafOfModules.IsFiniteType.{u, u, u} F := hFT
      letI : SheafOfModules.IsQuasicoherent.{u, u, u} F := hQC
      IsPureRelative f F ∧ ¬ IsUniversallyPureRelative f F

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.isClosed_range_iff_stableUnderSpecialization
declarations.doc:
The image of a quasi-compact morphism of schemes is closed if and only if it
is stable under specialization.
declarations.statement:
public theorem isClosed_range_iff_stableUnderSpecialization
    {X S : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ S) [QuasiCompact f] :
    IsClosed (Set.range (f : X → S)) ↔
      StableUnderSpecialization (Set.range (f : X → S))

declarations.name: Stacks.Modules.tilde_isLocallyFree_iff_module
declarations.doc:
The sheaf `M̃` associated to an `R`-module `M` is a locally free `𝒪_X`-module on
`X = Spec R`, in the sense of Stacks Tag 01C6, if and only if `M` is a locally free
`R`-module.
declarations.comment: locally free

declarations.name: Stacks.Modules.tilde_isFiniteLocallyFree_iff_module
declarations.doc:
The sheaf `M̃` associated to an `R`-module `M` is a finite locally free `𝒪_X`-module on
`X = Spec R`, in the sense of Stacks Tag 01C6, if and only if `M` is a finite locally free
`R`-module.
declarations.comment: finite locally free

declarations.name: Stacks.Modules.tilde_isFiniteLocallyFreeOfRank_iff_module
declarations.doc:
The sheaf `M̃` associated to an `R`-module `M` is a finite locally free `𝒪_X`-module of rank
`r` on `X = Spec R`, in the sense of Stacks Tag 01C6, if and only if `M` is a finite locally free
`R`-module of rank `r`.
declarations.statement:
theorem tilde_isFiniteLocallyFreeOfRank_iff_module (r : ℕ) :
    AlgebraicGeometry.SheafOfModules.IsFiniteLocallyFreeOfRank.{u, u, u}
        (tilde (R := CommRingCat.of R) (ModuleCat.of R M)) r ↔
      Module.IsFiniteLocallyFreeOfRank R M r
declarations.comment: finite locally free of rank r

declarations.name: tilde_isLocallyFree_iff
declarations.doc:
**Statement 1 (locally free case).** `M~` is a locally free `O_X`-module if
and only if `M` is a locally free `R`-module.

PROOF (complete modulo the two helper lemmas): rewrite the sheaf side via
`isLocallyFree_iff_basicOpen`, then:
* (⇒) For each point `x` choose (by `choose`) a standard open `D(g x) ∋ x` on which
  the sheaf is free; the family `(g x)` covers `Spec R` (each `x ∈ D(g x)`), so
  `Ideal.span (range g) = ⊤` by `iSup_basicOpen_eq_top_iff`, and by Helper 1 each
  `M_{g x}` is free — giving `Module.IsLocallyFree R M` with `ι := PrimeSpectrum R`.
* (⇐) Given a covering family `f : ι → R` with span `⊤` and each `M_{f i}` free:
  for any `x`, the cover gives `i` with `x ∈ D(f i)`, and Helper 1 makes the sheaf
  free on `D(f i)`.
declarations.statement:
theorem tilde_isLocallyFree_iff (R : Type u) [CommRing R] (M : Type u)
    [AddCommGroup M] [Module R M] :
    (AlgebraicGeometry.tilde (R := CommRingCat.of R) (ModuleCat.of R M)).IsLocallyFree ↔
      Module.IsLocallyFree R M

declarations.name: tilde_isFiniteLocallyFree_iff
declarations.doc:
**Statement 2 (finite locally free case).** `M~` is a finite locally free
`O_X`-module if and only if `M` is a finite locally free `R`-module.

PROOF (complete modulo `isFiniteLocallyFree_iff_basicOpen` and
`tilde_restrict_basicOpen_finiteFree_iff`): same covering combinatorics as
Statement 1, now carrying the finiteness witness `Finite I` through the helpers.
declarations.statement:
theorem tilde_isFiniteLocallyFree_iff (R : Type u) [CommRing R] (M : Type u)
    [AddCommGroup M] [Module R M] :
    (AlgebraicGeometry.tilde (R := CommRingCat.of R) (ModuleCat.of R M)).IsFiniteLocallyFree ↔
      Module.IsFiniteLocallyFree R M

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.Modules.IsLocallyProjective
declarations.doc:
A sheaf of modules on a scheme is locally projective if its sections on every affine open
are projective over the ring of functions on that open.
declarations.statement:
public abbrev IsLocallyProjective {X : Scheme.{u}}
    (M : SheafOfModules.{m} X.ringCatSheaf) : Prop

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.isLocallyProjective_iff_exists_affineOpen_cover
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 05JQ.** A quasi-coherent sheaf of modules is locally projective
if and only if its sections are projective on every member of some affine open cover.
declarations.statement:
theorem isLocallyProjective_iff_exists_affineOpen_cover {X : Scheme.{u}} (M : X.Modules)
    [M.IsQuasicoherent] :
    Scheme.Modules.IsLocallyProjective M ↔
      ∃ (ι : Type u) (U : ι → X.Opens),
        IsOpenCover U ∧
          (∀ i, IsAffineOpen (U i)) ∧
          ∀ i, Module.Projective Γ(X, U i) Γ(M, U i)
declarations.comment: affine open cover characterization

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.isLocallyProjective_tilde_iff_projective
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 05JQ.** The sheaf associated to a module on an affine scheme is
locally projective if and only if the original module is projective.
declarations.statement:
theorem isLocallyProjective_tilde_iff_projective (R : CommRingCat.{u})
    (M : ModuleCat.{u} R) :
    Scheme.Modules.IsLocallyProjective (tilde M) ↔ Module.Projective R M
declarations.comment: affine specialization

declarations.name: Stacks.QcohAlgebraFPColimit.exists_directedSystem_of_isFinitePresentation
declarations.doc:
Let `X` be a quasi-compact and quasi-separated scheme and let `𝒜` be a quasi-coherent sheaf of
commutative `𝒪_X`-algebras. Then there are a directed set `I`, a system `(𝒜ᵢ, φᵢᵢ')` over `I` of
`𝒪_X`-algebras and morphisms `φᵢ : 𝒜ᵢ ⟶ 𝒜` with each `𝒜ᵢ` quasi-coherent of finite
presentation, such that the `φᵢ` induce an isomorphism `colim 𝒜ᵢ ≅ 𝒜`.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_directedSystem_of_isFinitePresentation (X : Scheme.{u}) [CompactSpace ↥X]
    [QuasiSeparatedSpace ↥X] (A : X.QuasicoherentAlgebra)
    (hA : Scheme.QuasicoherentAlgebra.IsQuasicoherent A) :
    ∃ (I : Type (u + 1)) (_ : PartialOrder I) (_ : Nonempty I) (_ : IsDirected I (· ≤ ·))
      (F : Functor I X.QuasicoherentAlgebra) (φ : F ⟶ (Functor.const I).obj A),
      (∀ i, Scheme.QuasicoherentAlgebra.IsQuasicoherent (F.obj i) ∧
        Scheme.QuasicoherentAlgebra.IsOfFinitePresentation (F.obj i)) ∧
        Nonempty (IsColimit (Cocone.mk A φ))

declarations.name: Stacks.AlgebraicGeometry.FiniteTypeSubalgebraFiltered.isFiltered_finiteTypeSubalgebra
declarations.doc:
The finite type quasi-coherent subalgebras of a quasi-coherent sheaf of commutative
`𝒪_X`-algebras form a filtered category. No hypothesis on `X` is needed.

An upper bound of two subalgebras is the image of the morphism to `A` out of the pushed-forward
structure sheaf of the fibre product of their relative spectra, and the category is nonempty
because it contains the image of the initial algebra sheaf `𝒪_X`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isFiltered_finiteTypeSubalgebra {X : Scheme.{u}} (A : AlgebraSheaf X)
    (hA : AlgebraSheaf.IsQuasicoherent A) :
    IsFiltered (FiniteTypeSubalgebras.FiniteTypeSubalgebra A)
declarations.comment: directedness

declarations.name: Stacks.AlgebraicGeometry.FiniteTypeSubalgebraFiltered.nonempty_isColimit_finiteTypeSubalgebraCocone
declarations.doc:
On a quasi-compact and quasi-separated scheme, a quasi-coherent sheaf of commutative
`𝒪_X`-algebras is the colimit of the canonical diagram of its finite type quasi-coherent
subalgebras, with the inclusions of the subobjects as the structure morphisms.

The affine sections hypothesis of `nonempty_isColimit_of_affineSections` is
`Stacks.AlgebraicGeometry.SubalgebraGeneratedByModule.exists_finiteTypeSubalgebra_section`: a
section over an affine open lies in the subalgebra generated by a finite type quasi-coherent
submodule.
declarations.statement:
theorem nonempty_isColimit_finiteTypeSubalgebraCocone {X : Scheme.{u}} [CompactSpace X]
    [QuasiSeparatedSpace X] (A : AlgebraSheaf X) (hA : AlgebraSheaf.IsQuasicoherent A) :
    Nonempty (IsColimit (FiniteTypeSubalgebras.finiteTypeSubalgebraCocone A))
declarations.comment: the colimit

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.Modules.schemeTheoreticSupport
declarations.doc:
**The scheme-theoretic support of a finite type quasi-coherent module**, as an ideal sheaf:
its component at an affine open `U` is the annihilator of the `Γ(X, U)`-module `Γ(F, U)`. The
closed subscheme it cuts out is the smallest one from which `F` is a direct image.
declarations.statement: def schemeTheoreticSupport : X.IdealSheafData
declarations.comment: the closed subscheme

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.Modules.schemeTheoreticSupport_ideal
declarations.doc:
On an affine open `U = Spec A` the scheme-theoretic support of `F` is cut out by the
annihilator of the `A`-module `Γ(F, U)`; equivalently, if `F|_U` is `M~` then the
scheme-theoretic support meets `U` in `Spec (A / Ann_A M)`.
declarations.statement:
theorem schemeTheoreticSupport_ideal (U : X.affineOpens) :
    (schemeTheoreticSupport F).ideal U = Module.annihilator Γ(X, U.1) Γ(F, U.1)
declarations.comment: part (1): affine annihilator formula

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.Modules.exists_module_on_schemeTheoreticSupport
declarations.doc:
A quasi-coherent module of finite type is the direct image of a quasi-coherent module of
finite type on its scheme-theoretic support.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_module_on_schemeTheoreticSupport :
    ∃ G : (schemeTheoreticSupport F).subscheme.Modules,
      G.IsQuasicoherent ∧ G.IsFiniteType ∧
        Nonempty ((Scheme.Modules.pushforward
          (schemeTheoreticSupport F).subschemeι).obj G ≅ F)
declarations.comment: existence of the descended module

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.Modules.schemeTheoreticSupport_isSmallest
declarations.doc:
Every closed subscheme of `X` from which `F` is a direct image contains the
scheme-theoretic support of `F`; equivalently, its ideal sheaf is contained in the ideal sheaf
of the scheme-theoretic support.
declarations.statement:
theorem schemeTheoreticSupport_isSmallest (J : X.IdealSheafData)
    (G : J.subscheme.Modules)
    (e : (Scheme.Modules.pushforward J.subschemeι).obj G ≅ F) :
    J ≤ schemeTheoreticSupport F
declarations.comment: minimality

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.Modules.module_on_schemeTheoreticSupport_unique
declarations.doc:
A descent of `F` to its scheme-theoretic support is unique up to a unique isomorphism
compatible with the chosen identifications of the direct images with `F`.
declarations.statement:
theorem module_on_schemeTheoreticSupport_unique
    (G H : (schemeTheoreticSupport F).subscheme.Modules)
    (eG : (Scheme.Modules.pushforward (schemeTheoreticSupport F).subschemeι).obj G ≅ F)
    (eH : (Scheme.Modules.pushforward (schemeTheoreticSupport F).subschemeι).obj H ≅ F) :
    ∃! φ : G ≅ H,
      (Scheme.Modules.pushforward (schemeTheoreticSupport F).subschemeι).map φ.hom ≫
        eH.hom = eG.hom
declarations.comment: part (2): uniqueness

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.Modules.module_on_schemeTheoreticSupport_isFiniteType
declarations.doc: Every descent of `F` to its scheme-theoretic support is of finite type.
declarations.statement:
theorem module_on_schemeTheoreticSupport_isFiniteType
    (G : (schemeTheoreticSupport F).subscheme.Modules)
    (e : (Scheme.Modules.pushforward (schemeTheoreticSupport F).subschemeι).obj G ≅ F) :
    G.IsFiniteType
declarations.comment: part (3): finite type

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.Modules.supp_eq_support_schemeTheoreticSupport
declarations.doc: The support of `F` is the closed set underlying its scheme-theoretic support.
declarations.statement:
theorem supp_eq_support_schemeTheoreticSupport :
    SheafOfModules.supp F = ((schemeTheoreticSupport F).support : Set X)
declarations.comment: part (4): support on the ambient scheme

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.Modules.module_on_schemeTheoreticSupport_support
declarations.doc: A descent of `F` to its scheme-theoretic support has support the whole closed subscheme.
declarations.statement:
theorem module_on_schemeTheoreticSupport_support
    (G : (schemeTheoreticSupport F).subscheme.Modules)
    (e : (Scheme.Modules.pushforward (schemeTheoreticSupport F).subschemeι).obj G ≅ F) :
    SheafOfModules.supp G = Set.univ
declarations.comment: part (4): support on the closed subscheme

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.Modules.schemeTheoreticSupport
declarations.doc:
**The scheme-theoretic support of a finite type quasi-coherent module**, as an ideal sheaf:
its component at an affine open `U` is the annihilator of the `Γ(X, U)`-module `Γ(F, U)`. The
closed subscheme it cuts out is the smallest one from which `F` is a direct image.
declarations.statement: def schemeTheoreticSupport : X.IdealSheafData
declarations.comment: the scheme-theoretic support

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.universallyClosed_tfae
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 05JX.** A quasi-compact morphism is universally closed precisely when all of its
locally finitely presented base changes are closed, or equivalently when its
base changes to all finite-dimensional affine spaces are closed.
declarations.statement:
theorem universallyClosed_tfae {X S : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ S)
    [QuasiCompact f] :
    List.TFAE
      [UniversallyClosed f,
       ∀ (S' : Scheme.{u}) (g : S' ⟶ S),
         LocallyOfFinitePresentation g → IsClosedMap (pullback.snd f g),
       ∀ n : ℕ, IsClosedMap (AffineSpace.map (ULift.{u} (Fin n)) f)]

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.universallyClosed_tfae_valuative
declarations.doc:
For a finite type morphism to a locally Noetherian scheme, universal closedness, closedness
after adjoining any finite number of affine coordinates, the existence part of the valuative
criterion, and its restriction to discrete valuation rings are equivalent.
declarations.statement:
theorem universallyClosed_tfae_valuative {X S : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ S)
    [LocallyOfFiniteType f] [QuasiCompact f] [IsLocallyNoetherian S] :
    List.TFAE
      [ UniversallyClosed f,
        ∀ n : ℕ, IsClosedMap (AffineSpace.map (ULift.{u} (Fin n)) f),
        ValuativeCriterion.Existence f,
        ∀ (D : ValuativeCommSq f), IsDiscreteValuationRing D.R → D.commSq.HasLift ]

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.isLocallyProjective_of_pullback_fpqc
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 05JZ.** Local projectivity of a quasi-coherent module descends
along an fpqc covering.
declarations.statement:
theorem isLocallyProjective_of_pullback_fpqc {X : Scheme.{u}} (F : X.Modules)
    (hF : F.IsQuasicoherent) {I : Type v} (X' : I → Scheme.{u}) (f : ∀ i, X' i ⟶ X)
    (hfpqc : Presieve.ofArrows X' f ∈ Scheme.fpqcPrecoverage X)
    (hprojective : ∀ i,
      Scheme.Modules.IsLocallyProjective ((Scheme.Modules.pullback (f i)).obj F)) :
    Scheme.Modules.IsLocallyProjective F

declarations.name: Stacks.FiniteFactorization.exists_isOpenImmersion_isFinite_factorization
declarations.doc:
**Zariski's Main Theorem (Stacks Project, Tag 05K0).**  A quasi-finite separated morphism
`f : X ⟶ S` onto a quasi-compact quasi-separated scheme factors as a quasi-compact open
immersion `j : X ⟶ T` followed by a finite morphism `π : T ⟶ S`.

Quasi-finiteness is Stacks 02NG, that is, locally quasi-finite and of finite type, which in
Mathlib's vocabulary is `AlgebraicGeometry.LocallyQuasiFinite`,
`AlgebraicGeometry.LocallyOfFiniteType` and `AlgebraicGeometry.QuasiCompact` together.

The affine case of the factorization, [Stacks, Tag 03GU], is
`AlgebraicGeometry.exists_isOpenImmersion_isFinite_factorization`; it is a different statement
and is not used here.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_isOpenImmersion_isFinite_factorization {X S : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ S)
    [IsSeparated f] [LocallyQuasiFinite f] [LocallyOfFiniteType f] [QuasiCompact f]
    [CompactSpace S] [QuasiSeparatedSpace S] :
    ∃ (T : Scheme.{u}) (j : X ⟶ T) (π : T ⟶ S),
      IsOpenImmersion j ∧ QuasiCompact j ∧ IsFinite π ∧ f = j ≫ π

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.isPureAlong_iff_pushforward
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 05K1.** Purity along a fibre is unchanged by pushing a finite type
quasi-coherent module forward along a closed immersion.
declarations.statement:
theorem isPureAlong_iff_pushforward :
    IsPureAlong (prePureSituationComp i f F s) ↔
      IsPureAlong (prePureSituationPushforward i f F s)
declarations.comment: purity along the fibre

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.isUniversallyPureAlong_iff_pushforward
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 05K1.** Universal purity along a fibre is unchanged by pushing a finite
type quasi-coherent module forward along a closed immersion.
declarations.statement:
theorem isUniversallyPureAlong_iff_pushforward :
    IsUniversallyPureAlong (prePureSituationComp i f F s) ↔
      IsUniversallyPureAlong (prePureSituationPushforward i f F s)
declarations.comment: universal purity along the fibre

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.isUniversallyPureRelative_of_support_isProperOver
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 05K3, part (1).** A finite type quasi-coherent module whose support is
proper over the base is universally pure relative to that base.
declarations.statement:
theorem isUniversallyPureRelative_of_support_isProperOver {X S : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ S)
    [LocallyOfFiniteType f] [QuasiCompact f] (F : X.Modules) [F.IsFiniteType]
    [F.IsQuasicoherent]
    (hF : IsProperOver f (⟨SheafOfModules.supp F, SheafOfModules.isClosed_supp F⟩ : Closeds X)) :
    IsUniversallyPureRelative f F
declarations.comment: part (1)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.isUniversallyPureRelative_of_isProper
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 05K3, part (2).** A finite type quasi-coherent module on a scheme which
is proper over the base is universally pure relative to that base.
declarations.statement:
theorem isUniversallyPureRelative_of_isProper {X S : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ S) [IsProper f]
    (F : X.Modules) [F.IsFiniteType] [F.IsQuasicoherent] :
    IsUniversallyPureRelative f F
declarations.comment: part (2)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.isSchemeUniversallyPureRelative_of_isProper
declarations.doc: **Stacks Project, Tag 05K3, part (3).** A proper scheme is universally pure over its base.
declarations.statement:
theorem isSchemeUniversallyPureRelative_of_isProper {X S : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ S) [IsProper f] :
    @IsUniversallyPureRelative.{u} X S f _ _ (SheafOfModules.unit.{u} X.ringCatSheaf)
      (structureSheaf_isFiniteType X)
      (Stacks.AlgebraicGeometry.AffineQcohPushforward.isQuasicoherent_unit X)
declarations.comment: part (3)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.isPureRelative_iff_isFinite_schemeTheoreticSupport
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 05K4, conditions (1) and (2).** Let `f : X ⟶ S` be separated of finite
type and let `ℱ` be a finite type quasi-coherent `𝒪_X`-module with finite support on every fibre
of `f`. Then `ℱ` is pure relative to `S` if and only if its scheme-theoretic support is finite
over `S`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isPureRelative_iff_isFinite_schemeTheoreticSupport {X S : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ S)
    [LocallyOfFiniteType f] [QuasiCompact f] [IsSeparated f] (F : X.Modules) [F.IsFiniteType]
    [F.IsQuasicoherent]
    (hfinite : ∀ s : S,
      (SheafOfModules.supp ((Scheme.Modules.pullback (f.fiberι s)).obj F)).Finite) :
    IsPureRelative f F ↔
      IsFinite ((Scheme.Modules.schemeTheoreticSupport F).subschemeι ≫ f)
declarations.comment: conditions (1) and (2)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.isUniversallyPureRelative_iff_isFinite_schemeTheoreticSupport
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 05K4, conditions (2) and (3).** Let `f : X ⟶ S` be separated of finite
type and let `ℱ` be a finite type quasi-coherent `𝒪_X`-module with finite support on every fibre
of `f`. Then `ℱ` is universally pure relative to `S` if and only if its scheme-theoretic support
is finite over `S`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isUniversallyPureRelative_iff_isFinite_schemeTheoreticSupport {X S : Scheme.{u}}
    (f : X ⟶ S) [LocallyOfFiniteType f] [QuasiCompact f] [IsSeparated f] (F : X.Modules)
    [F.IsFiniteType] [F.IsQuasicoherent]
    (hfinite : ∀ s : S,
      (SheafOfModules.supp ((Scheme.Modules.pullback (f.fiberι s)).obj F)).Finite) :
    IsUniversallyPureRelative f F ↔
      IsFinite ((Scheme.Modules.schemeTheoreticSupport F).subschemeι ≫ f)
declarations.comment: conditions (2) and (3)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.isSchemePureRelative_iff_isFinite
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 05K4, in particular.** A separated quasi-finite scheme over `S` is pure
relative to `S` if and only if its structure morphism is finite.
declarations.statement:
theorem isSchemePureRelative_iff_isFinite {X S : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ S)
    [LocallyOfFiniteType f] [QuasiCompact f] [LocallyQuasiFinite f] [IsSeparated f] :
    IsSchemePureRelative f ↔ IsFinite f
declarations.comment: in particular: quasi-finite separated morphisms

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.universallyPure_of_flat_geometricallyIntegral
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 05K5.** A flat finite type morphism with geometrically integral
fibres has universally pure structure sheaf over its base.
declarations.statement:
theorem universallyPure_of_flat_geometricallyIntegral {X S : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ S)
    [LocallyOfFiniteType f] [QuasiCompact f] [Flat f] [GeometricallyIntegral f] :
    @IsUniversallyPureRelative.{u} X S f _ _
      (SheafOfModules.unit.{u} X.ringCatSheaf)
      (structureSheaf_isFiniteType X)
      (Stacks.AlgebraicGeometry.AffineQcohPushforward.isQuasicoherent_unit X)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.isUniversallyPureRelative_of_pushforward_isLocallyProjective
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 05K6.** For an affine morphism of finite type, a finite type
quasi-coherent module with locally projective direct image is universally pure over the base.

The affine base change used along the way is the third assertion of Stacks Tag 02KG,
`Stacks.AlgebraicGeometry.AffineBaseChangeLocality.baseChangeIso`, bound to `bc` below and
threaded through the private lemmas in the shape in which they take it.
declarations.statement:
public theorem isUniversallyPureRelative_of_pushforward_isLocallyProjective
    {X S : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ S) [LocallyOfFiniteType f] [IsAffineHom f]
    (F : X.Modules) [F.IsFiniteType] [F.IsQuasicoherent]
    (hF : Scheme.Modules.IsLocallyProjective ((Scheme.Modules.pushforward f).obj F)) :
    IsUniversallyPureRelative f F

declarations.name: ideal_eq_mul_colon_of_isPrincipal
declarations.doc:
For a commutative ring `R`, a principal ideal `J` and an ideal `I` with
`I ≤ J`, the ideal `I` factors as the product of `J` with the colon ideal
`(I : J)`.
declarations.statement:
theorem ideal_eq_mul_colon_of_isPrincipal {R : Type*} [CommRing R]
    (I J : Ideal R) (hJ : J.IsPrincipal) (hIJ : I ≤ J) :
    I = J * (I.colon J)

declarations.name: isOkaFamilyUniversal_meetsSubmonoidFamily
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Tag 05KA.** For a commutative semiring `R` and a multiplicative subset
`S` of `R`, the family of ideals meeting `S` is an Oka family.
declarations.statement:
theorem isOkaFamilyUniversal_meetsSubmonoidFamily {R : Type*} [CommSemiring R]
    (S : Submonoid R) : IsOkaFamilyUniversal (meetsSubmonoidFamily S)

declarations.name: Stacks.Algebra.OkaFamily.Ideal.oka_generators_and_isOka_fg
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Tag 05KB.** Let `R` be a ring, `I ⊆ R` an ideal and `a ∈ R`. If `(I : a)` is
generated by `a₁, …, aₙ` and `(I, a)` is generated by `a, b₁, …, bₘ` with `b₁, …, bₘ ∈ I`, then
`I` is generated by `aa₁, …, aaₙ, b₁, …, bₘ`; and the family of finitely generated ideals is an
Oka family. The second part is Mathlib's `Ideal.isOka_fg`.
declarations.statement:
theorem Ideal.oka_generators_and_isOka_fg (R : Type*) [CommRing R] :
    (∀ (I : Ideal R) (a : R) (n m : ℕ) (α : Fin n → R) (β : Fin m → R),
      I.colon (Ideal.span {a}) = Ideal.span (Set.range α) →
      I ⊔ Ideal.span {a} = Ideal.span (insert a (Set.range β)) → (∀ j, β j ∈ I) →
      I = Ideal.span (Set.range (fun i => a * α i) ∪ Set.range β)) ∧
    _root_.Ideal.IsOka (Submodule.FG (R := R) (M := R))

registrations.name: Ideal.isOka_fg
registrations.comment: (1): `Ideal.FG` is an Oka predicate

registrations.name: Ideal.IsOka.isPrime_of_maximal_not
registrations.comment: (1), for the Oka family `Submodule.IsPrincipal` (`Ideal.isOka_isPrincipal`)

declarations.name: Ideal.isPrime_of_maximal_disjoint_nonZeroDivisors
declarations.doc: An ideal maximal among the ideals which do not contain a nonzerodivisor is prime.
declarations.statement:
theorem Ideal.isPrime_of_maximal_disjoint_nonZeroDivisors {R : Type*} [CommSemiring R]
    (I : Ideal R) (hI : Maximal (fun J : Ideal R ↦ Disjoint (J : Set R) (R⁰ : Set R)) I) :
    I.IsPrime

declarations.name: isDomain_of_forall_nonzero_prime_containsNonZeroDivisor
declarations.doc:
(Characterization of a domain.) If `R` is nonzero and every nonzero prime
ideal of `R` contains a nonzerodivisor, then `R` is a domain.
declarations.statement:
theorem isDomain_of_forall_nonzero_prime_containsNonZeroDivisor [Nontrivial R]
    (h : ∀ P : Ideal R, P.IsPrime → P ≠ ⊥ →
      ¬ Disjoint (P : Set R) (nonZeroDivisors R : Set R)) :
    IsDomain R

declarations.name: pure_fg_tfae
declarations.statement:
theorem pure_fg_tfae (R : Type*) [CommRing R] (I : Ideal R) :
    [ -- (1) `I` is pure and finitely generated
      I.IsPure ∧ I.FG,
      -- (2) `I` is generated by an idempotent
      ∃ e : R, e ^ 2 = e ∧ I = Ideal.span {e},
      -- (3) `I` is pure and `V(I)` is open in `Spec(R)`
      I.IsPure ∧ IsOpen (PrimeSpectrum.zeroLocus (I : Set R)),
      -- (4) `R/I` is a projective `R`-module
      Module.Projective R (R ⧸ I) ].TFAE

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.relativeAssassin_pullback_subset_preimage
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 05KL.** After arbitrary base change, the relative assassin of the
pulled-back module is contained in the inverse image of the original relative assassin.
declarations.statement:
public theorem relativeAssassin_pullback_subset_preimage
    {X S S' : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ S) (g : S' ⟶ S) (F : X.Modules)
    [F.IsQuasicoherent] [LocallyOfFiniteType f] :
    Stacks.Divisors.relativeAssassin (pullback.snd (C := Scheme.{u}) f g)
        ((Scheme.Modules.pullback (pullback.fst (C := Scheme.{u}) f g)).obj F) ⊆
      (pullback.fst (C := Scheme.{u}) f g) ⁻¹'
        Stacks.Divisors.relativeAssassin f F
declarations.comment: unconditional containment

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.preimage_relativeAssassin_eq_pullback_of_locallyQuasiFinite
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 05KL.** A locally quasi-finite base change pulls the relative
assassin back exactly.
declarations.statement:
public theorem preimage_relativeAssassin_eq_pullback_of_locallyQuasiFinite
    {X S S' : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ S) (g : S' ⟶ S) (F : X.Modules)
    [F.IsQuasicoherent] [LocallyOfFiniteType f]
    [LocallyOfFiniteType g] [LocallyQuasiFinite g] :
    (pullback.fst (C := Scheme.{u}) f g) ⁻¹' Stacks.Divisors.relativeAssassin f F =
      Stacks.Divisors.relativeAssassin (pullback.snd (C := Scheme.{u}) f g)
        ((Scheme.Modules.pullback (pullback.fst (C := Scheme.{u}) f g)).obj F)
declarations.comment: equality for locally quasi-finite base change

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.preimage_relativeAssassin_eq_pullback_of_isAlgebraic_residueField
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 05KL.** If every residue-field extension induced by the base-change
morphism is algebraic, then it pulls the relative assassin back exactly.
declarations.statement:
public theorem preimage_relativeAssassin_eq_pullback_of_isAlgebraic_residueField
    {X S S' : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ S) (g : S' ⟶ S) (F : X.Modules)
    [F.IsQuasicoherent] [LocallyOfFiniteType f]
    (hg : ∀ s' : S',
      letI := (g.residueFieldMap s').hom.toAlgebra
      Algebra.IsAlgebraic (S.residueField (g s')) (S'.residueField s')) :
    (pullback.fst (C := Scheme.{u}) f g) ⁻¹' Stacks.Divisors.relativeAssassin f F =
      Stacks.Divisors.relativeAssassin (pullback.snd (C := Scheme.{u}) f g)
        ((Scheme.Modules.pullback (pullback.fst (C := Scheme.{u}) f g)).obj F)
declarations.comment: equality for algebraic residue-field extensions

declarations.name: Stacks.RelativeAssassin.exists_open_forall_not_associatedPoints_fibre_subset
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 05KN.** Let `f : X ⟶ Y` be a finite type morphism, `F` a
quasi-coherent `𝒪_X`-module of finite type and `U ⊆ X` open, and let `Y` be irreducible with
generic point `η`. If the associated points of `F` on the fibre over `η` are not all contained
in `U`, then the same failure of containment holds on the fibre over every point of some
nonempty open of `Y`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem exists_open_forall_not_associatedPoints_fibre_subset {X Y : Scheme.{u}}
    (f : X ⟶ Y) [LocallyOfFiniteType f] [QuasiCompact f]
    (F : X.Modules) [F.IsQuasicoherent] [F.IsFiniteType] (U : X.Opens)
    [IrreducibleSpace Y] (η : Y) (hη : IsGenericPoint η Set.univ)
    (hηU : ¬ Stacks.Divisors.associatedPoints
        ((Scheme.Modules.pullback (f.fiberι η)).obj F) ⊆ f.fiberι η ⁻¹' (U : Set X)) :
    ∃ V : Y.Opens, (V : Set Y).Nonempty ∧ ∀ y ∈ V,
      ¬ Stacks.Divisors.associatedPoints
        ((Scheme.Modules.pullback (f.fiberι y)).obj F) ⊆ f.fiberι y ⁻¹' (U : Set X)

declarations.name: Stacks.Divisors.exists_open_associatedPoints_fiber_subset
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 05KP.** Let `f : X ⟶ Y` be a finite type morphism of schemes, `F` a
finite type quasi-coherent module on `X` and `U ⊆ X` open. If `Y` is irreducible with generic
point `η` and all associated points of `F` restricted to the fibre over `η` lie in `U`, then
there is a nonempty open `V ⊆ Y` such that the same containment holds in the fibre over every
point of `V`.

The target is replaced by its reduction, which is integral because the closed immersion of the
reduction is a homeomorphism, and the containment is transported across that base change by
Stacks 05KQ.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_open_associatedPoints_fiber_subset {X Y : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ Y)
    (F : X.Modules) [LocallyOfFiniteType f] [QuasiCompact f] [F.IsQuasicoherent]
    [F.IsFiniteType] [IrreducibleSpace Y] (U : X.Opens) (η : Y)
    (hη : IsGenericPoint η Set.univ)
    (hηU : associatedPoints ((Scheme.Modules.pullback (f.fiberι η)).obj F) ⊆
      (f.fiberι η) ⁻¹' (U : Set X)) :
    ∃ V : Y.Opens, (V : Set Y).Nonempty ∧ ∀ y ∈ V,
      associatedPoints ((Scheme.Modules.pullback (f.fiberι y)).obj F) ⊆
        (f.fiberι y) ⁻¹' (U : Set X)

declarations.name: Stacks.RelativeAssassin.associatedPoints_fiber_subset_preimage_iff_baseChange
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 05KQ.** After arbitrary base change, the associated points of the
pullback module on a fibre lie in the pulled-back open exactly when they did so on the original
fibre.
declarations.statement:
theorem associatedPoints_fiber_subset_preimage_iff_baseChange
    {X S S' : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ S) [LocallyOfFiniteType f]
    (F : X.Modules) [F.IsQuasicoherent] [F.IsFiniteType]
    (U : X.Opens) (g : S' ⟶ S) (s' : S') :
    Stacks.Divisors.associatedPoints
          ((Scheme.Modules.pullback (f.fiberι (g s'))).obj F) ⊆
        (f.fiberι (g s')) ⁻¹' (U : Set X) ↔
      Stacks.Divisors.associatedPoints
            ((Scheme.Modules.pullback ((pullback.snd f g).fiberι s')).obj
              ((Scheme.Modules.pullback (pullback.fst f g)).obj F)) ⊆
          ((pullback.snd f g).fiberι s') ⁻¹'
            ((pullback.fst f g) ⁻¹' (U : Set X))

declarations.name: Stacks.RelativeAssassin.isLocallyConstructible_fibrewiseContainment
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 05KR.** Let `f : X ⟶ Y` be a morphism of finite presentation, let `F`
be a quasi-coherent `𝒪_X`-module of finite presentation and let `U ⊆ X` be an open subscheme
with `U ⟶ Y` quasi-compact. Then the set of points `y` of `Y` over which every associated point
of the fibre `F_y` lies in the fibre `U_y` is locally constructible in `Y`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isLocallyConstructible_fibrewiseContainment (f : X ⟶ Y)
    (hf : AlgebraicGeometry.FinitePresentation f) (F : X.Modules) [F.IsQuasicoherent]
    [F.IsFinitePresentation] (U : X.Opens) [QuasiCompact (U.ι ≫ f)] :
    IsLocallyConstructible (fibrewiseContainment f F U)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.instIsFilteredOppositeElementaryEtaleNeighborhood
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 05KS.** The opposite of the category of elementary
étale neighborhoods of a point is filtered.
declarations.statement:
instance instIsFilteredOppositeElementaryEtaleNeighborhood
    (S : Scheme.{u}) (s : S) :
    IsFiltered (ElementaryEtaleNeighborhood S s)ᵒᵖ
declarations.comment: the indexing category is filtered

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.isColimit_globalSections
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 05KS.** A henselization of the local ring of a
scheme at a point is a colimit of the rings of global sections of its
elementary étale neighborhoods.
declarations.statement:
lemma isColimit_globalSections (S : Scheme.{u}) (s : S)
    (Rh : Type u) [CommRing Rh] [IsLocalRing Rh]
    [Algebra (S.presheaf.stalk s) Rh]
    [IsLocalRing.IsHenselization (S.presheaf.stalk s)
      (IsLocalRing.ResidueField (S.presheaf.stalk s)) Rh] :
    ∃ ι : globalSections S s ⟶
        (Functor.const _).obj (CommRingCat.of Rh),
      (∀ U x, IsLocalRing.residue Rh ((ι.app U).hom x) =
        henselizationResidueFieldMap S s Rh
          (elementaryEtaleAugmentation S s U.unop x)) ∧
      (∀ U : (ElementaryEtaleNeighborhood S s)ᵒᵖ,
        IsOverStalk S s Rh U.unop (ι.app U).hom) ∧
      (∀ ι' : globalSections S s ⟶ (Functor.const _).obj (CommRingCat.of Rh),
        (∀ U x, IsLocalRing.residue Rh ((ι'.app U).hom x) =
          henselizationResidueFieldMap S s Rh
            (elementaryEtaleAugmentation S s U.unop x)) →
        (∀ U : (ElementaryEtaleNeighborhood S s)ᵒᵖ,
          IsOverStalk S s Rh U.unop (ι'.app U).hom) → ι' = ι) ∧
      Nonempty (IsColimit (Cocone.mk _ ι))
declarations.comment: the henselization is the colimit

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.ElementaryEtaleFlatness.exists_elementaryEtaleNeighborhood_open_flat
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 05KT.** Flatness at a point of a finite type quasi-coherent module
spreads to an open neighbourhood after base change to the local scheme of a suitable
elementary étale neighbourhood of the image point.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_elementaryEtaleNeighborhood_open_flat
    {X S : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ S) [LocallyOfFiniteType f]
    (F : X.Modules) [F.IsQuasicoherent] [F.IsFiniteType]
    (x : X)
    (hF : AlgebraicGeometry.IsFlatOverAt f.toLRSHom.toShHom F x) :
    ∃ (U : AlgebraicGeometry.EtaleNeighborhood S (f x)) (_ : U.IsElementary),
      let g := U.scheme.fromSpecStalk U.point ≫ U.toBase
      let P : Scheme.{u} := pullback f g
      ∃ (z : P) (_ : pullback.fst f g z = x)
      (_ : ∀ z' : P, pullback.fst f g z' = x → z' = z) (V : P.Opens),
      z ∈ V ∧
        AlgebraicGeometry.IsFlatOver
          (((V.ι : V.toScheme ⟶ P) ≫ pullback.snd f g).toLRSHom.toShHom)
          ((Scheme.Modules.pullback
            ((V.ι : V.toScheme ⟶ P) ≫ pullback.fst f g)).obj F)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.existsElementaryEtaleNeighborhoodFlatOver
declarations.doc:
For a morphism `f : X ⟶ S` locally of finite type and a quasi-coherent `𝒪_X`-module `F` of
finite type which is flat over `S` at `x`, there is an elementary étale neighbourhood `(S', s')` of
`(S, f x)` and an open subscheme of `X ×_S Spec 𝒪_{S', s'}` containing the unique point over `x` on
which the pullback of `F` is flat over `𝒪_{S', s'}`.
declarations.statement:
theorem existsElementaryEtaleNeighborhoodFlatOver :
    ExistsElementaryEtaleNeighborhoodFlatOver.{u}

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.exists_elementaryEtaleNeighborhood_isFinitePresentation_isFlatOver_fiber
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 05KU.** Let `f : X ⟶ S` be of finite presentation, let `F` be a
quasi-coherent `𝒪_X`-module of finite type, and let `s` be a point of `S` such that `F` is flat
over `S` at every point of the fibre `X_s`. Then there are an elementary étale neighbourhood
`(S', s')` of `(S, s)` and an open `V ⊆ X ×_S Spec 𝒪_{S', s'}` containing the whole fibre
`X_s = X ×_S s'` such that the pullback of `F` to `V` is of finite presentation as an
`𝒪_V`-module and flat over `𝒪_{S', s'}`.

The fibre `X ×_S s'` is read as the set of points of `X ×_S Spec 𝒪_{S', s'}` whose image in `X`
lies over `s`.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_elementaryEtaleNeighborhood_isFinitePresentation_isFlatOver_fiber
    {X S : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ S) (hf : FinitePresentation f) (F : X.Modules)
    [F.IsQuasicoherent] [F.IsFiniteType] (s : S)
    (hflat : ∀ x : X, f x = s → IsFlatOverAt f.toLRSHom.toShHom F x) :
    ∃ (U : EtaleNeighborhood S s) (_ : U.IsElementary)
      (V : (pullback f (U.scheme.fromSpecStalk U.point ≫ U.toBase)).Opens),
      (∀ z : ↑(pullback f (U.scheme.fromSpecStalk U.point ≫ U.toBase)),
          f (pullback.fst f (U.scheme.fromSpecStalk U.point ≫ U.toBase) z) = s → z ∈ V) ∧
      ((Scheme.Modules.pullback (V.ι ≫ pullback.fst f
          (U.scheme.fromSpecStalk U.point ≫ U.toBase))).obj F).IsFinitePresentation ∧
      IsFlatOver
        (V.ι ≫ pullback.snd f
          (U.scheme.fromSpecStalk U.point ≫ U.toBase)).toLRSHom.toShHom
        ((Scheme.Modules.pullback (V.ι ≫ pullback.fst f
          (U.scheme.fromSpecStalk U.point ≫ U.toBase))).obj F)
