declarations.name: Module.FlatAtPointSituation.condition_of_hom
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 05MK.** The flatness condition is preserved by a morphism of the
category `C` of local `A`-algebras; this is what makes `F_lf` a functor.
declarations.statement:
theorem condition_of_hom (S : FlatAtPointSituation.{u, v, w}) {R T : LocalAlgCat.{u, x} S.A}
    (f : R ⟶ T) (h : S.Condition R) : S.Condition T
declarations.comment: base-change stability

declarations.name: Module.FlatAtPointSituation.flatAtPointFunctor
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 05MK.** The functor `F_lf` on the category `C` of local `A`-algebras:
it takes the value a singleton where the flatness condition holds, and the empty set elsewhere.
Functoriality is `condition_of_hom`.
declarations.statement:
def flatAtPointFunctor (S : FlatAtPointSituation.{u, v, w}) :
    LocalAlgCat.{u, x} S.A ⥤ Type
declarations.comment: the functor

declarations.name: Module.FlatAtPointSituation.ConditionOn
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 05ML.** The flatness condition on a local `A`-algebra `R`: the base
change of `M` is flat over `R` at every prime of `B ⊗[A] R` containing the extensions of the
maximal ideals of `R` and of `B`. This is the condition of Stacks Tag 05LQ for the ideals
`I' = m_R` and `J = m_B`.
declarations.statement:
def ConditionOn (S : FlatAtPointSituation.{u, v, w}) (R : Type x) [CommRing R] [IsLocalRing R]
    [Algebra S.A R] : Prop

declarations.name: Module.FlatAtPointSituation.Condition
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 05ML.** The flatness condition read on an object of the category `C`
of Stacks Tag 05MK.
declarations.statement: abbrev Condition (S : FlatAtPointSituation.{u, v, w}) (R : LocalAlgCat.{u, x} S.A) : Prop

declarations.name: Module.FlatAtPointSituation.condition_iff_of_flat
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 05MN part (1)**, read on a morphism of the category `C` of local
`A`-algebras of Stacks Tag 05MK: if `f : R ⟶ T` is flat then `F_lf(R) = F_lf(T)`, both being
determined by the flatness condition of Stacks Tag 05ML.
declarations.comment: flat_base_change

declarations.name: Module.FlatAtPointSituation.flatAtPointFunctor_obj_eq_of_flat
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 05MN part (1)**, in the shape the source states it: the functor `F_lf`
of Stacks Tag 05MM takes the same value at the two ends of a flat morphism of the category `C`.

The values are `PLift` of the flatness condition of Stacks Tag 05ML, so this is
`Module.FlatAtPointSituation.condition_iff_of_flat` read through `propext`.
declarations.statement:
theorem flatAtPointFunctor_obj_eq_of_flat (S : FlatAtPointSituation.{u, v, w})
    {R T : LocalAlgCat.{u, x} S.A} (f : R ⟶ T) (hf : f.hom.toRingHom.Flat) :
    S.flatAtPointFunctor.obj R = S.flatAtPointFunctor.obj T
declarations.comment: flat_base_change

declarations.name: Module.FlatAtPointSituation.condition_colimit_iff
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 05MN part (2)**, as an equivalence: the flatness condition of
Stacks Tag 05ML holds over the apex of a filtered colimit of local `A`-algebras exactly when it
holds at one of the stages. The easy direction is base-change stability,
`Module.FlatAtPointSituation.condition_of_hom`.

Beyond the hypotheses of the source nothing is assumed about the colimit: that it is computed on
the underlying sets, which is what Stacks Tag 05LT needs, is proved in
`Stacks.CommAlgCat.forget_preservesFilteredColimitsOfSize`. The two `UnivLE` hypotheses are the
size condition that result carries, namely that the index category be no larger than the
algebras; a directed system in the sense of the source is indexed by a set and satisfies it.
declarations.statement:
theorem condition_colimit_iff
    (hS : (algebraMap S.A S.B).EssentiallyOfFinitePresentation)
    [Module.FinitePresentation S.B S.M]
    (hτ : IsColimit (toCommAlgCat.mapCocone τ)) :
    S.Condition τ.pt ↔ ∃ lam, S.Condition (F.obj lam)
declarations.comment: limit_preserving

declarations.name: Module.FlatAtPointSituation.isColimitMapCoconeFlatAtPointFunctor
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 05MN part (2).** If `A → B` is essentially of finite presentation and
`M` is a `B`-module of finite presentation, then the functor `F_lf` of Stacks Tag 05MM is limit
preserving: for a directed system `{A_i}` of objects of the category `C` of Stacks Tag 05MK,
`F_lf(colim A_i) = colim F_lf(A_i)`.

The colimit of the system is read off the underlying system of `A`-algebras; it does lie in `C`,
by `LocalAlgCat.isLocalRing_pt_of_isColimit` and `LocalAlgCat.isLocalHom_ι_of_isColimit`. The
statement is that the induced cocone of sets is a colimit, which by
`CategoryTheory.Limits.Types.FilteredColimit.isColimitOf` amounts to the descent statement
`Module.FlatAtPointSituation.exists_condition_of_isColimit`, every value of `F_lf` having at
most one element.

That the colimit of `A`-algebras is computed on the underlying sets is not assumed but proved,
in `Stacks.CommAlgCat.forget_preservesFilteredColimitsOfSize`; the two `UnivLE` hypotheses are
the size condition it carries, that the index category of the directed system be no larger than
the algebras.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def isColimitMapCoconeFlatAtPointFunctor
    (hS : (algebraMap S.A S.B).EssentiallyOfFinitePresentation)
    [Module.FinitePresentation S.B S.M]
    (hτ : IsColimit (toCommAlgCat.mapCocone τ)) :
    IsColimit (S.flatAtPointFunctor.mapCocone τ)
declarations.comment: limit_preserving

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.FreeAtGenericPointsSituation
declarations.doc:
The standing situation of a smooth morphism with geometrically irreducible fibres and a
finite type quasi-coherent module on its source.
declarations.statement: structure FreeAtGenericPointsSituation
declarations.comment: the situation

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.FreeAtGenericPointsSituation.Condition
declarations.doc:
The module pulled back to `X ×_S T` is free of rank `p` near the generic point of
every fibre over `T`.
declarations.statement:
abbrev Condition (D : FreeAtGenericPointsSituation.{u}) (p : ℕ)
    (T : Over D.S) : Prop
declarations.comment: the fibrewise condition

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.FreeAtGenericPointsSituation.condition_of_hom
declarations.doc: The fibrewise generic-point condition is preserved by a further base change.
declarations.statement:
theorem condition_of_hom (D : FreeAtGenericPointsSituation.{u}) (p : ℕ)
    {T T' : Over D.S} (g : T' ⟶ T) (h : D.Condition p T) :
    D.Condition p T'
declarations.comment: base-change stability

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.FreeAtGenericPointsSituation.freeAtGenericPointsFunctor
declarations.doc:
The subterminal set-valued functor recording whether the pulled-back module is free of
rank `p` near the generic point of every fibre.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def freeAtGenericPointsFunctor
    (D : FreeAtGenericPointsSituation.{u}) (p : ℕ) :
    (Over D.S)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u
declarations.comment: the functor

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.FreeAtGenericPointsSituation.freeAtGenericPointsFunctor_limitPreserving_small
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 05MS, part (2).** The generic-rank functor of a module of finite
presentation is limit preserving: over a cofiltered limit of affine schemes over the base the
functor has a section as soon as one stage of the system has one.

The approximation statement which `freeAtGenericPointsFunctor_limitPreserving_small_iff`
identifies with this clause is
`AlgebraicGeometry.FreeAtGenericPointsSituation.exists_condition_of_isLimit`, so nothing is
assumed here.
declarations.statement:
theorem freeAtGenericPointsFunctor_limitPreserving_small [D.F.IsFinitePresentation] :
    LimitPreserving.{u, u, u, u, u + 1, u} (Over.forget D.S)
      (D.freeAtGenericPointsFunctor p)
declarations.comment: part (2), the generic-rank functor is limit preserving

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.FreeAtGenericPointsSituation.freeAtGenericPointsFunctor_isSheaf_fpqc
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 05MS, part (1).** The generic-rank functor satisfies the sheaf property
for the fpqc topology.

By `freeAtGenericPointsFunctor_isSheaf_fpqc_of_fpqcCover` this is fpqc-locality of the
generic-point condition, and the source proves that locality in two steps: descent along the
covering gives a free stalk of rank `p` at the generic point of every fibre over the base
(`stalkFreeOfRank_of_fpqcCover`), and
`AlgebraicGeometry.freeAtPointOfRank_of_forall_stalkFreeOfRank` spreads those free stalks out to
neighbourhoods.
declarations.statement:
theorem freeAtGenericPointsFunctor_isSheaf_fpqc (D : FreeAtGenericPointsSituation.{u}) (p : ℕ) :
    Presheaf.IsSheaf (Scheme.fpqcTopology.over D.S) (D.freeAtGenericPointsFunctor p)
declarations.comment: part (1), the generic-rank functor is an fpqc sheaf

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.FlatDimensionSituation
declarations.doc:
A morphism of schemes `f : X ⟶ S` locally of finite type together with a quasi-coherent
module `F` of finite type on `X` and a bound `n` on fibre dimensions.
declarations.statement: public structure FlatDimensionSituation
declarations.comment: the situation

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.FlatDimensionSituation.baseChangeMap
declarations.doc: The base-changed morphism `X_T = X ×_S T ⟶ T`.
declarations.statement:
public noncomputable abbrev baseChangeMap (D : FlatDimensionSituation.{u}) (T : Over D.S) :

declarations.comment: the base-changed morphism

The base change `F_T` of the module, i.e. its pullback along the projection
`X_T = X ×_S T ⟶ X`.

declarations.doc: The base-changed morphism `X_T ⟶ T` is again locally of finite type.

public noncomputable instance baseChangeModule_isFiniteType (D : FlatDimensionSituation.{u})

declarations.comment: F_T is of finite type

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.FlatDimensionSituation.IsFlatInDimensionsGEAfterBaseChange
declarations.doc: The base-changed module `F_T` is flat over `T` in dimensions `≥ n`.
declarations.statement:
public noncomputable abbrev IsFlatInDimensionsGEAfterBaseChange
    (D : FlatDimensionSituation.{u}) (T : Over D.S) : Prop
declarations.comment: the condition tested by the functor

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.FlatDimensionSituation.isFlatInDimensionsGEAfterBaseChange_of_hom
declarations.doc:
Flatness of the base-changed module in dimensions `≥ n` is inherited along a morphism
`T' ⟶ T` of schemes over `S`.
declarations.comment: base-change stability of the condition

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.FlatDimensionSituation.flatDimensionFunctor
declarations.doc:
The functor `F_n : (Sch/S)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Sets` sending a scheme `T` over `S` to a singleton if `F_T`
is flat over `T` in dimensions `≥ n`, and to the empty set otherwise.
declarations.statement:
public noncomputable def flatDimensionFunctor (D : FlatDimensionSituation.{u}) :
    (Over D.S)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type
declarations.comment: the functor F_n

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.FlatDimensionSituation.flatDimensionFunctor_isSheaf_fpqc_and_limitPreserving
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 05MV.** In Situation 05MT:

1. the functor `F_n` satisfies the sheaf property for the fpqc topology; and
2. if `f` is quasi-compact and locally of finite presentation and `F` is of finite presentation,
   then the functor `F_n` is limit preserving, i.e. it carries a cofiltered inverse limit of
   affine schemes over `S` to a filtered colimit of sets.

The three finiteness assumptions of (2) are hypotheses of (2) only: (1) holds in the ambient
situation alone.
declarations.statement:
public theorem flatDimensionFunctor_isSheaf_fpqc_and_limitPreserving
    (D : FlatDimensionSituation.{max u v w}) :
    Presheaf.IsSheaf (Scheme.fpqcTopology.over D.S) D.flatDimensionFunctor ∧
      (QuasiCompact D.f → LocallyOfFinitePresentation D.f → D.F.IsFinitePresentation →
        LimitPreserving.{max u v w, 0, v, w, max u v w + 1, max u v w}
          (Over.forget D.S) D.flatDimensionFunctor)
declarations.comment: parts (1) and (2)

declarations.doc: A morphism of schemes together with a quasi-coherent module on its source.
declarations.statement: public structure FlatnessSituation

declarations.doc: The fibre product `X ×_S T`.

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.FlatnessSituation.flatFunctor_isSheaf_fpqc
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 05MY.** Part (1): the flatness functor of a quasi-coherent module
satisfies the sheaf condition for the fpqc topology on schemes over the base.
declarations.statement:
public theorem flatFunctor_isSheaf_fpqc :
    Presheaf.IsSheaf (Scheme.fpqcTopology.over D.S) D.flatFunctor
declarations.comment: flat_functor_fpqc_sheaf

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.FlatnessSituation.flatFunctor_limitPreserving
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 05MY.** Part (2): for a quasi-compact morphism which is locally of
finite presentation and a quasi-coherent module of finite presentation, the flatness functor is
limit preserving: it carries a cofiltered inverse limit of affine schemes over the base to a
filtered colimit of sets.
declarations.comment: flat_functor_limit_preserving

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isLocallyOfFinitePresentation_terminal_iff_limitPreserving
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 05N0.** An algebraic space `X` over a scheme `S` is locally of finite
presentation over `S` if and only if `X`, read as a functor on the big fppf site of `S`, is
limit preserving.

This is the case of Stacks 04AK in which the target is the terminal presheaf, so that the
morphism is the structure morphism of `X` to `S`. Only the implication (1) ⇒ (2) of Stacks
04AK is used; the converse is obtained from Stacks 0CM6 instead, so no undischarged
hypothesis enters. Compare Stacks 05LX,
`AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.locallyOfFinitePresentation_iff_isLimitPreserving_yoneda`, which is
this statement for a scheme.
declarations.statement:
theorem isLocallyOfFinitePresentation_terminal_iff_limitPreserving
    {X : (BigFppfOver B S hS)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u} (hX : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS X) :
    IsLocallyOfFinitePresentation B S hS (terminal.from X) ↔
      LimitPreserving.{u, u, u, u, u + 1, u} (BigFppfOver.toScheme B S hS) X

declarations.name: Ordinal.exists_factorization_of_mk_lt_cof
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 05N2.** Let `β` be an ordinal and `(F_α)_{α < β}` an ordinal-indexed direct
system with colimit `DirectLimit F f` and canonical maps `ι_α : F_α → DirectLimit F f`,
`x ↦ ⟦⟨α, x⟩⟧`. Let `S` be a set and `φ : S → DirectLimit F f` a function. If the
cofinality of `β` exceeds the cardinality of `S`, then `φ` factors through a single stage:
there are an `α < β` and a `φ_α : S → F_α` with `ι_α ∘ φ_α = φ`.

declarations.name: Cardinal.exists_ordinal_cof_gt
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 05N3.** For every cardinal `κ` there is an ordinal `α` with `κ < cf(α)`:
the successor of the infinite cardinal `κ ⊔ ℵ₀` is regular, so the ordinal it indexes has
cofinality `(κ ⊔ ℵ₀)⁺`, which is strictly greater than `κ`.
declarations.statement: theorem exists_ordinal_cof_gt (κ : Cardinal) : ∃ α : Ordinal, κ < α.cof

declarations.name: Module.exists_finite_isBaseChange_of_surjective_algebraMap
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 05N5.** Let `R` be a ring, `S ⊆ R` a multiplicative subset, `Rₛ = S⁻¹R` and let
`R'` be a quotient of `Rₛ` (for instance `R' = S⁻¹(R/I) = Rₛ/I·Rₛ` for an ideal `I ⊆ R`). For
every finite `R'`-module `M'` there is a finite `R`-module `M` and an `R`-linear map
`g : M → M'` exhibiting `M'` as the base change `R' ⊗_R M`, i.e. as `S⁻¹(M/IM)`; and if `M'` is
finitely presented over `R'`, then `M` may be taken finitely presented over `R`.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_finite_isBaseChange_of_surjective_algebraMap {R : Type u} [CommRing R]
    (S : Submonoid R) (Rₛ : Type v) [CommRing Rₛ] [Algebra R Rₛ] [IsLocalization S Rₛ]
    {R' : Type w} [CommRing R'] [Algebra R R'] [Algebra Rₛ R'] [IsScalarTower R Rₛ R']
    (M' : Type t) [AddCommGroup M'] [Module R M'] [Module R' M'] [IsScalarTower R R' M']
    [Module.Finite R' M'] (hsurj : Function.Surjective (algebraMap Rₛ R')) :
    ∃ (M : Type u) (_ : AddCommGroup M) (_ : Module R M) (g : M →ₗ[R] M'),
      Module.Finite R M ∧ IsBaseChange R' g ∧
        (Module.FinitePresentation R' M' → Module.FinitePresentation R M)
declarations.comment:
Stated for an arbitrary surjection `Rₛ → R'` from a localization `Rₛ = S⁻¹R`
in place of `R' = S⁻¹(R/I)`, of which it is the case `R' = Rₛ ⧸ I·Rₛ`; `S⁻¹(M/IM)` is the base
change `R' ⊗_R M`, pinned by `IsBaseChange R' g` for the source's map `g : M → M'`. Items (1)
and (2) are the two conjuncts.

declarations.name: Module.exists_finite_isLocalizedModule_comp
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 05N6.** Let `R` be a ring, `S ⊆ R` a multiplicative subset, `M` an `R`-module and
`f : M → Mₛ` a localization of `M` at `S`, over a localization `Rₛ` of `R` at `S`.

1. If `Mₛ = S⁻¹M` is a finite `Rₛ`-module, then there is a finite `R`-module `M'` and an
   `R`-linear map `φ : M' → M` inducing an isomorphism `S⁻¹M' ≅ S⁻¹M`, spelled
   `IsLocalizedModule S (f ∘ₗ φ)`.
2. If `Mₛ` is moreover a finitely presented `Rₛ`-module, then `M'` is of finite presentation
   over `R`.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_finite_isLocalizedModule_comp {R : Type u} [CommRing R] (S : Submonoid R)
    (Rₛ : Type v) [CommRing Rₛ] [Algebra R Rₛ] [IsLocalization S Rₛ]
    {M : Type w} [AddCommGroup M] [Module R M]
    {Mₛ : Type t} [AddCommGroup Mₛ] [Module R Mₛ] [Module Rₛ Mₛ] [IsScalarTower R Rₛ Mₛ]
    (f : M →ₗ[R] Mₛ) [IsLocalizedModule S f] [Module.Finite Rₛ Mₛ] :
    ∃ (M' : Type u) (_ : AddCommGroup M') (_ : Module R M') (φ : M' →ₗ[R] M),
      Module.Finite R M' ∧ IsLocalizedModule S (f ∘ₗ φ) ∧
        (Module.FinitePresentation Rₛ Mₛ → Module.FinitePresentation R M')
declarations.comment:
Localizations are abstract (`IsLocalization S Rₛ`, `IsLocalizedModule S f`); the
induced isomorphism `S⁻¹M' → S⁻¹M` is pinned as `IsLocalizedModule S (f ∘ₗ φ)`; `M'` is produced
in the universe of `R`. Items (1) and (2) are the two conjuncts, (2) as an implication about the
same `M'`.

declarations.name: Module.exists_finitePresentation_and_baseChange_eq_of_lift_bijective
declarations.doc:
Let `A` be a ring, let `S` be a directed system of `A`-algebras over a nonempty directed
preorder `J` with transition maps `f i j : S i →ₐ[A] S j`, and let `R` be an `A`-algebra
receiving compatible maps `algebraMap (S j) R` which exhibit it as the colimit `colim_j S j`.
Then the category of finitely presented `R`-modules is the colimit of the categories of finitely
presented `S j`-modules:

1. every finitely presented `R`-module `M` is isomorphic to the base change `R ⊗[S j] M_j` of a
   finitely presented `S j`-module, for some `j`;
2. for `A`-modules `M`, `N` with `M` finitely presented, every `R`-linear map
   `R ⊗[A] M → R ⊗[A] N` is the base change of an `S j`-linear map `S j ⊗[A] M → S j ⊗[A] N`
   for some `j`, in the sense that the square with the canonical maps
   `S j ⊗[A] M → R ⊗[A] M` commutes;
3. for `A`-modules `M`, `N` with `M` finite, two `A`-linear maps `u, u' : M → N` with
   `u ⊗ 1_R = u' ⊗ 1_R` satisfy `u ⊗ 1_{S j} = u' ⊗ 1_{S j}` for some `j`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem exists_finitePresentation_and_baseChange_eq_of_lift_bijective
    {J : Type w} [Preorder J] [Nonempty J] [IsDirectedOrder J] {A : Type u} [CommRing A]
    {S : J → Type v} [∀ j, CommRing (S j)] [∀ j, Algebra A (S j)]
    (f : ∀ i j, i ≤ j → S i →ₐ[A] S j) [DirectedSystem S fun i j h ↦ ⇑(f i j h)]
    {R : Type v} [CommRing R] [Algebra A R] [∀ j, Algebra (S j) R]
    [∀ j, IsScalarTower A (S j) R]
    (hf : ∀ i j (h : i ≤ j) (x : S i), algebraMap (S j) R (f i j h x) = algebraMap (S i) R x)
    (hR : Function.Bijective (DirectLimit.Algebra.lift S f R
      (fun j ↦ IsScalarTower.toAlgHom A (S j) R) hf)) :
    (∀ (M : Type t) [AddCommGroup M] [Module R M] [Module.FinitePresentation R M],
        ∃ (j : J) (Mj : Type v) (_ : AddCommGroup Mj) (_ : Module (S j) Mj),
          Module.FinitePresentation (S j) Mj ∧ Nonempty (R ⊗[S j] Mj ≃ₗ[R] M)) ∧
    (∀ (M : Type t) [AddCommGroup M] [Module A M] [Module.FinitePresentation A M]
        (N : Type t') [AddCommGroup N] [Module A N] (φ : R ⊗[A] M →ₗ[R] R ⊗[A] N),
        ∃ (j : J) (φj : S j ⊗[A] M →ₗ[S j] S j ⊗[A] N), ∀ x : S j ⊗[A] M,
          φ (LinearMap.rTensor M (IsScalarTower.toAlgHom A (S j) R).toLinearMap x) =
            LinearMap.rTensor N (IsScalarTower.toAlgHom A (S j) R).toLinearMap (φj x)) ∧
    (∀ (M : Type t) [AddCommGroup M] [Module A M] [Module.Finite A M]
        (N : Type t') [AddCommGroup N] [Module A N] (u u' : M →ₗ[A] N),
        u.baseChange R = u'.baseChange R →
          ∃ j : J, u.baseChange (S j) = u'.baseChange (S j))
declarations.comment:
The colimit is a `DirectedSystem` of `A`-algebras whose comparison map
`colim_j S j → R` is bijective, as in 00QN; items (2) and (3) are stated over an arbitrary base
ring `A` and with the finiteness hypotheses of 05LI (3) and (1), of which they are instances, the
source's form being `A = R_λ` and the system restricted to `μ ≥ λ`; `φ = φ_μ ⊗ 1_R` is the
commuting square with the canonical maps `LinearMap.rTensor M (algebraMap (S j) R)`. See the
module docstring.

declarations.name: Algebra.TensorProduct.exists_of_directLimit
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 05N8.** Let `A` be a ring, let `B`, `C` be `A`-algebras, and let `R` be the colimit
of a directed system `G` of `A`-algebras with transition maps `f` and structure maps
`g i : G i →ₐ[A] R`.

1. If `B` is of finite type over `A` and `u, u' : B →ₐ[A] C` satisfy `u ⊗ 1 = u' ⊗ 1` over `R`,
   then `u ⊗ 1 = u' ⊗ 1` over `G i` for some `i`.
2. If `C` is of finite type over `A` and `u ⊗ 1` is surjective over `R`, then `u ⊗ 1` is
   surjective over `G i` for some `i`.
3. If `C` is of finite presentation over `A`, then every `R`-algebra map
   `v : R ⊗[A] C →ₐ[R] R ⊗[A] B` is the base change of a `G i`-algebra map
   `vᵢ : G i ⊗[A] C →ₐ[G i] G i ⊗[A] B` for some `i`.
4. If `B` is of finite type and `C` of finite presentation over `A` and `u ⊗ 1` is bijective over
   `R`, then `u ⊗ 1` is bijective over `G i` for some `i`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem exists_of_directLimit {A : Type u} [CommRing A]
    {B : Type v} [CommRing B] [Algebra A B] {C : Type w} [CommRing C] [Algebra A C]
    {ι : Type t} [Preorder ι] [Nonempty ι] [IsDirectedOrder ι]
    {G : ι → Type s} [∀ i, CommRing (G i)] [∀ i, Algebra A (G i)]
    (f : ∀ i j, i ≤ j → G i →ₐ[A] G j) [DirectedSystem G fun i j h ↦ ⇑(f i j h)]
    {R : Type r} [CommRing R] [Algebra A R] (g : ∀ i, G i →ₐ[A] R)
    (hg : ∀ i j h x, g j (f i j h x) = g i x)
    (hR : Function.Bijective (DirectLimit.Algebra.lift G f R g hg)) :
    (Algebra.FiniteType A B → ∀ u u' : B →ₐ[A] C,
        lTensor (S := R) R u = lTensor (S := R) R u' →
        ∃ i, lTensor (S := G i) (G i) u = lTensor (S := G i) (G i) u') ∧
    (Algebra.FiniteType A C → ∀ u : B →ₐ[A] C,
        Function.Surjective (lTensor (S := R) R u) →
        ∃ i, Function.Surjective (lTensor (S := G i) (G i) u)) ∧
    (Algebra.FinitePresentation A C → ∀ v : R ⊗[A] C →ₐ[R] R ⊗[A] B,
        ∃ (i : ι) (vᵢ : G i ⊗[A] C →ₐ[G i] G i ⊗[A] B),
          (v.restrictScalars A).comp (rTensor C (g i)) =
            (rTensor B (g i)).comp (vᵢ.restrictScalars A)) ∧
    (Algebra.FiniteType A B → Algebra.FinitePresentation A C → ∀ u : B →ₐ[A] C,
        Function.Bijective (lTensor (S := R) R u) →
        ∃ i, Function.Bijective (lTensor (S := G i) (G i) u))
declarations.comment:
The four items are the four conjuncts, each carrying only its own finiteness
hypothesis. `B ⊗_A R` is `R ⊗[A] B` and `u ⊗ 1` is `Algebra.TensorProduct.lTensor`;
`R = colim_i R_i` is bijectivity of `DirectLimit.Algebra.lift`, as in `00QN`; item (3)'s
`v = v_i ⊗ 1` is the commuting square with the comparison maps `rTensor _ (g i)`. See the module
docstring.

declarations.name: CommRingCat.exists_isPushout_and_exists_eq_comp_and_exists_comp_eq_of_isColimit
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 05N9.** Let `R = colim_λ R_λ` be a filtered colimit of rings, given by a filtered
diagram `F` with colimit cocone `c`.

1. Every finitely presented `R`-algebra `A` is the base change of a finitely presented
   `R_λ`-algebra `A'`, in the sense that the square `R_λ → A'`, `R_λ → R`, `A' → A`, `R → A` is
   a pushout.
2. If `A'` is of finite presentation over `R_λ` and `B` is the base change to `R` of an
   `R_λ`-algebra `B'`, then every `R_λ`-algebra map `ρ : A' → B` factors as `ρ = σ ≫ t` through
   the base change `Bₖ` of `B'` to some `R_μ` with `μ ≥ λ`, by an `R_λ`-algebra map `σ` and the
   canonical map `t : Bₖ → B`. Transposed along the pushout of item 1, this says that every
   `R`-algebra map `A' ⊗_{R_λ} R → B' ⊗_{R_λ} R` is the base change of an `R_μ`-algebra map
   `A' ⊗_{R_λ} R_μ → B' ⊗_{R_λ} R_μ`.
3. If `A'` is of finite type over `R_λ` and `φ, ψ : A' → B'` are `R_λ`-algebra maps whose base
   changes to `R` agree, then their base changes to `R_μ` agree for some `μ ≥ λ`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem exists_isPushout_and_exists_eq_comp_and_exists_comp_eq_of_isColimit
    {J : Type v} [Category.{w} J] [IsFiltered J] {F : J ⥤ CommRingCat.{u}} {c : Cocone F}
    (hc : IsColimit c) [PreservesColimit F (forget CommRingCat.{u})] :
    (∀ (A : CommRingCat.{u}) (f : c.pt ⟶ A), f.hom.FinitePresentation →
        ∃ (j : J) (A' : CommRingCat.{u}) (f' : F.obj j ⟶ A') (a : A' ⟶ A),
          f'.hom.FinitePresentation ∧ IsPushout f' (c.ι.app j) a f) ∧
    (∀ (j : J) (A' B' B : CommRingCat.{u}) (f' : F.obj j ⟶ A') (g' : F.obj j ⟶ B')
        (g : c.pt ⟶ B) (b : B' ⟶ B), f'.hom.FinitePresentation →
        IsPushout g' (c.ι.app j) b g →
        ∀ ρ : A' ⟶ B, f' ≫ ρ = c.ι.app j ≫ g →
          ∃ (k : J) (h : j ⟶ k) (Bₖ : CommRingCat.{u}) (gₖ : F.obj k ⟶ Bₖ) (bₖ : B' ⟶ Bₖ)
              (t : Bₖ ⟶ B) (σ : A' ⟶ Bₖ), IsPushout g' (F.map h) bₖ gₖ ∧ bₖ ≫ t = b ∧
            gₖ ≫ t = c.ι.app k ≫ g ∧ f' ≫ σ = F.map h ≫ gₖ ∧ ρ = σ ≫ t) ∧
    (∀ (j : J) (A' B' B : CommRingCat.{u}) (f' : F.obj j ⟶ A') (g' : F.obj j ⟶ B')
        (g : c.pt ⟶ B) (b : B' ⟶ B), f'.hom.FiniteType → IsPushout g' (c.ι.app j) b g →
        ∀ φ ψ : A' ⟶ B', f' ≫ φ = g' → f' ≫ ψ = g' → φ ≫ b = ψ ≫ b →
          ∃ (k : J) (h : j ⟶ k) (Bₖ : CommRingCat.{u}) (gₖ : F.obj k ⟶ Bₖ) (bₖ : B' ⟶ Bₖ),
            IsPushout g' (F.map h) bₖ gₖ ∧ φ ≫ bₖ = ψ ≫ bₖ)
declarations.comment:
The colimit is a colimit cocone in `CommRingCat` over a filtered category, an
algebra is a ring map, and `A ≅ A_λ ⊗_{R_λ} R` is `IsPushout`, so no tensor product is
constructed. Items (2) and (3) are transposed along that pushout, which is Mathlib's spelling
and drops the source's finite presentation of `B_λ`; item (3) needs `A_λ` of finite type only.
See the module docstring.

declarations.name: Stacks.SheafOfModules.TensorSheafification.tensorSheafifyIso
declarations.doc:
The canonical isomorphism of sheaves of `𝒪`-modules
`(F' ⊗ G')^# ≅ ((F')^# ⊗ (G')^#)^#` induced by the sheafification units.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def tensorSheafifyIso
    (F' G' : PresheafOfModules.{w} (structureRingPresheaf 𝒪)) :
    (sheafify 𝒪 h𝒪).obj (PresheafOfModules.tensorObj (O := 𝒪) F' G') ≅
      (sheafify 𝒪 h𝒪).obj
        (PresheafOfModules.tensorObj (O := 𝒪)
          ((SheafOfModules.forget (structureSheaf 𝒪 h𝒪) ⋙
              PresheafOfModules.restrictScalars (𝟙 (structureSheaf 𝒪 h𝒪).obj)).obj
            ((sheafify 𝒪 h𝒪).obj F'))
          ((SheafOfModules.forget (structureSheaf 𝒪 h𝒪) ⋙
              PresheafOfModules.restrictScalars (𝟙 (structureSheaf 𝒪 h𝒪).obj)).obj
            ((sheafify 𝒪 h𝒪).obj G')))

declarations.name: Stacks.SheafOfModules.FlatSheafification.sheafTensorRight_preservesColimits
declarations.doc: Tensoring on the right with `F` preserves all colimits indexed in the module universe.
declarations.statement:
public lemma sheafTensorRight_preservesColimits
    {C : Type u} [Category.{v} C] (J : GrothendieckTopology C)
    [J.HasSheafCompose (forget₂ CommRingCat.{w} RingCat.{w})]
    [J.WEqualsLocallyBijective AddCommGrpCat.{z}]
    [HasWeakSheafify J AddCommGrpCat.{z}]
    (O : Sheaf J CommRingCat.{w})
    (F : SheafOfModules.{z} (Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf O)) :
    PreservesColimitsOfSize.{max u z, z}
      ((Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.sheafTensor.{u, v, w, z, z} (J := J) O).flip.obj F)
declarations.comment: for the right-handed tensor endofunctor (sheafTensor O).flip.obj F

declarations.name: Stacks.SheafOfModules.TensorColimits.tensorLeft_preservesColimits
declarations.doc:
Tensoring with a fixed sheaf of modules commutes with all small colimits, independently of
the ring universe.

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.SheafOfModules.sheafTensorLeft_preservesColimits
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 05NB.** Tensoring with a fixed sheaf of modules commutes with
all small colimits, independently of the ring universe.
declarations.statement:
theorem sheafTensorLeft_preservesColimits (R : Sheaf J CommRingCat.{w})
    (F : _root_.SheafOfModules.{z} (Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf R)) :
    PreservesColimitsOfSize.{a, z} (sheafTensorLeft J R F)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.SheafOfModules.IsFlat
declarations.doc:
A sheaf of modules is flat when tensoring on the right with it is an exact
endofunctor on sheaves of modules.

This is part (3) of tag 03ER for the native tensor bifunctor, and part (4) just below
is stated in terms of it. `Stacks.SheafOfModules.IsFlat` uses the same native tensor
functor.
declarations.statement:
abbrev IsFlat {O : Sheaf J CommRingCat.{w}}
    [J.WEqualsLocallyBijective AddCommGrpCat.{z}]
    [HasWeakSheafify J AddCommGrpCat.{z}]
    (F : _root_.SheafOfModules.{z} (Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf O)) : Prop
declarations.comment: the definition: F is flat when G ↦ G ⊗_{O_X} F is exact

declarations.name: Stacks.SheafOfModules.flat_stalk_of_isFlat
declarations.doc:
**Tag 05NE, in the spellings the determinant development uses.** A flat sheaf of modules on
a ringed space has flat stalks, for the module structure
`Stacks.SheafOfModules.stalkModule`.

The content is `AlgebraicGeometry.SheafOfModules.isFlat_iff_stalk_flat`; what this adds is that
the index `structureSheafRing Y` of the determinant development is
`Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf Y.sheaf`, and that
`Stacks.SheafOfModules.stalkModule` is the module structure that theorem's statement supplies
by `inferInstanceAs`. Both hold by `rfl`, but the universe arguments of
`AlgebraicGeometry.SheafOfModules.IsFlat` are not determined by `F` alone, so they are written
out; this is the spelling Tag 08BL uses as well.
declarations.comment: flat implies stalkwise flat, for a ringed space, in the `structureSheafRing` spelling

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.SheafOfModules.isFlat_iff_stalk_flat
declarations.doc:
A module sheaf on a ringed space is flat precisely when each of its
stalks is flat over the corresponding stalk of the structure sheaf.
declarations.statement:
public theorem isFlat_iff_stalk_flat {X : TopCat.{u}}
    (O : Sheaf (Opens.grothendieckTopology X) CommRingCat.{u})
    (F : _root_.SheafOfModules.{u} (Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf.{u, u, u} O)) :
    IsFlat F ↔
      ∀ x : X,
        letI : Module (TopCat.Presheaf.stalk (C := CommRingCat.{u}) (X := X) O.obj x)
          (TopCat.Presheaf.stalk (C := AddCommGrpCat.{u}) (X := X) F.val.presheaf x) :=
          inferInstanceAs (Module (TopCat.Presheaf.stalk (C := CommRingCat.{u}) (X := X) O.obj x)
          (TopCat.Presheaf.stalk (C := AddCommGrpCat.{u}) (X := X)
              ((id F.val : _root_.PresheafOfModules.{u}
                (O.obj ⋙ forget₂ CommRingCat.{u} RingCat.{u})).presheaf) x))
        Module.Flat (TopCat.Presheaf.stalk (C := CommRingCat.{u}) (X := X) O.obj x)
          (TopCat.Presheaf.stalk (C := AddCommGrpCat.{u}) (X := X) F.val.presheaf x)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.SheafOfModules.IsFlatAt
declarations.doc:
An `𝒪_X`-module `F` on a ringed space `X` is *flat at* `x : X` if its stalk `F_x` is a flat
`𝒪_{X,x}`-module.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def IsFlatAt {X : RingedSpace.{u}}
    (F : _root_.SheafOfModules.{u} ((sheafCompose (Opens.grothendieckTopology X)
      (forget₂ CommRingCat.{u} RingCat.{u})).obj X.sheaf))
    (x : X) : Prop

declarations.name: Stacks.SheafOfModules.FlatColimits.isFlat_colimit
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 03EU part (2), filtered colimits.** A filtered colimit of flat
sheaves of modules is flat.
declarations.statement:
theorem isFlat_colimit {O : Sheaf J CommRingCat.{w}}
    {I : Type z} [Category.{z} I] [IsFiltered I]
    (F : I ⥤ _root_.SheafOfModules.{z} (Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf O))
    (hF : ∀ i, IsFlat (F.obj i)) :
    IsFlat (colimit F)
declarations.comment: filtered_colimits_flat

declarations.name: Stacks.SheafOfModules.FlatColimits.isFlat_coproduct
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 03EU part (2), direct sums.** An arbitrary direct sum of flat sheaves
of modules is flat. An arbitrary coproduct is the filtered colimit of its finite subcoproducts,
so this follows from the finite case `isFlat_coproduct_finite` and the filtered-colimit case
`isFlat_colimit`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isFlat_coproduct {O : Sheaf J CommRingCat.{w}} {ι : Type z}
    (F : ι → _root_.SheafOfModules.{z} (Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf O))
    (hF : ∀ i, IsFlat (F i)) :
    IsFlat (∐ F)
declarations.comment: direct_sums_flat

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.SheafOfModules.isFlat_jShriek_unit
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 05NH.** The extension by zero of the structure sheaf of an open subset of a ringed
space is a flat sheaf of modules.
declarations.statement:
theorem isFlat_jShriek_unit {X : TopCat.{u}} (U : Opens X)
    (O : Sheaf (Opens.grothendieckTopology X) CommRingCat.{u}) :
    IsFlat.{u, u, u, u} (O := O)
      ((ExtensionByZeroModules.jShriek U (Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf.{u, u, u} O)).obj
        (_root_.SheafOfModules.unit
          (ExtensionByZeroModules.resRing U
            (Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf.{u, u, u} O))))

declarations.name: Stacks.SheafOfModules.exists_epi_from_flat
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 05NI, part (2).** Every sheaf of modules on a ringed space is a quotient of a flat
sheaf of modules: the explicit cover of part (1) is a direct sum of extensions by zero of
structure sheaves, each flat by Stacks 05NH, and a direct sum of flat sheaves is flat.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_epi_from_flat {X : TopCat.{u}}
    (O : Sheaf (Opens.grothendieckTopology X) CommRingCat.{u})
    (F : _root_.SheafOfModules.{u} (Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf.{u, u, u} O)) :
    ∃ (P : _root_.SheafOfModules.{u} (Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf.{u, u, u} O))
        (f : P ⟶ F),
      IsFlat.{u, u, u, u} (O := O) P ∧ Epi f
declarations.comment: part (2)

declarations.name: Stacks.SheafOfModules.exists_epi_from_coproduct_jShriek_unit
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 05NI, part (1).** Every sheaf of modules is a quotient of a coproduct of extensions
by zero of structure sheaves on open subspaces.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_epi_from_coproduct_jShriek_unit :
    ∃ (I : Type u) (U : I → Opens X),
      ∃ f : (∐ fun i : I =>
        (ExtensionByZeroModules.jShriek (U i) O).obj
          (_root_.SheafOfModules.unit (ExtensionByZeroModules.resRing (U i) O))) ⟶ F,
        Epi f
declarations.comment: part (1)

declarations.name: Stacks.SheafOfModules.FlatCover.sheafTensorRight_shortExact_of_isFlat_X₃
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 03EX, sheaf case.** If the final term of a short exact sequence of
sheaves of modules is flat, tensoring the sequence with any sheaf of modules gives a short exact
sequence.

This is `shortExact_map_sheafTensorFlipObj` with the composite-is-zero witness carried
explicitly, so that the statement does not mention the zero-morphism-preservation instance of
the tensor functor.

Taking the site to be the site of opens of a topological space and `O` its structure sheaf,
this is **Stacks Tag 05NJ**: a short exact sequence `0 → ℱ'' → ℱ' → ℱ → 0` of `𝒪_X`-modules on
a ringed space with `ℱ` flat stays short exact after `- ⊗_{𝒪_X} 𝒢`.
declarations.statement:
theorem sheafTensorRight_shortExact_of_isFlat_X₃
    (O : Sheaf J CommRingCat.{w})
    (S : ShortComplex (SheafOfModules.{w} (Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf O)))
    (G : SheafOfModules.{w} (Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf O))
    (hS : S.ShortExact)
    (hflat : AlgebraicGeometry.SheafOfModules.IsFlat.{v, u, w, w} (O := O) S.X₃) :
    ∃ h : ((Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.sheafTensor O).flip.obj G).map S.f ≫
        ((Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.sheafTensor O).flip.obj G).map S.g = 0,
      (ShortComplex.mk (((Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.sheafTensor O).flip.obj G).map S.f)
        (((Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.sheafTensor O).flip.obj G).map S.g) h).ShortExact
declarations.comment: ringed spaces, as the special case of a general site

declarations.name: Stacks.SheafOfModules.FlatShortExact.isFlat_middle_of_shortExact
declarations.doc:
**Statement 1** (Stacks Tag 05NK, extension of flat modules is flat).  Given a short
exact sequence `0 → F₂ → F₁ → F₀ → 0` of sheaves of `O_X`-modules (encoded as a short
complex `S` in the abelian category `SheafOfModules (structureSheafRing X)` together with the
hypothesis `S.ShortExact`), if `S.X₁ = F₂` and `S.X₃ = F₀` are flat then the middle term
`S.X₂ = F₁` is flat.

PROOF.  By `isFlat_iff_stalkModule_flat` it suffices to show, for each `x`, that
the canonical stalk module `(S.X₂)_x` is flat.  By `stalkShortExact` we have a
short exact sequence of `O_{X,x}`-modules `0 → (S.X₁)_x → (S.X₂)_x → (S.X₃)_x → 0`.
By hypotheses `h₂, h₀` (via `isFlat_iff_stalkModule_flat`) the outer modules are
flat, so `Module.Flat.of_shortExact_extension` gives flatness of the middle.
declarations.statement:
theorem isFlat_middle_of_shortExact
    (S : ShortComplex (SheafOfModules (structureSheafRing X)))
    (hS : S.ShortExact) (h₂ : IsFlat S.X₁) (h₀ : IsFlat S.X₃) :
    IsFlat S.X₂

declarations.name: Stacks.SheafOfModules.FlatShortExact.isFlat_sub_of_shortExact
declarations.doc:
**Statement 2** (Stacks Tag 05NK, kernel of an epimorphism of flat modules is flat).
Given a short exact sequence `0 → F₂ → F₁ → F₀ → 0` of sheaves of `O_X`-modules (encoded as
a short complex `S` with `S.ShortExact`), if `S.X₂ = F₁` and `S.X₃ = F₀` are flat then the
left term `S.X₁ = F₂` is flat.

PROOF.  By `isFlat_iff_stalkModule_flat` it suffices to show `(S.X₁)_x` is flat for
each `x`.  By `stalkShortExact` we have the short exact sequence of stalk modules
`0 → (S.X₁)_x → (S.X₂)_x → (S.X₃)_x → 0`; by `h₁, h₀` the modules `(S.X₂)_x` and
`(S.X₃)_x` are flat, so `Module.Flat.of_shortExact_kernel` gives flatness of
`(S.X₁)_x`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isFlat_sub_of_shortExact
    (S : ShortComplex (SheafOfModules (structureSheafRing X)))
    (hS : S.ShortExact) (h₁ : IsFlat S.X₂) (h₀ : IsFlat S.X₃) :
    IsFlat S.X₁

declarations.name: Stacks.SheafOfModules.FlatResolution.acyclic_map_sheafTensorRight_of_isFlat
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 03EZ, sheaf case.** An exact `ℕ`-indexed complex of sheaves of modules all of
whose terms are flat stays exact after tensoring with an arbitrary sheaf of modules.

This is also **Stacks 05NL**, the same statement for a ringed space: a ringed space is the
ringed site of its lattice of opens, its `O_X`-modules are the sheaves of modules over the
structure ring sheaf of that site, and the tensor product is `sheafTensorRight`.  The
site-level statement is recorded against the ringed-space tag for the same reason that the
site-level flatness of Stacks 03ER(3) is recorded against Stacks 05ND in
`StacksFrontier/CategoryTheory/Sites/Modules/Flat.lean`.
declarations.statement:
theorem acyclic_map_sheafTensorRight_of_isFlat
    (K : ChainComplex
      (_root_.SheafOfModules.{w} (Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf R)) ℕ)
    (hK : K.Acyclic)
    (hflat : ∀ i, AlgebraicGeometry.SheafOfModules.IsFlat.{v, u, w, w} (O := R) (K.X i))
    (G : _root_.SheafOfModules.{w} (Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf R)) :
    ((Functor.mapHomologicalComplex
      ((Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.sheafTensor.{u, v, w, w, w} R).flip.obj G)
      (ComplexShape.down ℕ)).obj K).Acyclic
declarations.comment: ringed spaces, as the special case of a general site

declarations.name: Stacks.Injectives.IsSmallWithRespectTo
declarations.doc:
An object `A` is `α`-small with respect to `I` if `Hom(A, -)` preserves the colimit of
every `α`-indexed system all of whose transition morphisms belong to `I`.
declarations.statement:
abbrev IsSmallWithRespectTo {C : Type u} [Category.{v} C] (A : C)
    (I : MorphismProperty C) (α : Ordinal.{w}) : Prop

declarations.name: Stacks.Injectives.isSmallWithRespectTo_monomorphisms_of_mk_submodule_lt_cof
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 05NT.** Let `R` be a ring, let `M` be an `R`-module and let `κ` be the
cardinality of the set of submodules of `M`. If `α` is an ordinal whose cofinality is
bigger than `κ`, then `M` is `α`-small with respect to injections, i.e. for every system
`(B_β)_{β ∈ α}` of `R`-modules with injective transition maps the canonical map
`colim_β Hom(M, B_β) ⟶ Hom(M, colim_β B_β)` is bijective.
declarations.statement:
theorem isSmallWithRespectTo_monomorphisms_of_mk_submodule_lt_cof
    {R : Type u} [Ring R] (M : ModuleCat.{u} R) (α : Ordinal.{u})
    (hα : Cardinal.mk (Submodule R M) < α.cof) :
    IsSmallWithRespectTo M (MorphismProperty.monomorphisms (ModuleCat.{u} R)) α

declarations.name: baerE_lof
declarations.doc:
The top horizontal arrow `⨁_{(a, φ)} a → M` of the defining square of `𝐌(M)`, read on
the summands: the element `x` of the ideal `a`, placed in the summand indexed by the pair
`(a, φ)`, is sent to `φ x ∈ M`.  The direct sum over the sigma type `I(M) = Σ a, Hom(a, M)`
realizes the iterated coproduct `⨁_a ⨁_{φ ∈ Hom(a, M)}`.
declarations.statement:
theorem baerE_lof (a : Ideal R) (φ : a →ₗ[R] M) (x : a) :
    baerE R M (DirectSum.lof R (BaerIndex R M) (fun i => (i.1 : Type u)) ⟨a, φ⟩ x) = φ x
declarations.comment: the top horizontal arrow

declarations.name: baerD_lof
declarations.doc:
The left vertical arrow `⨁_{(a, φ)} a → ⨁_{(a, φ)} R` of the defining square of `𝐌(M)`,
read on the summands: the element `x` of the ideal `a`, placed in the summand indexed by the
pair `(a, φ)`, is sent to the same element `x`, now viewed in the copy of `R` indexed by that
same pair `(a, φ)`.
declarations.statement:
theorem baerD_lof (a : Ideal R) (φ : a →ₗ[R] M) (x : a) :
    baerD R M (DirectSum.lof R (BaerIndex R M) (fun i => (i.1 : Type u)) ⟨a, φ⟩ x)
      = DirectSum.lof R (BaerIndex R M) (fun _ => R) ⟨a, φ⟩ (x : R)
declarations.comment: the left vertical arrow

declarations.name: baer_pushout_universal
declarations.doc:
The module `𝐌(M)`, together with the canonical maps `u_M : M → 𝐌(M)` and
`v_M : T(M) → 𝐌(M)`, is the pushout of `M ← S(M) → T(M)`: for every `R`-module `N` and every
pair of maps `f : M → N`, `g : T(M) → N` making the outer square commute, there is a unique
`k : 𝐌(M) → N` with `k ∘ u_M = f` and `k ∘ v_M = g`.  Together with `baer_pushout_square`,
`baerE_lof` and `baerD_lof` this says that the square

    ⨁_{(a, φ)} a  --e_M-->  M
         |                   |
        d_M                 u_M
         v                   v
    ⨁_{(a, φ)} R  --v_M-->  𝐌(M)

is the pushout square defining `𝐌(M)`.
declarations.statement:
theorem baer_pushout_universal (f : M →ₗ[R] N) (g : BaerT R M →ₗ[R] N)
    (h : f.comp (baerE R M) = g.comp (baerD R M)) :
    ∃! k : BaerM R M →ₗ[R] N, k.comp (baerUMap R M) = f ∧ k.comp (baerV R M) = g
declarations.comment: the pushout defining 𝐌(M)

declarations.name: baer_functorial
declarations.doc:
Statement 1 (Functoriality).  The construction `M ↦ (u_M : M → 𝐌(M))` is functorial:
there is an assignment `MMap` on `R`-module morphisms `χ : M → N`, giving a map
`MMap χ : 𝐌(M) → 𝐌(N)`, such that

1. `MMap id = id` (identities are preserved);
2. `MMap (χ' ∘ χ) = MMap χ' ∘ MMap χ` (composition is preserved);
3. the maps `u_M` are a natural transformation `𝟭 ⟹ 𝐌`, i.e.
   `MMap χ ∘ u_M = u_N ∘ χ` for every `χ : M → N`.

Here the morphism action `MMap` is quantified existentially, modelling "there is a
functor `𝐌` with `u` a natural transformation from the identity to `𝐌`".
declarations.statement:
theorem baer_functorial :
    ∃ MMap : ∀ {M N : Type u} [AddCommGroup M] [Module R M] [AddCommGroup N] [Module R N],
        (M →ₗ[R] N) → (BaerM R M →ₗ[R] BaerM R N),
      (∀ (M : Type u) [AddCommGroup M] [Module R M],
          MMap (LinearMap.id : M →ₗ[R] M) = LinearMap.id) ∧
      (∀ {M N P : Type u} [AddCommGroup M] [Module R M] [AddCommGroup N] [Module R N]
          [AddCommGroup P] [Module R P] (χ : M →ₗ[R] N) (χ' : N →ₗ[R] P),
          MMap (χ'.comp χ) = (MMap χ').comp (MMap χ)) ∧
      (∀ {M N : Type u} [AddCommGroup M] [Module R M] [AddCommGroup N] [Module R N]
          (χ : M →ₗ[R] N),
          (MMap χ).comp (baerUMap R M) = (baerUMap R N).comp χ)

declarations.name: baer_uMap_injective
declarations.doc: Statement 2 (Injectivity).  The canonical map `u_M : M → 𝐌(M)` is injective.
declarations.statement: theorem baer_uMap_injective : Function.Injective (baerUMap R M)

declarations.name: baer_extension
declarations.doc:
Statement 3 (Extension property).  For every ideal `a` and `R`-module map
`φ : a → M`, there is an `R`-module map `φ' : R → 𝐌(M)` with `φ' |_a = u_M ∘ φ`, i.e.
`φ' (a) = u_M (φ a)` for all `a ∈ a`.
declarations.statement:
theorem baer_extension (a : Ideal R) (φ : a →ₗ[R] M) :
    ∃ φ' : R →ₗ[R] BaerM R M,
      φ'.comp a.subtype = (baerUMap R M).comp φ

declarations.name: Stacks.Injectives.baerIterateFunctor
declarations.doc:
`M_α`, functorially in `M`: the top stage of the transfinite iteration of
the Baer construction through the ordinal `α`.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def baerIterateFunctor (R : Type u) [CommRing R]
    (α : Ordinal.{u}) : ModuleCat.{u} R ⥤ ModuleCat.{u} R
declarations.comment: the functorial transfinite construction

declarations.name: Stacks.Injectives.baerIterateEmbedding
declarations.doc: The canonical natural map `M ⟶ M_α`.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def baerIterateEmbedding (R : Type u) [CommRing R]
    (α : Ordinal.{u}) : 𝟭 (ModuleCat.{u} R) ⟶ baerIterateFunctor R α
declarations.comment: the natural map to the iterate

declarations.name: Stacks.Injectives.baerIterate_injective_of_cofinality
declarations.doc:
If the cofinality of `α` exceeds the cardinality of the set of ideals of `R`, then the
top stage `M_α` of the transfinite Baer iteration is an injective `R`-module.
declarations.statement:
theorem baerIterate_injective_of_cofinality
    (R : Type u) [CommRing R] (α : Ordinal.{u})
    (hα : Cardinal.mk (Ideal R) < α.cof) (M : ModuleCat.{u} R) :
    Injective ((baerIterateFunctor R α).obj M)
declarations.comment: injectivity of the target

declarations.name: Stacks.Injectives.mono_baerIterateEmbedding
declarations.doc:
The canonical natural map from a module to any transfinite Baer iterate is a monomorphism.
Together with `baerIterate_injective_of_cofinality`, its components give functorial injective
embeddings.
declarations.statement:
theorem mono_baerIterateEmbedding
    (R : Type u) [CommRing R] (α : Ordinal.{u}) (M : ModuleCat.{u} R) :
    Mono ((baerIterateEmbedding R α).app M)
declarations.comment: the natural embedding
