registrations.comment: Mor_{Ab(C)}(Z_X^#, G) = G(X)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.isFlat_tilde_iff_flat
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 05P0.** The sheaf associated to a module on an affine
scheme is flat if and only if the module is flat.
declarations.statement:
theorem isFlat_tilde_iff_flat {R : CommRingCat.{u}} (M : ModuleCat.{u} R) :
    AlgebraicGeometry.SheafOfModules.IsFlat (tilde M) ↔ Module.Flat R M

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.Modules.flat_finitePresentation_locallyFree_fiberRank_tfae
declarations.doc:
For a sheaf of modules `F` on a scheme `X` the following are equivalent: `F` is flat and of
finite presentation; `F` is of finite presentation and all its stalks are free; `F` is locally
free and of finite type; `F` is finite locally free; `F` is of finite type, all its stalks are
free, and its fibre rank is locally constant.

Quasi-coherence is not assumed: it is implied by each of the five conditions.
declarations.statement:
theorem flat_finitePresentation_locallyFree_fiberRank_tfae {X : Scheme.{u}} (F : X.Modules) :
    List.TFAE [
      AlgebraicGeometry.SheafOfModules.IsFlat
          (C := TopologicalSpace.Opens X.toTopCat)
          (J := Opens.grothendieckTopology X.toTopCat) (O := X.sheaf) F ∧
        F.IsFinitePresentation,
      F.IsFinitePresentation ∧
        (∀ x : X,
          letI : Module (X.presheaf.stalk x) (F.presheaf.stalk x) :=
            PresheafOfModules.instModuleCarrierStalkCommRingCatCarrierAbPresheafOpensCarrier
              (R := X.presheaf) F.val x
          Module.Free (X.presheaf.stalk x) (F.presheaf.stalk x)),
      _root_.SheafOfModules.IsLocallyFree.{u, u, u} F ∧
        _root_.SheafOfModules.IsFiniteType.{u, u, u} F,
      AlgebraicGeometry.SheafOfModules.IsFiniteLocallyFree.{u, u, u} (R := X.ringCatSheaf) F,
      _root_.SheafOfModules.IsFiniteType.{u, u, u} F ∧
        (∀ x : X,
          letI : Module (X.presheaf.stalk x) (F.presheaf.stalk x) :=
            PresheafOfModules.instModuleCarrierStalkCommRingCatCarrierAbPresheafOpensCarrier
              (R := X.presheaf) F.val x
          Module.Free (X.presheaf.stalk x) (F.presheaf.stalk x)) ∧
        IsLocallyConstant (fiberRank F)]

declarations.name: Stacks.FiniteLocallyFree.ModuleTFAE.finiteLocallyFree_tfae
declarations.doc:
A quasi-coherent sheaf of modules on a scheme is finite locally free exactly
when it satisfies any of the five equivalent flatness, presentation, stalk, or
rank conditions.

`AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.Modules.flat_finitePresentation_locallyFree_fiberRank_tfae` in
`StacksFrontier.AlgebraicGeometry.FiberRank.LocallyFree` carries the tag too, and states the same
list of five conditions without assuming quasi-coherence, so it implies this statement outright.
Both carry the tag: a Stacks tag is registered once per clause or part of its statement, and more
than one carrier is expected rather than a defect.
declarations.statement:
theorem finiteLocallyFree_tfae {X : Scheme.{u}} (F : X.Modules)
    [F.IsQuasicoherent] :
    List.TFAE [
      AlgebraicGeometry.SheafOfModules.IsFlat F ∧ F.IsFinitePresentation,
      F.IsFinitePresentation ∧
        (∀ x : X,
          letI : Module (X.presheaf.stalk x) (F.presheaf.stalk x) :=
            PresheafOfModules.instModuleCarrierStalkCommRingCatCarrierAbPresheafOpensCarrier
              (R := X.presheaf) F.val x
          Module.Free (X.presheaf.stalk x) (F.presheaf.stalk x)),
      SheafOfModules.IsLocallyFree F ∧ F.IsFiniteType,
      AlgebraicGeometry.SheafOfModules.IsFiniteLocallyFree F,
      F.IsFiniteType ∧
        (∀ x : X,
          letI : Module (X.presheaf.stalk x) (F.presheaf.stalk x) :=
            PresheafOfModules.instModuleCarrierStalkCommRingCatCarrierAbPresheafOpensCarrier
              (R := X.presheaf) F.val x
          Module.Free (X.presheaf.stalk x) (F.presheaf.stalk x)) ∧
        IsLocallyConstant (fiberRank F)]

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.isVariety_pullback
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 05P3.** The fibre product of two varieties over an
algebraically closed field is a variety.
declarations.statement:
public instance isVariety_pullback (k : Type u) [Field k] [IsAlgClosed k]
    {X Y : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ Spec (.of k)) (g : Y ⟶ Spec (.of k))
    [IsVariety k f] [IsVariety k g] :
    IsVariety k (pullback.fst f g ≫ f)

declarations.name: Module.FlatAtPointSituation.flatAtPointFunctor_eq_of_finite
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 05P4.** Replacing the local algebra of a flat-at-a-point situation by
a finite local extension, and its module by an isomorphic module over that extension, does not
change the flat-at-a-point functor.
declarations.statement:
public theorem flatAtPointFunctor_eq_of_finite (S : FlatAtPointSituation.{u, v, w})
    {C : Type x} [CommRing C] [IsLocalRing C] [Algebra S.A C] [IsLocalHom (algebraMap S.A C)]
    {N : Type y} [AddCommGroup N] [Module C N] (f : S.B →ₐ[S.A] C)
    (hf : IsLocalHom f.toRingHom) (hfinite : f.toRingHom.Finite)
    (e : letI : Module S.B N := Module.compHom N f.toRingHom
      S.M ≃ₗ[S.B] N) :
    flatAtPointFunctor.{u, v, w, z} S =
      flatAtPointFunctor.{u, x, y, z} ({ A := S.A, B := C, M := N } :
        FlatAtPointSituation.{u, x, y})

declarations.name: Module.FlatAtPointSituation.flatAtPointFunctor_baseChange
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 05P5.** A flat local extension of the local algebra, with the module
extended along it, does not change the flat-at-a-point functor.
declarations.statement:
public theorem flatAtPointFunctor_baseChange (S : FlatAtPointSituation.{u, v, w}) (C : Type z)
    [CommRing C] [IsLocalRing C] [Algebra S.B C] [IsLocalHom (algebraMap S.B C)]
    [Module.Flat S.B C] :
    (S.flatAtPointFunctor : LocalAlgCat.{u, x} S.A ⥤ Type) =
      (baseChange S C).flatAtPointFunctor

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.FlatnessSituation.HasUniversalFlattening
declarations.doc:
A quasi-coherent module admits a universal flattening when its flatness functor is
represented by a scheme over the base.
declarations.statement:
public noncomputable abbrev FlatnessSituation.HasUniversalFlattening
    (D : FlatnessSituation.{u}) : Prop
declarations.comment: the universal flattening of a module

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.HasUniversalFlattening
declarations.doc: A scheme over `S` admits a universal flattening when its structure sheaf does.
declarations.statement: public noncomputable abbrev HasUniversalFlattening {X S : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ S) : Prop
declarations.comment: the universal flattening of a scheme

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.FlatnessSituation.HasFlatteningStratification
declarations.doc:
A quasi-coherent module has a flattening stratification if its flatness functor is
represented by the monomorphism associated to a locally finite scheme-theoretic stratification
of the base: closed subschemes `J i`, indexed by a partial order, whose supports cover `S` and
form a locally finite family, with `J i ⊔ J j` the infimum of the `J k` for `k ≤ i` and `k ≤ j`,
together with opens `U i` of the subschemes `J i` whose images are the supports of `J i` minus
those of the `J j` with `j < i`, such that the representing object is isomorphic over `S` to the
coproduct of the `U i` and its structure morphism is a monomorphism.
declarations.statement: public def FlatnessSituation.HasFlatteningStratification (D : FlatnessSituation.{u}) : Prop
declarations.comment: the module

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.HasFlatteningStratification
declarations.doc: A scheme over `S` has a flattening stratification when its structure sheaf does.
declarations.statement: public abbrev HasFlatteningStratification {X S : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ S) : Prop
declarations.comment: the scheme

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.fittingClosedSubscheme_antitone
declarations.doc:
The closed subschemes cut out by the Fitting ideals of a quasi-coherent module of finite type
decrease with the index: for `i ≤ j` the `j`-th one admits a morphism over the base scheme to the
`i`-th one, namely the inclusion of closed subschemes coming from the inclusion of Fitting
ideals.
declarations.statement:
theorem fittingClosedSubscheme_antitone {S : Scheme.{u}} (F : S.Modules) [F.IsFiniteType]
    [F.IsQuasicoherent] {i j : ℕ} (hij : i ≤ j) :
    Nonempty (fittingClosedSubscheme F (j : ℤ) ⟶ fittingClosedSubscheme F (i : ℤ))
declarations.comment: the Fitting ideals cut out a descending chain of closed subschemes

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.fittingClosedSubscheme_iInter_range_eq_empty
declarations.doc:
The Fitting closed subschemes of a quasi-coherent module of finite type exhaust the base
scheme: the images in `S` of the subschemes indexed by the natural numbers meet in the empty set.
Indeed, if `x` lies in an affine open `U` whose module of sections is generated by `n` elements,
then the `n`-th Fitting ideal is the unit ideal on `U`, so `x` avoids the `n`-th member.
declarations.statement:
theorem fittingClosedSubscheme_iInter_range_eq_empty {S : Scheme.{u}} (F : S.Modules)
    [F.IsFiniteType] [F.IsQuasicoherent] :
    (⋂ i : ℕ, Set.range (fittingClosedSubscheme F (i : ℤ)).hom.base) = ∅
declarations.comment: property (1): the Fitting closed subschemes have empty intersection

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.fittingClosedSubscheme_finitePresentation
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 05P8.** The closed subscheme of `S` cut out by the `r`-th Fitting ideal
of a finitely presented sheaf of modules `F` is of finite presentation over `S`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem fittingClosedSubscheme_finitePresentation {S : Scheme.{u}} (F : S.Modules)
    [F.IsFinitePresentation] (r : ℕ) :
    FinitePresentation
      (@fittingClosedSubscheme S F (SheafOfModules.instIsFiniteTypeOfIsFinitePresentation F)
        (SheafOfModules.instIsQuasicoherentOfIsFinitePresentation F) (r : ℤ)).hom
declarations.comment: finite presentation of the morphism Z_r to S

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.fittingGeneratorOpen_finitePresentation
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 05P8.** The open complement in `S` of the closed subscheme cut out by
the `r`-th Fitting ideal of a finitely presented sheaf of modules `F` — the locus where `F` is
generated by `r` sections — is of finite presentation over `S`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem fittingGeneratorOpen_finitePresentation {S : Scheme.{u}} (F : S.Modules)
    [F.IsFinitePresentation] (r : ℕ) :
    FinitePresentation
      (@fittingGeneratorOpen S F (SheafOfModules.instIsFiniteTypeOfIsFinitePresentation F)
        (SheafOfModules.instIsQuasicoherentOfIsFinitePresentation F) r).ι
declarations.comment: finite presentation of the morphism S minus Z_r to S

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.locallyGenerated_iff_factorsThrough_fittingGeneratorOpen
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 05P8.** The pullback of a finite type quasi-coherent module `F` along
`f : T ⟶ S` is generated by `r` sections near every point of `T` if and only if `f` factors
uniquely through the open complement of the `r`-th Fitting closed subscheme of `F`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem locallyGenerated_iff_factorsThrough_fittingGeneratorOpen
    {S T : Scheme.{u}} (F : S.Modules) [F.IsFiniteType] [F.IsQuasicoherent]
    (r : ℕ) (f : T ⟶ S) :
    (∀ t : T, IsGeneratedByNear ((Scheme.Modules.pullback f).obj F) r t) ↔
      ∃! g : T ⟶ (fittingGeneratorOpen F r).toScheme,
        g ≫ (fittingGeneratorOpen F r).ι = f
declarations.comment: property (2): representability of the functor of generation by <= r sections

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.isImmersion_fittingRankStratum
declarations.doc:
The structural morphism of the rank `r` Fitting stratum is a locally closed immersion: it
is the inclusion of an open subscheme followed by a closed immersion.
declarations.comment: property (3): the rank r stratum is a locally closed subscheme

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.rankRFunctor_representableBy_fittingRankStratum
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 05P8.** The rank `r` functor of a finite type quasi-coherent module
`F` on `S` is represented by the rank `r` Fitting stratum of `F`, a locally closed subscheme of
`S`.
declarations.comment: property (3): representability of the functor of local freeness of rank r

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.finitePresentation_fittingRankStratum
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 05P8.** The structural morphism of the rank `r` Fitting stratum of a
finitely presented sheaf of modules `F` on `S` — the locally closed subscheme of `S` over which
`F` pulls back to a module finite locally free of rank `r` — is of finite presentation.
declarations.statement:
public theorem finitePresentation_fittingRankStratum {S : Scheme.{u}} (F : S.Modules)
    [F.IsFinitePresentation] (r : ℕ) :
    FinitePresentation
      (@fittingRankStratum S F (SheafOfModules.instIsFiniteTypeOfIsFinitePresentation F)
        (SheafOfModules.instIsQuasicoherentOfIsFinitePresentation F) r).hom
declarations.comment: finite presentation of the morphism Z_(r-1) minus Z_r to S

declarations.name: Stacks.Fitting.idealSheaf_monotone
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 05P8.** The Fitting ideal sheaves increase, so the closed subschemes
they cut out form a decreasing chain.
declarations.statement: theorem idealSheaf_monotone {X : Scheme.{u}} (F : X.Modules) : Monotone (idealSheaf F)
declarations.comment: decreasing closed subschemes

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.rankStratum_isFiniteLocallyFreeOfRank
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 05P9.** The module restricts to a finite locally free module of rank
`r` on the `r`-th Fitting rank stratum.
declarations.comment: rank on each stratum

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.flat_iff_existsUnique_lift
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 05P9.** A pullback of a finitely presented module is flat exactly when
the morphism to the base factors, necessarily uniquely, through the flattening stratification —
the disjoint union of the Fitting rank strata.
declarations.statement:
public theorem flat_iff_existsUnique_lift {T : Scheme.{u}} (g : T ⟶ S) :
    SheafOfModules.IsFlat (C := TopologicalSpace.Opens T.toTopCat)
        (J := Opens.grothendieckTopology T.toTopCat) (O := T.sheaf)
        ((Scheme.Modules.pullback g).obj F) ↔
      ∃! h : T ⟶ @flatnessStratification S F
          (SheafOfModules.instIsFiniteTypeOfIsFinitePresentation F)
          (SheafOfModules.instIsQuasicoherentOfIsFinitePresentation F),
        h ≫ @flatnessStratificationHom S F
          (SheafOfModules.instIsFiniteTypeOfIsFinitePresentation F)
          (SheafOfModules.instIsQuasicoherentOfIsFinitePresentation F) = g
declarations.comment: representability

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.flatnessStratification_finitePresentation
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 05P9.** The structural morphism of the flattening stratification is of
finite presentation: it is locally of finite presentation because each stratum is, quasi-compact
because the Fitting generator opens exhaust the base, and quasi-separated because it is
injective.
declarations.statement:
public theorem flatnessStratification_finitePresentation :
    FinitePresentation (@flatnessStratificationHom S F
      (SheafOfModules.instIsFiniteTypeOfIsFinitePresentation F)
      (SheafOfModules.instIsQuasicoherentOfIsFinitePresentation F))
declarations.comment: finite presentation of the disjoint union

registrations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.finitePresentation_fittingRankStratum
registrations.comment: finite presentation of each stratum

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.FlatnessSituation.exists_closedUniversalFlattening_of_isArtinianRing
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 05PB.** A quasi-coherent module on a scheme over the spectrum of an
Artinian ring admits a universal flattening, and the representing morphism is a closed
immersion.
declarations.statement:
public theorem exists_closedUniversalFlattening_of_isArtinianRing {R : Type u} [CommRing R]
    [IsArtinianRing R] (D : FlatnessSituation.{u}) (hS : D.S = Spec (.of R)) :
    ∃ W : Over D.S, IsClosedImmersion W.hom ∧ Nonempty (D.flatFunctor.RepresentableBy W)
declarations.comment: the closed universal flattening

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.FlatnessSituation.hasFlatteningStratification_of_isArtinianRing
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 05PB.** A quasi-coherent module on a scheme over the spectrum of an
Artinian ring has a flattening stratification.
declarations.statement:
public theorem hasFlatteningStratification_of_isArtinianRing {R : Type u} [CommRing R]
    [IsArtinianRing R] (D : FlatnessSituation.{u}) (hS : D.S = Spec (.of R)) :
    D.HasFlatteningStratification
declarations.comment: the flattening stratification

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.mono_pullbackPushforwardUnit_of_relativeAssassin_subset_range
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 05PD.** Let `S` be a scheme, let `g : X' ⟶ X` be a flat morphism of
schemes over `S` with `X` locally of finite type over `S`, and let `F` be a finite type
quasi-coherent `𝒪_X`-module which is flat over `S`. If `Ass_{X/S}(F) ⊆ g(X')`, then the
canonical map `F ⟶ g_* g^* F` is injective.
declarations.statement:
theorem mono_pullbackPushforwardUnit_of_relativeAssassin_subset_range
    {X' X S : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ S) (g : X' ⟶ X)
    [LocallyOfFiniteType f] [Flat g]
    (F : X.Modules) [F.IsQuasicoherent] [F.IsFiniteType]
    (hF : IsFlatOver f.toLRSHom.toShHom F)
    (hAss : Stacks.Divisors.relativeAssassin f F ⊆ Set.range g.base) :
    Mono ((Scheme.Modules.pullbackPushforwardAdjunction g).unit.app F)
declarations.comment: injectivity

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.mono_baseChange_pullbackPushforwardUnit_of_relativeAssassin_subset_range
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 05PD.** The canonical map of the preceding statement remains injective
after an arbitrary base change `h : T ⟶ S`: the map
`F_T ⟶ (g_T)_* (g_T)^* F_T` on `X ×_S T` is injective as well.
declarations.statement:
theorem mono_baseChange_pullbackPushforwardUnit_of_relativeAssassin_subset_range
    {X' X S : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ S) (g : X' ⟶ X)
    [LocallyOfFiniteType f] [Flat g]
    (F : X.Modules) [F.IsQuasicoherent] [F.IsFiniteType]
    (hF : IsFlatOver f.toLRSHom.toShHom F)
    (hAss : Stacks.Divisors.relativeAssassin f F ⊆ Set.range g.base) :
    ∀ (T : Scheme.{u}) (h : T ⟶ S),
      Mono ((Scheme.Modules.pullbackPushforwardAdjunction (compBaseChangeMap f g h)).unit.app
        ((Scheme.Modules.pullback (pullback.fst f h)).obj F))
declarations.comment: after arbitrary base change

declarations.name: Module.exists_ideal_bijective_rTensor_iff_map_eq_bot
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 05PE.** A surjection from a projective module has a
flattening ideal: after every base change, the map is an isomorphism exactly
when the image of this ideal vanishes.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_ideal_bijective_rTensor_iff_map_eq_bot
    (u : M →ₗ[A] N) (hu : Function.Surjective u) [Module.Projective A M] :
    ∃ I : Ideal A, ∀ (B : Type*) [CommRing B] [Algebra A B],
      Function.Bijective (u.rTensor B) ↔ Ideal.map (algebraMap A B) I = ⊥

declarations.name: Stacks.Flatness.exists_closedImmersion_representableBy_isomorphismFunctor_finitePresentation
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 05PF.** Let `f : X ⟶ S` be a morphism of finite presentation (locally
of finite presentation, quasi-compact and quasi-separated, Tag 01TP) and let `u : F ⟶ G` be a
surjection of quasi-coherent modules on `X` with `F` of finite presentation, flat over `S` and
pure relative to `S`.  Then the functor `F_iso` on schemes over `S`, whose value at
`T` is a point exactly when the base change `u_T` is an isomorphism, is represented by a closed
immersion `Z ⟶ S`; moreover `Z ⟶ S` is of finite presentation if `G` is of finite presentation.

The representing closed immersion comes from the étale-local devissage
`Stacks.Flatness.exists_closedImmersion_representableBy_isomorphismFunctor`: purity reduces the
question étale locally on `S` to an affine situation with projective sections, cut out by the
flattening ideal of Tag 05PE, and the local closed subschemes glue by fpqc descent (Tags 05MJ,
03I0).  Its finite presentation is
`Stacks.Flatness.finitePresentation_hom_of_representableBy_isomorphismFunctor`, from Tag 05MJ(4)
and Tag 05LX.

The instance `F.IsFiniteType` is part of the statement because purity relative to `S` is phrased
for modules of finite type; it follows from `F.IsFinitePresentation` by
`Stacks.AlgebraicGeometry.CoherentTFAE.isQuasicoherent_isFiniteType_of_isFinitePresentation`, so
it adds nothing to the source's assumptions.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_closedImmersion_representableBy_isomorphismFunctor_finitePresentation
    (D : ModuleMapBaseChangeSituation.{u})
    [LocallyOfFinitePresentation D.f] [QuasiCompact D.f] [QuasiSeparated D.f]
    [D.F.IsFinitePresentation] [D.F.IsFiniteType] [Epi D.hom]
    (hflat : IsFlatOver D.f.toLRSHom.toShHom D.F)
    (hpure : IsPureRelative D.f D.F) :
    ∃ W : Over D.S, IsClosedImmersion W.hom ∧
      Nonempty (D.isomorphismFunctor.RepresentableBy W) ∧
      (D.G.IsFinitePresentation → FinitePresentation W.hom)
declarations.comment: both assertions: representability by a closed immersion, which is of finite presentation when `G` is

declarations.name: Module.FlatAtPointSituation.exists_ideal_condition_iff_map_eq_bot_of_henselian
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 05PG.** Let `A → B` be a local homomorphism of local rings with `A`
henselian and `B` essentially of finite type over `A`, and let `M` be a finite `B`-module. There
is an ideal `I ⊆ A` such that `A ⧸ I` corepresents the functor `F_lf` of Stacks Tag 05MK: for
every local `A`-algebra `A'` with local structure map, the base change of `M` is flat over `A'`
at every prime of `B ⊗_A A'` containing the extensions of the maximal ideals of `A'` and of `B`
exactly when `I` dies in `A'`. If `B` is essentially of finite presentation over `A` and `M` is
of finite presentation over `B`, then `I` is finitely generated.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_ideal_condition_iff_map_eq_bot_of_henselian
    (S : FlatAtPointSituation.{u, v, w}) [HenselianLocalRing S.A]
    [Algebra.EssFiniteType S.A S.B] [Module.Finite S.B S.M] :
    ∃ I : Ideal S.A,
      (∀ R : LocalAlgCat.{u, x} S.A, S.Condition R ↔ Ideal.map (algebraMap S.A R) I = ⊥) ∧
      ((algebraMap S.A S.B).EssentiallyOfFinitePresentation →
        Module.FinitePresentation S.B S.M → I.FG)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.exists_closedSubscheme_flatOverAt_iff_factorStalk
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 05PH.** A closed subscheme detects flatness of the
pulled-back module at every point of the distinguished fibre lying above `x`.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_closedSubscheme_flatOverAt_iff_factorStalk
    {X S : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ S) [LocallyOfFiniteType f]
    (F : X.Modules) [F.IsQuasicoherent] [F.IsFiniteType]
    (x : X) (s : S) (hxs : f x = s)
    [HenselianLocalRing (S.presheaf.stalk s)]
    [IsIso (S.fromSpecStalk s)] :
    ∃ I : S.IdealSheafData,
      ∀ {T : Scheme.{u}} (g : T ⟶ S) (t : T) (_ht : g t = s),
        (∀ y : pullback (C := Scheme.{u}) f g,
            (pullback.snd f g y = t) →
            (pullback.fst f g y = x) →
              AlgebraicGeometry.IsFlatOverAt
                (pullback.snd f g).toLRSHom.toShHom
                ((Scheme.Modules.pullback (pullback.fst f g)).obj F) y) ↔
          ∃ h : Spec (T.presheaf.stalk t) ⟶ I.subscheme,
            h ≫ I.subschemeι = T.fromSpecStalk t ≫ g
declarations.comment: the local flattening subscheme

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.exists_finitePresentation_closedSubscheme_flatOverAt_iff_factorStalk
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 05PH.** Under pointwise finite-presentation
hypotheses, the local flattening subscheme can be finitely presented.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_finitePresentation_closedSubscheme_flatOverAt_iff_factorStalk
    {X S : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ S) [LocallyOfFiniteType f]
    (F : X.Modules) [F.IsQuasicoherent] [F.IsFiniteType]
    (x : X) (s : S) (hxs : f x = s)
    [HenselianLocalRing (S.presheaf.stalk s)]
    [IsIso (S.fromSpecStalk s)]
    (hfp : FinitePresentationAt f x)
    (hFfp :
      letI : Module (X.presheaf.stalk x)
          (TopCat.Presheaf.stalk (C := Ab.{u}) F.val.presheaf x) :=
        PresheafOfModules.instModuleCarrierStalkCommRingCatCarrierAbPresheafOpensCarrier
          (R := X.presheaf) F.val x
      Module.FinitePresentation (X.presheaf.stalk x)
        (TopCat.Presheaf.stalk (C := Ab.{u}) F.val.presheaf x)) :
    ∃ I : S.IdealSheafData,
      FinitePresentation I.subschemeι ∧
      ∀ {T : Scheme.{u}} (g : T ⟶ S) (t : T) (_ht : g t = s),
        (∀ y : pullback (C := Scheme.{u}) f g,
            (pullback.snd f g y = t) →
            (pullback.fst f g y = x) →
              AlgebraicGeometry.IsFlatOverAt
                (pullback.snd f g).toLRSHom.toShHom
                ((Scheme.Modules.pullback (pullback.fst f g)).obj F) y) ↔
          ∃ h : Spec (T.presheaf.stalk t) ⟶ I.subscheme,
            h ≫ I.subschemeι = T.fromSpecStalk t ≫ g
declarations.comment: finite-presentation refinement

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.exists_finitePresentation_closedSubscheme_flatOverAt_iff_factors
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 05PI.** When the morphism and the module are in addition locally of
finite presentation and the chosen subset of the closed fibre is closed and quasi-compact, the
closed subscheme of the henselian local base detecting flatness along that subset can be chosen
of finite presentation.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_finitePresentation_closedSubscheme_flatOverAt_iff_factors
    (A : Type u) [CommRing A] [HenselianLocalRing A]
    {X : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ Spec (.of A)) [LocallyOfFiniteType f]
    [LocallyOfFinitePresentation f]
    (F : X.Modules) [F.IsFiniteType] [F.IsQuasicoherent]
    [F.IsFinitePresentation]
    (E : Set (f.fiber (IsLocalRing.closedPoint A)))
    (_ : IsClosed E) (hEcompact : IsCompact E) :
    ∃ I : (Spec (.of A)).IdealSheafData,
      FinitePresentation I.subschemeι ∧
      ∀ (T : Scheme.{u}) (g : T ⟶ Spec (.of A)) (t : T)
        (_ : g t = IsLocalRing.closedPoint A),
        (∀ y : (pullback f g : Scheme.{u}),
          (pullback.snd f g) y = t →
          (pullback.fst f g) y ∈
            (f.fiberι (IsLocalRing.closedPoint A)) '' E →
          AlgebraicGeometry.IsFlatOverAt (pullback.snd f g).toLRSHom.toShHom
            ((Scheme.Modules.pullback (pullback.fst f g)).obj F) y) ↔
        ∃ h : Spec (T.presheaf.stalk t) ⟶ I.subscheme,
          h ≫ I.subschemeι = T.fromSpecStalk t ≫ g
declarations.comment: finite-presentation refinement

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.exists_closedSubscheme_flatOverAt_iff_factors
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 05PI.** Flatness of a finite type quasi-coherent module along an
arbitrary subset `E` of the closed fibre, after an arbitrary pointed base change of a henselian
local base, is detected by a closed subscheme of that base: the flatness condition for a pointed
scheme `(T, t)` over `(Spec A, closed point)` holds exactly when `Spec O_{T,t} ⟶ Spec A` factors
through the closed subscheme.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_closedSubscheme_flatOverAt_iff_factors
    (A : Type u) [CommRing A] [HenselianLocalRing A]
    {X : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ Spec (.of A)) [LocallyOfFiniteType f]
    (F : X.Modules) [F.IsFiniteType] [F.IsQuasicoherent]
    (E : Set (f.fiber (IsLocalRing.closedPoint A))) :
    ∃ I : (Spec (.of A)).IdealSheafData,
      ∀ (T : Scheme.{u}) (g : T ⟶ Spec (.of A)) (t : T)
        (_ : g t = IsLocalRing.closedPoint A),
        (∀ y : (pullback f g : Scheme.{u}),
          (pullback.snd f g) y = t →
          (pullback.fst f g) y ∈
            (f.fiberι (IsLocalRing.closedPoint A)) '' E →
          AlgebraicGeometry.IsFlatOverAt (pullback.snd f g).toLRSHom.toShHom
            ((Scheme.Modules.pullback (pullback.fst f g)).obj F) y) ↔
        ∃ h : Spec (T.presheaf.stalk t) ⟶ I.subscheme,
          h ≫ I.subschemeι = T.fromSpecStalk t ≫ g
declarations.comment: closed flattening subscheme

declarations.name: Stacks.Sites.EpiPretopology.exists_pretopology_epiCoverings
declarations.doc:
**Statement 1 (Stacks Tag 05PM).** The assignment `U ↦ EpiCoverings U`
satisfies the three pretopology axioms and hence determines a pretopology on the
abelian category `𝒜`, with coverings given exactly by `EpiCoverings`.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_pretopology_epiCoverings :
    ∃ K : Pretopology 𝒜, ∀ U : 𝒜, K.coverings U = EpiCoverings 𝒜 U

declarations.name: Stacks.Injectives.preadditiveYoneda_obj_isSheaf
declarations.doc:
Additive representable presheaves on an abelian category are sheaves for the topology
generated by epimorphism covers.
declarations.statement:
theorem preadditiveYoneda_obj_isSheaf (X : 𝒜) :
    Presheaf.IsSheaf (epiPretopology 𝒜).toGrothendieck (preadditiveYoneda.obj X)
declarations.comment: the embedding

declarations.name: Stacks.Injectives.yonedaSheaf
declarations.doc:
The Yoneda functor from an abelian category to abelian sheaves for its epimorphism
topology. Its underlying presheaf functor is definitionally the additive Yoneda functor.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def yonedaSheaf :
    𝒜 ⥤ Sheaf (epiPretopology 𝒜).toGrothendieck AddCommGrpCat.{v}
declarations.comment: the embedding

declarations.name: Stacks.Injectives.yonedaSheaf_full
declarations.doc: The Yoneda functor into abelian sheaves is full.
declarations.statement: theorem yonedaSheaf_full : (yonedaSheaf 𝒜).Full
declarations.comment: the embedding

declarations.name: Stacks.Injectives.yonedaSheaf_faithful
declarations.doc: The Yoneda functor into abelian sheaves is faithful.
declarations.statement: theorem yonedaSheaf_faithful : (yonedaSheaf 𝒜).Faithful
declarations.comment: the embedding

declarations.name: Stacks.Injectives.yonedaSheaf_preservesFiniteLimits
declarations.doc: The Yoneda functor into abelian sheaves preserves finite limits.
declarations.statement: theorem yonedaSheaf_preservesFiniteLimits : PreservesFiniteLimits (yonedaSheaf 𝒜)
declarations.comment: the embedding

declarations.name: Stacks.Injectives.yonedaSheaf_preservesFiniteColimits
declarations.doc: The Yoneda functor into abelian sheaves preserves finite colimits.
declarations.statement: theorem yonedaSheaf_preservesFiniteColimits : PreservesFiniteColimits (yonedaSheaf 𝒜)
declarations.comment: the embedding

declarations.name: Stacks.Injectives.epiPretopology_hasEnoughPoints
declarations.doc:
The site on an abelian category whose covers are singleton epimorphisms has enough
points.
declarations.comment: enough points

declarations.name: Stacks.Injectives.preservesFiniteLimits_sheafSections
declarations.doc:
Finite limits of abelian sheaves are computed sectionwise: taking sections over a fixed
object is left exact.
declarations.statement:
theorem preservesFiniteLimits_sheafSections (U : Cᵒᵖ) :
    PreservesFiniteLimits ((sheafSections J AddCommGrpCat.{max u v}).obj U)
declarations.comment: diagram chasing: sections

declarations.name: Stacks.Injectives.isLimit_of_forall_isLimit_sheafSections
declarations.doc:
A cone of abelian sheaves which becomes a limit cone after taking sections over every object
is a limit cone.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def isLimit_of_forall_isLimit_sheafSections {T : Type*} [Category T]
    {K : T ⥤ Sheaf J AddCommGrpCat.{max u v}} (c : Cone K)
    (h : ∀ U : Cᵒᵖ,
      IsLimit (((sheafSections J AddCommGrpCat.{max u v}).obj U).mapCone c)) :
    IsLimit c
declarations.comment: diagram chasing: sections

declarations.name: Stacks.Injectives.mono_iff_forall_injective_app
declarations.doc:
A morphism of abelian sheaves is a monomorphism if and only if it is injective on sections
over every object.
declarations.statement:
theorem mono_iff_forall_injective_app {F G : Sheaf J AddCommGrpCat.{max u v}} (f : F ⟶ G) :
    Mono f ↔ ∀ U : Cᵒᵖ, Function.Injective (f.hom.app U)
declarations.comment: diagram chasing: sections

declarations.name: Stacks.Injectives.epi_iff_forall_exists_local_lift
declarations.doc:
A morphism of abelian sheaves `f : F ⟶ G` is an epimorphism if and only if every section of
`G` over an object `U` lifts along `f` on the arrows of some covering sieve of `U`.
declarations.statement:
theorem epi_iff_forall_exists_local_lift {F G : Sheaf J AddCommGrpCat.{max u v}} (f : F ⟶ G) :
    Epi f ↔ ∀ (U : C) (s : ToType (G.obj.obj (op U))),
      ∃ R : Sieve U, R ∈ J U ∧ ∀ ⦃V : C⦄ (g : V ⟶ U), R g →
        ∃ t : ToType (F.obj.obj (op V)), f.hom.app (op V) t = G.obj.map g.op s
declarations.comment: diagram chasing: sections

declarations.name: Stacks.Injectives.exact_of_forall_exists_local_lift
declarations.doc:
A short complex of abelian sheaves is exact as soon as every section of its middle term
annihilated by the second map lifts along the first map on the arrows of some covering sieve.
declarations.statement:
theorem exact_of_forall_exists_local_lift {S : ShortComplex (Sheaf J AddCommGrpCat.{max u v})}
    (h : ∀ (U : C) (a : ToType (S.X₂.obj.obj (op U))), S.g.hom.app (op U) a = 0 →
      ∃ R : Sieve U, R ∈ J U ∧ ∀ ⦃V : C⦄ (φ : V ⟶ U), R φ →
        ∃ b : ToType (S.X₁.obj.obj (op V)),
          S.f.hom.app (op V) b = S.X₂.obj.map φ.op a) :
    S.Exact
declarations.comment: diagram chasing: sections

declarations.name: Stacks.Injectives.exact_iff_forall_sheafFiber_exact
declarations.doc:
Let `{p_i}` be a conservative family of points of a site. A short complex of abelian sheaves
is exact if and only if the short complex of stalks at `p_i` is exact for every `i`.
declarations.statement:
theorem exact_iff_forall_sheafFiber_exact
    {P : ObjectProperty (GrothendieckTopology.Point.{max u v} J)}
    (hP : P.IsConservativeFamilyOfPoints)
    (S : ShortComplex (Sheaf J AddCommGrpCat.{max u v})) :
    S.Exact ↔ ∀ Φ : P.FullSubcategory,
      (S.map (Φ.obj.sheafFiber (A := AddCommGrpCat.{max u v}))).Exact
declarations.comment: diagram chasing: stalks

declarations.name: Stacks.Injectives.exists_conservativeFamily_exact_iff
declarations.doc:
On a site which has a conservative family of points
(`CategoryTheory.GrothendieckTopology.HasConservativeFamily`) there is a conservative family of
points on whose stalks the exactness of short complexes of abelian sheaves can be tested.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_conservativeFamily_exact_iff (J : GrothendieckTopology C)
    (h : GrothendieckTopology.HasConservativeFamily.{max u v} J) :
    ∃ P : ObjectProperty (GrothendieckTopology.Point.{max u v} J),
      P.IsConservativeFamilyOfPoints ∧
      ∀ S : ShortComplex (Sheaf J AddCommGrpCat.{max u v}),
        (S.Exact ↔ ∀ Φ : P.FullSubcategory,
          (S.map (Φ.obj.sheafFiber (A := AddCommGrpCat.{max u v}))).Exact)
declarations.comment: diagram chasing: stalks

declarations.name: exists_small_abelian_full_subcategory
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 05PQ**, first assertion. Let `𝒜` be an abelian category — in particular one whose
objects form a class — and let `A : S → 𝒜` be a family of objects indexed by a set `S`. There
is an object property `P` whose full subcategory `𝒜' = P.FullSubcategory` has a set of objects,
contains every `A s`, and admits an abelian structure for which the inclusion `P.ι` is additive
and exact.

Nothing beyond `Abelian 𝒜` is assumed; compare
`exists_small_abelian_subcategory_with_enough_injectives` (Stacks 0010), which additionally
assumes `EnoughInjectives 𝒜` and produces a subcategory with enough injectives.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_small_abelian_full_subcategory (A : S → 𝒜) :
    ∃ (P : ObjectProperty 𝒜),
      Small.{max v w} P.FullSubcategory ∧
      (∀ s, P (A s)) ∧
      ∃ (_ : Abelian P.FullSubcategory),
        P.ι.Additive ∧
        Nonempty (PreservesFiniteLimits P.ι) ∧
        Nonempty (PreservesFiniteColimits P.ι)
declarations.comment: the small abelian subcategory

declarations.name: Stacks.Injectives.exists_small_abelian_subcategory_yonedaSheaf
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 05PQ.** Let `𝒜` be an abelian category — in particular one whose objects form a
class, so that Tag 05PN does not apply to `𝒜` itself — and let `A : S → 𝒜` be a family of
objects indexed by a set `S`. There is an object property `P` such that the full subcategory
`𝒜' = P.FullSubcategory` has a set of objects, contains every `A s`, and admits an abelian
structure for which:

* the inclusion `P.ι : 𝒜' ⥤ 𝒜` is additive and exact, and
* there is a full, faithful and exact functor from `𝒜'` to the category of abelian sheaves on
  the epimorphism site of `𝒜'`, a site which has a conservative family of points.

The second item is Tag 05PN applied to `𝒜'`, and together with the first it is what lets a
result in `𝒜` whose proof is a diagram chase be proved by chasing in abelian sheaves.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_small_abelian_subcategory_yonedaSheaf (A : S → 𝒜) :
    ∃ (P : ObjectProperty 𝒜),
      Small.{max v w} P.FullSubcategory ∧
      (∀ s, P (A s)) ∧
      ∃ (_ : Abelian P.FullSubcategory),
        P.ι.Additive ∧
        Nonempty (PreservesFiniteLimits P.ι) ∧
        Nonempty (PreservesFiniteColimits P.ι) ∧
        ∃ F : P.FullSubcategory ⥤
            Sheaf (epiPretopology P.FullSubcategory).toGrothendieck AddCommGrpCat.{v},
          F.Full ∧ F.Faithful ∧
            Nonempty (PreservesFiniteLimits F) ∧ Nonempty (PreservesFiniteColimits F) ∧
            GrothendieckTopology.HasConservativeFamily.{max u v}
              (epiPretopology P.FullSubcategory).toGrothendieck

declarations.name: Stacks.Injectives.oppEpiSheaf_enoughInjectives
declarations.doc: **Stacks 05PR**, first clause. `Ab(C)` has enough injectives.
declarations.statement: theorem oppEpiSheaf_enoughInjectives : EnoughInjectives (oppEpiSheaf A)
declarations.comment: Ab(C) has enough injectives

declarations.name: Stacks.Injectives.oppEpiSheaf_exists_injective_coseparator
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 05PR**, second clause: `Ab(C)` has a cogenerator. The source omits the details; here
it comes from `Ab(C)` being a Grothendieck abelian category, which moreover makes the cogenerator
injective.
declarations.statement:
theorem oppEpiSheaf_exists_injective_coseparator :
    ∃ G : oppEpiSheaf A, Injective G ∧ IsCoseparator G
declarations.comment: Ab(C) has a cogenerator

declarations.name: Stacks.Injectives.oppEpiEmbedding_full
declarations.doc: **Stacks 05PR**, third clause. The functor `i : A ⥤ D` is full.
declarations.statement: theorem oppEpiEmbedding_full : (oppEpiEmbedding A).Full
declarations.comment: the embedding i : A ⥤ D

declarations.name: Stacks.Injectives.oppEpiEmbedding_faithful
declarations.doc: **Stacks 05PR**, third clause. The functor `i : A ⥤ D` is faithful.
declarations.statement: theorem oppEpiEmbedding_faithful : (oppEpiEmbedding A).Faithful
declarations.comment: the embedding i : A ⥤ D

declarations.name: Stacks.Injectives.oppEpiEmbedding_preservesFiniteLimits
declarations.doc: **Stacks 05PR**, third clause. The functor `i : A ⥤ D` is left exact.
declarations.statement:
theorem oppEpiEmbedding_preservesFiniteLimits :
    PreservesFiniteLimits (oppEpiEmbedding A)
declarations.comment: the embedding i : A ⥤ D

declarations.name: Stacks.Injectives.oppEpiEmbedding_preservesFiniteColimits
declarations.doc: **Stacks 05PR**, third clause. The functor `i : A ⥤ D` is right exact.
declarations.statement:
theorem oppEpiEmbedding_preservesFiniteColimits :
    PreservesFiniteColimits (oppEpiEmbedding A)
declarations.comment: the embedding i : A ⥤ D

declarations.name: Stacks.Injectives.oppEpiSheafOp_enoughProjectives
declarations.doc: **Stacks 05PR**, fourth clause. `D = Bᵒᵖ` has enough projectives.
declarations.statement: theorem oppEpiSheafOp_enoughProjectives : EnoughProjectives (oppEpiSheaf A)ᵒᵖ
declarations.comment: D has enough projectives

declarations.name: Stacks.Injectives.oppEpiSheafOp_exists_projective_separator
declarations.doc: **Stacks 05PR**, fourth clause. `D = Bᵒᵖ` has a generator, hence a projective generator.
declarations.statement:
theorem oppEpiSheafOp_exists_projective_separator :
    ∃ P : (oppEpiSheaf A)ᵒᵖ, Projective P ∧ IsSeparator P
declarations.comment: D has a projective generator

declarations.name: Stacks.Injectives.exists_projectiveSeparator_hom_fullyFaithful_exact
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 05PR**, last clause. There is a projective generator `P` of `D = Bᵒᵖ` such that

`A ⟶ Mod_R, X ↦ Hom_D(P, X)` with `R = Mor_D(P, P)`

is a fully faithful exact functor. This is the Freyd--Mitchell embedding theorem for a small
abelian category, obtained along the route of Tag 05PR.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_projectiveSeparator_hom_fullyFaithful_exact :
    ∃ P : (oppEpiSheaf A)ᵒᵖ, Projective P ∧ IsSeparator P ∧
      (oppEpiEmbedding A ⋙ preadditiveCoyonedaObj P).Full ∧
      (oppEpiEmbedding A ⋙ preadditiveCoyonedaObj P).Faithful ∧
      PreservesFiniteLimits (oppEpiEmbedding A ⋙ preadditiveCoyonedaObj P) ∧
      PreservesFiniteColimits (oppEpiEmbedding A ⋙ preadditiveCoyonedaObj P)
declarations.comment: the embedding into `Hom_D(P, -)` for a projective generator `P`

declarations.name: Stacks.Injectives.exists_ring_moduleEmbedding
declarations.doc:
**The Freyd--Mitchell embedding theorem**, in the form Tag 05PR retrieves it: for every
abelian category `A` there are a ring `R` and a fully faithful exact functor `A ⥤ Mod_R`.

The functor produced here is `X ↦ Hom_D(P, X)` for a projective generator `P` of the opposite of
the category of abelian sheaves on the epimorphism site of `Aᵒᵖ`, as in Tag 05PR. The conclusion
is the same as Mathlib's `CategoryTheory.Abelian.freyd_mitchell`, which carries Tag 05PP and is
proved instead through Gabriel--Popescu; what Tag 05PR asserts, and what this declaration
records, is that the theorem is retrieved from Tag 05PN by the route above.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_ring_moduleEmbedding (A : Type u) [Category.{v} A] [Abelian A] :
    ∃ (R : Type (max u v)) (_ : Ring R) (F : A ⥤ ModuleCat.{max u v} R),
      F.Full ∧ F.Faithful ∧ PreservesFiniteLimits F ∧ PreservesFiniteColimits F

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.EssentiallyConstantInd.IsEssentiallyConstantWith
declarations.doc:
`M` is essentially constant as an ind-object with value `t.pt`, with respect
to the cocone `t`, witnessed by an index `i` and a morphism `r : t.pt ⟶ M i`, if
`r` splits the coprojection `c_i` and is cofinal.
declarations.statement:
structure IsEssentiallyConstantWith (M : J ⥤ C) (t : Cocone M) (i : J)
    (r : t.pt ⟶ M.obj i) : Prop
declarations.comment: (1), filtered case, conditions (a) and (b) with value t.pt

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.EssentiallyConstantInd.IsEssentiallyConstantInd
declarations.doc:
`M` is an *essentially constant ind-object* if there exist a cocone `t`, an
index `i`, and a morphism `r : t.pt ⟶ M i` witnessing it.
declarations.statement: def IsEssentiallyConstantInd (M : I ⥤ C) : Prop
declarations.comment: (1), filtered case: the predicate that M is essentially constant

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.EssentiallyConstantPro.IsEssentiallyConstantPro
declarations.doc:
`M` is an *essentially constant pro-object* if there exist a cone `c`, an
index `i`, and a morphism `s : M i ⟶ c.pt` witnessing it.
declarations.statement: def IsEssentiallyConstantPro (M : I ⥤ C) : Prop
declarations.comment: (2), cofiltered case: the predicate that M is essentially constant

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.IsEssentiallyConstantSystem
declarations.doc:
A directed system `(M_i, f_ii')`, i.e. a functor `M : I ⥤ 𝒞` on a directed set, is an
*essentially constant system* when the diagram `M` is essentially constant.
declarations.statement: def IsEssentiallyConstantSystem (M : I ⥤ C) : Prop
declarations.comment: directed system

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.IsEssentiallyConstantInverseSystem
declarations.doc:
A directed inverse system `(M_i, f_ii')`, i.e. a functor `M : Iᵒᵖ ⥤ 𝒞` on the opposite of a
directed set, is an *essentially constant inverse system* when the diagram `M` is essentially
constant as a pro-object, i.e. when the opposite diagram `Mᵒᵖ` is an essentially constant
diagram.
declarations.statement: def IsEssentiallyConstantInverseSystem (M : Iᵒᵖ ⥤ C) : Prop
declarations.comment: directed inverse system

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.EssentiallyConstantInd.isEssentiallyConstantWith_of_bijective_homComparison
declarations.doc:
If `homComparison M t W` is bijective for every `W`, then `M` is essentially constant as an
ind-object with value `t.pt`, with respect to the cocone `t`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isEssentiallyConstantWith_of_bijective_homComparison (M : I ⥤ C) [IsFiltered I]
    (t : Cocone M) (h : ∀ W : C, Function.Bijective (homComparison M t W)) :
    ∃ (i : I) (r : t.pt ⟶ M.obj i), IsEssentiallyConstantWith M t i r

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.EssentiallyConstantInd.isEssentiallyConstantWith_of_bijective_homComparisonInv
declarations.doc:
If `homComparisonInv M r W` is bijective for every `W`, for a morphism `r : X ⟶ M i`, then
`X` is the apex of a cocone with respect to which `M` is essentially constant, so `X` is a value of
the essentially constant system.
declarations.statement:
theorem isEssentiallyConstantWith_of_bijective_homComparisonInv (M : I ⥤ C) [IsFiltered I]
    (X : C) (i : I) (r : X ⟶ M.obj i)
    (h : ∀ W : C, Function.Bijective (homComparisonInv M r W)) :
    ∃ (t : Cocone M), t.pt = X ∧
      ∃ (i' : I) (r' : t.pt ⟶ M.obj i'), IsEssentiallyConstantWith M t i' r'

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.EssentiallyConstantInd.essentiallyConstantInd_tfae
declarations.doc:
For a filtered diagram `M : I ⥤ C` the four conditions (1) `M` is an essentially constant
ind-object, (2) some cocone has bijective `homComparison` at every `W`, (3) some colimit cocone
does, and (4) some `r : X ⟶ M i` has bijective `homComparisonInv` at every `W`, are equivalent.
declarations.statement:
theorem essentiallyConstantInd_tfae (M : I ⥤ C) [IsFiltered I] :
    [ IsEssentiallyConstantInd M,
      HasCoconeWithBijectiveHomComparison M,
      HasColimitWithBijectiveHomComparison M,
      HasCoreflectionWithBijectiveHomComparison M ].TFAE

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.EssentiallyConstantPro.isEssentiallyConstantWith_of_bijective_homComparison
declarations.doc:
If the comparison map `colim_i Mor(M_i, W) → Mor(c.pt, W)` is bijective for every `W` at the
cone `c`, then `M` is essentially constant as a pro-object with value `c.pt`, with respect to the
cone `c`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isEssentiallyConstantWith_of_bijective_homComparison (M : I ⥤ C) [IsCofiltered I]
    (c : Cone M)
    (h : ∀ W : Cᵒᵖ, Function.Bijective
      (EssentiallyConstantInd.homComparison M.op c.op W)) :
    ∃ (i : I) (s : M.obj i ⟶ c.pt), IsEssentiallyConstantWith M c i s

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.EssentiallyConstantPro.isEssentiallyConstantWith_of_bijective_homComparisonInv
declarations.doc:
If the reverse comparison map `Mor(X, W) → colim_j Mor(M_j, W)` is bijective for every `W`
at `(X, i, s)`, then `X` is the apex of a cone with respect to which `M` is essentially constant,
so `X` is a value of the essentially constant system.
declarations.statement:
theorem isEssentiallyConstantWith_of_bijective_homComparisonInv (M : I ⥤ C) [IsCofiltered I]
    (X : C) (i : I) (s : M.obj i ⟶ X)
    (h : ∀ W : Cᵒᵖ, Function.Bijective
      (EssentiallyConstantInd.homComparisonInv M.op s.op W)) :
    ∃ c : Cone M, c.pt = X ∧
      ∃ (i' : I) (s' : M.obj i' ⟶ c.pt), IsEssentiallyConstantWith M c i' s'

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.EssentiallyConstantPro.essentiallyConstantPro_tfae
declarations.doc:
For a cofiltered diagram `M : I ⥤ C` the four conditions (1) `M` is an essentially constant
pro-object, (2) some cone has a bijective Hom-colimit comparison at every `W`, (3) some limit cone
does, and (4) some `s : M i ⟶ X` has a bijective reverse comparison at every `W`, are
equivalent.
declarations.statement:
theorem essentiallyConstantPro_tfae [IsCofiltered I] (M : I ⥤ C) :
    [ IsEssentiallyConstantPro M,
      HasConeWithBijectiveHomColimit M,
      HasLimitWithBijectiveHomColimit M,
      HasReflectionWithBijectiveHomColimit M ].TFAE

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.MorphismProperty.isFiltered_under_and_nonempty_isColimit_underHomCoconeULift
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 05Q0**: let `W` be a left multiplicative system on `C`, let `L : C ⥤ D` be a
localization functor of `C` at `W`, and let `X`, `Y` be objects of `C`. Then the category `Y/S`
(Mathlib's `W.Under ⊤ Y`) of the morphisms `s : Y ⟶ Y'` of `W`, with morphisms the commutative
triangles `s ≫ a = t` for arbitrary `a`, is filtered, and the morphisms `L.obj X ⟶ L.obj Y` of
`W⁻¹C` are the filtered colimit `colim_{(s : Y ⟶ Y') ∈ Y/S} Mor_C(X, Y')` (formula 05Q1): the
cocone `underHomCoconeULift`, whose leg at `s` sends `f : X ⟶ Y'` to the left fraction `s⁻¹ f`,
is a colimit cocone. Both sides are lifted by `ULift` to a common universe, so no condition
relates the universe of the morphisms of `D` to that of the morphisms of `C`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isFiltered_under_and_nonempty_isColimit_underHomCoconeULift (X Y : C) :
    IsFiltered (W.Under ⊤ Y) ∧ Nonempty (IsColimit (W.underHomCoconeULift L X Y))
declarations.comment: Mathlib's W.Under ⊤ Y is the category Y/S, and HasLeftCalculusOfFractions is LMS1-LMS3; the filteredness of Y/S is isFiltered_under_of_hasLeftCalculusOfFractions and formula 05Q1 is isColimitUnderHomCoconeULift, for any localization L of C at W

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.MorphismProperty.Q_preservesFiniteColimits
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 05Q2.** For a left multiplicative system `W` on `C`, the localization functor
`Q : C ⥤ W⁻¹C` commutes with finite colimits. This does not assert that `W⁻¹C` has finite
colimits: only that `Q` carries a finite colimit cocone of `C` to a colimit cocone.
declarations.statement:
theorem Q_preservesFiniteColimits
    {C : Type*} [Category C] (W : MorphismProperty C) [W.HasLeftCalculusOfFractions] :
    Limits.PreservesFiniteColimits W.Q

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.MorphismProperty.exists_leftFraction_lift_of_commSq
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 05Q3**.
A commutative square in the left localisation `W⁻¹C` between images of
morphisms `f : X ⟶ Y` and `f' : X' ⟶ Y'` of `C` lifts to a commutative
diagram in `C` involving two morphisms in `W`.
declarations.statement:
lemma exists_leftFraction_lift_of_commSq
    {X Y X' Y' : C} (f : X ⟶ Y) (f' : X' ⟶ Y')
    (a : (LeftFraction.Localization.Q W).obj X ⟶ (LeftFraction.Localization.Q W).obj X')
    (b : (LeftFraction.Localization.Q W).obj Y ⟶ (LeftFraction.Localization.Q W).obj Y')
    (sq : (LeftFraction.Localization.Q W).map f ≫ b =
      a ≫ (LeftFraction.Localization.Q W).map f') :
    ∃ (X'' Y'' : C) (g : X ⟶ X'') (s : X' ⟶ X'') (hs : W s)
      (h : Y ⟶ Y'') (t : Y' ⟶ Y'') (ht : W t) (f'' : X'' ⟶ Y''),
      f ≫ h = g ≫ f'' ∧ s ≫ f'' = f' ≫ t ∧
      a = (LeftFraction.mk g s hs).map (LeftFraction.Localization.Q W)
            (Localization.inverts _ _) ∧
      b = (LeftFraction.mk h t ht).map (LeftFraction.Localization.Q W)
            (Localization.inverts _ _)

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.MorphismProperty.isCofiltered_over
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 05Q4**, first claim: for a right multiplicative system `W` on `C` and an
object `X` of `C`, the category `S/X = W.Over ⊤ X` of `W`-morphisms to `X` is cofiltered
in the sense of Stacks 04AZ, i.e. its identity diagram is a cofiltered diagram.
declarations.statement: theorem isCofiltered_over (X : C) : (𝟭 (W.Over ⊤ X)).IsCofiltered

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.MorphismProperty.isColimitOverHomCocone
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 05Q4**, second claim: for a right multiplicative system `W` on `C`, a
localization functor `L : C ⥤ D` of `C` at `W` and objects `X`, `Y` of `C`, the
morphisms `L.obj X ⟶ L.obj Y` of `W⁻¹C` are the colimit
`colim_{(s : X' ⟶ X) ∈ (S/X)ᵒᵖ} Mor_C(X', Y)`, in the sense that the tautological cocone
`overHomCocone`, whose leg at `s` sends `f` to the right fraction `f s⁻¹`, is a colimit
cocone. The index category `(S/X)ᵒᵖ` is filtered by `isCofiltered_over`, so this
exhibits the morphisms of `W⁻¹C` as a filtered colimit of morphisms of `C`.
declarations.statement: noncomputable def isColimitOverHomCocone (X Y : C) : IsColimit (W.overHomCocone L X Y)

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.MorphismProperty.Q_preservesFiniteLimits
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 05Q6.** For a right multiplicative system `W` on `C`, the localization functor
`Q : C ⥤ W⁻¹C` commutes with finite limits. This does not assert that `W⁻¹C` has finite
limits: only that `Q` carries a finite limit cone of `C` to a limit cone.
declarations.statement:
theorem Q_preservesFiniteLimits
    {C : Type*} [Category C] (W : MorphismProperty C)
    [W.HasRightCalculusOfFractions] :
    PreservesFiniteLimits W.Q

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.MorphismProperty.exists_rightFraction_lift_of_commSq
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 05Q7.**
Let `W : MorphismProperty C` admit a right calculus of fractions and let
`L : C ⥤ D` be a localization of `C` at `W`. Given morphisms `f : X ⟶ Y` and
`f' : X' ⟶ Y'` in `C`, and morphisms `a : L.obj X ⟶ L.obj X'`,
`b : L.obj Y ⟶ L.obj Y'` in `D` such that `a ≫ L.map f' = L.map f ≫ b`,
there exist objects `X''`, `Y''` in `C`, a morphism `f'' : X'' ⟶ Y''`,
morphisms `s : X'' ⟶ X`, `t : Y'' ⟶ Y` with `W s`, `W t`, and morphisms
`g : X'' ⟶ X'`, `h : Y'' ⟶ Y'` such that
`s ≫ f = f'' ≫ t`, `g ≫ f' = f'' ≫ h`,
`L.map s ≫ a = L.map g`, and `L.map t ≫ b = L.map h`.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_rightFraction_lift_of_commSq
    [L.IsLocalization W] [HasRightCalculusOfFractions W]
    {X Y X' Y' : C} (f : X ⟶ Y) (f' : X' ⟶ Y')
    (a : L.obj X ⟶ L.obj X') (b : L.obj Y ⟶ L.obj Y')
    (sq : a ≫ L.map f' = L.map f ≫ b) :
    ∃ (X'' Y'' : C) (f'' : X'' ⟶ Y'')
      (s : X'' ⟶ X) (_ : W s) (t : Y'' ⟶ Y) (_ : W t)
      (g : X'' ⟶ X') (h : Y'' ⟶ Y'),
        s ≫ f = f'' ≫ t ∧ g ≫ f' = f'' ≫ h ∧
        L.map s ≫ a = L.map g ∧
        L.map t ≫ b = L.map h

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.MorphismProperty.IsSaturated
declarations.doc:
`W` is a *saturated multiplicative system* when it is a multiplicative system — MS1 together
with the two Ore conditions MS2 and the two cancellation conditions MS3, i.e. both a left and a
right calculus of fractions — and satisfies MS4: for composable `f : X ⟶ Y`, `g : Y ⟶ Z`,
`h : Z ⟶ T`, if `W (f ≫ g)` and `W (g ≫ h)` then `W g`.
declarations.statement: structure IsSaturated (W : MorphismProperty C) : Prop

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.MorphismProperty.invertedClosure_eq_satClosure
declarations.doc:
`Ŝ = S'`: a morphism becomes invertible in the localization exactly
when it has a `W`-partner on each side.
declarations.statement: theorem invertedClosure_eq_satClosure : W.invertedClosure = W.satClosure

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.MorphismProperty.le_invertedClosure
declarations.doc: `W ≤ Ŝ`: every morphism of `W` is inverted by `Q`.
declarations.statement: theorem le_invertedClosure : W ≤ W.invertedClosure

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.MorphismProperty.isSaturated_invertedClosure
declarations.doc:
`Ŝ` is itself a saturated multiplicative system: it has a left and a right calculus of
fractions and satisfies MS4.
declarations.statement: theorem isSaturated_invertedClosure : IsSaturated W.invertedClosure

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.MorphismProperty.invertedClosure_le_of_isSaturated
declarations.doc:
`Ŝ` is the *smallest* saturated multiplicative system containing `W`:
it is contained in every saturated multiplicative system containing `W`.
declarations.statement:
theorem invertedClosure_le_of_isSaturated (W' : MorphismProperty C)
    (hW' : IsSaturated W') (hWW' : W ≤ W') : W.invertedClosure ≤ W'

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.MorphismProperty.IsSaturated.invertedClosure_eq
declarations.doc: If `W` is already saturated then `Ŝ = W`.
declarations.statement:
theorem IsSaturated.invertedClosure_eq (hW : IsSaturated W) :
    W.invertedClosure = W

registrations.comment: part 1
