declarations.name: CategoryTheory.Localization.preadditive_eq_of_hasLeftCalculusOfFractions
declarations.doc:
If `L : C ⥤ D` is a localization functor for a morphism property `W` with a left calculus
of fractions on a preadditive category `C`, then there is at most one preadditive structure
on `D` making `L` additive.
declarations.statement:
lemma preadditive_eq_of_hasLeftCalculusOfFractions [W.HasLeftCalculusOfFractions]
    (P₁ P₂ : Preadditive D) (h₁ : @Functor.Additive _ _ _ _ _ P₁ L)
    (h₂ : @Functor.Additive _ _ _ _ _ P₂ L) : P₁ = P₂
declarations.comment: Uniqueness, for a left multiplicative system.

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.Localization.functor_additive'
declarations.doc:
The localization functor `L` is additive for the preadditive structure
`Localization.preadditive'` given by a right calculus of fractions.
declarations.statement:
lemma functor_additive' [W.HasRightCalculusOfFractions] :
    letI := preadditive' L W
    L.Additive
declarations.comment: Existence, for a right multiplicative system.

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.Localization.preadditive_eq_of_hasRightCalculusOfFractions
declarations.doc:
If `L : C ⥤ D` is a localization functor for a morphism property `W` with a right calculus
of fractions on a preadditive category `C`, then there is at most one preadditive structure
on `D` making `L` additive.
declarations.statement:
lemma preadditive_eq_of_hasRightCalculusOfFractions [W.HasRightCalculusOfFractions]
    (P₁ P₂ : Preadditive D) (h₁ : @Functor.Additive _ _ _ _ _ P₁ L)
    (h₂ : @Functor.Additive _ _ _ _ _ P₂ L) : P₁ = P₂
declarations.comment: Uniqueness, for a right multiplicative system.

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.Localization.existsUnique_preadditive_functor_additive
declarations.doc:
Let `C` be a preadditive category and `W` a morphism property on `C` with a left or a right
calculus of fractions (i.e. a left or right multiplicative system), and let `L : C ⥤ D` be a
localization functor for `W` (e.g. `W.Q : C ⥤ W.Localization`). Then there is a unique
preadditive structure on `D` such that `L` is additive.
declarations.statement:
theorem existsUnique_preadditive_functor_additive
    (hW : W.HasLeftCalculusOfFractions ∨ W.HasRightCalculusOfFractions) :
    ∃! P : Preadditive D, @Functor.Additive _ _ _ _ _ P L

declarations.name: Stacks.Localization.exists_preadditive_additive_hasFiniteBiproducts
declarations.doc:
Let `C` be an additive category (a preadditive category with finite biproducts) and let `W`
be a left or right multiplicative system (a morphism property with a left or a right calculus of
fractions). Then the target `D` of any localization functor `L : C ⥤ D` for `W` (for instance
`W.Q : C ⥤ W.Localization`) is an additive category and `L` is additive: there is a preadditive
structure on `D` for which `L` is additive and `D` has a zero object and finite biproducts.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_preadditive_additive_hasFiniteBiproducts [Preadditive C] [HasFiniteBiproducts C]
    (hW : W.HasLeftCalculusOfFractions ∨ W.HasRightCalculusOfFractions) :
    ∃ P : Preadditive D, letI := P; L.Additive ∧ HasZeroObject D ∧ HasFiniteBiproducts D

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.Localization.isZero_obj_iff
declarations.doc:
An object `X` is sent to zero by a zero-morphism-preserving localization functor for a
morphism property `W` with left calculus of fractions if and only if the zero morphism
`0 : X ⟶ Y` belongs to `W` for some object `Y`.
declarations.statement:
lemma isZero_obj_iff [W.HasLeftCalculusOfFractions] (X : C) :
    IsZero (L.obj X) ↔ ∃ (Y : C), W (0 : X ⟶ Y)

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.Localization.isZero_obj_iff'
declarations.doc:
An object `X` is sent to zero by a zero-morphism-preserving localization functor for a
morphism property `W` with right calculus of fractions if and only if the zero morphism
`0 : Z ⟶ X` belongs to `W` for some object `Z`.
declarations.statement:
lemma isZero_obj_iff' [W.HasRightCalculusOfFractions] (X : C) :
    IsZero (L.obj X) ↔ ∃ (Z : C), W (0 : Z ⟶ X)

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.Localization.preservesCokernel
declarations.doc:
A zero-morphism-preserving localization functor for a morphism property with left calculus
of fractions preserves cokernels.
declarations.statement:
theorem preservesCokernel {X Y : C} (f : X ⟶ Y) [HasCokernel f] :
    PreservesColimit (parallelPair f 0) L
declarations.comment: part (1) for a morphism of `C`

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.Localization.hasCokernels
declarations.doc:
If `C` has cokernels and `L : C ⥤ D` is a zero-morphism-preserving localization functor
for a morphism property with left calculus of fractions, then `D` has cokernels.
declarations.statement: theorem hasCokernels [HasCokernels C] : HasCokernels D
declarations.comment: part (1)

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.Localization.preservesKernel
declarations.doc:
A zero-morphism-preserving localization functor for a morphism property with right
calculus of fractions preserves kernels.
declarations.statement:
lemma preservesKernel {X Y : C} (f : X ⟶ Y) [HasKernel f] :
    PreservesLimit (parallelPair f 0) L
declarations.comment: part (2) for a morphism of `C`

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.Localization.hasKernels
declarations.doc:
If `C` has kernels and `L : C ⥤ D` is a zero-morphism-preserving localization functor for
a morphism property with right calculus of fractions, then `D` has kernels.
declarations.statement: theorem hasKernels [HasKernels C] : HasKernels D
declarations.comment: part (2)

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.Localization.abelian
declarations.doc:
The localization of an abelian category at a morphism property with left and right
calculi of fractions is abelian, provided it has been endowed with a preadditive structure
making the localization functor additive (see
`Mathlib/CategoryTheory/Localization/CalculusOfFractions/Preadditive.lean`).
declarations.statement: def abelian : Abelian D
declarations.comment: part (3)

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.Localization.preservesFiniteLimits
declarations.doc:
A localization functor between abelian categories for a morphism property with right
calculus of fractions preserves finite limits. The abelian structure on the localized
category can be obtained from `CategoryTheory.Localization.abelian`.
declarations.statement: theorem preservesFiniteLimits : PreservesFiniteLimits L
declarations.comment: part (3)

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.Localization.preservesFiniteColimits
declarations.doc:
A localization functor between abelian categories for a morphism property with left
calculus of fractions preserves finite colimits. The abelian structure on the localized
category can be obtained from `CategoryTheory.Localization.abelian`.
declarations.statement: lemma preservesFiniteColimits : PreservesFiniteColimits L
declarations.comment: part (3)

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.FilteredObject.exact_map_eval_of_exact_map_gr
declarations.doc:
Stacks 05QH (2): if `gr(A) → gr(B) → gr(C)` is exact then `F^pA → F^pB → F^pC` is exact for
every `p`; needs only a zero step of `B`.
declarations.statement:
theorem exact_map_eval_of_exact_map_gr (hS : ∀ p, (S.map (gr p)).Exact)
    [HasBotStep S.X₂.filtration] (p : ℤ) : (S.map (eval (op p))).Exact
declarations.comment: (2); needs only a zero step of `B`

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.FilteredObject.exact_map_quot_of_exact_map_gr
declarations.doc:
Stacks 05QH (3): if `gr(A) → gr(B) → gr(C)` is exact then `A/F^pA → B/F^pB → C/F^pC` is
exact for every `p`; needs only a top step of `B`.
declarations.statement:
theorem exact_map_quot_of_exact_map_gr (hS : ∀ p, (S.map (gr p)).Exact)
    [HasTopStep S.X₂.filtration] (p : ℤ) : (S.map (quot (op p))).Exact
declarations.comment: (3); needs only a top step of `B`

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.FilteredObject.exact_map_forget_of_exact_map_gr
declarations.doc:
Stacks 05QH (5): if `gr(A) → gr(B) → gr(C)` is exact then `A → B → C` is exact in `𝒜`; needs
only a finite filtration on `B`.
declarations.statement:
theorem exact_map_forget_of_exact_map_gr (hS : ∀ p, (S.map (gr p)).Exact)
    [HasTopStep S.X₂.filtration] [HasBotStep S.X₂.filtration] : (S.map forget).Exact
declarations.comment: (5); needs only a finite filtration on `B`

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.FilteredObject.isStrict_f_of_exact_map_gr
declarations.doc:
Stacks 05QH (4) for `A → B`: if `gr(A) → gr(B) → gr(C)` is exact then `A → B` is strict; needs
only a zero step of `B`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isStrict_f_of_exact_map_gr (hS : ∀ p, (S.map (gr p)).Exact)
    [HasBotStep S.X₂.filtration] : IsStrict S.f
declarations.comment: (4) for `A → B`; needs only a zero step of `B`

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.FilteredObject.isStrict_g_of_exact_map_gr
declarations.doc:
Stacks 05QH (4) for `B → C`: if `gr(A) → gr(B) → gr(C)` is exact then `B → C` is strict; needs
only a top step of `B`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isStrict_g_of_exact_map_gr (hS : ∀ p, (S.map (gr p)).Exact)
    [HasTopStep S.X₂.filtration] : IsStrict S.g
declarations.comment: (4) for `B → C`; needs only a top step of `B`

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.FilteredObject.exact_of_exact_map_grGraded
declarations.doc:
Stacks 05QH: let `A → B → C` be a complex of filtered objects of an abelian category with
`gr(A) → gr(B) → gr(C)` exact and `B` finitely filtered (Stacks assumes `A`, `B`, `C` finite).
Then (1) `gr^p(A) → gr^p(B) → gr^p(C)` is exact for every `p`, (2) `F^pA → F^pB → F^pC` is
exact for every `p`, (3) `A/F^pA → B/F^pB → C/F^pC` is exact for every `p`, (4) `A → B` and
`B → C` are strict, and (5) `A → B → C` is exact in `𝒜`.
declarations.statement:
theorem exact_of_exact_map_grGraded [IsFinite S.X₂.filtration] (hS : (S.map grGraded).Exact) :
    (∀ p, (S.map (gr p)).Exact) ∧ (∀ p, (S.map (eval (op p))).Exact) ∧
      (∀ p, (S.map (quot (op p))).Exact) ∧ (IsStrict S.f ∧ IsStrict S.g) ∧
      (S.map forget).Exact
declarations.comment: needs only a finite filtration on `B`; `A` and `C` are arbitrary

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.FilteredObject.exact_map_grGraded_iff
declarations.doc: Exactness in `Gr(𝒜)` of `gr` applied to a short complex is exactness of every `gr^p`.
declarations.statement:
lemma exact_map_grGraded_iff (S : ShortComplex (FilteredObject C ℤᵒᵖ)) :
    (S.map grGraded).Exact ↔ ∀ p, (S.map (gr p)).Exact
declarations.comment: (1): exactness of `gr(A) → gr(B) → gr(C)` is exactness of every `gr^p`

registrations.name: CategoryTheory.Pretriangulated.rot_of_distTriang
registrations.comment: pieces on the right: rotation Y → Z → X[1] → Y[1], last map -f[1]

registrations.name: CategoryTheory.Pretriangulated.inv_rot_of_distTriang
registrations.comment: pieces on the left: inverse rotation Z[-1] → X → Y → Z, first map -h[-1]

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.Pretriangulated.PretriangulatedSubcategory
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 05QM.** A *pre-triangulated subcategory* of the pre-triangulated category
`(D, [ ], T)`: a pair `(D', T')` where

1. `D'` is an additive (not necessarily full) subcategory of `D`
   (`toAdditiveSubcategory`), preserved under `[1]` (`shift_obj`, `shift_hom`), such that
   the induced functor `[1] : D' → D'` is an auto-equivalence (`isEquivalence_shift`);
2. `T' ⊆ T` (`triangles`, `triangles_subset`) is a set of distinguished triangles of `D` all
   of whose objects and morphisms lie in `D'` (`isTriangle_of_mem`);
3. `(D', [ ], T')` is a pre-triangulated category, i.e. satisfies TR1 (`isomorphic_mem`,
   `contractible_mem`, `exists_mem`), TR2 (`rotate_mem_iff`) and TR3 (`complete`), stated
   internally to `D'`: for triangles of `D'`, isomorphisms of triangles of `D'`, zero
   objects of `D'`, and morphisms of `D'`.
declarations.statement: structure PretriangulatedSubcategory extends AdditiveSubcategory D
declarations.comment:
Pre-triangulated subcategory; the subcategory `D'` is a possibly non-full
additive subcategory, and TR1-TR3 for `(D', [ ], T')` are stated internally to `D'`.

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.Pretriangulated.TriangulatedSubcategory
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 05QM.** A *triangulated subcategory* of the triangulated category
`(D, [ ], T)`: a pre-triangulated subcategory `(D', T')` such that `(D', [ ], T')` is
moreover a triangulated category, i.e. satisfies TR4 internally to `D'` (`octahedron`):
given triangles `(X, Y, Q₁, f, p₁, d₁)`, `(X, Z, Q₂, g ∘ f, p₂, d₂)` and
`(Y, Z, Q₃, g, p₃, d₃)` of `T'`, there are morphisms `a : Q₁ ⟶ Q₂` and `b : Q₂ ⟶ Q₃` of `D'`
such that `(Q₁, Q₂, Q₃, a, b, p₁[1] ∘ d₃)` lies in `T'`, `(id_X, g, a)` is a morphism of
triangles from the first to the second triangle, and `(f, id_Z, b)` is a morphism of
triangles from the second to the third.
declarations.statement: structure TriangulatedSubcategory [IsTriangulated D] extends PretriangulatedSubcategory D
declarations.comment:
Triangulated subcategory; TR4 for `(D', [ ], T')` is stated internally to
`D'`.

declarations.name: comp_middle_zero_of_endomorphisms
declarations.doc:
If `(0, b, 0)` and `(0, b', 0)` are endomorphisms of a distinguished triangle
`T = (X, Y, Z, f, g, h)`, then the composite of their middle components vanishes,
i.e. `b ∘ b' = 0` (written `ψ.hom₂ ≫ φ.hom₂ = 0` in Lean's diagrammatic order
with `b = φ.hom₂`, `b' = ψ.hom₂`).
declarations.statement:
theorem comp_middle_zero_of_endomorphisms (T : Triangle C)
    (hT : T ∈ distinguishedTriangles)
    (φ ψ : TriangleMorphism T T)
    (hφ₁ : φ.hom₁ = 0)
    (hψ₃ : ψ.hom₃ = 0) :
    ψ.hom₂ ≫ φ.hom₂ = 0

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.Pretriangulated.complete_distinguished_triangle_morphism₂_idempotent
declarations.doc:
Let `T = (X, Y, Z, f, g, h)` be a distinguished triangle in
a pre-triangulated category, and let `a : X ⟶ X`, `c : Z ⟶ Z` be idempotents
such that `h ≫ a⟦1⟧' = c ≫ h`. Then `(a, c)` extends to an *idempotent*
endomorphism `φ : T ⟶ T` of the triangle, i.e. there is `b : Y ⟶ Y` with
`b ≫ b = b` making `(a, b, c)` an endomorphism of `T`.
declarations.statement:
theorem complete_distinguished_triangle_morphism₂_idempotent (T : Triangle C)
    (hT : T ∈ distTriang C) (a : T.obj₁ ⟶ T.obj₁) (c : T.obj₃ ⟶ T.obj₃)
    (comm : T.mor₃ ≫ a⟦(1 : ℤ)⟧' = c ≫ T.mor₃) (ha : a ≫ a = a) (hc : c ≫ c = c) :
    ∃ φ : T ⟶ T, φ ≫ φ = φ ∧ φ.hom₁ = a ∧ φ.hom₃ = c

declarations.name: productTriangle_distinguished_iff
declarations.doc:
The direct sum of two triangles is distinguished if and only if both summand triangles are
distinguished. Here `T : WalkingPair → Triangle C` packages the pair `(T₁, T₂)`, and
`productTriangle T` is the direct-sum triangle `T₁ ⊕ T₂`.
declarations.statement:
theorem productTriangle_distinguished_iff
    {C : Type*} [Category C] [Preadditive C] [HasZeroObject C] [HasShift C ℤ]
    [∀ n : ℤ, (CategoryTheory.shiftFunctor C n).Additive] [CategoryTheory.Pretriangulated C]
    [HasBinaryBiproducts C] (T : WalkingPair → Triangle C) :
    (productTriangle T ∈ distTriang C) ↔
      (∀ p : WalkingPair, T p ∈ distTriang C)

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.Pretriangulated.isIso_biprod_desc_of_distTriang
declarations.doc:
Let `T = (X, Y, Z, f, g, h)` be a distinguished triangle in a
pre-triangulated category. For any right inverse `s : Z ⟶ Y` of `g`, the map
`f ⊕ s : X ⊕ Z ⟶ Y` is an isomorphism.
declarations.statement:
theorem isIso_biprod_desc_of_distTriang (T : Triangle C) (hT : T ∈ distTriang C)
    (s : T.obj₃ ⟶ T.obj₂) (hs : s ≫ T.mor₂ = 𝟙 T.obj₃) :
    IsIso (biprod.desc T.mor₁ s)
declarations.comment:
(2): for any right inverse `s` of `g`, the map `f ⊕ s : X ⊕ Z ⟶ Y` is an
  isomorphism.

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.Pretriangulated.exists_section_mor₂_of_mor₃_eq_zero
declarations.doc:
Let `T = (X, Y, Z, f, g, h)` be a distinguished triangle in a pre-triangulated category.
If `h = 0`, then `g` has a right inverse `s : Z ⟶ Y`.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_section_mor₂_of_mor₃_eq_zero (T : Triangle C) (hT : T ∈ distTriang C)
    (h : T.mor₃ = 0) : ∃ s : T.obj₃ ⟶ T.obj₂, s ≫ T.mor₂ = 𝟙 T.obj₃
declarations.comment: (1): if `h = 0`, then `g` has a right inverse `s : Z ⟶ Y`.

registrations.name: CategoryTheory.Pretriangulated.binaryBiproductTriangle_distinguished
registrations.comment:
(3): for any objects `X'`, `Z'` the triangle
  `(X', X' ⊕ Z', Z', (1, 0), (0, 1), 0)` is distinguished.

declarations.name: hasKernel_iff_hasCokernel_iff_split
declarations.doc:
In a pre-triangulated category `C`, for a
morphism `f : X ⟶ Y` the following are equivalent:

1. `f` has a kernel;
2. `f` has a cokernel;
3. there are objects `K, Z, Q` with `f` isomorphic, in the arrow category, to the
   composite of the second projection `K ⊞ Z ⟶ Z` with the first coprojection
   `Z ⟶ Z ⊞ Q`, namely `biprod.snd ≫ biprod.inl`.
declarations.statement:
theorem hasKernel_iff_hasCokernel_iff_split (C : Type*) [Category C] [HasZeroObject C]
    [Preadditive C] [HasShift C ℤ] [∀ n : ℤ, (shiftFunctor C n).Additive] [Pretriangulated C]
    {X Y : C} (f : X ⟶ Y) :
    [HasKernel f,
     HasCokernel f,
     ∃ (K Z Q : C),
       Nonempty (Arrow.mk f ≅ Arrow.mk (biprod.snd ≫ biprod.inl : K ⊞ Z ⟶ Z ⊞ Q))].TFAE

declarations.name: isIdempotentComplete_of_hasCountableProducts
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 05QV(1)**: a preadditive category in which every object has a countable power, and in
which every split epimorphism has a kernel, is idempotent complete. A kernel of an idempotent
`p : Z ⟶ Z` is read off a kernel of its telescope `idempotentTelescope p`, an endomorphism of the
single countable power `∏ₙ Z`; that is why no product beyond those powers is assumed.
declarations.statement:
lemma isIdempotentComplete_of_hasCountableProducts [∀ Z : C, HasProduct fun _ : ℕ => Z]
    (h : ∀ {X Y : C} (f : X ⟶ Y) [IsSplitEpi f], HasKernel f) : IsIdempotentComplete C

declarations.name: isIdempotentComplete_of_hasCountableCoproducts
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 05QV(2)**: a preadditive category in which every object has a countable copower, and in
which every split monomorphism has a cokernel, is idempotent complete. This is 05QV(1) in `Cᵒᵖ`,
where the copowers of `C` are the countable powers.
declarations.statement:
lemma isIdempotentComplete_of_hasCountableCoproducts [∀ Z : C, HasCoproduct fun _ : ℕ => Z]
    (h : ∀ {X Y : C} (f : X ⟶ Y) [IsSplitMono f], HasCokernel f) : IsIdempotentComplete C

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.Pretriangulated.isIdempotentComplete_of_hasCountableProducts_or_coproducts
declarations.doc:
A pre-triangulated category in which every object has a countable power
`∏_{n : ℕ} Z` is Karoubian, i.e. idempotent complete; and so is one in which every object has a
countable copower `∐_{n : ℕ} Z`. In particular a pre-triangulated category with countable
products, or with countable coproducts, is Karoubian.
declarations.statement:
theorem isIdempotentComplete_of_hasCountableProducts_or_coproducts :
    (∀ [∀ Z : C, HasProduct fun _ : ℕ => Z], IsIdempotentComplete C) ∧
      (∀ [∀ Z : C, HasCoproduct fun _ : ℕ => Z], IsIdempotentComplete C)

declarations.name: Stacks.Triangulated.SubcategoryWithTriangles.statement1
declarations.doc:
**Statement 1** (Tag 05QX, equivalence of (1) and (2)). For an additive full
subcategory `D'` (described by `P`) of a pre-triangulated category `D`,
condition (1) (there *exists* a set `T'` making `(D', T')` a pre-triangulated
subcategory) is equivalent to condition (2).

PROOF SKETCH. `(1) ⇒ (2)`: destruct the existential witness `T'` and apply
`condition2_of_isPretri` (Sub-lemma C). `(2) ⇒ (1)`: provide
`restrictedTriangles P` as the witness, valid by `restrictedTriangles_isPretri`
(Sub-lemma D).
declarations.statement:
theorem statement1 (P : ObjectProperty C)
    (hP : IsAdditiveFullSubcategory P) :
    Condition1 P ↔ Condition2 P

declarations.name: Stacks.Triangulated.SubcategoryWithTriangles.statement2
declarations.doc:
**Statement 2** (Tag 05QX, characterization of `T'`). When the equivalent
conditions hold, the set `T'` is uniquely determined: *any* `T'` making
`(D', T')` a pre-triangulated subcategory coincides with the set of all
distinguished triangles of `D` whose three vertices lie in `D'`
(`restrictedTriangles P`), and this set indeed makes `(D', T')` a
pre-triangulated subcategory.

The two conjuncts express precisely this: (a) any valid `T'` equals
`restrictedTriangles P` (uniqueness, quantified over an arbitrary candidate
`T'`), and (b) `restrictedTriangles P` is itself valid (given condition (2)).

PROOF SKETCH. The first conjunct is `unique_restrictedTriangles` (Sub-lemma E),
applied to each candidate `T'`. The second conjunct is
`restrictedTriangles_isPretri` (Sub-lemma D).
declarations.statement:
theorem statement2 (P : ObjectProperty C)
    (hP : IsAdditiveFullSubcategory P) :
    (∀ T' : Set (Triangle C),
        IsPretriangulatedSubcategoryWithTriangles P T' →
          T' = restrictedTriangles P) ∧
      (Condition2 P →
        IsPretriangulatedSubcategoryWithTriangles P (restrictedTriangles P))

declarations.name: Stacks.Triangulated.SubcategoryWithTriangles.statement3
declarations.doc:
**Statement 3** (Tag 05QX, the triangulated case). If `D` is moreover a
triangulated category (it satisfies the octahedral condition TR4), then
conditions (1) and (2) are further equivalent to:
`(D', restrictedTriangles P)` is a *triangulated* subcategory of `D`, i.e. it is
a pre-triangulated subcategory whose induced pre-triangulated structure on `D'`
again satisfies TR4 (the octahedral axiom internal to `D'`, with the full
morphism-of-triangles compatibility conditions).

PROOF SKETCH. First conjunct `Condition1 P ↔ Condition2 P`: this is exactly
`statement1 P hP`. Second conjunct `Condition2 P ↔
IsTriangulatedSubcategoryWithTriangles P (restrictedTriangles P)`:
* `(⇒)`: from `Condition2 P`, the pre-triangulated half is
  `restrictedTriangles_isPretri P hP h2` (Sub-lemma D), and the octahedral half
  is `internalTR4_restrictedTriangles P hP` (Sub-lemma F); package them into the
  `IsTriangulatedSubcategoryWithTriangles` structure (constructor from its
  `toIsPretriangulatedSubcategoryWithTriangles` field plus `internalTR4`).
* `(⇐)`: an `IsTriangulatedSubcategoryWithTriangles P (restrictedTriangles P)`
  contains (via `.toIsPretriangulatedSubcategoryWithTriangles`) a witness for
  `Condition1 P`; convert to `Condition2 P` through `condition2_of_isPretri`
  (Sub-lemma C), or equivalently the forward direction of `statement1`.
declarations.statement:
theorem statement3 (P : ObjectProperty C)
    (hP : IsAdditiveFullSubcategory P) [IsTriangulated C] :
    (Condition1 P ↔ Condition2 P) ∧
      (Condition2 P ↔
        IsTriangulatedSubcategoryWithTriangles P (restrictedTriangles P))

declarations.name: main_statement_comp_triangulated_homological
declarations.doc:
**Statement 1** (Stacks 13.4.20, first part). If `F : D' → D` is an exact
(triangulated) functor between pre-triangulated categories and `H : D → A` is a
homological functor to an abelian category, then the composition `F ⋙ H` is a
homological functor.
declarations.statement:
theorem main_statement_comp_triangulated_homological
    {D' : Type u₁} {D : Type u₂} {A : Type u₃}
    [Category.{v₁} D'] [Category.{v₂} D] [Category.{v₃} A]
    [HasShift D' ℤ] [HasShift D ℤ]
    [HasZeroObject D'] [HasZeroObject D]
    [Preadditive D'] [Preadditive D]
    [∀ (n : ℤ), (shiftFunctor D' n).Additive] [∀ (n : ℤ), (shiftFunctor D n).Additive]
    [Pretriangulated D'] [Pretriangulated D] [Abelian A]
    (F : D' ⥤ D) [F.CommShift ℤ] [F.IsTriangulated]
    (H : D ⥤ A) [H.IsHomological] :
    (F ⋙ H).IsHomological

declarations.name: main_statement_comp_homological_exact
declarations.doc:
**Statement 2** (Stacks 13.4.20, second part). If `H : D → A` is a
homological functor and `G : A → A'` is an exact functor of abelian categories
(additive and preserving finite limits and colimits), then the composition
`H ⋙ G` is a homological functor.
declarations.statement:
theorem main_statement_comp_homological_exact
    {D : Type u₁} {A : Type u₂} {A' : Type u₃}
    [Category.{v₁} D] [Category.{v₂} A] [Category.{v₃} A']
    [HasShift D ℤ] [HasZeroObject D] [Preadditive D]
    [∀ (n : ℤ), (shiftFunctor D n).Additive]
    [Pretriangulated D] [Abelian A] [Abelian A']
    (H : D ⥤ A) [H.IsHomological]
    (G : A ⥤ A') [G.Additive] [PreservesFiniteLimits G] [PreservesFiniteColimits G] :
    (H ⋙ G).IsHomological

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.Triangulated.exists_nine_diagram
declarations.doc:
Let `C` be a triangulated category. Given a commutative square
`u₁ ≫ b₁ = a₁ ≫ v₁` and distinguished triangles `(u₁, u₂, u₃)`, `(v₁, v₂, v₃)` on its two
horizontal morphisms and `(a₁, a₂, a₃)`, `(b₁, b₂, b₃)` on its two vertical ones, there are an
object `Z''`, a third row `(w₁, w₂, w₃)` and a third column `(c₁, c₂, c₃)`, both distinguished
triangles, such that the resulting `4 × 4` diagram — whose fourth row and fourth column are the
first row and the first column shifted by `1` — has all its squares commutative, except the
lower right one, which anticommutes.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_nine_diagram {X Y Z X' Y' Z' X'' Y'' : C}
    {u₁ : X ⟶ Y} {u₂ : Y ⟶ Z} {u₃ : Z ⟶ X⟦(1 : ℤ)⟧}
    (hu : Triangle.mk u₁ u₂ u₃ ∈ distTriang C)
    {v₁ : X' ⟶ Y'} {v₂ : Y' ⟶ Z'} {v₃ : Z' ⟶ X'⟦(1 : ℤ)⟧}
    (hv : Triangle.mk v₁ v₂ v₃ ∈ distTriang C)
    {a₁ : X ⟶ X'} {a₂ : X' ⟶ X''} {a₃ : X'' ⟶ X⟦(1 : ℤ)⟧}
    (ha : Triangle.mk a₁ a₂ a₃ ∈ distTriang C)
    {b₁ : Y ⟶ Y'} {b₂ : Y' ⟶ Y''} {b₃ : Y'' ⟶ Y⟦(1 : ℤ)⟧}
    (hb : Triangle.mk b₁ b₂ b₃ ∈ distTriang C)
    (comm : u₁ ≫ b₁ = a₁ ≫ v₁) :
    ∃ (Z'' : C) (w₁ : X'' ⟶ Y'') (w₂ : Y'' ⟶ Z'') (w₃ : Z'' ⟶ X''⟦(1 : ℤ)⟧)
      (c₁ : Z ⟶ Z') (c₂ : Z' ⟶ Z'') (c₃ : Z'' ⟶ Z⟦(1 : ℤ)⟧),
      Triangle.mk w₁ w₂ w₃ ∈ distTriang C ∧ Triangle.mk c₁ c₂ c₃ ∈ distTriang C ∧
      u₂ ≫ c₁ = b₁ ≫ v₂ ∧ u₃ ≫ a₁⟦(1 : ℤ)⟧' = c₁ ≫ v₃ ∧
      v₁ ≫ b₂ = a₂ ≫ w₁ ∧ v₂ ≫ c₂ = b₂ ≫ w₂ ∧ v₃ ≫ a₂⟦(1 : ℤ)⟧' = c₂ ≫ w₃ ∧
      w₁ ≫ b₃ = a₃ ≫ u₁⟦(1 : ℤ)⟧' ∧ w₂ ≫ c₃ = b₃ ≫ u₂⟦(1 : ℤ)⟧' ∧
      w₃ ≫ a₃⟦(1 : ℤ)⟧' = -(c₃ ≫ u₃⟦(1 : ℤ)⟧')

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.MorphismProperty.isCompatibleWithTriangulation_iff_shift_one_and_hasMS6
declarations.doc:
For a class `W` satisfying MS1, being compatible with the triangulated structure in the
sense of `MorphismProperty.IsCompatibleWithTriangulation` is equivalent to the two axioms as
Stacks states them: MS5 in the form `f ∈ W ⇔ f[1] ∈ W`, and MS6. The passage between the two
forms of MS5 is `isCompatibleWithShift_iff_of_hasMS6`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isCompatibleWithTriangulation_iff_shift_one_and_hasMS6
    {C : Type u} [Category.{v} C] [HasShift C ℤ] [Preadditive C]
    [Limits.HasZeroObject C] [∀ n : ℤ, (shiftFunctor C n).Additive]
    [Pretriangulated C] (W : MorphismProperty C) [W.IsMultiplicative] :
    W.IsCompatibleWithTriangulation ↔
      (∀ ⦃X Y : C⦄ (f : X ⟶ Y), W f ↔ W (f⟦(1 : ℤ)⟧')) ∧ W.HasMS6
declarations.comment: with MS5 in the form `f ∈ S ⇔ f[1] ∈ S`

registrations.name: CategoryTheory.MorphismProperty.IsCompatibleWithTriangulation
registrations.comment: a multiplicative system compatible with the triangulated structure

registrations.name: CategoryTheory.MorphismProperty.IsCompatibleWithTriangulation.toIsCompatibleWithShift
registrations.comment: MS5, as stability under every shift `[n]`, `n : ℤ`; for a class with MS1 and MS6 this is equivalent to Stacks' form `f ∈ S ⇔ f[1] ∈ S` by Remark 0H30, `MorphismProperty.isCompatibleWithShift_iff_of_hasMS6`

registrations.name: CategoryTheory.MorphismProperty.IsCompatibleWithTriangulation.compatible_with_triangulation
registrations.comment: MS6

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.MorphismProperty.isIso_mem_of_hasMS6
declarations.doc:
If `W` contains all identities and satisfies MS6, then `W` contains every isomorphism of
`C`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isIso_mem_of_hasMS6
    {C : Type u} [Category.{v} C] [HasShift C ℤ] [Preadditive C]
    [Limits.HasZeroObject C] [∀ n : ℤ, (shiftFunctor C n).Additive]
    [Pretriangulated C] (W : MorphismProperty C)
    [W.ContainsIdentities] [W.HasMS6]
    {X Y : C} (f : X ⟶ Y) [IsIso f] : W f

declarations.name: isCompatibleWithTriangulation_oreConditions
declarations.doc:
If `W` satisfies MS1 (`W.IsMultiplicative`), MS5 and MS6
(`W.IsCompatibleWithTriangulation`), then `W` satisfies MS2: both the left (LMS2) and the right
(RMS2) Ore conditions hold.
declarations.statement:
theorem isCompatibleWithTriangulation_oreConditions
    {C : Type u} [Category.{v} C] [HasShift C ℤ] [Preadditive C]
    [Limits.HasZeroObject C] [∀ n : ℤ, (shiftFunctor C n).Additive]
    [Pretriangulated C] (W : MorphismProperty C)
    [W.IsMultiplicative]
    [W.IsCompatibleWithTriangulation] :
    (∀ ⦃X Y : C⦄ (φ : W.RightFraction X Y),
        ∃ ψ : W.LeftFraction X Y, φ.f ≫ ψ.s = φ.s ≫ ψ.f)
    ∧
    (∀ ⦃X Y : C⦄ (φ : W.LeftFraction X Y),
        ∃ ψ : W.RightFraction X Y, ψ.s ≫ φ.f = ψ.f ≫ φ.s)

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.Functor.isSaturated_and_isCompatibleWithTriangulation_inverseImage_isomorphisms
declarations.doc:
Let `F : C ⥤ D` be an exact functor of pre-triangulated categories. The class
`W = (isomorphisms D).inverseImage F` of morphisms of `C` inverted by `F` is a saturated
multiplicative system (MS1, MS2, MS3 and the cancellation axiom MS4) compatible with the
triangulated structure on `C` (MS5, MS6).
declarations.statement:
theorem Functor.isSaturated_and_isCompatibleWithTriangulation_inverseImage_isomorphisms
    (F : C ⥤ D) [F.CommShift ℤ] [F.IsTriangulated] :
    ((isomorphisms D).inverseImage F).IsSaturated ∧
      ((isomorphisms D).inverseImage F).IsCompatibleWithTriangulation

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.Functor.isSaturated_and_isCompatibleWithTriangulation
declarations.doc:
Let `H : 𝒟 ⥤ 𝒜` be a homological functor from a pre-triangulated category to an abelian
category. Then
`S = {f ∈ Arrows(𝒟) ∣ Hⁱ(f) is an isomorphism for all i ∈ ℤ}`
is a saturated multiplicative system compatible with the triangulated
structure on `𝒟` (MS5 and MS6).
declarations.statement:
theorem CategoryTheory.Functor.isSaturated_and_isCompatibleWithTriangulation
    {D : Type u₁} [Category.{v₁} D] [HasZeroObject D] [HasShift D ℤ] [Preadditive D]
    [∀ n : ℤ, (shiftFunctor D n).Additive] [Pretriangulated D]
    {A : Type u₂} [Category.{v₂} A] [Abelian A] (H : D ⥤ A) [H.IsHomological]
    (S : MorphismProperty D)
    (hS : ∀ ⦃X Y : D⦄ (f : X ⟶ Y), S f ↔ ∀ i : ℤ, IsIso (H.map (f⟦i⟧'))) :
    S.IsSaturated ∧ S.IsCompatibleWithTriangulation

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.Triangulated.Localization.existsUnique_pretriangulated_and_isTriangulated
declarations.doc:
Let `C` be a pre-triangulated category, let `W` be a multiplicative system of morphisms of `C`
compatible with the triangulated structure, and let `L : C ⥤ D` be a localization functor for `W`,
where `D` is additive, has a shift with which `L` commutes, and `L` is additive. Then there is a
unique pre-triangulated structure on `D` making `L` exact, namely
`CategoryTheory.Triangulated.Localization.pretriangulated L W`, and it is triangulated whenever `C`
is.
declarations.statement:
theorem existsUnique_pretriangulated_and_isTriangulated :
    (letI := pretriangulated L W; L.IsTriangulated) ∧
      (∀ h : Pretriangulated D, (letI := h; L.IsTriangulated) → h = pretriangulated L W) ∧
        (letI := pretriangulated L W; IsTriangulated C → IsTriangulated D)

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.Functor.isTriangulated_of_localization
declarations.doc:
Let `C` be a pre-triangulated category, `W` a multiplicative system of morphisms of `C`
compatible with the triangulated structure, and `L : C ⥤ D` the (exact) localization functor. If
`F : C ⥤ E` is an exact functor to a pre-triangulated category and `F' : D ⥤ E` is its
factorization through `L`, then `F'`, for the commutation with the shift it inherits from that
factorization, is exact.
declarations.statement:
theorem isTriangulated_of_localization
    {E : Type u₃} [Category.{v₃} E] [HasZeroObject E] [HasShift E ℤ] [Preadditive E]
    [∀ n : ℤ, (shiftFunctor E n).Additive] [Pretriangulated E]
    (F : C ⥤ E) [F.CommShift ℤ] [F.IsTriangulated] (F' : D ⥤ E) [Lifting L W F F'] :
    letI := commShiftOfLocalization L W ℤ F F'
    F'.IsTriangulated

declarations.name: StacksLocalizationKernel.statementA
declarations.doc:
Let `S` be a multiplicative system compatible with the triangulated structure and `Q` a
localization functor for `S`. For an object `Z`, the conditions `Cond1` to `Cond4` are
equivalent.
declarations.statement:
theorem statementA
    (S : MorphismProperty 𝒟)
    {𝒟_S : Type*} [Category 𝒟_S] (Q : 𝒟 ⥤ 𝒟_S) [Q.IsLocalization S]
    (Z : 𝒟)
    (hL : S.HasLeftCalculusOfFractions)
    (hR : S.HasRightCalculusOfFractions) (hcompat : S.IsCompatibleWithTriangulation) :
    [Cond1 Q Z, Cond2 S Z, Cond3 S Z, Cond4 S Z].TFAE

declarations.name: StacksLocalizationKernel.statementB
declarations.doc:
Let `S` be a saturated multiplicative system compatible with the triangulated structure and
`Q` a localization functor for `S`. For an object `Z`, the conditions `Cond1` to `Cond7` are
equivalent.
declarations.statement:
theorem statementB
    (S : MorphismProperty 𝒟)
    {𝒟_S : Type*} [Category 𝒟_S] (Q : 𝒟 ⥤ 𝒟_S) [Q.IsLocalization S]
    (Z : 𝒟)
    (hL : S.HasLeftCalculusOfFractions)
    (hR : S.HasRightCalculusOfFractions) (hcompat : S.IsCompatibleWithTriangulation)
    (hsat : S.IsSaturatedMultiplicative) :
    [Cond1 Q Z, Cond2 S Z, Cond3 S Z, Cond4 S Z,
     Cond5 S Z, Cond6 S Z, Cond7 S Z].TFAE

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.MorphismProperty.IsSaturated.isFiltered_and_final_component
declarations.doc:
Let `W` be a saturated multiplicative system of a pre-triangulated category `C`, compatible
with the triangulated structure, and let `T = (X, Y, Z, f, g, h)` be a distinguished triangle of
`C`. Let `ℐ` be the category of `W`-morphisms of triangles out of `T`: the full subcategory of
`Under T` in `Triangle C` whose objects are the morphisms of triangles `(s, s', s'') : T ⟶ T'` with
`T'` distinguished and `s, s', s''` in `W`.

Then `ℐ` is filtered, and the three functors `ℐ ⥤ X/W`, `ℐ ⥤ Y/W`, `ℐ ⥤ Z/W` given by
`(s, s', s'') ↦ s`, `s'`, `s''` — the projections `Triangle.π₁`, `Triangle.π₂`, `Triangle.π₃` read
on morphisms under `T` — are cofinal.
declarations.statement:
theorem CategoryTheory.MorphismProperty.IsSaturated.isFiltered_and_final_component
    {W : MorphismProperty C} (hW : W.IsSaturated) [W.IsCompatibleWithTriangulation]
    {T : Triangle C} (hT : T ∈ distTriang C) (ℐ : ObjectProperty (Under T))
    (hℐ : ∀ A : Under T, ℐ A ↔
      A.right ∈ distTriang C ∧ W A.hom.hom₁ ∧ W A.hom.hom₂ ∧ W A.hom.hom₃) :
    IsFiltered ℐ.FullSubcategory ∧
      (MorphismProperty.Comma.lift (ℐ.ι ⋙ Under.post Triangle.π₁)
        (fun A => ((hℐ _).1 A.2).2.1) (fun _ => trivial) (fun _ => trivial) :
          ℐ.FullSubcategory ⥤ W.Under ⊤ T.obj₁).Final ∧
      (MorphismProperty.Comma.lift (ℐ.ι ⋙ Under.post Triangle.π₂)
        (fun A => ((hℐ _).1 A.2).2.2.1) (fun _ => trivial) (fun _ => trivial) :
          ℐ.FullSubcategory ⥤ W.Under ⊤ T.obj₂).Final ∧
      (MorphismProperty.Comma.lift (ℐ.ι ⋙ Under.post Triangle.π₃)
        (fun A => ((hℐ _).1 A.2).2.2.2) (fun _ => trivial) (fun _ => trivial) :
          ℐ.FullSubcategory ⥤ W.Under ⊤ T.obj₃).Final

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.ObjectProperty.IsSaturated
declarations.doc:
A property `P` of the objects of a category with zero morphisms is *saturated* if whenever
a biproduct `X ⊞ Y` is isomorphic to an object satisfying `P`, then both `X` and `Y` are
isomorphic to objects satisfying `P`; equivalently, the objects isomorphic to an object
satisfying `P` are closed under direct summands. For a pre-triangulated subcategory, this is
also called being a *thick* subcategory.
declarations.statement: public class IsSaturated : Prop

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.Functor.isTriangulated_and_isSaturated_kernel
declarations.doc:
Let `F : C ⥤ D` be an exact functor of pre-triangulated categories. The full subcategory of `C`
spanned by the objects `X` with `F X = 0`, namely `F.kernel`, is a pre-triangulated subcategory of
`C` which is saturated. It is strictly full (`ObjectProperty.IsClosedUnderIsomorphisms`) without
any hypothesis on `F`, and it is a triangulated subcategory as soon as `C` is a triangulated
category, by `CategoryTheory.ObjectProperty.instIsTriangulatedFullSubcategory`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isTriangulated_and_isSaturated_kernel (F : C ⥤ D) [F.CommShift ℤ]
    [F.IsTriangulated] :
    F.kernel.IsTriangulated ∧ F.kernel.IsSaturated

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.Functor.isTriangulated_and_isSaturated_homologicalKernel
declarations.doc:
Let `H : C ⥤ A` be a homological functor from a pre-triangulated category to an abelian
category. The full subcategory of `C` spanned by the objects `X` with `H (X⟦n⟧) = 0` for all
`n : ℤ`, namely `H.homologicalKernel`, is a pre-triangulated subcategory of `C` which is saturated.
It is strictly full (`ObjectProperty.IsClosedUnderIsomorphisms`), and it is a triangulated
subcategory as soon as `C` is a triangulated category, by
`CategoryTheory.ObjectProperty.instIsTriangulatedFullSubcategory`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isTriangulated_and_isSaturated_homologicalKernel (H : C ⥤ A) [H.IsHomological] :
    H.homologicalKernel.IsTriangulated ∧ H.homologicalKernel.IsSaturated

declarations.name: StacksBoundedSubcategories.boundedBelow_strictlyFull
declarations.doc: The property `D_H^+` of being `H`-bounded below is closed under isomorphisms.
declarations.statement:
theorem boundedBelow_strictlyFull (H : D ⥤ A) [H.IsHomological] :
    (boundedBelow H).IsClosedUnderIsomorphisms
declarations.comment: D_H^+ strictly full

declarations.name: StacksBoundedSubcategories.boundedBelow_isTriangulated
declarations.doc:
`D_H^+` is a pre-triangulated subcategory: it contains a zero object, is stable under every
shift `[n]`, and is closed under cones of distinguished triangles with two vertices in `D_H^+`.
declarations.statement:
theorem boundedBelow_isTriangulated (H : D ⥤ A) [H.IsHomological]
    [H.ShiftSequence ℤ] :
    (boundedBelow H).IsTriangulated
declarations.comment: D_H^+ pre-triangulated

declarations.name: StacksBoundedSubcategories.boundedBelow_isSaturated
declarations.doc:
`D_H^+` is saturated: if `X ⊞ Y` is bounded below then so are `X` and `Y`, each being a retract
of the biproduct.
declarations.statement:
theorem boundedBelow_isSaturated (H : D ⥤ A) [H.IsHomological] :
    IsSaturated (boundedBelow H)
declarations.comment: D_H^+ saturated

theorem boundedAbove_isSaturated (H : D ⥤ A) [H.IsHomological] :

declarations.doc: The property `D_H^b` of being `H`-bounded is closed under isomorphisms.
declarations.statement:

    (bounded H).IsClosedUnderIsomorphisms

declarations.name: StacksBoundedSubcategories.bounded_isTriangulated
declarations.doc:
`D_H^b` is a pre-triangulated subcategory: it contains a zero object, is stable under every

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.Functor.kernel_isStacksKernel
declarations.doc:
**Definition 05RF (1).** The kernel `Ker(F)` of an exact functor `F : C ⥤ D` of
pre-triangulated categories is the strictly full saturated (pre-)triangulated subcategory of
`C` of Lemma 05RC: its objects are the `X` with `F X = 0`. In Lean this is Mathlib's
`CategoryTheory.Functor.kernel`.
declarations.statement:
theorem kernel_isStacksKernel (F : C ⥤ D) [F.CommShift ℤ] [F.IsTriangulated] :
    (∀ X, F.kernel X ↔ IsZero (F.obj X)) ∧ F.kernel.IsClosedUnderIsomorphisms ∧
      F.kernel.IsTriangulated ∧ F.kernel.IsSaturated
declarations.comment:
(1): Ker(F) for an exact functor: the strictly full saturated triangulated
subcategory of objects with F(X) = 0 (Mathlib's Functor.kernel; see 05RC)

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.Functor.homologicalKernel_isStacksKernel
declarations.doc:
**Definition 05RF (2).** The kernel `Ker(H)` of a homological functor `H : C ⥤ A` from a
pre-triangulated category to an abelian category is the strictly full saturated
(pre-)triangulated subcategory of `C` of Lemma 05RD: its objects are the `X` with `H (X⟦n⟧) = 0`
for all `n : ℤ`. In Lean this is Mathlib's `CategoryTheory.Functor.homologicalKernel`.
declarations.statement:
theorem homologicalKernel_isStacksKernel (H : C ⥤ A) [H.IsHomological] :
    (∀ X, H.homologicalKernel X ↔ ∀ n : ℤ, IsZero (H.obj (X⟦n⟧))) ∧
      H.homologicalKernel.IsClosedUnderIsomorphisms ∧
      H.homologicalKernel.IsTriangulated ∧ H.homologicalKernel.IsSaturated
declarations.comment:
(2): Ker(H) for a homological functor: the strictly full saturated triangulated
subcategory of objects with H(X[n]) = 0 for all n (Mathlib's Functor.homologicalKernel; see 05RD)

registrations.name: CategoryTheory.Functor.kernel
registrations.comment:
(1) the kernel Ker(F) of an exact functor F : D ⥤ D': the objects X with
  F(X) = 0, as an `ObjectProperty`; it is strictly full and, by 05RC
  (`CategoryTheory.Functor.isTriangulated_and_isSaturated_kernel`), a saturated
  (pre-)triangulated subcategory

registrations.name: CategoryTheory.Functor.homologicalKernel
registrations.comment:
(2) the kernel Ker(H) of a homological functor H : D ⥤ A to an abelian
  category: the objects X with H(X[n]) = 0 for all n : ℤ, as an `ObjectProperty`; it is strictly
  full and, by 05RD (`CategoryTheory.Functor.isTriangulated_and_isSaturated_homologicalKernel`),
  a saturated (pre-)triangulated subcategory

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.ObjectProperty.hasCalculusOfFractions_isCompatibleWithTriangulation_and_isSaturated_iff
declarations.doc:
Let `C` be a triangulated category, let `P` be a full triangulated subcategory of `C`, and let
`S` be the class of morphisms `f` that fit into a distinguished triangle `(X, Y, Z, f, g, h)` with
`Z` isomorphic to an object of `P`. Then `S` is a multiplicative system (MS1, MS2, MS3, i.e. a left
and a right calculus of fractions) compatible with the triangulated structure on `C` (MS5, MS6),
and `S` is a saturated multiplicative system ([Stacks, Tag 05Q8]) if and only if `P` is saturated
([Stacks, Tag 05RB]).
declarations.statement:
theorem hasCalculusOfFractions_isCompatibleWithTriangulation_and_isSaturated_iff
    (P : ObjectProperty C) [P.IsTriangulated] (S : MorphismProperty C)
    (hS : ∀ ⦃X Y : C⦄ (f : X ⟶ Y), S f ↔ ∃ (Z : C) (g : Y ⟶ Z) (h : Z ⟶ X⟦(1 : ℤ)⟧),
      Triangle.mk f g h ∈ distTriang C ∧ P.isoClosure Z) :
    (S.HasLeftCalculusOfFractions ∧ S.HasRightCalculusOfFractions ∧
      S.IsCompatibleWithTriangulation) ∧ (S.IsSaturated ↔ P.IsSaturated)

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.ObjectProperty.verdierQuotient
declarations.doc:
The *quotient category* `C/P` of a pretriangulated category `C` by a subcategory
`P : ObjectProperty C`: the localization `S⁻¹C` of `C` at the class `S = P.trW` of morphisms whose
cone lies in `P`, which for `P` a full triangulated subcategory of a triangulated category is a
multiplicative system ([Stacks, Tag 05RG]). The *quotient functor* `Q : C ⥤ C/P` is the
localization functor `P.trW.Q` of this localization.

In that triangulated situation this is the Verdier quotient: `C/P` is then triangulated and the
quotient functor is exact ([Stacks, Tag 05R6]).
declarations.statement: public abbrev verdierQuotient (P : ObjectProperty C) : Type u

declarations.name: VerdierQuotientUniversalProperty.homological_universal_property
declarations.doc:
**Universal property of the Verdier quotient for homological functors**.

Let `C` be a triangulated category, `P` a full triangulated subcategory (an
`ObjectProperty` with `P.IsTriangulated`), and `Q = P.trW.Q : C ⥤ C / P` the Verdier
quotient functor. Let `A` be abelian and `H : C ⥤ A` a homological functor whose
homological kernel contains `P` (this is the hypothesis `B ⊆ Ker(H)`). Then:

* **Existence + structure**: there is a functor `H' : C / P ⥤ A` together with a natural
  isomorphism `fac : Q ⋙ H' ≅ H` (the factorization `H = H' ∘ Q`), and `H'` is again
  homological.
* **Uniqueness (up to unique natural isomorphism)**: for any functor `G : C / P ⥤ A`
  equipped with a natural isomorphism `α : Q ⋙ G ≅ H`, there is a *unique* natural
  isomorphism `e : G ≅ H'` compatible with the factorization isomorphisms, i.e. such that
  `whiskerLeft Q e.hom ≫ fac.hom = α.hom`.
declarations.statement:
theorem homological_universal_property
    {C A : Type*} [Category C] [Preadditive C] [HasZeroObject C] [HasShift C ℤ]
    [∀ n : ℤ, (shiftFunctor C n).Additive] [Pretriangulated C] [IsTriangulated C]
    [Category A] [Abelian A]
    (P : ObjectProperty C) [P.IsTriangulated]
    (H : C ⥤ A) [H.IsHomological]
    (hker : P ≤ H.homologicalKernel) :
    ∃ (H' : P.trW.Localization ⥤ A) (fac : P.trW.Q ⋙ H' ≅ H),
      H'.IsHomological ∧
      ∀ (G : P.trW.Localization ⥤ A) (α : P.trW.Q ⋙ G ≅ H),
        ∃! e : G ≅ H', Functor.whiskerLeft P.trW.Q e.hom ≫ fac.hom = α.hom

declarations.name: VerdierQuotientUniversalProperty.exact_universal_property
declarations.doc:
**Universal property of the Verdier quotient for exact (triangulated) functors**.

Let `C` be a triangulated category, `P` a full triangulated subcategory, and
`Q = P.trW.Q : C ⥤ C / P` the Verdier quotient functor. Let `D'` be pretriangulated and
`F : C ⥤ D'` an exact (triangulated) functor: it is additive (`F.Additive`), commutes
with the shift (`F.CommShift ℤ`), and sends distinguished triangles to distinguished
triangles (`F.IsTriangulated`). Assume its kernel contains `P`, i.e. `F` sends every
object of `P` to a zero object (the hypothesis `B ⊆ Ker(F)`). Then:

* **Existence + structure**: there is a functor `F' : C / P ⥤ D'` equipped with a
  `CommShift ℤ` structure, a natural isomorphism `fac : Q ⋙ F' ≅ F` (the factorization
  `F = F' ∘ Q`) which commutes with the shift structures on both sides
  (`NatTrans.CommShift fac.hom ℤ`), and `F'` is again additive (`F'.Additive`) and
  exact/triangulated (`F'.IsTriangulated`).
* **Uniqueness (up to unique natural isomorphism)**: for any functor `G : C / P ⥤ D'`
  equipped with a natural isomorphism `α : Q ⋙ G ≅ F`, there is a *unique* natural
  isomorphism `e : G ≅ F'` compatible with the factorization isomorphisms, i.e. such that
  `whiskerLeft Q e.hom ≫ fac.hom = α.hom`.
declarations.statement:
theorem exact_universal_property
    {C D' : Type*} [Category C] [Preadditive C] [HasZeroObject C] [HasShift C ℤ]
    [∀ n : ℤ, (shiftFunctor C n).Additive] [Pretriangulated C] [IsTriangulated C]
    [Category D'] [Preadditive D'] [HasZeroObject D'] [HasShift D' ℤ]
    [∀ n : ℤ, (shiftFunctor D' n).Additive] [Pretriangulated D']
    (P : ObjectProperty C) [P.IsTriangulated]
    (F : C ⥤ D') [F.Additive] [F.CommShift ℤ] [F.IsTriangulated]
    (hker : ∀ X, P X → IsZero (F.obj X)) :
    ∃ (F' : P.trW.Localization ⥤ D') (_ : F'.CommShift ℤ) (fac : P.trW.Q ⋙ F' ≅ F)
      (_ : NatTrans.CommShift fac.hom ℤ),
      F'.Additive ∧ F'.IsTriangulated ∧
      ∀ (G : P.trW.Localization ⥤ D') (α : P.trW.Q ⋙ G ≅ F),
        ∃! e : G ≅ F', Functor.whiskerLeft P.trW.Q e.hom ≫ fac.hom = α.hom

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.ObjectProperty.kernel_iff_exists_isoClosure_biprod_and_isLeast_kernel
declarations.doc:
Let `C` be a triangulated category, let `P` be a full triangulated subcategory of `C` and let
`L : C ⥤ D` be a localization of `C` at the class `P.trW` of morphisms whose cone lies in `P`, i.e.
a quotient functor `C ⥤ C/P` ([Stacks, Tag 05RI]). Then an object `Z` of `C` lies in the kernel of
`L` if and only if there is an object `Z'` such that `Z ⊞ Z'` is isomorphic to an object of `P`;
and the kernel of `L` is the smallest strictly full saturated ([Stacks, Tag 05RB]) triangulated
subcategory of `C` containing `P`.
declarations.statement:
theorem kernel_iff_exists_isoClosure_biprod_and_isLeast_kernel
    (P : ObjectProperty C) [P.IsTriangulated] (L : C ⥤ D) [L.IsLocalization P.trW] :
    (∀ Z : C, L.kernel Z ↔ ∃ Z' : C, P.isoClosure (Z ⊞ Z')) ∧
      IsLeast {P' : ObjectProperty C | P'.IsClosedUnderIsomorphisms ∧ P'.IsTriangulated ∧
        P'.IsSaturated ∧ P ≤ P'} L.kernel

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.ObjectProperty.isLeast_trW_kernel_and_isLeast_kernel_and_orderIso
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 05RL].** Let `C` be a triangulated category. Consider the constructions
`S ↦ B(S) = Ker(Q : C → S⁻¹C)` (the kernel of a localization `L : C ⥤ D` of `C` at `S`) on
multiplicative systems `S` compatible with the triangulated structure, and `P ↦ S(P) = P.trW`
(the morphisms fitting in a distinguished triangle whose third object is isomorphic to an object
of `P`) on full triangulated subcategories `P`. Then

1. `S(B(S))` is the saturation of `S`: the smallest saturated multiplicative system
   ([Stacks, Tag 05Q8]) of `C` containing `S`;
2. `B(S(P))` is the saturation of `P`: the smallest strictly full saturated
   ([Stacks, Tag 05RB]) triangulated subcategory of `C` containing `P`;
3. in particular the two constructions — `B` computed with the canonical localization
   `S.Q : C ⥤ S.Localization` — are mutually inverse, order preserving bijections between the
   (partially ordered) set of saturated multiplicative systems of `C` compatible with the
   triangulated structure and the (partially ordered) set of strictly full saturated triangulated
   subcategories of `C`.

Part (2) is [Stacks, Tag 05RK] (`kernel_iff_exists_isoClosure_biprod_and_isLeast_kernel`), and
that `S(P)` is a multiplicative system compatible with the triangulation is Mathlib's
`ObjectProperty.trW` instances, with saturation from [Stacks, Tag 05RG]. A strictly full
triangulated subcategory `P` is recovered from `S(P)` as the objects `X` with `(X ⟶ 0) ∈ S(P)`,
which makes `P ↦ S(P)` an order embedding.
declarations.statement:
theorem isLeast_trW_kernel_and_isLeast_kernel_and_orderIso :
    (∀ (S : MorphismProperty C) [S.HasLeftCalculusOfFractions]
        [S.HasRightCalculusOfFractions] [S.IsCompatibleWithTriangulation]
        (L : C ⥤ D) [L.IsLocalization S],
      IsLeast {S' : MorphismProperty C | S'.IsSaturated ∧ S ≤ S'} L.kernel.trW) ∧
    (∀ (P : ObjectProperty C) [P.IsTriangulated] (L : C ⥤ D) [L.IsLocalization P.trW],
      IsLeast {P' : ObjectProperty C | P'.IsClosedUnderIsomorphisms ∧ P'.IsTriangulated ∧
        P'.IsSaturated ∧ P ≤ P'} L.kernel) ∧
    ∃ e : {S : MorphismProperty C // S.IsSaturated ∧ S.IsCompatibleWithTriangulation} ≃o
        {P : ObjectProperty C // P.IsClosedUnderIsomorphisms ∧ P.IsTriangulated ∧ P.IsSaturated},
      (∀ S, (e S).1 = S.1.Q.kernel) ∧ ∀ P, (e.symm P).1 = P.1.trW

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.Functor.isSaturated_homologicalKernel_and_mem_trW_iff_and_exists_lift
declarations.doc:
Let `H : C ⥤ A` be a homological functor from a triangulated category to an abelian category,
write `Hⁱ = H(-⟦i⟧)`, and let `L : C ⥤ D` be a localization of `C` at the class of morphisms whose
cone lies in the kernel of `H`. Then:

* `Ker(H)` is a strictly full saturated ([Stacks, Tag 05RB]) triangulated subcategory of `C`;
* the multiplicative system attached to it by [Stacks, Tag 05RL] is saturated ([Stacks, Tag 05Q8]),
  compatible with the triangulated structure, and is the class
  `S = {f ∣ Hⁱ(f) is an isomorphism for all i ∈ ℤ}`;
* `H` factors through `L`, and so does every `Hⁱ`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isSaturated_homologicalKernel_and_mem_trW_iff_and_exists_lift
    (H : C ⥤ A) [H.IsHomological] (L : C ⥤ D)
    [L.IsLocalization H.homologicalKernel.trW] :
    (H.homologicalKernel.IsClosedUnderIsomorphisms ∧ H.homologicalKernel.IsTriangulated ∧
        H.homologicalKernel.IsSaturated) ∧
      (H.homologicalKernel.trW.IsSaturated ∧
          H.homologicalKernel.trW.IsCompatibleWithTriangulation ∧
          ∀ ⦃X Y : C⦄ (f : X ⟶ Y),
            H.homologicalKernel.trW f ↔ ∀ i : ℤ, IsIso (H.map (f⟦i⟧'))) ∧
      (∃ H' : D ⥤ A, Nonempty (L ⋙ H' ≅ H)) ∧
      ∀ i : ℤ, ∃ H' : D ⥤ A, Nonempty (L ⋙ H' ≅ shiftFunctor C i ⋙ H)

declarations.name: HomotopyCategory.isTriangulated_minus_bounded
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 05RQ.** Let `A` be an additive category. The categories `K⁻(A)` of complexes
bounded above and `K^b(A)` of bounded complexes are full triangulated subcategories of `K(A)`.
For `K⁺(A)` this is `(HomotopyCategory.plus A).IsTriangulated`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem isTriangulated_minus_bounded
    (A : Type*) [Category* A] [Preadditive A] [HasZeroObject A] [HasBinaryBiproducts A] :
    ((CochainComplex.minus A).strictMap (quotient A (ComplexShape.up ℤ))).IsTriangulated ∧
      ((CochainComplex.plus A ⊓ CochainComplex.minus A).strictMap
        (quotient A (ComplexShape.up ℤ))).IsTriangulated
declarations.comment: K⁻(A) and K^b(A); K⁺(A) is (HomotopyCategory.plus A).IsTriangulated

declarations.name: HomotopyCategory.isSaturated_subcategoryAcyclic_and_quasiIso_and_kernel_eq
declarations.statement:
public theorem isSaturated_subcategoryAcyclic_and_quasiIso_and_kernel_eq
    (L : HomotopyCategory A (ComplexShape.up ℤ) ⥤ D)
    [L.IsLocalization (HomotopyCategory.quasiIso A (ComplexShape.up ℤ))] :
    ((HomotopyCategory.subcategoryAcyclic A).IsClosedUnderIsomorphisms ∧
        (HomotopyCategory.subcategoryAcyclic A).IsTriangulated ∧
        (HomotopyCategory.subcategoryAcyclic A).IsSaturated) ∧
      ((HomotopyCategory.quasiIso A (ComplexShape.up ℤ)).IsSaturated ∧
        (HomotopyCategory.subcategoryAcyclic A).trW =
          HomotopyCategory.quasiIso A (ComplexShape.up ℤ)) ∧
      L.kernel = HomotopyCategory.subcategoryAcyclic A ∧
      ∀ n : ℤ, ∃ H : D ⥤ A,
        Nonempty (L ⋙ H ≅ HomotopyCategory.homologyFunctor A (ComplexShape.up ℤ) n)

declarations.name: DerivedCategory.plus_iff
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 05RU.** The objects of the bounded below derived category `D^{+}(A)`, the full
subcategory `DerivedCategory.Plus C` of `D(A)` on the object property `plus` of the canonical
t-structure, are exactly the `X` with `H^n(X) = 0` for all `n ≪ 0`.
declarations.comment: Ob(D^+(A)) = {X | H^n(X) = 0 for all n ≪ 0}

declarations.name: DerivedCategory.minus_iff
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 05RU.** The objects of the bounded above derived category `D^{-}(A)`, the full
subcategory `DerivedCategory.Minus C` of `D(A)` on the object property `minus` of the canonical
t-structure, are exactly the `X` with `H^n(X) = 0` for all `n ≫ 0`.
declarations.comment: Ob(D^-(A)) = {X | H^n(X) = 0 for all n ≫ 0}

declarations.name: DerivedCategory.bounded_iff
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 05RU.** The objects of the bounded derived category `D^b(A)`, the full subcategory
`DerivedCategory.Bounded C` of `D(A)` on the object property `bounded` of the canonical
t-structure, are exactly the `X` with `H^n(X) = 0` for all `|n| ≫ 0`: a single bound in the
source's condition, against the two unrelated bounds of `bounded = plus ⊓ minus`.
declarations.comment: Ob(D^b(A)) = {X | H^n(X) = 0 for all |n| ≫ 0}

declarations.name: CochainComplex.exists_quasiIso_isStrictlyGE_of_isZero_homology
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 05RV (1).** Let `K` be a cochain complex in an abelian category — or, as stated
here, in any category with zero morphisms, a zero object and homology — with `H^n(K) = 0` for all
`n ≪ 0`. Then there is a quasi-isomorphism `K ⟶ L` with `L` bounded below. The witness is the
canonical truncation `K.πTruncGE a : K ⟶ τ_{≥ a}K`, for `a` below which the cohomology vanishes.

declarations.name: CochainComplex.exists_quasiIso_isStrictlyLE_of_isZero_homology
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 05RV (2).** Let `K` be a cochain complex in an abelian category — or, as stated
here, in any category with zero morphisms, a zero object and homology — with `H^n(K) = 0` for all
`n ≫ 0`. Then there is a quasi-isomorphism `M ⟶ K` with `M` bounded above. The witness is the
canonical truncation `K.ιTruncLE b : τ_{≤ b}K ⟶ K`, for `b` above which the cohomology
vanishes.

declarations.name: CochainComplex.exists_quasiIso_square_of_isGE_of_isLE
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 05RV (3).** Let `K` be a cochain complex in an abelian category — or, as stated
here, in any category with zero morphisms, a zero object and homology — whose cohomology
vanishes in degrees `< a` and in degrees `> b`. Then there is a commutative square of
quasi-isomorphisms
```
  M ⟶ N
  ↓    ↓
  K ⟶ L
```
with `L` concentrated in degrees `≥ a`, `M` in degrees `≤ b`, and `N` in degrees `a ≤ n ≤ b`,
i.e. `N` bounded. Parts (1) and (2) of the source are
`CochainComplex.exists_quasiIso_isStrictlyGE_of_isZero_homology` and
`CochainComplex.exists_quasiIso_isStrictlyLE_of_isZero_homology`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem exists_quasiIso_square_of_isGE_of_isLE
    (K : CochainComplex C ℤ) (a b : ℤ) [K.IsGE a] [K.IsLE b] :
    ∃ (L M N : CochainComplex C ℤ) (f : K ⟶ L) (g : M ⟶ K) (u : M ⟶ N) (v : N ⟶ L)
      (_ : QuasiIso f) (_ : QuasiIso g) (_ : QuasiIso u) (_ : QuasiIso v)
      (_ : L.IsStrictlyGE a) (_ : M.IsStrictlyLE b) (_ : N.IsStrictlyGE a)
      (_ : N.IsStrictlyLE b), g ≫ f = u ≫ v

declarations.name: HomotopyCategory.isSaturated_subcategoryAcyclic_inverseImage_and_quasiIso_and_isLocalization
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 05RW.** Let `A` be an abelian category. For every triangulated subcategory `P` of
the homotopy category `K(A)` — in particular for `K⁺(A)`, `K⁻(A)` and `Kᵇ(A)` — the acyclic
objects of `P` form a strictly full saturated triangulated subcategory `Ac_P` of `P`, the
quasi-isomorphisms `Qis_P` of `P` form a saturated multiplicative system compatible with the
triangulation which is the class `Ac_P.trW` corresponding to `Ac_P` under [Stacks, Tag 05RL],
and the kernel of any localization `L` of `P` at `Qis_P` is `Ac_P`. Moreover:

1. `DerivedCategory.Plus.Qh : K⁺(A) ⥤ D⁺(A)` is a localization at `Qis⁺(A)`, so that
   `K⁺(A)/Ac⁺(A) = Qis⁺(A)⁻¹K⁺(A) ⥤ D⁺(A)` is an equivalence;
2. the functor `K⁻(A) ⥤ D⁻(A)` induced by `Qh` is a localization at `Qis⁻(A)`;
3. the functor `Kᵇ(A) ⥤ Dᵇ(A)` induced by `Qh` is a localization at `Qisᵇ(A)`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem isSaturated_subcategoryAcyclic_inverseImage_and_quasiIso_and_isLocalization :
    (∀ (P : ObjectProperty (HomotopyCategory A (ComplexShape.up ℤ))) [P.IsTriangulated]
        (L : P.FullSubcategory ⥤ D)
        [L.IsLocalization ((HomotopyCategory.quasiIso A (ComplexShape.up ℤ)).inverseImage P.ι)],
      (((HomotopyCategory.subcategoryAcyclic A).inverseImage P.ι).IsClosedUnderIsomorphisms ∧
          ((HomotopyCategory.subcategoryAcyclic A).inverseImage P.ι).IsTriangulated ∧
          ((HomotopyCategory.subcategoryAcyclic A).inverseImage P.ι).IsSaturated) ∧
        (((HomotopyCategory.quasiIso A (ComplexShape.up ℤ)).inverseImage P.ι).IsSaturated ∧
          ((HomotopyCategory.quasiIso A
            (ComplexShape.up ℤ)).inverseImage P.ι).IsCompatibleWithTriangulation ∧
          ((HomotopyCategory.subcategoryAcyclic A).inverseImage P.ι).trW =
            (HomotopyCategory.quasiIso A (ComplexShape.up ℤ)).inverseImage P.ι) ∧
        L.kernel = (HomotopyCategory.subcategoryAcyclic A).inverseImage P.ι) ∧
    (DerivedCategory.Plus.Qh (C := A)).IsLocalization (HomotopyCategory.Plus.quasiIso A) ∧
    (∃ F : ((CochainComplex.minus A).strictMap
          (HomotopyCategory.quotient A (ComplexShape.up ℤ))).FullSubcategory ⥤
        DerivedCategory.Minus A,
      Nonempty (F ⋙ DerivedCategory.Minus.ι ≅
          ((CochainComplex.minus A).strictMap
            (HomotopyCategory.quotient A (ComplexShape.up ℤ))).ι ⋙ DerivedCategory.Qh) ∧
        F.IsLocalization ((HomotopyCategory.quasiIso A (ComplexShape.up ℤ)).inverseImage
          ((CochainComplex.minus A).strictMap
            (HomotopyCategory.quotient A (ComplexShape.up ℤ))).ι)) ∧
    (∃ F : ((CochainComplex.plus A ⊓ CochainComplex.minus A).strictMap
          (HomotopyCategory.quotient A (ComplexShape.up ℤ))).FullSubcategory ⥤
        DerivedCategory.Bounded A,
      Nonempty (F ⋙ DerivedCategory.Bounded.ι ≅
          ((CochainComplex.plus A ⊓ CochainComplex.minus A).strictMap
            (HomotopyCategory.quotient A (ComplexShape.up ℤ))).ι ⋙ DerivedCategory.Qh) ∧
        F.IsLocalization ((HomotopyCategory.quasiIso A (ComplexShape.up ℤ)).inverseImage
          ((CochainComplex.plus A ⊓ CochainComplex.minus A).strictMap
            (HomotopyCategory.quotient A (ComplexShape.up ℤ))).ι))

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.FiniteFilteredObject
declarations.doc:
The category `Fil^f(C)` of *finite filtered objects* of `C`: the full subcategory of the
category `Fil(C) = FilteredObject C ℤᵒᵖ` of filtered objects `(X, F)` on those whose filtration
`F` is finite.
declarations.statement: public abbrev FiniteFilteredObject (C : Type u) [Category.{v} C]

declarations.name: CochainComplex.filteredQuasiIso
declarations.doc:
A morphism `α : K^• ⟶ L^•` of filtered cochain complexes of an abelian category `A` is a
**filtered quasi-isomorphism** if `gr^p(α) : gr^p K^• ⟶ gr^p L^•` is a quasi-isomorphism for
every `p : ℤ`, equivalently if `gr(α)` is a quasi-isomorphism.
declarations.statement: public def filteredQuasiIso : MorphismProperty (FilteredObject (CochainComplex A ℤ) ℤᵒᵖ)
declarations.comment: part (1)

declarations.name: CochainComplex.filteredAcyclic
declarations.doc:
A filtered cochain complex `K^•` of an abelian category `A` is **filtered acyclic** if the
complex `gr^p K^•` is acyclic for every `p : ℤ`, equivalently if `gr(K^•)` is acyclic.
declarations.statement: public def filteredAcyclic : ObjectProperty (FilteredObject (CochainComplex A ℤ) ℤᵒᵖ)
declarations.comment: part (2)

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.FiniteFilteredObject.homologyFunctor_gr_isHomological
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 05S0 (1).** The functor `K(Fil^f(𝒜)) ⥤ Gr(𝒜)`, `K^• ↦ H^0(gr(K^•))`, is
homological.

theorem homologyFunctor_gr_isHomological :

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.FiniteFilteredObject.homologyFunctor_grP_isHomological
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 05S0 (2).** For every `p : ℤ`, the functor `K(Fil^f(𝒜)) ⥤ 𝒜`,
`K^• ↦ H^0(gr^p(K^•))`, is homological.
declarations.statement:
theorem homologyFunctor_grP_isHomological (p : ℤ) :
    ((grP (𝒜 := 𝒜) p).mapHomotopyCategory (ComplexShape.up ℤ) ⋙
      HomotopyCategory.homologyFunctor 𝒜 (ComplexShape.up ℤ) 0).IsHomological

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.FiniteFilteredObject.homologyFunctor_forget_isHomological
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 05S0 (3).** The functor `K(Fil^f(𝒜)) ⥤ 𝒜`, `K^• ↦ H^0((forget F)K^•)`, is
homological.
declarations.statement:
theorem homologyFunctor_forget_isHomological :
    ((forget (𝒜 := 𝒜)).mapHomotopyCategory (ComplexShape.up ℤ) ⋙

declarations.name: HomotopyCategory.filteredAcyclic_isTriangulated_and_trW_eq_filteredQuasiIso
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 05S1.** Let `𝒜` be an abelian category. The full subcategory `FAc(𝒜)` of
`K(Fil^f(𝒜))` of filtered acyclic complexes is a strictly full saturated triangulated subcategory
of `K(Fil^f(𝒜))`. The corresponding saturated multiplicative system of [Stacks, Tag 05RL], the
class `FAc(𝒜).trW` of morphisms whose cone is filtered acyclic, is the class `FQis(𝒜)` of
filtered quasi-isomorphisms; it is a saturated multiplicative system (left and right calculus of
fractions, saturated) compatible with the triangulated structure. In particular the kernel of the
localisation functor `Qh : K(Fil^f(𝒜)) ⥤ DF(𝒜) = FQis(𝒜)⁻¹K(Fil^f(𝒜))` — and of every
localisation of `K(Fil^f(𝒜))` at `FQis(𝒜)` — is `FAc(𝒜)`, and the functor
`H^0 ∘ gr : K(Fil^f(𝒜)) ⥤ Gr(𝒜)` factors through `Qh`.
declarations.statement:
theorem filteredAcyclic_isTriangulated_and_trW_eq_filteredQuasiIso :
    ((filteredAcyclic 𝒜).IsClosedUnderIsomorphisms ∧ (filteredAcyclic 𝒜).IsTriangulated ∧
        (filteredAcyclic 𝒜).IsSaturated) ∧
      ((filteredAcyclic 𝒜).trW = filteredQuasiIso 𝒜 ∧
        (filteredQuasiIso 𝒜).HasLeftCalculusOfFractions ∧
        (filteredQuasiIso 𝒜).HasRightCalculusOfFractions ∧
        (filteredQuasiIso 𝒜).IsCompatibleWithTriangulation ∧
        (filteredQuasiIso 𝒜).IsSaturated) ∧
      (CochainComplex.FilteredDerivedCategory.Qh (𝒜 := 𝒜)).kernel = filteredAcyclic 𝒜 ∧
      (∀ {D : Type*} [Category* D] (L : HomotopyCategory (FiniteFilteredObject 𝒜) (.up ℤ) ⥤ D)
          [L.IsLocalization (filteredQuasiIso 𝒜)], L.kernel = filteredAcyclic 𝒜) ∧
      ∃ F : CochainComplex.FilteredDerivedCategory 𝒜 ⥤ GradedObject ℤ 𝒜,
        Nonempty (CochainComplex.FilteredDerivedCategory.Qh ⋙ F ≅
          (FiniteFilteredObject.gr (𝒜 := 𝒜)).mapHomotopyCategory (.up ℤ) ⋙
          HomotopyCategory.homologyFunctor (GradedObject ℤ 𝒜) (.up ℤ) 0)

declarations.name: CochainComplex.FilteredDerivedCategory
declarations.doc:
The **filtered derived category** `DF(A)` of an abelian category `A`: the localisation of
`K(Fil^f(A))` at the class `FQis(A)` of filtered quasi-isomorphisms, equivalently the quotient
`K(Fil^f(A))/FAc(A)` by the filtered acyclic complexes ([Stacks, Tag 05S1]). Here `K(Fil^f(A))` is
modelled by the cochain complexes of `A` filtered by subcomplexes whose filtration is finite in
each degree — for every `n` some `F^p K^n` is all of `K^n` and some `F^q K^n` is zero — and the
localisation functor `Q : K(Fil^f(A)) ⥤ DF(A)` is `MorphismProperty.Q`, whose kernel is `FAc(A)`
([Stacks, Tag 05S1]). It is triangulated, with the structure induced along
`K(Fil^f(A)) ⥤ DF(A)` (`CochainComplex.FilteredDerivedCategory.Qh`), which is exact.
declarations.statement: public abbrev FilteredDerivedCategory

declarations.name: CochainComplex.FilteredDerivedCategory.isTriangulated_grDF_forgetDF_grGradedDF
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 05S3.** Let `𝒜` be an abelian category, `DF(𝒜) = FQis(𝒜)⁻¹K(Fil^f(𝒜))` its filtered
derived category and `Gr(𝒜)` the abelian category of graded objects of `𝒜`. The functors
`gr^p, (forget F) : K(Fil^f(𝒜)) ⥤ K(𝒜)` and `gr : K(Fil^f(𝒜)) ⥤ K(Gr(𝒜))` induce canonical exact
functors `gr^p, (forget F) : DF(𝒜) ⥤ D(𝒜)` and `gr : DF(𝒜) ⥤ D(Gr(𝒜))` which commute with the
localisation functors. Each induced functor (`grDF p`, `forgetDF`, `grGradedDF`) is triangulated,
and it comes with an isomorphism `Qh ⋙ gr^p ≅ gr^p ⋙ Q`, `Qh ⋙ (forget F) ≅ (forget F) ⋙ Q`,
resp. `Qh ⋙ gr ≅ gr ⋙ Q`, between the two composites `K(Fil^f(𝒜)) ⥤ D(𝒜)`, resp.
`K(Fil^f(𝒜)) ⥤ D(Gr(𝒜))`, which is compatible with the shifts. The functors are the
factorisations through the localisation `Qh` given by its universal property
([Stacks, Tag 05R7]); `(forget F)` factors because a filtered quasi-isomorphism of complexes of
finitely filtered objects is a quasi-isomorphism
(`CochainComplex.isIso_Q_map_gradedPiece_and_forget_of_filteredQuasiIso`).
declarations.statement:
theorem isTriangulated_grDF_forgetDF_grGradedDF :
    (∀ p : ℤ, (grDF (𝒜 := 𝒜) p).IsTriangulated ∧
      ∃ e : Qh (𝒜 := 𝒜) ⋙ grDF p ≅
          (FiniteFilteredObject.grP p).mapHomotopyCategory _ ⋙ DerivedCategory.Qh,
        NatTrans.CommShift e.hom ℤ) ∧
    ((forgetDF (𝒜 := 𝒜)).IsTriangulated ∧
      ∃ e : Qh (𝒜 := 𝒜) ⋙ forgetDF ≅
          FiniteFilteredObject.forget.mapHomotopyCategory _ ⋙ DerivedCategory.Qh,
        NatTrans.CommShift e.hom ℤ) ∧
    ((grGradedDF (𝒜 := 𝒜)).IsTriangulated ∧
      ∃ e : Qh (𝒜 := 𝒜) ⋙ grGradedDF (𝒜 := 𝒜) ≅
          FiniteFilteredObject.gr.mapHomotopyCategory _ ⋙ DerivedCategory.Qh,
        NatTrans.CommShift e.hom ℤ)

declarations.name: CochainComplex.filteredPlus
declarations.doc:
The filtered cochain complexes `X` of an abelian category `A` whose associated graded is
bounded below, i.e. such that `H^n(gr(X)) = 0` for `n ≪ 0`: there is an `n : ℤ`, independent of
`p`, with `H^i(gr^p X) = 0` for all `i < n` and all `p`. These are the objects of the **bounded
below filtered derived category** `DF^{+}(A)`, the full subcategory of `DF(A)` on the objects `X`
such that `gr(X)` lies in the bounded below derived category (`D^{+}(Gr(A))`, written `D^{+}(A)`
in the source).
declarations.statement: public def filteredPlus : ObjectProperty (FilteredObject (CochainComplex A ℤ) ℤᵒᵖ)
declarations.comment: DF^+(A), the bounded below filtered derived category

declarations.name: CochainComplex.filteredMinus
declarations.doc:
The filtered cochain complexes `X` of an abelian category `A` whose associated graded is
bounded above, i.e. such that `H^n(gr(X)) = 0` for `n ≫ 0`: there is an `n : ℤ`, independent of
`p`, with `H^i(gr^p X) = 0` for all `n < i` and all `p`. These are the objects of the **bounded
above filtered derived category** `DF^{-}(A)`, the full subcategory of `DF(A)` on the objects `X`
such that `gr(X)` lies in the bounded above derived category (`D^{-}(Gr(A))`, written `D^{-}(A)`
in the source).
declarations.statement: public def filteredMinus : ObjectProperty (FilteredObject (CochainComplex A ℤ) ℤᵒᵖ)
declarations.comment: DF^-(A), the bounded above filtered derived category

declarations.name: CochainComplex.filteredBounded
declarations.doc:
The filtered cochain complexes `X` of an abelian category `A` whose associated graded is
bounded, i.e. such that `H^n(gr(X)) = 0` for `|n| ≫ 0`: there are `a b : ℤ`, independent of `p`,
with `H^i(gr^p X) = 0` for `i < a` and for `b < i`, for every `p`. These are the objects of the
**bounded filtered derived category** `DF^b(A)`, the full subcategory of `DF(A)` on the objects
`X` such that `gr(X)` lies in the bounded derived category (`D^b(Gr(A))`, written `D^b(A)` in the
source).
declarations.statement: public def filteredBounded : ObjectProperty (FilteredObject (CochainComplex A ℤ) ℤᵒᵖ)
declarations.comment: DF^b(A), the bounded filtered derived category

declarations.name: CochainComplex.exists_filteredQuasiIso_bounded_of_isGE_of_isLE_gradedPiece
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 05S5.** Let `𝒜` be an abelian category and let `K^•` be a filtered cochain complex
of `𝒜` whose filtration is finite in each degree, i.e. an object of `K(Fil^f(𝒜))`. Then, writing
`gr^p` for the graded pieces of the filtration:

1. if `H^n(gr(K^•)) = 0` for all `n < a`, i.e. every `gr^p(K^•)` is cohomologically `≥ a`, there
   is a filtered quasi-isomorphism `K^• ⟶ L^•` with `L^n = 0` for all `n < a`;
2. if `H^n(gr(K^•)) = 0` for all `n > b`, i.e. every `gr^p(K^•)` is cohomologically `≤ b`, there
   is a filtered quasi-isomorphism `M^• ⟶ K^•` with `M^n = 0` for all `n > b`;
3. if `H^n(gr(K^•)) = 0` for all `n < a` and for all `n > b`, i.e. `H^n(gr(K^•)) = 0` for
   `|n| ≫ 0`, there is a commutative square

   ```
   M^• ⟶ K^•
    ↓       ↓
   N^• ⟶ L^•
   ```

   of morphisms of filtered complexes all four of which are filtered quasi-isomorphisms, with
   `L^•` bounded below (`L^n = 0` for `n < a`), `M^•` bounded above (`M^n = 0` for `n > b`) and
   `N^•` bounded (`N^n = 0` for `n < a` and for `n > b`);

and in each case the complexes produced again have finite filtration in each degree, i.e. lie in
`K(Fil^f(𝒜))`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem exists_filteredQuasiIso_bounded_of_isGE_of_isLE_gradedPiece
    (K : FilteredObject (CochainComplex 𝒜 ℤ) ℤᵒᵖ)
    (hK : ∀ n : ℤ, ∃ p q : ℤ, IsIso ((K.filtration.ι.app (op p)).f n) ∧
      IsZero ((K.filtration.obj (op q)).X n)) :
    (∀ a : ℤ, (∀ p : ℤ, ((FilteredObject.gr p).obj K).IsGE a) →
        ∃ (L : FilteredObject (CochainComplex 𝒜 ℤ) ℤᵒᵖ) (α : K ⟶ L)
          (_ : CochainComplex.filteredQuasiIso 𝒜 α) (_ : L.X.IsStrictlyGE a),
          ∀ n : ℤ, ∃ p q : ℤ, IsIso ((L.filtration.ι.app (op p)).f n) ∧
            IsZero ((L.filtration.obj (op q)).X n)) ∧
      (∀ b : ℤ, (∀ p : ℤ, ((FilteredObject.gr p).obj K).IsLE b) →
        ∃ (M : FilteredObject (CochainComplex 𝒜 ℤ) ℤᵒᵖ) (α : M ⟶ K)
          (_ : CochainComplex.filteredQuasiIso 𝒜 α) (_ : M.X.IsStrictlyLE b),
          ∀ n : ℤ, ∃ p q : ℤ, IsIso ((M.filtration.ι.app (op p)).f n) ∧
            IsZero ((M.filtration.obj (op q)).X n)) ∧
      (∀ a b : ℤ, (∀ p : ℤ, ((FilteredObject.gr p).obj K).IsGE a) →
        (∀ p : ℤ, ((FilteredObject.gr p).obj K).IsLE b) →
        ∃ (L M N : FilteredObject (CochainComplex 𝒜 ℤ) ℤᵒᵖ) (f : M ⟶ K) (g : M ⟶ N) (h : K ⟶ L)
          (i : N ⟶ L) (_ : CommSq f g h i) (_ : CochainComplex.filteredQuasiIso 𝒜 f)
          (_ : CochainComplex.filteredQuasiIso 𝒜 g) (_ : CochainComplex.filteredQuasiIso 𝒜 h)
          (_ : CochainComplex.filteredQuasiIso 𝒜 i) (_ : L.X.IsStrictlyGE a)
          (_ : M.X.IsStrictlyLE b) (_ : N.X.IsStrictlyGE a) (_ : N.X.IsStrictlyLE b),
          (∀ n : ℤ, ∃ p q : ℤ, IsIso ((L.filtration.ι.app (op p)).f n) ∧
              IsZero ((L.filtration.obj (op q)).X n)) ∧
            (∀ n : ℤ, ∃ p q : ℤ, IsIso ((M.filtration.ι.app (op p)).f n) ∧
              IsZero ((M.filtration.obj (op q)).X n)) ∧
            (∀ n : ℤ, ∃ p q : ℤ, IsIso ((N.filtration.ι.app (op p)).f n) ∧
              IsZero ((N.filtration.obj (op q)).X n)))

declarations.name: CochainComplex.FilteredDerivedCategory.isSaturated_filteredAcyclic_and_isLocalization
declarations.doc:
Let `𝒜` be an abelian category. For every triangulated subcategory `P` of `K(Fil^f(𝒜))` — in
particular for `K⁺(Fil^f(𝒜))`, `K⁻(Fil^f(𝒜))` and `Kᵇ(Fil^f(𝒜))` — the filtered acyclic objects
`FAc_P(𝒜)` of `P` form a strictly full saturated triangulated subcategory of `P`, the filtered
quasi-isomorphisms `FQis_P(𝒜)` of `P` form a saturated multiplicative system compatible with the
triangulation which is the class `FAc_P(𝒜).trW` corresponding to `FAc_P(𝒜)` under
[Stacks, Tag 05RL], and the kernel of any localisation of `P` at `FQis_P(𝒜)` is `FAc_P(𝒜)`.
Moreover:

1. the functor `K⁺(Fil^f(𝒜)) ⥤ DF⁺(𝒜)` induced by `Qh : K(Fil^f(𝒜)) ⥤ DF(𝒜)` has kernel
   `FAc⁺(𝒜)` and is a localisation at `FQis⁺(𝒜)`, so that
   `K⁺(Fil^f(𝒜))/FAc⁺(𝒜) = FQis⁺(𝒜)⁻¹K⁺(Fil^f(𝒜)) ⥤ DF⁺(𝒜)` is an equivalence;
2. the functor `K⁻(Fil^f(𝒜)) ⥤ DF⁻(𝒜)` induced by `Qh` has kernel `FAc⁻(𝒜)` and is a
   localisation at `FQis⁻(𝒜)`;
3. the functor `Kᵇ(Fil^f(𝒜)) ⥤ DFᵇ(𝒜)` induced by `Qh` has kernel `FAcᵇ(𝒜)` and is a
   localisation at `FQisᵇ(𝒜)`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem isSaturated_filteredAcyclic_and_isLocalization :
    (∀ (P : ObjectProperty (HomotopyCategory (FiniteFilteredObject 𝒜) (.up ℤ))) [P.IsTriangulated]
        {D : Type*} [Category* D] (L : P.FullSubcategory ⥤ D)
        [L.IsLocalization ((HomotopyCategory.filteredQuasiIso 𝒜).inverseImage P.ι)],
      (((HomotopyCategory.filteredAcyclic 𝒜).inverseImage P.ι).IsClosedUnderIsomorphisms ∧
          ((HomotopyCategory.filteredAcyclic 𝒜).inverseImage P.ι).IsTriangulated ∧
          ((HomotopyCategory.filteredAcyclic 𝒜).inverseImage P.ι).IsSaturated) ∧
        (((HomotopyCategory.filteredQuasiIso 𝒜).inverseImage P.ι).IsSaturated ∧
          ((HomotopyCategory.filteredQuasiIso 𝒜).inverseImage P.ι).IsCompatibleWithTriangulation ∧
          ((HomotopyCategory.filteredAcyclic 𝒜).inverseImage P.ι).trW =
            (HomotopyCategory.filteredQuasiIso 𝒜).inverseImage P.ι) ∧
        L.kernel = (HomotopyCategory.filteredAcyclic 𝒜).inverseImage P.ι) ∧
    (∃ F : HomotopyCategory.Plus (FiniteFilteredObject 𝒜) ⥤ (plus 𝒜).FullSubcategory,
      Nonempty (F ⋙ (plus 𝒜).ι ≅ HomotopyCategory.Plus.ι _ ⋙ Qh) ∧
        F.IsLocalization ((HomotopyCategory.filteredQuasiIso 𝒜).inverseImage
          (HomotopyCategory.Plus.ι _)) ∧
        F.kernel = (HomotopyCategory.filteredAcyclic 𝒜).inverseImage (HomotopyCategory.Plus.ι _)) ∧
    (∃ F : ((CochainComplex.minus _).strictMap
          (HomotopyCategory.quotient (FiniteFilteredObject 𝒜) (.up ℤ))).FullSubcategory ⥤
        (minus 𝒜).FullSubcategory,
      Nonempty (F ⋙ (minus 𝒜).ι ≅ ((CochainComplex.minus _).strictMap
          (HomotopyCategory.quotient (FiniteFilteredObject 𝒜) (.up ℤ))).ι ⋙ Qh) ∧
        F.IsLocalization ((HomotopyCategory.filteredQuasiIso 𝒜).inverseImage
          ((CochainComplex.minus _).strictMap
            (HomotopyCategory.quotient (FiniteFilteredObject 𝒜) (.up ℤ))).ι) ∧
        F.kernel = (HomotopyCategory.filteredAcyclic 𝒜).inverseImage
          ((CochainComplex.minus _).strictMap
            (HomotopyCategory.quotient (FiniteFilteredObject 𝒜) (.up ℤ))).ι) ∧
    (∃ F : ((CochainComplex.plus _ ⊓ CochainComplex.minus _).strictMap
          (HomotopyCategory.quotient (FiniteFilteredObject 𝒜) (.up ℤ))).FullSubcategory ⥤
        (bounded 𝒜).FullSubcategory,
      Nonempty (F ⋙ (bounded 𝒜).ι ≅ ((CochainComplex.plus _ ⊓ CochainComplex.minus _).strictMap
          (HomotopyCategory.quotient (FiniteFilteredObject 𝒜) (.up ℤ))).ι ⋙ Qh) ∧
        F.IsLocalization ((HomotopyCategory.filteredQuasiIso 𝒜).inverseImage
          ((CochainComplex.plus _ ⊓ CochainComplex.minus _).strictMap
            (HomotopyCategory.quotient (FiniteFilteredObject 𝒜) (.up ℤ))).ι) ∧
        F.kernel = (HomotopyCategory.filteredAcyclic 𝒜).inverseImage
          ((CochainComplex.plus _ ⊓ CochainComplex.minus _).strictMap
            (HomotopyCategory.quotient (FiniteFilteredObject 𝒜) (.up ℤ))).ι)

declarations.name: CochainComplex.FilteredDerivedCategory.isTriangulated_isLocalization_Qplus_Qminus_Qbounded
declarations.doc:
The functors `K⁺(Fil^f(𝒜)) ⥤ DF⁺(𝒜)`, `K⁻(Fil^f(𝒜)) ⥤ DF⁻(𝒜)`
and `Kᵇ(Fil^f(𝒜)) ⥤ DFᵇ(𝒜)` induced by `Qh` are exact localisations at `FQis⁺(𝒜)`,
`FQis⁻(𝒜)`, `FQisᵇ(𝒜)`: so the induced equivalences
`FQis^*(𝒜)⁻¹K^*(Fil^f(𝒜)) ⥤ DF^*(𝒜)` are equivalences of triangulated categories.
declarations.statement:
theorem isTriangulated_isLocalization_Qplus_Qminus_Qbounded :
    ((Qplus (𝒜 := 𝒜)).IsTriangulated ∧ (Qplus (𝒜 := 𝒜)).IsLocalization
        ((HomotopyCategory.filteredQuasiIso 𝒜).inverseImage (HomotopyCategory.Plus.ι _))) ∧
      ((Qminus (𝒜 := 𝒜)).IsTriangulated ∧ (Qminus (𝒜 := 𝒜)).IsLocalization
        ((HomotopyCategory.filteredQuasiIso 𝒜).inverseImage (Kminus (𝒜 := 𝒜)).ι)) ∧
      ((Qbounded (𝒜 := 𝒜)).IsTriangulated ∧ (Qbounded (𝒜 := 𝒜)).IsLocalization
        ((HomotopyCategory.filteredQuasiIso 𝒜).inverseImage (Kbounded (𝒜 := 𝒜)).ι))
declarations.comment: the equivalences are equivalences of triangulated categories

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.Functor.IsRightDerivedValueAt
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 05S9(1)**. The cocone `c` on the ind-object
`X/W ⟶ 𝒟'`, `(s : X ⟶ X') ↦ F(X')`
exhibits its vertex `c.pt` as a *value of the right derived functor `RF` at `X`*: the ind-object
is essentially constant with value `c.pt`, i.e. there are an index `s₀` and a section
`r : c.pt ⟶ F(X'₀)` of the coprojection at `s₀` such that every transition morphism of the
ind-object factors through `r` after enlarging the index.

Accordingly, `RF` *is defined at* `X` means `∃ c, F.IsRightDerivedValueAt W X c`, and the value
`RF(X)` is `c.pt`.
declarations.statement:
public def IsRightDerivedValueAt (F : D ⥤ D') (W : MorphismProperty D) (X : D)
    (c : Cocone (MorphismProperty.Under.forget W ⊤ X ⋙ Under.forget X ⋙ F)) : Prop

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.Functor.IsLeftDerivedValueAt
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 05S9(2)**. The cone `c` on the pro-object
`W/X ⟶ 𝒟'`, `(s : X' ⟶ X) ↦ F(X')`
exhibits its vertex `c.pt` as a *value of the left derived functor `LF` at `X`*: the pro-object
is essentially constant with value `c.pt`, i.e. there are an index `s₀` and a retraction
`r : F(X'₀) ⟶ c.pt` of the projection at `s₀` such that every transition morphism of the
pro-object factors through `r` after refining the index.

Accordingly, `LF` *is defined at* `X` means `∃ c, F.IsLeftDerivedValueAt W X c`, and the value
`LF(X)` is `c.pt`.
declarations.statement:
public def IsLeftDerivedValueAt (F : D ⥤ D') (W : MorphismProperty D) (X : D)
    (c : Cone (MorphismProperty.Over.forget W ⊤ X ⋙ Over.forget X ⋙ F)) : Prop

declarations.name: StacksDerivedFunctor.rightDerivedMap
declarations.doc:
The morphism `RF(f) : RF X ⟶ RF Y` induced by `f : X ⟶ Y` between two values, characterised
by `rightDerivedMap_spec` together with `rightDerivedMap_unique`.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def rightDerivedMap [S.HasLeftCalculusOfFractions]
    (hX : F.IsRightDerivedValueAt S X cX) (_hY : F.IsRightDerivedValueAt S Y cY) (f : X ⟶ Y) :
    cX.pt ⟶ cY.pt
declarations.comment:
(1), the morphism itself; `rightDerivedMap_spec` is its defining property and
`rightDerivedMap_unique` is its uniqueness

declarations.name: StacksDerivedFunctor.rightDerivedMap_spec
declarations.doc: `RF(f)` makes each square of Statement 1 commute.
declarations.statement:
lemma rightDerivedMap_spec [S.HasLeftCalculusOfFractions]
    (hX : F.IsRightDerivedValueAt S X cX) (hY : F.IsRightDerivedValueAt S Y cY) (f : X ⟶ Y)
    (X' Y' : C) (s : X ⟶ X') (s' : Y ⟶ Y') (f' : X' ⟶ Y') (hs : S s) (hs' : S s')
    (hsq : f ≫ s' = s ≫ f') :
    cX.ι.app (Under.mk ⊤ s hs) ≫ rightDerivedMap S F hX hY f =
      F.map f' ≫ cY.ι.app (Under.mk ⊤ s' hs')
declarations.comment: (1), the defining property of `rightDerivedMap`
