declarations.name: StacksDerivedFunctor.rightDerivedMap_unique
declarations.doc: `RF(f)` is the only morphism with that property.
declarations.statement:
lemma rightDerivedMap_unique [S.HasLeftCalculusOfFractions]
    (hX : F.IsRightDerivedValueAt S X cX) (hY : F.IsRightDerivedValueAt S Y cY) (f : X ⟶ Y)
    (φ : cX.pt ⟶ cY.pt)
    (hφ : ∀ (X' Y' : C) (s : X ⟶ X') (s' : Y ⟶ Y') (f' : X' ⟶ Y')
      (hs : S s) (hs' : S s') (_ : f ≫ s' = s ≫ f'),
      cX.ι.app (Under.mk ⊤ s hs) ≫ φ = F.map f' ≫ cY.ι.app (Under.mk ⊤ s' hs')) :
    φ = rightDerivedMap S F hX hY f
declarations.comment: (1), uniqueness of `rightDerivedMap`

declarations.name: StacksDerivedFunctor.leftDerivedMap
declarations.doc:
The morphism `LF(f) : LF X ⟶ LF Y` induced by `f : X ⟶ Y` between two values, characterised
by `leftDerivedMap_spec` together with `leftDerivedMap_unique`.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def leftDerivedMap [S.HasRightCalculusOfFractions]
    (_hX : F.IsLeftDerivedValueAt S X dX) (hY : F.IsLeftDerivedValueAt S Y dY) (f : X ⟶ Y) :
    dX.pt ⟶ dY.pt
declarations.comment:
(2), the morphism itself; `leftDerivedMap_spec` is its defining property and
`leftDerivedMap_unique` is its uniqueness

declarations.name: StacksDerivedFunctor.leftDerivedMap_spec
declarations.doc: `LF(f)` makes each square of Statement 2 commute.
declarations.statement:
lemma leftDerivedMap_spec [S.HasRightCalculusOfFractions]
    (hX : F.IsLeftDerivedValueAt S X dX) (hY : F.IsLeftDerivedValueAt S Y dY) (f : X ⟶ Y)
    (X' Y' : C) (s : X' ⟶ X) (s' : Y' ⟶ Y) (f' : X' ⟶ Y') (hs : S s) (hs' : S s')
    (hsq : s ≫ f = f' ≫ s') :
    leftDerivedMap S F hX hY f ≫ dY.π.app (Over.mk ⊤ s' hs') =
      dX.π.app (Over.mk ⊤ s hs) ≫ F.map f'
declarations.comment: (2), the defining property of `leftDerivedMap`

declarations.name: StacksDerivedFunctor.leftDerivedMap_unique
declarations.doc: `LF(f)` is the only morphism with that property.
declarations.statement:
lemma leftDerivedMap_unique [S.HasRightCalculusOfFractions]
    (hX : F.IsLeftDerivedValueAt S X dX) (hY : F.IsLeftDerivedValueAt S Y dY) (f : X ⟶ Y)
    (φ : dX.pt ⟶ dY.pt)
    (hφ : ∀ (X' Y' : C) (s : X' ⟶ X) (s' : Y' ⟶ Y) (f' : X' ⟶ Y')
      (hs : S s) (hs' : S s') (_ : s ≫ f = f' ≫ s'),
      φ ≫ dY.π.app (Over.mk ⊤ s' hs') = dX.π.app (Over.mk ⊤ s hs) ≫ F.map f') :
    φ = leftDerivedMap S F hX hY f
declarations.comment: (2), uniqueness of `leftDerivedMap`

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.Functor.exists_isRightDerivedValueAt_iff_and_isIso_of_mem
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 05SB**(1). Let `F : C ⥤ H` be a functor, `W` a class of morphisms of
`C` with left calculus of fractions and `s : X ⟶ Y` a morphism in `W`. Then:

* the right derived functor of `F` is defined at `X` if and only if it is defined
  at `Y`, definedness being essential constancy of the ind-object on `X/W` as in
  Stacks 05S9;
* if `c` is a value of `RF` at `X` and `d` is a value of `RF` at `Y`, there is a
  morphism `φ : RF(X) ⟶ RF(Y)` compatible with the coprojections of `c` and `d`
  along every square `a.hom ≫ f = s ≫ b.hom` — that is, the map `RF(s)` of Stacks
  05SA — and `φ` is an isomorphism.

Item (2) of the source, for the left derived functor, is
`Functor.exists_isLeftDerivedValueAt_iff_and_isIso_of_mem`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem Functor.exists_isRightDerivedValueAt_iff_and_isIso_of_mem
    (F : C ⥤ H) (W : MorphismProperty C) [W.HasLeftCalculusOfFractions]
    {X Y : C} {s : X ⟶ Y} (hs : W s) :
    ((∃ c, F.IsRightDerivedValueAt W X c) ↔ (∃ d, F.IsRightDerivedValueAt W Y d)) ∧
      ∀ {c : Cocone (MorphismProperty.Under.forget W ⊤ X ⋙ Under.forget X ⋙ F)}
        {d : Cocone (MorphismProperty.Under.forget W ⊤ Y ⋙ Under.forget Y ⋙ F)},
        F.IsRightDerivedValueAt W X c → F.IsRightDerivedValueAt W Y d →
          ∃ φ : c.pt ⟶ d.pt,
            (∀ (a : W.Under ⊤ X) (b : W.Under ⊤ Y) (f : a.right ⟶ b.right),
              a.hom ≫ f = s ≫ b.hom → c.ι.app a ≫ φ = F.map f ≫ d.ι.app b) ∧ IsIso φ

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.Functor.exists_isLeftDerivedValueAt_iff_and_isIso_of_mem
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 05SB**(2). Let `F : C ⥤ H` be a functor, `W` a class of morphisms of
`C` with right calculus of fractions and `s : X ⟶ Y` a morphism in `W`. Then:

* the left derived functor of `F` is defined at `X` if and only if it is defined
  at `Y`, definedness being essential constancy of the pro-object on `W/X` as in
  Stacks 05S9;
* if `c` is a value of `LF` at `X` and `d` is a value of `LF` at `Y`, there is a
  morphism `φ : LF(X) ⟶ LF(Y)` compatible with the projections of `c` and `d`
  along every square `a.hom ≫ s = f ≫ b.hom` — that is, the map `LF(s)` of Stacks
  05SA — and `φ` is an isomorphism.

The proof applies item (1) to `F.op`, `W.op` and `s.op`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem Functor.exists_isLeftDerivedValueAt_iff_and_isIso_of_mem
    (F : C ⥤ H) (W : MorphismProperty C) [W.HasRightCalculusOfFractions]
    {X Y : C} {s : X ⟶ Y} (hs : W s) :
    ((∃ c, F.IsLeftDerivedValueAt W X c) ↔ (∃ d, F.IsLeftDerivedValueAt W Y d)) ∧
      ∀ {c : Cone (MorphismProperty.Over.forget W ⊤ X ⋙ Over.forget X ⋙ F)}
        {d : Cone (MorphismProperty.Over.forget W ⊤ Y ⋙ Over.forget Y ⋙ F)},
        F.IsLeftDerivedValueAt W X c → F.IsLeftDerivedValueAt W Y d →
          ∃ φ : c.pt ⟶ d.pt,
            (∀ (a : W.Over ⊤ X) (b : W.Over ⊤ Y) (f : a.left ⟶ b.left),
              a.hom ≫ s = f ≫ b.hom → φ ≫ d.π.app b = c.π.app a ≫ F.map f) ∧ IsIso φ

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.Functor.exists_isRightDerivedValueAt_and_isLeftDerivedValueAt_and_triangle_distinguished
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 05SC**. Let `F : C ⥤ H` be an exact functor of pretriangulated categories and let
`W` be a saturated multiplicative system in `C` (Stacks 05Q8) compatible with the triangulation.
Let `T = (X, Y, Z, f, g, h)` be a distinguished triangle of `C`.

If the right derived functor `RF` of `F` with respect to `W` is defined at two of `X`, `Y`, `Z`
— that is, if for two of them the ind-object `(s : X ⟶ X') ↦ F(X')` over `X/W` is essentially
constant — then it is defined at the third; moreover, for any values `RF(X)`, `RF(Y)`, `RF(Z)` at
the three objects there are morphisms `RF(f)`, `RF(g)`, `RF(h)` between them, each characterised
by compatibility with the coprojections as in Stacks 05SA, such that
`(RF(X), RF(Y), RF(Z), RF(f), RF(g), RF(h))` is a distinguished triangle of `H`. That is the first
conjunct.

Similarly for the left derived functor `LF`, the second conjunct: if `LF` is defined at two of
`X`, `Y`, `Z` — if for two of them the pro-object `(s : X' ⟶ X) ↦ F(X')` over `W/X` is essentially
constant — then it is defined at the third, and for any values `LF(X)`, `LF(Y)`, `LF(Z)` there are
morphisms `LF(f)`, `LF(g)`, `LF(h)`, each characterised by compatibility with the projections as
in the dual of Stacks 05SA, such that `(LF(X), LF(Y), LF(Z), LF(f), LF(g), LF(h))` is a
distinguished triangle of `H`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem exists_isRightDerivedValueAt_and_isLeftDerivedValueAt_and_triangle_distinguished
    (F : C ⥤ H) [F.CommShift ℤ] [F.IsTriangulated] (W : MorphismProperty C)
    (hW : W.IsSaturated) [W.IsCompatibleWithTriangulation]
    (T : Triangle C) (hT : T ∈ distTriang C) :
    (((∃ c, F.IsRightDerivedValueAt W T.obj₁ c) → (∃ c, F.IsRightDerivedValueAt W T.obj₂ c) →
          ∃ c, F.IsRightDerivedValueAt W T.obj₃ c) ∧
        ((∃ c, F.IsRightDerivedValueAt W T.obj₂ c) → (∃ c, F.IsRightDerivedValueAt W T.obj₃ c) →
          ∃ c, F.IsRightDerivedValueAt W T.obj₁ c) ∧
        ((∃ c, F.IsRightDerivedValueAt W T.obj₃ c) → (∃ c, F.IsRightDerivedValueAt W T.obj₁ c) →
          ∃ c, F.IsRightDerivedValueAt W T.obj₂ c) ∧
        ∀ (cX : Cocone (MorphismProperty.Under.forget W ⊤ T.obj₁ ⋙ Under.forget T.obj₁ ⋙ F))
          (_ : F.IsRightDerivedValueAt W T.obj₁ cX)
          (cY : Cocone (MorphismProperty.Under.forget W ⊤ T.obj₂ ⋙ Under.forget T.obj₂ ⋙ F))
          (_ : F.IsRightDerivedValueAt W T.obj₂ cY)
          (cZ : Cocone (MorphismProperty.Under.forget W ⊤ T.obj₃ ⋙ Under.forget T.obj₃ ⋙ F))
          (_ : F.IsRightDerivedValueAt W T.obj₃ cZ),
          ∃ (u : cX.pt ⟶ cY.pt) (v : cY.pt ⟶ cZ.pt) (w : cZ.pt ⟶ cX.pt⟦(1 : ℤ)⟧),
            Triangle.mk u v w ∈ distTriang H ∧
            (∀ (s : W.Under ⊤ T.obj₁) (t : W.Under ⊤ T.obj₂) (f' : s.right ⟶ t.right),
              T.mor₁ ≫ t.hom = s.hom ≫ f' → cX.ι.app s ≫ u = F.map f' ≫ cY.ι.app t) ∧
            (∀ (t : W.Under ⊤ T.obj₂) (r : W.Under ⊤ T.obj₃) (g' : t.right ⟶ r.right),
              T.mor₂ ≫ r.hom = t.hom ≫ g' → cY.ι.app t ≫ v = F.map g' ≫ cZ.ι.app r) ∧
            ∀ (r : W.Under ⊤ T.obj₃) (s : W.Under ⊤ T.obj₁) (h' : r.right ⟶ s.right⟦(1 : ℤ)⟧),
              T.mor₃ ≫ s.hom⟦(1 : ℤ)⟧' = r.hom ≫ h' →
                cZ.ι.app r ≫ w =
                  F.map h' ≫ (F.commShiftIso (1 : ℤ)).hom.app s.right ≫
                    (cX.ι.app s)⟦(1 : ℤ)⟧') ∧
      (((∃ c, F.IsLeftDerivedValueAt W T.obj₁ c) → (∃ c, F.IsLeftDerivedValueAt W T.obj₂ c) →
            ∃ c, F.IsLeftDerivedValueAt W T.obj₃ c) ∧
          ((∃ c, F.IsLeftDerivedValueAt W T.obj₂ c) → (∃ c, F.IsLeftDerivedValueAt W T.obj₃ c) →
            ∃ c, F.IsLeftDerivedValueAt W T.obj₁ c) ∧
          ((∃ c, F.IsLeftDerivedValueAt W T.obj₃ c) → (∃ c, F.IsLeftDerivedValueAt W T.obj₁ c) →
            ∃ c, F.IsLeftDerivedValueAt W T.obj₂ c) ∧
          ∀ (cX : Cone (MorphismProperty.Over.forget W ⊤ T.obj₁ ⋙ Over.forget T.obj₁ ⋙ F))
            (_ : F.IsLeftDerivedValueAt W T.obj₁ cX)
            (cY : Cone (MorphismProperty.Over.forget W ⊤ T.obj₂ ⋙ Over.forget T.obj₂ ⋙ F))
            (_ : F.IsLeftDerivedValueAt W T.obj₂ cY)
            (cZ : Cone (MorphismProperty.Over.forget W ⊤ T.obj₃ ⋙ Over.forget T.obj₃ ⋙ F))
            (_ : F.IsLeftDerivedValueAt W T.obj₃ cZ),
            ∃ (u : cX.pt ⟶ cY.pt) (v : cY.pt ⟶ cZ.pt) (w : cZ.pt ⟶ cX.pt⟦(1 : ℤ)⟧),
              Triangle.mk u v w ∈ distTriang H ∧
              (∀ (s : W.Over ⊤ T.obj₁) (t : W.Over ⊤ T.obj₂) (f' : s.left ⟶ t.left),
                s.hom ≫ T.mor₁ = f' ≫ t.hom → u ≫ cY.π.app t = cX.π.app s ≫ F.map f') ∧
              (∀ (t : W.Over ⊤ T.obj₂) (r : W.Over ⊤ T.obj₃) (g' : t.left ⟶ r.left),
                t.hom ≫ T.mor₂ = g' ≫ r.hom → v ≫ cZ.π.app r = cY.π.app t ≫ F.map g') ∧
              ∀ (r : W.Over ⊤ T.obj₃) (s : W.Over ⊤ T.obj₁) (h' : r.left ⟶ s.left⟦(1 : ℤ)⟧),
                r.hom ≫ T.mor₃ = h' ≫ s.hom⟦(1 : ℤ)⟧' →
                  w ≫ (cX.π.app s)⟦(1 : ℤ)⟧' =
                    cZ.π.app r ≫ F.map h' ≫ (F.commShiftIso (1 : ℤ)).hom.app s.left)

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.Functor.exists_isDerivedValueAt_biprod_and_isIso_biprod_lift
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 05SD**. Let `F : C ⥤ H` be an exact functor of pretriangulated categories and let
`W` be a saturated multiplicative system in `C` (Stacks 05Q8) compatible with the triangulation.
Let `X` and `Y` be objects of `C` and write `X ⊞ Y` for their direct sum. Then, `RF` and `LF`
being the right and left derived functors of `F` with respect to `W` and definedness and values
being as in Stacks 05S9:

1. if `RF` is defined at `X` and at `Y`, then `RF` is defined at `X ⊞ Y`, and likewise for `LF`;
2. if `H` is Karoubian (`IsIdempotentComplete`) and `RF` is defined at `X ⊞ Y`, then `RF` is
   defined at `X` and at `Y`, and likewise for `LF`;

and in either case `RF(X ⊞ Y) = RF(X) ⊞ RF(Y)`: for values `cX`, `cY`, `cXY` of `RF` at `X`, `Y`
and `X ⊞ Y` there are morphisms `p₁ : RF(X ⊞ Y) ⟶ RF(X)` and `p₂ : RF(X ⊞ Y) ⟶ RF(Y)`, namely
the maps `RF(biprod.fst)` and `RF(biprod.snd)` of Stacks 05SA — each pinned by compatibility with
the coprojections along every commutative square, which determines it uniquely — such that
`biprod.lift p₁ p₂` is an isomorphism; and likewise for `LF`, with the projections of the
cones.
declarations.statement:
public theorem exists_isDerivedValueAt_biprod_and_isIso_biprod_lift
    (F : C ⥤ H) [F.CommShift ℤ]
    [F.IsTriangulated] (W : MorphismProperty C) (hW : W.IsSaturated)
    [W.IsCompatibleWithTriangulation] (X Y : C) :
    -- (1) for `RF` and for `LF`
    ((∃ c, F.IsRightDerivedValueAt W X c) → (∃ c, F.IsRightDerivedValueAt W Y c) →
        ∃ c, F.IsRightDerivedValueAt W (X ⊞ Y) c) ∧
      ((∃ c, F.IsLeftDerivedValueAt W X c) → (∃ c, F.IsLeftDerivedValueAt W Y c) →
        ∃ c, F.IsLeftDerivedValueAt W (X ⊞ Y) c) ∧
      -- (2) for `RF` and for `LF`, over a Karoubian target
      (IsIdempotentComplete H → (∃ c, F.IsRightDerivedValueAt W (X ⊞ Y) c) →
        (∃ c, F.IsRightDerivedValueAt W X c) ∧ ∃ c, F.IsRightDerivedValueAt W Y c) ∧
      (IsIdempotentComplete H → (∃ c, F.IsLeftDerivedValueAt W (X ⊞ Y) c) →
        (∃ c, F.IsLeftDerivedValueAt W X c) ∧ ∃ c, F.IsLeftDerivedValueAt W Y c) ∧
      -- `RF(X ⊞ Y) = RF(X) ⊞ RF(Y)`
      (∀ (cX : Cocone (MorphismProperty.Under.forget W ⊤ X ⋙ Under.forget X ⋙ F))
        (_ : F.IsRightDerivedValueAt W X cX)
        (cY : Cocone (MorphismProperty.Under.forget W ⊤ Y ⋙ Under.forget Y ⋙ F))
        (_ : F.IsRightDerivedValueAt W Y cY)
        (cXY : Cocone (MorphismProperty.Under.forget W ⊤ (X ⊞ Y) ⋙ Under.forget (X ⊞ Y) ⋙ F))
        (_ : F.IsRightDerivedValueAt W (X ⊞ Y) cXY),
        ∃ (p₁ : cXY.pt ⟶ cX.pt) (p₂ : cXY.pt ⟶ cY.pt),
          (∀ (a : W.Under ⊤ (X ⊞ Y)) (b : W.Under ⊤ X) (g : a.right ⟶ b.right),
            biprod.fst ≫ b.hom = a.hom ≫ g → cXY.ι.app a ≫ p₁ = F.map g ≫ cX.ι.app b) ∧
          (∀ (a : W.Under ⊤ (X ⊞ Y)) (b : W.Under ⊤ Y) (g : a.right ⟶ b.right),
            biprod.snd ≫ b.hom = a.hom ≫ g → cXY.ι.app a ≫ p₂ = F.map g ≫ cY.ι.app b) ∧
          IsIso (biprod.lift p₁ p₂)) ∧
      -- `LF(X ⊞ Y) = LF(X) ⊞ LF(Y)`
      ∀ (cX : Cone (MorphismProperty.Over.forget W ⊤ X ⋙ Over.forget X ⋙ F))
        (_ : F.IsLeftDerivedValueAt W X cX)
        (cY : Cone (MorphismProperty.Over.forget W ⊤ Y ⋙ Over.forget Y ⋙ F))
        (_ : F.IsLeftDerivedValueAt W Y cY)
        (cXY : Cone (MorphismProperty.Over.forget W ⊤ (X ⊞ Y) ⋙ Over.forget (X ⊞ Y) ⋙ F))
        (_ : F.IsLeftDerivedValueAt W (X ⊞ Y) cXY),
        ∃ (p₁ : cXY.pt ⟶ cX.pt) (p₂ : cXY.pt ⟶ cY.pt),
          (∀ (a : W.Over ⊤ (X ⊞ Y)) (b : W.Over ⊤ X) (g : a.left ⟶ b.left),
            g ≫ b.hom = a.hom ≫ biprod.fst → p₁ ≫ cX.π.app b = cXY.π.app a ≫ F.map g) ∧
          (∀ (a : W.Over ⊤ (X ⊞ Y)) (b : W.Over ⊤ Y) (g : a.left ⟶ b.left),
            g ≫ b.hom = a.hom ≫ biprod.snd → p₂ ≫ cY.π.app b = cXY.π.app a ≫ F.map g) ∧
          IsIso (biprod.lift p₁ p₂)

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.Functor.isTriangulated_and_exists_leftDerivedFunctor
declarations.statement:
public theorem isTriangulated_and_exists_leftDerivedFunctor
    (F : C ⥤ H) [F.CommShift ℤ] [F.IsTriangulated]
    (W : MorphismProperty C) (hW : W.IsSaturated) [W.IsCompatibleWithTriangulation]
    (E : ObjectProperty C) (hE : ∀ X, E X ↔ ∃ c, F.IsLeftDerivedValueAt W X c)
    (L : C ⥤ D) [L.IsLocalization W] [L.CommShift ℤ] [L.Additive] :
    letI := hW.hasLeftCalculusOfFractions
    letI := Triangulated.Localization.pretriangulated L W
    -- (1) `E` is a strictly full triangulated subcategory of `C`
    ∃ (_ : E.IsClosedUnderIsomorphisms) (_ : E.IsTriangulated),
      -- (3) an element of `W` with source or target in `E` has both in `E`
      (∀ {X Y : C} (s : X ⟶ Y), W s → (E X ↔ E Y)) ∧
      -- (8) over a Karoubian target, `E` is saturated
      (IsIdempotentComplete H → E.IsSaturated) ∧
      -- (5) `S_E` is a saturated multiplicative system compatible with the triangulation
      ∃ (hSE : (W.inverseImage E.ι).IsSaturated)
        (_ : (W.inverseImage E.ι).IsCompatibleWithTriangulation)
        (LF : E.FullSubcategory ⥤ H) (_ : LF.CommShift ℤ)
        (π : ∀ X : E.FullSubcategory, (Functor.const (W.Over ⊤ X.obj)).obj (LF.obj X) ⟶
          MorphismProperty.Over.forget W ⊤ X.obj ⋙ Over.forget X.obj ⋙ F),
        -- (2) `LF : E ⥤ H` is exact
        LF.IsTriangulated ∧
        -- its value at `X` is a value of `LF` at `X` (Stacks 05S9(2))
        (∀ X : E.FullSubcategory,
          F.IsLeftDerivedValueAt W X.obj (Cone.mk (LF.obj X) (π X))) ∧
        -- and its action on morphisms is the map of Stacks 05SA(2)
        (∀ {X Y : E.FullSubcategory} (f : X ⟶ Y) (a : W.Over ⊤ X.obj) (b : W.Over ⊤ Y.obj)
          (g : a.left ⟶ b.left), a.hom ≫ E.ι.map f = g ≫ b.hom →
            LF.map f ≫ (π Y).app b = (π X).app a ≫ F.map g) ∧
        -- (4) `LF` inverts `S_E`
        (W.inverseImage E.ι).IsInvertedBy LF ∧
        letI := hSE.hasLeftCalculusOfFractions
        ∀ (EL : Type u₄) [Category.{v₄} EL] [HasZeroObject EL] [HasShift EL ℤ] [Preadditive EL]
          [∀ n : ℤ, (shiftFunctor EL n).Additive] (LE : E.FullSubcategory ⥤ EL)
          [LE.IsLocalization (W.inverseImage E.ι)] [LE.CommShift ℤ] [LE.Additive],
          letI := Triangulated.Localization.pretriangulated LE (W.inverseImage E.ι)
          -- (6) `S_E⁻¹E ⥤ W⁻¹C` is fully faithful and exact
          (∀ (Φ : EL ⥤ D) [Lifting LE (W.inverseImage E.ι) (E.ι ⋙ L) Φ],
            Φ.Full ∧ Φ.Faithful ∧
              (letI := Functor.commShiftOfLocalization LE (W.inverseImage E.ι) ℤ (E.ι ⋙ L) Φ;
                Φ.IsTriangulated)) ∧
            -- (7) `LF` factors through an exact functor `S_E⁻¹E ⥤ H`
            ∀ (LF' : EL ⥤ H) [Lifting LE (W.inverseImage E.ι) LF LF'],
              letI := Functor.commShiftOfLocalization LE (W.inverseImage E.ι) ℤ LF LF';
              LF'.IsTriangulated
declarations.comment: LF: items (1)-(8) for the subcategory on which the left derived functor is defined ('a similar result holds for LF'); the RF statement is isTriangulated_and_exists_rightDerivedFunctor

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.Functor.isTriangulated_and_exists_rightDerivedFunctor
declarations.statement:
public theorem isTriangulated_and_exists_rightDerivedFunctor
    (F : C ⥤ H) [F.CommShift ℤ] [F.IsTriangulated]
    (W : MorphismProperty C) (hW : W.IsSaturated) [W.IsCompatibleWithTriangulation]
    (E : ObjectProperty C) (hE : ∀ X, E X ↔ ∃ c, F.IsRightDerivedValueAt W X c)
    (L : C ⥤ D) [L.IsLocalization W] [L.CommShift ℤ] [L.Additive] :
    letI := hW.hasLeftCalculusOfFractions
    letI := Triangulated.Localization.pretriangulated L W
    -- (1) `E` is a strictly full triangulated subcategory of `C`
    ∃ (_ : E.IsClosedUnderIsomorphisms) (_ : E.IsTriangulated),
      -- (3) an element of `W` with source or target in `E` has both in `E`
      (∀ {X Y : C} (s : X ⟶ Y), W s → (E X ↔ E Y)) ∧
      -- (8) over a Karoubian target, `E` is saturated
      (IsIdempotentComplete H → E.IsSaturated) ∧
      -- (5) `S_E` is a saturated multiplicative system compatible with the triangulation
      ∃ (hSE : (W.inverseImage E.ι).IsSaturated)
        (_ : (W.inverseImage E.ι).IsCompatibleWithTriangulation)
        (RF : E.FullSubcategory ⥤ H) (_ : RF.CommShift ℤ)
        (ι : ∀ X : E.FullSubcategory, MorphismProperty.Under.forget W ⊤ X.obj ⋙
          Under.forget X.obj ⋙ F ⟶ (Functor.const (W.Under ⊤ X.obj)).obj (RF.obj X)),
        -- (2) `RF : E ⥤ H` is exact
        RF.IsTriangulated ∧
        -- its value at `X` is a value of `RF` at `X` (Stacks 05S9)
        (∀ X : E.FullSubcategory,
          F.IsRightDerivedValueAt W X.obj (Cocone.mk (RF.obj X) (ι X))) ∧
        -- and its action on morphisms is the map of Stacks 05SA
        (∀ {X Y : E.FullSubcategory} (f : X ⟶ Y) (a : W.Under ⊤ X.obj) (b : W.Under ⊤ Y.obj)
          (g : a.right ⟶ b.right), E.ι.map f ≫ b.hom = a.hom ≫ g →
            (ι X).app a ≫ RF.map f = F.map g ≫ (ι Y).app b) ∧
        -- (4) `RF` inverts `S_E`
        (W.inverseImage E.ι).IsInvertedBy RF ∧
        letI := hSE.hasLeftCalculusOfFractions
        ∀ (EL : Type u₄) [Category.{v₄} EL] [HasZeroObject EL] [HasShift EL ℤ] [Preadditive EL]
          [∀ n : ℤ, (shiftFunctor EL n).Additive] (LE : E.FullSubcategory ⥤ EL)
          [LE.IsLocalization (W.inverseImage E.ι)] [LE.CommShift ℤ] [LE.Additive],
          letI := Triangulated.Localization.pretriangulated LE (W.inverseImage E.ι)
          -- (6) `S_E⁻¹E ⥤ W⁻¹C` is fully faithful and exact
          (∀ (Φ : EL ⥤ D) [Lifting LE (W.inverseImage E.ι) (E.ι ⋙ L) Φ],
            Φ.Full ∧ Φ.Faithful ∧
              (letI := Functor.commShiftOfLocalization LE (W.inverseImage E.ι) ℤ (E.ι ⋙ L) Φ;
                Φ.IsTriangulated)) ∧
            -- (7) `RF` factors through an exact functor `S_E⁻¹E ⥤ H`
            ∀ (RF' : EL ⥤ H) [Lifting LE (W.inverseImage E.ι) RF RF'],
              letI := Functor.commShiftOfLocalization LE (W.inverseImage E.ι) ℤ RF RF';
              RF'.IsTriangulated
declarations.comment: RF: items (1)-(8) for the subcategory on which the right derived functor is defined; the LF statement is isTriangulated_and_exists_leftDerivedFunctor

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.Equivalence.mkOfIsos
declarations.doc:
Constructs an equivalence of categories from a fully faithful functor `F`, a family of objects
`j : D → C` and a family of isomorphisms `i : ∀ X, X ≅ F.obj (j X)`. The constructed equivalence
has an inverse that agrees with `j` on objects and a counit with components given by `i`.
This is similar to `F.asEquivalence`, but gives more control over the resulting equivalence.
declarations.statement:
def CategoryTheory.Equivalence.mkOfIsos {C D : Type*} [Category* C] [Category* D] (F : C ⥤ D)
    (hF : F.FullyFaithful) (j : D → C) (i : ∀ X, X ≅ F.obj (j X)) : C ≌ D

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.Equivalence.existsUnique_functor_of_isos
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 05SG.** Let `F : C ⥤ D` be fully faithful and, for every object `X` of `D`, let
`j X` be an object of `C` and `i X : X ≅ F.obj (j X)` an isomorphism. Then there is a unique
functor `G : D ⥤ C` such that `G` extends the rule `j` on objects (`h : ∀ X, G.obj X = j X`) and
the isomorphisms `i X` define an isomorphism of functors `α : 𝟭 D ≅ G ⋙ F` (the component of `α`
at `X` is `i X`, transported along `h X`). Moreover, any such `G` and `F` are quasi-inverse
equivalences of categories: there is an equivalence `e : C ≌ D` with `e.functor = F` and
`e.inverse = G`.
declarations.statement:
theorem existsUnique_functor_of_isos (F : C ⥤ D) (hF : F.FullyFaithful) (j : D → C)
    (i : ∀ X, X ≅ F.obj (j X)) :
    (∃! G : D ⥤ C, ∃ h : ∀ X, G.obj X = j X, ∃ α : 𝟭 D ≅ G ⋙ F,
        ∀ X, α.hom.app X = (i X).hom ≫ eqToHom (congrArg F.obj (h X).symm)) ∧
      ∀ G : D ⥤ C, (∃ h : ∀ X, G.obj X = j X, ∃ α : 𝟭 D ≅ G ⋙ F,
        ∀ X, α.hom.app X = (i X).hom ≫ eqToHom (congrArg F.obj (h X).symm)) →
        ∃ e : C ≌ D, e.functor = F ∧ e.inverse = G
declarations.comment:
existence and uniqueness of the functor `j` extending the rule on objects for
which the `i_X` form an isomorphism `id ≅ F ∘ j`, and that `j` and `F` are quasi-inverse
equivalences; the equivalence itself is `CategoryTheory.Equivalence.mkOfIsos`

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.EssentiallyConstantInd.IsEssentiallyConstantInd.comp
declarations.doc: (ind) Essential constancy is stable under postcomposition by any functor.
declarations.statement:
theorem comp {M : I ⥤ C} (h : IsEssentiallyConstantInd M) (F : C ⥤ D) :
    IsEssentiallyConstantInd (M ⋙ F)

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.EssentiallyConstantInd.IsEssentiallyConstantInd.op_comp
declarations.doc: (pro) Essential constancy as a pro-object is stable under postcomposition.
declarations.statement:
theorem op_comp {M : I ⥤ C} (h : IsEssentiallyConstantInd M.op) (F : C ⥤ D) :
    IsEssentiallyConstantInd (M ⋙ F).op

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.FilteredObject.isStrict_iff_isIso_coimageImageComparison
declarations.doc:
Stacks 05SI: a morphism `f : A ⟶ B` of filtered objects of an abelian category is strict if
and only if the canonical morphism `Coim(f) ⟶ Im(f)` of Stacks 0107, computed in `Fil(𝒜)`, is an
isomorphism. The comparison is always an isomorphism in `𝒜`; the content is that the quotient
filtration on `Coim(f)` and the induced filtration on `Im(f)` agree.
declarations.statement:
theorem isStrict_iff_isIso_coimageImageComparison (f : A ⟶ B) :
    IsStrict f ↔ IsIso (Abelian.coimageImageComparison f)
declarations.comment: for an arbitrary index category `I`

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.FilteredObject.isStrict_comp_iff_of_mono
declarations.doc:
Stacks 05SJ (2), as an equivalence: if `g : B ⟶ D` is a strict monomorphism, then `f ≫ g` is
strict if and only if `f` is. Indeed `g` preserves intersections, so
`g(f(F^iA)) = g(f(A)) ∩ F^iD` unwinds to `g(f(F^iA)) = g(f(A) ∩ F^iB)`, and `g` is injective on
subobjects. This holds in any category with images and pullbacks.
declarations.statement:
theorem isStrict_comp_iff_of_mono {D : FilteredObject C I} (f : A ⟶ B) (g : B ⟶ D) [IsStrict g]
    [Mono g.hom] : IsStrict (f ≫ g) ↔ IsStrict f
declarations.comment: (2) as an equivalence: for a strict monomorphism `g`, `f ≫ g` is strict iff `f` is

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.FilteredObject.IsStrict.comp_of_mono
declarations.doc:
Stacks 05SJ (2): the composite of two strict morphisms is strict when the second one is a
monomorphism.
declarations.statement:
instance IsStrict.comp_of_mono {D : FilteredObject C I} (f : A ⟶ B) (g : B ⟶ D) [IsStrict f]
    [IsStrict g] [Mono g.hom] : IsStrict (f ≫ g)
declarations.comment: (2): `g ∘ f` is strict for strict `f`, `g` with `g` a monomorphism

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.FilteredObject.isStrict_comp_iff_of_epi
declarations.doc:
Stacks 05SJ (3), as an equivalence: if `f : A ⟶ B` is a strict epimorphism, then `f ≫ g` is
strict if and only if `g` is. Indeed `f(F^iA) = F^iB` and `g(f(A)) = g(B)`. This holds in any
balanced category with images and pullbacks.
declarations.statement:
theorem isStrict_comp_iff_of_epi {D : FilteredObject C I} (f : A ⟶ B) (g : B ⟶ D) [IsStrict f]
    [Epi f.hom] : IsStrict (f ≫ g) ↔ IsStrict g
declarations.comment: (3) as an equivalence: for a strict epimorphism `f`, `f ≫ g` is strict iff `g` is

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.FilteredObject.IsStrict.comp_of_epi
declarations.doc:
Stacks 05SJ (3): the composite of two strict morphisms is strict when the first one is an
epimorphism.
declarations.statement:
instance IsStrict.comp_of_epi {D : FilteredObject C I} (f : A ⟶ B) (g : B ⟶ D) [IsStrict f]
    [IsStrict g] [Epi f.hom] : IsStrict (f ≫ g)
declarations.comment: (3): `g ∘ f` is strict for strict `f`, `g` with `f` an epimorphism

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.FilteredObject.isStrict_comp_stacks_05SJ
declarations.doc:
Stacks 05SJ. Let `𝒜` be an abelian category and let `f : A ⟶ B`, `g : B ⟶ D` be strict
morphisms of filtered objects. Then (1) in general `f ≫ g` is not strict: there are strict
morphisms of `ℤ`-filtered vector spaces over any field `k` whose composite is not strict;
(2) if `g` is a monomorphism, then `f ≫ g` is strict; (3) if `f` is an epimorphism, then
`f ≫ g` is strict.
declarations.statement:
theorem isStrict_comp_stacks_05SJ (k : Type u) [Field k] (I : Type*) [Category* I] :
    (∃ (A B D : FilteredObject (ModuleCat.{u} k) ℤᵒᵖ) (f : A ⟶ B) (g : B ⟶ D),
      IsStrict f ∧ IsStrict g ∧ ¬ IsStrict (f ≫ g)) ∧
    (∀ {A B D : FilteredObject C I} (f : A ⟶ B) (g : B ⟶ D), IsStrict f → IsStrict g →
      Mono g.hom → IsStrict (f ≫ g)) ∧
    (∀ {A B D : FilteredObject C I} (f : A ⟶ B) (g : B ⟶ D), IsStrict f → IsStrict g →
      Epi f.hom → IsStrict (f ≫ g))
declarations.comment: (1) a counterexample in `k`-vector spaces for any field `k`, and in any abelian category with a nonzero object (`exists_isStrict_not_isStrict_comp`); (2) `g ∘ f` is strict for `g` a monomorphism; (3) `g ∘ f` is strict for `f` an epimorphism

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.FilteredObject.IsStrict.biprod_lift
declarations.doc:
Stacks 05SK, strictness: if `f : A ⟶ B` is a strict monomorphism of filtered objects and
`g : A ⟶ D` is any morphism of filtered objects, then `(f, g) : A ⟶ B ⊕ D` is strict. For a
monomorphism, strictness is the cartesian condition (0124), which is stable under pairing
(`isStrictHom_biprod_lift`); this needs only preadditivity, binary biproducts, images and pullbacks
in `𝒜`.
declarations.statement:
instance IsStrict.biprod_lift (f : A ⟶ B) (g : A ⟶ D) [Mono f.hom] [IsStrict f] :
    IsStrict (biprod.lift f g)
declarations.comment: `(f, g)` is strict, for any additive `𝒜` with images and pullbacks and any `I`

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.FilteredObject.isStrict_and_mono_biprod_lift
declarations.doc:
Stacks 05SK: if `f : A ⟶ B` is a strict monomorphism of filtered objects and `g : A ⟶ D` is
any morphism of filtered objects, then `(f, g) : A ⟶ B ⊕ D` is a strict monomorphism.
declarations.statement:
theorem isStrict_and_mono_biprod_lift (f : A ⟶ B) (g : A ⟶ D) [Mono f.hom] [IsStrict f] :
    IsStrict (biprod.lift f g) ∧ Mono (biprod.lift f g)
declarations.comment: for any additive `𝒜` with images and pullbacks, and any index category `I`

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.FilteredObject.IsStrict.biprod_desc
declarations.doc:
Stacks 05SL, strictness: if `f : B ⟶ A` is a strict epimorphism of filtered objects and
`g : D ⟶ A` is any morphism of filtered objects, then `f ⊕ g : B ⊕ D ⟶ A` is strict. This needs
only a balanced additive `𝒜` with images and pullbacks.
declarations.statement:
instance IsStrict.biprod_desc {D : FilteredObject C I} (f : B ⟶ A) (g : D ⟶ A) [Epi f.hom]
    [IsStrict f] : IsStrict (biprod.desc f g)
declarations.comment: `f ⊕ g` is strict, for any balanced additive `𝒜` with images and pullbacks

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.FilteredObject.isStrict_and_epi_biprod_desc
declarations.doc:
Stacks 05SL: if `f : B ⟶ A` is a strict epimorphism of filtered objects and `g : D ⟶ A` is any
morphism of filtered objects, then `f ⊕ g : B ⊕ D ⟶ A` is a strict epimorphism.
declarations.statement:
theorem isStrict_and_epi_biprod_desc {D : FilteredObject C I} (f : B ⟶ A) (g : D ⟶ A) [Epi f.hom]
    [IsStrict f] : IsStrict (biprod.desc f g) ∧ Epi (biprod.desc f g)
declarations.comment: for any balanced additive `𝒜` with images and pullbacks, and any `I`

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.FilteredObject.isPushout_quot_map
declarations.doc:
Stacks 05SM, the pushout: `B ⊔_A D` exists in `Fil(𝒜)` (`hasFiniteColimits`) and its
quotients by the steps are computed level-wise,
`(B ⊔_A D)/F^i(B ⊔_A D) = B/F^iB ⊔_{A/F^iA} D/F^iD`, for any index category `I` and any additive
`𝒜` with cokernels and strong epi images. (The steps themselves are not computed level-wise:
`F^i(B ⊔_A D)` is the image of `F^iB ⊕ F^iD`.)
declarations.statement:
theorem isPushout_quot_map (i : I) :
    IsPushout ((quot i).map f) ((quot i).map g) ((quot i).map (pushout.inl f g))
      ((quot i).map (pushout.inr f g))
declarations.comment: the pushout is level-wise on the quotients by the steps, for any `I`

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.FilteredObject.hasFiniteColimits
declarations.doc: `Fil(𝒜)` has all finite colimits; in particular the pushouts of Stacks 05SM exist.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable instance hasFiniteColimits [HasCokernels C] [HasImages C] [HasStrongEpiImages C] :
    HasFiniteColimits (FilteredObject C I)
declarations.comment: the pushout exists, for any `I`, `𝒜` additive with cokernels and strong epi images

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.FilteredObject.isStrict_pushout_inr
declarations.doc:
Stacks 05SM: if `f : A ⟶ B` is strict, so is its cobase change `f' : D ⟶ B ⊔_A D` along
any `g : A ⟶ D`. On the quotient by the step `i`, `Ker(D/F^iD ⟶ (B ⊔_A D)/F^i) = g_i(Ker f_i)`
since the quotients of the pushout are computed level-wise and the kernel of a cobase change is
the image of the kernel; by strictness `Ker f_i` is the image of `Ker f` in `A/F^iA`, so this is
the image in `D/F^iD` of `g(Ker f) = Ker f'`, which is the strictness of `f'`.
declarations.statement: instance isStrict_pushout_inr [IsStrict f] : IsStrict (pushout.inr f g)
declarations.comment: if `f` is strict, so is its cobase change `f' : D ⟶ B ⊔_A D`, for any `I`

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.FilteredObject.isStrict_pushout_inl
declarations.doc:
Stacks 05SM, symmetrically: if `g : A ⟶ D` is strict, so is its cobase change
`g' : B ⟶ B ⊔_A D` along any `f : A ⟶ B`.
declarations.statement: instance isStrict_pushout_inl [IsStrict g] : IsStrict (pushout.inl f g)
declarations.comment: if `g` is strict, so is its cobase change `g' : B ⟶ B ⊔_A D`, for any `I`

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.FilteredObject.hasFiniteLimits
declarations.doc:
`Fil(𝒜)` has all finite limits when `𝒜` is preadditive with a zero object, binary
biproducts and kernels; in particular the fibre products of Stacks 05SN exist.
declarations.statement: noncomputable instance hasFiniteLimits [HasKernels C] : HasFiniteLimits (FilteredObject C I)
declarations.comment: the fibre product exists, for any `I` and any additive `𝒜` with kernels

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.FilteredObject.isPullback_natTrans_app
declarations.doc:
Stacks 05SN, the fibre product: `B ×_A D` exists in `Fil(𝒜)` (`hasFiniteLimits`) and its
filtration is computed level-wise, `F^i(B ×_A D) = F^iB ×_{F^iA} F^iD`, for any index category
`I` and any additive `𝒜` with kernels.
declarations.statement:
theorem isPullback_natTrans_app (i : I) :
    IsPullback ((pullback.fst f g).natTrans.app i) ((pullback.snd f g).natTrans.app i)
      (f.natTrans.app i) (g.natTrans.app i)
declarations.comment: the fibre product is level-wise, `F^i(B ×_A D) = F^iB ×_{F^iA} F^iD`, for any `I`

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.FilteredObject.isStrict_pullback_snd
declarations.doc:
Stacks 05SN: if `f : B ⟶ A` is strict, so is its base change `f' : B ×_A D ⟶ D` along any
`g : D ⟶ A`.
declarations.statement: instance isStrict_pullback_snd [IsStrict f] : IsStrict (pullback.snd f g)
declarations.comment: if `f` is strict, so is its base change `f' : B ×_A D ⟶ D`, for any `I`

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.FilteredObject.isStrict_pullback_fst
declarations.doc:
Stacks 05SN, symmetrically: if `g : D ⟶ A` is strict, so is its base change
`g' : B ×_A D ⟶ B` along any `f : B ⟶ A`.
declarations.statement: instance isStrict_pullback_fst [IsStrict g] : IsStrict (pullback.fst f g)
declarations.comment: if `g` is strict, so is its base change `g' : B ×_A D ⟶ B`, for any `I`

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.FilteredObject.shortExact_subQuotShortComplex_map_grMap
declarations.doc:
Stacks 05SP (1), general form: for a short exact sequence `0 → Y → A → Z → 0` of `𝒜` with `A`
filtered, `Y` carrying the induced filtration and `Z` the quotient filtration, the sequence
`0 → gr(Y) → gr(A) → gr(Z) → 0` of graded pieces along any index arrow is short exact.
declarations.statement:
theorem shortExact_subQuotShortComplex_map_grMap (hS : (ShortComplex.mk m e w).ShortExact)
    {i j : I} (f : i ⟶ j) :
    ((subQuotShortComplex A m e w).map (grMap f)).ShortExact
declarations.comment: (1), general: any short exact `0 → Y → A → Z → 0` of `𝒜`, `Y` induced, `Z` quotient

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.FilteredObject.shortExact_subQuotShortComplex_cokernel_map_grMap
declarations.doc:
Stacks 05SP (1), literally: for `X ⊆ A` with the induced filtration and `A/X` with the
quotient filtration, `0 → gr(X) → gr(A) → gr(A/X) → 0` is short exact, along any index arrow.
declarations.comment: (1) literally: `X ⊆ A` induced, `A/X` quotient, along any index arrow

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.FilteredObject.shortExact_map_grMap
declarations.doc:
Stacks 05SP (1), intrinsically in `Fil(𝒜)`: if `0 → X → A → Q → 0` is a short exact sequence
of `𝒜` whose two morphisms are strict morphisms of filtered objects (equivalently, `X` has the
induced and `Q` the quotient filtration, Stacks 0124), then `0 → gr(X) → gr(A) → gr(Q) → 0` is
short exact, along any index arrow.
declarations.statement:
theorem shortExact_map_grMap (hS : (S.map forget).ShortExact) [IsStrict S.f] [IsStrict S.g]
    {i j : I} (f : i ⟶ j) : (S.map (grMap f)).ShortExact
declarations.comment: (1) in `Fil(𝒜)`: a short exact sequence of `𝒜` with strict morphisms, any arrow

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.FilteredObject.shortExact_map_grMap_kernel_ι_coimage_π
declarations.doc:
Stacks 05SP (2), first sequence: `0 → gr(Ker f) → gr(A) → gr(Coim f) → 0` is short exact, for
any morphism `f` of filtered objects, on Mathlib's kernel and coimage computed in `Fil(𝒜)`.
declarations.statement:
theorem shortExact_map_grMap_kernel_ι_coimage_π {i j : I} (φ : i ⟶ j) :
    ((ShortComplex.mk (kernel.ι f) (Abelian.coimage.π f) (cokernel.condition _)).map
      (grMap φ)).ShortExact
declarations.comment: (2) `0 → gr(Ker f) → gr(A) → gr(Coim f) → 0`, any `f`, along any index arrow

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.FilteredObject.shortExact_map_grMap_image_ι_cokernel_π
declarations.doc:
Stacks 05SP (2), second sequence: `0 → gr(Im f) → gr(B) → gr(Coker f) → 0` is short exact, for
any morphism `f` of filtered objects, on Mathlib's image and cokernel computed in `Fil(𝒜)`.
declarations.statement:
theorem shortExact_map_grMap_image_ι_cokernel_π {i j : I} (φ : i ⟶ j) :
    ((ShortComplex.mk (Abelian.image.ι f) (cokernel.π f) (kernel.condition _)).map
      (grMap φ)).ShortExact
declarations.comment: (2) `0 → gr(Im f) → gr(B) → gr(Coker f) → 0`, any `f`, along any index arrow

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.Functor.DeltaFunctorStructure.isCohomologicalDeltaFunctor_comp_shift
declarations.doc:
A homological functor composed with a `δ`-functor is a cohomological `δ`-functor. Let
`G : 𝒜 ⥤ 𝒟` be a `δ`-functor from an abelian category to a pre-triangulated category, with
`δ`-functor structure `h`, let `H : 𝒟 ⥤ ℬ` be a homological functor into an abelian category, and
assume `H ⁻¹(G(A)) = 0` for every `A` in `𝒜`. Let `δ` be the connecting
morphism `H ⁿ(G(C)) ⟶ H ⁿ⁺¹(G(A))` that the long exact homology sequence of `H` attaches to the
image under `G` of a short exact sequence `0 ⟶ A ⟶ B ⟶ C ⟶ 0` of `𝒜`. Then
`{H ⁿ ∘ G, δ}_{n ≥ 0}` is a cohomological `δ`-functor from `𝒜` to `ℬ`: the functors `H ⁿ ∘ G`
are additive, the sequence
`0 ⟶ H ⁰(G(A)) ⟶ H ⁰(G(B)) ⟶ H ⁰(G(C)) ⟶ H ¹(G(A)) ⟶ H ¹(G(B)) ⟶ ⋯` is exact, and `δ` is
natural in the short exact sequence.
declarations.statement:
theorem isCohomologicalDeltaFunctor_comp_shift (h : DeltaFunctorStructure 𝒜 𝒟 G)
    (H : 𝒟 ⥤ ℬ) [H.IsHomological] [H.ShiftSequence ℤ]
    (hH : ∀ A : 𝒜, IsZero ((H.shift (-1 : ℤ)).obj (G.obj A)))
    (δ : ∀ {S : ShortComplex 𝒜}, S.ShortExact → ∀ n : ℕ,
      (G ⋙ H.shift (n : ℤ)).obj S.X₃ ⟶ (G ⋙ H.shift ((n : ℤ) + 1)).obj S.X₁)
    (hδ : ∀ {S : ShortComplex 𝒜} (hS : S.ShortExact) (n : ℕ), δ hS n =
      H.homologySequenceδ (Triangle.mk (G.map S.f) (G.map S.g) (h.δ hS)) n ((n : ℤ) + 1) rfl) :
    (∀ n : ℕ, (G ⋙ H.shift (n : ℤ)).Additive) ∧
    (∀ {S : ShortComplex 𝒜}, S.ShortExact → Mono ((G ⋙ H.shift (0 : ℤ)).map S.f)) ∧
    (∀ {S : ShortComplex 𝒜} (_ : S.ShortExact) (n : ℕ),
      ∃ hz : (G ⋙ H.shift (n : ℤ)).map S.f ≫ (G ⋙ H.shift (n : ℤ)).map S.g = 0,
        (ShortComplex.mk _ _ hz).Exact) ∧
    (∀ {S : ShortComplex 𝒜} (hS : S.ShortExact) (n : ℕ),
      ∃ hz : (G ⋙ H.shift (n : ℤ)).map S.g ≫ δ hS n = 0,
        (ShortComplex.mk _ _ hz).Exact) ∧
    (∀ {S : ShortComplex 𝒜} (hS : S.ShortExact) (n : ℕ),
      ∃ hz : δ hS n ≫ (G ⋙ H.shift ((n : ℤ) + 1)).map S.f = 0,
        (ShortComplex.mk _ _ hz).Exact) ∧
    (∀ {S S' : ShortComplex 𝒜} (hS : S.ShortExact) (hS' : S'.ShortExact) (φ : S ⟶ S') (n : ℕ),
      (G ⋙ H.shift (n : ℤ)).map φ.τ₃ ≫ δ hS' n =
        δ hS n ≫ (G ⋙ H.shift ((n : ℤ) + 1)).map φ.τ₁)

declarations.name: trianglehOfDegreewiseSplit_iso_of_identity
declarations.doc:
The triangles in `K(𝒜)` attached to two families of degreewise splittings of a short complex
`S` of cochain complexes are equal, so they are isomorphic by an isomorphism whose three
components are the identities of `Q.obj S.X₁`, `Q.obj S.X₂`, `Q.obj S.X₃`. Equality transports
express these identities between the canonically equal objects of the two triangles.
declarations.statement:
theorem trianglehOfDegreewiseSplit_iso_of_identity
    {C : Type*} [Category C] [Preadditive C]
    (S : ShortComplex (CochainComplex C ℤ))
    (σ σ' : (n : ℤ) → (S.map (HomologicalComplex.eval C (ComplexShape.up ℤ) n)).Splitting) :
    ∃ e : CochainComplex.trianglehOfDegreewiseSplit S σ ≅
          CochainComplex.trianglehOfDegreewiseSplit S σ',
      e.hom.hom₁ = eqToHom (by simp) ∧ e.hom.hom₂ = eqToHom (by simp) ∧
        e.hom.hom₃ = eqToHom (by simp)

declarations.name: StacksDerivedShift.rightDerived_definedAt_iff_shift
declarations.doc:
**Statement (1) — `RF` and shifts (definedness biconditional).**
`RF` is defined at `X` if and only if `RF` is defined at `X[n]`.
declarations.statement:
theorem rightDerived_definedAt_iff_shift (X : D) (n : ℤ) :
    (∃ c, F.IsRightDerivedValueAt S X c) ↔ ∃ c, F.IsRightDerivedValueAt S (X⟦n⟧) c

declarations.name: StacksDerivedShift.rightDerived_value_shift_iso
declarations.doc:
**Statement (1) — canonical isomorphism of values `RF(X)[n] ≅ RF(X[n])`.**
Given a value `c` of `RF` at `X` and a value `d` of `RF` at `X[n]`, this is the canonical
isomorphism `c.pt⟦n⟧ ≅ d.pt`, returned as genuine `Iso` *data*: `shiftCocone` exhibits
`c.pt⟦n⟧` as a value at `X[n]`, a value is a colimit cocone, and the isomorphism is the
comparison of the two colimit cocones.

declarations.name: StacksDerivedShift.leftDerived_definedAt_iff_shift
declarations.doc:
**Statement (2) — `LF` and shifts (definedness biconditional).**
`LF` is defined at `X` if and only if `LF` is defined at `X[n]`.
declarations.statement:
theorem leftDerived_definedAt_iff_shift (X : D) (n : ℤ) :
    (∃ c, F.IsLeftDerivedValueAt S X c) ↔ ∃ c, F.IsLeftDerivedValueAt S (X⟦n⟧) c

declarations.name: StacksDerivedShift.leftDerived_value_shift_iso
declarations.doc:
**Statement (2) — canonical isomorphism of values `LF(X)[n] ≅ LF(X[n])`.**
Given a value `c` of `LF` at `X` and a value `d` of `LF` at `X[n]`, this is the canonical
isomorphism `c.pt⟦n⟧ ≅ d.pt`: `shiftCone` exhibits `c.pt⟦n⟧` as a value at `X[n]`, a value is a
limit cone, and the isomorphism is the comparison of the two limit cones.

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.Functor.IsRightDerivable
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 05SV(1)**. `F` is *right derivable* with respect to `W`, equivalently the right
derived functor `RF` is *everywhere defined*: `RF` is defined at every object `X` of `𝒟`, i.e.
every `X` carries a cocone on the ind-object `X/W ⟶ 𝒟'`, `(s : X ⟶ X') ↦ F(X')` exhibiting its
vertex as a value `RF(X)` in the sense of `CategoryTheory.Functor.IsRightDerivedValueAt`.
declarations.statement: public abbrev IsRightDerivable (F : D ⥤ D') (W : MorphismProperty D) : Prop

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.Functor.IsLeftDerivable
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 05SV(2)**. `F` is *left derivable* with respect to `W`, equivalently the left
derived functor `LF` is *everywhere defined*: `LF` is defined at every object `X` of `𝒟`, i.e.
every `X` carries a cone on the pro-object `W/X ⟶ 𝒟'`, `(s : X' ⟶ X) ↦ F(X')` exhibiting its
vertex as a value `LF(X)` in the sense of `CategoryTheory.Functor.IsLeftDerivedValueAt`.
declarations.statement: public abbrev IsLeftDerivable (F : D ⥤ D') (W : MorphismProperty D) : Prop

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.Functor.hasRightDerivedFunctor_of_isRightDerivable
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 05SW**, existence of `RF`: a functor that is right derivable (Tag 05SV) relative to a
class of morphisms with a left calculus of fractions has a total right derived functor
`RF : W⁻¹𝒞 ⥤ ℋ`.
declarations.statement:
theorem hasRightDerivedFunctor_of_isRightDerivable [W.HasLeftCalculusOfFractions]
    (h : F.IsRightDerivable W) : F.HasRightDerivedFunctor W
declarations.comment: existence of `RF : S⁻¹𝒟 ⥤ 𝒟'` for a right derivable `F`

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.Functor.hasLeftDerivedFunctor_of_isLeftDerivable
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 05SW**, existence of `LF`: a functor that is left derivable (Tag 05SV) relative to a
class of morphisms with a right calculus of fractions has a total left derived functor
`LF : W⁻¹𝒞 ⥤ ℋ`.
declarations.statement:
theorem hasLeftDerivedFunctor_of_isLeftDerivable [W.HasRightCalculusOfFractions]
    (h : F.IsLeftDerivable W) : F.HasLeftDerivedFunctor W
declarations.comment: existence of `LF : S⁻¹𝒟 ⥤ 𝒟'` for a left derivable `F`

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.Functor.totalRightDerived_isTriangulated_and_isRightDerivedValueAt
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 05SW**, right derived functor. In Situation 05S8 — `F : 𝒞 ⥤ ℋ` an exact functor of
pre-triangulated categories, `W` a saturated multiplicative system compatible with the
triangulated structure — let `L : 𝒞 ⥤ 𝒟` be a localization functor for `W`, exact for a
pre-triangulated structure on `𝒟` (e.g. that of Tag 05R6). If `F` is right derivable
(Tag 05SV), the total right derived functor `RF = F.totalRightDerived L W : W⁻¹𝒞 ⥤ ℋ`, with
comparison `α = F.totalRightDerivedUnit L W : F ⟶ L ⋙ RF`, exists
(`Functor.hasRightDerivedFunctor_of_isRightDerivable`) and

1. `RF` is exact (Tag 05SE);
2. `RF` extends the pointwise `RF` of Tag 05S9 on objects: for every `X`, `RF(L(X))`, with the
   coprojections `F(X') ⟶ RF(L(X')) ≅ RF(L(X))` at `(s : X ⟶ X')`, is a value of `RF` at `X`;
3. `RF` extends it on morphisms: `RF(L(f))` is the morphism of Tag 05SA, i.e. a morphism
   `RF(L(X)) ⟶ RF(L(Y))` is compatible with the coprojections along every square
   `f ≫ t = s ≫ g` with `s`, `t` in `W` if and only if it is `RF(L(f))`.
declarations.statement:
theorem totalRightDerived_isTriangulated_and_isRightDerivedValueAt
    (F : C ⥤ H) [F.CommShift ℤ] [F.IsTriangulated]
    (W : MorphismProperty C) (hW : W.IsSaturated) [W.IsCompatibleWithTriangulation]
    (L : C ⥤ D) [L.IsLocalization W] [L.CommShift ℤ] [L.IsTriangulated]
    (h : F.IsRightDerivable W) :
    haveI := hW.hasLeftCalculusOfFractions
    haveI := F.hasRightDerivedFunctor_of_isRightDerivable W h
    (F.totalRightDerived L W).IsTriangulated ∧
      (∀ X : C, F.IsRightDerivedValueAt W X
        (derivedUnitCocone F W L (F.totalRightDerived L W) (F.totalRightDerivedUnit L W) X)) ∧
      ∀ {X Y : C} (f : X ⟶ Y)
        (u : (F.totalRightDerived L W).obj (L.obj X) ⟶ (F.totalRightDerived L W).obj (L.obj Y)),
        (∀ (s : W.Under ⊤ X) (t : W.Under ⊤ Y) (g : s.right ⟶ t.right),
          f ≫ t.hom = s.hom ≫ g →
            (derivedUnitCocone F W L (F.totalRightDerived L W)
                (F.totalRightDerivedUnit L W) X).ι.app s ≫ u =
              F.map g ≫ (derivedUnitCocone F W L (F.totalRightDerived L W)
                (F.totalRightDerivedUnit L W) Y).ι.app t) ↔
          u = (L ⋙ F.totalRightDerived L W).map f
declarations.comment:
right derived functor `RF : S⁻¹𝒟 ⥤ 𝒟'`: exact, value at `X` the essentially
constant ind-object, `RF(f)` the map of 05SA

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.Functor.totalLeftDerived_isTriangulated_and_isLeftDerivedValueAt
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 05SW**, left derived functor. In Situation 05S8, with `L : 𝒞 ⥤ 𝒟` an exact
localization functor for `W`, if `F` is left derivable (Tag 05SV), the total left derived functor
`LF = F.totalLeftDerived L W : W⁻¹𝒞 ⥤ ℋ`, with comparison
`α = F.totalLeftDerivedCounit L W : L ⋙ LF ⟶ F`, exists
(`Functor.hasLeftDerivedFunctor_of_isLeftDerivable`) and, for the commutation with the shift of
`StacksDraft.PseudoCoherence.leftDerivedCommShift`,

1. `LF` is exact (Tag 05SE);
2. `LF` extends the pointwise `LF` of Tag 05S9 on objects: for every `X`, `LF(L(X))`, with the
   projections `LF(L(X)) ≅ LF(L(X')) ⟶ F(X')` at `(s : X' ⟶ X)`, is a value of `LF` at `X`;
3. `LF` extends it on morphisms: a morphism `LF(L(X)) ⟶ LF(L(Y))` is compatible with the
   projections along every square `s ≫ f = g ≫ t` with `s`, `t` in `W` if and only if it is
   `LF(L(f))` (Tag 05SA).
declarations.statement:
theorem totalLeftDerived_isTriangulated_and_isLeftDerivedValueAt
    (F : C ⥤ H) [F.CommShift ℤ] [F.IsTriangulated]
    (W : MorphismProperty C) (hW : W.IsSaturated) [W.IsCompatibleWithTriangulation]
    (L : C ⥤ D) [L.IsLocalization W] [L.CommShift ℤ] [L.IsTriangulated]
    (h : F.IsLeftDerivable W) :
    haveI := hW.hasRightCalculusOfFractions
    haveI := F.hasLeftDerivedFunctor_of_isLeftDerivable W h
    letI := StacksDraft.PseudoCoherence.leftDerivedCommShift (F.totalLeftDerived L W)
      (F.totalLeftDerivedCounit L W) W ℤ
    (F.totalLeftDerived L W).IsTriangulated ∧
      (∀ X : C, F.IsLeftDerivedValueAt W X
        (derivedCounitCone F W L (F.totalLeftDerived L W) (F.totalLeftDerivedCounit L W) X)) ∧
      ∀ {X Y : C} (f : X ⟶ Y)
        (u : (F.totalLeftDerived L W).obj (L.obj X) ⟶ (F.totalLeftDerived L W).obj (L.obj Y)),
        (∀ (s : W.Over ⊤ X) (t : W.Over ⊤ Y) (g : s.left ⟶ t.left),
          s.hom ≫ f = g ≫ t.hom →
            u ≫ (derivedCounitCone F W L (F.totalLeftDerived L W)
                (F.totalLeftDerivedCounit L W) Y).π.app t =
              (derivedCounitCone F W L (F.totalLeftDerived L W)
                (F.totalLeftDerivedCounit L W) X).π.app s ≫ F.map g) ↔
          u = (L ⋙ F.totalLeftDerived L W).map f
declarations.comment:
left derived functor `LF : S⁻¹𝒟 ⥤ 𝒟'`: exact, value at `X` the essentially
constant pro-object, `LF(f)` the map of 05SA

registrations.name: CategoryTheory.Functor.totalRightDerived
registrations.comment:
the functor RF : S⁻¹D ⥤ D' itself: Mathlib's total right derived functor, a
  left Kan extension along the localization, defined under `HasRightDerivedFunctor` rather than
  under 05SV derivability; for a right derivable F it exists and is the source's RF
  (`CategoryTheory.Functor.hasRightDerivedFunctor_of_isRightDerivable` and
  `CategoryTheory.Functor.totalRightDerived_isTriangulated_and_isRightDerivedValueAt`)

registrations.name: CategoryTheory.Functor.totalLeftDerived
registrations.comment:
the functor LF : S⁻¹D ⥤ D' itself: Mathlib's total left derived functor, a
  right Kan extension along the localization, defined under `HasLeftDerivedFunctor` rather than
  under 05SV derivability; for a left derivable F it exists and is the source's LF
  (`CategoryTheory.Functor.hasLeftDerivedFunctor_of_isLeftDerivable` and
  `CategoryTheory.Functor.totalLeftDerived_isTriangulated_and_isLeftDerivedValueAt`)

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.Functor.ComputesRightDerived
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 05SX(1)**. The object `X` of `𝒟` *computes* the right derived functor `RF` of
`F : 𝒟 ⥤ 𝒟'` relative to `W`: the right derived functor is defined at `X`, i.e. some cocone `c`
on the ind-object `X/W ⟶ 𝒟'`, `(s : X ⟶ X') ↦ F(X')` exhibits its vertex as a value `RF(X)`, and
the canonical map `F(X) ⟶ RF(X)` — the coprojection of `c` at the index `𝟙 X` — is an
isomorphism.
declarations.statement:
public abbrev ComputesRightDerived (F : D ⥤ D') (W : MorphismProperty D)
    [W.ContainsIdentities] (X : D) : Prop

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.Functor.ComputesLeftDerived
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 05SX(2)**. The object `X` of `𝒟` *computes* the left derived functor `LF` of
`F : 𝒟 ⥤ 𝒟'` relative to `W`: the left derived functor is defined at `X`, i.e. some cone `c` on
the pro-object `W/X ⟶ 𝒟'`, `(s : X' ⟶ X) ↦ F(X')` exhibits its vertex as a value `LF(X)`, and
the canonical map `LF(X) ⟶ F(X)` — the projection of `c` at the index `𝟙 X` — is an
isomorphism.
declarations.statement:
public abbrev ComputesLeftDerived (F : D ⥤ D') (W : MorphismProperty D)
    [W.ContainsIdentities] (X : D) : Prop

declarations.name: Stacks.DerivedFunctor.Shift.Situation.computesRightDerived_shift_iff
declarations.doc:
Stacks 13.14.11(1), Tag 05SY: `X` computes `RF` if and only if `X⟦n⟧` computes `RF`.

The shift restricts to an equivalence `rightShiftEquiv` of the index categories, under which the
ind-object at `X⟦n⟧` is the ind-object at `X` followed by `⟦n⟧` (`rightDiagramShiftIso`) and the
index `𝟙 (X⟦n⟧)` corresponds to `𝟙 X`; essential constancy and invertibility of the canonical map
are carried across. The converse applies this to `X⟦n⟧` and `-n` and uses
`computesRightDerived_of_iso` along `X⟦n⟧⟦-n⟧ ≅ X`.
declarations.statement:
theorem computesRightDerived_shift_iff (X : sit.D) (n : ℤ) :
    sit.F.ComputesRightDerived sit.S X ↔ sit.F.ComputesRightDerived sit.S (X⟦n⟧)

declarations.name: Stacks.DerivedFunctor.Shift.Situation.computesLeftDerived_shift_iff
declarations.doc:
Stacks 13.14.11(2), Tag 05SY: `X` computes `LF` if and only if `X⟦n⟧` computes `LF`.
Dual to `computesRightDerived_shift_iff`.
declarations.statement:
theorem computesLeftDerived_shift_iff (X : sit.D) (n : ℤ) :
    sit.F.ComputesLeftDerived sit.S X ↔ sit.F.ComputesLeftDerived sit.S (X⟦n⟧)

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.Functor.computesRightDerived_and_computesLeftDerived_of_distTriang
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 05SZ**. Let `F : 𝒟 ⥤ 𝒟'` be an exact functor of pretriangulated categories and let
`W` be a saturated multiplicative system in `𝒟` (Stacks 05Q8) compatible with the triangulation.
Let `T = (X, Y, Z, f, g, h)` be a distinguished triangle of `𝒟`.

If two of the three objects `X`, `Y`, `Z` compute the right derived functor `RF` — that is, `RF` is
defined at each of them and the canonical map `F(-) ⟶ RF(-)` is an isomorphism there (Stacks 05SX)
— then the third computes `RF` as well. Similarly for the left derived functor `LF`.

The source states only the case where `X` and `Y` are assumed to compute; the other two positions
are asserted as well because its applications use them (see the module docstring).
declarations.statement:
public theorem computesRightDerived_and_computesLeftDerived_of_distTriang (F : C ⥤ H)
    [F.CommShift ℤ] [F.IsTriangulated] (W : MorphismProperty C) [W.ContainsIdentities]
    (hW : W.IsSaturated) [W.IsCompatibleWithTriangulation]
    (T : Triangle C) (hT : T ∈ distTriang C) :
    (F.ComputesRightDerived W T.obj₁ → F.ComputesRightDerived W T.obj₂ →
        F.ComputesRightDerived W T.obj₃) ∧
      (F.ComputesRightDerived W T.obj₂ → F.ComputesRightDerived W T.obj₃ →
        F.ComputesRightDerived W T.obj₁) ∧
      (F.ComputesRightDerived W T.obj₃ → F.ComputesRightDerived W T.obj₁ →
        F.ComputesRightDerived W T.obj₂) ∧
      (F.ComputesLeftDerived W T.obj₁ → F.ComputesLeftDerived W T.obj₂ →
        F.ComputesLeftDerived W T.obj₃) ∧
      (F.ComputesLeftDerived W T.obj₂ → F.ComputesLeftDerived W T.obj₃ →
        F.ComputesLeftDerived W T.obj₁) ∧
      (F.ComputesLeftDerived W T.obj₃ → F.ComputesLeftDerived W T.obj₁ →
        F.ComputesLeftDerived W T.obj₂)

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.Functor.computesRightDerived_and_computesLeftDerived_of_biprod
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 05T0**. Let `F : 𝒟 ⥤ 𝒟'` be an additive functor of preadditive categories, `𝒟`
having binary biproducts, and let `W` be a saturated multiplicative system in `𝒟` (Stacks 05Q8).
Let `X` and `Y` be objects of `𝒟`. If the direct sum `X ⊞ Y` computes the right derived functor
`RF` — that is, `RF` is defined at `X ⊞ Y` and the canonical map `F(X ⊞ Y) ⟶ RF(X ⊞ Y)` is an
isomorphism (Stacks 05SX) — then `X` and `Y` compute `RF`. Similarly, if `X ⊞ Y` computes `LF`,
then `X` and `Y` compute `LF`.

Situation 05S8's triangulated hypotheses are not needed; see the module docstring.
declarations.statement:
public theorem computesRightDerived_and_computesLeftDerived_of_biprod (F : C ⥤ H) [F.Additive]
    (W : MorphismProperty C) [W.ContainsIdentities] (hW : W.IsSaturated) (X Y : C) :
    (F.ComputesRightDerived W (X ⊞ Y) →
        F.ComputesRightDerived W X ∧ F.ComputesRightDerived W Y) ∧
      (F.ComputesLeftDerived W (X ⊞ Y) →
        F.ComputesLeftDerived W X ∧ F.ComputesLeftDerived W Y)

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.Functor.isRightDerivable_and_isLeftDerivable_of_forall_exists_isDerivedValueAt
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 05T1**. Let `F : 𝒟 ⥤ 𝒟'` be a functor and let `W` be a class of morphisms of `𝒟`.

1. If `W` has a left calculus of fractions and if for every object `X` of `𝒟` there is a
   morphism `s : X ⟶ X'` in `W` such that the right derived functor `RF` is defined at `X'`,
   then `RF` is everywhere defined, i.e. `F` is right derivable.
2. If `W` has a right calculus of fractions and if for every object `X` of `𝒟` there is a
   morphism `s : X' ⟶ X` in `W` such that the left derived functor `LF` is defined at `X'`,
   then `LF` is everywhere defined, i.e. `F` is left derivable.

Definedness and values are those of Stacks 05S9, and everywhere-definedness that of Stacks 05SV.
The source assumes the stronger hypothesis that `X'` *computes* `RF`, resp. `LF` (Stacks 05SX),
and works in Situation 05S8; the canonical map `F(X') ⟶ RF(X')` plays no role and neither does
the triangulated structure, only the relevant calculus of fractions on `W`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem isRightDerivable_and_isLeftDerivable_of_forall_exists_isDerivedValueAt
    (F : D ⥤ D') (W : MorphismProperty D) :
    (W.HasLeftCalculusOfFractions →
        (∀ X : D, ∃ (X' : D) (s : X ⟶ X'), W s ∧ ∃ c, F.IsRightDerivedValueAt W X' c) →
        F.IsRightDerivable W) ∧
      (W.HasRightCalculusOfFractions →
        (∀ X : D, ∃ (X' : D) (s : X' ⟶ X), W s ∧ ∃ c, F.IsLeftDerivedValueAt W X' c) →
        F.IsLeftDerivable W)

declarations.name: DerivedFunctorComposition.exists_rightDerived_comparison
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Lemma 13.14.16, Statement 1 (Tag 05T2).**
Assume the data of Definition 4 and that the right derived functors `RF'`, `RG`
and `R(G∘F)` are everywhere defined.  Then there exists a natural transformation
`t : R(G∘F) ⟶ RG ∘ RF'` of functors `S⁻¹A ⥤ C` which is characterized at each
object `Q_A X` by the concrete composite of Tag 05T2: precomposing the component
`t_{Q_A X}` with the structure map `αGF.app X : (G∘F)(X) ⟶ R(G∘F)(Q_A X)` yields
the canonical map `G(F X) ⟶ RG(Q_B(F X))` followed by `RG` applied to the
structure map `αFp.app X` of `RF'`.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_rightDerived_comparison
    [RFp.IsRightDerivedFunctor αFp S] [RG.IsRightDerivedFunctor αG S']
    [RGF.IsRightDerivedFunctor αGF S] :
    ∃ t : RGF ⟶ RFp ⋙ RG,
      ∀ X : A, αGF.app X ≫ t.app (QA.obj X) = αG.app (F.obj X) ≫ RG.map (αFp.app X)

declarations.name: DerivedFunctorComposition.exists_leftDerived_comparison
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Lemma 13.14.16, Statement 2 (Tag 05T2).**
Dually to Statement 1: assume the data of Definition 4 and that the left derived
functors `LF'`, `LG` and `L(G∘F)` are everywhere defined.  Then there exists a
natural transformation `t : LG ∘ LF' ⟶ L(G∘F)` of functors `S⁻¹A ⥤ C`,
characterized at each object `Q_A X` by the concrete dual composite of Tag 05T2:
postcomposing the component `t_{Q_A X}` with the structure map
`βGF.app X : L(G∘F)(Q_A X) ⟶ (G∘F)(X)` yields `LG` applied to the structure map
`βFp.app X` of `LF'` followed by the canonical map `LG(Q_B(F X)) ⟶ G(F X)`.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_leftDerived_comparison
    [LFp.IsLeftDerivedFunctor βFp S] [LG.IsLeftDerivedFunctor βG S']
    [LGF.IsLeftDerivedFunctor βGF S] :
    ∃ t : LFp ⋙ LG ⟶ LGF,
      ∀ X : A, t.app (QA.obj X) ≫ βGF.app X = LG.map (βFp.app X) ≫ βG.app (F.obj X)

declarations.name: StacksDerivedFunctorComparison.definedAtR_big_iff_plus
declarations.doc:
**Statement (1), "defined at".** For `X` an object of `K⁺(A)`, the right derived functor of
`F : K(A) ⥤ D(B)` is defined at `X` (viewed in `K(A)` via `ι`) if and only if the right derived
functor of `F⁺ : K⁺(A) ⥤ D⁺(B)` is defined at `X`.
declarations.statement:
theorem definedAtR_big_iff_plus (X : HomotopyCategory.Plus A) :
    (∃ c, (Fbig F).IsRightDerivedValueAt (qisBig A) ((HomotopyCategory.Plus.ι A).obj X) c) ↔
      ∃ c, (Fplus F).IsRightDerivedValueAt (qisPlus A) X c

declarations.name: StacksDerivedFunctorComparison.valueR_big_iso_plus
declarations.doc:
**Statement (1), values.** When the right derived functors of `F : K(A) ⥤ D(B)` and of
`F⁺ : K⁺(A) ⥤ D⁺(B)` are defined at `X`, with values `cbig.pt` and `cplus.pt`, the values are
canonically isomorphic in `D(B)` via the embedding `D⁺(B) ↪ D(B)`: there is an isomorphism
`RF(X) ≅ ι(RF⁺(X))` compatible with the structure maps `F(X') ⟶ RF(X)` and `F⁺(X') ⟶ RF⁺(X)` of
every `s : X ⟶ X'` in `Qis⁺(A)`, in particular with the canonical maps at `𝟙 X`.
declarations.statement:
theorem valueR_big_iso_plus (X : HomotopyCategory.Plus A)
    {cbig : Cocone (MorphismProperty.Under.forget (qisBig A) ⊤ ((HomotopyCategory.Plus.ι A).obj X) ⋙
      Under.forget _ ⋙ Fbig F)}
    (hbig : (Fbig F).IsRightDerivedValueAt (qisBig A) ((HomotopyCategory.Plus.ι A).obj X) cbig)
    {cplus : Cocone (MorphismProperty.Under.forget (qisPlus A) ⊤ X ⋙ Under.forget X ⋙ Fplus F)}
    (hplus : (Fplus F).IsRightDerivedValueAt (qisPlus A) X cplus) :
    ∃ e : cbig.pt ≅ (Dplus.ι B).obj cplus.pt,
      ∀ s : (qisPlus A).Under ⊤ X,
        cbig.ι.app (MorphismProperty.Under.mk ⊤ ((HomotopyCategory.Plus.ι A).map s.hom) s.prop) ≫
          e.hom = (Dplus.ι B).map (cplus.ι.app s)
declarations.comment: (1), values

declarations.name: StacksDerivedFunctorComparison.computesR_big_iff_plus
declarations.doc:
**Statement (2).** For `X` an object of `K⁺(A)`, `X` computes the right derived functor of
`F : K(A) ⥤ D(B)` (viewed in `K(A)`) if and only if `X` computes the right derived functor of
`F⁺ : K⁺(A) ⥤ D⁺(B)`.
declarations.statement:
theorem computesR_big_iff_plus (X : HomotopyCategory.Plus A) :
    (Fbig F).ComputesRightDerived (qisBig A) ((HomotopyCategory.Plus.ι A).obj X) ↔
      (Fplus F).ComputesRightDerived (qisPlus A) X

declarations.name: StacksDerivedFunctorComparison.definedAtL_big_iff_minus
declarations.doc:
**Statement (3), "defined at".** For `X` an object of `K⁻(A)`, the left derived functor of
`F : K(A) ⥤ D(B)` is defined at `X` (viewed in `K(A)` via `ι`) if and only if the left derived
functor of `F⁻ : K⁻(A) ⥤ D⁻(B)` is defined at `X`.
declarations.statement:
theorem definedAtL_big_iff_minus (X : KMinus A) :
    (∃ c, (Fbig F).IsLeftDerivedValueAt (qisBig A) ((KMinus.ι A).obj X) c) ↔
      ∃ c, (Fminus F).IsLeftDerivedValueAt (qisMinus A) X c

declarations.name: StacksDerivedFunctorComparison.valueL_big_iso_minus
declarations.doc:
**Statement (3), values.** When the left derived functors of `F : K(A) ⥤ D(B)` and of
`F⁻ : K⁻(A) ⥤ D⁻(B)` are defined at `X`, with values `cbig.pt` and `cminus.pt`, the values are
canonically isomorphic in `D(B)` via the embedding `D⁻(B) ↪ D(B)`, compatibly with the structure
maps `LF(X) ⟶ F(X')` and `LF⁻(X) ⟶ F⁻(X')` of every `s : X' ⟶ X` in `Qis⁻(A)`, in particular
with the canonical maps at `𝟙 X`.
declarations.statement:
theorem valueL_big_iso_minus (X : KMinus A)
    {cbig : Cone (MorphismProperty.Over.forget (qisBig A) ⊤ ((KMinus.ι A).obj X) ⋙
      Over.forget _ ⋙ Fbig F)}
    (hbig : (Fbig F).IsLeftDerivedValueAt (qisBig A) ((KMinus.ι A).obj X) cbig)
    {cminus : Cone (MorphismProperty.Over.forget (qisMinus A) ⊤ X ⋙ Over.forget X ⋙ Fminus F)}
    (hminus : (Fminus F).IsLeftDerivedValueAt (qisMinus A) X cminus) :
    ∃ e : cbig.pt ≅ (Dminus.ι B).obj cminus.pt,
      ∀ s : (qisMinus A).Over ⊤ X,
        e.hom ≫ (Dminus.ι B).map (cminus.π.app s) =
          cbig.π.app (MorphismProperty.Over.mk ⊤ ((KMinus.ι A).map s.hom) s.prop)
declarations.comment: (3), values

declarations.name: StacksDerivedFunctorComparison.computesL_big_iff_minus
declarations.doc:
**Statement (4).** For `X` an object of `K⁻(A)`, `X` computes the left derived functor of
`F : K(A) ⥤ D(B)` (viewed in `K(A)`) if and only if `X` computes the left derived functor of
`F⁻ : K⁻(A) ⥤ D⁻(B)`.
declarations.statement:
theorem computesL_big_iff_minus (X : KMinus A) :
    (Fbig F).ComputesLeftDerived (qisBig A) ((KMinus.ι A).obj X) ↔
      (Fminus F).ComputesLeftDerived (qisMinus A) X

declarations.name: CochainComplex.exists_quasiIso_prop_isStrictlyGE
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 05T6.** Let `A` be an abelian category, let `P` be a class of objects of `A`
containing a zero object and such that every object of `A` is a subobject of an object
satisfying `P`, and let `a : ℤ`. Let `K` be a cochain complex with `H ^ n (K) = 0` for `n < a`.
Then there is a quasi-isomorphism `f : K ⟶ L` with all `L.X n` satisfying `P` and `L.X n = 0`
for `n < a`; and if moreover `K.X n = 0` for `n < a`, then `f` can be chosen with all `f.f n`
monomorphisms. (Part (2) of the source is the statement with the last clause dropped, part (1)
is the statement for a strictly bounded below `K`.)
declarations.statement:
public theorem exists_quasiIso_prop_isStrictlyGE (P : ObjectProperty A) [P.ContainsZero]
    (hP : ∀ X : A, ∃ (Y : A) (_ : P Y) (i : X ⟶ Y), Mono i) (a : ℤ)
    (K : CochainComplex A ℤ) [K.IsGE a] :
    ∃ (L : CochainComplex A ℤ) (f : K ⟶ L) (_ : QuasiIso f) (_ : ∀ n, P (L.X n))
      (_ : K.IsStrictlyGE a → ∀ n, Mono (f.f n)), L.IsStrictlyGE a

declarations.name: CochainComplex.exists_quasiIso_prop
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 05T7.** Let `A` be an abelian category, let `P` be a class of
objects of `A` containing a zero object and such that every object of `A` is a
quotient of an object satisfying `P`, and let `a : ℤ`.
(1) If `K.X n = 0` for `n > a`, there is a quasi-isomorphism `f : L ⟶ K` with
all `f.f n` epimorphisms, all `L.X n` satisfying `P`, and `L.X n = 0` for
`n > a`.
(2) If `H ^ n (K) = 0` for `n > a`, there is a quasi-isomorphism `f : L ⟶ K`
with all `L.X n` satisfying `P` and `L.X n = 0` for `n > a`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem exists_quasiIso_prop (P : ObjectProperty A)
    [P.ContainsZero] (hP : ∀ X : A, ∃ (Y : A) (_ : P Y) (p : Y ⟶ X), Epi p) (a : ℤ) :
    (∀ (K : CochainComplex A ℤ) [K.IsStrictlyLE a],
        ∃ (L : CochainComplex A ℤ) (f : L ⟶ K) (_ : ∀ n, Epi (f.f n)) (_ : QuasiIso f)
          (_ : ∀ n, P (L.X n)), L.IsStrictlyLE a) ∧
      (∀ (K : CochainComplex A ℤ) [K.IsLE a],
        ∃ (L : CochainComplex A ℤ) (f : L ⟶ K) (_ : QuasiIso f) (_ : ∀ n, P (L.X n)),
          L.IsStrictlyLE a)

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.Functor.hasPointwiseRightDerivedFunctor_and_le_rightAcyclic
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 05T8.** Let `F : C ⥤ D` be an additive functor between abelian categories and let
`I` be a class of objects of `C` such that every object of `C` is a subobject of an object
satisfying `I`, and such that for every short exact sequence `0 ⟶ P ⟶ Q ⟶ R ⟶ 0` with `P` and
`Q` satisfying `I` the object `R` satisfies `I` and `0 ⟶ F P ⟶ F Q ⟶ F R ⟶ 0` is short exact.
Then the pointwise right derived functor exists on `K⁺(C)`, and every object satisfying `I`
is acyclic for it.
declarations.statement:
public theorem hasPointwiseRightDerivedFunctor_and_le_rightAcyclic
    (F : C ⥤ D) [F.Additive] (I : ObjectProperty C)
    (hI₁ : ∀ X : C, ∃ (Y : C) (_ : I Y) (i : X ⟶ Y), Mono i)
    (hI₂ : ∀ S : ShortComplex C, S.ShortExact → I S.X₁ → I S.X₂ →
      I S.X₃ ∧ (S.map F).ShortExact) :
    ∃ h : (F.mapHomotopyCategoryPlus ⋙ DerivedCategory.Plus.Qh).HasPointwiseRightDerivedFunctor
        (HomotopyCategory.Plus.quasiIso C),
      letI := h
      I ≤ F.rightAcyclic
declarations.comment:
The right derived functor `RF` is defined everywhere on `K⁺(C)`, and every
  object of `I` is acyclic for it.

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.Functor.le_rightAcyclic
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 05T8.** Let `F : C ⥤ D` be an additive functor between abelian categories whose
right derived functor `RF : D⁺(C) ⥤ D⁺(D)` exists, and let `I` be a class of objects of `C` such
that every object of `C` is a subobject of an object satisfying `I`, and such that for every short
exact sequence `0 ⟶ P ⟶ Q ⟶ R ⟶ 0` with `P` and `Q` satisfying `I` the object `R` satisfies `I`
and `0 ⟶ F P ⟶ F Q ⟶ F R ⟶ 0` is short exact. Then every object satisfying `I` is acyclic for
`RF`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem le_rightAcyclic (F : C ⥤ D) [F.Additive]
    [(F.mapHomotopyCategoryPlus ⋙ DerivedCategory.Plus.Qh).HasRightDerivedFunctor
      (HomotopyCategory.Plus.quasiIso C)] (I : ObjectProperty C)
    (hI₁ : ∀ X : C, ∃ (Y : C) (_ : I Y) (i : X ⟶ Y), Mono i)
    (hI₂ : ∀ S : ShortComplex C, S.ShortExact → I S.X₁ → I S.X₂ →
      I S.X₃ ∧ (S.map F).ShortExact) :
    I ≤ F.rightAcyclic

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.Functor.RightAcyclicCriterion.map_quasiIso_nat
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 05T8 for `ℕ`-indexed complexes.** Let `F : C ⥤ D` be an additive functor between
abelian categories and let `I` be a class of objects of `C` adapted to `F` in the sense of
[Stacks 05T8]. Then `F` carries a quasi-isomorphism of cochain complexes indexed by `ℕ` whose
terms satisfy `I` to a quasi-isomorphism.

This is `CategoryTheory.Functor.RightAcyclicCriterion.map_quasiIso` transported along extension by
zero. The boundedness hypotheses of that statement are automatic here, an `ℕ`-indexed complex
being concentrated in the degrees `≥ 0`.
declarations.statement:
lemma map_quasiIso_nat (F : C ⥤ D) [F.Additive] (I : ObjectProperty C)
    (hI₁ : ∀ X : C, ∃ (Y : C) (_ : I Y) (i : X ⟶ Y), Mono i)
    (hI₂ : ∀ S : ShortComplex C, S.ShortExact → I S.X₁ → I S.X₂ →
      I S.X₃ ∧ (S.map F).ShortExact)
    {K L : CochainComplex C ℕ} (f : K ⟶ L) [QuasiIso f]
    (hIK : ∀ n, I (K.X n)) (hIL : ∀ n, I (L.X n)) :
    QuasiIso ((F.mapHomologicalComplex (ComplexShape.up ℕ)).map f)
declarations.comment: the quasi-isomorphism half, for `ℕ`-indexed complexes

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.InjectiveResolution.isIso_homologyMap_map_of_desc
declarations.doc:
**Right derived functors are computed by any resolution by `F`-adapted objects.** Let `I` be a
class of objects of `C` adapted to an additive functor `F` in the sense of [Stacks 05T8], let `J`
be an injective resolution of `X` with terms in `I`, and let `ε : X[0] ⟶ K` be a quasi-isomorphism
onto a cochain complex with terms in `I` — a resolution of `X` by `I`-objects, not required to be
injective. Then any descent `β : K ⟶ J.cocomplex` of the identity along `ε` induces an
isomorphism on the cohomology of the images under `F`.

Such a `β` exists by `CategoryTheory.InjectiveResolution.exists_desc_of_quasiIso` and is unique up
to homotopy by `CategoryTheory.InjectiveResolution.nonempty_descHomotopy_of_quasiIso`, so the
resulting identification `CategoryTheory.InjectiveResolution.isoRightDerivedObjOfQuasiIso` of
`(F.rightDerived n).obj X` with `Hⁿ(F(K))` does not depend on the choice.
declarations.statement:
lemma isIso_homologyMap_map_of_desc (F : C ⥤ D) [F.Additive] (I : ObjectProperty C)
    (hI₁ : ∀ Y : C, ∃ (Z : C) (_ : I Z) (i : Y ⟶ Z), Mono i)
    (hI₂ : ∀ S : ShortComplex C, S.ShortExact → I S.X₁ → I S.X₂ →
      I S.X₃ ∧ (S.map F).ShortExact)
    (J : InjectiveResolution X) {K : CochainComplex C ℕ}
    (ε : (CochainComplex.single₀ C).obj X ⟶ K) [QuasiIso ε] (β : K ⟶ J.cocomplex)
    (hβ : ε ≫ β = J.ι) (hIK : ∀ n, I (K.X n)) (hIJ : ∀ n, I (J.cocomplex.X n)) (n : ℕ) :
    IsIso (HomologicalComplex.homologyMap
      ((F.mapHomologicalComplex (ComplexShape.up ℕ)).map β) n)
declarations.comment: the computation of `Rⁿ F` by a resolution by `I`-objects, for `ℕ`-indexed resolutions

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.InjectiveResolution.isoRightDerivedObjOfQuasiIso
declarations.doc:
The identification of `(F.rightDerived n).obj X` with the degree-`n` cohomology of `F` applied
to a resolution of `X` by `F`-adapted objects, along a descent `β` of the identity. See
`CategoryTheory.InjectiveResolution.isIso_homologyMap_map_of_desc` for the hypotheses and for why
the choice of `β` does not matter.
declarations.statement:
def isoRightDerivedObjOfQuasiIso (F : C ⥤ D) [F.Additive] (I : ObjectProperty C)
    (hI₁ : ∀ Y : C, ∃ (Z : C) (_ : I Z) (i : Y ⟶ Z), Mono i)
    (hI₂ : ∀ S : ShortComplex C, S.ShortExact → I S.X₁ → I S.X₂ →
      I S.X₃ ∧ (S.map F).ShortExact)
    (J : InjectiveResolution X) {K : CochainComplex C ℕ}
    (ε : (CochainComplex.single₀ C).obj X ⟶ K) [QuasiIso ε] (β : K ⟶ J.cocomplex)
    (hβ : ε ≫ β = J.ι) (hIK : ∀ n, I (K.X n)) (hIJ : ∀ n, I (J.cocomplex.X n)) (n : ℕ) :
    (F.rightDerived n).obj X ≅
      (HomologicalComplex.homologyFunctor D (ComplexShape.up ℕ) n).obj
        ((F.mapHomologicalComplex (ComplexShape.up ℕ)).obj K)
declarations.comment: the resulting identification of `Rⁿ F (X)` with `Hⁿ (F (K))`

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.Functor.hasPointwiseRightDerivedFunctor_op_and_le_rightAcyclic_op
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 05T9.** Let `F : C ⥤ D` be an additive functor between abelian categories and let
`P` be a class of objects of `C` such that every object of `C` is a quotient of an object
satisfying `P`, and such that for every short exact sequence `0 ⟶ P ⟶ Q ⟶ R ⟶ 0` with `Q` and
`R` satisfying `P` the object `P` satisfies `P` and `0 ⟶ F P ⟶ F Q ⟶ F R ⟶ 0` is short exact.
Then the left derived functor `LF` is defined everywhere on `K⁻(C)`, i.e. the pointwise right
derived functor of `F.op` exists on `K⁺(Cᵒᵖ)`, and every object satisfying `P` is acyclic for
`LF`, i.e. its opposite is acyclic for the right derived functor of `F.op`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem hasPointwiseRightDerivedFunctor_op_and_le_rightAcyclic_op {C : Type u}
    {D : Type u'} [Category.{v} C] [Category.{v'} D] [Abelian C] [Abelian D]
    [HasDerivedCategory.{w} Cᵒᵖ] [HasDerivedCategory.{w'} Dᵒᵖ]
    (F : C ⥤ D) [F.Additive] (P : ObjectProperty C)
    (hP₁ : ∀ X : C, ∃ (Y : C) (_ : P Y) (p : Y ⟶ X), Epi p)
    (hP₂ : ∀ S : ShortComplex C, S.ShortExact → P S.X₂ → P S.X₃ →
      P S.X₁ ∧ (S.map F).ShortExact) :
    ∃ h : (F.op.mapHomotopyCategoryPlus ⋙ DerivedCategory.Plus.Qh).HasPointwiseRightDerivedFunctor
        (HomotopyCategory.Plus.quasiIso Cᵒᵖ),
      letI := h
      P.op ≤ F.op.rightAcyclic
declarations.comment:
The left derived functor `LF` (encoded as the right derived functor of `F.op`
  on `K⁺(Cᵒᵖ)`) is defined everywhere, and every object of `P` is acyclic for it.

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.Functor.hasDerivedFunctors_of_enough_acyclic_objects
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 05TA.** Let `F : C ⥤ D` be an additive functor of abelian categories.

1. If every object of `C` injects into an object `Y` acyclic for `RF` — that is, `Y[0]`
   computes the right derived functor of `K⁺(C) ⥤ D⁺(D)` in the sense of [Stacks, Tag 05SX],
   with no global existence of `RF` assumed — then `RF` is defined on all of `K⁺(C)`, the
   resulting functor `RF : D⁺(C) ⥤ D⁺(D)` is exact (triangulated), and every bounded below
   complex whose terms are acyclic for `RF` computes `RF`: the unit of `RF` is invertible there.
2. Dually, if every object of `C` is a quotient of an object acyclic for `LF`, then `LF` is
   defined on all of `K⁻(C)`, is exact, and is computed by bounded above complexes of objects
   acyclic for `LF`.

Part (2) is stated through opposite categories, as in [Stacks, Tag 0157]: `K⁻(C)` is `K⁺(Cᵒᵖ)`,
`LF` is the right derived functor of `F.op`, and acyclicity for `LF` is right acyclicity for
`F.op`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem hasDerivedFunctors_of_enough_acyclic_objects (F : C ⥤ D) [F.Additive] :
    ((∀ X : C, ∃ (Y : C) (i : X ⟶ Y), Mono i ∧
        (F.mapHomotopyCategoryPlus ⋙ DerivedCategory.Plus.Qh).ComputesRightDerived
          (HomotopyCategory.Plus.quasiIso C)
          ((HomotopyCategory.Plus.singleFunctor C 0).obj Y)) →
      ∃ h : (F.mapHomotopyCategoryPlus ⋙ DerivedCategory.Plus.Qh).HasPointwiseRightDerivedFunctor
          (HomotopyCategory.Plus.quasiIso C),
        letI := h
        ((F.mapHomotopyCategoryPlus ⋙ DerivedCategory.Plus.Qh).totalRightDerived
            DerivedCategory.Plus.Qh (HomotopyCategory.Plus.quasiIso C)).IsTriangulated ∧
          ∀ X : HomotopyCategory.Plus C,
            (∀ n : ℤ, F.rightAcyclic (X.obj.as.X n)) →
              IsIso (((F.mapHomotopyCategoryPlus ⋙ DerivedCategory.Plus.Qh).totalRightDerivedUnit
                DerivedCategory.Plus.Qh (HomotopyCategory.Plus.quasiIso C)).app X)) ∧
    ((∀ X : C, ∃ (Y : C) (p : Y ⟶ X), Epi p ∧
        (F.op.mapHomotopyCategoryPlus ⋙ DerivedCategory.Plus.Qh).ComputesRightDerived
          (HomotopyCategory.Plus.quasiIso Cᵒᵖ)
          ((HomotopyCategory.Plus.singleFunctor Cᵒᵖ 0).obj (Opposite.op Y))) →
      ∃ h : (F.op.mapHomotopyCategoryPlus ⋙ DerivedCategory.Plus.Qh).HasPointwiseRightDerivedFunctor
          (HomotopyCategory.Plus.quasiIso Cᵒᵖ),
        letI := h
        ((F.op.mapHomotopyCategoryPlus ⋙ DerivedCategory.Plus.Qh).totalRightDerived
            DerivedCategory.Plus.Qh (HomotopyCategory.Plus.quasiIso Cᵒᵖ)).IsTriangulated ∧
          ∀ X : HomotopyCategory.Plus Cᵒᵖ,
            (∀ n : ℤ, F.op.rightAcyclic (X.obj.as.X n)) →
              IsIso (((F.op.mapHomotopyCategoryPlus ⋙ DerivedCategory.Plus.Qh).totalRightDerivedUnit
                DerivedCategory.Plus.Qh (HomotopyCategory.Plus.quasiIso Cᵒᵖ)).app X))

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.Functor.isGE_and_isIso_homologyFunctor_map_of_isRightDerivedValueAt
declarations.doc:
**Right derived functors move to the right**, [StackProject 05TC].
Let `F : A ⥤ B` be an additive functor between abelian categories, let `K` be a cochain complex
of objects of `A`, let `a : ℤ`, and let `RF` be the right derived functor of
`K(A) ⥤ K(B) ⥤ D(B)` with respect to the quasi-isomorphisms. Assume `RF` is defined at `K`,
with value `RF(K) = c.pt` (Stacks 05S9: the ind-object `(s : K ⟶ L) ↦ F(L)` of `D(B)` is
essentially constant with value `c.pt`).
1. If `H^i(K) = 0` for all `i < a`, then `H^i(RF(K)) = 0` for all `i < a`.
2. If moreover `RF` is defined at `τ_{≤ a}K`, with value `RF(τ_{≤ a}K) = d.pt`, then there is a
   unique morphism `φ : RF(τ_{≤ a}K) ⟶ RF(K)` compatible with the coprojections of the two
   values along the canonical monomorphism `K.ιTruncLE a : τ_{≤ a}K ⟶ K` — that is, with
   `d.ι.app s ≫ φ = F(g) ≫ c.ι.app t` for every pair of indices `s`, `t` and every
   `g : s.right ⟶ t.right` with `ιTruncLE ≫ t.hom = s.hom ≫ g`, the morphism `RF(ιTruncLE)`
   of Stacks 05SA — and `H^i(φ)` is an isomorphism for all `i ≤ a`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem isGE_and_isIso_homologyFunctor_map_of_isRightDerivedValueAt
    {A B : Type*} [Category* A] [Category* B] [Abelian A] [Abelian B]
    [HasDerivedCategory B] (F : A ⥤ B) [F.Additive]
    (K : CochainComplex A ℤ) (a : ℤ)
    (c : Cocone (MorphismProperty.Under.forget (HomotopyCategory.quasiIso A (ComplexShape.up ℤ))
        ⊤ ((HomotopyCategory.quotient A (ComplexShape.up ℤ)).obj K) ⋙
      Under.forget ((HomotopyCategory.quotient A (ComplexShape.up ℤ)).obj K) ⋙
      F.mapHomotopyCategory (ComplexShape.up ℤ) ⋙ DerivedCategory.Qh))
    (hc : (F.mapHomotopyCategory (ComplexShape.up ℤ) ⋙ DerivedCategory.Qh).IsRightDerivedValueAt
      (HomotopyCategory.quasiIso A (ComplexShape.up ℤ))
      ((HomotopyCategory.quotient A (ComplexShape.up ℤ)).obj K) c) :
    (K.IsGE a → c.pt.IsGE a) ∧
    ∀ (d : Cocone (MorphismProperty.Under.forget
          (HomotopyCategory.quasiIso A (ComplexShape.up ℤ)) ⊤
          ((HomotopyCategory.quotient A (ComplexShape.up ℤ)).obj (K.truncLE a)) ⋙
        Under.forget ((HomotopyCategory.quotient A (ComplexShape.up ℤ)).obj (K.truncLE a)) ⋙
        F.mapHomotopyCategory (ComplexShape.up ℤ) ⋙ DerivedCategory.Qh)),
      (F.mapHomotopyCategory (ComplexShape.up ℤ) ⋙ DerivedCategory.Qh).IsRightDerivedValueAt
        (HomotopyCategory.quasiIso A (ComplexShape.up ℤ))
        ((HomotopyCategory.quotient A (ComplexShape.up ℤ)).obj (K.truncLE a)) d →
      ∃ φ : d.pt ⟶ c.pt,
        (∀ ψ : d.pt ⟶ c.pt,
          (∀ (s : (HomotopyCategory.quasiIso A (ComplexShape.up ℤ)).Under ⊤
                ((HomotopyCategory.quotient A (ComplexShape.up ℤ)).obj (K.truncLE a)))
             (t : (HomotopyCategory.quasiIso A (ComplexShape.up ℤ)).Under ⊤
                ((HomotopyCategory.quotient A (ComplexShape.up ℤ)).obj K))
             (g : s.right ⟶ t.right),
            (HomotopyCategory.quotient A (ComplexShape.up ℤ)).map (K.ιTruncLE a) ≫ t.hom =
                s.hom ≫ g →
              d.ι.app s ≫ ψ =
                (F.mapHomotopyCategory (ComplexShape.up ℤ) ⋙ DerivedCategory.Qh).map g ≫
                  c.ι.app t) ↔ ψ = φ) ∧
        ∀ i ≤ a, IsIso ((DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor B i).map φ)

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.Functor.isZero_and_preservesFiniteLimits_and_isIso_iff_of_isRightDerivable
declarations.doc:
**Right deriving is for left exact functors**, [Stacks, Tag 05TD].
Let `F : 𝒜 ⥤ ℬ` be an additive functor between abelian categories and assume that the right
derived functor `RF : D⁺(𝒜) ⥤ D⁺(ℬ)` is everywhere defined: for every bounded below complex `K`
the ind-object `(s : K ⟶ L) ↦ F(L)` over the quasi-isomorphisms `s` out of `K` is essentially
constant ([Stacks, Tag 05SV]). Let `RF`, with unit `α`, be the right derived functor, so that
`R ⁱ F = H ⁱ ∘ RF ∘ (·[0])`. Then
1. `R ⁱ F = 0` for `i < 0`,
2. `R ⁰ F` is left exact, and
