3. the canonical map `F ⟶ R ⁰ F`, that is `H ⁰(α)` at the complexes `X[0]`, is an
   isomorphism if and only if `F` is left exact.
declarations.statement:
public theorem isZero_and_preservesFiniteLimits_and_isIso_iff_of_isRightDerivable
    {A B : Type*} [Category* A] [Category* B] [Abelian A] [Abelian B]
    [HasDerivedCategory A] [HasDerivedCategory B] (F : A ⥤ B) [F.Additive]
    (hF : (F.mapHomotopyCategoryPlus ⋙ DerivedCategory.Plus.Qh).IsRightDerivable
      (HomotopyCategory.Plus.quasiIso A))
    (RF : DerivedCategory.Plus A ⥤ DerivedCategory.Plus B)
    (α : F.mapHomotopyCategoryPlus ⋙ DerivedCategory.Plus.Qh ⟶
      DerivedCategory.Plus.Qh ⋙ RF)
    [RF.IsRightDerivedFunctor α (HomotopyCategory.Plus.quasiIso A)] :
    (∀ i < 0, IsZero (DerivedCategory.Plus.singleFunctor A 0 ⋙ RF ⋙
        DerivedCategory.Plus.homologyFunctor B i)) ∧
      PreservesFiniteLimits (DerivedCategory.Plus.singleFunctor A 0 ⋙ RF ⋙
        DerivedCategory.Plus.homologyFunctor B 0) ∧
      ((∀ X : A, IsIso ((DerivedCategory.Plus.homologyFunctor B 0).map
          (α.app ((HomotopyCategory.Plus.singleFunctor A 0).obj X)))) ↔
        PreservesFiniteLimits F)

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.Functor.isDeltaFunctor_and_isUniversal_of_isRightDerivable
declarations.doc:
**The higher right derived functors form a universal `δ`-functor**, [Stacks, Tag 05TE].
Let `F : 𝒜 ⥤ ℬ` be an additive functor between abelian categories and assume that
`RF : D⁺(𝒜) ⥤ D⁺(ℬ)` is everywhere defined: the right derived functor of
`K⁺(F) ⋙ Q : K⁺(𝒜) ⥤ D⁺(ℬ)` with respect to the quasi-isomorphisms is defined at every object
([Stacks, Tag 05SV]). Let `(RF, α)` be the right derived functor, so that
`R ⁱ F = H ⁱ ∘ RF ∘ (·[0])`. Let `h` be a `δ`-functor structure on `A ↦ RF(A[0]) : 𝒜 ⥤ D⁺(ℬ)`
(the canonical one, `CategoryTheory.Functor.derivedDeltaFunctorStructureOfIsRightDerivable`, is
`Stacks.DerivedIndexing.singleDeltaFunctorStructure` composed with the exact functor `RF`; the
statement holds for every such structure), and let `δ` be the connecting
morphism `R ⁱ F(C) ⟶ R ⁱ⁺¹ F(A)` that the homology sequence of its distinguished triangles
attaches to a short exact sequence `0 ⟶ A ⟶ B ⟶ C ⟶ 0` of `𝒜`. Then
1. `{R ⁱ F, δ}_{i ≥ 0}` is a cohomological `δ`-functor from `𝒜` to `ℬ`: the `R ⁱ F` are additive,
   the long sequence `0 ⟶ R ⁰ F(A) ⟶ R ⁰ F(B) ⟶ R ⁰ F(C) ⟶ R ¹ F(A) ⟶ ⋯` is exact, and `δ` is
   natural in the short exact sequence; and
2. if every object of `𝒜` is a subobject of an object right acyclic for `F` — an object `I` such
   that `I[0]` computes `RF` ([Stacks, Tag 0157], [Stacks, Tag 05SX]) — then `{R ⁱ F, δ}_{i ≥ 0}`
   is a universal `δ`-functor: for every `δ`-functor `{G ⁱ, δ_G}_{i ≥ 0}` from `𝒜` to `ℬ` and
   every `t₀ : R ⁰ F ⟶ G ⁰` there is a unique family `t ⁱ : R ⁱ F ⟶ G ⁱ` commuting with `δ` and
   `δ_G` and with `t ⁰ = t₀`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem isDeltaFunctor_and_isUniversal_of_isRightDerivable (F : C ⥤ D) [F.Additive]
    (hF : (F.mapHomotopyCategoryPlus ⋙ DerivedCategory.Plus.Qh).IsRightDerivable
      (HomotopyCategory.Plus.quasiIso C))
    (RF : DerivedCategory.Plus C ⥤ DerivedCategory.Plus D)
    (α : F.mapHomotopyCategoryPlus ⋙ DerivedCategory.Plus.Qh ⟶ DerivedCategory.Plus.Qh ⋙ RF)
    [RF.IsRightDerivedFunctor α (HomotopyCategory.Plus.quasiIso C)]
    (h : DeltaFunctorStructure C (DerivedCategory.Plus D)
      (DerivedCategory.Plus.singleFunctor C 0 ⋙ RF))
    (δ : ∀ {S : ShortComplex C}, S.ShortExact → ∀ i : ℕ,
      (DerivedCategory.Plus.singleFunctor C 0 ⋙ RF ⋙
          DerivedCategory.Plus.homologyFunctor D i).obj S.X₃ ⟶
        (DerivedCategory.Plus.singleFunctor C 0 ⋙ RF ⋙
          DerivedCategory.Plus.homologyFunctor D (i + 1)).obj S.X₁)
    (hδ : ∀ {S : ShortComplex C} (hS : S.ShortExact) (i : ℕ), δ hS i =
      (DerivedCategory.Plus.homologyFunctor D 0).homologySequenceδ
        (Pretriangulated.Triangle.mk ((DerivedCategory.Plus.singleFunctor C 0 ⋙ RF).map S.f)
          ((DerivedCategory.Plus.singleFunctor C 0 ⋙ RF).map S.g) (h.δ hS)) i (i + 1) rfl) :
    ((∀ i : ℕ, (DerivedCategory.Plus.singleFunctor C 0 ⋙ RF ⋙
          DerivedCategory.Plus.homologyFunctor D i).Additive) ∧
      (∀ {S : ShortComplex C}, S.ShortExact →
        Mono ((DerivedCategory.Plus.singleFunctor C 0 ⋙ RF ⋙
          DerivedCategory.Plus.homologyFunctor D 0).map S.f)) ∧
      (∀ {S : ShortComplex C} (_ : S.ShortExact) (i : ℕ),
        ∃ hz : (DerivedCategory.Plus.singleFunctor C 0 ⋙ RF ⋙
              DerivedCategory.Plus.homologyFunctor D i).map S.f ≫
            (DerivedCategory.Plus.singleFunctor C 0 ⋙ RF ⋙
              DerivedCategory.Plus.homologyFunctor D i).map S.g = 0,
          (ShortComplex.mk _ _ hz).Exact) ∧
      (∀ {S : ShortComplex C} (hS : S.ShortExact) (i : ℕ),
        ∃ hz : (DerivedCategory.Plus.singleFunctor C 0 ⋙ RF ⋙
            DerivedCategory.Plus.homologyFunctor D i).map S.g ≫ δ hS i = 0,
          (ShortComplex.mk _ _ hz).Exact) ∧
      (∀ {S : ShortComplex C} (hS : S.ShortExact) (i : ℕ),
        ∃ hz : δ hS i ≫ (DerivedCategory.Plus.singleFunctor C 0 ⋙ RF ⋙
            DerivedCategory.Plus.homologyFunctor D (i + 1)).map S.f = 0,
          (ShortComplex.mk _ _ hz).Exact) ∧
      (∀ {S S' : ShortComplex C} (hS : S.ShortExact) (hS' : S'.ShortExact) (φ : S ⟶ S') (i : ℕ),
        (DerivedCategory.Plus.singleFunctor C 0 ⋙ RF ⋙
            DerivedCategory.Plus.homologyFunctor D i).map φ.τ₃ ≫ δ hS' i =
          δ hS i ≫ (DerivedCategory.Plus.singleFunctor C 0 ⋙ RF ⋙
            DerivedCategory.Plus.homologyFunctor D (i + 1)).map φ.τ₁)) ∧
    ((∀ A : C, ∃ (I : C) (u : A ⟶ I), Mono u ∧
        (F.mapHomotopyCategoryPlus ⋙ DerivedCategory.Plus.Qh).ComputesRightDerived
          (HomotopyCategory.Plus.quasiIso C) ((HomotopyCategory.Plus.singleFunctor C 0).obj I)) →
      ∀ (G : ℕ → C ⥤ D) (_ : ∀ i, (G i).Additive)
        (δG : ∀ {S : ShortComplex C}, S.ShortExact → ∀ i : ℕ,
          (G i).obj S.X₃ ⟶ (G (i + 1)).obj S.X₁),
        (∀ {S : ShortComplex C}, S.ShortExact → Mono ((G 0).map S.f)) →
        (∀ {S : ShortComplex C} (_ : S.ShortExact) (i : ℕ),
          ∃ hz : (G i).map S.f ≫ (G i).map S.g = 0, (ShortComplex.mk _ _ hz).Exact) →
        (∀ {S : ShortComplex C} (hS : S.ShortExact) (i : ℕ),
          ∃ hz : (G i).map S.g ≫ δG hS i = 0, (ShortComplex.mk _ _ hz).Exact) →
        (∀ {S : ShortComplex C} (hS : S.ShortExact) (i : ℕ),
          ∃ hz : δG hS i ≫ (G (i + 1)).map S.f = 0, (ShortComplex.mk _ _ hz).Exact) →
        (∀ {S S' : ShortComplex C} (hS : S.ShortExact) (hS' : S'.ShortExact) (φ : S ⟶ S')
          (i : ℕ), (G i).map φ.τ₃ ≫ δG hS' i = δG hS i ≫ (G (i + 1)).map φ.τ₁) →
        ∀ t₀ : DerivedCategory.Plus.singleFunctor C 0 ⋙ RF ⋙
            DerivedCategory.Plus.homologyFunctor D 0 ⟶ G 0,
          ∃! t : ∀ i : ℕ, DerivedCategory.Plus.singleFunctor C 0 ⋙ RF ⋙
              DerivedCategory.Plus.homologyFunctor D i ⟶ G i,
            t 0 = t₀ ∧ ∀ {S : ShortComplex C} (hS : S.ShortExact) (i : ℕ),
              (t i).app S.X₃ ≫ δG hS i = δ hS i ≫ (t (i + 1)).app S.X₁)

declarations.name: CochainComplex.bijective_precomp_quotient_map
declarations.doc:
If `I` is a K-injective cochain complex and `α : K ⟶ L` is a quasi-isomorphism, then
precomposition with the image of `α` in the homotopy category `K(A)` is a bijection
`Hom_{K(A)}(L, I) → Hom_{K(A)}(K, I)`.
declarations.statement:
lemma bijective_precomp_quotient_map [I.IsKInjective] (α : K ⟶ L) [QuasiIso α] :
    Function.Bijective (fun β : (HomotopyCategory.quotient A (ComplexShape.up ℤ)).obj L ⟶
        (HomotopyCategory.quotient A (ComplexShape.up ℤ)).obj I =>
      (HomotopyCategory.quotient A (ComplexShape.up ℤ)).map α ≫ β)

registrations.name: CochainComplex.IsKInjective.Qh_map_bijective
registrations.comment: the bijection `Mor_{K(A)}(K, I) → Mor_{D(A)}(K, I)` for a K-injective `I`

registrations.name: CochainComplex.isKInjective_of_injective
registrations.comment: a complex strictly bounded below with injective terms is K-injective

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.Functor.computesRightDerived_of_injective
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 05TH**, part (1). Let `K` be a bounded below complex of injective objects of an
abelian category `C`. Then `K` computes the right derived functor `RF` relative to the
quasi-isomorphisms of `K⁺(C)` (Stacks 05SX), for every functor `F : K⁺(C) ⥤ H`: `RF` is defined
at `K`, and the canonical map `F(K) ⟶ RF(K)` is an isomorphism. The source asks this for exact
functors into triangulated categories; it holds for all functors.
declarations.statement:
theorem computesRightDerived_of_injective {H : Type u₃} [Category.{v₃} H]
    (F : HomotopyCategory.Plus C ⥤ H) (K : HomotopyCategory.Plus C)
    [∀ n : ℤ, Injective (K.obj.as.X n)] :
    F.ComputesRightDerived (HomotopyCategory.Plus.quasiIso C) K
declarations.comment: (1); for every functor out of `K⁺(𝒜)`, exact or not. (2) is `CategoryTheory.Functor.computesRightDerived_single_of_injective`

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.Functor.computesRightDerived_single_of_injective
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 05TH**, part (2). Let `F : C ⥤ D` be an additive functor between abelian categories
and let `I` be an injective object of `C`. Then `I` is right acyclic for `F` in the sense of
Stacks 0157(3): the complex `I[0]` computes the right derived functor of
`K⁺(F) ⋙ Q⁺ : K⁺(C) ⥤ D⁺(D)` relative to the quasi-isomorphisms of `K⁺(C)` (Stacks 05SX).
declarations.statement:
theorem computesRightDerived_single_of_injective {D : Type u₂} [Category.{v₂} D] [Abelian D]
    [HasDerivedCategory.{w} D] (F : C ⥤ D) [F.Additive] (I : C) [Injective I] :
    (F.mapHomotopyCategoryPlus ⋙ DerivedCategory.Plus.Qh).ComputesRightDerived
      (HomotopyCategory.Plus.quasiIso C) ((HomotopyCategory.Plus.singleFunctor C 0).obj I)
declarations.comment: (2); right acyclicity is 0157(3) in the 05SX form, with no hypothesis that `𝒜` have enough injectives

declarations.name: HomotopyCategory.Plus.hasPointwiseRightDerivedFunctorAt_of_injective
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 05TH**, part (1), first half. Let `K` be a bounded below complex of injective
objects of an abelian category `C`. Then the right derived functor of any functor
`F : K⁺(C) ⥤ H` relative to the quasi-isomorphisms of `K⁺(C)` is defined at `K`, i.e. the
pointwise left Kan extension of `F` along a localization of `K⁺(C)` at the quasi-isomorphisms
exists at the image of `K`.

If `C` has enough injectives, this holds for every `K`; the content here is that termwise
injectivity of `K` suffices.
declarations.statement:
public instance hasPointwiseRightDerivedFunctorAt_of_injective {H : Type u₃} [Category.{v₃} H]
    (F : HomotopyCategory.Plus C ⥤ H) (K : HomotopyCategory.Plus C)
    [∀ n : ℤ, Injective (K.obj.as.X n)] :
    F.HasPointwiseRightDerivedFunctorAt (HomotopyCategory.Plus.quasiIso C) K
declarations.comment: part (1): RF is defined at a bounded below complex of injectives

declarations.name: hasPointwiseRightDerivedFunctor_of_isTriangulated
declarations.doc:
**Statement 1 (Stacks Tag 05TI, part 1).** Let `A` be an abelian category with enough
injectives. For every triangulated category `D` and every exact (triangulated) functor
`F : K^{+}(A) ⥤ D`, the right derived functor `RF : D^{+}(A) ⥤ D` of `F` with respect to
the quasi-isomorphisms is everywhere defined.
declarations.statement:
theorem hasPointwiseRightDerivedFunctor_of_isTriangulated {A : Type*} [Category A] [Abelian A]
  [EnoughInjectives A]
    {D : Type*} [Category D] [HasZeroObject D] [HasShift D ℤ] [Preadditive D]
    [∀ (n : ℤ), (shiftFunctor D n).Additive] [Pretriangulated D]
    (F : HomotopyCategory.Plus A ⥤ D) [F.CommShift ℤ] [F.IsTriangulated] :
    F.HasPointwiseRightDerivedFunctor (HomotopyCategory.Plus.quasiIso A)

declarations.name: hasPointwiseRightDerivedFunctor_mapPlus
declarations.doc:
**Statement 2 (Stacks Tag 05TI, part 2).** Let `A` be an abelian category with enough
injectives. For every abelian category `B` and every additive functor `F : A ⥤ B`, the
right derived functor `RF : D^{+}(A) ⥤ D^{+}(B)` of the composite
`K^{+}(F) ⋙ Q^{+}_{B} : K^{+}(A) ⥤ D^{+}(B)` is everywhere defined.
declarations.statement:
theorem hasPointwiseRightDerivedFunctor_mapPlus {A B : Type*} [Category A] [Abelian A]
  [EnoughInjectives A]
    [Category B] [Abelian B]
    (F : A ⥤ B) [F.Additive] :
    (mapPlus F ⋙ (HomotopyCategory.Plus.quasiIso B).Q).HasPointwiseRightDerivedFunctor
      (HomotopyCategory.Plus.quasiIso A)

declarations.name: HomotopyCategory.Plus.existsUnique_functor_of_resolutionFunctor
declarations.doc:
Let `C` be an abelian category, `ℐ ⊆ C` its full additive subcategory of injective
objects, and let `j` be a resolution functor for `C`, i.e. a right resolution
`(j K).w : K ⟶ (j K).X₁` in `K⁺(ℐ)` of every object `K` of `K⁺(C)`. Then there is a unique
way to make `K ↦ (j K).X₁` into a functor `F : K⁺(C) ⥤ K⁺(ℐ)` for which the comparison
maps `(j K).w` form a natural transformation `𝟭 K⁺(C) ⟶ F ⋙ (K⁺(ℐ) ⥤ K⁺(C))`; the latter
is then a `2`-isomorphism over `D⁺(C)`, since its components are quasi-isomorphisms.
declarations.statement:
public theorem existsUnique_functor_of_resolutionFunctor (j : ResolutionFunctor C) :
    ∃! F : HomotopyCategory.Plus C ⥤ HomotopyCategory.Plus (InjectiveObject C),
      ∃ (α : 𝟭 (HomotopyCategory.Plus C) ⟶ F ⋙ (localizerMorphism C).functor)
        (hα : ∀ K, quasiIso C (α.app K)),
        ∀ K, LocalizerMorphism.RightResolution.mk (α.app K) (hα K) = j K

declarations.name: HomotopyCategory.Plus.exists_equivalence_and_existsUnique_lift_of_quasiIso
declarations.doc:
Let `C` be an abelian category, `ℐ ⊆ C` its full additive subcategory of injective
objects, and let `F : K⁺(C) ⥤ K⁺(ℐ)` be a functor equipped with comparison maps
`α.app K : K ⟶ F K` in `K⁺(C)` that are quasi-isomorphisms, i.e. the functorial form of a
resolution functor ([Stacks, Tags 013W, 05TJ]). Then `F` factors through the localization
`Q : K⁺(C) ⥤ D⁺(C)` by a functor which is quasi-inverse to the canonical functor
`K⁺(ℐ) ⥤ D⁺(C)`, and the factorization is unique up to a unique natural transformation
over `F`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem exists_equivalence_and_existsUnique_lift_of_quasiIso
    (F : HomotopyCategory.Plus C ⥤ HomotopyCategory.Plus (InjectiveObject C))
    (α : 𝟭 (HomotopyCategory.Plus C) ⟶ F ⋙ (localizerMorphism C).functor)
    (hα : ∀ K, quasiIso C (α.app K)) :
    (∃ e : DerivedCategory.Plus C ≌ HomotopyCategory.Plus (InjectiveObject C),
      e.inverse = (localizerMorphism C).functor ⋙ DerivedCategory.Plus.Qh ∧
        Nonempty (DerivedCategory.Plus.Qh ⋙ e.functor ≅ F)) ∧
    ∀ (j₁ j₂ : DerivedCategory.Plus C ⥤ HomotopyCategory.Plus (InjectiveObject C))
      (e₁ : DerivedCategory.Plus.Qh ⋙ j₁ ≅ F) (e₂ : DerivedCategory.Plus.Qh ⋙ j₂ ≅ F),
      ∃! τ : j₁ ⟶ j₂,
        Functor.whiskerLeft DerivedCategory.Plus.Qh τ = e₁.hom ≫ e₂.inv

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.Functor.exists_iso_rightDerivedFunctorPlus_of_comp_Qh_iso_id
declarations.doc:
Let `F : C ⥤ D` be an additive functor between abelian categories with `C` having enough
injectives, let `ℐ ⊆ C` be the subcategory of injective objects, and let
`j' : D⁺(C) ⥤ K⁺(ℐ)` be a section up to isomorphism of the canonical functor
`K⁺(ℐ) ⥤ D⁺(C)`, i.e. the descent of a resolution functor
([Stacks, Tags 013W, 05TK]). Then the right derived functor `RF` of `F` is computed by
`F ∘ j'`: the triangle `D⁺(C) ⥤ K⁺(ℐ) ⥤ D⁺(D)`, `RF` is `2`-commutative, by the
`2`-isomorphism whose value at `X` is the unit of `RF` at the complex of injectives `j' X`
followed by `RF` applied to `ε.hom.app X`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem exists_iso_rightDerivedFunctorPlus_of_comp_Qh_iso_id
    (F : C ⥤ D) [F.Additive] [EnoughInjectives C]
    (j' : DerivedCategory.Plus C ⥤ HomotopyCategory.Plus (InjectiveObject C))
    (ε : j' ⋙ (HomotopyCategory.Plus.localizerMorphism C).functor ⋙ DerivedCategory.Plus.Qh ≅
      𝟭 (DerivedCategory.Plus C)) :
    ∃ e : j' ⋙ (HomotopyCategory.Plus.localizerMorphism C).functor ⋙
        F.mapHomotopyCategoryPlus ⋙ DerivedCategory.Plus.Qh ≅ F.rightDerivedFunctorPlus,
      ∀ X, e.hom.app X = F.rightDerivedFunctorPlusUnith.app
        ((HomotopyCategory.Plus.localizerMorphism C).functor.obj (j'.obj X)) ≫
          F.rightDerivedFunctorPlus.map (ε.hom.app X)

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.FilteredObject.isFilteredInjective_iff_nonempty_iso_stdBiprod
declarations.doc:
Let `𝒜` be an abelian category. An object `I` of `Fil^f(𝒜)` is filtered injective if and
only if there are integers `a ≤ b`, injective objects `I_n` of `𝒜` and an isomorphism
`I ≅ ⨁_{a ≤ n ≤ b} I_n` of filtered objects, where the right-hand side carries the filtration
`F^p = ⨁_{n ≥ p} I_n` (`FilteredObject.stdBiprod`). The finiteness of the filtration of `I` is
part of both sides, and is not a hypothesis.
declarations.statement:
theorem isFilteredInjective_iff_nonempty_iso_stdBiprod (I : FilteredObject 𝒜 ℤᵒᵖ) :
    I.IsFilteredInjective ↔ ∃ a b : ℤ, a ≤ b ∧ ∃ Inj : ℤ → 𝒜, (∀ n, Injective (Inj n)) ∧
      Nonempty (I ≅ stdBiprod a b Inj)

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.FilteredObject.isSplitMono_of_isFilteredInjective
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 05TQ.** Let `𝒜` be an abelian category. A strict monomorphism `u : I ⟶ A` of
filtered objects of `𝒜` whose source `I` is a filtered injective object of `Fil^f(𝒜)` — its
filtration is finite and every graded piece `gr^p(I) = F^p I / F^{p + 1} I` is an injective object
of `𝒜` — is a split monomorphism: it admits a retraction in the category of filtered objects.
declarations.statement:
public theorem isSplitMono_of_isFilteredInjective {𝒜 : Type u} [Category.{v} 𝒜] [Abelian 𝒜]
    {I A : FilteredObject 𝒜 ℤᵒᵖ} (u : I ⟶ A) [IsStrictHom u] (hI : I.IsFilteredInjective) :
    IsSplitMono u

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.FilteredObject.factors_of_isFilteredInjective
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 05TR.** Let `𝒜` be an abelian category, let `u : A ⟶ B` be a strict morphism of
filtered objects of `𝒜` and let `f : A ⟶ I` be a morphism into a filtered injective object `I` of
`Fil^f(𝒜)`: its filtration is finite and every graded piece `gr^p(I) = F^p I / F^{p + 1} I` is an
injective object of `𝒜`. Then `f` extends along `u`: there is a morphism `g : B ⟶ I` of filtered
objects with `f = u ≫ g`. The source assumes `u` to be a strict monomorphism; monomorphy is not
used, and is automatic on `Fil^f(𝒜)`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem factors_of_isFilteredInjective {𝒜 : Type u} [Category.{v} 𝒜] [Abelian 𝒜]
    {A B I : FilteredObject 𝒜 ℤᵒᵖ} (f : A ⟶ I) (u : A ⟶ B) [IsStrictHom u]
    (hI : I.IsFilteredInjective) :
    ∃ g : B ⟶ I, u ≫ g = f

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.FilteredObject.exists_mono_isStrict_isFilteredInjective
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 05TS.** Let `𝒜` be an abelian category with enough injectives. Every object `A` of
`Fil^f(𝒜)` admits a strict monomorphism `u : A ⟶ I` into a filtered injective object `I`: the
underlying morphism of `u` is a monomorphism of `𝒜` and `u` is strict.
declarations.statement:
public theorem _root_.CategoryTheory.FilteredObject.exists_mono_isStrict_isFilteredInjective
    [EnoughInjectives 𝒜] (A : FilteredObject 𝒜 ℤᵒᵖ) (hA : A.filtration.IsFinite) :
    ∃ (I : FilteredObject 𝒜 ℤᵒᵖ) (u : A ⟶ I), Mono u.hom ∧ IsStrict u ∧ I.IsFilteredInjective

declarations.name: CochainComplex.exists_filteredQuasiIso_isStrictlyGE_injective_gradedPiece
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 05TT.** Let `𝒜` be an abelian category with enough injectives and let `K^•` be a
filtered cochain complex of `𝒜` concentrated in degree `0` with finite filtration, i.e. `K^•` is
`A[0]` for an object `A` of `Fil^f(𝒜)`. Then there is a filtered quasi-isomorphism
`α : K^• ⟶ I^•`, that is, one whose graded pieces `gr^p(α)` are all quasi-isomorphisms, where
`I^•` is a complex of filtered injective objects with `I^n = 0` for `n < 0`: every term
`(I^n, F^• I^n)` is a filtered injective object of `Fil^f(𝒜)`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem exists_filteredQuasiIso_isStrictlyGE_injective_gradedPiece {𝒜 : Type u}
    [Category.{v} 𝒜] [Abelian 𝒜] [EnoughInjectives 𝒜]
    (K : FilteredObject (CochainComplex 𝒜 ℤ) ℤᵒᵖ) [K.X.IsStrictlyGE 0] [K.X.IsStrictlyLE 0]
    (hK : K.filtration.IsFinite) :
    ∃ (I : FilteredObject (CochainComplex 𝒜 ℤ) ℤᵒᵖ) (α : K ⟶ I)
      (_ : CochainComplex.filteredQuasiIso 𝒜 α) (_ : I.X.IsStrictlyGE 0),
      ∀ n : ℤ, (evalFil I n).IsFilteredInjective

declarations.name: CochainComplex.exists_hom_comp_eq_of_filteredQuasiIso_of_injective_gradedPiece
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 05TU.** Let `𝒜` be an abelian category, let `f : A ⟶ B` be a morphism of filtered
objects, placed in degree `0` by taking the filtered complexes `A` and `B` to be concentrated in
degree `0`, and let `a : A[0] ⟶ I^•` and `b : B[0] ⟶ J^•` be morphisms into filtered complexes with
degreewise finite filtrations, where `a` is a filtered quasi-isomorphism and `J^•` vanishes in
negative degrees and consists of filtered injective objects, i.e. every term `(J^n, F^• J^n)` is a
filtered injective object of `Fil^f(𝒜)`. Then `f` lifts to a morphism `g : I^• ⟶ J^•` with
`a ≫ g = f ≫ b` on the nose.

This is the lift that `CochainComplex.FilteredInjectiveResolution.exists_resolutionSystem` needs.

Three of the source's hypotheses are unused here and dropped: that `b` be a filtered
quasi-isomorphism, and that `I^•` vanish in negative degrees and have filtered injective graded
pieces. The lift comes from the surjectivity half of [Stacks, Tag 05TY], which asks only that `a`
be a filtered quasi-isomorphism into a complex of `K(Fil^f(𝒜))` and that the target `J^•` be
bounded below and filtered injective; the homotopy it produces is degenerate because `A` is
concentrated in degree `0`, which turns the commutation in `K(Fil^f(𝒜))` into an equality of
morphisms of filtered complexes.
declarations.statement:
public theorem exists_hom_comp_eq_of_filteredQuasiIso_of_injective_gradedPiece
    {𝒜 : Type u} [Category.{v} 𝒜] [Abelian 𝒜]
    {A B I J : FilteredObject (CochainComplex 𝒜 ℤ) ℤᵒᵖ}
    [A.X.IsStrictlyGE 0] [A.X.IsStrictlyLE 0] [J.X.IsStrictlyGE 0]
    (f : A ⟶ B) (a : A ⟶ I) (b : B ⟶ J) (ha : filteredQuasiIso 𝒜 a)
    (hAfin : ∀ n : ℤ, ∃ p q : ℤ, IsIso ((A.filtration.ι.app (op p)).f n) ∧
      IsZero ((A.filtration.obj (op q)).X n))
    (hIfin : ∀ n : ℤ, ∃ p q : ℤ, IsIso ((I.filtration.ι.app (op p)).f n) ∧
      IsZero ((I.filtration.obj (op q)).X n))
    (hJ : ∀ n : ℤ, (evalFil J n).IsFilteredInjective) :
    ∃ g : I ⟶ J, a ≫ g = f ≫ b

declarations.name: CochainComplex.exists_termwiseSplit_shortExact_of_filteredQuasiIso_of_injective_gr
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 05TV.** Let `𝒜` be an abelian category and let `0 → A → B → C → 0` be a short exact
sequence of `Fil^f(𝒜)`, i.e. morphisms `α : A ⟶ B`, `β : B ⟶ C` of filtered objects with finite
filtrations whose composite vanishes and whose graded pieces form short exact sequences
`0 → gr^p A → gr^p B → gr^p C → 0`.
Let `a : A[0] ⟶ I^•` and `c : C[0] ⟶ J^•` be filtered quasi-isomorphisms, where `I^•` and `J^•`
are complexes of filtered objects with finite filtrations, vanishing in negative degrees, and
where each `I^n` is a filtered injective object of `Fil^f(𝒜)`. Then
there are a complex `M^•` of filtered objects, morphisms `u : I^• ⟶ M^•`, `v : M^• ⟶ J^•` and
`b : B[0] ⟶ M^•` such that `0 → I^• → M^• → J^• → 0` is short exact, `α ≫ b = a ≫ u` and
`b ≫ v = β ≫ c`, and the sequence `0 → I^n → M^n → J^n → 0` splits in `Fil(𝒜)` in each degree
`n`: there are a retraction `r` of `u^n` and a section `s` of `v^n` compatible with the
filtrations. Filtered objects are placed in degree `0` by taking the filtered complexes `A`, `B`,
`C` to be concentrated in degree `0`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem exists_termwiseSplit_shortExact_of_filteredQuasiIso_of_injective_gr
    {𝒜 : Type u} [Category.{v} 𝒜] [Abelian 𝒜]
    {A B C I J : FilteredObject (CochainComplex 𝒜 ℤ) ℤᵒᵖ}
    [A.X.IsStrictlyGE 0] [A.X.IsStrictlyLE 0] [C.X.IsStrictlyGE 0] [C.X.IsStrictlyLE 0]
    [I.X.IsStrictlyGE 0] [J.X.IsStrictlyGE 0]
    (α : A ⟶ B) (β : B ⟶ C) (a : A ⟶ I) (c : C ⟶ J)
    (hcomp : α.hom ≫ β.hom = 0)
    (hgr : ∀ p : ℤ, (ShortComplex.mk ((gr p).map α)
      ((gr p).map β) (by
        have hz : ∀ q : ℤᵒᵖ, (α ≫ β).natTrans.app q = 0 := fun q =>
          zero_of_comp_mono (C.filtration.ι.app q) (by simp [hcomp])
        rw [← Functor.map_comp]
        apply coequalizer.hom_ext
        simp only [grMap_map, cokernel.π_desc, hz, zero_comp]
        exact comp_zero.symm)).ShortExact)
    (ha : filteredQuasiIso 𝒜 a) (hc : filteredQuasiIso 𝒜 c)
    (hA : ∀ n : ℤ, ∃ p q : ℤ, IsIso ((A.filtration.ι.app (op p)).f n) ∧
      IsZero ((A.filtration.obj (op q)).X n))
    (hB : ∀ n : ℤ, ∃ p q : ℤ, IsIso ((B.filtration.ι.app (op p)).f n) ∧
      IsZero ((B.filtration.obj (op q)).X n))
    (hC : ∀ n : ℤ, ∃ p q : ℤ, IsIso ((C.filtration.ι.app (op p)).f n) ∧
      IsZero ((C.filtration.obj (op q)).X n))
    (hJfin : ∀ n : ℤ, ∃ p q : ℤ, IsIso ((J.filtration.ι.app (op p)).f n) ∧
      IsZero ((J.filtration.obj (op q)).X n))
    (hI : ∀ n : ℤ, (evalFil I n).IsFilteredInjective) :
    ∃ (M : FilteredObject (CochainComplex 𝒜 ℤ) ℤᵒᵖ) (u : I ⟶ M) (v : M ⟶ J) (b : B ⟶ M)
      (huv : u.hom ≫ v.hom = 0), (ShortComplex.mk u.hom v.hom huv).ShortExact ∧
      α ≫ b = a ≫ u ∧ b ≫ v = β ≫ c ∧
      ∀ n : ℤ, ∃ (r : M.X.X n ⟶ I.X.X n) (s : J.X.X n ⟶ M.X.X n),
        u.hom.f n ≫ r = 𝟙 (I.X.X n) ∧ s ≫ v.hom.f n = 𝟙 (J.X.X n) ∧
        (∀ p : ℤ, ∃ rp : (M.filtration.obj (op p)).X n ⟶ (I.filtration.obj (op p)).X n,
          rp ≫ (I.filtration.ι.app (op p)).f n = (M.filtration.ι.app (op p)).f n ≫ r) ∧
        (∀ p : ℤ, ∃ sp : (J.filtration.obj (op p)).X n ⟶ (M.filtration.obj (op p)).X n,
          sp ≫ (M.filtration.ι.app (op p)).f n = (J.filtration.ι.app (op p)).f n ≫ s)

declarations.name: CochainComplex.exists_mono_isStrictHom_filteredQuasiIso_isStrictlyGE_injective_gradedPiece
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 05TW.** Let `𝒜` be an abelian category with enough injectives and let `K^•` be a
filtered cochain complex of `𝒜` with `K^n = 0` for `n < a` and with each `K^n` of finite
filtration, i.e. an object of `K^+(Fil^f(𝒜))`. Then there is a filtered quasi-isomorphism
`α : K^• ⟶ I^•`, that is, one whose graded pieces `gr^p(α)` are all quasi-isomorphisms, which is
moreover a strict monomorphism — degreewise, each `K^n ⟶ I^n` is a monomorphism with
`F^p K^n = (K^n) ∩ F^p I^n` — where `I^•` is a complex of filtered injective objects with
`I^n = 0` for `n < a`: every term `(I^n, F^• I^n)` is a filtered injective object of
`Fil^f(𝒜)`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem exists_mono_isStrictHom_filteredQuasiIso_isStrictlyGE_injective_gradedPiece
    (K : FilteredObject (CochainComplex 𝒜 ℤ) ℤᵒᵖ) (a : ℤ) [K.X.IsStrictlyGE a]
    (hK : ∀ n : ℤ, ∃ p q : ℤ, IsIso ((K.filtration.ι.app (op p)).f n) ∧
      IsZero ((K.filtration.obj (op q)).X n)) :
    ∃ (I : FilteredObject (CochainComplex 𝒜 ℤ) ℤᵒᵖ) (α : K ⟶ I)
      (_ : CochainComplex.filteredQuasiIso 𝒜 α) (_ : Mono α.hom)
      (_ : FilteredObject.IsStrictHom α) (_ : I.X.IsStrictlyGE a),
      ∀ n : ℤ, (evalFil I n).IsFilteredInjective

declarations.name: CochainComplex.exists_homotopy_zero_of_filteredAcyclic_of_injective_gradedPiece
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 05TX.** Let `𝒜` be an abelian category and let `K^•`, `I^•` be filtered cochain
complexes of `𝒜` whose terms have finite filtrations, i.e. objects of `K(Fil^f(𝒜))`. Assume `K^•`
is filtered acyclic, that is every `gr^p K^• = F^p K^•/F^{p + 1} K^•` is acyclic, and that `I^•`
is bounded below, `I^n = 0` for `n < n₀`, and consists of filtered injective objects of
`Fil^f(𝒜)`: every term `(I^n, F^• I^n)` is filtered injective. Then every morphism
`α : K^• ⟶ I^•` of filtered complexes is homotopic to zero by a filtered homotopy: there is a
homotopy `h` from `α` to `0` on the underlying complexes each of whose components
`h^{i,j} : K^i ⟶ I^j` carries `F^p K^i` into `F^p I^j`. Equivalently
`Hom_{K(Fil^f(𝒜))}(K^•, I^•) = 0`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem exists_homotopy_zero_of_filteredAcyclic_of_injective_gradedPiece
    {𝒜 : Type u} [Category.{v} 𝒜] [Abelian 𝒜]
    {K I : FilteredObject (CochainComplex 𝒜 ℤ) ℤᵒᵖ} (α : K ⟶ I) (n₀ : ℤ) [I.X.IsStrictlyGE n₀]
    (hK : filteredAcyclic 𝒜 K)
    (hKfin : ∀ n : ℤ, ∃ p q : ℤ, IsIso ((K.filtration.ι.app (op p)).f n) ∧
      IsZero ((K.filtration.obj (op q)).X n))
    (hI : ∀ n : ℤ, (evalFil I n).IsFilteredInjective) :
    ∃ h : Homotopy α.hom 0, ∀ i j p : ℤ,
      ∃ hp : (K.filtration.obj (op p)).X i ⟶ (I.filtration.obj (op p)).X j,
        hp ≫ (I.filtration.ι.app (op p)).f j
          = (K.filtration.ι.app (op p)).f i ≫ h.hom i j

declarations.name: CochainComplex.bijective_precomp_full_and_map_eq_iff_filteredHomotopy_of_injective_gradedPiece
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 05TY.** Let `𝒜` be an abelian category, let `Filf` be the class of filtered cochain
complexes of `𝒜` whose filtration is finite in each degree — so that `Filf.FullSubcategory` is
`K(Fil^f(𝒜))` — and let `Q` be a localisation of it at the filtered quasi-isomorphisms, that is,
the filtered derived category `DF(𝒜)` (Definition 05S2). Let `I^•` be a bounded below complex,
`I^n = 0` for `n < n₀`, consisting of filtered injective objects, that is with every `gr^p(I^n)`
an injective object of `𝒜`. Then:

1. for every filtered quasi-isomorphism `α : K^• ⟶ L^•` in `K(Fil^f(𝒜))`, precomposition with `α`
   is a bijection `Hom_{K(Fil^f(𝒜))}(L^•, I^•) ⟶ Hom_{K(Fil^f(𝒜))}(K^•, I^•)`: every
   `γ : K^• ⟶ I^•` is filtered homotopic to `α ≫ β` for some `β : L^• ⟶ I^•`, and if `α ≫ β` and
   `α ≫ β'` are filtered homotopic then so are `β` and `β'`;
2. for every `M^•` in `K(Fil^f(𝒜))`, `Hom_{K(Fil^f(𝒜))}(M^•, I^•) = Hom_{DF(𝒜)}(M^•, I^•)`: every
   `φ : Q.obj M^• ⟶ Q.obj I^•` is `Q.map f` for a morphism of filtered complexes `f : M^• ⟶ I^•`,
   and `Q.map f = Q.map g` exactly when `f` and `g` are filtered homotopic.

Here a *filtered homotopy* between morphisms of filtered complexes is a homotopy `h` of the
underlying complexes of `𝒜` each of whose components `h^{i,j}` carries `F^p` into `F^p`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem bijective_precomp_full_and_map_eq_iff_filteredHomotopy_of_injective_gradedPiece
    {𝒜 : Type u} [Category.{v} 𝒜] [Abelian 𝒜] {D : Type u'} [Category.{v'} D]
    (Filf : ObjectProperty (FilteredObject (CochainComplex 𝒜 ℤ) ℤᵒᵖ))
    (hFilf : ∀ K, Filf K ↔ ∀ n : ℤ, ∃ p q : ℤ,
      IsIso ((K.filtration.ι.app (op p)).f n) ∧ IsZero ((K.filtration.obj (op q)).X n))
    (Q : Filf.FullSubcategory ⥤ D)
    [Q.IsLocalization ((filteredQuasiIso 𝒜).inverseImage Filf.ι)]
    (I : Filf.FullSubcategory) (n₀ : ℤ) [I.obj.X.IsStrictlyGE n₀]
    (hI : ∀ p n : ℤ, Injective (((gr p).obj I.obj).X n)) :
    (∀ (K L : Filf.FullSubcategory) (α : K ⟶ L),
        (filteredQuasiIso 𝒜).inverseImage Filf.ι α →
        (∀ γ : K ⟶ I, ∃ β : L ⟶ I,
          ∃ h : Homotopy (Filf.ι.map (α ≫ β)).hom (Filf.ι.map γ).hom, ∀ i j p : ℤ,
            ∃ hp : (K.obj.filtration.obj (op p)).X i ⟶ (I.obj.filtration.obj (op p)).X j,
              hp ≫ (I.obj.filtration.ι.app (op p)).f j
                = (K.obj.filtration.ι.app (op p)).f i ≫ h.hom i j) ∧
        ∀ β β' : L ⟶ I,
          (∃ h : Homotopy (Filf.ι.map (α ≫ β)).hom (Filf.ι.map (α ≫ β')).hom, ∀ i j p : ℤ,
            ∃ hp : (K.obj.filtration.obj (op p)).X i ⟶ (I.obj.filtration.obj (op p)).X j,
              hp ≫ (I.obj.filtration.ι.app (op p)).f j
                = (K.obj.filtration.ι.app (op p)).f i ≫ h.hom i j) →
          ∃ h : Homotopy (Filf.ι.map β).hom (Filf.ι.map β').hom, ∀ i j p : ℤ,
            ∃ hp : (L.obj.filtration.obj (op p)).X i ⟶ (I.obj.filtration.obj (op p)).X j,
              hp ≫ (I.obj.filtration.ι.app (op p)).f j
                = (L.obj.filtration.ι.app (op p)).f i ≫ h.hom i j) ∧
      ∀ M : Filf.FullSubcategory,
        (∀ φ : Q.obj M ⟶ Q.obj I, ∃ f : M ⟶ I, Q.map f = φ) ∧
        ∀ f g : M ⟶ I, Q.map f = Q.map g ↔
          ∃ h : Homotopy (Filf.ι.map f).hom (Filf.ι.map g).hom, ∀ i j p : ℤ,
            ∃ hp : (M.obj.filtration.obj (op p)).X i ⟶ (I.obj.filtration.obj (op p)).X j,
              hp ≫ (I.obj.filtration.ι.app (op p)).f j
                = (M.obj.filtration.ι.app (op p)).f i ≫ h.hom i j

declarations.name: exists_filteredColimit_free_with_injective_reduction_and_isMittagLeffler
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 05U7.** Let `A → B` be a local homomorphism of local rings which is
essentially of finite type, and let `N` be a finite `B`-module which is flat as an `A`-module. If
`A` is henselian, then `N` is a filtered colimit `N = colim_i F_i` of free `A`-modules `F_i` such
that every transition map `F_i → F_{i'}` of the system induces an injective map
`F_i/𝔪_A F_i → F_{i'}/𝔪_A F_{i'}`. Also, `N` is a Mittag-Leffler `A`-module.

The colimit is computed in `ModuleCat A`, in the joint universe of `A` and `N`, so its vertex is
compared with the universe lift of `N`; `F_i/𝔪_A F_i` is `F_i ⧸ 𝔪_A • ⊤` and the induced map is
`Submodule.mapQ`. The Mittag-Leffler condition is that of Stacks 059F, with the finitely
presented source and the test module in arbitrary universes.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_filteredColimit_free_with_injective_reduction_and_isMittagLeffler
    {A : Type u} {B : Type v} {N : Type uM} [CommRing A] [CommRing B]
    [IsLocalRing B] [HenselianLocalRing A]
    [Algebra A B] [IsLocalHom (algebraMap A B)]
    (hB : Algebra.EssFiniteType A B)
    [AddCommGroup N] [Module A N] [Module B N] [IsScalarTower A B N]
    [Module.Finite B N] [Module.Flat A N] :
    (∃ (I : Type (max u uM)) (_ : SmallCategory I) (_ : IsFiltered I)
      (F : I ⥤ ModuleCat.{max u uM} A) (c : Cocone F),
      (∀ i, Module.Free A (F.obj i)) ∧
      (∀ {i j : I} (f : i ⟶ j), Function.Injective
        (Submodule.mapQ
          (maximalIdeal A • (⊤ : Submodule A (F.obj i)))
          (maximalIdeal A • (⊤ : Submodule A (F.obj j)))
          (F.map f).hom
          (Submodule.smul_top_le_comap_smul_top (maximalIdeal A)
            (F.map f).hom))) ∧
      Nonempty (IsColimit c) ∧
      Nonempty (c.pt ≅ ModuleCat.of A (ULift.{u} N))) ∧
    IsMittagLeffler.{u, uP, uM, max u uQ, uN} A N

declarations.name: isMittagLeffler_of_flat_finite_essFiniteType_local
declarations.doc:
Let `A → B` be an essentially finite type local homomorphism of local rings with `A`
henselian, and let `N` be a finite `B`-module which is flat over `A`. Then `N` is a
Mittag-Leffler `A`-module.
declarations.statement:
theorem isMittagLeffler_of_flat_finite_essFiniteType_local
    {A : Type u} {B : Type v} {N : Type uM} [CommRing A] [CommRing B]
    [IsLocalRing B] [HenselianLocalRing A]
    [Algebra A B] [IsLocalHom (algebraMap A B)]
    (hB : Algebra.EssFiniteType A B)
    [AddCommGroup N] [Module A N] [Module B N] [IsScalarTower A B N]
    [Module.Finite B N] [Module.Flat A N] :
    IsMittagLeffler.{u, uP, uM, max u uQ, uN} A N
declarations.comment: the Mittag-Leffler conclusion

declarations.name: exists_filteredColimit_free_with_injective_reduction
declarations.doc:
Let `A` be a henselian local ring, `A → B` a local homomorphism of local rings with `B`
essentially of finite type over `A`, and `N` a finite `B`-module which is flat over `A`. Then `N`
is a filtered colimit of free `A`-modules `F i` such that every transition map `F i → F j` induces
an injective map `F i / 𝔪_A F i → F j / 𝔪_A F j`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem exists_filteredColimit_free_with_injective_reduction
    {A : Type u} {B : Type v} {N : Type uM} [CommRing A] [CommRing B]
    [IsLocalRing B] [HenselianLocalRing A]
    [Algebra A B] [IsLocalHom (algebraMap A B)]
    (hB : Algebra.EssFiniteType A B)
    [AddCommGroup N] [Module A N] [Module B N] [IsScalarTower A B N]
    [Module.Finite B N] [Module.Flat A N] :
    ∃ (I : Type (max u uM)) (_ : SmallCategory I) (_ : IsFiltered I)
      (F : I ⥤ ModuleCat.{max u uM} A) (c : Cocone F),
      (∀ i, Module.Free A (F.obj i)) ∧
      (∀ {i j : I} (f : i ⟶ j), Function.Injective
        (Submodule.mapQ
          (maximalIdeal A • (⊤ : Submodule A (F.obj i)))
          (maximalIdeal A • (⊤ : Submodule A (F.obj j)))
          (F.map f).hom
          (Submodule.smul_top_le_comap_smul_top (maximalIdeal A)
            (F.map f).hom))) ∧
      Nonempty (IsColimit c) ∧
      Nonempty (c.pt ≅ ModuleCat.of A (ULift.{u} N))
declarations.comment: filtered-colimit presentation

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.conclusion_of_injectiveModuloMaximalIdeal
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 05U9.** Let `A → B` be a local homomorphism of local rings which is
essentially of finite type, let `M` be a flat `A`-module, let `N` be a finite `B`-module and let
`u : N → M` be an `A`-linear map whose reduction `ū : N ⧸ 𝔪_AN → M ⧸ 𝔪_AM` is injective. Then

1. `u` is `A`-universally injective,
2. `N` is of finite presentation over `B`, and
3. `N` is flat over `A`.

The hypotheses are the data of Situation 0AT0
(`AlgebraicGeometry.InjectiveModuloMaximalIdealSituation`) and the three conclusions are
`AlgebraicGeometry.InjectiveModuloMaximalIdealConclusion`.

Stacks 0AT2 reduces all three to the case where `B` is a localization at a prime of a
polynomial algebra over `A` in finitely many variables and `N` is of finite presentation over
`B`, and `AlgebraicGeometry.conclusion_of_presentation` settles that case through Claim 1 of the
source's proof.
declarations.statement:
theorem conclusion_of_injectiveModuloMaximalIdeal
    (S : InjectiveModuloMaximalIdealSituation.{u₁, u₂, u₃, u₄}) :
    InjectiveModuloMaximalIdealConclusion.{u₅} S
declarations.comment: universal injectivity, finite presentation and flatness

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.isFlatOverAt_iff_forall_isAssociatedPoint_specializes
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 05UA.** Let `f : X ⟶ S` be locally of finite type, let `F` be a quasi-coherent
`𝒪_X`-module of finite type and let `x ∈ X`. Then `F` is flat over `S` at `x` if and only if `F`
is flat over `S` at every associated point of the restriction of `F` to the fibre over `f x`
which specializes to `x`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isFlatOverAt_iff_forall_isAssociatedPoint_specializes {X S : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ S)
    [LocallyOfFiniteType f] (F : X.Modules) [F.IsQuasicoherent] [F.IsFiniteType] (x : X) :
    IsFlatOverAt f.toLRSHom.toShHom F x ↔
      ∀ x' : f.fiber (f x),
        x' ∈ Stacks.Divisors.associatedPoints
            ((Scheme.Modules.pullback (f.fiberι (f x))).obj F) →
          f.fiberι (f x) x' ⤳ x → IsFlatOverAt f.toLRSHom.toShHom F (f.fiberι (f x) x')
declarations.comment:
`Ass_{X_s}(F_s)` is `Stacks.Divisors.associatedPoints` of the pullback of `F` to
the scheme-theoretic fibre `f.fiber (f x)`, and flatness at a point is `IsFlatOverAt`.

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.isFlatOver_of_isFlatOverAt_closedFiber
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 05UB.** Let `S` be a local scheme with closed point `s`, let
`f : X ⟶ S` be locally of finite type and let `F` be a finite type quasi-coherent
`𝒪_X`-module. If every point of `Ass_{X/S}(F)` specializes to a point of the closed fibre
`X_s`, and `F` is flat over `S` at every point of `X_s`, then `F` is flat over `S`.

The criterion of Stacks 05UA is
`isFlatOverAt_iff_forall_isAssociatedPoint_specializes`, read at every point of the source.
Everything else is `isFlatOverAt_of_mem_relativeAssassin`: the two hypotheses on `F` give
flatness at every point of the relative assassin, which is what that criterion tests.
declarations.statement:
theorem isFlatOver_of_isFlatOverAt_closedFiber
    {X S : Scheme.{u}} [IsAffine S] [IsLocalRing Γ(S, ⊤)]
    (s : S) (_hs : s ∈ closedPoints S)
    (f : X ⟶ S) [LocallyOfFiniteType f]
    (F : X.Modules) [F.IsQuasicoherent] [F.IsFiniteType]
    (hass : ∀ x ∈ Stacks.Divisors.relativeAssassin f F,
      ∃ y : f.fiber s, Specializes x (f.fiberι s y))
    (hflat : ∀ y : f.fiber s, IsFlatOverAt f.toLRSHom.toShHom F (f.fiberι s y)) :
    IsFlatOver f.toLRSHom.toShHom F
declarations.comment:
`Ass_{X/S}(F)` is `Stacks.Divisors.relativeAssassin`, the closed fibre `X_s` is
`f.fiber s` placed in `X` by `f.fiberι s`, and flatness over the base at a point is
`IsFlatOverAt`. A local scheme is an affine scheme whose ring of global sections is local.

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.FreeAtGenericPointsSituation.isImmersion_representableBy_fittingRankStratum
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 05UC.** In Situation 05MP, for each `p ≥ 0` the functor `H_p` of
05MR is representable by a locally closed immersion `S_p ⟶ S`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isImmersion_representableBy_fittingRankStratum :
    ∃ W : Over D.S, IsImmersion W.hom ∧
      Nonempty ((D.freeAtGenericPointsFunctor p).RepresentableBy W)
declarations.comment: representability of H_p by a locally closed immersion

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.FreeAtGenericPointsSituation.finitePresentation_hom_of_representableBy
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 05UC.** In Situation 05MP, if `ℱ` is of finite presentation then
`S_p ⟶ S` is of finite presentation.

The assertion is proved for an arbitrary morphism representing the generic-rank functor, which
is legitimate because any two representatives are isomorphic over the base.
declarations.statement:
theorem finitePresentation_hom_of_representableBy [D.F.IsFinitePresentation]
    {W : Over D.S} (e : (D.freeAtGenericPointsFunctor p).RepresentableBy W) :
    FinitePresentation W.hom
declarations.comment: finite presentation of S_p ⟶ S when the module is of finite presentation

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.FlatDimensionSituation.isFlat_etaleChart_and_iff_of_relativeAssassin_subset
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 05UD.** In Situation 05MT, let `h : X' ⟶ X` be étale and let `F'_n` be
the functor of Stacks 05MU for `(f ∘ h, h^* F)`. Then `F_n` is a subfunctor of `F'_n`, and if
`h(X')` contains `Ass_{X/S}(F)` then `F_n = F'_n`.

Both functors are subterminal, so the first assertion is the implication between the two
conditions after every base change `T ⟶ S`, and the second is their equivalence.
declarations.statement:
theorem isFlat_etaleChart_and_iff_of_relativeAssassin_subset {X' : Scheme.{u}} (h : X' ⟶ D.X)
    [Etale h] :
    (∀ T : Over D.S, D.IsFlatInDimensionsGEAfterBaseChange T →
      (D.etaleChart h).IsFlatInDimensionsGEAfterBaseChange T) ∧
    (Stacks.Divisors.relativeAssassin D.f D.F ⊆ Set.range h → ∀ T : Over D.S,
      D.IsFlatInDimensionsGEAfterBaseChange T ↔
        (D.etaleChart h).IsFlatInDimensionsGEAfterBaseChange T)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.FreeAtGenericPointsSituation.exists_isSheaf_flatDimensionFunctor_and_iso_coproduct
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 05UE.** Let `f : X ⟶ S` be a smooth morphism of affine schemes with
geometrically irreducible fibres of dimension `d` and let `F` be a quasi-coherent `𝒪_X`-module
of finite presentation. Then there is a `c ≥ 0` with
```
F_d = ∐_{p = 0, …, c} H_p
```
where `F_d` is the functor of flatness in dimensions `≥ d` of Stacks 05MT and (05MU) and `H_p`
is the functor of Stacks 05MP, as functors on schemes over `S`.

The functor `F_d` itself (lifted to `Type (u + 1)`) is a Zariski sheaf, by the fpqc sheaf
property of Stacks 05MV, and as a sheaf it is isomorphic to the coproduct, in Zariski sheaves
over `S`, of the `H_p` for `p ≤ c`. The coproduct is the one of sheaves: the pointwise disjoint
union of the subterminal presheaves `H_p` is not a sheaf (it has `c + 1` elements over `∅`, and
misses the sections over a disconnected `T` with different generic ranks on its pieces), and
its sheafification is the coproduct of sheaves.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_isSheaf_flatDimensionFunctor_and_iso_coproduct [IsAffine D.X] [IsAffine D.S]
    [D.F.IsFinitePresentation] {d : ℕ} (hd : RelativeDimension D.f d) :
    ∃ (c : ℕ) (h : Presheaf.IsSheaf (Scheme.zariskiTopology.over D.S)
        ((D.toFlatDimensionSituation d).flatDimensionFunctor ⋙ uliftFunctor.{u + 1})),
      Nonempty ((⟨_, h⟩ : Sheaf (Scheme.zariskiTopology.over D.S) (Type (u + 1))) ≅
        ∐ fun p : Fin (c + 1) ↦
          (presheafToSheaf (Scheme.zariskiTopology.over D.S) (Type (u + 1))).obj
            (D.freeAtGenericPointsFunctor p.val ⋙ uliftFunctor.{u + 1}))

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.FlatDimensionSituation.exists_mono_finitePresentation_representableBy
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 05UF.** In Situation 05MT, let `s` be a point of `S` and let `d = n` be
the bound of the situation. Assume that

1. there exists a complete dévissage of `F/X/S` over `s`,
2. `X` is of finite presentation over `S`,
3. `F` is an `𝒪_X`-module of finite presentation, and
4. `F` is flat over `S` in dimensions `≥ d + 1`.

Then, after replacing `S` by an open neighbourhood `U` of `s`, the functor `F_d` of Stacks 05MU
is representable by a monomorphism `Z_d ⟶ U` of finite presentation.

Hypothesis (1) is the source's own: the existence of a complete dévissage is assumed by Tag
05UF, and is produced étale locally (Tag 05HU) only in the proof of Tag 05UG.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_mono_finitePresentation_representableBy (s : D.S)
    (hdev : Nonempty (CompleteDevissage D.f D.F s)) (hf : FinitePresentation D.f)
    [D.F.IsFinitePresentation] (h : IsFlatOverInDimensionsGE D.f D.F (D.n + 1)) :
    ∃ U : D.S.Opens, s ∈ U ∧ ∃ Z : Over U.toScheme,
      Mono Z.hom ∧ FinitePresentation Z.hom ∧
        Nonempty ((D.openFlatDimensionFunctor U).RepresentableBy Z)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.FlatDimensionSituation.exists_mono_finitePresentation_representableBy_of_isPure
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 05UG.** In Situation 05MT, assume moreover that `f` is of finite
presentation, that `F` is an `𝒪_X`-module of finite presentation, and that `F` is pure relative
to `S`. Then `F_n` is representable by a monomorphism `Z_n ⟶ S` of finite presentation.

`f` of finite presentation is spelled out as locally of finite presentation, quasi-compact and
quasi-separated.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_mono_finitePresentation_representableBy_of_isPure [LocallyOfFinitePresentation D.f]
    [QuasiCompact D.f] [QuasiSeparated D.f] [D.F.IsFinitePresentation]
    (hpure : IsPureRelative D.f D.F) :
    ∃ Z : Over D.S, Mono Z.hom ∧ FinitePresentation Z.hom ∧
      Nonempty (D.flatDimensionFunctor.RepresentableBy Z)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.exists_mono_finitePresentation_representableBy_of_isPureRelative
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 05UH, part (1).** Let `f : X ⟶ S` be of finite
presentation and let `F` be an `𝒪_X`-module of finite presentation which is pure relative to
`S`. Then the universal flattening `Z ⟶ S` of `F` exists and is a monomorphism of finite
presentation.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_mono_finitePresentation_representableBy_of_isPureRelative
    {X S : Scheme.{u}}
    (f : X ⟶ S) [LocallyOfFinitePresentation f] [QuasiCompact f] [QuasiSeparated f]
    (F : X.Modules) [F.IsQuasicoherent] [F.IsFiniteType] [F.IsFinitePresentation]
    (hpure : IsPureRelative f F) :
    ∃ Z : Over S, Mono Z.hom ∧ FinitePresentation Z.hom ∧
      Nonempty (Functor.RepresentableBy
        ({ S := S, X := X, f := f, F := F, isQuasicoherent := ‹F.IsQuasicoherent› } :
          FlatnessSituation.{u}).flatFunctor Z)
declarations.comment: part (1)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.exists_mono_finitePresentation_representableBy_of_isSchemePureRelative
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 05UH, part (2).** Let `f : X ⟶ S` be of finite
presentation and let `X` be pure relative to `S`. Then the universal flattening `Z ⟶ S` of `X`
exists and is a monomorphism of finite presentation.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_mono_finitePresentation_representableBy_of_isSchemePureRelative
    {X S : Scheme.{u}}
    (f : X ⟶ S) [LocallyOfFinitePresentation f] [QuasiCompact f] [QuasiSeparated f]
    (hpure : IsSchemePureRelative f) :
    ∃ Z : Over S, Mono Z.hom ∧ FinitePresentation Z.hom ∧
      Nonempty ((structureSheafFlatnessSituation f).flatFunctor.RepresentableBy Z)
declarations.comment: part (2)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.exists_mono_finitePresentation_representableBy_of_isProper
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 05UH, part (3).** Let `f : X ⟶ S` be proper
and of finite presentation and let `F` be an `𝒪_X`-module of finite presentation. Then the
universal flattening `Z ⟶ S` of `F` exists and is a monomorphism of finite presentation.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_mono_finitePresentation_representableBy_of_isProper
    {X S : Scheme.{u}}
    (f : X ⟶ S) [IsProper f] [LocallyOfFinitePresentation f] (F : X.Modules)
    [F.IsQuasicoherent] [F.IsFinitePresentation] :
    ∃ Z : Over S, Mono Z.hom ∧ FinitePresentation Z.hom ∧
      Nonempty (Functor.RepresentableBy
        ({ S := S, X := X, f := f, F := F, isQuasicoherent := ‹F.IsQuasicoherent› } :
          FlatnessSituation.{u}).flatFunctor Z)
declarations.comment: part (3)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.exists_mono_finitePresentation_representableBy_structureSheaf_of_isProper
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 05UH, part (4).** Let `f : X ⟶ S` be proper
and of finite presentation. Then the universal flattening `Z ⟶ S` of `X` exists, and it is a
monomorphism of finite presentation.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_mono_finitePresentation_representableBy_structureSheaf_of_isProper
    {X S : Scheme.{u}}
    (f : X ⟶ S) [IsProper f] [LocallyOfFinitePresentation f] :
    ∃ Z : Over S, Mono Z.hom ∧ FinitePresentation Z.hom ∧
      Nonempty ((structureSheafFlatnessSituation f).flatFunctor.RepresentableBy Z)
declarations.comment: part (4)

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.Functor.isStackInSetoids_twoFibreProduct
declarations.doc:
Let `𝒯` be a stack in groupoids and `𝒮` a stack over the site `(𝒞, J)`, and let `ℛ` be a
stack in setoids. Let `f : 𝒯 ⥤ 𝒮` and `g : ℛ ⥤ 𝒮` be 1-morphisms with `f` faithful. Then the
2-fibre product `𝒯 ×_{f, 𝒮, g} ℛ` is a stack in setoids.
declarations.statement:
theorem Functor.isStackInSetoids_twoFibreProduct (J : GrothendieckTopology 𝒞)
    (h𝒯 : Functor.IsStack p𝒯 J) (g𝒯 : p𝒯.IsFiberedInGroupoids)
    (hℛ : pℛ.IsStackInSetoids J) (h𝒮 : Functor.IsStack p𝒮 J)
    (hF : p𝒯.IsFibredOneMorphism p𝒮 f) (hG : pℛ.IsFibredOneMorphism p𝒮 g) [f.Faithful] :
    (TwoFibreProductOver.structureFunctor p𝒯 pℛ p𝒮 f g).IsStackInSetoids J

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.Functor.isStackInSetoids_twoFibreProduct_of_isStackInSetoids
declarations.doc:
Let `𝒮` be a stack over the site `(𝒞, J)` and let `𝒮₁`, `𝒮₂` be stacks in setoids, with
1-morphisms `f_i : 𝒮_i ⥤ 𝒮`. Then `𝒮₁ ×_{f₁, 𝒮, f₂} 𝒮₂` is a stack in setoids.
declarations.statement:
theorem Functor.isStackInSetoids_twoFibreProduct_of_isStackInSetoids
    (J : GrothendieckTopology 𝒞)
    (h𝒯 : p𝒯.IsStackInSetoids J) (hℛ : pℛ.IsStackInSetoids J)
    (h𝒮 : Functor.IsStack p𝒮 J)
    (hF : p𝒯.IsFibredOneMorphism p𝒮 f) (hG : pℛ.IsFibredOneMorphism p𝒮 g) :
    (TwoFibreProductOver.structureFunctor p𝒯 pℛ p𝒮 f g).IsStackInSetoids J

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.full_and_faithful_homFunctor_of_mono_representingMaps
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 05UK, with Stacks 003Z: the implication (1) ⟹ (2) of Stacks 04ZZ.** A 1-morphism
`j : 𝒳 ⟶ 𝒴` of categories fibred in groupoids over the big fppf site of `S` which is
representable by algebraic spaces and all of whose representing structural morphisms are
monomorphisms has fully faithful underlying functor.

Faithfulness is Stacks 04Y5 and uses only representability. For fullness: a morphism of the fibre
`𝒴_U` out of `j(a)` makes a second object of the fibre of `(Sch/U)_fppf ×_𝒴 𝒳` over the terminal
object of `(Sch/U)_fppf`, next to the one given by `a` itself; the representing algebraic space
has at most one section there because its structural morphism is injective on sections, so the two
objects are isomorphic and the `𝒳`-component of the isomorphism is the preimage sought.
declarations.statement:
theorem full_and_faithful_homFunctor_of_mono_representingMaps
    (B : BigFppfSite.{u}) (S : Scheme.{u}) (hS : B.Contains S)
    {𝒳 𝒴 : CatFiberedInGroupoids.{u, v, u + 1, w} (BigFppfOver B S hS)} (j : 𝒳 ⟶ 𝒴)
    (hj : IsRepresentableByAlgebraicSpaces B S hS j.hom)
    (hmono : ∀ (U : BigFppfOver B S hS)
      (y : BigFppfOver B U.left.1 U.left.2 ⥤ 𝒴.val.obj)
      (_hy : y ⋙ 𝒴.val.p = Over.map U.hom)
      (F : (BigFppfOver B U.left.1 U.left.2)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u)
      (hF : IsAlgebraicSpace B U.left.1 U.left.2 F),
        Nonempty (StacksRepresentableCFG.EquivalenceOver
          (TwoFibreProductOver.fst (Over.map U.hom) 𝒳.val.p 𝒴.val.p y
            (CatFiberedInGroupoids.homFunctor j))
          (presheafOfCategories (F ⋙ typeToCat)).p) →
        Mono (algebraicSpaceMap B S hS U
          ((spacesOverSmallerBaseFunctor B U.left.1 S U.left.2 hS U.hom).obj ⟨F, hF⟩)).hom) :
    (CatFiberedInGroupoids.homFunctor j).Full ∧
      (CatFiberedInGroupoids.homFunctor j).Faithful

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.isAlgebraicStack_of_smoothPresentation
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 05UL.** A stack in groupoids over the big fppf site of `S` which receives a
1-morphism from a category representable by an algebraic space that is representable by
algebraic spaces, surjective and smooth is an algebraic stack.
declarations.statement:
theorem isAlgebraicStack_of_smoothPresentation (v : 𝒰 ⟶ 𝒳)
    (h𝒳 : 𝒳.val.p.IsStack (BigFppfOver.topology B S hS))
    (h𝒰 : IsRepresentableByAlgebraicSpace B S hS 𝒰)
    (hv : IsRepresentableByAlgebraicSpaces B S hS v.hom)
    (hsurj : HasRelativeProperty.{u, u, u + 1, u + 1} B S hS
      (Space.surjectiveMorphismProperty B S hS) v hv)
    (hsmooth : HasRelativeProperty.{u, u, u + 1, u + 1} B S hS
      (Space.smoothMorphismProperty B S hS) v hv) :
    IsAlgebraicStack.{u, w} B S hS 𝒳.val

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.isAlgebraicStack_source_of_isRepresentableByAlgebraicSpaces
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 05UM.** If a 1-morphism `j : 𝒳 ⟶ 𝒴` of categories fibred in groupoids over the big
fppf site of `S` is representable by algebraic spaces and `𝒴` is an algebraic stack over `S`,
then `𝒳` is an algebraic stack over `S`.

The scheme atlas of `𝒴` base changes along `j` to a 1-morphism `W ⟶ 𝒳` which is again
representable by algebraic spaces (Stacks 0302), surjective and smooth (Stacks 045C), with `W`
representable by an algebraic space (Stacks 0300); the diagonal of `𝒳` is inherited from that of
`𝒴`, so the form of Stacks 05UL that takes the diagonal as a hypothesis applies.

The same statement is the algebraic-stack clause of **Stacks 05UN**, whose stack-in-groupoids
clause is `AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.isStack_of_isRepresentableByAlgebraicSpaces`; the two
clauses together are
`AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.isStack_and_isAlgebraicStack_of_isRepresentableByAlgebraicSpaces`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isAlgebraicStack_source_of_isRepresentableByAlgebraicSpaces (j : 𝒳 ⟶ 𝒴)
    (hj : IsRepresentableByAlgebraicSpaces B S hS j.hom)
    (h𝒴 : IsAlgebraicStack.{u, w} B S hS 𝒴.val) :
    IsAlgebraicStack.{u, w} B S hS 𝒳.val

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.isStack_and_isAlgebraicStack_of_isRepresentableByAlgebraicSpaces
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 05UN.** Let `j : 𝒳 ⟶ 𝒴` be a 1-morphism of categories fibred in groupoids over the
big fppf site of `S` which is representable by algebraic spaces. If `𝒴` is a stack in groupoids
then so is `𝒳`, and if `𝒴` is an algebraic stack then so is `𝒳`.

The first clause is `AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.isStack_of_isRepresentableByAlgebraicSpaces`, the
second `AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.isAlgebraicStack_source_of_isRepresentableByAlgebraicSpaces`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isStack_and_isAlgebraicStack_of_isRepresentableByAlgebraicSpaces (j : 𝒳 ⟶ 𝒴)
    (hj : IsRepresentableByAlgebraicSpaces B S hS j.hom) :
    (𝒴.val.p.IsStack (BigFppfOver.topology B S hS) →
        𝒳.val.p.IsStack (BigFppfOver.topology B S hS)) ∧
      (IsAlgebraicStack.{u, w} B S hS 𝒴.val → IsAlgebraicStack.{u, w} B S hS 𝒳.val)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.isStack_of_isRepresentableByAlgebraicSpaces
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 05UN, the stack-in-groupoids clause.** A category fibred in groupoids over the big
fppf site of `S` admitting a 1-morphism representable by algebraic spaces into a stack in
groupoids is itself a stack in groupoids.

This is the source's own proof of that clause: the criterion of Stacks 02ZY turns
representability by algebraic spaces into the faithfulness and sheaf hypotheses of
Stacks 0CKJ.
declarations.statement:
theorem isStack_of_isRepresentableByAlgebraicSpaces
    (B : AlgebraicGeometry.BigFppfSite.{u}) (S : Scheme.{u}) (hS : B.Contains S)
    {𝒳 𝒴 : CatFiberedInGroupoids.{u, v, u + 1, w}
      (AlgebraicGeometry.BigFppfOver B S hS)} (f : 𝒳 ⟶ 𝒴)
    (hf : AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.IsRepresentableByAlgebraicSpaces B S hS f.hom)
    (h𝒴 : 𝒴.val.p.IsStack (AlgebraicGeometry.BigFppfOver.topology B S hS)) :
    𝒳.val.p.IsStack (AlgebraicGeometry.BigFppfOver.topology B S hS)
declarations.comment: the stack-in-groupoids clause

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.exists_openSubstack_isOpenImmersion_smooth_surjective
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 05UP.** Let `𝒳` be an algebraic stack over `S`, let `U` be an algebraic space over
`S` with a surjective smooth 1-morphism `f : U ⟶ 𝒳`, and let `i : V ⟶ U` be an open immersion of
presheaves on the big fppf site of `S`. Then `V` is an algebraic space over `S` and there are an
algebraic stack `𝒴` over `S`, an open immersion `j : 𝒴 ⟶ 𝒳` and a surjective smooth 1-morphism
`q : V ⟶ 𝒴` making the square `(i, f, q, j)` 2-commute.

The algebraic stack `𝒴` is the open substack of `𝒳` whose points are the image of `|V|`, and `q`
is the factorization of `V ⟶ 𝒳` through it, so the three pieces are produced from one
construction rather than chosen from an existential; the 2-commutativity is an identity.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_openSubstack_isOpenImmersion_smooth_surjective
    {U V : (BigFppfOver B S hS)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u}
    (hU : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS U) {i : V ⟶ U}
    (hi : Space.IsOpenImmersion B S hS i)
    {𝒳 : AlgebraicStacks.{u, w} B S hS}
    (f : algebraicSpaceStack.{u, w} B S hS U hU ⟶ 𝒳)
    (hfsm : AlgebraicStacks.IsSmooth B S hS f)
    (_hfsurj : IsSurjective B S hS f) :
    ∃ (hV : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS V) (𝒴 : AlgebraicStacks.{u, w} B S hS)
      (j : 𝒴 ⟶ 𝒳) (q : algebraicSpaceStack.{u, w} B S hS V hV ⟶ 𝒴),
      AlgebraicStacks.IsOpenImmersion B S hS j ∧
        AlgebraicStacks.IsSmooth B S hS q ∧
          IsSurjective B S hS q ∧
            Nonempty (algebraicSpaceStackMap.{u, w} B S hS hV hU i ≫ f ≅ q ≫ j)
declarations.comment: the algebraic stack, the open immersion into the given stack and the smooth surjection from the open subspace, all three together with the 2-commutativity of the resulting square. The stack is constructed as the open substack of Stacks 04YM whose point set is the image of the points of the open subspace, by Stacks 06FJ

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.OpenSubstack.eq_of_isUnion
declarations.doc:
The union of a family of open substacks is unique: an open substack of `𝒳` which contains
every member of the family and is covered by the family is determined by the family. This is what
makes the notation `⋃_{i ∈ I} 𝒳ᵢ` of the source legitimate.
declarations.comment: uniqueness of the union

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.OpenSubstack.exists_openSubstack_of_isUnion
declarations.doc:
The members of a family of open substacks are open substacks of its union. If an open
substack `W` of `𝒳` is the union of a family `𝒰 : I → OpenSubstack 𝒳`, then each `𝒰 i` is an
open substack of `W`: there are open substacks `V i` of `W` whose objects are, under the
inclusion of `W` into `𝒳`, exactly the objects of `𝒰 i`.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_openSubstack_of_isUnion {𝒳 : AlgebraicStacks.{u, w} B S hS} {I : Type*}
    {𝒰 : I → OpenSubstack 𝒳} {W : OpenSubstack 𝒳} (h : IsUnion 𝒳 𝒰 W.property) :
    ∃ V : I → OpenSubstack (fullSubcategoryAlgebraicStack 𝒳 W.property W.isAlgebraic),
      ∀ (i : I) (x : 𝒳.val.val.obj),
        (𝒰 i).property x ↔ ∃ hx : W.property x, (V i).property ⟨x, hx⟩
declarations.comment: the members of the family are open substacks of the union

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.OpenSubstack.exists_isUnion
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 05UQ.** Let `𝒳` be an algebraic stack and `𝒳ᵢ ⊆ 𝒳`, `i ∈ I`, a collection of open
substacks. Then there is an open substack `⋃_{i ∈ I} 𝒳ᵢ ⊆ 𝒳` such that the `𝒳ᵢ` are open
substacks covering it.

The open substack is `AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.OpenSubstack.iUnion 𝒰`. It is the union of the
family in the sense of `AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.OpenSubstack.IsUnion`: it contains every `𝒳ᵢ`,
and every object of it lies, over the members of a covering sieve of the fppf topology, in some
`𝒳ᵢ`. Its points are `⋃_{i ∈ I} |𝒳ᵢ|`, so `∐_{i ∈ I} 𝒳ᵢ ⟶ ⋃_{i ∈ I} 𝒳ᵢ` is surjective. Each `𝒳ᵢ`
is an open substack `V i` of it. And it is the only open substack of `𝒳` that is the union of the
family, which is what makes the notation `⋃_{i ∈ I} 𝒳ᵢ` legitimate.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_isUnion {𝒳 : AlgebraicStacks.{u, w} B S hS} {I : Type*}
    (𝒰 : I → OpenSubstack 𝒳) :
    ∃ W : OpenSubstack 𝒳,
      (IsUnion 𝒳 𝒰 W.property ∧ W.pointSet B S hS = ⋃ i, (𝒰 i).pointSet B S hS ∧
        ∃ V : I → OpenSubstack (fullSubcategoryAlgebraicStack 𝒳 W.property W.isAlgebraic),
          ∀ (i : I) (x : 𝒳.val.val.obj),
            (𝒰 i).property x ↔ ∃ hx : W.property x, (V i).property ⟨x, hx⟩) ∧
      ∀ W' : OpenSubstack 𝒳, IsUnion 𝒳 𝒰 W'.property → W' = W

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.OpenSubstack.isUnion_pointsWithin
declarations.doc:
Let `Ω` be a set of points of `|𝒳|` consisting exactly of the classes of the field-valued
points of `𝒳` whose object lies in a member of the family. Then the locus
`AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.pointsWithin` of `Ω` is the union of the family: it contains every
member, and every object of it lies, over a covering sieve, in a member.
declarations.comment: the union of the family is the locus of the set of points lying in a member

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.exists_finset_pointSet_subset_of_isQuasiCompactStack
declarations.doc:
If a quasi-compact open substack `𝒳'` of an algebraic stack `𝒳` is covered by a family of
open substacks `𝒳ᵢ`, then finitely many of the `𝒳ᵢ` already cover the point set of `𝒳'`.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_finset_pointSet_subset_of_isQuasiCompactStack
    {𝒳 : AlgebraicStacks.{u, w} B S hS} (𝒳' : OpenSubstack 𝒳)
    (hqc : IsQuasiCompactStack.{u, w} B S hS
      (fullSubcategoryAlgebraicStack 𝒳 𝒳'.property 𝒳'.isAlgebraic).val
      (fullSubcategoryAlgebraicStack 𝒳 𝒳'.property 𝒳'.isAlgebraic).property)
    {I : Type*} (𝒰 : I → OpenSubstack 𝒳)
    (hcover : IsOpenSubstackCoverOn B S hS 𝒳 𝒳' 𝒰) :
    ∃ J : Finset I, 𝒳'.pointSet B S hS ⊆ ⋃ i ∈ J, (𝒰 i).pointSet B S hS
declarations.comment: the conclusion read on points: finitely many members of the family contain the point set of the quasi-compact open substack

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.exists_finset_le_of_isQuasiCompactStack
declarations.doc:
Let `𝒳` be an algebraic stack and `𝒳' ⊆ 𝒳` a quasi-compact open substack. Let `𝒳ᵢ ⊆ 𝒳`,
`i ∈ I`, be open substacks such that `𝒳' ⊆ ⋃_{i ∈ I} 𝒳ᵢ`, the union being
`AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.OpenSubstack.iUnion`. Then there is a finite subset `I' ⊆ I` such that
`𝒳' ⊆ ⋃_{i ∈ I'} 𝒳ᵢ`.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_finset_le_of_isQuasiCompactStack {𝒳 : AlgebraicStacks.{u, w} B S hS}
    (𝒳' : OpenSubstack 𝒳)
    (hqc : IsQuasiCompactStack.{u, w} B S hS
      (fullSubcategoryAlgebraicStack 𝒳 𝒳'.property 𝒳'.isAlgebraic).val
      (fullSubcategoryAlgebraicStack 𝒳 𝒳'.property 𝒳'.isAlgebraic).property)
    {I : Type*} (𝒰 : I → OpenSubstack 𝒳) (hle : 𝒳' ≤ OpenSubstack.iUnion 𝒰) :
    ∃ J : Finset I, 𝒳' ≤ OpenSubstack.iUnion (fun i : J => 𝒰 i)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.exists_finset_le_of_isQuasiCompactStack_unconditional
declarations.doc:
Let `𝒳'` be a quasi-compact open substack of an algebraic stack `𝒳` and let `𝒳ᵢ`, `i ∈ I`, be
open substacks of `𝒳` covering `𝒳'`. Then there is a finite `I' ⊆ I` such that `𝒳'` is contained
in every open substack containing `𝒳ᵢ` for all `i ∈ I'`, that is, `𝒳' ⊆ ⋃_{i ∈ I'} 𝒳ᵢ`.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_finset_le_of_isQuasiCompactStack_unconditional {𝒳 : AlgebraicStacks.{u, w} B S hS}
    (𝒳' : OpenSubstack 𝒳)
    (hqc : IsQuasiCompactStack.{u, w} B S hS
      (fullSubcategoryAlgebraicStack 𝒳 𝒳'.property 𝒳'.isAlgebraic).val
      (fullSubcategoryAlgebraicStack 𝒳 𝒳'.property 𝒳'.isAlgebraic).property)
    {I : Type*} (𝒰 : I → OpenSubstack 𝒳)
    (hcover : IsOpenSubstackCoverOn B S hS 𝒳 𝒳' 𝒰) :
    ∃ J : Finset I, ∀ W : OpenSubstack 𝒳,
      (∀ i ∈ J, (𝒰 i).property ≤ W.property) → 𝒳'.property ≤ W.property

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.Functor.final_of_isConnected_fiber
declarations.doc:
Any functor `F : I ⥤ I'` whose fibre categories are all connected and which is surjective on
arrows is final.
declarations.statement:
lemma CategoryTheory.Functor.final_of_isConnected_fiber {I I' : Type*} [Category* I] [Category* I']
    (F : I ⥤ I') [∀ i, IsConnected (F.Fiber i)] [F.SurjectiveOnArrows] :
    F.Final
declarations.comment: implies the lemma via `04E7`

declarations.name: colimit_flat_of_flat
declarations.doc:
Stacks 05UT: the direct limit (colimit) of a directed system of flat
$R$-modules is flat.
declarations.statement:
theorem colimit_flat_of_flat
    {R : Type*} [CommRing R]
    {ι : Type*} [Preorder ι] [IsDirected ι (· ≤ ·)] [Nonempty ι] [DecidableEq ι]
    (G : ι → Type*) [(i : ι) → AddCommGroup (G i)] [(i : ι) → Module R (G i)]
    (f : (i j : ι) → i ≤ j → G i →ₗ[R] G j) [DirectedSystem G (fun i j h => f i j h)]
    [∀ i, Module.Flat R (G i)] :
    Module.Flat R (Module.DirectLimit G f)

declarations.name: StacksColimitRingsFlat.flat_colimit
declarations.doc:
Let `{R_i, φ_{ii'}}` be a system of rings over the directed set `ι`, with colimit
`R = colim_i R_i`.

1. If `N` is an `R`-module which is flat as an `R_i`-module (via `R_i → R`) for all `i`, then
   `N` is flat as an `R`-module.
2. If each `M_i` is a flat `R_i`-module and the `f_{ii'} : M_i → M_{i'}` are
   `φ_{ii'}`-semilinear maps forming a system, then `M = colim_i M_i` (the colimit of the
   abelian groups, with its `R`-module structure `moduleDirectLimit`) is a flat `R`-module.
declarations.statement:
theorem flat_colimit :
    (∀ (N : Type*) [AddCommGroup N] [Module (ColimitRing G φ) N],
      (∀ i : ι, @Module.Flat (G i) N _ _ (Module.compHom N (structHom G φ i))) →
        Module.Flat (ColimitRing G φ) N) ∧
    ((∀ i : ι, Module.Flat (G i) (M i)) →
      Module.Flat (ColimitRing G φ) (_root_.DirectLimit M f))

declarations.name: Module.essentiallyOfFinitePresentation_and_flat_and_flat_of_flat_quotient_maximalIdeal
declarations.doc:
Let `R → S → S'` be local homomorphisms of local rings, let `𝔪` be the maximal
ideal of `R`, and let `M` be a nonzero `S'`-module of finite presentation. Assume `R → S'` is
essentially of finite presentation, `R → S` is essentially of finite type, `M` is flat over `R`,
and the fibre `M/𝔪M` is flat over `S/𝔪S`. Then `R → S` is essentially of finite presentation, `S`
is flat over `R`, and `M` is flat over `S`.

Here `𝔪S` is `(maximalIdeal R).map (algebraMap R S)` and `𝔪M` is `𝔪S • ⊤`, so that `M/𝔪M` is a
module over the fibre ring `S/𝔪S`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem
    Module.essentiallyOfFinitePresentation_and_flat_and_flat_of_flat_quotient_maximalIdeal
    {R S S' M : Type*} [CommRing R] [CommRing S] [CommRing S']
    [IsLocalRing R] [IsLocalRing S] [IsLocalRing S']
    [Algebra R S] [Algebra S S'] [Algebra R S'] [IsScalarTower R S S']
    [IsLocalHom (algebraMap R S)] [IsLocalHom (algebraMap S S')]
    [AddCommGroup M] [Module R M] [Module S M] [Module S' M]
    [IsScalarTower R S M] [IsScalarTower S S' M]
    [Algebra.EssFiniteType R S] [Module.FinitePresentation S' M] [Nontrivial M] [Module.Flat R M]
    [Module.Flat (S ⧸ (maximalIdeal R).map (algebraMap R S))
      (M ⧸ ((maximalIdeal R).map (algebraMap R S) • (⊤ : Submodule S M)))]
    (hS' : (algebraMap R S').EssentiallyOfFinitePresentation) :
    (algebraMap R S).EssentiallyOfFinitePresentation ∧ Module.Flat R S ∧ Module.Flat S M
declarations.comment:
"Essentially of finite type" is Mathlib's `Algebra.EssFiniteType` (Definition
00QM (1)); "essentially of finite presentation" is `RingHom.EssentiallyOfFinitePresentation`
(Definition 00QM (2)), Mathlib having no such predicate. The chain `R → S → S'` is
`IsScalarTower R S S'`, `𝔪S` is `(maximalIdeal R).map (algebraMap R S)` and `𝔪M` is `𝔪S • ⊤` over
`S`, so that the fibre `M/𝔪M` is a module over the ring `S/𝔪S`. "`M` is not zero" is
`Nontrivial M`. The three conclusions are conjoined; see the module docstring.

declarations.name: ToposPoint.epsilon_comp_eta
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 05UX.** For any set `E` there are canonical maps
`E ⟶ (p_* E)_p ⟶ E` whose composition is the identity of `E`.

Proof: apply naturality of the counit `ε` of `p⁻¹ ⊣ p_*` to the constant map
`i_e : PUnit → E`, then evaluate at `default : p⁻¹(p_*(PUnit))`.
declarations.statement: theorem epsilon_comp_eta (E : Type v) : p.epsilon E ∘ p.eta E = id

declarations.name: PointOfTopos.preservesLimitsOfSize_pushforward
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 05UY.** The pushforward `p_*` of a point of a topos commutes with arbitrary
limits, because it is a right adjoint.
declarations.statement: theorem preservesLimitsOfSize_pushforward : PreservesLimitsOfSize.{w₁, w₂} p.pushforward
declarations.comment: commutes with arbitrary limits

declarations.name: PointOfTopos.preservesFiniteLimits_pushforward
declarations.doc: **Stacks 05UY.** The pushforward `p_*` of a point of a topos is left exact.
declarations.statement: theorem preservesFiniteLimits_pushforward : PreservesFiniteLimits p.pushforward
declarations.comment: is left exact

declarations.name: PointOfTopos.faithful_pushforward
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 05UY.** The pushforward `p_*` of a point of a topos is faithful: the counit
`ε_E : p^{-1}p_*E → E` is a (split) epimorphism, and `ε` is natural.
declarations.statement: theorem faithful_pushforward : p.pushforward.Faithful
declarations.comment: is faithful

declarations.name: PointOfTopos.preservesEpimorphisms_pushforward
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 05UY.** The pushforward `p_*` of a point of a topos transforms surjections into
surjections: every epimorphism of sets is a *split* epimorphism, and a split epimorphism is
carried to a split epimorphism by any functor.
declarations.statement: theorem preservesEpimorphisms_pushforward : p.pushforward.PreservesEpimorphisms
declarations.comment:
transforms surjections into surjections. The other claim of the same sentence of
  the source — that `p_*` commutes with coequalizers — is FALSE and is not claimed anywhere in
  this file; see `Point.subsingleton_fiber_of_preservesCoequalizers`

declarations.name: PointOfTopos.reflectsMonomorphisms_pushforward
declarations.doc: **Stacks 05UY.** The pushforward `p_*` of a point of a topos reflects injections.
declarations.statement: theorem reflectsMonomorphisms_pushforward : p.pushforward.ReflectsMonomorphisms
declarations.comment: reflects injections

declarations.name: PointOfTopos.reflectsEpimorphisms_pushforward
declarations.doc: **Stacks 05UY.** The pushforward `p_*` of a point of a topos reflects surjections.
declarations.statement: theorem reflectsEpimorphisms_pushforward : p.pushforward.ReflectsEpimorphisms
declarations.comment: reflects surjections

declarations.name: PointOfTopos.reflectsIsomorphisms_pushforward
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 05UY.** The pushforward `p_*` of a point of a topos reflects isomorphisms: it
reflects both injections and surjections, and a map of sets which is both injective and
surjective is bijective.
declarations.statement: theorem reflectsIsomorphisms_pushforward : p.pushforward.ReflectsIsomorphisms
declarations.comment: reflects isomorphisms

declarations.name: PointOfTopos.preservesColimit_pushforward_of_equivalence
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 05UY, the coequalizer clause in its corrected form.** The pushforward `p_*` of a
point of a topos commutes with the coequalizer of `f, g : R ⇉ E` whenever the relation
`{(f r, g r)}` on `E` is an equivalence relation, i.e. it carries the quotient `E → E / ~` by an
equivalence relation to a coequalizer in `Sh(C)`.

The clause "commutes with coequalizers" of Stacks 05UY is false for arbitrary pairs
(`GrothendieckTopology.Point.not_preservesCoequalizers_pushforward_pointOfTopos_pointBot`), and
this is the statement that survives (see `errata.md`, 05UY). The quotient by an equivalence
relation is a split coequalizer (`Types.isSplitCoequalizerOfEquivalence`), and split coequalizers
are preserved by every functor (Mathlib's `IsSplitCoequalizer.map`).
declarations.statement:
theorem preservesColimit_pushforward_of_equivalence {R E : Type w} (f g : R ⟶ E)
    (h : _root_.Equivalence (Function.Coequalizer.Rel f g)) :
    PreservesColimit (parallelPair f g) p.pushforward
declarations.comment:
the coequalizer clause, corrected: `p_*` commutes with the coequalizer of a pair
  `R ⇉ E` which is an equivalence relation on `E`; for an arbitrary pair the clause is false, see
  `GrothendieckTopology.Point.not_preservesCoequalizers_pushforward_pointOfTopos_pointBot`

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.GrothendieckTopology.Point.not_preservesCoequalizers_pushforward_pointOfTopos_pointBot
declarations.doc:
**The coequalizer clause of Stacks 05UY is false.** There is a point `p` of a topos whose
pushforward `p_* : Set ⥤ Sh(C)` does not commute with coequalizers: take
`C = WalkingParallelPair`, `J = ⊥` (so that `Sh(C, ⊥)` is the category of presheaves,
`sheafBotEquivalence`) and `p` the point of the topos attached to the point `pointBot zero` of
the site, whose fibre functor is `Hom(zero, -)`, so that `u(one) = {left, right}` has two
elements. Since `Sh(C, ⊥) ⥤ PSh(C)` is an equivalence, a preservation of coequalizers by `p_*`
would make the skyscraper presheaf functor preserve them, which
`subsingleton_fiber_of_preservesCoequalizers` forbids.
declarations.statement:
theorem not_preservesCoequalizers_pushforward_pointOfTopos_pointBot :
    ¬PreservesColimitsOfShape WalkingParallelPair
      (pointBot.{0} (C := WalkingParallelPair) .zero).pointOfTopos.pushforward
declarations.comment:
the coequalizer clause is false: a point of the topos of presheaves on
  `WalkingParallelPair` whose pushforward does not commute with coequalizers; the corrected
  clause is `PointOfTopos.preservesColimit_pushforward_of_equivalence`

declarations.name: Stacks.Sheaves.StalkInverseImage.stalkAddEquiv
declarations.doc:
The stalk at `Φ` of the inverse image along `g` of a sheaf of `O`-modules is the stalk of
that sheaf at `Ψ`, as an isomorphism of additive groups. It is semilinear over
`Stacks.Sheaves.StalkInverseImage.stalkRingEquiv`; see
`Stacks.Sheaves.StalkInverseImage.stalkAddEquiv_smul`.
declarations.statement:
def stalkAddEquiv :
    (Stacks.sheafModuleFiber Ψ O).obj G ≃+
      (Stacks.sheafModuleFiber Φ (inverseImageRingSheaf g O)).obj
        ((inverseImageModules g O).obj G)
declarations.comment:
for sheaves of modules, at a point of a site, for a morphism of topoi whose
stalk functor at the target point is the inverse image followed by the stalk functor at the
source point

declarations.name: Stacks.Sheaves.StalkInverseImage.stalkAddEquiv_smul
declarations.doc:
The isomorphism of stalk modules is semilinear over the isomorphism of stalk rings: the
stalk at `Φ` of the inverse image of `G` is the stalk of `G` at `Ψ`, with the scalars carried
along `O_Ψ ≅ (g⁻¹O)_Φ`.
declarations.statement:
theorem stalkAddEquiv_smul (r : (Ψ.presheafFiber (A := RingCat.{w})).obj O.obj)
    (m : (Stacks.sheafModuleFiber Ψ O).obj G) :
    stalkAddEquiv g O Φ Ψ e G (r • m) =
      stalkRingEquiv g O Φ Ψ e r • stalkAddEquiv g O Φ Ψ e G m
declarations.comment: semilinearity of the comparison, for sheaves of modules

declarations.name: Stacks.Sheaves.StalkInverseImage.stalkNatIso
declarations.doc:
The stalk functor at `Ψ` is the inverse image of sheaves of modules followed by the stalk
functor at `Φ` and restriction of scalars along the isomorphism of stalk rings.
declarations.statement:
def stalkNatIso :
    Stacks.sheafModuleFiber Ψ O ≅
      inverseImageModules g O ⋙ Stacks.sheafModuleFiber Φ (inverseImageRingSheaf g O) ⋙
        ModuleCat.restrictScalars (stalkRingEquiv g O Φ Ψ e).toRingHom
declarations.comment: for sheaves of modules, as a natural isomorphism of stalk functors

declarations.name: Stacks.Sheaves.DerivedPullback.KFlatPullbackMorphismOfSites.targetStalkAddEquiv
declarations.doc:
**Module-level Stacks 05V1 at the named point of the target site.**  The stalk at `Φ` of
the inverse image of a sheaf of `O'`-modules is the stalk of that sheaf at `Ψ`, as an
isomorphism of additive groups; it is semilinear over `targetStalkRingEquiv`.
declarations.statement:
def targetStalkAddEquiv :
    (Stacks.sheafModuleFiber (targetPoint f hu Φ)
        (Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf Y.O)).obj G ≃+
      (Stacks.sheafModuleFiber Φ
          (inverseImageRingSheaf (f.toToposHom hu)
            (Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf Y.O))).obj
        ((inverseImageModules (f.toToposHom hu)
          (Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf Y.O)).obj G)
declarations.comment:
for sheaves of modules, at the point of the target site attached to a point of
the source site by part (2) of Stacks 00YA

declarations.name: Stacks.Sheaves.DerivedPullback.KFlatPullbackMorphismOfSites.targetStalkAddEquiv_smul
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 05V1 for sheaves of modules at the named point.**  The isomorphism of stalk
modules is semilinear over the isomorphism of stalk rings.
declarations.statement:
theorem targetStalkAddEquiv_smul
    (r : ((targetPoint f hu Φ).presheafFiber (A := RingCat.{u})).obj
      (Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf Y.O).obj)
    (m : (Stacks.sheafModuleFiber (targetPoint f hu Φ)
      (Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf Y.O)).obj G) :
    targetStalkAddEquiv f hu Φ G (r • m) =
      targetStalkRingEquiv f hu Φ r • targetStalkAddEquiv f hu Φ G m
declarations.comment:
semilinearity, at the point of the target site attached to a point of the source
site

declarations.name: Stacks.Sheaves.DerivedPullback.KFlatPullbackMorphismOfSites.targetStalkNatIso
declarations.doc:
**Module-level Stacks 05V1 at the named point, as a natural isomorphism of stalk
functors.**  The stalk functor at `Ψ` is the inverse image of sheaves of modules followed by
the stalk functor at `Φ` and restriction of scalars along the isomorphism of stalk rings.

This is the form a statement about complexes consumes:
`CategoryTheory.NatIso.mapHomologicalComplex` carries it to an isomorphism of the degreewise
functors on cochain complexes.
declarations.statement:
def targetStalkNatIso :
    Stacks.sheafModuleFiber (targetPoint f hu Φ) (Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf Y.O) ≅
      inverseImageModules (f.toToposHom hu) (Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf Y.O) ⋙
        Stacks.sheafModuleFiber Φ
            (inverseImageRingSheaf (f.toToposHom hu) (Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf Y.O)) ⋙
          ModuleCat.restrictScalars (targetStalkRingEquiv f hu Φ).toRingHom
declarations.comment:
for sheaves of modules, as a natural isomorphism of stalk functors, at the point
of the target site attached to a point of the source site

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.Functor.IsMorphismOfSites.exists_point_fiber_eq_and_sheafFiber_iso
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 05V1.** Let `f : D → C` be a morphism of sites given by the continuous functor
`u : C ⥤ D` (Stacks 00X1: `u_s` is exact) and let `q` be a point of `D` with fiber functor
`v = q.fiber`. Then `v ∘ u = u ⋙ q.fiber` is the fiber functor of a point `p` of `C`, and
there is an identification `(f⁻¹ F)_q ≅ F_p`, natural in the sheaf of sets `F` on `C`.

The point is `hu.comapPoint q` and the identification is `hu.sheafFiberComapPointIso q`.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_point_fiber_eq_and_sheafFiber_iso :
    haveI := hu.isContinuous
    ∃ p : Point.{u} J, p.fiber = u ⋙ q.fiber ∧
      Nonempty (p.sheafFiber (A := Type u) ≅
