        u.sheafPullback (Type u) J K ⋙ q.sheafFiber (A := Type u))
declarations.comment:
Stated for the morphisms of sites of Stacks 00X1
  (`Functor.IsMorphismOfSites`), with no flatness or cover-preservation assumption on `u`;
  the canonical point is `IsMorphismOfSites.comapPoint` and the canonical identification of
  stalk functors is `IsMorphismOfSites.sheafFiberComapPointIso`.

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.GrothendieckTopology.Point.sheafFiber_inverseImage
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks Project, Tag 05V2] at a point of the site.**  For a morphism of topoi `f` from
`Sh(C, J)` to `Sh(D, K)` and a point `Φ` of the site `(C, J)`, the fibre at `Φ` of the inverse
image of a sheaf `ℱ` on `(D, K)` is the stalk of `ℱ` at the composed point of `Sh(D, K)`.

No bridge between the two notions of point has to be built: a point of a site already *is* a point
of its topos, by `CategoryTheory.GrothendieckTopology.Point.pointOfTopos` (Stacks 00YA (1)), whose
inverse image is the fibre functor on the nose
(`CategoryTheory.GrothendieckTopology.Point.pointOfTopos_inverseImage`).  So
`MorphismOfTopoi.stalk_inverseImage` applies verbatim, and this statement is it.
declarations.comment: at a point of the site

declarations.name: MorphismOfTopoi.stalk_inverseImage
declarations.doc:
For a morphism of topoi `f : Sh(D) → Sh(C)`, a point `q` of `Sh(D)` and a sheaf `F` on `C`,
the stalk `(f⁻¹ F)_q` is the stalk `F_{f ∘ q}` at the composite point `f.compPoint q`.
declarations.statement:
theorem stalk_inverseImage (f : MorphismOfTopoi (Sheaf K (Type w)) (Sheaf J (Type w)))
    (q : PointOfTopos.{w, v', u'} K) (F : Sheaf J (Type w)) :
    q.stalk (f.inverseImage.obj F) = (f.compPoint q).stalk F

declarations.name: Stacks.StalkExact.exact_iff_forall_sheafFiber_exact_of_hasEnoughPoints
declarations.doc:
On a site with enough points, a short complex of abelian sheaves is exact if and only if its
stalks at all points are exact.

Points and "enough points" are Mathlib's (`GrothendieckTopology.Point`,
`GrothendieckTopology.HasEnoughPoints`); the form for the points of Stacks 00Y5 is
`Stacks.StalkExact.exact_iff_forall_abelianStalk_exact_of_hasEnoughSitePoints`.
declarations.statement:
theorem exact_iff_forall_sheafFiber_exact_of_hasEnoughPoints
    [GrothendieckTopology.HasEnoughPoints.{w} J] (S : ShortComplex (Sheaf J AddCommGrpCat.{w})) :
    S.Exact ↔ ∀ Φ : J.Point.{w}, (S.map (Φ.sheafFiber (A := AddCommGrpCat.{w}))).Exact
declarations.comment: enough Mathlib points (`GrothendieckTopology.HasEnoughPoints`)

declarations.name: Stacks.StalkExact.exact_iff_forall_abelianStalk_exact
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 05V3**, for the points of Stacks 00Y5. If `{p_i}_{i ∈ I}` is a conservative family
of points of the site, a short complex of abelian sheaves is exact if and only if its stalks at
the points `p_i` are exact.
declarations.statement:
theorem exact_iff_forall_abelianStalk_exact {I : Type t} {u : I → C ⥤ Type w}
    (hu : ∀ i, IsSitePoint K (u i)) (hc : IsConservativeFamilyOfSitePoints K u)
    (S : ShortComplex (Sheaf K.toGrothendieck AddCommGrpCat.{w})) :
    S.Exact ↔ ∀ i, (S.map (abelianStalk K (u i))).Exact
declarations.comment: conservative family of points in the sense of Stacks 00Y5

declarations.name: Stacks.StalkExact.exact_iff_forall_abelianStalk_exact_of_hasEnoughSitePoints
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 05V3**, for the points of Stacks 00Y5. If the site has enough points, a short complex
of abelian sheaves is exact if and only if its stalks at all points are exact.
declarations.statement:
theorem exact_iff_forall_abelianStalk_exact_of_hasEnoughSitePoints (h : HasEnoughSitePoints K)
    (S : ShortComplex (Sheaf K.toGrothendieck AddCommGrpCat.{w})) :
    S.Exact ↔ ∀ u : C ⥤ Type w, IsSitePoint K u → (S.map (abelianStalk K u)).Exact
declarations.comment: enough points, for the points of Stacks 00Y5

registrations.name: Stacks.StalkExact.exact_iff_forall_sheafFiber_exact
registrations.comment: conservative family of Mathlib points (`GrothendieckTopology.Point`)

declarations.name: Stacks.FlatChangeOfRings.isFlat_extendScalars
declarations.doc:

commutative rings takes a flat sheaf of modules to a flat sheaf of modules.
declarations.statement:
theorem isFlat_extendScalars (hG : SheafOfModules.IsFlat G) :
    SheafOfModules.IsFlat ((extendScalars f).obj G)

declarations.name: Stacks.FlatChangeOfRings.isFlat_pullback_ringSheafMapId

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.RingedToposHom.pullbackModulesSquareIso
declarations.doc:
**The formula of Stacks 05V5.** Let

```
  P ⟶ X
  ↓     ↓
  Q ⟶ Y
```

be a commutative square of morphisms of ringed topoi — the hypothesis `h` says that the two
composites `P ⟶ Y` agree. Then pulling a sheaf of `O_Y`-modules back along the bottom and then
down the right is the same as pulling it back down the left and then along the top:

`f^* ⋙ π^* ≅ ρ^* ⋙ γ^*`.

Stacks 05V5 is this applied to the square whose left column is a point `p` of `Sh(C)`, whose
right column is the point `q = f ∘ p` of `Sh(D)`, and whose bottom row is the induced morphism
of ringed points: the left-hand composite is then `F ↦ (f^*F)_p` and the right-hand one is
`F ↦ F_q ⊗_{O_{D,q}} O_{C,p}`. The square itself is not constructed here — see the
module docstring.
declarations.statement:
def pullbackModulesSquareIso {P : RingedTopos.{v, u, w}} {Q : RingedTopos.{v', u', w'}}
    [P.J.HasSheafCompose (forget RingCat.{w})]
    [P.J.HasSheafCompose (forget₂ CommRingCat.{w} RingCat.{w})]
    [P.J.HasSheafCompose (forget AddCommGrpCat.{w})]
    [HasWeakSheafify P.J AddCommGrpCat.{w}] [P.J.WEqualsLocallyBijective AddCommGrpCat.{w}]
    [Q.J.HasSheafCompose (forget RingCat.{w'})]
    [Q.J.HasSheafCompose (forget₂ CommRingCat.{w'} RingCat.{w'})]
    [Q.J.HasSheafCompose (forget AddCommGrpCat.{w'})]
    [HasWeakSheafify Q.J AddCommGrpCat.{w'}] [Q.J.WEqualsLocallyBijective AddCommGrpCat.{w'}]
    (f : RingedToposHom X Y) (π : RingedToposHom P X) (ρ : RingedToposHom Q Y)
    (γ : RingedToposHom P Q) (h : f.comp π = ρ.comp γ) :
    f.toModulesHom.pullbackModules ⋙ π.toModulesHom.pullbackModules ≅
      ρ.toModulesHom.pullbackModules ⋙ γ.toModulesHom.pullbackModules
declarations.comment:
the formula, for a commutative square of morphisms of ringed topoi; the
square over a point `p` and the point `q = f ∘ p` is not constructed

declarations.name: Stacks.Sheaves.StalkPullback.pointStalkFunctorIso
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 05V5**, for a morphism of ringed topoi `f : (Sh(C), 𝒪) ⟶ (Sh(D), 𝒪')` and a point
`Φ` of the source site `C`: the stalk at `Φ` of the pullback of a sheaf of `𝒪'`-modules is the
extension of scalars along `𝒪'_q ⟶ 𝒪_Φ` of its stalk at the composite point `q = f ∘ Φ`,
naturally in the module.

The point `q` of the target site is `targetSitePoint`, built from `f` and `Φ` by Stacks 00YA;
nothing about it is assumed.
declarations.statement:
def pointStalkFunctorIso :
    f.pullbackModules ⋙ Stacks.sheafModuleFiberOfCommRing Φ X.O ≅
      Stacks.sheafModuleFiberOfCommRing (targetSitePoint f Φ) Y.O ⋙
        ModuleCat.extendScalars (pointStalkRingMap f Φ)
declarations.comment:
the formula `(f^*𝓕)_p ≅ 𝓕_q ⊗_{𝒪'_q} 𝒪_p`, naturally in `𝓕`, for an arbitrary
morphism of ringed topoi and a point `p` of the source site, with `q = f ∘ p` built from the
morphism and the point by Stacks 00YA

declarations.name: Stacks.Sheaves.StalkPullback.toposPointStalkFunctorIso
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 05V5**, for a morphism of ringed topoi and a point `p` of the source *topos*
`Sh(C)`: the stalk at `p` of the pullback of a sheaf of `𝒪'`-modules is the extension of scalars
along `𝒪'_q ⟶ 𝒪_p` of its stalk at `q = f ∘ p`, naturally in the module.

The stalk functor on sheaves of modules is taken over a point of the site, so `p` is presented
by `p.sitePoint` through Stacks 00YA part (2); on sheaves of sets that is `p⁻¹` itself, by
`CategoryTheory.PointOfTopos.sheafFiberIsoInverseImage`.
declarations.statement:
def toposPointStalkFunctorIso :
    f.pullbackModules ⋙ Stacks.sheafModuleFiberOfCommRing p.sitePoint X.O ≅
      Stacks.sheafModuleFiberOfCommRing (toposTargetSitePoint f p) Y.O ⋙
        ModuleCat.extendScalars (toposPointStalkRingMap f p)
declarations.comment:
the formula `(f^*𝓕)_p ≅ 𝓕_q ⊗_{𝒪'_q} 𝒪_p`, naturally in `𝓕`, for an arbitrary
morphism of ringed topoi and a point `p` of the source topos `Sh(C)`, with `q = f ∘ p` built
from the morphism and the point by Stacks 00YA

declarations.name: Stacks.Sheaves.StalkPullback.stalkFunctorIso
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 05V5 at a matched pair of points**, as a natural isomorphism of stalk functors:
the stalk at `Φ` of the pullback of a sheaf of `𝒪'`-modules is the extension of scalars along
`𝒪'_Ψ ⟶ 𝒪_Φ` of its stalk at `Ψ`.

This is the clause of Stacks 05V5 that
`AlgebraicGeometry.RingedToposHom.pullbackModulesSquareIso` states for a commutative square of
morphisms of ringed topoi without constructing the square over a point; here the point of the
target topos and the identification of stalk functors are the data `Ψ` and `e`.
declarations.statement:
def stalkFunctorIso :
    f.pullbackModules ⋙ Stacks.sheafModuleFiberOfCommRing Φ X.O ≅
      Stacks.sheafModuleFiberOfCommRing Ψ Y.O ⋙
        ModuleCat.extendScalars (stalkRingMap f Φ Ψ e)
declarations.comment:
the formula `(f^*G)_Φ ≅ G_Ψ ⊗_{O'_Ψ} O_Φ`, naturally in the `O'`-module `G`, for
a morphism of ringed topoi together with a point `Ψ` of the target site whose stalk functor on
sheaves of sets is the inverse image followed by the stalk functor at `Φ`

declarations.name: Stacks.Sheaves.DerivedPullback.KFlatPullbackMorphismOfSites.stalkFunctorIso
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 05V5 at the point `Ψ` of the target site**, as a natural isomorphism of stalk
functors: the stalk at `Φ` of the pullback of a sheaf of `O'`-modules is the extension of
scalars along `O'_Ψ ⟶ O_Φ` of its stalk at `Ψ`.

This is the clause of Stacks 05V5 that
`AlgebraicGeometry.RingedToposHom.pullbackModulesSquareIso` names as missing: there the formula
is proved for a commutative square of morphisms of ringed topoi, with the square over a point
`p` and the point `q = f ∘ p` left unconstructed, and `Ψ = targetPoint f hu Φ` is that point.
declarations.statement:
def stalkFunctorIso :
    f.pullbackTopos ⋙ Stacks.sheafModuleFiberOfCommRing Φ X.O ≅
      Stacks.sheafModuleFiberOfCommRing (targetPoint f hu Φ) Y.O ⋙
        ModuleCat.extendScalars (stalkRingMap f hu Φ)

declarations.name: Stacks.Sheaves.DerivedPullback.StalkBaseChangeOfToposHom.stalkFunctorIso
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 05V5 at the point `Ψ` of the target site, for an arbitrary morphism of ringed
topoi**, as a natural isomorphism of stalk functors: the stalk at `Φ` of the pullback of a sheaf
of `O'`-modules is the extension of scalars along `O'_Ψ ⟶ O_Φ` of its stalk at `Ψ`.

Nothing is assumed about the underlying sites: the pullback of Stacks 03D6 part (2) is built
from the inverse image of Stacks 03D2, so the geometric half of the comparison is the one of
Stacks 05V1 at `Ψ` and the algebraic half is the stalkwise formula for the extension of
scalars.
declarations.statement:
def stalkFunctorIso :
    g.pullbackModules ⋙ Stacks.sheafModuleFiberOfCommRing Φ X.O ≅
      Stacks.sheafModuleFiberOfCommRing (targetPoint g Φ) Y.O ⋙
        ModuleCat.extendScalars (stalkRingMap g Φ)

declarations.name: Stacks.Topos.Skyscraper.skyscraperAb_exact
declarations.doc: The direct image `p_* : Ab ⥤ Ab(C)` of a point of a topos is exact.
declarations.statement:
theorem skyscraperAb_exact [HasSheafify J AddCommGrpCat.{w}] :
    exactFunctor AddCommGrpCat.{w} (Sheaf J AddCommGrpCat.{w}) (skyscraperAb p)
declarations.comment: (1) p_* is exact

declarations.name: Stacks.Topos.Skyscraper.abelianEta
declarations.doc:
The canonical map from an abelian group into the stalk of its skyscraper,
natural in the abelian group. Its underlying map is the elementwise map of
Stacks Project, Tag 05UX.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def abelianEta (p : PointOfTopos.{w, v, u} J) :
    NatTrans (Functor.id (CommGrp (Type w))) (stalkSkyscraperAbFunctor p)
declarations.comment: skyscraper_splitting

declarations.name: Stacks.Topos.Skyscraper.abelianEta_hom
declarations.doc:
The natural section on abelian group objects has the canonical underlying
map of Stacks Project, Tag 05UX.
declarations.statement:
theorem abelianEta_hom (p : PointOfTopos.{w, v, u} J)
    (A : CommGrp (Type w)) :
    ((abelianEta p).app A).hom.hom.hom = (p.counitSection.app A.X)
declarations.comment: skyscraper_splitting

declarations.name: Stacks.Topos.Skyscraper.stalkSkyscraperAbFunctorIsoBiprod
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 05V7.** The decomposition
`p⁻¹p_*A = A ⊕ Iₚ(A)` is functorial in the abelian group `A`.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def stalkSkyscraperAbFunctorIsoBiprod
    (p : PointOfTopos.{w, v, u} J) :
    Iso (stalkSkyscraperAbFunctor p ⋙ commGrpAddEquivalence.functor)
      (commGrpAddEquivalence.functor ⊞ kernelComplementAbFunctor p)
declarations.comment: skyscraper_splitting

declarations.name: Stacks.Topos.Skyscraper.stalkSkyscraperAbFunctorIsoBiprod_fst
declarations.doc: The first projection of the splitting is the canonical counit.
declarations.statement:
theorem stalkSkyscraperAbFunctorIsoBiprod_fst
    (p : PointOfTopos.{w, v, u} J) :
    (stalkSkyscraperAbFunctorIsoBiprod p).hom ≫ biprod.fst =
      Functor.whiskerRight (abelianCounit p) commGrpAddEquivalence.functor
declarations.comment: skyscraper_splitting

declarations.name: Stacks.Topos.Skyscraper.stalkSkyscraperAbFunctorIsoBiprod_inl
declarations.doc:
The first inclusion of the splitting is the canonical map from an
abelian group into the stalk of its skyscraper.
declarations.statement:
theorem stalkSkyscraperAbFunctorIsoBiprod_inl
    (p : PointOfTopos.{w, v, u} J) :
    Functor.whiskerRight (abelianEta p) commGrpAddEquivalence.functor ≫
      (stalkSkyscraperAbFunctorIsoBiprod p).hom = biprod.inl
declarations.comment: skyscraper_splitting

declarations.name: Stacks.Topos.Skyscraper.auxKernelComplementAbFunctorObjIso
declarations.doc:
Objectwise, the auxiliary kernel functor is canonically isomorphic to the
prescribed `Iₚ`.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def auxKernelComplementAbFunctorObjIso
    (p : PointOfTopos.{w, v, u} J)
    (A : CommGrp (Type w)) :
    (auxKernelComplementAbFunctor p).obj A ≅ PointOfTopos.kernelComplementOfCounit p A
declarations.comment: skyscraper_splitting

declarations.name: Stacks.Topos.Skyscraper.kernelComplementAbFunctorNatIso
declarations.doc:
The identification of the kernel summand with `Iₚ` is natural, not merely
an objectwise identification.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def kernelComplementAbFunctorNatIso
    (p : PointOfTopos.{w, v, u} J) :
    Iso (kernelComplementAbFunctor p ⋙ commGrpAddEquivalence.inverse)
      (auxKernelComplementAbFunctor p)
declarations.comment: skyscraper_splitting

declarations.name: Stacks.Sheaves.RingedPoint.RingedPointSituation.pushforwardModules_exact
declarations.doc: **Stacks 05V8.** The direct image of modules from a ringed point is exact.
declarations.statement:
theorem pushforwardModules_exact
    [HasWeakSheafify s.point.J AddCommGrpCat.{w}]
    [s.point.J.WEqualsLocallyBijective AddCommGrpCat.{w}] :
    exactFunctor
      (SheafOfModules.{w} (Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf s.point.O))
      (SheafOfModules.{w} (Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf X.O))
      (pushforwardModules s.toRingedToposHom)
declarations.comment: exactness of the direct image

declarations.name: Stacks.Sheaves.RingedPoint.RingedPointSituation.pullbackPushforwardModules_counit_epi
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 05V8.** The canonical map `p^*p_*M ⟶ M` is a surjection of `O_p`-modules: it is
the counit of the pullback-pushforward adjunction of Stacks 03D7, hence a morphism of sheaves
of modules, and it is an epimorphism because the direct image is faithful.
declarations.statement:
theorem pullbackPushforwardModules_counit_epi
    [HasWeakSheafify X.J AddCommGrpCat.{w}]
    [X.J.WEqualsLocallyBijective AddCommGrpCat.{w}]
    [HasWeakSheafify s.point.J AddCommGrpCat.{w}]
    [s.point.J.WEqualsLocallyBijective AddCommGrpCat.{w}]
    (M : SheafOfModules.{w} (Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf s.point.O)) :
    Epi ((pullbackAdjPushforwardModules s.toRingedToposHom).counit.app M)
declarations.comment: surjectivity of the counit

declarations.name: Stacks.Sheaves.RingedPoint.RingedPointSituation.pullbackPushforwardModules_counit_stalk
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 05V8.** The canonical surjection `p⁻¹p_*M ⟶ M` of Stacks 05V7 — the counit of the
adjunction `p⁻¹ ⊣ p_*` of the point — is `O_p`-linear: under the canonical identification
`p⁻¹p_*M = (p^*p_*M)^♭` it is the underlying map of the counit `p^*p_*M ⟶ M` of the adjunction
of Stacks 03D7 for modules, which is a morphism of sheaves of `O_p`-modules by construction.

This is the source's argument: `p⁻¹O = O_p`, hence `p^* = p⁻¹`, hence the map of Stacks 05V7 is
the counit of the adjunction for modules, "whence linear".
declarations.statement:
theorem pullbackPushforwardModules_counit_stalk
    [HasWeakSheafify s.point.J AddCommGrpCat.{w}]
    [s.point.J.WEqualsLocallyBijective AddCommGrpCat.{w}]
    (M : SheafOfModules.{w} (Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf s.point.O)) :
    (Sheaf.moduleSheafFunctor (Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf s.point.O) ⋙
      s.pointEquiv.functor).map
        ((pullbackAdjPushforwardModules s.toRingedToposHom).counit.app M) =
      (s.pullbackPushforwardStalkIso M).hom ≫
        p.adj.counit.app (s.pointEquiv.functor.obj
          ((Sheaf.moduleSheafFunctor
            (Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf s.point.O)).obj M))
declarations.comment: (2) the canonical surjection p⁻¹p_*M → M is O_p-linear

declarations.name: Stacks.Sheaves.RingedPoint.GSets.realSMul_eq_twistedSMul
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 05V8, part (3).** The `𝒪_p`-module structure on `p⁻¹p_*M = Map(G, M)`
is `(r f)(σ) = σ(r) f(σ)`.

This is the source's own justification, and it is applied to the actual structure rather than
assumed of it: `realSMul` is `G`-equivariant (`translate_realSMul`) and evaluation at `1_G` is
`R`-linear for it (`realSMul_one`), and by `twistedSMul_eq_of_equivariant_of_evalOne` there is
exactly one such scalar action, namely `twistedSMul`.
declarations.statement:
theorem realSMul_eq_twistedSMul (r : R) (f : G → M) :
    realSMul G R M r f = twistedSMul G R M r f
declarations.comment: (3) the O_p-module structure on p⁻¹p_*M is (r f)(σ) = σ(r) f(σ)

declarations.name: Stacks.Sheaves.RingedPoint.GSets.not_isRealLinear_skyscraperSection
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 05V8, part (3).** The functorial direct sum decomposition
`p⁻¹p_*M = M ⊕ I(M)` of Stacks 05V7 is **not** `𝒪_p`-linear in general.

Take for `p` the point of the topos of `G`-sets whose inverse image forgets the action, and for
`𝒪` the sheaf of rings attached to a commutative ring `R` with an action of `G`, so that
`𝒪_p = R`. Then `p⁻¹p_*R = Map(G, R)`, the counit is evaluation at `1_G` and the canonical
section of the splitting sends `r` to the constant function with value `r`. That section is not
linear for the actual `𝒪_p`-module structure on `p⁻¹p_*R` — the pointwise action of the sections
of `𝒪` over `{}_G G`, read through `𝒪_p = R`, which is `realSMul` — as soon as some `σ` moves
some `r`: by `realSMul_eq_twistedSMul` that action carries the constant function `1` to
`σ ↦ σ(r₀)`, which is not constant.
declarations.statement:
theorem not_isRealLinear_skyscraperSection
    (e : Action (Type w) G ≌ Sheaf J (Type w)) {σ₀ : G} {r₀ : R} (h : σ₀ • r₀ ≠ r₀) :
    ¬ IsRealLinear G R R (fun r =>
      skyscraperStalkEquiv G e R ((forgetfulPoint G e).counitSection.app R r))
declarations.comment: (3) the splitting is not O_p-linear in general

declarations.name: Stacks.Sites.GSets.skyscraperStalkEquiv
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 05V9.** The identification `p⁻¹p_*E = Map(G, E)`: the direct image of
`E` is the `G`-set `Map(G, E)` and the inverse image forgets the action.
declarations.statement:
def skyscraperStalkEquiv (E : Type w) :
    ((forgetfulPoint G e).pushforward ⋙ (forgetfulPoint G e).inverseImage).obj E ≃ (G → E)
declarations.comment: p⁻¹p_*M = Map(G, M)

declarations.name: Stacks.Sites.GSets.counit_app_eq_skyscraperStalkEquiv_one
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 05V9.** Under the identification of `p⁻¹p_*E` with `Map(G, E)` the
counit `p⁻¹p_*E ⟶ E` is evaluation at `1_G`.
declarations.statement:
theorem counit_app_eq_skyscraperStalkEquiv_one (E : Type w)
    (x : ((forgetfulPoint G e).pushforward ⋙ (forgetfulPoint G e).inverseImage).obj E) :
    (forgetfulPoint G e).adj.counit.app E x = skyscraperStalkEquiv G e E x 1
declarations.comment: the counit p⁻¹p_*M → M is evaluation at 1_G

declarations.name: Stacks.Sites.GSets.skyscraperStalkEquiv_counitSection
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 05V9.** Under the identification of `p⁻¹p_*E` with `Map(G, E)` the
canonical section of the counit sends `m` to the constant function with value `m`.
declarations.statement:
theorem skyscraperStalkEquiv_counitSection (E : Type w) (m : E) :
    skyscraperStalkEquiv G e E ((forgetfulPoint G e).counitSection.app E m) =
      Function.const G m
declarations.comment: M → Map(G, M) assigns to m the constant function with value m

declarations.name: Stacks.Sites.GSets.kernelCounitEquiv
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 05V9.** `I(M) = {f : G → M | f(1_G) = 0}`: the kernel of the counit at
an abelian group object `A` is the set of functions `G → A` vanishing at `1_G`. An abelian group
object is written multiplicatively, so its zero is denoted `1`.

declarations.name: Stacks.Sites.GSets.stalkEquivSectionsAtRegular
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 05V9.** The stalk `𝒪_p` of the sheaf of rings attached to `R` is its
ring of sections over an object presenting the regular `G`-set; with
`sectionsAtRegularRingEquiv` this is `𝒪_p = R`.
declarations.comment: 𝒪_p = R forgetting the G-action: the stalk is the ring of sections over {}_G G

declarations.name: Stacks.Sites.GSets.sectionsAtRegularRingEquiv
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 05V9.** `𝒪_p = R` where we forget the `G`-action: evaluation at the
base point is a ring isomorphism from the sections of the sheaf of rings attached to `R` over an
object presenting the regular `G`-set onto `R`.
declarations.statement: def sectionsAtRegularRingEquiv : (equivariantSubring G R (ι.obj u₀)) ≃+* R
declarations.comment: 𝒪_p = R forgetting the G-action: that ring is R

declarations.name: Stacks.SheafOfModules.isFlatModuleStalk_of_isFlat
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 05VB.** Let `(C, O)` be a ringed site and let `Φ` be a point of `C`. If
`F` is a flat sheaf of `O`-modules, then the stalk of `F` at `Φ` is a flat module over the stalk
of `O` at `Φ`.

The proof runs the equational criterion for flatness on both sides. A relation `∑ fᵢ xᵢ = 0` in
the stalk is lifted to a relation among sections over a neighbourhood of `Φ`; the local
equational criterion for a flat sheaf of modules, Stacks 08FC part (2), factors those sections
through a finite free module on a covering of that neighbourhood; the point's fibre meets one
member of the covering, and the germs of that factorisation exhibit the original relation as
trivial, which is flatness of the stalk by Mathlib's equational criterion.
declarations.statement:
theorem isFlatModuleStalk_of_isFlat (Φ : J.Point.{max v w})
    (O : Sheaf J CommRingCat.{max v w})
    (F : _root_.SheafOfModules.{max v w} (commRingSheafToRingSheaf O)) (hF : IsFlat F) :
    IsFlatModuleStalk Φ O F

declarations.name: Stacks.isFlatModuleStalk_of_isFlat
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 05VB.**  The stalk at a point of a site of a flat sheaf of `O`-modules is a flat
module over the stalk of `O`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isFlatModuleStalk_of_isFlat
    (F : _root_.SheafOfModules.{max v w} (commRingSheafToRingSheaf O))
    (hF : SheafOfModules.IsFlat F) (Φ : J.Point.{max v w}) :
    IsFlatModuleStalk Φ O F

declarations.name: Stacks.isFlat_iff_forall_isFlatModuleStalk_of_weakSheafify
declarations.doc:
A sheaf of modules is flat if and only if its stalks at a conservative family of points are
flat, assuming `HasWeakSheafify J AddCommGrpCat.{w}` and
`J.WEqualsLocallyBijective AddCommGrpCat.{w}`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isFlat_iff_forall_isFlatModuleStalk_of_weakSheafify {C : Type u} [Category.{v} C]
    [LocallySmall.{w} C] {J : GrothendieckTopology C}
    [J.HasSheafCompose (forget₂ CommRingCat.{w} RingCat.{w})]
    [J.WEqualsLocallyBijective AddCommGrpCat.{w}] [HasWeakSheafify J AddCommGrpCat.{w}]
    {t : Type*} (p : t → J.Point.{w})
    (hp : (ObjectProperty.ofObj p).IsConservativeFamilyOfPoints) (O : Sheaf J CommRingCat.{w})
    (F : SheafOfModules.{w} (commRingSheafToRingSheaf O)) :
    SheafOfModules.IsFlat F ↔ ∀ i, IsFlatModuleStalk (p i) O F

declarations.name: Stacks.Sheaves.RingedToposModules.isFlat_pullbackModules
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 05VD.**  The pullback of a flat sheaf of modules along a morphism of
ringed topoi is flat.

All five universe parameters of the tagged statement are free here; what the tag does not state
are the sheafification hypotheses in the `variable` block above — `HasSheafCompose` for the three
forgetful functors, `HasWeakSheafify` and `WEqualsLocallyBijective` for `AddCommGrpCat`, and
`HasSheafify` for `Type` — on each of the two sites.  They arise because `Stacks.ringSheaf` and
`Stacks.SheafOfModules.IsFlat` take them as instance binders where a `ringSheaf` construction
could build them internally, so they are a formulation difference rather than added mathematical
strength; but they are *not* nothing, and a consumer whose binder context lacks them cannot apply
this theorem without supplying them.

They need not be supplied when each ringed topos has its section universe equal to the `max` of
its site's object and morphism universes, which is what
`Stacks.Sheaves.RingedToposModules.isFlat_pullbackModules_maxSectionUniverse` below records: at
that shape every one of them is an instance of the pinned Mathlib, so that statement of Stacks
05VD assumes nothing beyond the source's own hypotheses.  Both object universes and both morphism
universes stay free there; it is only the two section universes that are determined.
declarations.statement:
theorem isFlat_pullbackModules (hG : Stacks.SheafOfModules.IsFlat (O := Y.O) G) :
    Stacks.SheafOfModules.IsFlat (O := X.O) ((f.pullbackModules).obj G)
declarations.comment: ringed topoi, at free universes, assuming on each site the HasSheafCompose, HasWeakSheafify, WEqualsLocallyBijective and HasSheafify instances of the variable block; isFlat_pullbackModules_maxSectionUniverse is the same statement with all of them derived

declarations.name: Stacks.Sheaves.RingedToposModules.isFlat_pullbackModules_maxSectionUniverse
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 05VD, assuming nothing the source does not assume.**  The pullback of a
flat sheaf of modules along a morphism of ringed topoi is flat.

This is `Stacks.Sheaves.RingedToposModules.isFlat_pullbackModules` with every one of its
sheafification hypotheses discharged by instance search instead of assumed.  That is possible
exactly when each ringed topos has its section universe equal to the `max u v` of its site's
object and morphism universes, which is the shape above; the two object universes and the two
morphism universes remain free and independent.

Where each hypothesis comes from, and which of them need the section universe at all:

* the three `HasSheafCompose` hypotheses hold at **every** universe and for every site, so they
  were never where the narrowing lived: `forget AddCommGrpCat` by
  `CategoryTheory.hasSheafCompose_of_preservesMulticospan`, and `forget RingCat` and
  `forget₂ CommRingCat RingCat` by `CategoryTheory.hasSheafComposeEssentiallySmallSite`;
* `HasSheafify J (Type (max u v))` is `CategoryTheory.instHasSheafifyType`, and it too is less
  rigid than it looks: `HasSheafify J (Type w)` holds for a free `w` under
  `UnivLE.{max u v, w}`, by
  `CategoryTheory.instHasSheafifyOfPreservesLimitsForgetOfHasFiniteLimitsOfSmallOppositeCover`;
* `HasWeakSheafify J AddCommGrpCat.{max u v}` is `CategoryTheory.instHasWeakSheafifyOfHasSheafify`
  applied to that same plus-construction instance at `AddCommGrpCat`;
* `J.WEqualsLocallyBijective AddCommGrpCat.{max u v}` follows from the previous one by the
  concrete-category instance of `Mathlib/CategoryTheory/Sites/LocallyBijective.lean`, built on
  `CategoryTheory.GrothendieckTopology.WEqualsLocallyBijective.mk'`.

**Why the section universe cannot be left free.**  Exactly one of the five resists:
`HasWeakSheafify J AddCommGrpCat.{w}` for a free `w`, which fails even under
`UnivLE.{max u v, w}`.  The plus construction needs `PreservesColimitsOfShape (J.Cover X)ᵒᵖ
(forget AddCommGrpCat.{w})`, and the only instance supplying it is
`AddCommGrpCat.FilteredColimits.forget_preservesFilteredColimits`, which is
`PreservesFilteredColimits (forget AddCommGrpCat.{w})` — filtered shapes in the *same* universe
`w` as the groups, while the cover categories live in `max u v`.  The two agree precisely at
`w = max u v`.  Since `Stacks.SheafOfModules.IsFlat` takes `HasWeakSheafify` as an instance
binder, this blocks the statement and not merely the proof.  For a `w` strictly below `max u v`
there is nothing to lift at all: sheafification of `AddCommGrpCat.{w}`-valued presheaves on a
site whose covers are `max u v`-large does not exist in general.  So
`isFlat_pullbackModules` above, with the hypotheses carried and all five universes free, and this
statement, with the section universes determined and no hypotheses, are each the strongest
available in their own direction, and neither subsumes the other.
declarations.statement:
theorem isFlat_pullbackModules_maxSectionUniverse
    (hG : Stacks.SheafOfModules.IsFlat (J := Y.J) (O := Y.O) G) :
    Stacks.SheafOfModules.IsFlat (J := X.J) (O := X.O) ((f.pullbackModules).obj G)
declarations.comment: ringed topoi whose section universe is the max of their site's object and morphism universes -- object and morphism universes free and independent -- with no sheafification hypothesis assumed: HasSheafCompose, HasWeakSheafify, WEqualsLocallyBijective and HasSheafify are all derived

declarations.name: Stacks.ModuleUp.isFlat_pullback_of_representablyFlat
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 05VD for a morphism of ringed sites, assuming nothing the source does not assume.**

This is `Stacks.ModuleUp.isFlat_pullback` with every sheafification hypothesis of the section
above discharged by instance search instead of assumed: `HasWeakSheafify` for `CommRingCat`,
`RingCat` and `AddCommGrpCat` on both sites, `HasSheafCompose` for
`forget₂ CommRingCat RingCat` on both sites, `WEqualsLocallyBijective` for `RingCat` and
`AddCommGrpCat` on both sites, and the two `HasLeftKanExtension` families.  All eleven are
instances of the pinned Mathlib for a small site, so what is left — `RepresentablyFlat u` and
`u.IsContinuous K J` — is exactly the situation the source's proof reduces to.

They are kept as binders in the section above because they are wanted at *elaboration* time by
the definitions there: with them removed, `Stacks.ModuleUp.upSheafUnitRingOfCommRing` no longer
elaborates and `Stacks.ModuleUp.upSheafify_comp_bridge` exhausts the `isDefEq` heartbeat budget
re-deriving `J.PreservesSheafification (forget₂ CommRingCat RingCat)`, the synthesis already
recorded as too expensive in the implementation notes.  Discharging them once, here, at the
statement of the theorem costs nothing.

**The single-universe restriction is not liftable on this branch.**  The sites are small
categories in `Type w` with the structure sheaves and modules also at `w`.  This is forced by
`PresheafOfModules.pullbackObjIsDefined_eq_top`, the only unconditional source of
`(PresheafOfModules.pushforward φ).IsRightAdjoint` and hence of `SheafOfModules.pullback`
itself, which Mathlib states for `{C D : Type u} [SmallCategory C] [SmallCategory D]` and
`RingCat.{u}`.  Nothing weaker is available, so the object, morphism and section universes
cannot be separated here without first generalizing that Mathlib declaration.
declarations.statement:
theorem isFlat_pullback_of_representablyFlat {R : Sheaf J CommRingCat.{w}}
    {O : Sheaf K CommRingCat.{w}}
    (η : O ⟶ (u.sheafPushforwardContinuous CommRingCat.{w} K J).obj R)
    (F : _root_.SheafOfModules.{w} (Stacks.commRingSheafToRingSheaf (J := K) O))
    (hF : Stacks.SheafOfModules.IsFlat (J := K) (O := O) F) :
    Stacks.SheafOfModules.IsFlat (J := J) (O := R)
      ((SheafOfModules.pullback.{w} (ringSheafMapOfPushforward u J η)).obj F)
declarations.comment: ringed sites, for a morphism of sites given by a continuous representably flat functor, with no sheafification hypothesis assumed: the HasWeakSheafify, HasSheafCompose, WEqualsLocallyBijective and HasLeftKanExtension instances are all derived. The reduction of an arbitrary morphism of ringed sites to this case is Stacks 03CR

declarations.name: Stacks.Examples.exists_faithfullyFlat_free_baseChange_directSum
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 05VF.** A countable direct sum of rank one locally free modules is projective and
becomes free after a faithfully flat base change.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_faithfullyFlat_free_baseChange_directSum {R : Type u} [CommRing R]
    (L : ℕ → Type u) [∀ n, AddCommGroup (L n)] [∀ n, Module R (L n)]
    (hL : ∀ n, Module.IsFiniteLocallyFreeOfRank R (L n) 1) :
    ∃ (S : Type u) (_ : CommRing S) (_ : Algebra R S),
      Module.Projective R (⨁ n, L n) ∧ Module.FaithfullyFlat R S ∧
        Module.Free S (S ⊗[R] (⨁ n, L n))
declarations.comment: a countable direct sum of rank one locally free modules becomes free after a faithfully flat base change

declarations.name: Stacks.Examples.CircleTorus.exists_ring_faithfullyFlat_free_baseChange_not_isLocallyFree
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 05VF.** Being locally free does not descend along faithfully flat ring maps. The
direct sum `⨁ k, pointIdeal k` over the coordinate ring of a countable product of circles over `ℚ`
is a countable direct sum of rank one locally free modules which is projective and not locally
free (Stacks 05WL), and it becomes free over a faithfully flat algebra.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_ring_faithfullyFlat_free_baseChange_not_isLocallyFree :
    ∃ (R : Type) (_ : CommRing R) (L : ℕ → Type) (_ : ∀ n, AddCommGroup (L n))
      (_ : ∀ n, Module R (L n)),
      (∀ n, Module.IsFiniteLocallyFreeOfRank R (L n) 1) ∧ ¬ Module.IsLocallyFree R (⨁ n, L n) ∧
        ∃ (S : Type) (_ : CommRing S) (_ : Algebra R S), Module.Projective R (⨁ n, L n) ∧
          Module.FaithfullyFlat R S ∧ Module.Free S (S ⊗[R] (⨁ n, L n))
declarations.comment: being locally free does not descend along faithfully flat ring maps: a projective countable direct sum of rank one locally free modules which is not locally free becomes free after a faithfully flat base change

declarations.name: Stacks.Sheaves.GlobalTypeComparison.isFree_iff
declarations.doc:
**Descent, Lemma 05VG for Modules on Sites, Definition 03DE (1).**  A module is free if
and only if its image under the comparison is free: both sides are the assertion that some
family of global sections exhibits the module as a coproduct of copies of the structure
sheaf, and `Stacks.Sheaves.GlobalTypeComparison.isColimitCofanMap` and
`.isColimitCofanOfMap` move such a family in the two directions without changing its index
type.
declarations.statement: theorem isFree_iff (F : SheafOfModules.{w} R₁) : F.IsFree ↔ (Φ.obj F).IsFree
declarations.comment: free; global properties only, and the comparison functor of 03DX hypothesised

declarations.name: Stacks.Sheaves.GlobalTypeComparison.isFiniteFree_iff
declarations.doc:
**Descent, Lemma 05VG for Modules on Sites, Definition 03DE (2).**  A module is finite
free if and only if its image under the comparison is finite free.  The ring and module
universes agreeing, `SheafOfModules.isFiniteFree_iff_exists_isColimit` reduces both sides to
a cofan with index type `Fin n`, and the same `n` works on both sides.
declarations.statement:
theorem isFiniteFree_iff (F : SheafOfModules.{w} R₁) :
    SheafOfModules.IsFiniteFree R₁ F ↔ SheafOfModules.IsFiniteFree R₂ (Φ.obj F)
declarations.comment: finite free; global properties only, and the comparison functor of 03DX hypothesised

declarations.name: Stacks.Sheaves.GlobalTypeComparison.isGeneratedByGlobalSections_iff
declarations.doc:
**Descent, Lemma 05VG for Modules on Sites, Definition 03DE (3).**  A module is generated
by global sections if and only if its image under the comparison is.
declarations.statement:
theorem isGeneratedByGlobalSections_iff (F : SheafOfModules.{w} R₁) :
    F.IsGeneratedByGlobalSections ↔ (Φ.obj F).IsGeneratedByGlobalSections
declarations.comment: generated by global sections; global properties only, and the comparison functor of 03DX hypothesised

declarations.name: Stacks.Sheaves.GlobalTypeComparison.isGeneratedByGlobalSectionsOfCard_iff
declarations.doc:
**Descent, Lemma 05VG for Modules on Sites, Definition 03DE (4).**  A module is generated
by `r` global sections if and only if its image under the comparison is: the transported
generating family is indexed by the same type, so the same `r` works.
declarations.statement:
theorem isGeneratedByGlobalSectionsOfCard_iff (F : SheafOfModules.{w} R₁) (r : ℕ) :
    F.IsGeneratedByGlobalSectionsOfCard r ↔
      (Φ.obj F).IsGeneratedByGlobalSectionsOfCard r
declarations.comment: generated by r global sections; global properties only, and the comparison functor of 03DX hypothesised

declarations.name: Stacks.Sheaves.GlobalTypeComparison.exists_isGeneratedByGlobalSectionsOfCard_iff
declarations.doc:
**Descent, Lemma 05VG for Modules on Sites, Definition 03DE (5).**  A module is generated
by finitely many global sections if and only if its image under the comparison is.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_isGeneratedByGlobalSectionsOfCard_iff (F : SheafOfModules.{w} R₁) :
    (∃ r : ℕ, F.IsGeneratedByGlobalSectionsOfCard r) ↔
      ∃ r : ℕ, (Φ.obj F).IsGeneratedByGlobalSectionsOfCard r
declarations.comment: generated by finitely many global sections; global properties only, and the comparison functor of 03DX hypothesised

declarations.name: Stacks.Sheaves.GlobalTypeComparison.isPresentedByGlobalSections_iff
declarations.doc:
**Descent, Lemma 05VG for Modules on Sites, Definition 03DE (6).**  A module has a global
presentation if and only if its image under the comparison has one.

The preservation half maps the two coproducts and the cokernel across.  The reverse half
cannot take preimages of the two given coproducts, `Φ` not being essentially surjective; it
takes `SheafOfModules.free` on the two given index types instead, compares them with the given
coproducts through `Stacks.Sheaves.GlobalTypeComparison.mapFreeIso`, and moves the cokernel
across that comparison with `CategoryTheory.Limits.Cofork.isColimitOfIsos` before reflecting
it along `Φ`.  The two index types are unchanged.
declarations.statement:
theorem isPresentedByGlobalSections_iff (F : SheafOfModules.{w} R₁) :
    F.IsPresentedByGlobalSections ↔ (Φ.obj F).IsPresentedByGlobalSections
declarations.comment: global presentation; global properties only, and the comparison functor of 03DX hypothesised

declarations.name: Stacks.Sheaves.GlobalTypeComparison.isFinitelyPresentedByGlobalSections_iff
declarations.doc:
**Descent, Lemma 05VG for Modules on Sites, Definition 03DE (7).**  A module has a finite
global presentation if and only if its image under the comparison has one, with the same two
finite index types `Fin n` and `Fin k`.

Those index types do not live in the universe of sections, so the two coproducts the reverse
half builds are the free modules on `ULift (Fin n)` and `ULift (Fin k)`, with their cofans
reindexed by `CategoryTheory.Limits.Cofan.isColimitEquivOfEquiv`; the presentation produced is
still indexed by `Fin n` and `Fin k`, so the finiteness is not weakened.
declarations.statement:
theorem isFinitelyPresentedByGlobalSections_iff (F : SheafOfModules.{w} R₁) :
    F.IsFinitelyPresentedByGlobalSections ↔
      (Φ.obj F).IsFinitelyPresentedByGlobalSections
declarations.comment: finite global presentation; global properties only, and the comparison functor of 03DX hypothesised

declarations.name: Stacks.Sheaves.LocalTypeComparison.isFlat_iff
declarations.doc:
**Descent, Lemma 05VG for Modules on Sites, Definition 03ER (3): flatness.**  A sheaf of
modules on the target of an equivalence of ringed topoi is flat if and only if its image under
the comparison is flat.

The forward implication is Modules on Sites, Lemma 05VD,
`Stacks.Sheaves.RingedToposModules.isFlat_pullbackModules`, which holds for an arbitrary
morphism of ringed topoi.  The reverse one applies 05VD to the inverse morphism
`AlgebraicGeometry.RingedToposHom.inverse` and carries the conclusion back along
`AlgebraicGeometry.RingedToposHom.pullbackModulesInverseObjIso`, the identification of the
round trip with the identity, using that flatness is invariant under isomorphism of sheaves of
modules.  This is the pattern of the three statements of Modules on Sites, Lemma 03DM in
`StacksFrontier.Algebra.Category.ModuleCat.Sheaf.ModuleTypesUnderEquivalence`, which flatness is
not a clause of, 03DM covering 03DL rather than 03ER.

The three universes of each ringed topos are taken equal because
`Stacks.Sheaves.RingedToposModules.isFlat_pullbackModules` already forces the source's object
and section universes to agree; applying it to `f` and to the inverse of `f` in turn forces the
same of the target, and the round-trip isomorphism needs the two section universes to agree.
declarations.statement:
theorem isFlat_iff (f : AlgebraicGeometry.RingedToposHom X Y)
    [f.toToposHom.pushforward.IsEquivalence] [IsIso f.fSharp]
    (F : SheafOfModules.{u} ((Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf (J := Y.J)) Y.O)) :
    Stacks.SheafOfModules.IsFlat (O := Y.O) F ↔
      Stacks.SheafOfModules.IsFlat (O := X.O)
        ((f.toModulesHom.pullbackModules).obj F)
declarations.comment: flat; local properties, with the comparison of 03DX carried as an equivalence of ringed topoi rather than of quasi-coherent modules alone

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.BigFppfOver.isFlat_baseAssociatedModule_iff
declarations.doc:
**Descent, Lemma 05VG for Modules on Sites, Definition 03ER (3), at the big site
`(Sch/S)_τ`, for every `τ ∈ {Zariski, étale, smooth, syntomic, fppf}`.**  A quasi-coherent
`𝒪_S`-module `𝓗` is flat if and only if `𝓗ᵃ` is flat as an `𝒪`-module on `(Sch/S)_τ`.

The `only if` half is `AlgebraicGeometry.BigFppfOver.isFlat_baseAssociatedModule_of_isFlat`,
which needs neither quasi-coherence nor anything about the coverings of the big site; the `if`
half is `AlgebraicGeometry.BigFppfOver.isFlat_of_isFlat_baseAssociatedModule`, and that is where
the source's quasi-coherence hypothesis is used — the sections of `𝓗ᵃ` at an object `T → S` are
the sections of the pullback of `𝓗` to `T` only for a quasi-coherent `𝓗`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem isFlat_baseAssociatedModule_iff :
    Stacks.SheafOfModules.IsFlat.{u, u, u, u} (O := S.zariskiRingedSite.O) 𝓗 ↔
      Stacks.SheafOfModules.IsFlat.{u, u + 1, u, u} (O := (baseRingedSite B S hS τ).O)
        ((baseAssociatedModule B S hS τ).obj 𝓗)
declarations.comment: flat (03ER (3)), big site (Sch/S)_τ at every τ, at the comparison functor of 03DX itself

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Cells05VG.isCoherentOnSite_iff_smallZariskiAssociatedModule
declarations.doc:
**Descent, Lemma 05VG, coherent (03DL (8)), on the small site `S_Zar`.**  For a locally
Noetherian scheme `S`, a quasi-coherent `𝒪_S`-module `𝓕` is coherent on `(Opens(S), 𝒪_S)` if
and only if `𝓕^a` is coherent as an `𝒪`-module on `S_Zar`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isCoherentOnSite_iff_smallZariskiAssociatedModule [IsLocallyNoetherian S]
    (𝓕 : S.Modules) [𝓕.IsQuasicoherent] :
    SheafOfModules.IsCoherentOnSite 𝓕 ↔
      SheafOfModules.IsCoherentOnSite ((SmallZariski.associatedModule B S hS).obj 𝓕)
declarations.comment: coherent, small site S_Zar, S locally Noetherian

quasi-coherent `𝒪_S`-module `𝓕` is of finite presentation if and only if `𝓕^a` is of finite
presentation as an `𝒪`-module on `(Sch/S)_τ`, where `𝓕 ↦ 𝓕^a` is the functor of Descent,

declarations.statement:
theorem isFinitePresentationOnSite_baseAssociatedModule_iff (τ : SiteKind) (𝓕 : S.Modules)
    [𝓕.IsQuasicoherent] :
    SheafOfModules.IsFinitePresentationOnSite (R := S.ringCatSheaf) 𝓕 ↔
      ((baseAssociatedModule B S hS τ).obj 𝓕).IsFinitePresentationOnSite
declarations.comment: of finite presentation (03DL (7)), on (Sch/S)_τ for every τ ∈ {Zariski, étale, smooth, syntomic, fppf}, at the functor 𝓕 ↦ 𝓕ᵃ of 03DX

declarations.statement:
theorem isFinitePresentationOnSite_iff_associatedModule (𝓕 : S.Modules) :

      ((associatedModule B S hS).obj 𝓕).IsFinitePresentationOnSite

declarations.doc:

on the small site `S_τ`, for every `τ ∈ {smooth, syntomic, fppf}`.**  A quasi-coherent
`𝒪_S`-module `𝓕` is of finite presentation if and only if `𝓕^a` is of finite presentation as an
`𝒪`-module on `S_τ`, where `𝓕 ↦ 𝓕^a` is the pullback along `(S_τ, 𝒪) ⟶ (S_Zar, 𝒪_S)`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isFinitePresentationOnSite_iff_associatedModule (𝓕 : S.Modules) [𝓕.IsQuasicoherent] :
    SheafOfModules.IsFinitePresentationOnSite (R := S.ringCatSheaf) 𝓕 ↔
      ((associatedModule B S hS κ).obj 𝓕).IsFinitePresentationOnSite
declarations.comment: of finite presentation (03DL (7)), on S_τ for every τ ∈ {smooth, syntomic, fppf}, at the functor 𝓕 ↦ 𝓕ᵃ

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.Modules.isFinitePresentationOnSite_iff_associatedModule
declarations.doc:
**Descent, Lemma 05VG, for the property "of finite presentation" (Modules on Sites,
Definition 03DL (7)).**  For a quasi-coherent `𝒪_S`-module `𝓕`, `𝓕` is of finite presentation
if and only if `𝓕^a` is of finite presentation as an `𝒪`-module, at each of the functors
`𝓕 ↦ 𝓕^a` of Descent, Proposition 03DX: on the big site `(Sch/S)_τ` for every
`τ ∈ {Zariski, étale, smooth, syntomic, fppf}`, on `S_Zar`, on `S_étale`, and on the small site
`S_τ` for every `τ ∈ {smooth, syntomic, fppf}`.  Both sides are finite presentation in the sense
of Definition 03DL (7), `SheafOfModules.IsFinitePresentationOnSite`; on the left it is taken on
the site of opens of `S`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isFinitePresentationOnSite_iff_associatedModule (𝓕 : S.Modules) [𝓕.IsQuasicoherent] :
    (∀ τ : SiteKind, SheafOfModules.IsFinitePresentationOnSite (R := S.ringCatSheaf) 𝓕 ↔
        ((BigFppfOver.baseAssociatedModule Bf S hf τ).obj 𝓕).IsFinitePresentationOnSite) ∧
      (SheafOfModules.IsFinitePresentationOnSite (R := S.ringCatSheaf) 𝓕 ↔
        ((SmallZariski.associatedModule Bz S hz).obj 𝓕).IsFinitePresentationOnSite) ∧
      (SheafOfModules.IsFinitePresentationOnSite (R := S.ringCatSheaf) 𝓕 ↔
        ((SmallEtale.associatedModule Be S he).obj 𝓕).IsFinitePresentationOnSite) ∧
      ∀ κ : FlatSiteKind, SheafOfModules.IsFinitePresentationOnSite (R := S.ringCatSheaf) 𝓕 ↔
        ((SmallFlatSite.associatedModule Bf S hf κ).obj 𝓕).IsFinitePresentationOnSite
declarations.comment: of finite presentation (03DL (7)): 𝓕 has 𝒫 ⇔ 𝓕ᵃ has 𝒫 on (Sch/S)_τ for every τ, on S_Zar, on S_étale, and on S_τ for τ ∈ {smooth, syntomic, fppf}

        SheafOfModules.IsFree ((BigFppfOver.baseAssociatedModule Bf S hf τ).obj 𝓕)) ∧
      (SheafOfModules.IsFree (R := S.ringCatSheaf) 𝓕 ↔
        SheafOfModules.IsFree ((SmallZariski.associatedModule Bz S hz).obj 𝓕)) ∧
      (SheafOfModules.IsFree (R := S.ringCatSheaf) 𝓕 ↔

      ∀ κ : FlatSiteKind, SheafOfModules.IsFree (R := S.ringCatSheaf) 𝓕 ↔
        SheafOfModules.IsFree ((SmallFlatSite.associatedModule Bf S hf κ).obj 𝓕)

        SheafOfModules.IsFiniteLocallyFreeOnSite ((SmallZariski.associatedModule Bz S hz).obj 𝓕)) ∧
      (SheafOfModules.IsFiniteLocallyFreeOnSite (R := S.ringCatSheaf) 𝓕 ↔
        SheafOfModules.IsFiniteLocallyFreeOnSite ((SmallEtale.associatedModule Be S he).obj 𝓕)) ∧

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.Modules.isFlat_iff_associatedModule
declarations.doc:
**Descent, Lemma 05VG, for the property "flat" (Modules on Sites, Definition 03ER (3)).**
For a quasi-coherent `𝒪_S`-module `𝓕`, `𝓕` is flat if and only if `𝓕^a` is flat as an `𝒪`-module,
at each of the comparison functors `𝓕 ↦ 𝓕^a` of Descent, Proposition 03DX: on the big site
`(Sch/S)_τ` for every `τ ∈ {Zariski, étale, smooth, syntomic, fppf}`, on `S_Zar`, on `S_étale`, and
on the small site `S_τ` for every `τ ∈ {smooth, syntomic, fppf}`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isFlat_iff_associatedModule (𝓕 : S.Modules) [h𝓕 : 𝓕.IsQuasicoherent] :
    (∀ τ : SiteKind,
      Stacks.SheafOfModules.IsFlat.{u, u, u, u} (O := S.zariskiRingedSite.O) 𝓕 ↔
        Stacks.SheafOfModules.IsFlat.{u, u + 1, u, u}
          (O := (BigFppfOver.baseRingedSite Bf S hf τ).O)
          ((BigFppfOver.baseAssociatedModule Bf S hf τ).obj 𝓕)) ∧
      (Stacks.SheafOfModules.IsFlat.{u, u, u, u} (O := S.zariskiRingedSite.O) 𝓕 ↔
        Stacks.SheafOfModules.IsFlat.{u, u + 1, u, u} (O := (smallZariskiRingedSite Bz S hz).O)
          ((SmallZariski.associatedModule Bz S hz).obj 𝓕)) ∧
      (Stacks.SheafOfModules.IsFlat.{u, u, u, u} (O := S.zariskiRingedSite.O) 𝓕 ↔
        Stacks.SheafOfModules.IsFlat.{u, u + 1, u, u} (O := (smallEtaleRingedSite Be S he).O)
          ((SmallEtale.associatedModule Be S he).obj 𝓕)) ∧
      ∀ κ : FlatSiteKind,
        Stacks.SheafOfModules.IsFlat.{u, u, u, u} (O := S.zariskiRingedSite.O) 𝓕 ↔
          Stacks.SheafOfModules.IsFlat.{u, u + 1, u, u}
            (O := (SmallFlatSite.ringedSite Bf S hf κ).O)
            ((SmallFlatSite.associatedModule Bf S hf κ).obj 𝓕)
declarations.comment: flat: 𝓕 has 𝒫 ⇔ 𝓕ᵃ has 𝒫 on (Sch/S)_τ for every τ, on S_Zar, on S_étale, and on S_τ for τ ∈ {smooth, syntomic, fppf}

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.Modules.isCoherent_iff_associatedModule
declarations.doc:
**Descent, Lemma 05VG, for the property "coherent" (Modules on Sites, Definition 03DL (8)).**
For a locally Noetherian scheme `S` and a quasi-coherent `𝒪_S`-module `𝓕`, `𝓕` is coherent if and
only if `𝓕^a` is coherent as an `𝒪`-module, at the comparison functors `𝓕 ↦ 𝓕^a` of Descent,
Proposition 03DX for the small sites `S_Zar` and `S_étale`. These are the sites, and locally
Noetherian is the hypothesis, under which the source asserts the coherent case.
declarations.statement:
theorem isCoherent_iff_associatedModule [IsLocallyNoetherian S] (𝓕 : S.Modules)
    [𝓕.IsQuasicoherent] :
    (𝓕.IsCoherent ↔
        SheafOfModules.IsCoherentOnSite ((SmallZariski.associatedModule Bz S hz).obj 𝓕)) ∧
      (𝓕.IsCoherent ↔
        SheafOfModules.IsCoherentOnSite ((SmallEtale.associatedModule Be S he).obj 𝓕))
declarations.comment: coherent, S locally Noetherian: 𝓕 has 𝒫 ⇔ 𝓕ᵃ has 𝒫 on S_Zar and on S_étale

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.SmallEtale.isFiniteLocallyFree_of_isFiniteLocallyFreeOnSite_associatedModule
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 05VG for the clause 03DL (2) at `τ = étale`, the reflection half.**  A
quasi-coherent `𝒪_S`-module whose associated module on the small étale site of `S` is finite
locally free is finite locally free.
declarations.statement:
theorem isFiniteLocallyFree_of_isFiniteLocallyFreeOnSite_associatedModule
    (𝓕 : S.Modules) [𝓕.IsQuasicoherent]
    (h : SheafOfModules.IsFiniteLocallyFreeOnSite ((associatedModule B S hS).obj 𝓕)) :
    AlgebraicGeometry.SheafOfModules.IsFiniteLocallyFree.{u, u, u} 𝓕
declarations.comment: finite locally free, τ = étale, small sites: the reflection half

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.SmallEtale.isFiniteLocallyFreeOnSite_associatedModule
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 05VG for the clause 03DL (2) at `τ = étale`, the forward half.**  The associated
module on the small étale site of a finite locally free `𝒪_S`-module is finite locally free.

Stacks 03DN tests the conclusion on a single family covering the final object.  A finite locally
free `𝓕` is finite free over the members of some Zariski covering of `S`; the images of those
opens in `S_étale` cover its final object by
`AlgebraicGeometry.SmallEtale.coversTop_opensToSmallEtale_ulift`, and over each of them `𝓕^a` is
the pullback of `𝓕|_V` along the localized comparison of structure sheaves by Stacks 03DV
(`AlgebraicGeometry.SmallEtale.associatedModuleOverObjIso`), which is finite free because a
pullback of modules carries a finite free module to a finite free one.
declarations.statement:
theorem isFiniteLocallyFreeOnSite_associatedModule (𝓕 : S.Modules)
    (h : AlgebraicGeometry.SheafOfModules.IsFiniteLocallyFree.{u, u, u} 𝓕) :
    SheafOfModules.IsFiniteLocallyFreeOnSite ((associatedModule B S hS).obj 𝓕)
declarations.comment: finite locally free, τ = étale, small sites: the forward half

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.SmallEtale.isFiniteLocallyFreeOnSite_associatedModule_iff
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 05VG for the clause 03DL (2) at `τ = étale`.**  A quasi-coherent `𝒪_S`-module is
finite locally free if and only if its associated module on the small étale site of `S` is.
declarations.statement:
theorem isFiniteLocallyFreeOnSite_associatedModule_iff (𝓕 : S.Modules) [𝓕.IsQuasicoherent] :
    SheafOfModules.IsFiniteLocallyFreeOnSite ((associatedModule B S hS).obj 𝓕) ↔
      AlgebraicGeometry.SheafOfModules.IsFiniteLocallyFree.{u, u, u} 𝓕
declarations.comment: finite locally free, τ = étale, small sites

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.SmallEtale.isFiniteType_associatedModule_iff
declarations.doc:
**Descent, Lemma 05VG for Modules on Sites, Definition 03DL (5), at the small étale site.**
An `𝒪_S`-module `𝓕` is of finite type if and only if `𝓕ᵃ` is of finite type as an `𝒪`-module on
`S_étale`.

Both implications are Stacks 08HD in the categorical rendering of 03DL (5),
`AlgebraicGeometry.SmallEtale.isFiniteTypeOnSite_associatedModule` and
`AlgebraicGeometry.SmallEtale.isFiniteTypeOnSite_of_associatedModule`; the comparison of that
rendering with Mathlib's `SheafOfModules.IsFiniteType` is
`Stacks.SheafOfModules.isFiniteTypeOnSite_of_isFiniteType` in one direction and
`Stacks.SheafOfModules.isFiniteType_of_isFiniteTypeOnSite` in the other.

The clause string records the scope: this is clause 03DL (5) of 05VG at the **small** site for
`τ = étale`.  The small Zariski site is
`AlgebraicGeometry.SmallZariski.isFiniteType_iff_associatedModule`.  No quasi-coherence is
assumed, so this is the clause over a weaker hypothesis than the source's.
declarations.comment: finite type (03DL (5)), small site at τ = étale, at the comparison functor of 03DX itself

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.SmallEtale.isFinitePresentation_associatedModule_iff
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 05VG for Modules on Sites, Definition 03DL (7) at `τ = étale` on the small
site.**  A quasi-coherent `𝒪_S`-module is of finite presentation if and only if its associated
module on the small étale site of `S` is of finite presentation.

The forward implication is
`AlgebraicGeometry.SmallEtale.isFinitePresentation_associatedModule_of_isFinitePresentation`
and needs no quasi-coherence; the reverse one is
`AlgebraicGeometry.SmallEtale.isFinitePresentation_of_isFinitePresentation_associatedModule`,
which goes through the reflection step and fpqc descent on `S`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isFinitePresentation_associatedModule_iff (𝓕 : S.Modules)
    (h𝓕 : SheafOfModules.IsQuasicoherent (R := S.ringCatSheaf) 𝓕) :
    SheafOfModules.IsFinitePresentation (R := S.ringCatSheaf) 𝓕 ↔
      ((associatedModule B S hS).obj 𝓕).IsFinitePresentation
declarations.comment: finite presentation; the local clause 03DL (7) of the small-site comparison at τ = étale, for a quasi-coherent module on a scheme, with the comparison read as the associated-module functor of Stacks 03DU (4) rather than as a morphism of ringed topoi

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.SmallEtale.isFlat_associatedModule_iff
declarations.doc:
**Descent, Lemma 05VG for Modules on Sites, Definition 03ER (3), on the small étale site.**
A sheaf of `𝒪_S`-modules is flat if and only if `𝓕ᵃ` is flat as an `𝒪`-module on `S_étale`.

The `only if` half is Stacks 05VD at `ε`; the `if` half is étale descent of flatness, in the form
`Stacks.Sheaves.RingedToposModules.isFlat_of_isFlat_pullbackModules` — a pullback of sheaves of
modules which preserves and reflects monomorphisms reflects flatness.  Both hypotheses hold at
`ε` by the exactness and zero-detection assertions of Stacks 08H8, recorded above as instances.

`𝓕` is arbitrary: no quasi-coherence is needed, so this is the source's clause over a weaker
hypothesis.  The small Zariski counterpart is
`AlgebraicGeometry.SmallZariski.isFlat_iff_associatedModule`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem isFlat_associatedModule_iff (𝓕 : S.Modules) :
    Stacks.SheafOfModules.IsFlat (O := S.zariskiRingedSite.O) 𝓕 ↔
      Stacks.SheafOfModules.IsFlat (O := (smallEtaleRingedSite B S hS).O)
        ((associatedModule B S hS).obj 𝓕)
declarations.comment: flat (03ER (3)), small site at τ = étale, at the comparison functor of 03DX itself

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.SmallEtale.isLocallyGeneratedByOnSite_associatedModule_iff
declarations.doc:
**Descent, Lemma 05VG for Modules on Sites, Definition 03DL (4), at the small étale site, as
an equivalence.**  A quasi-coherent `𝒪_S`-module `𝓕` is locally generated by `r` sections on the
small Zariski site of `S` if and only if `𝓕ᵃ` is locally generated by `r` sections as an
`𝒪`-module on `S_étale`.

The `only if` half is `isLocallyGeneratedByOnSite_associatedModule_of_isLocallyGeneratedByOnSite`,
which needs no quasi-coherence; the `if` half is `isLocallyGeneratedByOnSite_of_associatedModule`,
which uses it, and quasi-coherence is the hypothesis the source's clause carries.

The clause string records the scope: this is clause 03DL (4) of 05VG at the **small** site for
`τ = étale`.  The small Zariski site is
`AlgebraicGeometry.SmallZariski.isLocallyGeneratedByOnSite_iff_associatedModule`, where the
comparison is an equivalence of ringed topoi and Stacks 03DM applies directly.
declarations.statement:
theorem isLocallyGeneratedByOnSite_associatedModule_iff (𝓕 : S.Modules)
    [h𝓕 : 𝓕.IsQuasicoherent] (r : ℕ) :
    SheafOfModules.IsLocallyGeneratedByOnSite (R := S.ringCatSheaf) 𝓕 r ↔
      SheafOfModules.IsLocallyGeneratedByOnSite ((associatedModule B S hS).obj 𝓕) r
declarations.comment: locally generated by r sections (03DL (4)), small site at τ = étale, at the comparison functor of 03DX itself

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.SmallFlatSite.isFlat_associatedModule_iff
declarations.doc:
**Descent, Lemma 05VG for Modules on Sites, Definition 03ER (3), on the small `τ`-site, for
every `τ ∈ {smooth, syntomic, fppf}`.**  A quasi-coherent `𝒪_S`-module `𝓗` is flat if and only if
`𝓗ᵃ` is flat as an `𝒪`-module on `S_τ`.

The `only if` half is `AlgebraicGeometry.SmallFlatSite.isFlat_associatedModule_of_isFlat`, the
`if` half `AlgebraicGeometry.SmallFlatSite.isFlat_of_isFlat_associatedModule`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isFlat_associatedModule_iff :
    Stacks.SheafOfModules.IsFlat.{u, u, u, u} (O := S.zariskiRingedSite.O) 𝓗 ↔
      Stacks.SheafOfModules.IsFlat.{u, u + 1, u, u} (O := (ringedSite B S hS κ).O)
        ((associatedModule B S hS κ).obj 𝓗)
declarations.comment: flat (03ER (3)): 𝓕 ↔ 𝓕^a, small site S_τ at every τ ∈ {smooth, syntomic, fppf} (the small sites extending the source's)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.SmallFlatSite.isFree_iff_associatedModule
declarations.doc:
**Descent, Lemma 05VG for Modules on Sites, Definition 03DE (1), on the small `τ`-site, for
every `τ ∈ {smooth, syntomic, fppf}`.**  A quasi-coherent `𝒪_S`-module is free if and only if
`𝓕^a` is so as an `𝒪`-module on `S_τ`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isFree_iff_associatedModule
    (F : (SheafOfModules.isQuasicoherent S.ringCatSheaf).FullSubcategory) :
    F.obj.IsFree ↔ ((associatedModuleQcoh B S hS κ).obj F).IsFree
declarations.comment: free (03DE (1)): 𝓕 ↔ 𝓕^a, small site S_τ at every τ ∈ {smooth, syntomic, fppf} (the small sites extending the source's)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.SmallFlatSite.isFiniteFree_iff_associatedModule
declarations.doc:
**Descent, Lemma 05VG for Modules on Sites, Definition 03DE (2), on the small `τ`-site, for
every `τ ∈ {smooth, syntomic, fppf}`.**  A quasi-coherent `𝒪_S`-module is finite free, with the
same rank if and only if `𝓕^a` is so as an `𝒪`-module on `S_τ`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isFiniteFree_iff_associatedModule
    (F : (SheafOfModules.isQuasicoherent S.ringCatSheaf).FullSubcategory) :
    SheafOfModules.IsFiniteFree S.ringCatSheaf F.obj ↔
      SheafOfModules.IsFiniteFree (ringStructureSheaf B S hS κ)
        ((associatedModuleQcoh B S hS κ).obj F)
declarations.comment: finite free (03DE (2)): 𝓕 ↔ 𝓕^a, small site S_τ at every τ ∈ {smooth, syntomic, fppf} (the small sites extending the source's)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.SmallFlatSite.isGeneratedByGlobalSections_iff_associatedModule
declarations.doc:
**Descent, Lemma 05VG for Modules on Sites, Definition 03DE (3), on the small `τ`-site, for

declarations.doc:
**Descent, Lemma 05VG for Modules on Sites, Definition 03DL (2), on the small `τ`-site, for
every `τ ∈ {smooth, syntomic, fppf}`.**  A quasi-coherent `𝒪_S`-module `𝓗` is finite locally free
if and only if `𝓗^a` is finite locally free as an `𝒪`-module on `S_τ`.

The lower shriek to the big `τ`-site carries `𝓗^a|_{S_τ}` to `𝓗^a|_{(Sch/S)_τ}`, finite local
freeness holds for a module on `S_τ` exactly when it holds for its lower shriek
(`AlgebraicGeometry.SmallFlatSite.isFiniteLocallyFreeOnSite_lowerShriek_iff`), and on the big site
this is `AlgebraicGeometry.BigFppfOver.isFiniteLocallyFreeOnSite_baseAssociatedModule_iff`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isFiniteLocallyFreeOnSite_iff_associatedModule (𝓗 : S.Modules)
    [𝓗.IsQuasicoherent] :
    SheafOfModules.IsFiniteLocallyFreeOnSite (R := S.ringCatSheaf) 𝓗 ↔
      SheafOfModules.IsFiniteLocallyFreeOnSite ((associatedModule B S hS κ).obj 𝓗)
declarations.comment: finite locally free (03DL (2)): 𝓕 ↔ 𝓕^a, small site S_τ at every τ ∈ {smooth, syntomic, fppf} (the small sites extending the source's)

declarations.statement:
theorem isLocallyGeneratedBySectionsOnSite_iff_associatedModule (𝓕 : S.Modules)

    SheafOfModules.IsLocallyGeneratedBySectionsOnSite 𝓕 ↔

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.SmallEtale.isCoherentOnSite_associatedModule_iff
declarations.doc:
**Descent, Lemma 05VG for coherence, at the small site for `τ = étale`.**  For a locally
Noetherian scheme `S`, a quasi-coherent `𝒪_S`-module `𝓕` is coherent if and only if `𝓕ᵃ` is
coherent as an `𝒪`-module on `S_étale`.

Coherence on `S_étale` is Modules on Sites, Definition 03DL (8), and coherence of `𝓕` is the
ringed-space predicate of Stacks 01BV at the Zariski site of `S`.  The source excludes coherence
from the general assertion of 05VG and asserts exactly this restricted case, with the two
hypotheses carried here: `S` locally Noetherian and `𝓕` quasi-coherent.

Both directions run through Stacks 01XZ on the scheme, as the source does.  Forward: `𝓕` is of
finite presentation, so `𝓕ᵃ` is of finite presentation by clause 03DL (7) of 05VG
(`AlgebraicGeometry.SmallEtale.isFinitePresentation_associatedModule_iff`), and a module of
finite presentation on a ringed site with coherent structure sheaf is coherent
(`Stacks.SheafOfModules.isCoherentOnSite_of_isFinitePresentation_of_unit`, applied to
`AlgebraicGeometry.SmallEtale.isCoherentOnSite_unit`).  Backward: coherence on the site contains
finite type, so `𝓕` is of finite type by clause 03DL (5) of 05VG
(`AlgebraicGeometry.SmallEtale.isFiniteType_associatedModule_iff`), and a quasi-coherent module of
finite type over a locally Noetherian scheme is coherent.

The clause string records the scope: this is the coherence clause of 05VG at the **small** site
for `τ = étale`.  The small Zariski site is
`AlgebraicGeometry.SmallZariski.isCoherentOnSite_associatedModule_iff`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem isCoherentOnSite_associatedModule_iff [IsLocallyNoetherian S] (𝓕 : S.Modules)
    [𝓕.IsQuasicoherent] :
    𝓕.IsCoherent ↔
      SheafOfModules.IsCoherentOnSite ((associatedModule B S hS).obj 𝓕)
declarations.comment: coherent (03DL (8)), small site at τ = étale over a locally Noetherian base, at the comparison functor of 03DX itself

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.SmallZariski.isCoherentOnSite_associatedModule_iff
declarations.doc:
**Descent, Lemma 05VG for coherence, at the small site for `τ = Zariski`.**  For a locally
Noetherian scheme `S`, a quasi-coherent `𝒪_S`-module `𝓕` is coherent if and only if `𝓕ᵃ` is
coherent as an `𝒪`-module on `S_Zar`.

This is the `τ = Zariski` half of the one case in which 05VG asserts coherence, under the two
hypotheses the source carries: `S` locally Noetherian and `𝓕` quasi-coherent.  The route is the
same as at `τ = étale`, with clause 03DL (7) read off
`AlgebraicGeometry.SmallZariski.isFinitePresentation_iff_associatedModule` and clause 03DL (5)
off `AlgebraicGeometry.SmallZariski.isFiniteType_iff_associatedModule`.

The clause string records the scope: this is the coherence clause of 05VG at the **small** site
for `τ = Zariski`.  The small étale site is
`AlgebraicGeometry.SmallEtale.isCoherentOnSite_associatedModule_iff`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem isCoherentOnSite_associatedModule_iff [IsLocallyNoetherian S] (𝓕 : S.Modules)
    [𝓕.IsQuasicoherent] :
    𝓕.IsCoherent ↔
      SheafOfModules.IsCoherentOnSite ((associatedModule B S hS).obj 𝓕)
declarations.comment: coherent (03DL (8)), small site at τ = Zariski over a locally Noetherian base, at the comparison functor of 03DX itself

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.Modules.isCoherentOnSite_iff_isCoherentOnSite_associatedModule
declarations.doc:
**Descent, Lemma 05VG, for the property "coherent" (Modules on Sites, Definition 03DL (8)).**
Let `S` be a locally Noetherian scheme and `𝓕` a quasi-coherent `𝒪_S`-module.  Then `𝓕` is
coherent if and only if `𝓕^a` is coherent as an `𝒪`-module, at the comparison functor
`𝓕 ↦ 𝓕^a` of Descent, Proposition 03DX (2) for `τ = Zariski`
(`AlgebraicGeometry.SmallZariski.associatedModule`, to `S_Zar`) and for `τ = étale`
(`AlgebraicGeometry.SmallEtale.associatedModule`, to `S_étale`).

"Coherent" is the one predicate `SheafOfModules.IsCoherentOnSite` of Definition 03DL (8) on both
sides: for `𝓕` on the ringed site `(Opens(S), 𝒪_S)`, for `𝓕^a` on `(S_Zar, 𝒪)` and on
`(S_étale, 𝒪)`.  On `𝓕` it agrees with coherence of `𝒪_S`-modules in the sense of Stacks 01BV by
`AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.Modules.isCoherentOnSite_iff_isCoherent`.  These are exactly the sites,
and locally Noetherian is exactly the hypothesis, under which the source asserts the coherent
case.
declarations.statement:
theorem isCoherentOnSite_iff_isCoherentOnSite_associatedModule [IsLocallyNoetherian S]
    (𝓕 : S.Modules) [𝓕.IsQuasicoherent] :
    (SheafOfModules.IsCoherentOnSite 𝓕 ↔
        SheafOfModules.IsCoherentOnSite ((SmallZariski.associatedModule Bz S hz).obj 𝓕)) ∧
      (SheafOfModules.IsCoherentOnSite 𝓕 ↔
        SheafOfModules.IsCoherentOnSite ((SmallEtale.associatedModule Be S he).obj 𝓕))
declarations.comment: coherent (03DL (8)) on both sides, S locally Noetherian: 𝓕 has 𝒫 on (Opens(S), 𝒪_S) ⇔ 𝓕ᵃ has 𝒫 on S_Zar, and ⇔ 𝓕ᵃ has 𝒫 on S_étale, at the comparison functors of 03DX (2)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.SmallZariski.isFlat_iff_associatedModuleEquivalence
declarations.doc:
**Descent, Lemma 05VG for Modules on Sites, Definition 03ER (3), at the equivalence
`QCoh(𝒪_S) ≌ QCoh(S_Zar, 𝒪)` of Descent, Proposition 03DX (2).**  A quasi-coherent
`𝒪_S`-module `𝓕` is flat if and only if `𝓕^a` is flat as an `𝒪`-module on `S_Zar`.

There is no hypothesis beyond `𝓕`: the comparison `S_Zar → (S, 𝒪_S)` is proved to be an
equivalence of ringed topoi
(`AlgebraicGeometry.SmallZariski.isEquivalence_pushforward_toOpensRingedToposHom`,
`AlgebraicGeometry.SmallZariski.isIso_fSharp_toOpensRingedToposHom`), and
`AlgebraicGeometry.SmallZariski.isFlat_iff_associatedModule` transfers flatness across it.
declarations.statement:
theorem isFlat_iff_associatedModuleEquivalence
    (𝓕 : (SheafOfModules.isQuasicoherent S.ringCatSheaf).FullSubcategory) :
    Stacks.SheafOfModules.IsFlat.{u, u, u, u} (O := S.zariskiRingedSite.O) 𝓕.obj ↔
      Stacks.SheafOfModules.IsFlat.{u, u + 1, u, u} (O := (smallZariskiRingedSite B S hS).O)
        ((associatedModuleEquivalence B S hS).functor.obj 𝓕).obj
declarations.comment: flat (03ER (3)), small site S_Zar, at the equivalence QCoh(𝒪_S) ≌ QCoh(S_Zar, 𝒪) of 03DX (2) itself, with no hypothesis

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.SmallEtale.isFlat_iff_associatedModuleEquivalence
declarations.doc:
**Descent, Lemma 05VG for Modules on Sites, Definition 03ER (3), at the equivalence
`QCoh(𝒪_S) ≌ QCoh(S_étale, 𝒪)` of Descent, Proposition 03DX (2).**  A quasi-coherent
`𝒪_S`-module `𝓕` is flat if and only if `𝓕^a` is flat as an `𝒪`-module on `S_étale`.

There is no hypothesis beyond `𝓕`, and no equivalence of ringed topoi is involved: the
comparison `S_étale → S_Zar` is not one.  The proof is
`AlgebraicGeometry.SmallEtale.isFlat_associatedModule_iff` — Stacks 05VD for the `only if` half,
and for the `if` half the reflection of flatness by a pullback of modules which preserves and
reflects monomorphisms, both of which hold at `ε` by Stacks 08H8.
declarations.statement:
theorem isFlat_iff_associatedModuleEquivalence
    (𝓕 : (SheafOfModules.isQuasicoherent S.ringCatSheaf).FullSubcategory) :
    Stacks.SheafOfModules.IsFlat.{u, u, u, u} (O := S.zariskiRingedSite.O) 𝓕.obj ↔
      Stacks.SheafOfModules.IsFlat.{u, u + 1, u, u} (O := (smallEtaleRingedSite B S hS).O)
        ((associatedModuleEquivalence' B S hS).functor.obj 𝓕).obj
declarations.comment: flat (03ER (3)), small site S_étale, at the equivalence QCoh(𝒪_S) ≌ QCoh(S_étale, 𝒪) of 03DX (2) itself, with no hypothesis

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.SmallFlatSite.isFlat_iff_associatedModuleEquivalence
declarations.doc:
**Descent, Lemma 05VG for Modules on Sites, Definition 03ER (3), at the equivalence
`QCoh(𝒪_S) ≌ QCoh(S_τ, 𝒪)` of the small site `S_τ`, for every `τ ∈ {smooth, syntomic, fppf}`.**
A quasi-coherent `𝒪_S`-module `𝓕` is flat if and only if `𝓕^a` is flat as an `𝒪`-module on
`S_τ`.

There is no hypothesis beyond `𝓕`, and no equivalence of ringed topoi is involved.  The proof is
`AlgebraicGeometry.SmallFlatSite.isFlat_associatedModule_iff`, both of whose halves are the
equational criterion of Stacks 08FC.
declarations.statement:
theorem isFlat_iff_associatedModuleEquivalence
    (𝓕 : (SheafOfModules.isQuasicoherent S.ringCatSheaf).FullSubcategory) :
    Stacks.SheafOfModules.IsFlat.{u, u, u, u} (O := S.zariskiRingedSite.O) 𝓕.obj ↔
      Stacks.SheafOfModules.IsFlat.{u, u + 1, u, u} (O := (ringedSite B S hS κ).O)
        ((associatedModuleEquivalence B S hS κ).functor.obj 𝓕).obj
declarations.comment: flat (03ER (3)), small site S_τ for every τ ∈ {smooth, syntomic, fppf}, at the equivalence QCoh(𝒪_S) ≌ QCoh(S_τ, 𝒪) of 03DX itself, with no hypothesis

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.SmallZariski.isFiniteLocallyFreeOnSite_associatedModule_iff
declarations.doc:
**Descent, Lemma 05VG for Modules on Sites, Definition 03DL (2), at the small Zariski site,
as an equivalence.**  An `𝒪_S`-module `𝓕` is finite locally free on the small Zariski site of `S`
if and only if `𝓕^a` is finite locally free as an `𝒪`-module on `S_Zar`.

The `only if` half is
`SmallZariski.isFiniteLocallyFreeOnSite_associatedModule_of_isFiniteLocallyFreeOnSite` and the
`if` half is
`AlgebraicGeometry.SmallZariski.isFiniteLocallyFreeOnSite_of_associatedModule`.  **Neither needs
quasi-coherence**, so this is the clause over a weaker hypothesis than the source's, which
carries it: at `τ = Zariski` the comparison of Remark 03FH is an equivalence of ringed sites and
its localization at an open of `S` is one too, so no restriction to the quasi-coherent modules
is needed.

The clause string records the scope: this is clause 03DL (2) of 05VG at the **small** site for
`τ = Zariski`.  The small étale site is
`AlgebraicGeometry.SmallEtale.isFiniteLocallyFreeOnSite_associatedModule_iff` and the five big
sites `(Sch/S)_τ` are
`AlgebraicGeometry.BigFppfOver.isFiniteLocallyFreeOnSite_baseAssociatedModule_iff`; with this
statement the clause is covered at every one of 05VG's seven comparison functors.
declarations.comment: finite locally free (03DL (2)), small site at τ = Zariski, at the comparison functor of 03DX itself

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.SmallZariski.isLocallyGeneratedByOnSite_iff_associatedModule
declarations.doc:
**Descent, Lemma 05VG for Modules on Sites, Definition 03DL (4), on the small Zariski
site.**  A sheaf of `𝒪_S`-modules is locally generated by `r` sections if and only if `𝓕^a` is
locally generated by `r` sections as an `𝒪`-module on `S_Zar`.

This is Stacks 03DM for that clause,
`AlgebraicGeometry.RingedToposHom.isLocallyGeneratedByOnSite_iff_pullbackModules`, instantiated
at `AlgebraicGeometry.SmallZariski.toOpensRingedToposHom` and transported along
`AlgebraicGeometry.SmallZariski.associatedModuleIsoPullbackModules`.  No quasi-coherence is
needed, the comparison being an equivalence of the whole module categories.
declarations.statement:
theorem isLocallyGeneratedByOnSite_iff_associatedModule
    (F : SheafOfModules.{u} S.ringCatSheaf) (r : ℕ) :
    F.IsLocallyGeneratedByOnSite r ↔
      ((associatedModuleOfSheaf B S hS).obj F).IsLocallyGeneratedByOnSite r
declarations.comment: locally generated by r sections (03DL (4)), small site at τ = Zariski, at the comparison functor of 03DX itself

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.SmallZariski.isFiniteType_iff_associatedModule
declarations.doc:
**Descent, Lemma 05VG for Modules on Sites, Definition 03DL (5), on the small Zariski
site.**  A sheaf of `𝒪_S`-modules is of finite type if and only if `𝓕^a` is of finite type as
an `𝒪`-module on `S_Zar`.

This is Stacks 03DM for that clause,
`AlgebraicGeometry.RingedToposHom.isFiniteType_iff_pullbackModules`, instantiated at
`AlgebraicGeometry.SmallZariski.toOpensRingedToposHom` and transported along
`AlgebraicGeometry.SmallZariski.associatedModuleIsoPullbackModules`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isFiniteType_iff_associatedModule (F : SheafOfModules.{u} S.ringCatSheaf) :
    F.IsFiniteType ↔ ((associatedModuleOfSheaf B S hS).obj F).IsFiniteType
declarations.comment: finite type (03DL (5)), small site at τ = Zariski, at the comparison functor of 03DX itself

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.SmallZariski.isFinitePresentation_iff_associatedModule
declarations.doc:
**Descent, Lemma 05VG for Modules on Sites, Definition 03DL (7), on the small Zariski
site.**  A sheaf of `𝒪_S`-modules is of finite presentation if and only if `𝓕^a` is of finite
presentation as an `𝒪`-module on `S_Zar`.

This is Stacks 03DM for that clause,
`AlgebraicGeometry.RingedToposHom.isFinitePresentation_iff_pullbackModules`, instantiated at
`AlgebraicGeometry.SmallZariski.toOpensRingedToposHom` and transported along
`AlgebraicGeometry.SmallZariski.associatedModuleIsoPullbackModules`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isFinitePresentation_iff_associatedModule (F : SheafOfModules.{u} S.ringCatSheaf) :
    F.IsFinitePresentation ↔ ((associatedModuleOfSheaf B S hS).obj F).IsFinitePresentation
declarations.comment: finite presentation (03DL (7)), small site at τ = Zariski, at the comparison functor of 03DX itself

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.SmallZariski.isFlat_iff_associatedModule
declarations.doc:
**Descent, Lemma 05VG for Modules on Sites, Definition 03ER (3), on the small Zariski
site.**  A sheaf of `𝒪_S`-modules is flat if and only if `𝓕^a` is flat as an `𝒪`-module on
`S_Zar`.

This is `AlgebraicGeometry.RingedToposHom.isFlat_iff_pullbackModules` — the flatness clause for
an equivalence of ringed topoi, whose forward half is Modules on Sites, Lemma 05VD — instantiated
at
`AlgebraicGeometry.SmallZariski.toOpensRingedToposHom` and transported along
`AlgebraicGeometry.SmallZariski.associatedModuleIsoPullbackModules` by
`Stacks.ModuleUp.isFlat_of_iso_anySite`.  No quasi-coherence is needed, the comparison being an
equivalence of the whole module categories; the source's clause carries quasi-coherence, so this
is the clause over a weaker hypothesis than the source's.
declarations.statement:
public theorem isFlat_iff_associatedModule (F : SheafOfModules.{u} S.ringCatSheaf) :
    Stacks.SheafOfModules.IsFlat (O := S.zariskiRingedSite.O) F ↔
      Stacks.SheafOfModules.IsFlat (O := (smallZariskiRingedSite B S hS).O)
        ((associatedModuleOfSheaf B S hS).obj F)
declarations.comment: flat (03ER (3)), small site at τ = Zariski, at the comparison functor of 03DX itself

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.SmallZariski.isFree_iff_associatedModule
declarations.doc:
**Descent, Lemma 05VG for Modules on Sites, Definition 03DE (1), on the small Zariski
site.**  A sheaf of `𝒪_S`-modules is free if and only if `𝓕^a` is free as an `𝒪`-module on
`S_Zar`.  No quasi-coherence is needed, the comparison being an equivalence of the whole module
categories.
declarations.statement:
theorem isFree_iff_associatedModule (F : SheafOfModules.{u} S.ringCatSheaf) :
    F.IsFree ↔ ((associatedModuleOfSheaf B S hS).obj F).IsFree
declarations.comment: free, small site at τ = Zariski, at the comparison functor of 03DX itself

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.SmallZariski.isFiniteFree_iff_associatedModule
declarations.doc:
**Descent, Lemma 05VG for Modules on Sites, Definition 03DE (2), on the small Zariski
site.**  A sheaf of `𝒪_S`-modules is finite free if and only if `𝓕^a` is, with the same
rank.
declarations.statement:
theorem isFiniteFree_iff_associatedModule (F : SheafOfModules.{u} S.ringCatSheaf) :
    SheafOfModules.IsFiniteFree S.ringCatSheaf F ↔
      SheafOfModules.IsFiniteFree (structureSheaf B S hS)
        ((associatedModuleOfSheaf B S hS).obj F)
declarations.comment: finite free, small site at τ = Zariski, at the comparison functor of 03DX itself

theorem isGeneratedByGlobalSections_iff_associatedModule

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.SmallZariski.isGeneratedByGlobalSectionsOfCard_iff_associatedModule

**Descent, Lemma 05VG for Modules on Sites, Definition 03DE (4), on the small Zariski

declarations.statement:
theorem isGeneratedByGlobalSectionsOfCard_iff_associatedModule

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.SmallZariski.exists_isGeneratedByGlobalSectionsOfCard_iff_associatedModule
declarations.doc:
**Descent, Lemma 05VG for Modules on Sites, Definition 03DE (5), on the small Zariski

declarations.statement:

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.SmallZariski.isPresentedByGlobalSections_iff_associatedModule

theorem isPresentedByGlobalSections_iff_associatedModule
