declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.AffineLineInvolution.not_isSeparated_squaringMap
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 05VS, part (5)**, which is also the last assertion of the example of **Stacks
05Z6**: the squaring map `X ⟶ 𝐀¹_k` on the involution quotient is not separated. Its relative
diagonal has the relation of Stacks 02Z1 as a represented base change, and that relation is
not a closed immersion.
declarations.statement:
theorem not_isSeparated_squaringMap (hchar : (2 : k) ≠ 0) :
    ¬ Space.IsSeparated B (Spec (.of k)) hk (squaringMap k B hk)
declarations.comment: part (5): the squaring morphism is not separated

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.AffineLineInvolution.squaringMap
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 05VS, part (1).** The canonical morphism from the involution quotient to the
affine line, descended from squaring the coordinate: the point with coordinate `x` is sent to
the point with coordinate `x ^ 2`. This is the morphism `X ⟶ 𝐀¹_k` of the remark.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def squaringMap (B : BigFppfSite.{u}) (hk : B.Contains (Spec (.of k)))
    [HasSheafify (BigFppfOver.topology B (Spec (.of k)) hk) (Type u)] :
    (involutionQuotient k B hk).obj ⟶
      Stacks.Groupoids.points (Over.post (X := B.obj hk) B.inclusion) (affineLine k)
declarations.comment: part (1): the morphism X ⟶ 𝐀¹_k squaring the coordinate

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.AffineLineInvolution.isIso_squaringMap_pullback_puncturedAffineLine
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 05VS, part (2).** Over a field in which `2` is invertible, the squaring map from
the involution quotient to the affine line is an isomorphism away from the origin: its base
change along the inclusion of the punctured affine line is an isomorphism.
declarations.statement:
theorem isIso_squaringMap_pullback_puncturedAffineLine (hchar : (2 : k) ≠ 0)
    (B : BigFppfSite.{u}) (hk : B.Contains (Spec (.of k)))
    [HasSheafify (BigFppfOver.topology B (Spec (.of k)) hk) (Type u)] :
    IsIso (pullback.snd (squaringMap k B hk)
      ((Over.post (X := B.obj hk) B.inclusion).op.whiskerLeft
        (yoneda.map (puncturedAffineLineInclusion k))))
declarations.comment: part (2): an isomorphism away from the origin

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.AffineLineInvolution.existsUnique_pointsMap_squaringMap_eq_originPoint
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 05VS, part (3).** Exactly one point of the involution quotient lies over the
origin of the affine line under the morphism descended from squaring the coordinate.

The quotient projection is locally surjective, hence surjective on the points of Stacks 03BU,
so every point of the quotient over the origin comes from a point of the affine line whose
square is the origin; such a point is the origin by
`AlgebraicGeometry.AffineLineInvolution.eq_affineLineZero_of_square_eq`, and the image of the
origin is the point sought. No assumption on the characteristic is needed: in characteristic
two the relation is the diagonal and the statement is that squaring is injective on
field-valued points.
declarations.statement:
theorem existsUnique_pointsMap_squaringMap_eq_originPoint (B : BigFppfSite.{u})
    (hk : B.Contains (Spec (.of k)))
    [HasSheafify (BigFppfOver.topology B (Spec (.of k)) hk) (Type u)] :
    ∃! x : Space.points B (Spec (.of k)) hk (involutionQuotient k B hk).obj,
      Space.pointsMap B (Spec (.of k)) hk _ (squaringMap k B hk) x = originPoint k B hk
declarations.comment: part (3): exactly one point above the origin

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.AffineLineInvolution.universallyInjective_squaringMap
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 05VS, part (4).** Away from characteristic two the morphism descended from
squaring the coordinate is universally injective.

Universal injectivity is tested on field-valued points by
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.universallyInjective_of_fieldPoints`, so it suffices to make two
sections of the quotient over the spectrum of a field with the same square agree over a further
field spectrum. The quotient projection is locally surjective, so after two successive
restrictions both sections are classes of points `t₁`, `t₂` of the affine line with the same
square. Over a field the coordinate of `t₁` is zero or a unit: in the first case the common
square is the origin and both points are the origin, the test object being reduced; in the
second the common square lies in the punctured line, and
`AlgebraicGeometry.AffineLineInvolution.quotient_eq_of_square_eq` identifies the two classes.
declarations.statement:
theorem universallyInjective_squaringMap (hchar : (2 : k) ≠ 0) (B : BigFppfSite.{u})
    (hk : B.Contains (Spec (.of k)))
    [HasSheafify (BigFppfOver.topology B (Spec (.of k)) hk) (Type u)] :
    Space.UniversallyInjective B (Spec (.of k)) hk (squaringMap k B hk)
declarations.comment: part (4): universally injective

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isFlatOverAt_exists_chartDiagram_iff_isFlatOverAtGeometricPoint
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 05VU.**  Let `f : X ⟶ Y` be a morphism of algebraic spaces over `S`, let `F` be a
quasi-coherent `𝒪_X`-module and let `x̄` be a geometric point of `X`.  The following are
equivalent:

1. there is a commuting square of étale scheme charts `U ⟶ V` over `f` and a point `u` of `U`
   above the image of `x̄` in `|X|` at which the restriction of `F` to `U` is flat over `V`;
2. the geometric stalk `F_{x̄}` is flat over the étale local ring `𝒪_{Y, ȳ}`, where
   `ȳ = f ∘ x̄`.

Condition (1) is `AlgebraicGeometry.Space.IsFlatOverAtOnChartDiagram`, the ringed-space
predicate of Stacks 08KT on the square, the condition "above `x`" being
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.ChartPoint`; condition (2) is
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.IsFlatOverAtGeometricPoint`.  Condition (2) mentions no chart, so the
equivalence also says that condition (1) does not depend on the chosen square or point.
declarations.statement:
theorem isFlatOverAt_exists_chartDiagram_iff_isFlatOverAtGeometricPoint
    {Xs Ys : AlgebraicSpaces B S hS} (f : Xs ⟶ Ys)
    (F : Modules.{u, u} B S hS Xs.1 Xs.2) [F.IsQuasicoherentOnSite]
    (xbar : GeometricPoint B S hS Xs.1) :
    (∃ (d : ChartDiagram B S hS Xs.1 Ys.1 f.hom) (u : chartScheme d.U),
        ChartPoint B S hS d.U.obj.left d.U.obj.hom u xbar.image ∧
        IsFlatOverAtOnChartDiagram B S hS Xs.2 F d u) ↔
      IsFlatOverAtGeometricPoint B S hS f F xbar

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.IsFlatOver
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 05VV.** An `𝒪_X`-module is *flat over* `Y` along `f : X ⟶ Y` when, on every
commuting square of étale scheme charts of `f`, its restriction to the chart of `X` is flat
over the chart of `Y`.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable abbrev IsFlatOver (B : BigFppfSite.{u}) (S : Scheme.{u}) (hS : B.Contains S)
    {X Y : (BigFppfOver B S hS)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u} (hX : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS X) (f : X ⟶ Y)
    (F : Modules.{u, u} B S hS X hX) : Prop
declarations.comment: flatness over the target

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.IsFlatOverAtPoint
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 05VV at a point of `|X|`.** An `𝒪_X`-module is *flat over* `Y` *at* a point `x` of
`|X|` when, on some commuting square of étale scheme charts of `f` and at some point of the
chart of `X` lying over `x`, the restriction of `F` to that chart is flat over the chart of `Y`
at that point, in the stalkwise sense of Stacks 08KT part (1) for ringed spaces.

Quantifying existentially over the charts is what the source does: this is condition (1) of
Stacks 05VU, which that lemma identifies with the geometric-stalk condition (2) at `x`.  That
lemma is *not* unavailable in this development — it is registered, for a quasi-coherent module,
as `AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isFlatOverAt_exists_chartDiagram_iff_isFlatOverAtGeometricPoint` of
`StacksFrontier/AlgebraicGeometry/Spaces/FlatModuleAtGeometricPointEquiv.lean`, which is downstream
of this file; so the identification, and with it the independence of the chosen square, is made
there and not here.  The consequence this definition's consumers want is
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isFlatOverAtPoint_iff_isFlatOverAtOnChartDiagram` of
`StacksFrontier/AlgebraicGeometry/Spaces/FlatModulePointChartIndependence.lean`: the condition may
be read on any one square through the point.

This is the pointwise form of `AlgebraicGeometry.Space.IsFlatOver`, which asks the same
ringed-space condition at *every* point of *every* chart square; the global predicate restricts
to this one at every chart point, which is
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isFlatOverAtPoint_of_isFlatOver`; that the global predicate is exactly
the conjunction of this one over all `x` of `|X|` is
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isFlatOver_iff_forall_isFlatOverAtPoint` of
`StacksFrontier/AlgebraicGeometry/Spaces/FlatModuleAllPoints.lean`, again downstream of this file
because the converse direction rests on the chart independence.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def IsFlatOverAtPoint (B : BigFppfSite.{u}) (S : Scheme.{u}) (hS : B.Contains S)
    {X Y : (BigFppfOver B S hS)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u} (hX : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS X) (f : X ⟶ Y)
    (F : Modules.{u, u} B S hS X hX) (x : points B S hS X) : Prop
declarations.comment: flatness over the target at a point of |X|

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isFlatOver_iff_forall_isFlatOverAtPoint
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 05VV, the all-`x` characterisation.** For a quasi-coherent `𝒪_X`-module `F`,
flatness of `F` over `Y` in the every-chart sense of `AlgebraicGeometry.Space.IsFlatOver` holds
exactly when `F` is flat over `Y` at every point of `|X|` in the pointwise sense of
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.IsFlatOverAtPoint`, which is condition (1) of Stacks 05VU at that
point.  This is the form in which the source states the definition: `F` is flat over `Y` when
the equivalent conditions of Stacks 05VU hold at every point of `|X|`.

The forward direction holds for an arbitrary `𝒪_X`-module; quasi-coherence is what makes the
pointwise condition chart-independent and so is needed only for the converse.
declarations.statement:
theorem isFlatOver_iff_forall_isFlatOverAtPoint {X Y : AlgebraicSpaces B S hS} (f : X ⟶ Y)
    (F : Modules.{u, u} B S hS X.1 X.2) (hF : F.IsQuasicoherentOnSite) :
    IsFlatOver B S hS X.2 f.hom F ↔
      ∀ x : points B S hS X.1, IsFlatOverAtPoint B S hS X.2 f.hom F x
declarations.comment: the all-x characterisation, for a quasi-coherent module

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isFlatOver_modulePullback_of_isFinitePresentationOnSite
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 05VW, the final assertion, for a module of finite presentation.**  In a cartesian
square of algebraic spaces

```
X' --g'--> X
|f'        |f
v          v
Y' --g---> Y
```

the inverse image of an `𝒪_X`-module of finite presentation flat over `Y` is flat over `Y'`.

This is `AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isFlatOver_modulePullback`, whose two quasi-coherence instances
finite presentation supplies: the module is quasi-coherent because it is of finite presentation,
and its inverse image is of finite presentation by
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isFinitePresentationOnSite_modulePullback`, hence quasi-coherent for the
same reason.
declarations.statement:
theorem isFlatOver_modulePullback_of_isFinitePresentationOnSite
    (B : BigFppfSite.{u}) (S : Scheme.{u}) (hS : B.Contains S)
    {X Y X' Y' : AlgebraicSpaces B S hS} {g' : X' ⟶ X} {f' : X' ⟶ Y'} {f : X ⟶ Y} {g : Y' ⟶ Y}
    (hpb : IsPullback g' f' f g) (F : Modules.{u, u} B S hS X.1 X.2)
    (hF : SheafOfModules.IsFinitePresentationOnSite F)
    (hflat : IsFlatOver B S hS X.2 f.hom F) :
    IsFlatOver B S hS X'.2 f'.hom ((modulePullback B S hS g').obj F)
declarations.comment: the final assertion for a module of finite presentation

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isFlatOverAtGeometricPoint_modulePullback
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 05VW, part (1).**  In a cartesian square of algebraic spaces

```
X' --g'--> X
|f'        |f
v          v
Y' --g---> Y
```

let `x̄'` be a geometric point of `X'` and let `F` be an `𝒪_X`-module flat over `Y` at the image
`x̄` of `x̄'`.  Then the pullback `(g')^* F` is flat over `Y'` at `x̄'`.

At the geometric stalks this is base change of flatness over a pushout of rings: the stalk of
`(g')^* F` at `x̄'` is `𝒪_{X', x̄'} ⊗_{𝒪_{X, x̄}} F_{x̄}` by Stacks 05VQ, and `𝒪_{X', x̄'}` is flat
over `𝒪_{X, x̄} ⊗_{𝒪_{Y, ȳ}} 𝒪_{Y', ȳ'}`, so flatness of `F_{x̄}` over `𝒪_{Y, ȳ}` passes to
flatness of the base change over `𝒪_{Y', ȳ'}`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isFlatOverAtGeometricPoint_modulePullback
    {X Y X' Y' : AlgebraicSpaces B S hS} {g' : X' ⟶ X} {f' : X' ⟶ Y'} {f : X ⟶ Y} {g : Y' ⟶ Y}
    (hpb : IsPullback g' f' f g) (F : Modules.{u, u} B S hS X.1 X.2)
    (x' : GeometricPoint B S hS X'.1)
    (hF : IsFlatOverAtGeometricPoint B S hS f F (geometricPointMap g'.hom x')) :
    IsFlatOverAtGeometricPoint B S hS f' ((modulePullback B S hS g').obj F) x'
declarations.comment:
part (1): the pullback of a module flat over the target at a point is flat over
  the new target at every point above it

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isFlatOverAtGeometricPoint_of_modulePullback
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 05VW, part (2).**  In a cartesian square of algebraic spaces

```
X' --g'--> X
|f'        |f
v          v
Y' --g---> Y
```

let `x̄'` be a geometric point of `X'`, let `F` be an `𝒪_X`-module and suppose that `g` is flat
at the image `ȳ'` of `x̄'` in `Y'`.  If the pullback `(g')^* F` is flat over `Y'` at `x̄'`, then
`F` is flat over `Y` at the image `x̄` of `x̄'`.

Flatness of `g` at `ȳ'` makes `(g')^* F` flat over `Y` at `x̄'` by Stacks 05VX, part (1); over
the étale local rings that reads as flatness of `𝒪_{X', x̄'} ⊗_{𝒪_{X, x̄}} F_{x̄}` over
`𝒪_{Y, ȳ}` through Stacks 05VQ.  The same flatness of `g` makes `𝒪_{X, x̄} → 𝒪_{X', x̄'}` flat,
and it is a local homomorphism of local rings, hence faithfully flat; so flatness of `F_{x̄}`
over `𝒪_{Y, ȳ}` follows by Stacks 0584 (2).
declarations.statement:
theorem isFlatOverAtGeometricPoint_of_modulePullback
    {X Y X' Y' : AlgebraicSpaces B S hS} {g' : X' ⟶ X} {f' : X' ⟶ Y'} {f : X ⟶ Y} {g : Y' ⟶ Y}
    (hpb : IsPullback g' f' f g) (F : Modules.{u, u} B S hS X.1 X.2)
    (x' : GeometricPoint B S hS X'.1)
    (hg : IsFlatAt B S hS g.hom (geometricPointMap f'.hom x').image)
    (hF : IsFlatOverAtGeometricPoint B S hS f' ((modulePullback B S hS g').obj F) x') :
    IsFlatOverAtGeometricPoint B S hS f F (geometricPointMap g'.hom x')
declarations.comment:
part (2): relative flatness of a module at a point descends along a base change
  flat at the image point

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isFlatOver_modulePullback
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 05VW, the final assertion.**  In a cartesian square of algebraic spaces

```
X' --g'--> X
|f'        |f
v          v
Y' --g---> Y
```

the pullback of a quasi-coherent `𝒪_X`-module flat over `Y` is flat over `Y'`.

Chartwise flatness of Stacks 05VV is flatness of the geometric stalks over the étale local rings
of the base at every geometric point, by Stacks 05VU, and that pointwise condition is carried by
the base change at each geometric point of `X'`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isFlatOver_modulePullback {X Y X' Y' : AlgebraicSpaces B S hS} {g' : X' ⟶ X}
    {f' : X' ⟶ Y'} {f : X ⟶ Y} {g : Y' ⟶ Y} (hpb : IsPullback g' f' f g)
    (F : Modules.{u, u} B S hS X.1 X.2) [F.IsQuasicoherentOnSite]
    [((modulePullback B S hS g').obj F).IsQuasicoherentOnSite]
    (hF : IsFlatOver B S hS X.2 f.hom F) :
    IsFlatOver B S hS X'.2 f'.hom ((modulePullback B S hS g').obj F)
declarations.comment:
the final assertion: the pullback of a quasi-coherent module flat over the target
  is flat over the new target

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.mem_flatLocus_modulePullback_of_mem_flatLocus
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 05VW, part (1), at a point of the point space.**  In a cartesian square of
algebraic spaces

```
X' --g'--> X
|f'        |f
v          v
Y' --g---> Y
```

let `F` be a quasi-coherent `𝒪_X`-module and let `x'` be a point of `|X'|`.  If `F` is flat over
`Y` at the image of `x'` in `|X|`, then the inverse image `(g')^*F` is flat over `Y'` at `x'`,
flatness at a point being membership of the relative flat locus of Stacks 0DLR.

A geometric point of `X'` above `x'` exists by Stacks 04XE, flatness at a point is flatness of
the geometric stalk there by
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.mem_flatLocus_iff_isFlatOverAtGeometricPoint`, and the implication
between the two geometric-stalk conditions is part (1) of Stacks 05VW,
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isFlatOverAtGeometricPoint_modulePullback`.  The inverse image is
quasi-coherent by Stacks 03GA.
declarations.statement:
theorem mem_flatLocus_modulePullback_of_mem_flatLocus {g' : X' ⟶ X} {f' : X' ⟶ Y'} {f : X ⟶ Y}
    {g : Y' ⟶ Y} (sq : IsPullback g'.hom f'.hom f.hom g.hom)
    (F : Modules.{u, u} B S hS X.1 X.2) [F.IsQuasicoherentOnSite] (x' : points B S hS X'.1)
    (hx : pointsMap B S hS X'.1 g'.hom x' ∈ flatLocus B S hS X.2 f.hom F) :
    x' ∈ flatLocus B S hS X'.2 f'.hom ((modulePullback B S hS g').obj F)
declarations.comment: part (1) read at a point of the point space of Stacks 03BU, flatness at a point being membership of the relative flat locus of Stacks 0DLR

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.mem_flatLocus_of_mem_flatLocus_modulePullback
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 05VW, part (2), at a point of the point space.**  In a cartesian square of
algebraic spaces

```
X' --g'--> X
|f'        |f
v          v
Y' --g---> Y
```

let `F` be a quasi-coherent `𝒪_X`-module, let `x'` be a point of `|X'|` and suppose that `g` is
flat at the image of `x'` in `|Y'|`.  If the inverse image `(g')^*F` is flat over `Y'` at `x'`,
then `F` is flat over `Y` at the image of `x'` in `|X|`, flatness at a point being membership of
the relative flat locus of Stacks 0DLR.

The proof is that of part (1) read in the opposite direction: a geometric point of `X'` above
`x'` exists by Stacks 04XE, flatness at a point is flatness of the geometric stalk there by
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.mem_flatLocus_iff_isFlatOverAtGeometricPoint`, and the implication
between the two geometric-stalk conditions is part (2) of Stacks 05VW,
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isFlatOverAtGeometricPoint_of_modulePullback`.  The inverse image is
quasi-coherent by Stacks 03GA.
declarations.statement:
theorem mem_flatLocus_of_mem_flatLocus_modulePullback {g' : X' ⟶ X} {f' : X' ⟶ Y'} {f : X ⟶ Y}
    {g : Y' ⟶ Y} (sq : IsPullback g'.hom f'.hom f.hom g.hom)
    (F : Modules.{u, u} B S hS X.1 X.2) [F.IsQuasicoherentOnSite] (x' : points B S hS X'.1)
    (hg : IsFlatAt B S hS g.hom (pointsMap B S hS X'.1 f'.hom x'))
    (hx : x' ∈ flatLocus B S hS X'.2 f'.hom ((modulePullback B S hS g').obj F)) :
    pointsMap B S hS X'.1 g'.hom x' ∈ flatLocus B S hS X.2 f.hom F
declarations.comment: part (2) read at a point of the point space of Stacks 03BU, flatness at a point being membership of the relative flat locus of Stacks 0DLR

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isFlatOverAtPoint_baseChange
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 05VW.**  Let

```
X' --g'--> X
|f'        |f
v          v
Y' --g---> Y
```

be a cartesian square of algebraic spaces over `S`, let `F` be a quasi-coherent `𝒪_X`-module
and write `F' = (g')^*F`.  For every point `x'` of `|X'|` with image `x` in `|X|`:

1. if `F` is flat over `Y` at `x`, then `F'` is flat over `Y'` at `x'`;
2. if `g` is flat at the image `f'(x')` of `x'` in `|Y'|` and `F'` is flat over `Y'` at `x'`,
   then `F` is flat over `Y` at `x`;

and in particular, if `F` is flat over `Y`, then `F'` is flat over `Y'`.

Flatness of a module over the target at a point of the point space is
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.IsFlatOverAtPoint` of Stacks 05VV, flatness over the target is
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.IsFlatOver` of Stacks 05VV, and flatness of `g` at a point is
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.IsFlatAt` of Stacks 03ML part (2).

At a point, a geometric point of `X'` above `x'` exists by Stacks 0488 part (1), flatness at a
point is flatness of the geometric stalk there by Stacks 05VU,
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.mem_flatLocus_iff_isFlatOverAtGeometricPoint`, and the two parts are
then `AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isFlatOverAtGeometricPoint_modulePullback` and
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isFlatOverAtGeometricPoint_of_modulePullback`.  The final assertion is
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isFlatOver_modulePullback`, the quasi-coherence of `F'` it asks for
being Stacks 03GA,
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isQuasicoherentOnSite_modulePullback_of_isQuasicoherentOnSite`, so that
nothing beyond quasi-coherence of `F` is assumed.
declarations.statement:
theorem isFlatOverAtPoint_baseChange {g' : X' ⟶ X} {f' : X' ⟶ Y'}
    {f : X ⟶ Y} {g : Y' ⟶ Y} (hpb : IsPullback g' f' f g) (F : Modules.{u, u} B S hS X.1 X.2)
    [F.IsQuasicoherentOnSite] :
    (∀ x' : points B S hS X'.1,
        IsFlatOverAtPoint B S hS X.2 f.hom F (pointsMap B S hS X'.1 g'.hom x') →
          IsFlatOverAtPoint B S hS X'.2 f'.hom ((modulePullback B S hS g').obj F) x') ∧
      (∀ x' : points B S hS X'.1, IsFlatAt B S hS g.hom (pointsMap B S hS X'.1 f'.hom x') →
        IsFlatOverAtPoint B S hS X'.2 f'.hom ((modulePullback B S hS g').obj F) x' →
          IsFlatOverAtPoint B S hS X.2 f.hom F (pointsMap B S hS X'.1 g'.hom x')) ∧
      (IsFlatOver B S hS X.2 f.hom F →
        IsFlatOver B S hS X'.2 f'.hom ((modulePullback B S hS g').obj F))
declarations.comment: parts (1) and (2) at a point of |X'|, flatness at a point being Stacks 05VV (1), and the final assertion, for a quasi-coherent module

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isFlatOverAtGeometricPoint_comp
declarations.doc:
If an `𝒪_X`-module `F` is flat at a geometric point `x̄` of `X` over `Y` and `Y` is flat
over `Z` at the image `ȳ` of `x̄`, then `F` is flat at `x̄` over `Z`.

Over the étale local rings this is transitivity of flatness: `F_{x̄}` is flat over `𝒪_{Y, ȳ}`
and `𝒪_{Y, ȳ}` is flat over `𝒪_{Z, z̄}`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isFlatOverAtGeometricPoint_comp {X Y Z : AlgebraicSpaces B S hS}
    (f : X ⟶ Y) (g : Y ⟶ Z) (F : Modules.{u, m} B S hS X.1 X.2)
    (xbar : GeometricPoint B S hS X.1)
    (hF : IsFlatOverAtGeometricPoint B S hS f F xbar)
    (hg : IsFlatAt B S hS g.hom (geometricPointMap f.hom xbar).image) :
    IsFlatOverAtGeometricPoint B S hS (f ≫ g) F xbar
declarations.comment: part (1): flatness of a module at a point composes with flatness of the base

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isFlatAt_of_isFaithfullyFlatOverAtGeometricPoint
declarations.doc:
If the geometric stalk `F_{x̄}` of an `𝒪_X`-module at a geometric point `x̄` of `X` is a
faithfully flat module over the étale local ring `𝒪_{Y, ȳ}` of the image `ȳ` of `x̄`, and `F` is
flat at `x̄` over `Z`, then `Y` is flat over `Z` at `ȳ`.

Over the étale local rings this is flat permanence (Stacks 039V): `F_{x̄}` is flat over
`𝒪_{Z, z̄}` and faithfully flat over `𝒪_{Y, ȳ}`, hence `𝒪_{Y, ȳ}` is flat over `𝒪_{Z, z̄}`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isFlatAt_of_isFaithfullyFlatOverAtGeometricPoint {X Y Z : AlgebraicSpaces B S hS}
    (f : X ⟶ Y) (g : Y ⟶ Z) (F : Modules.{u, m} B S hS X.1 X.2)
    (xbar : GeometricPoint B S hS X.1)
    (hff : IsFaithfullyFlatOverAtGeometricPoint B S hS f F xbar)
    (hfg : IsFlatOverAtGeometricPoint B S hS (f ≫ g) F xbar) :
    IsFlatAt B S hS g.hom (geometricPointMap f.hom xbar).image
declarations.comment:
part (3): flatness of the base at a point descends from a faithfully flat
  geometric stalk

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isFlatAt_of_nontrivial_fibre_of_isFlatOverAtGeometricPoint
declarations.doc:
Let `F` be an `𝒪_X`-module and let `x̄` be a geometric point of `X` with image `ȳ` in `Y`.
If `F` is flat at `x̄` over `Y`, the fibre of `F` at `x̄` is nonzero and `F` is flat at `x̄` over
`Z`, then `Y` is flat over `Z` at `ȳ`.

The fibre of `F` at `x̄` is the quotient `F_{x̄} ⧸ 𝔪_{x̄} F_{x̄}` of the geometric stalk by the
maximal ideal of `𝒪_{X, x̄}`; it is the pullback `x̄^* F` of `F` along `x̄`, regarded as a
representative of its image point with values in an algebraically closed field.  Since
`𝒪_{Y, ȳ} → 𝒪_{X, x̄}` is a local homomorphism, nonvanishing of that fibre forces the fibre of
`F_{x̄}` over `𝒪_{Y, ȳ}` to be nonzero as well, so that `F_{x̄}` is a faithfully flat
`𝒪_{Y, ȳ}`-module (Stacks 00HP) and part (3) applies.
declarations.statement:
theorem isFlatAt_of_nontrivial_fibre_of_isFlatOverAtGeometricPoint
    {X Y Z : AlgebraicSpaces B S hS}
    (f : X ⟶ Y) (g : Y ⟶ Z) (F : Modules.{u, m} B S hS X.1 X.2)
    (xbar : GeometricPoint B S hS X.1)
    (hf : IsFlatOverAtGeometricPoint B S hS f F xbar)
    (hfibre :
      letI := isLocalRing_etaleLocalRing B S hS X.1 X.2 xbar
      Nontrivial ((geometricModuleStalk B S hS X xbar F) ⧸
        (IsLocalRing.maximalIdeal (etaleLocalRing B S hS X.1 xbar)) •
          (⊤ : Submodule (etaleLocalRing B S hS X.1 xbar)
            (geometricModuleStalk B S hS X xbar F))))
    (hfg : IsFlatOverAtGeometricPoint B S hS (f ≫ g) F xbar) :
    IsFlatAt B S hS g.hom (geometricPointMap f.hom xbar).image
declarations.comment:
part (2): flatness of the base at a point descends from a module flat over
  both and with nonzero fibre at a representative of the point

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.relativeFlatnessPermanence_modulePullback
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 05VY.**  Let `S` be a scheme contained in the big fppf site `B`, let
`f : X ⟶ Y` and `g : Y ⟶ Z` be morphisms of algebraic spaces over `S`, let `G` be a
quasi-coherent `𝒪_Y`-module and let `x` be a point of `|X|`, with image `y` in `|Y|`.  Then:

1. if `f` is flat at `x`, then `G` is flat over `Z` at `y` if and only if `f^*G` is flat over
   `Z` at `x`;
2. in particular, if `f` is surjective and flat, then `G` is flat over `Z` if and only if
   `f^*G` is flat over `Z`.

A geometric point above `x` turns each side of (1) into the geometric-stalk condition (2) of
Stacks 05VU; there the stalk of `f^*G` is `𝒪_{X, x̄} ⊗_{𝒪_{Y, ȳ}} G_ȳ` by Stacks 05VQ and
`𝒪_{Y, ȳ} ⟶ 𝒪_{X, x̄}` is faithfully flat, so the equivalence is Stacks 0584 (2).  For (2) the
morphism `f` is flat at every point, and surjectivity of `|X| → |Y|` puts a point of `|X|`
above every point of `|Y|`.
declarations.statement:
theorem relativeFlatnessPermanence_modulePullback (B : BigFppfSite.{u}) (S : Scheme.{u})
    (hS : B.Contains S) {X Y Z : AlgebraicSpaces B S hS} (f : X ⟶ Y) (g : Y ⟶ Z)
    (G : Modules.{u, u} B S hS Y.1 Y.2) [G.IsQuasicoherentOnSite] (x : points B S hS X.1) :
    (IsFlatAt B S hS f.hom x →
        (IsFlatOverAtPoint B S hS Y.2 g.hom G (pointsMap B S hS X.1 f.hom x) ↔
          IsFlatOverAtPoint B S hS X.2 (f ≫ g).hom ((modulePullback B S hS f).obj G) x)) ∧
      (IsSurjective B S hS f.hom → IsFlat B S hS f.hom →
        (IsFlatOver B S hS Y.2 g.hom G ↔
          IsFlatOver B S hS X.2 (f ≫ g).hom ((modulePullback B S hS f).obj G)))

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isLocallyOfFiniteType_of_isUnramified
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 05VZ.** An unramified morphism of algebraic spaces is locally of finite type. In
every étale chart the underlying scheme morphism is unramified, hence locally of finite type by
`AlgebraicGeometry.locallyOfFiniteType_of_unramified`.

This is also the local-finite-type half of the implication (1) ⇒ (3) of
[Stacks Project, Tag 05W6].
declarations.statement:
theorem isLocallyOfFiniteType_of_isUnramified {f : X ⟶ Y} (hf : IsUnramified B S hS f) :
    IsLocallyOfFiniteType B S hS f

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isQuasiFiniteAt_of_isUnramifiedAt
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 05W0**, the pointwise statement: a morphism of algebraic spaces over `S` which is
unramified at a point of its source is quasi-finite at that point.

The open subspace witnessing unramifiedness at the point witnesses quasi-finiteness there, by
the global statement applied to the restriction of the morphism.
declarations.statement:
theorem isQuasiFiniteAt_of_isUnramifiedAt {f : X ⟶ Y} {x : points B S hS X}
    (hf : IsUnramifiedAt B S hS f x) : IsQuasiFiniteAt B S hS f x
declarations.comment: pointwise statement

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isLocallyQuasiFinite_of_isUnramified
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 05W0, the global consequence.** An unramified morphism of algebraic spaces over `S`
is locally quasi-finite: on every commuting square of étale scheme charts the induced scheme
morphism is unramified, hence locally of finite type and locally quasi-finite.
declarations.comment: global consequence

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isLocallyQuasiFinite_of_isUnramified
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 05W0, the global consequence.** An unramified morphism of algebraic spaces over `S`
is locally quasi-finite: on every commuting square of étale scheme charts the induced scheme
morphism is unramified, hence locally of finite type and locally quasi-finite.
declarations.comment: an unramified morphism is locally quasi-finite

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isUnramified_of_isOpenImmersion_pullbackDiagonal
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 05W1, part (2).** A morphism of algebraic spaces over `S` which is locally of
finite type and whose relative diagonal is an open immersion is unramified.

On a commuting square of surjective étale charts the relative diagonal of the morphism `α` of
the site sits over the relative diagonal of `f`, which is étale after every represented base
change because it is an open immersion after every such base change. Both legs of that square
are therefore étale, so the relative diagonal of `α` is étale by
[Stacks Project, Tag 03FV]; it is also a split monomorphism, hence universally injective, so
it is an open immersion by [Stacks Project, Tag 02LC]. Now `α` is unramified by
[Stacks Project, Tag 02GE], and one surjective étale square suffices by
[Stacks Project, Tag 03MJ].
declarations.statement:
theorem isUnramified_of_isOpenImmersion_pullbackDiagonal (hX : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS X)
    (hY : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS Y) (f : X ⟶ Y) (hft : IsLocallyOfFiniteType B S hS f)
    (hdiag : IsOpenImmersion B S hS (pullback.diagonal f)) :
    IsUnramified B S hS f
declarations.comment: part (2)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isOpenImmersion_diagonal_of_isUnramified
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 05W1, part (1).** The relative diagonal of an unramified morphism of algebraic
spaces over `S` is an open immersion.

Each represented base change of the relative diagonal is a monomorphism of schemes, because
the relative diagonal is a base change of the absolute diagonal of the source
(`AlgebraicGeometry.isPullback_pullbackDiagonal_diag`) and the absolute diagonal of an algebraic
space is a monomorphism after every represented base change
(`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.monomorphisms_diag_of_representable`, part (2) of
[Stacks Project, Tag 02X4]). It is moreover étale, which is
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.presheaf_etale_diagonal_of_isUnramified`. A morphism of schemes which
is étale and universally injective — in particular one which is étale and a monomorphism — is
an open immersion by [Stacks Project, Tag 025G].
declarations.statement:
theorem isOpenImmersion_diagonal_of_isUnramified
    (hX : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS X) (hY : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS Y) (f : X ⟶ Y)
    (hf : IsUnramified B S hS f) :
    IsOpenImmersion B S hS (pullback.diagonal f)
declarations.comment: part (1)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isUnramified_of_isOpenImmersion_diagonal
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 05W1, part (2).** A morphism of algebraic spaces over `S` which is locally of
finite type and whose relative diagonal is an open immersion is unramified.

Let `a : h_U ⟶ X`, `b : h_V ⟶ Y` be étale charts over `h : U ⟶ V`, and let
`p : h_U ⟶ X ×_Y h_V` be the induced morphism. The morphism `p` is representable, because
`p` composed with the base change `X ×_Y h_V ⟶ X` of `b` is the representable `a` and
representability cancels (`CategoryTheory.Functor.relativelyRepresentable.hasOfPostcompProperty`,
[Stacks Project, Tag 05L9]). Its kernel pair `R` is, by
`CategoryTheory.Limits.isPullback_kernelPair_diagonal`, a base change of the relative diagonal
of `f`, so `R ⟶ U ×_V U` is an open immersion by hypothesis.

The relative diagonal `U ⟶ U ×_V U` factors through `R` by a section `σ` of its first
projection, and it remains to see that `σ` is an open immersion. The relative diagonal
`d : U ⟶ R_a` of `p` over the kernel pair `R_a` of `a` *is* one: it is a section of the étale
first projection of `R_a`, hence étale by `AlgebraicGeometry.Etale.of_comp`, and a split
monomorphism, hence an open immersion by [Stacks Project, Tag 025G]. The comparison
`e : R ⟶ R_a` is a monomorphism because the two projections of `R` are jointly monic, and
`σ` is the base change of `d` along `e` — the square `𝟙, σ, d, e` is cartesian because `e` is a
monomorphism. Composing the two open immersions and transporting along the comparison of the
fibre product of `h` with itself in the site and in schemes gives that the diagonal of the
scheme morphism is an open immersion, and part (2) of [Stacks Project, Tag 02GE] concludes.
declarations.statement:
theorem isUnramified_of_isOpenImmersion_diagonal (f : X ⟶ Y)
    (hft : IsLocallyOfFiniteType B S hS f)
    (hoi : IsOpenImmersion B S hS (pullback.diagonal f)) :
    IsUnramified B S hS f
declarations.comment: part (2)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.unramifiedLocus
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 05W2, part (1).** The open subspace of the source of a morphism of algebraic
spaces over `S` cut out by the points at which the morphism is unramified.

Openness of that set of points is `AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isOpen_setOf_isUnramifiedAt`, and
the open subspace realizing it is produced by the correspondence of part (1) of
[Stacks Project, Tag 03BZ] between the open subspaces of an algebraic space and the open
subsets of its point space. No finiteness hypothesis is needed, because unramifiedness at a
point is stated as the existence of an open subspace on which the morphism is unramified; the
source's local-finite-type assumption is only used for its part (2).
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def unramifiedLocus (hX : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS X) (f : X ⟶ Y) :
    {U : Subfunctor X // IsOpenSubspace B S hS U}
declarations.comment: part (1): the open unramified locus

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.range_pointsMap_unramifiedLocus
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 05W2, part (1).** The points of `AlgebraicGeometry.Space.unramifiedLocus` are
exactly the points at which the morphism is unramified.
declarations.statement:
theorem range_pointsMap_unramifiedLocus (hX : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS X) (f : X ⟶ Y) :
    Set.range (pointsMap B S hS (unramifiedLocus B S hS hX f).1.toFunctor
        (unramifiedLocus B S hS hX f).1.ι) =
      {x : points B S hS X | IsUnramifiedAt B S hS f x}
declarations.comment: part (1): the points of the open unramified locus

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isUnramifiedAt_iff_of_isPullback
declarations.doc:
**Part (2) of Stacks 05W2, read at a point.** In a cartesian square of algebraic spaces over
`S` whose right vertical arrow `f` is locally of finite type, the base change `f'` is unramified
at a point `x'` of its source exactly when `f` is unramified at the image of `x'`; that is,
forming the unramified locus commutes with base change.

Read on the compatible pointed charts of
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.exists_etaleChartAtPoint_pair_of_isPullback`, each side is
unramifiedness of a morphism of schemes at corresponding points of a cartesian square of
schemes whose right vertical arrow is locally of finite type.

The source assumes all four corners of the square algebraic; only the three producing the charts
and the source of the base change are needed, the latter merely to read unramifiedness at a
point of it off a single chart.
declarations.statement:
theorem isUnramifiedAt_iff_of_isPullback {X' X Y' Y : (BigFppfOver B S hS)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u}
    {g' : X' ⟶ X} {f' : X' ⟶ Y'} {f : X ⟶ Y} {g : Y' ⟶ Y} (sq : IsPullback g' f' f g)
    (hX' : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS X') (hX : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS X)
    (hY' : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS Y') (hY : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS Y)
    (hf : IsLocallyOfFiniteType B S hS f) (x' : points B S hS X') :
    IsUnramifiedAt B S hS f (pointsMap B S hS X' g' x') ↔ IsUnramifiedAt B S hS f' x'
declarations.comment: part (2): base-change invariance of the unramified locus, pointwise

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isEtale_of_isEtale_over
declarations.doc:
A morphism between two algebraic spaces which are étale over a common algebraic space is
itself étale.
declarations.statement:
theorem isEtale_of_isEtale_over {F G H : (BigFppfOver B S hS)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u}
    (hF : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS F) (hG : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS G)
    (_hH : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS H) (f : F ⟶ G) (g : F ⟶ H) (h : G ⟶ H)
    (hg : IsEtale B S hS g) (hh : IsEtale B S hS h) (hfg : f ≫ h = g) :
    IsEtale B S hS f
declarations.comment: a morphism over Z between algebraic spaces étale over Z is étale

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isIso_of_isEtale_of_universallyInjective_of_isSurjective
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 05W5.** A morphism of algebraic spaces over `S` which is étale, universally
injective and surjective is an isomorphism.

An étale morphism is unramified, so its relative diagonal is an open immersion; together with
universal injectivity this makes the morphism a monomorphism. An étale surjection is flat and
locally of finite presentation, hence a one-member fppf covering of its target and so surjective
as a map of fppf sheaves.
declarations.statement:
theorem isIso_of_isEtale_of_universallyInjective_of_isSurjective
    (hX : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS X) (hY : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS Y) (f : X ⟶ Y)
    (he : IsEtale B S hS f) (hui : UniversallyInjective B S hS f)
    (hsurj : IsSurjective B S hS f) : IsIso f

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isOpenImmersion_of_isEtale_of_universallyInjective
declarations.doc: An étale universally injective morphism of algebraic spaces over `S` is an open immersion.
declarations.statement:
theorem isOpenImmersion_of_isEtale_of_universallyInjective (hX : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS X)
    (hY : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS Y) (f : X ⟶ Y) (he : IsEtale B S hS f)
    (hui : UniversallyInjective B S hS f) :
    IsOpenImmersion B S hS f
declarations.comment: the open immersion clause

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isSeparated_isLocallyQuasiFinite_of_isLocallyOfFiniteType_mono
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0463.** A monomorphism of algebraic spaces over `S` which is locally of finite type
is separated and locally quasi-finite.

Separatedness is [Stacks Project, Tag 042N], already available as
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isSeparated_of_mono`; local quasi-finiteness goes through
unramifiedness, which a monomorphism locally of finite type has by
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isUnramified_of_isLocallyOfFiniteType_of_mono`.

These are two of the three assertions of the "moreover" clause of
[Stacks Project, Tag 05W6], reached from its condition (3); the equivalence of conditions (1)
and (3) carries them over to condition (1), and the two unconditional equivalences below carry
them over to conditions (2) and (4).
declarations.statement:
theorem isSeparated_isLocallyQuasiFinite_of_isLocallyOfFiniteType_mono (f : X ⟶ Y)
    (h : IsLocallyOfFiniteType B S hS f ∧ Mono f) :
    IsSeparated B S hS f ∧ IsLocallyQuasiFinite B S hS f
declarations.comment: separated and locally quasi-finite, from condition (3)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isUnramified_mono_iff_isUnramified_universallyInjective
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 05W6, conditions (1) and (2).** A morphism of algebraic spaces over `S` is
unramified and a monomorphism if and only if it is unramified and universally injective.

The forward implication is
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isUnramified_universallyInjective_of_isUnramified_mono`. The converse
is `AlgebraicGeometry.Space.mono_of_isOpenImmersion_diagonal_of_universallyInjective`, whose
open-immersion input is part (1) of [Stacks Project, Tag 05W1], specialised to `f`; that is
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isOpenImmersion_diagonal_of_isUnramified`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isUnramified_mono_iff_isUnramified_universallyInjective
    (hX : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS X) (hY : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS Y) (f : X ⟶ Y) :
    (IsUnramified B S hS f ∧ Mono f) ↔
      (IsUnramified B S hS f ∧ UniversallyInjective B S hS f)
declarations.comment: conditions (1) and (2)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isUnramified_mono_iff_universallyInjective_locallyOfFiniteType_formallyUnramified
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 05W6, conditions (1) and (4).** A morphism of algebraic spaces over `S` is
unramified and a monomorphism if and only if it is universally injective, locally of finite
type and formally unramified.

The forward implication is, in this namespace,
`universallyInjective_isLocallyOfFiniteType_formallyUnramified_of_isUnramified_mono`.
For the converse, local finite type together with formal unramifiedness on étale charts is
unramifiedness, which is the available half of [Stacks Project, Tag 04GA]; passing from
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.FormallyUnramified` to the chart condition is condition (1) implies
condition (2) of [Stacks Project, Tag 04G8], supplied by
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.holdsOnEveryEtaleChart_of_formallyUnramified` of
`StacksFrontier.AlgebraicGeometry.Spaces.FormallyUnramifiedEtaleCharts`. The monomorphism is then
obtained as in
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isUnramified_mono_iff_isUnramified_universallyInjective`, from part (1)
of [Stacks Project, Tag 05W1]. Both inputs being available, this equivalence is unconditional
and carries the tag.
declarations.statement:
theorem isUnramified_mono_iff_universallyInjective_locallyOfFiniteType_formallyUnramified
    (hX : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS X) (hY : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS Y) (f : X ⟶ Y) :
    (IsUnramified B S hS f ∧ Mono f) ↔
      (UniversallyInjective B S hS f ∧ IsLocallyOfFiniteType B S hS f ∧
        FormallyUnramified (B := B) (S := S) (hS := hS) f)
declarations.comment: conditions (1) and (4)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isUnramified_mono_iff_isLocallyOfFiniteType_mono
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 05W6, conditions (1) and (3).** A morphism of algebraic spaces over `S` is
unramified and a monomorphism if and only if it is locally of finite type and a monomorphism.
declarations.statement:
theorem isUnramified_mono_iff_isLocallyOfFiniteType_mono
    (_hX : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS X) (_hY : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS Y) (f : X ⟶ Y) :
    (IsUnramified B S hS f ∧ Mono f) ↔ (IsLocallyOfFiniteType B S hS f ∧ Mono f)
declarations.comment: conditions (1) and (3)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isUnramified_mono_tfae_and_relativelyRepresentable_isSeparated_isLocallyQuasiFinite
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 05W6.** Let `f : X ⟶ Y` be a morphism of algebraic spaces over a scheme `S`. The
following are equivalent:

1. `f` is unramified and a monomorphism,
2. `f` is unramified and universally injective,
3. `f` is locally of finite type and a monomorphism,
4. `f` is universally injective, locally of finite type and formally unramified.

Moreover, in that case `f` is representable, separated and locally quasi-finite.

The equivalences run through condition (1). The "moreover" clause is taken at condition (3):
separatedness and local quasi-finiteness are [Stacks Project, Tag 0463], and representability
follows from them by [Stacks Project, Tag 0418].
declarations.statement:
theorem isUnramified_mono_tfae_and_relativelyRepresentable_isSeparated_isLocallyQuasiFinite
    (hX : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS X) (hY : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS Y) (f : X ⟶ Y) :
    List.TFAE
      [IsUnramified B S hS f ∧ Mono f,
        IsUnramified B S hS f ∧ UniversallyInjective B S hS f,
        IsLocallyOfFiniteType B S hS f ∧ Mono f,
        UniversallyInjective B S hS f ∧ IsLocallyOfFiniteType B S hS f ∧
          FormallyUnramified (B := B) (S := S) (hS := hS) f] ∧
      ((IsUnramified B S hS f ∧ Mono f) →
        yoneda.relativelyRepresentable f ∧ IsSeparated B S hS f ∧
          IsLocallyQuasiFinite B S hS f)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.closedImmersion_conditions_tfae
declarations.doc: The five equivalent conditions characterizing closed immersions of algebraic spaces.
declarations.statement:
public theorem closedImmersion_conditions_tfae
    (B : BigFppfSite.{u}) (S : Scheme.{u}) (hS : B.Contains S)
    {X Y : (BigFppfOver B S hS)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u}
    (hX : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS X)
    (hY : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS Y)
    (f : X ⟶ Y) :
    List.TFAE
      [IsClosedImmersion B S hS f,
       UniversallyClosed B S hS f ∧
         (IsUnramified B S hS f ∧ Mono f),
       UniversallyClosed B S hS f ∧
         (IsUnramified B S hS f ∧
           UniversallyInjective B S hS f),
       UniversallyClosed B S hS f ∧
         (IsLocallyOfFiniteType B S hS f ∧ Mono f),
       UniversallyClosed B S hS f ∧
         (UniversallyInjective B S hS f ∧
           (IsLocallyOfFiniteType B S hS f ∧
             FormallyUnramified f))]

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.Functor.isStackInSetoids_of_isStackInSetoids_twoFibreProduct
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 05W9**. In a 2-cartesian diagram of stacks in groupoids over a site, if `F` is fully
faithful, every object of a fibre of `𝒮₁` is locally in the essential image of `F`, and the 2-fibre
product `𝒮₂ ×_{𝒮₁} 𝒯₁` is a stack in setoids, then `𝒯₁` is a stack in setoids.

Being a stack and having groupoid fibres are hypotheses — they are what makes `𝒯₁` a stack in
groupoids — so the content is thinness of the fibres of `𝒯₁`, and that is
`CategoryTheory.Functor.eq_id_of_fibre_isThin_of_locallyEssSurj` applied to `β ∘ α⁻¹`, the fibres
of `𝒯₁` being groupoids.
declarations.statement:
theorem isStackInSetoids_of_isStackInSetoids_twoFibreProduct (hFeq : F ⋙ p𝒮₁ = p𝒮₂)
    (hGeq : G ⋙ p𝒮₁ = p𝒯₁) (hgpd₁ : p𝒮₁.IsFiberedInGroupoids)
    (hgpd₂ : p𝒮₂.IsFiberedInGroupoids) (hgpdT : p𝒯₁.IsFiberedInGroupoids)
    [F.Full] [F.Faithful] {J : GrothendieckTopology 𝒞} (hstack : p𝒯₁.IsStack J)
    (hloc : LocallyEssSurjOnFibers hgpd₁.isFibered hFeq J)
    (hT₂ : (TwoFibreProductOver.structureFunctor p𝒮₂ p𝒯₁ p𝒮₁ F G).IsStackInSetoids J) :
    p𝒯₁.IsStackInSetoids J

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.isStackInGroupoids_finiteCoverProjection
declarations.doc:
**The category `ℋ_d` of degree-`d` finite locally free covers is a stack in groupoids over
the big fppf site of `S`.**
declarations.comment:
The category `ℋ_d` of degree-`d` finite locally free covers, i.e. the case
`𝒳 = 𝒴 = S` of the source's `ℋ_d(𝒳/𝒴)`, is a stack in groupoids over the big fppf site of `S`.
All three conditions of Stacks 02ZI are discharged: condition (1) is
`AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.isFiberedInGroupoids_finiteCoverProjection`, condition (2) is
`AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.isom_isSheaf_finiteCoverProjection`, and condition (3), effectivity of
descent data, is `AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.descentDatum_isEffective_finiteCoverProjection`.

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.isStackInGroupoids_finiteHilbertProjection
declarations.doc:
The relative finite Hilbert category `ℋ_d(𝒳/𝒴)` of a 1-morphism `F : 𝒳 ⟶ 𝒴` of stacks in
groupoids over the big fppf site of a scheme `S`, endowed with its forgetful functor to the site,
is a stack in groupoids over `(Sch/S)_fppf`.

    (finiteHilbertProjection (B := B) (S := S) (hS := hS)

      (BigFppfOver.topology B S hS)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.forgetToProduct
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 05WD.** The 1-morphism `ℋ_d(𝒳/𝒴) ⟶ ℋ_d(𝒳) × 𝒴` of the equation: the pairing of
the two legs `AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.forgetRelativeStructure` and
`AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.forgetTarget`.

      absoluteHilbertTargetProduct
        (B := B) (S := S) (hS := hS) (d := d) (𝒳 := 𝒳) (𝒴 := 𝒴)
declarations.comment: the 1-morphism of the equation, as the pairing of the two legs

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.isRepresentableByAlgebraicSpace_of_isOpenSubstackCover
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 05WE.** Let `𝒳` be an algebraic stack over `S` and let `𝒰 i`, `i ∈ I`, be open
substacks of `𝒳` which cover `𝒳` and are each representable by an algebraic space over `S`. Then
`𝒳` is representable by an algebraic space.

The covering hypothesis makes `𝒳` a stack in setoids,
`AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.isStackInSetoids_of_isOpenSubstackCover`, which is the first step of the
source's proof; the second step is the implication (1) ⟹ (3) of Stacks 04SZ,
`AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.isRepresentableByAlgebraicSpace_of_isStackInSetoids`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isRepresentableByAlgebraicSpace_of_isOpenSubstackCover
    (𝒳 : AlgebraicStacks.{u, w} B S hS) {I : Type*} (𝒰 : I → OpenSubstack 𝒳)
    (hcover : IsOpenSubstackCover 𝒳 𝒰)
    (hspace : ∀ i, IsRepresentableByAlgebraicSpace B S hS
      (fullSubcategoryAlgebraicStack 𝒳 (𝒰 i).property (𝒰 i).isAlgebraic).val) :
    IsRepresentableByAlgebraicSpace B S hS 𝒳.val

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.exists_equivalenceOver_yoneda_of_isOpenSubstackCover
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 05WF.** Let `𝒳` be an algebraic stack over `S` and let `𝒰 i`, `i ∈ I`, be open
substacks of `𝒳` which cover `𝒳` and are each a scheme, that is, equivalent over the site to the
category of elements of the representable presheaf of an object of the site. Then `𝒳` is a scheme.

The first step of the source's proof is Stacks 05WE,
`AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.isRepresentableByAlgebraicSpace_of_isOpenSubstackCover`: it makes `𝒳` an
algebraic space `F`. The second step is the schematic locus of Stacks 03JH: each substack gives an
open immersion `h_{T_i} ⟶ F` whose image is therefore contained in the locus, the covering
hypothesis puts every section of `F` locally in one of those images, and the locus is a sheaf, so
it is all of `F` and `F` is a scheme. See the implementation notes of this module.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_equivalenceOver_yoneda_of_isOpenSubstackCover
    (𝒳 : AlgebraicStacks.{u, w} B S hS) {I : Type*} (𝒰 : I → OpenSubstack 𝒳)
    (hcover : IsOpenSubstackCover 𝒳 𝒰)
    (hscheme : ∀ i, ∃ T : BigFppfOver B S hS, Nonempty
      (StacksRepresentableCFG.EquivalenceOver
        (fullSubcategoryAlgebraicStack 𝒳 (𝒰 i).property (𝒰 i).isAlgebraic).val.val.p
        (presheafOfCategories (yoneda.obj T ⋙ typeToCat)).p)) :
    ∃ T : BigFppfOver B S hS, Nonempty
      (StacksRepresentableCFG.EquivalenceOver 𝒳.val.val.p
        (presheafOfCategories (yoneda.obj T ⋙ typeToCat)).p)

declarations.name: Stacks.Chow.chowClass_overProdOpens_section_ne_zero
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 05WK.** Let the base be a situation for Chow homology with vanishing dimension
function, the case of the spectrum of a field. Let `X i` be proper over the base, each with a
section `P i` and a point `Q i` whose residue field has degree two over the base, and let `U i`
be the complement of `Q i`. The sections assemble into a section of the product of the `U i` over
the base, and the prime cycle of each of its points is not rationally equivalent to zero: the
class of `P 1 × ⋯ × P n` is nonzero in the zeroth Chow group of `U 1 ×_S ⋯ ×_S U n`.
declarations.statement:
theorem chowClass_overProdOpens_section_ne_zero (C : ChowSituation.{u})
    (hδ : ∀ s : C.S, C.dimensionFunction s = 0) {n : ℕ} {X : Fin n → Scheme.{u}}
    (f : ∀ i, X i ⟶ C.S) [∀ i, IsProper (f i)] (P : ∀ i, C.S ⟶ X i)
    (hP : ∀ i, P i ≫ f i = 𝟙 C.S) (Q : ∀ i, X i) (hQ : ∀ i, (f i).residueDegree (Q i) = 2)
    (U : ∀ i, (X i).Opens) (hU : ∀ i, (U i : Set (X i)) = {Q i}ᶜ) :
    ∃ σ : C.S ⟶ (overProd fun i ↦ (U i).ι ≫ f i).left,
      σ ≫ (overProd fun i ↦ (U i).ι ≫ f i).hom = 𝟙 C.S ∧
        (∀ i, σ ≫ overProdπ (fun i ↦ (U i).ι ≫ f i) i ≫ (U i).ι = P i) ∧
          ∀ s₀ : C.S, ∃ α : CycleGroup C (overProd fun i ↦ (U i).ι ≫ f i).hom 0,
            α.1 = @Function.locallyFinsuppWithin.single _ _ ℤ
                (Classical.decEq (overProd fun i ↦ (U i).ι ≫ f i).left) _ (σ.base s₀) (1 : ℤ) ∧
              QuotientAddGroup.mk' (rationalEquivalences C
                (overProd fun i ↦ (U i).ι ≫ f i).hom 0) α ≠ 0

declarations.name: Stacks.Examples.CircleTorus.exists_countable_projective_directSum_isFiniteLocallyFreeOfRank_one_not_isLocallyFree
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 05WL.** There is a countable ring `R` and a projective `R`-module which is a direct
sum of countably many finite locally free modules of rank one but is not locally free. The ring
is the coordinate ring of a countable product of circles over `ℚ`, and the summands are the ideals
of a rational point in the factors.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_countable_projective_directSum_isFiniteLocallyFreeOfRank_one_not_isLocallyFree :
    ∃ (R : Type) (_ : CommRing R), Countable R ∧ ∃ L : ℕ → ModuleCat.{0} R,
      (∀ n, Module.IsFiniteLocallyFreeOfRank R (L n) 1) ∧
        Module.Projective R (DirectSum ℕ fun n => L n) ∧
          ¬ Module.IsLocallyFree R (DirectSum ℕ fun n => L n)
declarations.comment: a countable ring with a countable direct sum of invertible (finite locally free rank one) modules that is projective but not locally free

declarations.name: Stacks.Topologies.Fppf.exists_openCover_finiteLocallyFree_refinement
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 05WN.** Let `𝒮 = {S_i ⟶ S}` be an fppf covering of a scheme. Then
there are a Zariski open covering `S = ⋃ U_j`, surjective finite locally free morphisms
`W_j ⟶ U_j`, Zariski open coverings `W_j = ⋃_k W_{j,k}`, and surjective finite locally free
morphisms `T_{j,k} ⟶ W_{j,k}`, such that the composites `{T_{j,k} ⟶ S}` form an fppf covering
refining `𝒮`.

This is `exists_openCover_finiteLocallyFree_refinement_of_hasQuasiFiniteSlices` applied to
`AlgebraicGeometry.hasQuasiFiniteSlices`, the form of [Stacks, Tag 0570] used here.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_openCover_finiteLocallyFree_refinement (S : Scheme.{u})
    (𝒮 : S.Cover.{v} Scheme.fppfPrecoverage) :
    ∃ (𝒰 : S.OpenCover.{max u v})
      (W : 𝒰.I₀ → Scheme.{u})
      (g : ∀ j, W j ⟶ 𝒰.X j)
      (𝒲 : ∀ j, (W j).OpenCover.{max u v})
      (T : ∀ j, (𝒲 j).I₀ → Scheme.{u})
      (h : ∀ j k, T j k ⟶ (𝒲 j).X k),
      (∀ j, Surjective (g j) ∧ Stacks.Morphisms.IsFiniteLocallyFree (g j)) ∧
      (∀ j k, Surjective (h j k) ∧ Stacks.Morphisms.IsFiniteLocallyFree (h j k)) ∧
      Presieve.ofArrows
          (fun jk : Σ j, (𝒲 j).I₀ ↦ T jk.1 jk.2)
          (fun jk ↦ h jk.1 jk.2 ≫ (𝒲 jk.1).f jk.2 ≫ g jk.1 ≫ 𝒰.f jk.1) ∈
        Scheme.fppfPrecoverage S ∧
      ∀ j k, ∃ i, ∃ l : T j k ⟶ 𝒮.X i,
        l ≫ 𝒮.f i = h j k ≫ (𝒲 j).f k ≫ g j ≫ 𝒰.f j

declarations.name: IsLocalRing.IsHenselization.isLocalization_and_finite_of_quasiFiniteAt
declarations.doc:
**Henselization and quasi-finite ring maps** (Stacks 05WP). Let `R → S` be of finite type,
let `q` be a prime of `S` lying over `p`, and assume `R → S` is quasi-finite at `q`. Let `Rh` and
`Sh` be henselizations of `R_p` and `S_q`, let `Rh → Sh` be the local ring map over `R_p → S_q`
of Lemma 04GS, and let `T = Rh ⊗_{R_p} S_q`, mapping to `Sh` through the square. Then the ideal
`𝔪_{S_q} T` generated by `q` is prime, `Sh` is the localization of `T` at it, and `Sh` is finite
over `Rh`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isLocalization_and_finite_of_quasiFiniteAt
    [Algebra.FiniteType R S] [Algebra.QuasiFiniteAt R q] :
    ∃ _ : ((maximalIdeal Sq).map (algebraMap Sq T)).IsPrime,
      IsLocalization.AtPrime Sh ((maximalIdeal Sq).map (algebraMap Sq T)) ∧
        Module.Finite Rh Sh
declarations.comment:
The square of Lemma 04GS is the algebra structure `algebraMap Rh Sh`, local and
compatible with `R_p → S_q → S_q^h` — conditions which by Lemma 04GS determine it — and the
tensor product is any `Algebra.IsPushout Rp Sq Rh T`, whose map to `S_q^h` is the algebra
structure `algebraMap T Sh` compatible with `Rh` and `S_q`. The prime generated by `q` is
`𝔪_{S_q} T`. Quasi-finiteness at `q` is `Algebra.FiniteType R S` with
`Algebra.QuasiFiniteAt R q`, as in Lemma 04GH. See the module docstring.

declarations.name: IsLocalRing.IsHenselization.quotient_of_le_maximalIdeal
declarations.doc:
**Henselization is compatible with quotients** (Stacks 05WQ), with the base and the
henselization in independent universes. Let `(R, 𝔪, κ)` be a local ring, let `Rh` be a
henselization of `R` and let `I ⊆ 𝔪` be an ideal. Then `Rh/I Rh` is a henselization of `R/I`,
with respect to the residue field of `R/I`.

`Rh/I Rh` is henselian because a quotient of a henselian local ring by a proper ideal is
(`Stacks.Henselian.henselianLocalRing_quotient`); it is ind-étale over `R/I` by
`IsLocalRing.IsHenselization.indEtale_quotient`; and its residue field is that of `R/I` because
the two quotient maps `R → R/I` and `Rh → Rh/I Rh` are surjective local maps, hence
isomorphisms on residue fields, and the third side of the square is the identification carried by
the henselization.
declarations.statement:
theorem quotient_of_le_maximalIdeal [IsHenselization R (ResidueField R) Rh]
    {I : Ideal R} (hI : I ≤ maximalIdeal R) :
    letI : IsLocalRing (R ⧸ I) := isLocalRing_quotient_of_le_maximalIdeal I hI
    letI : IsLocalRing (Rh ⧸ I.map (algebraMap R Rh)) :=
      isLocalRing_quotient_of_le_maximalIdeal (I.map (algebraMap R Rh))
        ((Ideal.map_mono hI).trans (map_maximalIdeal (R := R) (L := ResidueField R)).le)
    IsHenselization (R ⧸ I) (ResidueField (R ⧸ I)) (Rh ⧸ I.map (algebraMap R Rh))
declarations.comment:
`R^h` is the henselization of `R` in the sense of Definition 04GQ (1),
`IsHenselization R (ResidueField R) Rh`, which by Lemma 04GN exists and by Lemma 08HT is unique
up to unique isomorphism over `R`; the conclusion says that `R^h/IR^h` is the henselization of
`R/I` in the same sense, `IsHenselization (R ⧸ I) (ResidueField (R ⧸ I)) (Rh ⧸ I.map (algebraMap
R Rh))`, for the `R/I`-algebra structure induced by `R → R^h`. The locality of the two quotients
follows from `I ⊆ 𝔪` and is supplied in the statement. The base and the henselization live in
independent universes.

declarations.name: Algebra.IsPushout.strictHenselization_and_finite_of_quasiFiniteAt
declarations.doc:
**The strict henselization of `S_q` for a quasi-finite ring map** (Stacks 05WR). Let `R → S` be
of finite type, let `q` be a prime of `S` lying over `p` at which `R → S` is quasi-finite, and let
`Rp`, `Sq` be the localizations. Let `Rsh` be a strict henselization of `Rp`: henselian, ind-étale
over `Rp`, with maximal ideal generated by `𝔪_{R_p}` and residue field `κ₁` a separable algebraic
closure of `κ(p)`. Let `κ₂` be a separable algebraic closure of `κ(q)` containing `κ₁`, let `T` be
the base change `Rsh ⊗_{Rp} Sq` and let `π : T → κ₂` be the map induced by `Rsh → κ₁ → κ₂` and
`Sq → κ(q) → κ₂`. Let `Ssh` be the localization of `T` at the prime `ker π`. Then `Ssh` is finite
over `Rsh` by a local ring map, `Sq → Ssh` is a strict henselization of `Sq` whose residue field is
`κ₂`, and `κ₂/κ₁` is finite and purely inseparable.
declarations.statement:
theorem Algebra.IsPushout.strictHenselization_and_finite_of_quasiFiniteAt
    {R S Rp Sq Rsh T Ssh κ₂ : Type u}
    [CommRing R] [CommRing S] [CommRing Rp] [CommRing Sq] [CommRing Rsh] [CommRing T]
    [CommRing Ssh] [Field κ₂] [Algebra R S]
    (p : Ideal R) (q : Ideal S) [p.IsPrime] [q.IsPrime] [q.LiesOver p]
    [Algebra.FiniteType R S] [Algebra.QuasiFiniteAt R q]
    [Algebra R Rp] [IsLocalRing Rp] [IsLocalization.AtPrime Rp p]
    [Algebra S Sq] [IsLocalRing Sq] [IsLocalization.AtPrime Sq q]
    [Algebra R Sq] [Algebra Rp Sq] [IsScalarTower R S Sq] [IsScalarTower R Rp Sq]
    [Algebra Rp Rsh] [HenselianLocalRing Rsh] [IsLocalHom (algebraMap Rp Rsh)]
    [IsSepClosure (ResidueField Rp) (ResidueField Rsh)]
    (hind : (CommAlgCat.etale.{u} Rp).ind.{u} (CommAlgCat.of Rp Rsh))
    (hmax : (maximalIdeal Rp).map (algebraMap Rp Rsh) = maximalIdeal Rsh)
    [Algebra (ResidueField Sq) κ₂] [IsSepClosure (ResidueField Sq) κ₂]
    [Algebra (ResidueField Rsh) κ₂]
    [Algebra Rp T] [Algebra Rsh T] [Algebra Sq T]
    [IsScalarTower Rp Rsh T] [IsScalarTower Rp Sq T]
    (hT : Algebra.IsPushout Rp Sq Rsh T)
    (π : T →+* κ₂)
    (hπRsh : π.comp (algebraMap Rsh T) = (algebraMap (ResidueField Rsh) κ₂).comp (residue Rsh))
    (hπSq : π.comp (algebraMap Sq T) = (algebraMap (ResidueField Sq) κ₂).comp (residue Sq))
    [(RingHom.ker π).IsPrime]
    [Algebra T Ssh] [IsLocalRing Ssh] [IsLocalization.AtPrime Ssh (RingHom.ker π)]
    [Algebra Sq Ssh] [Algebra Rsh Ssh] [IsScalarTower Sq T Ssh] [IsScalarTower Rsh T Ssh] :
    ∃ _ : IsLocalHom (algebraMap Sq Ssh),
      Module.Finite Rsh Ssh ∧ IsLocalHom (algebraMap Rsh Ssh) ∧ HenselianLocalRing Ssh ∧
        (CommAlgCat.etale.{u} Sq).ind.{u} (CommAlgCat.of Sq Ssh) ∧
        (maximalIdeal Sq).map (algebraMap Sq Ssh) = maximalIdeal Ssh ∧
        IsSepClosure (ResidueField Sq) (ResidueField Ssh) ∧
        (∃ e : ResidueField Ssh ≃+* κ₂,
          (e : ResidueField Ssh →+* κ₂).comp ((residue Ssh).comp (algebraMap T Ssh)) = π) ∧
        Module.Finite (ResidueField Rsh) κ₂ ∧ IsPurelyInseparable (ResidueField Rsh) κ₂
declarations.comment:
Stated as the construction of `S_q^{sh}`: `Ssh` is the localization of the base
change `T` at the prime `ker π`, and the conclusion is that it is a strict henselization of `S_q` —
the items of Lemma 04GP, as in Lemmas 05WP and 05WS — with residue field `κ₂`, finite and local
over `R_p^{sh}`, and that `κ₂/κ₁` is finite purely inseparable. With the uniqueness of Lemma 08HT,
which the source's proof invokes here too, this is the source's identification of `S_q^{sh}` with
that localization; the top arrow of the source's square is `algebraMap Rsh Ssh`. `κ₁` is
`ResidueField Rsh`, and that its image in `κ₂` is the separable subfield of Lemma 030K is a
consequence, not a hypothesis. See the module docstring.

declarations.name: IsLocalRing.strictHenselization_quotient
declarations.doc:
**Strict henselization is compatible with quotients** (Stacks 05WS). Let `(R, 𝔪, κ)` be a
local ring and let `R → Rsh` be a strict henselization of `R`, that is: `Rsh` is a henselian local
ring whose residue field is a separable algebraic closure `κ^{sep}` of `κ`, it is a filtered
colimit of étale `R`-algebras, and `𝔪 Rsh` is its maximal ideal. Let `I ⊆ 𝔪` be an ideal. Then
`Rsh/I Rsh` is a strict henselization of `R/I`, for the induced `R/I`-algebra structure: it is a
henselian local ring, it is a filtered colimit of étale `R/I`-algebras, the ideal generated by the
image of `𝔪/I` is its maximal ideal, and its residue field is again a separable algebraic closure
of `κ`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem IsLocalRing.strictHenselization_quotient {R Rsh : Type u} [CommRing R]
    [CommRing Rsh] [IsLocalRing R] [Algebra R Rsh] [HenselianLocalRing Rsh]
    [IsLocalHom (algebraMap R Rsh)] [IsSepClosure (ResidueField R) (ResidueField Rsh)]
    (hind : (CommAlgCat.etale.{u} R).ind.{u} (CommAlgCat.of R Rsh))
    (hmax : (maximalIdeal R).map (algebraMap R Rsh) = maximalIdeal Rsh)
    (I : Ideal R) (hI : I ≤ maximalIdeal R) :
    ∃ (_ : IsLocalRing (R ⧸ I)) (_ : IsLocalRing (Rsh ⧸ I.map (algebraMap R Rsh)))
        (_ : IsLocalHom (algebraMap (R ⧸ I) (Rsh ⧸ I.map (algebraMap R Rsh)))),
      HenselianLocalRing (Rsh ⧸ I.map (algebraMap R Rsh)) ∧
      (CommAlgCat.etale.{u} (R ⧸ I)).ind.{u}
        (CommAlgCat.of (R ⧸ I) (Rsh ⧸ I.map (algebraMap R Rsh))) ∧
      (maximalIdeal (R ⧸ I)).map (algebraMap (R ⧸ I) (Rsh ⧸ I.map (algebraMap R Rsh))) =
        maximalIdeal (Rsh ⧸ I.map (algebraMap R Rsh)) ∧
      IsSepClosure (ResidueField (R ⧸ I))
        (ResidueField (Rsh ⧸ I.map (algebraMap R Rsh)))
declarations.comment:
"`Rsh` is a strict henselization of `R`" is spelled by the properties of
Lemma 04GP, which by Lemma 08HT determine a strict henselization up to isomorphism over the base
(Definition 04GQ(3)), in the shape `IsLocalRing.exists_henselization` (04GN) gives the
henselization; the conclusion asserts the same properties for `R/I → Rsh/I Rsh`.
`IsSepClosure κ κ_sh` is items (2) and (5) together. `I R^{sh}` is `I.map (algebraMap R Rsh)`, and
the `R/I`-algebra structure on `Rsh/I Rsh` is Mathlib's induced one. See the module docstring.

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isLocallyOfFinitePresentation_of_comp
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 05WT.** If a composite of morphisms of algebraic spaces over `S` is locally of
finite presentation and its second factor is locally of finite type, then its first factor is
locally of finite presentation.

Being locally of finite presentation is étale local on the source and target by **Stacks 04R3**
and cancels against being locally of finite type at the level of schemes by **Stacks 02FV**,
part (1), so this is the two-property cancellation of the chart condition at those two
properties.
declarations.statement:
theorem isLocallyOfFinitePresentation_of_comp
    {F G H : (BigFppfOver B S hS)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u}
    (hF : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS F) (hG : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS G)
    (hH : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS H)
    (f : F ⟶ G) (g : G ⟶ H)
    (hfg : IsLocallyOfFinitePresentation B S hS (f ≫ g))
    (hg : IsLocallyOfFiniteType B S hS g) :
    IsLocallyOfFinitePresentation B S hS f

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isOpen_flatLocus_of_isFinitePresentationOnCharts
declarations.doc:
Let `f : X ⟶ Y` be a morphism of algebraic spaces over `S` which is locally of finite
presentation and let `F` be an `𝒪_X`-module which is quasi-coherent of finite presentation on
charts. The set of points of `|X|` at which `F` is flat over `Y` is open.
declarations.statement:
theorem isOpen_flatLocus_of_isFinitePresentationOnCharts (hX : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS X)
    (f : X ⟶ Y) (F : Modules.{u, u} B S hS X hX)
    (hf : IsLocallyOfFinitePresentation B S hS f)
    (hqc : IsQuasicoherentOnCharts B S hS hX F)
    (hfp : IsFinitePresentationOnCharts B S hS hX F) :
    IsOpen (flatLocus B S hS hX f F)
declarations.comment: openness of the flat locus; quasi-coherence and finite presentation of the module are read on the Zariski site of every etale scheme chart

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isOpen_setOf_forall_isFlatOverAtGeometricPoint
declarations.doc:
For a morphism of algebraic spaces locally of finite presentation and a quasi-coherent module
which is of finite presentation on charts, the set of points of the source over which the
geometric stalks of the module are flat over the étale local rings of the target is open.
declarations.statement:
theorem isOpen_setOf_forall_isFlatOverAtGeometricPoint (f : Xs ⟶ Ys)
    (F : Modules.{u, u} B S hS Xs.1 Xs.2) [F.IsQuasicoherentOnSite]
    (hf : IsLocallyOfFinitePresentation B S hS f.hom)
    (hfp : IsFinitePresentationOnCharts B S hS Xs.2 F) :
    IsOpen {x : points B S hS Xs.1 | ∀ xbar : GeometricPoint B S hS Xs.1,
      xbar.image = x → IsFlatOverAtGeometricPoint B S hS f F xbar}
declarations.comment: openness of the flat locus, read through condition (2) of Stacks 05VU; finite presentation of the module is read on the Zariski site of every etale scheme chart

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.flatLocus_modulePullback_eq_preimage_of_isFinitePresentationOnSite
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 05WW, the set equality, with no hypothesis beyond the source's own.** In a
cartesian square of algebraic spaces over `S` with `f : X ⟶ Y`, `g : Y' ⟶ Y`, `f' : X' ⟶ Y'`
and `g' : X' ⟶ X` whose base morphism `g` is flat, the locus of points of `|X'|` at which the
inverse image `(g')^*F` of an `𝒪_X`-module of finite presentation on the small étale site is
flat over `Y'` is the inverse image under `|g'| : |X'| ⟶ |X|` of the locus of points of `|X|`
at which `F` is flat over `Y`.

Both inclusions are the two implications of Stacks 05VW, read at a geometric representative of
the point: the inclusion `⊆` is
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isFlatOverAtGeometricPoint_of_modulePullback`, flatness of `g` being
read pointwise by Stacks 03MM (`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isFlat_iff_forall_isFlatAt`), and the
inclusion `⊇` is `AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isFlatOverAtGeometricPoint_modulePullback`, both
proved in this development.

Finite presentation of `f` is not needed for the equality, and finite presentation of `F`
enters only as the quasi-coherence of `F` and of its inverse image under which flatness at a
point of `|X|` agrees with flatness at a geometric point above it; the finite-presentation
hypotheses of Stacks 05WW are what makes the right-hand side open, by Stacks 05WV, and are
used in `flatLocus_modulePullback_eq_preimage_and_isOpen_of_isFinitePresentationOnSite`.
declarations.statement:
theorem flatLocus_modulePullback_eq_preimage_of_isFinitePresentationOnSite
    {f : X ⟶ Y} {g : Y' ⟶ Y} {f' : X' ⟶ Y'}
    {g' : X' ⟶ X} (sq : IsPullback g'.hom f'.hom f.hom g.hom)
    (F : Modules.{u, u} B S hS X.1 X.2) (hF : SheafOfModules.IsFinitePresentationOnSite F)
    (hg : IsFlat B S hS g.hom) :
    flatLocus B S hS X'.2 f'.hom ((modulePullback B S hS g').obj F) =
      pointsMap B S hS X'.1 g'.hom ⁻¹' flatLocus B S hS X.2 f.hom F
declarations.comment: the set equality; the finite-presentation hypotheses of the source enter through Stacks 05WV in flatLocus_modulePullback_eq_preimage_and_isOpen_of_isFinitePresentationOnSite

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.flatLocus_modulePullback_eq_preimage_and_isOpen_of_isFinitePresentationOnSite
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 05WW, with no hypothesis beyond the source's own.** Let a cartesian square of
algebraic spaces over `S` be given, with `f : X ⟶ Y`, `g : Y' ⟶ Y`, `f' : X' ⟶ Y'` and
`g' : X' ⟶ X`.  Assume `g` is flat, `f` is locally of finite presentation, and the `𝒪_X`-module
`F` is of finite presentation on the small étale site.  Then the locus of points of `|X'|` at
which the inverse image `(g')^*F` is flat over `Y'` is the inverse image under
`|g'| : |X'| ⟶ |X|` of the open subset of Stacks 05WV, and is therefore itself open.

The equality is
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.flatLocus_modulePullback_eq_preimage_of_isFinitePresentationOnSite`,
which is where Stacks 05VW and the flatness of `g` are used.  Openness of the subset of `|X|`
is Stacks 05WV, `AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isOpen_flatLocus_of_isFinitePresentationOnCharts`,
whose chartwise hypotheses on `F` are supplied by the finite presentation of `F` on the site,
and the map on points is continuous by clause (2) of Stacks 03BX.
declarations.statement:
theorem flatLocus_modulePullback_eq_preimage_and_isOpen_of_isFinitePresentationOnSite
    {f : X ⟶ Y} {g : Y' ⟶ Y} {f' : X' ⟶ Y'}
    {g' : X' ⟶ X} (sq : IsPullback g'.hom f'.hom f.hom g.hom)
    (F : Modules.{u, u} B S hS X.1 X.2) (hg : IsFlat B S hS g.hom)
    (hf : IsLocallyOfFinitePresentation B S hS f.hom)
    (hF : SheafOfModules.IsFinitePresentationOnSite F) :
    flatLocus B S hS X'.2 f'.hom ((modulePullback B S hS g').obj F) =
        pointsMap B S hS X'.1 g'.hom ⁻¹' flatLocus B S hS X.2 f.hom F ∧
      IsOpen (flatLocus B S hS X'.2 f'.hom ((modulePullback B S hS g').obj F))
declarations.comment: the locus on the base change is the inverse image of the open subset of Stacks 05WV, hence open

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.exists_chartPoint_isFibreFlatOnChartSquares_iff_isFibreFlatOverAtGeometricPoint
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 05WY: condition (3) if and only if condition (1), with condition (3) carrying a
point of `U` above `x`.**  In Situation 05WX the following are equivalent, for a geometric point
`x̄` of `X`:

1. writing `ȳ = f ∘ x̄` and `z̄ = h ∘ ȳ`, the fibre `F_x̄ / 𝔪_z̄ F_x̄` is flat over
   `𝒪_{Y, ȳ} / 𝔪_z̄ 𝒪_{Y, ȳ}`;
3. there is a commuting diagram of schemes `U ⟶ V ⟶ W` étale over `f` and `h`, **and a point
   `u` of `U` mapping to the image of `x̄` in `|X|`**, at which the fibre of `F|_U` over the
   fibre of `V` is flat.

This is condition (3) as the source states it: the source picks a diagram *and a point
`u ∈ U` mapping to `x`*, with no lift of the geometric point chosen.
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.exists_flatQuotSMul_chart_iff_isFibreFlatOverAtGeometricPoint` is the
same equivalence with the point presented as a lift of `x̄` to the chart.

Condition (3) is read on the local rings of the charts rather than on the scheme-theoretic
fibres `U_w` and `V_w`, through the canonical identifications
`𝒪_{V_w, v} = 𝒪_{V, v}/𝔪_w 𝒪_{V, v}` and `(F_w)_u = (F|_U)_u/𝔪_w (F|_U)_u` which the source
records at the start of its proof.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_chartPoint_isFibreFlatOnChartSquares_iff_isFibreFlatOverAtGeometricPoint
    {X Y Z : AlgebraicSpaces B S hS} (f : X ⟶ Y) (h : Y ⟶ Z)
    (F : Modules.{u, u} B S hS X.1 X.2) [F.IsQuasicoherentOnSite]
    (xbar : GeometricPoint B S hS X.1) :
    (∃ (U : SmallEtale B S hS X.1) (Vc : SmallEtale B S hS Y.1) (Wc : SmallEtale B S hS Z.1)
        (g₁ : U.obj.left ⟶ Vc.obj.left)
        (_hcomm₁ : U.obj.hom ≫ f.hom = yoneda.map g₁ ≫ Vc.obj.hom)
        (g₂ : Vc.obj.left ⟶ Wc.obj.left)
        (_hcomm₂ : Vc.obj.hom ≫ h.hom = yoneda.map g₂ ≫ Wc.obj.hom)
        (u : chartScheme U),
      ChartPoint B S hS U.obj.left U.obj.hom u xbar.image ∧
        IsFibreFlatOnChartSquares B S hS X.1 X.2 F U Vc Wc g₁ g₂ u) ↔
      IsFibreFlatOverAtGeometricPoint B S hS f h F xbar
declarations.comment: (1) iff (3), with condition (3) carrying a point u of U above x as the source states it rather than a lift of the geometric point; condition (3) read on the local rings of the charts

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isFibreFlatOverAtGeometricPoint_congr_of_image_eq
declarations.doc:
**The condition of Stacks 05WY at a geometric point depends only on the point of `|X|` it
lies over.**  For two geometric points `x̄`, `x̄'` of `X` with the same image in `|X|`,
condition (1) of Stacks 05WY holds at `x̄` exactly when it holds at `x̄'`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isFibreFlatOverAtGeometricPoint_congr_of_image_eq {X Y Z : AlgebraicSpaces B S hS}
    (f : X ⟶ Y) (h : Y ⟶ Z) (F : Modules.{u, u} B S hS X.1 X.2) [F.IsQuasicoherentOnSite]
    (xbar xbar' : GeometricPoint B S hS X.1) (himage : xbar.image = xbar'.image) :
    IsFibreFlatOverAtGeometricPoint B S hS f h F xbar ↔
      IsFibreFlatOverAtGeometricPoint B S hS f h F xbar'
declarations.comment: well-posedness of 'pick a geometric point xbar of X lying over x' in condition (1): the condition at a geometric point depends only on its image in |X|

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isFlatOverAtGeometricPoint_fieldFibreSpace_iff_isFibreFlatOverAtGeometricPoint
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 05WY: condition (2) if and only if condition (1).**  In Situation 05WX let `z` be a
field-valued point of `Z` with field of definition `K`, let `X_z = Spec(K) ×_{z, Z} X` and
`Y_z = Spec(K) ×_{z, Z} Y` be the field fibres and let `F_z` be the pullback of `F` to `X_z`.
Then for a geometric point `x̄_z` of `X_z`, the module `F_z` is flat over `Y_z` at `x̄_z` exactly
when condition (1) of Stacks 05WY holds at the image `x̄` of `x̄_z` in `X`.

This is condition (2) of the source.  Relative flatness at a point is read at a geometric point,
as condition (2) of Stacks 05VU
(`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isFlatOverAt_exists_chartDiagram_iff_isFlatOverAtGeometricPoint`
identifies that with the chartwise condition of Definition 05VV which the source cites), and the
statement is at *every* geometric point of `X_z` rather than only at one above the `K`-rational
point `x` of `X_z` that the source's representative `x : Spec(K) ⟶ X` defines — which is the
source's condition (2) together with its independence of the choice of representative, since
condition (1) at the image of `x̄_z` depends only on that image
(`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isFibreFlatOverAtGeometricPoint_congr_of_image_eq`).
declarations.statement:
theorem isFlatOverAtGeometricPoint_fieldFibreSpace_iff_isFibreFlatOverAtGeometricPoint
    {X Y Z : AlgebraicSpaces B S hS} (f : X ⟶ Y) (h : Y ⟶ Z)
    (F : Modules.{u, u} B S hS X.1 X.2) (z : FieldValuedPoint B S hS Z.1)
    (xz : GeometricPoint B S hS (fieldFibreSpace (f ≫ h) z).1) :
    IsFlatOverAtGeometricPoint B S hS
        (ObjectProperty.homMk (fieldFibreSourceMap B S hS f.hom h.hom z) :
          fieldFibreSpace (f ≫ h) z ⟶ fieldFibreSpace h z)
        ((modulePullback B S hS (ObjectProperty.homMk
            (pullback.fst (f.hom ≫ h.hom) (yonedaEquiv.symm z.value)) :
              fieldFibreSpace (f ≫ h) z ⟶ X)).obj F) xz ↔
      IsFibreFlatOverAtGeometricPoint B S hS f h F
        (geometricPointMap (ObjectProperty.homMk
          (pullback.fst (f.hom ≫ h.hom) (yonedaEquiv.symm z.value)) :
            fieldFibreSpace (f ≫ h) z ⟶ X).hom xz)
declarations.comment: (1) iff (2): flatness of the pullback of F to the field fibre X_z over Y_z at a geometric point of X_z, read at a geometric point as in Stacks 05VU, iff condition (1) at the image of that point in X

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isFlatOverAtGeometricPoint_fieldFibreSpace_iff_isFibreFlatOverAtGeometricPoint_of_image_eq
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 05WY, condition (2) against condition (1) at a chosen geometric point of `X`.**
Condition (2) at a geometric point `x̄_z` of the field fibre `X_z` holds exactly when
condition (1) holds at *any* geometric point `x̄` of `X` with the same image in `|X|` as the image
of `x̄_z`.

This is the form the source's condition (1) takes: "pick a geometric point `x̄` of `X` lying
over `x`".
declarations.statement:
theorem isFlatOverAtGeometricPoint_fieldFibreSpace_iff_isFibreFlatOverAtGeometricPoint_of_image_eq
    {X Y Z : AlgebraicSpaces B S hS} (f : X ⟶ Y) (h : Y ⟶ Z)
    (F : Modules.{u, u} B S hS X.1 X.2) [F.IsQuasicoherentOnSite]
    (z : FieldValuedPoint B S hS Z.1)
    (xz : GeometricPoint B S hS (fieldFibreSpace (f ≫ h) z).1)
    (xbar : GeometricPoint B S hS X.1)
    (himage : (geometricPointMap (ObjectProperty.homMk
        (pullback.fst (f.hom ≫ h.hom) (yonedaEquiv.symm z.value)) :
          fieldFibreSpace (f ≫ h) z ⟶ X).hom xz).image = xbar.image) :
    IsFlatOverAtGeometricPoint B S hS
        (ObjectProperty.homMk (fieldFibreSourceMap B S hS f.hom h.hom z) :
          fieldFibreSpace (f ≫ h) z ⟶ fieldFibreSpace h z)
        ((modulePullback B S hS (ObjectProperty.homMk
            (pullback.fst (f.hom ≫ h.hom) (yonedaEquiv.symm z.value)) :
              fieldFibreSpace (f ≫ h) z ⟶ X)).obj F) xz ↔
      IsFibreFlatOverAtGeometricPoint B S hS f h F xbar
declarations.comment: (1) iff (2) with condition (1) at an arbitrary chosen geometric point of X above the point, as the source states condition (1)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isFlatOverAtPoint_fieldFibreSpace_iff_isFibreFlatOverAtGeometricPoint
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 05WY: condition (2) in the chartwise form of Definition 05VV, if and only if
condition (1).**  The pullback `F_z` of `F` to the field fibre `X_z` is flat at the image in
`|X_z|` of a geometric point `x̄_z`, over `Y_z`, in the sense of Definition 05VV, exactly when
condition (1) of Stacks 05WY holds at the image of `x̄_z` in `X`.

This is condition (2) with flatness at a point spelled by
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.IsFlatOverAtPoint`, the predicate of Definition 05VV that the source
cites, rather than at a geometric point.
declarations.statement:
theorem isFlatOverAtPoint_fieldFibreSpace_iff_isFibreFlatOverAtGeometricPoint
    {X Y Z : AlgebraicSpaces B S hS} (f : X ⟶ Y) (h : Y ⟶ Z)
    (F : Modules.{u, u} B S hS X.1 X.2) [F.IsQuasicoherentOnSite]
    (z : FieldValuedPoint B S hS Z.1)
    (xz : GeometricPoint B S hS (fieldFibreSpace (f ≫ h) z).1) :
    IsFlatOverAtPoint B S hS (fieldFibreSpace (f ≫ h) z).2
        (ObjectProperty.homMk (fieldFibreSourceMap B S hS f.hom h.hom z) :
          fieldFibreSpace (f ≫ h) z ⟶ fieldFibreSpace h z).hom
        ((modulePullback B S hS (ObjectProperty.homMk
            (pullback.fst (f.hom ≫ h.hom) (yonedaEquiv.symm z.value)) :
              fieldFibreSpace (f ≫ h) z ⟶ X)).obj F) xz.image ↔
      IsFibreFlatOverAtGeometricPoint B S hS f h F
        (geometricPointMap (ObjectProperty.homMk
          (pullback.fst (f.hom ≫ h.hom) (yonedaEquiv.symm z.value)) :
            fieldFibreSpace (f ≫ h) z ⟶ X).hom xz)
declarations.comment: (1) iff (2) with condition (2) in the chartwise form of Definition 05VV, which is the predicate the source cites
