declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isFlatOverAtGeometricPoint_fieldFibreSpace_iff_exists_chartPoint
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 05WY: condition (2) if and only if condition (3).**  In Situation 05WX, flatness of
the pullback `F_z` over `Y_z` at a geometric point `x̄_z` of the field fibre `X_z` holds exactly
when there is a commuting diagram of schemes `U ⟶ V ⟶ W` étale over `f` and `h` and a point `u`
of `U` above the image of `x̄_z` in `|X|`, at which the fibre of `F|_U` over the fibre of `V` is
flat.
declarations.statement:
theorem isFlatOverAtGeometricPoint_fieldFibreSpace_iff_exists_chartPoint
    {X Y Z : AlgebraicSpaces B S hS} (f : X ⟶ Y) (h : Y ⟶ Z)
    (F : Modules.{u, u} B S hS X.1 X.2) [F.IsQuasicoherentOnSite]
    (z : FieldValuedPoint B S hS Z.1)
    (xz : GeometricPoint B S hS (fieldFibreSpace (f ≫ h) z).1) :
    IsFlatOverAtGeometricPoint B S hS
        (ObjectProperty.homMk (fieldFibreSourceMap B S hS f.hom h.hom z) :
          fieldFibreSpace (f ≫ h) z ⟶ fieldFibreSpace h z)
        ((modulePullback B S hS (ObjectProperty.homMk
            (pullback.fst (f.hom ≫ h.hom) (yonedaEquiv.symm z.value)) :
              fieldFibreSpace (f ≫ h) z ⟶ X)).obj F) xz ↔
      ∃ (U : SmallEtale B S hS X.1) (Vc : SmallEtale B S hS Y.1) (Wc : SmallEtale B S hS Z.1)
          (g₁ : U.obj.left ⟶ Vc.obj.left)
          (_hcomm₁ : U.obj.hom ≫ f.hom = yoneda.map g₁ ≫ Vc.obj.hom)
          (g₂ : Vc.obj.left ⟶ Wc.obj.left)
          (_hcomm₂ : Vc.obj.hom ≫ h.hom = yoneda.map g₂ ≫ Wc.obj.hom)
          (u : chartScheme U),
        ChartPoint B S hS U.obj.left U.obj.hom u
            (geometricPointMap (ObjectProperty.homMk
              (pullback.fst (f.hom ≫ h.hom) (yonedaEquiv.symm z.value)) :
                fieldFibreSpace (f ≫ h) z ⟶ X).hom xz).image ∧
          IsFibreFlatOnChartSquares B S hS X.1 X.2 F U Vc Wc g₁ g₂ u
declarations.comment: (2) iff (3), composed through condition (1); condition (3) carrying a point u of U above x as the source states it, read on the local rings of the charts

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isFlatOnFibreAtFieldValuedPoint_iff_isFibreFlatOverAtGeometricPoint
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 05WY, (1) `⟺` (2).** Let `f : X ⟶ Y` and `h : Y ⟶ Z` be morphisms of algebraic
spaces over `S`, let `F` be a quasi-coherent `𝒪_X`-module and let `x` be a point of `|X|`.  For
every geometric point `x̄` of `X` lying over `x` and every field-valued point
`x : Spec(K) ⟶ X` in the class of `x`, with `z = h ∘ f ∘ x`, the following are equivalent:

1. the module `F_{x̄}/𝔪_{z̄} F_{x̄}` is flat over `𝒪_{Y, ȳ}/𝔪_{z̄} 𝒪_{Y, ȳ}`, where `ȳ = f ∘ x̄`
   and `z̄ = h ∘ ȳ`;
2. the pullback `F_z` of `F` to `X_z = Spec(K) ×_{z, Z} X` is flat over
   `Y_z = Spec(K) ×_{z, Z} Y` at the `K`-rational point of `X_z` determined by `x`, in the sense
   of Stacks 05VV.

In particular neither condition depends on the choices made.
declarations.statement:
theorem isFlatOnFibreAtFieldValuedPoint_iff_isFibreFlatOverAtGeometricPoint
    (F : Modules.{u, u} B S hS X.1 X.2) [F.IsQuasicoherentOnSite] (x : points B S hS X.1)
    (xbar : GeometricPoint B S hS X.1) (hxbar : xbar.LiesOver x)
    (hp : p.class B S hS X.1 = x) :
    IsFlatOnFibreAtFieldValuedPoint B S hS f h p F ↔
      IsFibreFlatOverAtGeometricPoint B S hS f h F xbar
declarations.comment: (1) iff (2), for every geometric point over x and every field-valued representative of x

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.exists_flatQuotSMul_chart_iff_isFibreFlatOverAtGeometricPoint
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 05WY: condition (3) if and only if condition (1).** In Situation 05WX — a scheme
`S`, algebraic spaces `X`, `Y`, `Z` over `S` with `f : X ⟶ Y` and `h : Y ⟶ Z`, a quasi-coherent
`𝒪_X`-module `F` and a geometric point `x̄` of `X` — the following are equivalent:

1. writing `ȳ = f ∘ x̄` and `z̄ = h ∘ ȳ`, the fibre `F_x̄ / 𝔪_z̄ F_x̄` is flat over
   `𝒪_{Y, ȳ} / 𝔪_z̄ 𝒪_{Y, ȳ}`;
3. there is a commuting diagram of schemes `U ⟶ V ⟶ W` étale over `f` and `h`, and a point `u`
   of `U` above the image of `x̄`, at which the fibre of `F|_U` over the fibre of `V` is flat.

Condition (3) of the source reads the second condition on the scheme-theoretic fibres `U_w` and
`V_w`; here it is read on their local rings, through the canonical identifications
`𝒪_{V_w, v} = 𝒪_{V, v}/𝔪_w 𝒪_{V, v}` and `(F_w)_u = (F|_U)_u/𝔪_w (F|_U)_u` which the source
records at the start of its proof. The point `u` above `x̄` is presented as a lift of `x̄` to the
chart, which is the same data by Stacks 05VN
(`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.exists_chartLift_of_chartPoint` and
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.chartPoint_isChartPoint`).

Condition (2) of the source, flatness of the pullback of `F` to the fibre `X_z` over `Y_z` in
the sense of Stacks 05VV, is not among the conditions compared here; it is
`Space.isFlatOverAtGeometricPoint_fieldFibreSpace_iff_isFibreFlatOverAtGeometricPoint`
of `StacksFrontier/AlgebraicGeometry/Spaces/FibreFlatnessFieldFibre.lean`, and
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isFlatOverAtGeometricPoint_fieldFibreSpace_iff_exists_chartPoint`
composes it with this lemma.

Such a diagram always exists (`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.exists_chartSquares`), which is what the
second direction uses: take `W ⟶ Z` surjective étale, then `V ⟶ W ×_Z Y` and `U ⟶ V ×_Y X`
surjective étale, and a point of `U` above the image of `x̄`.  Since no diagram is privileged,
condition (3) in fact holds at *every* diagram as soon as it holds at one, which is
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.forall_flatQuotSMul_chart_iff_isFibreFlatOverAtGeometricPoint`.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_flatQuotSMul_chart_iff_isFibreFlatOverAtGeometricPoint
    {X Y Z : AlgebraicSpaces B S hS} (f : X ⟶ Y) (h : Y ⟶ Z)
    (F : Modules.{u, u} B S hS X.1 X.2) [F.IsQuasicoherentOnSite]
    (xbar : GeometricPoint B S hS X.1) :
    (∃ (N : SmallEtaleNeighborhood xbar) (Vc : SmallEtale B S hS Y.1)
        (g₁ : N.chart.obj.left ⟶ Vc.obj.left)
        (hcomm₁ : N.chart.obj.hom ≫ f.hom = yoneda.map g₁ ≫ Vc.obj.hom)
        (Wc : SmallEtale B S hS Z.1) (g₂ : Vc.obj.left ⟶ Wc.obj.left)
        (hcomm₂ : Vc.obj.hom ≫ h.hom = yoneda.map g₂ ≫ Wc.obj.hom),
      Module.FlatQuotSMul
        (((BigFppfOver.toScheme B S hS).map g₁).stalkMap (chartPoint B S hS X.1 N)).hom
        ((maximalIdeal ↥(chartLocalRing B S hS Z.1 (targetNeighborhood B S hS
              (targetNeighborhood B S hS N Vc g₁ hcomm₁) Wc g₂ hcomm₂))).map
          (((BigFppfOver.toScheme B S hS).map g₂).stalkMap
            (chartPoint B S hS Y.1 (targetNeighborhood B S hS N Vc g₁ hcomm₁))).hom)
        (((maximalIdeal ↥(chartLocalRing B S hS Z.1 (targetNeighborhood B S hS
                (targetNeighborhood B S hS N Vc g₁ hcomm₁) Wc g₂ hcomm₂))).map
            (((BigFppfOver.toScheme B S hS).map g₂).stalkMap
              (chartPoint B S hS Y.1 (targetNeighborhood B S hS N Vc g₁ hcomm₁))).hom).map
          (((BigFppfOver.toScheme B S hS).map g₁).stalkMap (chartPoint B S hS X.1 N)).hom)
        rfl ↥(chartZariskiModuleStalk B S hS X.1 X.2 N F)) ↔
      IsFibreFlatOverAtGeometricPoint B S hS f h F xbar
declarations.comment: (1) iff (3), condition (3) read on the local rings of the charts

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.forall_flatQuotSMul_chart_iff_isFibreFlatOverAtGeometricPoint
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 05WY: condition (3) at an arbitrary chosen diagram if and only if condition (1).**
In Situation 05WX the chart condition (3) of Stacks 05WY holds on *every* pointed pair of
composable commuting squares of étale scheme charts `U ⟶ V ⟶ W` of `f` and `h` exactly when
condition (1) holds at `x̄`.

This is the "any choice works" reading of condition (3) the source intends: the source says
"choose a commutative diagram", so the condition must not depend on the choice.  Together with
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.exists_flatQuotSMul_chart_iff_isFibreFlatOverAtGeometricPoint` it says
that the some-diagram and every-diagram readings of condition (3) agree, a diagram existing by
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.exists_chartSquares`.
declarations.statement:
theorem forall_flatQuotSMul_chart_iff_isFibreFlatOverAtGeometricPoint
    {X Y Z : AlgebraicSpaces B S hS} (f : X ⟶ Y) (h : Y ⟶ Z)
    (F : Modules.{u, u} B S hS X.1 X.2) [F.IsQuasicoherentOnSite]
    (xbar : GeometricPoint B S hS X.1) :
    (∀ (N : SmallEtaleNeighborhood xbar) (Vc : SmallEtale B S hS Y.1)
        (g₁ : N.chart.obj.left ⟶ Vc.obj.left)
        (hcomm₁ : N.chart.obj.hom ≫ f.hom = yoneda.map g₁ ≫ Vc.obj.hom)
        (Wc : SmallEtale B S hS Z.1) (g₂ : Vc.obj.left ⟶ Wc.obj.left)
        (hcomm₂ : Vc.obj.hom ≫ h.hom = yoneda.map g₂ ≫ Wc.obj.hom),
      Module.FlatQuotSMul
        (((BigFppfOver.toScheme B S hS).map g₁).stalkMap (chartPoint B S hS X.1 N)).hom
        ((maximalIdeal ↥(chartLocalRing B S hS Z.1 (targetNeighborhood B S hS
              (targetNeighborhood B S hS N Vc g₁ hcomm₁) Wc g₂ hcomm₂))).map
          (((BigFppfOver.toScheme B S hS).map g₂).stalkMap
            (chartPoint B S hS Y.1 (targetNeighborhood B S hS N Vc g₁ hcomm₁))).hom)
        (((maximalIdeal ↥(chartLocalRing B S hS Z.1 (targetNeighborhood B S hS
                (targetNeighborhood B S hS N Vc g₁ hcomm₁) Wc g₂ hcomm₂))).map
            (((BigFppfOver.toScheme B S hS).map g₂).stalkMap
              (chartPoint B S hS Y.1 (targetNeighborhood B S hS N Vc g₁ hcomm₁))).hom).map
          (((BigFppfOver.toScheme B S hS).map g₁).stalkMap (chartPoint B S hS X.1 N)).hom)
        rfl ↥(chartZariskiModuleStalk B S hS X.1 X.2 N F)) ↔
      IsFibreFlatOverAtGeometricPoint B S hS f h F xbar
declarations.comment: (1) iff (3) at an arbitrary chosen diagram: the every-diagram reading of condition (3), read on the local rings of the charts

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.IsFlatOnFibreAt
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 05WZ, part (1).** The restriction of an `𝒪_X`-module `F` to its fibre over the
image `z` of a point `x` of `|X|` is *flat at `x` over the fibre of `Y` over `z`* when the
condition of Stacks 05WY holds at every geometric point of `X` above `x`.

The source defines this by "the equivalent conditions of Lemma 05WY are satisfied"; the
condition used is `AlgebraicGeometry.Space.IsFibreFlatOverAtGeometricPoint`, condition (1) of
that lemma, whose equivalence with condition (3) is
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.exists_flatQuotSMul_chart_iff_isFibreFlatOverAtGeometricPoint`.  See
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isFlatOnFibreAt_iff_isFibreFlatOverAtGeometricPoint` for the reading at
a single chosen geometric point.
declarations.statement:
def IsFlatOnFibreAt {X Y Z : AlgebraicSpaces B S hS} (f : X ⟶ Y) (h : Y ⟶ Z)
    (F : Modules.{u, m} B S hS X.1 X.2) (x : points B S hS X.1) : Prop
declarations.comment: part (1), defined through the Lemma 05WY notion IsFibreFlatOverAtGeometricPoint (its condition (1)), asked at every geometric point over x; equal to that condition at any one such point by isFlatOnFibreAt_iff_...

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.IsFlatFibreAt
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 05WZ, part (2).** The fibre of `X` over the image `z` of a point `x` of `|X|` is
*flat at `x` over the fibre of `Y` over `z`* when part (1) holds for `F = 𝒪_X`.
declarations.statement:
def IsFlatFibreAt {X Y Z : AlgebraicSpaces B S hS} (f : X ⟶ Y) (h : Y ⟶ Z)
    (x : points B S hS X.1) : Prop
declarations.comment: part (2), part (1) at F = O_X, hence defined through the Lemma 05WY notion IsFibreFlatOverAtGeometricPoint at every geometric point over x

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.IsFlatFibre
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 05WZ, part (3).** The fibre of `X` over a point `z` of `|Z|` is *flat over the
fibre of `Y` over `z`* when part (2) holds at every point of `|X|` lying over `z`.
declarations.statement:
def IsFlatFibre {X Y Z : AlgebraicSpaces B S hS} (f : X ⟶ Y) (h : Y ⟶ Z)
    (z : points B S hS Z.1) : Prop
declarations.comment: part (3), part (2) at every point of |X| over z, hence defined through the Lemma 05WY notion IsFibreFlatOverAtGeometricPoint

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isFlatOverAtGeometricPoint_and_isFibreFlat_iff
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 05X0.** Let `f : X ⟶ Y` and `g : Y ⟶ Z` be morphisms of algebraic spaces over a
scheme `S`, let `F` be an `𝒪_X`-module which is quasi-coherent on the small étale site and of
finite presentation on charts, and let `x̄` be a geometric point of `X` with images `ȳ` and `z̄`.
Assume `X` is locally of finite presentation over `Z` and `Y` is locally of finite type over
`Z`, and assume `F_{x̄} ≠ 0`.  Then

1. `F` is flat over `Z` at `x̄` and the restriction of `F` to its fibre over `z̄` is flat at `x̄`
   over the fibre of `Y` over `z̄`

holds exactly when

2. `Y` is flat over `Z` at `ȳ` and `F` is flat over `Y` at `x̄`

holds.  The fibre condition of (1) is the one of Stacks 05WY, as the source's definition
(Stacks 05WZ) prescribes.
declarations.statement:
theorem isFlatOverAtGeometricPoint_and_isFibreFlat_iff {X Y Z : AlgebraicSpaces B S hS}
    (f : X ⟶ Y) (g : Y ⟶ Z) (F : Modules.{u, u} B S hS X.1 X.2) [F.IsQuasicoherentOnSite]
    (hp : IsLocallyOfFinitePresentation B S hS (f ≫ g).hom)
    (hq : IsLocallyOfFiniteType B S hS g.hom)
    (hfp : IsFinitePresentationOnCharts B S hS X.2 F)
    (xbar : GeometricPoint B S hS X.1)
    (hne : Nontrivial (geometricModuleStalk B S hS X xbar F)) :
    (IsFlatOverAtGeometricPoint B S hS (f ≫ g) F xbar ∧
        IsFibreFlatOverAtGeometricPoint B S hS f g F xbar) ↔
      (IsFlatAt B S hS g.hom (geometricPointMap f.hom xbar).image ∧
        IsFlatOverAtGeometricPoint B S hS f F xbar)
declarations.comment: the equivalence of (1) and (2) at a geometric point `x̄`: flatness over `Z` and over `Y` at `x̄` are condition (2) of Stacks 05VU, the fibre condition of (1) is the one of Stacks 05WY named by the source's definition 05WZ, and flatness of `Y` over `Z` at `ȳ` is Space.IsFlatAt at its image point. Hypothesis (2) of the source is read on the Zariski site of every etale chart; the openness assertion is isOpen_setOf_... below.

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.setOf_isFlatOverAtGeometricPoint_and_isFibreFlat_eq
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 05X0, the openness assertion.** Under the hypotheses of Stacks 05X0, the set of
points of `|X|` lying in the support of `F` at which conditions (1) and (2) hold at every
geometric point above them is the intersection of that support with the open set
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isOpen_flatLocus_inter_flatLocus` is about, namely the locus where `F`
is flat both over `Z` and over `Y`.  So that set is open in the support of `F`.

A point of the support at which (1) and (2) hold lies in both flat loci by (1) and (2); and at a
point of the support lying in both loci condition (1) holds, the fibre condition being a base
change of flatness over `Y`, hence so does condition (2) by the equivalence.
declarations.statement:
theorem setOf_isFlatOverAtGeometricPoint_and_isFibreFlat_eq (f : X ⟶ Y) (g : Y ⟶ Z)
    (F : Modules.{u, u} B S hS X.1 X.2) [F.IsQuasicoherentOnSite]
    (hp : IsLocallyOfFinitePresentation B S hS (f ≫ g).hom)
    (hq : IsLocallyOfFiniteType B S hS g.hom)
    (hfp : IsFinitePresentationOnCharts B S hS X.2 F) :
    {x : points B S hS X.1 |
        x ∈ supportOfSheaf B S hS X.1 ((SheafOfModules.toSheaf _).obj F) ∧
        ∀ xbar : GeometricPoint B S hS X.1, xbar.image = x →
          (IsFlatOverAtGeometricPoint B S hS (f ≫ g) F xbar ∧
              IsFibreFlatOverAtGeometricPoint B S hS f g F xbar) ∧
            (IsFlatAt B S hS g.hom (geometricPointMap f.hom xbar).image ∧
              IsFlatOverAtGeometricPoint B S hS f F xbar)} =
      (flatLocus B S hS X.2 (f ≫ g).hom F ∩ flatLocus B S hS X.2 f.hom F) ∩
        supportOfSheaf B S hS X.1 ((SheafOfModules.toSheaf _).obj F)
declarations.comment: the openness assertion: the locus where (1) and (2) hold is the support of the module intersected with the locus where the module is flat over both `Z` and `Y`, which is open by Space.isOpen_flatLocus_inter_flatLocus. Conditions (1) and (2) are read at every geometric point above the point of `|X|`, which is no restriction: by Stacks 05VU the conditions do not depend on the geometric point chosen above it.

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isOpen_setOf_isFlatOverAtGeometricPoint_and_isFibreFlat
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 05X0, the openness assertion in the subspace of the support.** Under the hypotheses
of Stacks 05X0 the set of points of the support of `F` at which conditions (1) and (2) hold is
open in the support.

This is `AlgebraicGeometry.Space.setOf_isFlatOverAtGeometricPoint_and_isFibreFlat_eq` read in
the subspace topology: the set is the inverse image in the support of the open set of
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isOpen_flatLocus_inter_flatLocus`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isOpen_setOf_isFlatOverAtGeometricPoint_and_isFibreFlat (f : X ⟶ Y) (g : Y ⟶ Z)
    (F : Modules.{u, u} B S hS X.1 X.2) [F.IsQuasicoherentOnSite]
    (hp : IsLocallyOfFinitePresentation B S hS (f ≫ g).hom)
    (hq : IsLocallyOfFiniteType B S hS g.hom)
    (hfp : IsFinitePresentationOnCharts B S hS X.2 F) :
    IsOpen {x : (supportOfSheaf B S hS X.1 ((SheafOfModules.toSheaf _).obj F) :
        Set (points B S hS X.1)) |
      ∀ xbar : GeometricPoint B S hS X.1, xbar.image = (x : points B S hS X.1) →
        (IsFlatOverAtGeometricPoint B S hS (f ≫ g) F xbar ∧
            IsFibreFlatOverAtGeometricPoint B S hS f g F xbar) ∧
          (IsFlatAt B S hS g.hom (geometricPointMap f.hom xbar).image ∧
            IsFlatOverAtGeometricPoint B S hS f F xbar)}
declarations.comment: the openness assertion, read in the subspace topology of the support: the locus where (1) and (2) hold is open in Supp(F). Conditions (1) and (2) are read at every geometric point above the point of `|X|`, which by Stacks 05VU does not depend on the geometric point chosen. Finite presentation of the module is read on the Zariski site of every etale scheme chart.

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isFlat_of_flatFibreCharts_finitePresentation
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 05X1, the first conclusion.** Let `f : X ⟶ Y` and `g : Y ⟶ Z` be
morphisms of algebraic spaces over a scheme `S`. If `X` is locally of finite presentation over
`Z`, `X` is flat over `Z`, the fibres of `X` over the points of `Z` are flat over the
corresponding fibres of `Y` in the chart sense of
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.HasFlatFibreCharts`, and `Y` is locally of finite type over `Z`, then
`f` is flat.
declarations.statement:
theorem isFlat_of_flatFibreCharts_finitePresentation
    (hX : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS X) (hY : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS Y)
    (hZ : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS Z) (f : X ⟶ Y) (g : Y ⟶ Z)
    (hfp : IsLocallyOfFinitePresentation B S hS (f ≫ g))
    (hflat : IsFlat B S hS (f ≫ g)) (hft : IsLocallyOfFiniteType B S hS g)
    (hfib : HasFlatFibreCharts B S hS f g) :
    IsFlat B S hS f
declarations.comment: the first conclusion: flatness of `f`. Hypotheses (1), (2) and (4) are the library spellings Space.IsLocallyOfFinitePresentation of `f ≫ g`, Space.IsFlat of `f ≫ g` and Space.IsLocallyOfFiniteType of `g`; hypothesis (3) is CARRIED in its every-etale-chart reading Space.HasFlatFibreCharts, as in the locally Noetherian form Space.isFlat_of_flatFibreCharts of Stacks 0APS, the comparison of a fibre of an algebraic space with the scheme-theoretic fibre of a chart being available in this library only for properties of objects (Space.hasEtaleLocalProperty_fiberAt_iff) and not for a property of a morphism between two such fibres.

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isFlat_of_flatFibreCharts_finitePresentation_of_isSurjective
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 05X1, the second conclusion.** In the situation of
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isFlat_of_flatFibreCharts_finitePresentation`, if `f` is in addition
surjective then `Y` is flat over `Z`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isFlat_of_flatFibreCharts_finitePresentation_of_isSurjective
    (hX : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS X) (hY : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS Y)
    (hZ : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS Z) (f : X ⟶ Y) (g : Y ⟶ Z)
    (hfp : IsLocallyOfFinitePresentation B S hS (f ≫ g))
    (hflat : IsFlat B S hS (f ≫ g)) (hft : IsLocallyOfFiniteType B S hS g)
    (hfib : HasFlatFibreCharts B S hS f g) (hfs : IsSurjective B S hS f) :
    IsFlat B S hS g
declarations.comment: the second conclusion: flatness of `Y` over `Z` for surjective `f`, with surjectivity taken as Space.IsSurjective of Stacks 03ME. Hypotheses (1), (2) and (4) are the library spellings Space.IsLocallyOfFinitePresentation of `f ≫ g`, Space.IsFlat of `f ≫ g` and Space.IsLocallyOfFiniteType of `g`; hypothesis (3) is CARRIED in its every-etale-chart reading Space.HasFlatFibreCharts, as in the locally Noetherian form Space.isFlat_of_flatFibreCharts_of_isSurjective of Stacks 0APS, the comparison of a fibre of an algebraic space with the scheme-theoretic fibre of a chart being available in this library only for properties of objects and not for a property of a morphism between two such fibres.

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.flatLocus_modulePullback_eq_preimage_of_isFlatOverBase
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 05X2, the base-change assertion.** Let `f : X ⟶ Y` be a morphism of algebraic
spaces over `S` whose source and target are given over an algebraic space `Z` by `f ≫ q` and
`q : Y ⟶ Z`, and let `F` be a quasi-coherent `𝒪_X`-module.  Assume `X` is locally of finite
presentation over `Z`, that `F` is of finite presentation, that `F` is flat over `Z`, and that
`Y` is locally of finite type over `Z`.  Then for a base change along an arbitrary morphism
`h : Z' ⟶ Z`, presented by the cartesian squares `Y' = Y ×_Z Z'` and `X' = X ×_Y Y'`, the locus
of points of `|X'|` at which the inverse image of `F` is flat over `Y'` is the inverse image
under `|X'| ⟶ |X|` of the locus of points of `|X|` at which `F` is flat over `Y`.
declarations.statement:
theorem flatLocus_modulePullback_eq_preimage_of_isFlatOverBase
    {f : X ⟶ Y} {q : Y ⟶ Z} {h : Z' ⟶ Z} {g : Y' ⟶ Y} {q' : Y' ⟶ Z'}
    {g' : X' ⟶ X} {f' : X' ⟶ Y'}
    (sqY : IsPullback g q' q h) (sqX : IsPullback g' f' f g)
    (F : Modules.{u, u} B S hS X.1 X.2) [F.IsQuasicoherentOnSite]
    (hFfp : F.IsFinitePresentation)
    (hp : IsLocallyOfFinitePresentation B S hS (f ≫ q).hom)
    (hq : IsLocallyOfFiniteType B S hS q.hom)
    (hFZ : IsFlatOver B S hS X.2 (f ≫ q).hom F) :
    flatLocus B S hS X'.2 f'.hom ((modulePullback B S hS g').obj F) =
      pointsMap B S hS X'.1 g'.hom ⁻¹' flatLocus B S hS X.2 f.hom F
declarations.comment: base change: the locus on the base change is the inverse image of the locus downstairs. Hypotheses (1)-(4) of the source are the finite presentation of `X` over `Z`, of the module on the small etale site, the flatness of the module over `Z`, and the finite type of `Y` over `Z`. The openness assertion is Space.isOpen_flatLocus_of_isLocallyOfFinitePresentation_comp.

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isOpen_flatLocus_of_isLocallyOfFinitePresentation_comp
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 05X2, the openness assertion.** Let `f : X ⟶ Y` be a morphism of algebraic spaces
over `S` whose source and target are given over an algebraic space `Z` by `p : X ⟶ Z` and
`q : Y ⟶ Z` with `f ≫ q = p`.  If `p` is locally of finite presentation and `q` is locally of
finite type, then the locus of points of `|X|` at which an `𝒪_X`-module which is quasi-coherent
of finite presentation on charts is flat over `Y` is open.

The tag sits on
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isOpen_flatLocus_of_isFinitePresentationOnSite_comp`, which is this
assertion with hypothesis (2) of the source read where the source reads it, on the small étale
site; this form is the special case of it at a module whose finite presentation is available
only chartwise.
declarations.statement:
theorem isOpen_flatLocus_of_isLocallyOfFinitePresentation_comp
    (hX : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS X) (hY : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS Y)
    (hZ : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS Z) (f : X ⟶ Y) (p : X ⟶ Z) (q : Y ⟶ Z) (hfq : f ≫ q = p)
    (F : Modules.{u, u} B S hS X hX)
    (hp : IsLocallyOfFinitePresentation B S hS p)
    (hq : IsLocallyOfFiniteType B S hS q)
    (hqc : IsQuasicoherentOnCharts B S hS hX F)
    (hfp : IsFinitePresentationOnCharts B S hS hX F) :
    IsOpen (flatLocus B S hS hX f F)
declarations.comment: openness; hypothesis (3), flatness over the base, is not needed for this half

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isOpen_flatLocus_of_isFinitePresentationOnSite_comp
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 05X2, the openness assertion, from finite presentation on the small étale site.**
Let `f : X ⟶ Y` be a morphism of algebraic spaces over `S` whose source and target are given
over an algebraic space `Z` by `p : X ⟶ Z` and `q : Y ⟶ Z` with `f ≫ q = p`.  If `p` is locally
of finite presentation and `q` is locally of finite type, then the locus of points of `|X|` at
which an `𝒪_X`-module of finite presentation on the small étale site is flat over `Y` is open.

Hypothesis (2) of the source, finite presentation of the module, is Stacks 03DL (7) on the small
étale site of `X`; the quasi-coherence of the module which the source assumes in its preamble
follows from it, by `SheafOfModules.isQuasicoherentOnSite_of_isFinitePresentationOnSite`.  Both
are passed to the charts by
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isFinitePresentationOnCharts_of_isFinitePresentationOnSite` and
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isQuasicoherentOnCharts_of_isFinitePresentationOnSite`, so this form
asks no chartwise hypothesis and
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isOpen_flatLocus_of_isLocallyOfFinitePresentation_comp` is the special
case of it at a module whose finite presentation is only available chartwise.
declarations.statement:
theorem isOpen_flatLocus_of_isFinitePresentationOnSite_comp
    (hX : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS X) (hY : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS Y)
    (hZ : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS Z) (f : X ⟶ Y) (p : X ⟶ Z) (q : Y ⟶ Z) (hfq : f ≫ q = p)
    (F : Modules.{u, u} B S hS X hX)
    (hp : IsLocallyOfFinitePresentation B S hS p)
    (hq : IsLocallyOfFiniteType B S hS q)
    (hFfp : SheafOfModules.IsFinitePresentationOnSite F) :
    IsOpen (flatLocus B S hS hX f F)
declarations.comment: openness; hypothesis (3), flatness over the base, is not needed for this half

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isOpen_setOf_isFlatAt_of_isLocallyOfFinitePresentation_comp
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 05X3, the openness assertion.** Let `f : X ⟶ Y` be a morphism of algebraic spaces
over `S` whose source and target are given over a third algebraic space `Z` by morphisms
`p : X ⟶ Z` and `q : Y ⟶ Z` with `f ≫ q = p`. If `p` is locally of finite presentation and `q`
is locally of finite type, then the set of points of `|X|` at which `f` is flat is open.

Flatness of `p`, which the source assumes, is not needed here: the two finiteness hypotheses
already make `f` locally of finite presentation by Stacks 05WT, so the openness of the flat
locus of a morphism locally of finite presentation applies to `f` itself. The same reduction
is how the scheme-level assertion of Stacks 05VK is proved.
declarations.statement:
theorem isOpen_setOf_isFlatAt_of_isLocallyOfFinitePresentation_comp
    {Z : (BigFppfOver B S hS)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u} (hX : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS X)
    (hY : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS Y) (hZ : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS Z)
    (f : X ⟶ Y) (p : X ⟶ Z) (q : Y ⟶ Z) (hfq : f ≫ q = p)
    (hp : IsLocallyOfFinitePresentation B S hS p)
    (hq : IsLocallyOfFiniteType B S hS q) :
    IsOpen {x : points B S hS X | IsFlatAt B S hS f x}
declarations.comment: openness of the flat locus

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.flatLocusOpenAndStableUnderBaseChange
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 05X3.** For a commutative triangle of algebraic spaces over `S` given by
`f : X ⟶ Y`, `p : X ⟶ Z` and `q : Y ⟶ Z` with `f ≫ q = p`, with `p` locally of finite
presentation and flat and `q` locally of finite type, the locus of points of `|X|` at which `f`
is flat is open and its formation commutes with base change along any morphism `Z' ⟶ Z`.

The openness assertion is
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isOpen_setOf_isFlatAt_of_isLocallyOfFinitePresentation_comp` and the
base-change assertion is `AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isFlatAt_baseChangeOverBase_iff`.
declarations.statement:
theorem flatLocusOpenAndStableUnderBaseChange
    {X Y Z : (BigFppfOver B S hS)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u} (hX : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS X)
    (hY : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS Y) (hZ : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS Z)
    (f : X ⟶ Y) (p : X ⟶ Z) (q : Y ⟶ Z) (hfq : f ≫ q = p)
    (hp : IsLocallyOfFinitePresentation B S hS p) (hpflat : IsFlat B S hS p)
    (hq : IsLocallyOfFiniteType B S hS q) :
    IsOpen {x : points B S hS X | IsFlatAt B S hS f x} ∧
      ∀ (Z' : (BigFppfOver B S hS)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u), IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS Z' →
        ∀ (g : Z' ⟶ Z) (x' : points B S hS (pullback p g)),
          IsFlatAt B S hS (baseChangeOverBase B S hS f p q hfq g) x' ↔
            IsFlatAt B S hS f
              (pointsMap B S hS (pullback p g) (pullback.fst p g) x')
declarations.comment: openness and base change of the relative flat locus

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.exists_isOpenSubspace_forall_factorsThrough_iff_isUnramified_baseChange
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 05X8.** Let `f : X ⟶ Y` be a morphism of algebraic spaces over `S` whose source and
target are given over a third algebraic space `Z` by morphisms `p : X ⟶ Z` and `q : Y ⟶ Z` with
`f ≫ q = p`. If `p` is locally of finite type and closed, then there is an open subspace `W` of
`Z` through which a morphism `Z' ⟶ Z` from an algebraic space factors exactly when the base
change of `f` along it is unramified.

The open subspace is the one cut out, through the correspondence of Stacks 03BZ, by the
complement of the image under `p` of the set of points at which `f` is not unramified: that set
is closed because the unramified locus of part (1) of Stacks 05W2 is open, and its image is
closed because `p` is. Factoring through `W` is the containment of the image of the points of
`Z'` in that complement, by Stacks 03IE, while unramifiedness of the base change is
unramifiedness at each of its points, by Stacks 03ZK; part (2) of Stacks 05W2 identifies the
latter with unramifiedness of `f` at each point of `X` lying over a point of the image of `Z'`,
and the two conditions then agree by a complementation.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_isOpenSubspace_forall_factorsThrough_iff_isUnramified_baseChange
    (hX : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS X) (hY : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS Y)
    (hZ : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS Z) (f : X ⟶ Y) (p : X ⟶ Z) (q : Y ⟶ Z) (hfq : f ≫ q = p)
    (hp : IsLocallyOfFiniteType B S hS p) (hpc : IsClosedMorphism B S hS p) :
    ∃ W : Subfunctor Z, IsOpenSubspace B S hS W ∧
      ∀ (Z' : (BigFppfOver B S hS)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u) (_ : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS Z') (g : Z' ⟶ Z),
        (∃ r : Z' ⟶ W.toFunctor, r ≫ W.ι = g) ↔
          IsUnramified B S hS (baseChangeOverBase B S hS f p q hfq g)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.exists_isOpenSubspace_iff_isUnramified_universallyInjective_baseChange
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 05X9.** Let `f : X ⟶ Y` be a morphism of algebraic spaces over `S` whose source and
target are given over a third algebraic space `Z` by morphisms `p : X ⟶ Z` and `q : Y ⟶ Z` with
`f ≫ q = p`. If `p` is locally of finite type and closed and the morphism `X ×_Y X ⟶ Z` given by
the first projection followed by `p` is closed, then there is an open subspace `W` of `Z`
through which a morphism `Z' ⟶ Z` from an algebraic space factors exactly when the base change
of `f` along it is unramified and universally injective.

The open subspace is cut out, through the correspondence of Stacks 03BZ, by the point set of the
open subspace of Stacks 05X8 intersected with the complement of the image under `X ×_Y X ⟶ Z` of
the complement of the image of the relative diagonal of the base change of `f` over that open
subspace; that image is an open subspace of `X ×_Y X` because the relative diagonal of an
unramified morphism is an open immersion by part (1) of Stacks 05W1 and because `X ×_Z W₀` sits
inside `X ×_Y X` as a base change of `W₀`. Factoring through the intersection is, by Stacks 03IE,
the conjunction of factoring through the open subspace of Stacks 05X8 and of every point of
`X ×_Y X` over the image of `Z'` lying in the image of the diagonal, and the second condition is
universal injectivity of the base change.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_isOpenSubspace_iff_isUnramified_universallyInjective_baseChange
    (hX : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS X) (hY : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS Y)
    (hZ : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS Z) (f : X ⟶ Y) (p : X ⟶ Z) (q : Y ⟶ Z) (hfq : f ≫ q = p)
    (hp : IsLocallyOfFiniteType B S hS p) (hpc : IsClosedMorphism B S hS p)
    (hp₂ : IsClosedMorphism B S hS (pullback.fst f f ≫ p)) :
    ∃ W : Subfunctor Z, IsOpenSubspace B S hS W ∧
      ∀ (Z' : (BigFppfOver B S hS)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u) (_ : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS Z') (g : Z' ⟶ Z),
        (∃ r : Z' ⟶ W.toFunctor, r ≫ W.ι = g) ↔
          IsUnramified B S hS (baseChangeOverBase B S hS f p q hfq g) ∧
            UniversallyInjective B S hS (baseChangeOverBase B S hS f p q hfq g)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.exists_isOpenSubspace_iff_isClosedImmersion_baseChange
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 05XA.** Let `f : X ⟶ Y` be a morphism of algebraic spaces over `S` whose source and
target are given over a third algebraic space `Z` by morphisms `p : X ⟶ Z` and `q : Y ⟶ Z` with
`f ≫ q = p`. If `p` is locally of finite type and universally closed and `q` is separated, then
there is an open subspace `W` of `Z` through which a morphism `Z' ⟶ Z` from an algebraic space
factors exactly when the base change of `f` along it is a closed immersion.

The open subspace is the one of Stacks 05X9 for the same triangle, over which the base change
of `f` is unramified and universally injective: it is available because `p` is closed and
because `X ×_Y X ⟶ Z` is closed, being a base change of `f` followed by `p`. Every base change
of `f` is universally closed, since `f` is by part (1) of Stacks 04NX, so the three conditions
of Stacks 05W8 for the base change reduce to the two cut out by that subspace.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_isOpenSubspace_iff_isClosedImmersion_baseChange
    (hX : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS X) (hY : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS Y)
    (hZ : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS Z) (f : X ⟶ Y) (p : X ⟶ Z) (q : Y ⟶ Z) (hfq : f ≫ q = p)
    (hp : IsLocallyOfFiniteType B S hS p) (hpuc : UniversallyClosed B S hS p)
    (hq : IsSeparated B S hS q) :
    ∃ W : Subfunctor Z, IsOpenSubspace B S hS W ∧
      ∀ (Z' : (BigFppfOver B S hS)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u) (_ : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS Z') (g : Z' ⟶ Z),
        (∃ r : Z' ⟶ W.toFunctor, r ≫ W.ι = g) ↔
          IsClosedImmersion B S hS (baseChangeOverBase B S hS f p q hfq g)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.exists_isOpenSubspace_iff_isFlat_baseChange
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 05XB.**  Let `f : X ⟶ Y` be a morphism of algebraic
spaces over `S` whose source and target are given over a third algebraic space `Z` by morphisms
`p : X ⟶ Z` and `q : Y ⟶ Z` with `f ≫ q = p`.  If `p` is locally of finite presentation, flat
and closed and `q` is locally of finite type, then there is an open subspace `W` of `Z` through
which a morphism `Z' ⟶ Z` from an algebraic space factors exactly when the base change of `f`
along it is flat.

The open subspace is cut out, through the correspondence of Stacks 03BZ, by the complement of
the image under `p` of the set of points of `X` at which `f` is not flat, which is closed by the
openness half of Stacks 05X3 and whose image is closed because `p` is.  Factoring through it
is the containment of the image of the points of `Z'` in that complement by Stacks 03IE, and
flatness of the base change is flatness at each of its points by Stacks 03MM, which the
base-change half of Stacks 05X3 reads off from flatness of `f` over the image of `Z'`.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_isOpenSubspace_iff_isFlat_baseChange
    (hX : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS X) (hY : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS Y)
    (hZ : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS Z) (f : X ⟶ Y) (p : X ⟶ Z) (q : Y ⟶ Z) (hfq : f ≫ q = p)
    (hp : IsLocallyOfFinitePresentation B S hS p) (hpflat : IsFlat B S hS p)
    (hpc : IsClosedMorphism B S hS p) (hq : IsLocallyOfFiniteType B S hS q) :
    ∃ W : Subfunctor Z, IsOpenSubspace B S hS W ∧
      ∀ (Z' : (BigFppfOver B S hS)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u) (_ : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS Z') (g : Z' ⟶ Z),
        (∃ r : Z' ⟶ W.toFunctor, r ≫ W.ι = g) ↔
          IsFlat B S hS (baseChangeOverBase B S hS f p q hfq g)
declarations.comment: the open subspace of the base over which the morphism becomes flat

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.exists_isOpenSubspace_iff_isSurjective_isFlat_baseChange
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 05XC.**  Let `f : X ⟶ Y` be a morphism of algebraic
spaces over `S` whose source and target are given over a third algebraic space `Z` by morphisms
`p : X ⟶ Z` and `q : Y ⟶ Z` with `f ≫ q = p`.  If `p` is locally of finite presentation, flat
and closed and `q` is locally of finite type and closed, then there is an open subspace `W` of
`Z` through which a morphism `Z' ⟶ Z` from an algebraic space factors exactly when the base
change of `f` along it is surjective and flat.

The open subspace is cut out by the point set of the subspace `W₀` of Stacks 05XB intersected
with the locus of points of `Z` whose fibre in `|Y|` lies in the image of `X ×_Z W₀ ⟶ Y`.  That
locus is open because `q` is closed and because `X ×_Z W₀ ⟶ Y` is open on points, being the
base change of `f` over `W₀` — flat by the choice of `W₀` and locally of finite presentation,
hence universally open by Stacks 042S — followed by the open immersion `Y ×_Z W₀ ⟶ Y`.  Over
`W₀` its image coincides with the image of `f`, and containment of the image of `Z'` in the
locus is surjectivity of the base change.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_isOpenSubspace_iff_isSurjective_isFlat_baseChange
    (hX : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS X) (hY : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS Y)
    (hZ : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS Z) (f : X ⟶ Y) (p : X ⟶ Z) (q : Y ⟶ Z) (hfq : f ≫ q = p)
    (hp : IsLocallyOfFinitePresentation B S hS p) (hpflat : IsFlat B S hS p)
    (hpc : IsClosedMorphism B S hS p) (hq : IsLocallyOfFiniteType B S hS q)
    (hqc : IsClosedMorphism B S hS q) :
    ∃ W : Subfunctor Z, IsOpenSubspace B S hS W ∧
      ∀ (Z' : (BigFppfOver B S hS)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u) (_ : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS Z') (g : Z' ⟶ Z),
        (∃ r : Z' ⟶ W.toFunctor, r ≫ W.ι = g) ↔
          IsSurjective B S hS (baseChangeOverBase B S hS f p q hfq g) ∧
            IsFlat B S hS (baseChangeOverBase B S hS f p q hfq g)
declarations.comment: the open subspace of the base over which the morphism becomes surjective and flat

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.exists_isOpenSubspace_iff_isIso_baseChange
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 05XD.**  Let `f : X ⟶ Y` be a morphism of algebraic
spaces over `S` whose source and target are given over a third algebraic space `Z` by morphisms
`p : X ⟶ Z` and `q : Y ⟶ Z` with `f ≫ q = p`.  If `p` is locally of finite presentation, flat
and universally closed and `q` is locally of finite type, closed and separated, then there is an
open subspace `W` of `Z` through which a morphism `Z' ⟶ Z` from an algebraic space factors
exactly when the base change of `f` along it is an isomorphism.

The open subspace is the intersection, formed on point sets through the correspondence of
Stacks 03BZ, of the open subspace of Stacks 05XC over which the base change is surjective and
flat with that of Stacks 05XA over which it is a closed immersion.  A surjective flat closed
immersion is an isomorphism, and an isomorphism is surjective, flat and a closed immersion.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_isOpenSubspace_iff_isIso_baseChange
    (hX : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS X) (hY : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS Y)
    (hZ : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS Z) (f : X ⟶ Y) (p : X ⟶ Z) (q : Y ⟶ Z) (hfq : f ≫ q = p)
    (hp : IsLocallyOfFinitePresentation B S hS p) (hpflat : IsFlat B S hS p)
    (hpuc : UniversallyClosed B S hS p) (hq : IsLocallyOfFiniteType B S hS q)
    (hqc : IsClosedMorphism B S hS q) (hqsep : IsSeparated B S hS q) :
    ∃ W : Subfunctor Z, IsOpenSubspace B S hS W ∧
      ∀ (Z' : (BigFppfOver B S hS)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u) (_ : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS Z') (g : Z' ⟶ Z),
        (∃ r : Z' ⟶ W.toFunctor, r ≫ W.ι = g) ↔
          IsIso (baseChangeOverBase B S hS f p q hfq g)
declarations.comment: the open subspace of the base over which the morphism becomes an isomorphism

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.isRepresentableByAlgebraicSpaces_of_comp
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 05XK.** Let `f : 𝒳 ⟶ 𝒴` and `g : 𝒴 ⟶ 𝒵` be 1-morphisms of categories fibred in
groupoids over the big fppf site of `S`. If `f ≫ g` and `g` are representable by algebraic
spaces, then so is `f`.

This is cancellation of a representable postcomposition,
`AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.isRepresentableByAlgebraicSpaces_of_postcomp`, applied to the triangle
formed by `f`, `g` and `f ≫ g`, whose comparison 2-cell is the identity.
declarations.statement:
theorem isRepresentableByAlgebraicSpaces_of_comp
    (B : BigFppfSite.{u}) (S : Scheme.{u}) (hS : B.Contains S)
    {𝒳 𝒴 𝒵 : CatFiberedInGroupoids.{u, v, u + 1, w} (BigFppfOver B S hS)}
    (f : 𝒳 ⟶ 𝒴) (g : 𝒴 ⟶ 𝒵)
    (hfg : IsRepresentableByAlgebraicSpaces B S hS (f ≫ g).hom)
    (hg : IsRepresentableByAlgebraicSpaces B S hS g.hom) :
    IsRepresentableByAlgebraicSpaces B S hS f.hom
declarations.comment: representability

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.isEtale_algebraicSpaceMap_of_comp
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 05XK.** Let `f : 𝒳 ⟶ 𝒴` and `g : 𝒴 ⟶ 𝒵` be 1-morphisms of categories fibred in
groupoids over the big fppf site of `S`, with `f ≫ g` and `g` representable by algebraic spaces.
If every algebraic space representing a base change of `f ≫ g`, respectively of `g`, along a
scheme-valued point of `𝒵` has étale structural morphism, then so does every algebraic space
representing a base change of `f` along a scheme-valued point of `𝒴`.

Together with `AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.isRepresentableByAlgebraicSpaces_of_comp` this is the
statement that an intervening 1-morphism of a factorization through an étale representable
1-morphism is itself representable and étale, in the sense of Stacks 04XB at
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.IsEtale`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isEtale_algebraicSpaceMap_of_comp
    (B : BigFppfSite.{u}) (S : Scheme.{u}) (hS : B.Contains S)
    {𝒳 𝒴 𝒵 : CatFiberedInGroupoids.{u, v, u + 1, w} (BigFppfOver B S hS)}
    (f : 𝒳 ⟶ 𝒴) (g : 𝒴 ⟶ 𝒵)
    (hfg : IsRepresentableByAlgebraicSpaces B S hS (f ≫ g).hom)
    (hg : IsRepresentableByAlgebraicSpaces B S hS g.hom)
    (hEfg : ∀ (U : BigFppfOver B S hS)
      (z : BigFppfOver B U.left.1 U.left.2 ⥤ 𝒵.val.obj)
      (_hz : z ⋙ 𝒵.val.p = Over.map U.hom)
      (F : (BigFppfOver B U.left.1 U.left.2)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u)
      (hF : IsAlgebraicSpace B U.left.1 U.left.2 F),
      Nonempty (StacksRepresentableCFG.EquivalenceOver
        (TwoFibreProductOver.fst (Over.map U.hom) 𝒳.val.p 𝒵.val.p z
          (CatFiberedInGroupoids.homFunctor (f ≫ g)))
        (presheafOfCategories (F ⋙ typeToCat)).p) →
      Space.IsEtale B S hS (algebraicSpaceMap B S hS U
        ((spacesOverSmallerBaseFunctor B U.left.1 S U.left.2 hS U.hom).obj ⟨F, hF⟩)).hom)
    (hEg : ∀ (U : BigFppfOver B S hS)
      (z : BigFppfOver B U.left.1 U.left.2 ⥤ 𝒵.val.obj)
      (_hz : z ⋙ 𝒵.val.p = Over.map U.hom)
      (F : (BigFppfOver B U.left.1 U.left.2)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u)
      (hF : IsAlgebraicSpace B U.left.1 U.left.2 F),
      Nonempty (StacksRepresentableCFG.EquivalenceOver
        (TwoFibreProductOver.fst (Over.map U.hom) 𝒴.val.p 𝒵.val.p z
          (CatFiberedInGroupoids.homFunctor g))
        (presheafOfCategories (F ⋙ typeToCat)).p) →
      Space.IsEtale B S hS (algebraicSpaceMap B S hS U
        ((spacesOverSmallerBaseFunctor B U.left.1 S U.left.2 hS U.hom).obj ⟨F, hF⟩)).hom) :
    ∀ (U : BigFppfOver B S hS)
      (y : BigFppfOver B U.left.1 U.left.2 ⥤ 𝒴.val.obj)
      (_hy : y ⋙ 𝒴.val.p = Over.map U.hom)
      (F : (BigFppfOver B U.left.1 U.left.2)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u)
      (hF : IsAlgebraicSpace B U.left.1 U.left.2 F),
      Nonempty (StacksRepresentableCFG.EquivalenceOver
        (TwoFibreProductOver.fst (Over.map U.hom) 𝒳.val.p 𝒴.val.p y
          (CatFiberedInGroupoids.homFunctor f))
        (presheafOfCategories (F ⋙ typeToCat)).p) →
      Space.IsEtale B S hS (algebraicSpaceMap B S hS U
        ((spacesOverSmallerBaseFunctor B U.left.1 S U.left.2 hS U.hom).obj ⟨F, hF⟩)).hom
declarations.comment: étaleness

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.isStackInSetoids_of_fppf_baseChange
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 05XL.** Let `𝒳 ⟶ 𝒵` and `𝒴 ⟶ 𝒵` be 1-morphisms of categories fibred in groupoids over
the big fppf site of `S`, with `𝒳` a stack. If `𝒴` and `𝒵` are represented by algebraic spaces `Y`
and `Z` over `S` through chosen equivalences over the site, the morphism `a : Y ⟶ Z` these
equivalences associate to `𝒴 ⟶ 𝒵` is surjective, flat and locally of finite presentation, and the
2-fibre product `𝒴 ×_𝒵 𝒳` is a stack in setoids, then `𝒳` is a stack in setoids.
declarations.statement:
theorem isStackInSetoids_of_fppf_baseChange
    {𝒳 𝒴 𝒵 : CatFiberedInGroupoids.{u, u, u + 1, w} (BigFppfOver B S hS)}
    (f : 𝒳 ⟶ 𝒵) (g : 𝒴 ⟶ 𝒵)
    (h𝒳 : 𝒳.val.p.IsStack (BigFppfOver.topology B S hS))
    (Y Z : (BigFppfOver B S hS)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u)
    (hY : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS Y) (hZ : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS Z)
    (eY : StacksRepresentableCFG.EquivalenceOver 𝒴.val.p
      (presheafOfCategories (Y ⋙ typeToCat)).p)
    (eZ : StacksRepresentableCFG.EquivalenceOver 𝒵.val.p
      (presheafOfCategories (Z ⋙ typeToCat)).p)
    (a : Y ⟶ Z)
    (ha : ∀ y : 𝒴.val.obj,
      a.app (op (𝒴.val.p.obj y)) (PresheafOfCategories.sectionOfObj eY y rfl) =
        PresheafOfCategories.sectionOfObj eZ ((CatFiberedInGroupoids.homFunctor g).obj y)
          (Functor.congr_obj (CatFiberedInGroupoids.homFunctor_comp_p g) y))
    (hsurj : Space.IsSurjective B S hS a) (hflat : Space.IsFlat B S hS a)
    (hlfp : Space.IsLocallyOfFinitePresentation B S hS a)
    (hP : (TwoFibreProductOver.structureFunctor 𝒴.val.p 𝒳.val.p 𝒵.val.p
        (CatFiberedInGroupoids.homFunctor g) (CatFiberedInGroupoids.homFunctor f)).IsStackInSetoids
      (BigFppfOver.topology B S hS)) :
    𝒳.val.p.IsStackInSetoids (BigFppfOver.topology B S hS)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.mapAbsolute
declarations.doc:
The 1-morphism `ℋ_d(𝒳') ⟶ ℋ_d(𝒳)` of absolute degree-`d` finite Hilbert stacks induced by a
1-morphism `G : 𝒳' ⟶ 𝒳` of stacks in groupoids: the canonical 1-morphism of finite Hilbert
stacks for the 2-commutative square whose two columns are the structure morphisms of `𝒳'` and
`𝒳`.
declarations.comment: the induced 1-morphism of absolute finite Hilbert stacks

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.mapAbsolute_comp_forgetAbsoluteStructure
declarations.doc:
The induced 1-morphism of absolute finite Hilbert stacks leaves the underlying degree-`d`
finite locally free cover unchanged.
declarations.statement:
theorem mapAbsolute_comp_forgetAbsoluteStructure :
    BasedFunctor.comp (mapAbsolute B S hS d 𝒳' 𝒳 G)
        (forgetAbsoluteStructure (B := B) (S := S) (hS := hS) (d := d) (𝒳 := 𝒳)) =
      forgetAbsoluteStructure (B := B) (S := S) (hS := hS) (d := d) (𝒳 := 𝒳')
declarations.comment: compatibility with the forgetful 1-morphism `ℋ_d(𝒳) ⟶ ℋ_d`

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.mapRelative
declarations.doc:
The canonical 1-morphism `ℋ_d(𝒳'/𝒴') ⟶ ℋ_d(𝒳/𝒴)` of degree-`d` finite Hilbert stacks
attached to a 2-commutative square of stacks in groupoids with horizontal arrows `G` and `H`,
vertical arrows `F'` and `F`, and 2-isomorphism `γ : H ∘ F' ⟶ F ∘ G`.
declarations.comment: the canonical 1-morphism

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.mapRelative_obj_α
declarations.doc:
The canonical 1-morphism sends an object with identification `α` to one whose identification
is `α` transported across the given 2-isomorphism.
declarations.statement:
theorem mapRelative_obj_α (P : FiniteHilbert.Object B S hS 𝒳' 𝒴' F' d) :
    ((mapRelative B S hS d 𝒳' 𝒴' 𝒳 𝒴 F' F G H γ).obj P).α =
      squareComparison γ P.x ≫ H.map P.α
declarations.comment: action on the identification

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.mapRelative_comp_forgetRelativeStructure
declarations.doc:
The canonical 1-morphism is compatible with the forgetful 1-morphisms to the absolute finite
Hilbert stacks: on them it induces the 1-morphism attached to `G`.
declarations.statement:
theorem mapRelative_comp_forgetRelativeStructure :
    BasedFunctor.comp (mapRelative B S hS d 𝒳' 𝒴' 𝒳 𝒴 F' F G H γ)
        (forgetRelativeStructure (B := B) (S := S) (hS := hS) (d := d) (𝒳 := 𝒳) (𝒴 := 𝒴)
          (F := F)) =
      BasedFunctor.comp
        (forgetRelativeStructure (B := B) (S := S) (hS := hS) (d := d) (𝒳 := 𝒳') (𝒴 := 𝒴')
          (F := F'))
        (mapAbsolute B S hS d 𝒳' 𝒳 G)
declarations.comment: compatibility with the forgetful 1-morphism `ℋ_d(𝒳/𝒴) ⟶ ℋ_d(𝒳)`

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.mapRelative_comp_forgetTarget
declarations.doc:
The canonical 1-morphism is compatible with the forgetful 1-morphisms to the target stacks: on
them it induces `H`.
declarations.statement:
theorem mapRelative_comp_forgetTarget :
    BasedFunctor.comp (mapRelative B S hS d 𝒳' 𝒴' 𝒳 𝒴 F' F G H γ)
        (forgetTarget (B := B) (S := S) (hS := hS) (d := d) (𝒳 := 𝒳) (𝒴 := 𝒴) (F := F)) =
      BasedFunctor.comp
        (forgetTarget (B := B) (S := S) (hS := hS) (d := d) (𝒳 := 𝒳') (𝒴 := 𝒴') (F := F')) H
declarations.comment: compatibility with the forgetful 1-morphism `ℋ_d(𝒳/𝒴) ⟶ 𝒴`

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.mapRelative_comp_forgetRelativeToFiniteCover
declarations.doc:
The canonical 1-morphism leaves the underlying degree-`d` finite locally free cover
unchanged.
declarations.statement:
theorem mapRelative_comp_forgetRelativeToFiniteCover :
    BasedFunctor.comp (mapRelative B S hS d 𝒳' 𝒴' 𝒳 𝒴 F' F G H γ)
        (forgetRelativeToFiniteCover (B := B) (S := S) (hS := hS) (d := d) (𝒳 := 𝒳) (𝒴 := 𝒴)
          (F := F)) =
      forgetRelativeToFiniteCover (B := B) (S := S) (hS := hS) (d := d) (𝒳 := 𝒳') (𝒴 := 𝒴')
        (F := F')
declarations.comment: compatibility with the forgetful 1-morphism `ℋ_d(𝒳/𝒴) ⟶ ℋ_d`

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.isEquivalence_hilbertComparison
declarations.doc:
If the comparison functor of the given square is an equivalence, then so is the comparison
functor `ℋ_d(𝒳'/𝒴') ⥤ ℋ_d(𝒳/𝒴) ×_𝒴 𝒴'` of the induced square.
declarations.statement:
theorem isEquivalence_hilbertComparison
    (h : (sourceComparison B S hS 𝒳' 𝒴' 𝒳 𝒴 F' F G H γ).IsEquivalence) :
    (hilbertComparison B S hS d 𝒳' 𝒴' 𝒳 𝒴 F' F G H γ).IsEquivalence
declarations.comment: the comparison functor is an equivalence

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.isTwoFibreProduct_hilbertSquare
declarations.doc:
If the given 2-commutative square of stacks in groupoids is 2-cartesian, then so is the
induced square of degree-`d` finite Hilbert stacks: the canonical 1-morphism
`ℋ_d(𝒳'/𝒴') ⟶ ℋ_d(𝒳/𝒴)` and the forgetful 1-morphism `ℋ_d(𝒳'/𝒴') ⟶ 𝒴'` exhibit `ℋ_d(𝒳'/𝒴')`
as the 2-fibre product `𝒴' ×_𝒴 ℋ_d(𝒳/𝒴)`.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def isTwoFibreProduct_hilbertSquare
    (hcart : Bicategory.IsTwoFibreProduct (sourceSquare B S hS 𝒳' 𝒴' 𝒳 𝒴 F' F G H γ)) :
    Bicategory.IsTwoFibreProduct (hilbertSquare B S hS d 𝒳' 𝒴' 𝒳 𝒴 F' F G H γ)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isSurjective_restrictionOfScalars_projection_of_isPullback
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 05XQ for the fibre data of Stacks 05YD.**  Let `z : Z ⟶ Q` be a finite locally free
morphism of algebraic spaces over `S`, let `U` be an object of the big fppf category over `S`,
let `Z_U` be an algebraic space exhibited as a base change `U ×_{a, Q} Z` of `z`, and let
`w : W ⟶ Z_U` be surjective and étale.  Then the restriction of scalars `Res_{Z_U/U}(W) ⟶ U` is
surjective.

Stacks 05XQ is formalized at a morphism of the site whose underlying morphism of schemes is finite,
as `AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isSurjective_restrictionOfScalars_projection`.  Here `Z_U` is only
*isomorphic* to a representable presheaf: `z` is affine, hence representable, so the chosen
represented base change `ψ : Z' ⟶ U` of `z` along `a` identifies `Z_U` with `yoneda.obj Z'`, and
`ψ` is finite as a morphism of schemes by
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isFinite_of_isPullback_of_isFiniteLocallyFree`.  Transporting the
section produced over `Z'` back along that identification gives a pair of Stacks 05Y9 over a
surjective base change of `U`, which is what surjectivity of the projection asks for.
declarations.statement:
theorem isSurjective_restrictionOfScalars_projection_of_isPullback
    {Z Q : AlgebraicSpaces B S hS} (z : Z ⟶ Q) (hz : IsFiniteLocallyFree B S hS z)
    (U : BigFppfOver B S hS) (ZU W : AlgebraicSpaces B S hS)
    (ζ : ZU ⟶ (⟨yoneda.obj U, isAlgebraicSpace_yoneda B S hS U⟩ : AlgebraicSpaces B S hS))
    (w : W ⟶ ZU) (a : yoneda.obj U ⟶ Q.obj) (ι : ZU.obj ⟶ Z.obj)
    (sq : IsPullback ζ.hom ι a z.hom)
    (hw_surjective : IsSurjective B S hS w.hom) (hw_etale : IsEtale B S hS w.hom) :
    IsSurjective B S hS (restrictionOfScalars B S hS w ζ).projection
declarations.comment: surjectivity of `Res_{Z_U/U}(W) ⟶ U` for `Z_U` a base change of a finite locally free morphism of algebraic spaces

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.exists_surjective_etale_sectionsOver
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 05XQ.** Let `Z → U` be a finite morphism of schemes, let `W` be an algebraic space
over `U` and let `w : W → Z` be surjective and étale. Then there is a surjective étale morphism
`T → U` together with a section of `W_T → Z_T`.
declarations.statement:
theorem Space.exists_surjective_etale_sectionsOver (B : BigFppfSite.{u}) (U : Scheme.{u})
    (hU : B.Contains U) (Z : BigFppfOver B U hU) [IsFinite (B.inclusion.map Z.hom)]
    (W : (BigFppfOver B U hU)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u) (w : W ⟶ yoneda.obj Z)
    (hW : IsAlgebraicSpace B U hU W) (hw_surjective : Space.IsSurjective B U hU w)
    (hw_etale : Space.IsEtale B U hU w) :
    ∃ T : BigFppfOver B U hU, Surjective (B.inclusion.map T.hom) ∧
      Etale (B.inclusion.map T.hom) ∧ Nonempty (Space.SectionsOver B U hU Z T W w)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isSurjective_restrictionOfScalars_projection
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 05XQ.** Let `ζ : Z ⟶ U` be a morphism of the big fppf site of `S` whose underlying
morphism of schemes is finite, let `W` be an algebraic space over `S` and let `w : W ⟶ Z` be
surjective and étale. Then the restriction of scalars `Res_{Z/U}(W) ⟶ U` of Stacks 05YA — the
functor assigning to `T` a morphism `T ⟶ U` together with a section of `W_T ⟶ Z_T` — is
surjective.

A point of `U` is hit by a point of `Res_{Z/U}(W)` because the base change `τ : T ⟶ U` of
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.exists_surjective_etale_section_of_isFinite` carries a section, so
`h_T ⟶ U` factors through `Res_{Z/U}(W)`, and `τ` is surjective on points.
declarations.statement:
theorem Space.isSurjective_restrictionOfScalars_projection (B : BigFppfSite.{u})
    (S : Scheme.{u}) (hS : B.Contains S) {U Z : BigFppfOver B S hS} (ζ : Z ⟶ U)
    [IsFinite ((BigFppfOver.toScheme B S hS).map ζ)] (W : AlgebraicSpaces B S hS)
    (w : W ⟶ (schemeSpace Z : AlgebraicSpaces B S hS))
    (hw_surjective : Space.IsSurjective B S hS w.hom)
    (hw_etale : Space.IsEtale B S hS w.hom) :
    Space.IsSurjective B S hS
      (Space.restrictionOfScalars B S hS w
        (ObjectProperty.homMk (yoneda.map ζ) :
          (schemeSpace Z : AlgebraicSpaces B S hS) ⟶
            schemeSpace U)).projection
declarations.comment: surjectivity of `Res_{Z/U}(W) ⟶ U` for `Z ⟶ U` finite

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.exists_surjective_etale_sectionOverBase
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 05XQ over a base object of the site.** Let `ζ : Z ⟶ U` be a morphism of the big
fppf site of `S` whose underlying morphism of schemes is finite, let `W` be an algebraic space
over `S` and let `w : W ⟶ h_Z` be surjective and étale. Then there is an object `T` of the big
fppf site of `S` and a morphism `r : T ⟶ U`, surjective and étale on underlying schemes,
together with a section of `W ⟶ h_Z` over `T ×_U Z`, that is a morphism `h_{T ×_U Z} ⟶ W`
whose composite with `w` is the projection to `h_Z`.
declarations.statement:
theorem Space.exists_surjective_etale_sectionOverBase (B : BigFppfSite.{u}) (S : Scheme.{u})
    (hS : B.Contains S) (U Z : BigFppfOver B S hS) (ζ : Z ⟶ U)
    (hζ : IsFinite ((BigFppfOver.toScheme B S hS).map ζ))
    (W : (BigFppfOver B S hS)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u) (w : W ⟶ yoneda.obj Z)
    (hW : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS W) (hw_surjective : Space.IsSurjective B S hS w)
    (hw_etale : Space.IsEtale B S hS w) :
    ∃ (T : BigFppfOver B S hS) (r : T ⟶ U),
      Surjective ((BigFppfOver.toScheme B S hS).map r) ∧
      Etale ((BigFppfOver.toScheme B S hS).map r) ∧
      ∃ σ : pullback (yoneda.map r) (yoneda.map ζ) ⟶ W,
        σ ≫ w = pullback.snd (yoneda.map r) (yoneda.map ζ)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isAlgebraicSpace_isEtale_restrictionOfScalars_of_isPullback
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 05XR for the fibre data of Stacks 05YD and Stacks 05Y5.** Let `z : Z ⟶ Q` be a
finite locally free morphism of algebraic spaces over `S`, let `U` be an object of the big fppf
category over `S`, let `Z_U` be an algebraic space exhibited as a base change `U ×_{a, Q} Z` of
`z` and let `w : W ⟶ Z_U` be an étale morphism of algebraic spaces over `S`. Then the restriction
of scalars `Res_{Z_U/U}(W)` is an algebraic space over `S` and its projection to `U` is étale.
declarations.statement:
theorem isAlgebraicSpace_isEtale_restrictionOfScalars_of_isPullback
    {Z Q : AlgebraicSpaces B S hS} (z : Z ⟶ Q) (hz : IsFiniteLocallyFree B S hS z)
    (U : BigFppfOver B S hS) (ZU W : AlgebraicSpaces B S hS)
    (ζ : ZU ⟶ (schemeSpace U : AlgebraicSpaces B S hS))
    (w : W ⟶ ZU) (a : yoneda.obj U ⟶ Q.obj) (ι : ZU.obj ⟶ Z.obj)
    (sq : IsPullback ζ.hom ι a z.hom) (hw : IsEtale B S hS w.hom) :
    IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS (restrictionOfScalars B S hS w ζ).presheaf ∧
      IsEtale B S hS (restrictionOfScalars B S hS w ζ).projection
declarations.comment: the restriction of scalars of a base change of a finite locally free morphism along an étale morphism is an algebraic space étale over the base

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isAlgebraicSpace_restrictionOfScalars
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 05XR, the algebraic space.** The restriction of scalars `Res_{Z/Q}(X)` of an étale
`x : X ⟶ Z` along a finite `z : Z ⟶ Q` is an algebraic space over `S`.

The source states this for `z` finite locally free and for `Q` an object of the site; finiteness
of `z` is all that is used, and `Q` is an arbitrary algebraic space over `S`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isAlgebraicSpace_restrictionOfScalars (hx : IsEtale B S hS x.hom)
    (hz : IsFinite B S hS z.hom) :
    IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS (restrictionOfScalars B S hS x z).presheaf
declarations.comment: algebraic space

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isEtale_projection_restrictionOfScalars
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 05XR, the étale morphism.** The projection `Res_{Z/Q}(X) ⟶ Q` of the restriction of
scalars of an étale `x : X ⟶ Z` along a finite `z : Z ⟶ Q` is étale.

The source states this for `z` finite locally free and for `Q` an object of the site; finiteness
of `z` is all that is used, and `Q` is an arbitrary algebraic space over `S`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isEtale_projection_restrictionOfScalars (hx : IsEtale B S hS x.hom)
    (hz : IsFinite B S hS z.hom) :
    IsEtale B S hS (restrictionOfScalars B S hS x z).projection
declarations.comment: étale morphism

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.exists_sectionSpace
declarations.doc:
The natural, small-valued functor of sections of `W → Z` of Stacks 05XR exists: there
is a presheaf on the big fppf site of `U` whose value at `T` is the set of sections of
`W_T → Z_T`, naturally in `T`, the restriction maps being base change. Stacks 05XR itself is
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isAlgebraicSpace_sectionSpace_and_isEtale`.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_sectionSpace (Z : BigFppfOver B U hU)
    (W : (BigFppfOver B U hU)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u) (w : W ⟶ yoneda.obj Z) :
    ∃ F : (BigFppfOver B U hU)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u,
      ∃ e : ∀ T : BigFppfOver B U hU, F.obj (Opposite.op T) ≃
          SectionsOver B U hU Z T W w,
        ∀ (T T' : BigFppfOver B U hU) (f : T' ⟶ T)
          (s : F.obj (Opposite.op T)),
          ((e T') (F.map f.op s)).1 =
            prod.map (yoneda.map f) (𝟙 (yoneda.obj Z)) ≫ ((e T) s).1
declarations.comment: the functor

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isAlgebraicSpace_sectionSpace_of_isEtale
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 05XR, the algebraicity of the space of sections, in general.** Let `Z ⟶ U` be a
morphism of the big fppf site of `U` whose underlying morphism of schemes is finite, and let
`w : W ⟶ h_Z` be an étale morphism of presheaves with `W` an algebraic space over `U`. Then the
space of sections of `W_T ⟶ Z_T` is an algebraic space over `U`.

No separatedness is assumed: a surjective étale chart of `W` whose scheme is separated exists by
Stacks 03FX, and along such a chart the comparison of the spaces of sections is surjective and
étale by `AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isEtale_and_isSurjective_of_isPullback_sectionSpaceMap`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isAlgebraicSpace_sectionSpace_of_isEtale (hW : IsAlgebraicSpace B U hU W)
    (hw : IsEtale B U hU w)
    (hZfin : _root_.AlgebraicGeometry.IsFinite (B.inclusion.map Z.hom)) :
    IsAlgebraicSpace B U hU (sectionSpace B U hU Z W w)
declarations.comment: the space of sections is an algebraic space, with no separatedness

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isEtale_sectionSpace_of_isEtale
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 05XR, the étaleness of the space of sections over the base, in general.** Under the
hypotheses of `AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isAlgebraicSpace_sectionSpace_of_isEtale` the structure
morphism of the space of sections to `U` is étale.
declarations.statement:
theorem isEtale_sectionSpace_of_isEtale (hW : IsAlgebraicSpace B U hU W)
    (hw : IsEtale B U hU w)
    (hZfin : _root_.AlgebraicGeometry.IsFinite (B.inclusion.map Z.hom)) :
    IsEtale B U hU (terminal.from (sectionSpace B U hU Z W w))
declarations.comment: the space of sections is étale over the base, with no separatedness

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isAlgebraicSpace_sectionSpace_and_isEtale
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 05XR.** Let `Z ⟶ U` be a finite morphism of schemes, let `W` be an algebraic space
over `U` and let `w : W ⟶ Z` be étale. Then the functor of sections of `W_T ⟶ Z_T` over `T/U` is an
algebraic space, and its structure morphism to `U` is étale.

The source asks `Z ⟶ U` to be finite locally free; only finiteness is used.
declarations.statement:
theorem isAlgebraicSpace_sectionSpace_and_isEtale (hW : IsAlgebraicSpace B U hU W)
    (hw : IsEtale B U hU w) (hZfin : _root_.AlgebraicGeometry.IsFinite (B.inclusion.map Z.hom)) :
    IsAlgebraicSpace B U hU (sectionSpace B U hU Z W w) ∧
      IsEtale B U hU (terminal.from (sectionSpace B U hU Z W w))

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.isRelativelyEtale_mapRelativeFibered
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 05XS, part (1).** Let `G : 𝒳' ⟶ 𝒳` and `H : 𝒴' ⟶ 𝒴` be 1-morphisms of stacks in
groupoids over the big fppf site of `S` which are representable by algebraic spaces and étale,
and let `γ : H ∘ F' ⟶ F ∘ G` make the square with vertical arrows `F'`, `F` 2-commute. Then the
canonical 1-morphism `ℋ_d(𝒳'/𝒴') ⟶ ℋ_d(𝒳/𝒴)` of Stacks 05XN is representable by algebraic
spaces and étale.

The proof is the source's. The 1-morphism is 2-isomorphic to the composite of
`ℋ_d(𝒳'/𝒴') ⟶ ℋ_d((𝒳 ×_𝒴 𝒴')/𝒴')`, which is representable by algebraic spaces and étale by
Stacks 05YG because `𝒳' ⟶ 𝒳 ×_𝒴 𝒴'` is by Stacks 05XK, with
`ℋ_d((𝒳 ×_𝒴 𝒴')/𝒴') ⟶ ℋ_d(𝒳/𝒴)`, which is a base change of `H` by Stacks 05XP and therefore
representable by algebraic spaces and étale by Stacks 045C.
declarations.statement:
theorem isRelativelyEtale_mapRelativeFibered
    (γ : BasedFunctor.comp F' H ≅ BasedFunctor.comp G F)
    (hG : IsRelativelyEtale B S hS (stackMapFibered B S hS G))
    (hH : IsRelativelyEtale B S hS (stackMapFibered B S hS H)) :
    IsRelativelyEtale B S hS (mapRelativeFibered B S hS d 𝒳 𝒴 F 𝒳' 𝒴' F' G H γ)
declarations.comment: part (1)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.isSurjectiveOnObjects_mapRelativeFibered
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 05XS, part (2).** Let `G : 𝒳' ⟶ 𝒳` and `H : 𝒴' ⟶ 𝒴` be 1-morphisms of stacks in
groupoids over the big fppf site of `S` which are representable by algebraic spaces and étale,
and let `γ : H ∘ F' ⟶ F ∘ G` make the square with vertical arrows `F'`, `F` 2-commute. If
moreover `H` is surjective and the induced 1-morphism `𝒳' ⟶ 𝒳 ×_𝒴 𝒴'` to the 2-fibre product is
surjective, then the canonical 1-morphism `ℋ_d(𝒳'/𝒴') ⟶ ℋ_d(𝒳/𝒴)` of Stacks 05XN is surjective.

The induced 1-morphism is `AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.targetFibreProductComparison`, into the
2-fibre product over the site of Stacks 0040, which the source writes `𝒴' ×_𝒴 𝒳`. The proof is
the source's: `ℋ_d(𝒳'/𝒴') ⟶ ℋ_d((𝒳 ×_𝒴 𝒴')/𝒴')` is surjective by Stacks 05YG, the base change
`ℋ_d((𝒳 ×_𝒴 𝒴')/𝒴') ⟶ ℋ_d(𝒳/𝒴)` of `H` is surjective as `H` is, and composites of surjective
1-morphisms are surjective.
declarations.statement:
theorem isSurjectiveOnObjects_mapRelativeFibered
    (γ : BasedFunctor.comp F' H ≅ BasedFunctor.comp G F)
    (hG : IsRelativelyEtale B S hS (stackMapFibered B S hS G))
    (hH : IsRelativelyEtale B S hS (stackMapFibered B S hS H))
    (hHSurj : IsSurjectiveOnObjects B S hS (stackFibered B S hS 𝒴').val.p
      (stackFibered B S hS 𝒴).val.p
      (CatFiberedInGroupoids.homFunctor (stackMapFibered B S hS H)))
    (hcomparison : IsSurjectiveOnObjects B S hS (stackFibered B S hS 𝒳').val.p
      (stackFibered B S hS (targetFibreProduct B S hS 𝒳 𝒴 F 𝒴' H)).val.p
      (CatFiberedInGroupoids.homFunctor (stackMapFibered B S hS
        (targetFibreProductComparison B S hS 𝒳 𝒴 F 𝒳' 𝒴' F' G H γ)))) :
    IsSurjectiveOnObjects B S hS (finiteHilbertFibered B S hS d 𝒳' 𝒴' F').val.p
      (finiteHilbertFibered B S hS d 𝒳 𝒴 F).val.p
      (CatFiberedInGroupoids.homFunctor
        (mapRelativeFibered B S hS d 𝒳 𝒴 F 𝒳' 𝒴' F' G H γ))
declarations.comment: part (2)

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.exists_finCategory_functor_of_finitelyGeneratedShape
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Tag 05XU.**  Let `I` be a small category whose objects form a finite type
and whose morphisms are generated, by composition, from a finite list of arrows.
Then there exist a finite category `J` and a functor `F : J ⥤ I` such that:

* (a) `J` is a finite category (witnessed by the `FinCategory J` instance);
* (b) for every category `C` and every diagram `M : I ⥤ C`:
    - `HasLimit M ↔ HasLimit (F ⋙ M)` and `HasColimit M ↔ HasColimit (F ⋙ M)`
      (existence equivalences), and
    - whenever both limits exist, the *canonical comparison morphism*
      `limit.pre M F : limit M ⟶ limit (F ⋙ M)` is an isomorphism; dually, whenever
      both colimits exist, `colimit.pre M F : colimit (F ⋙ M) ⟶ colimit M` is an
      isomorphism.  Since these comparison morphisms are, by construction,
      compatible with the projections / injections through `F`
      (`limit.pre_π`, `colimit.ι_pre`), this is precisely the statement that `M` and
      `F ⋙ M` have canonically isomorphic (co)limits via the comparison induced by
      `F`;
* (c) `J` is connected iff `I` is connected; and
* (d) `J` is nonempty iff `I` is nonempty.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_finCategory_functor_of_finitelyGeneratedShape {I : Type u} [SmallCategory I]
    (hI : FinitelyGeneratedShape I) :
    ∃ (J : Type u) (_ : SmallCategory J) (_ : FinCategory J) (F : J ⥤ I),
      -- (b) existence equivalences for limits and colimits, for every diagram
      (∀ {C : Type u'} [Category.{v'} C] (M : I ⥤ C),
        (HasLimit M ↔ HasLimit (F ⋙ M)) ∧
        (HasColimit M ↔ HasColimit (F ⋙ M))) ∧
      -- (b) the canonical comparison morphism on limits is an isomorphism
      (∀ {C : Type u'} [Category.{v'} C] (M : I ⥤ C) [HasLimit M] [HasLimit (F ⋙ M)],
        IsIso (limit.pre M F)) ∧
      -- (b) the canonical comparison morphism on colimits is an isomorphism
      (∀ {C : Type u'} [Category.{v'} C] (M : I ⥤ C) [HasColimit M] [HasColimit (F ⋙ M)],
        IsIso (colimit.pre M F)) ∧
      -- (c) connectedness is preserved
      (IsConnected J ↔ IsConnected I) ∧
      -- (d) nonemptiness is preserved
      (Nonempty J ↔ Nonempty I)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.forgetRelativeStructure_faithful
declarations.doc:
For a positive degree `d`, the 1-morphism `ℋ_d(𝒳/𝒴) ⟶ ℋ_d(𝒳)` from the relative to the
absolute finite Hilbert category is faithful.
declarations.statement:
theorem forgetRelativeStructure_faithful (hd : 0 < d) :
    (forgetRelativeStructure (B := B) (S := S) (hS := hS)
      (d := d) (𝒳 := 𝒳) (𝒴 := 𝒴) (F := F)).toFunctor.Faithful

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.hasRepresentableDiagonal_of_flatPresentation
declarations.doc:
Let `u : 𝒰 ⟶ 𝒳` be a 1-morphism of categories fibred in groupoids over the
big fppf site of `S` with `𝒳` a stack, `𝒰` representable by an algebraic space and `u`
representable by algebraic spaces, surjective, flat and locally of finite presentation. Then
the diagonal of `𝒳` is representable by algebraic spaces.
declarations.statement:
theorem hasRepresentableDiagonal_of_flatPresentation (u : 𝒰 ⟶ 𝒳)
    (h𝒳 : 𝒳.val.p.IsStack (BigFppfOver.topology B S hS))
    (h𝒰 : IsRepresentableByAlgebraicSpace B S hS 𝒰)
    (hu : IsRepresentableByAlgebraicSpaces B S hS u.hom)
    (hsurj : HasRelativeProperty B S hS (Space.surjectiveMorphismProperty B S hS) u hu)
    (hflat : @HasRelativeProperty.{u, u, u + 1, u + 1} B S hS
      (fun ⦃X Y : AlgebraicSpaces B S hS⦄ (k : X ⟶ Y) => Space.IsFlat B S hS k.hom)
      (Space.isFlat_isStableUnderBaseChange B S hS)
      ((Space.isFlat_isLocalAtTarget_fpqc B S hS).of_le
        (Space.fppfPrecoverage_le_fpqcPrecoverage B S hS))
      𝒰 𝒳 u hu)
    (hlfp : HasRelativeProperty B S hS
      (fun ⦃X Y : AlgebraicSpaces B S hS⦄ (k : X ⟶ Y) =>
        Space.IsLocallyOfFinitePresentation B S hS k.hom) u hu) :
    HasRepresentableDiagonal B S hS 𝒳

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.isAlgebraicStack_of_isAlgebraicMorphism
declarations.doc:
Let `F : 𝒳 ⟶ 𝒴` be a 1-morphism of stacks in groupoids over the big fppf site of `S`. If `𝒴`
is an algebraic stack and `F` is algebraic in the sense of Stacks 06CF, then `𝒳` is an algebraic
stack.
declarations.statement:
theorem isAlgebraicStack_of_isAlgebraicMorphism
    (B : BigFppfSite.{u}) (S : Scheme.{u}) (hS : B.Contains S)
    {𝒳 𝒴 : StackInGroupoids.{w, u, u, u + 1, u + 1}
      (BigFppfOver B S hS) (BigFppfOver.topology B S hS)}
    (f : 𝒳 ⟶ 𝒴)
    (h𝒳 : 𝒳.toBasedCategory.p.IsStack (BigFppfOver.topology B S hS))
    (h𝒴 : IsAlgebraicStack.{u, w} B S hS 𝒴.toBasedCategory)
    (hf : IsAlgebraicMorphism.{u, w, w, w} B S hS (𝒳 := 𝒳) (𝒴 := 𝒴) f.hom) :
    IsAlgebraicStack.{u, w} B S hS 𝒳.toBasedCategory

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.RelativeMorphism
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 05Y1.** A pair `(a, b)` for the relative morphism functor of `z : Z ⟶ Q` and
`x : X ⟶ Q` at a test presheaf `T`: a morphism `a : T ⟶ Q` together with a morphism
`b : T ×_{a, Q} Z ⟶ X` lying over `Q`. The source's other description of `b`, as a morphism
`T ×_{a, Q} Z ⟶ T ×_{a, Q} X` over `T`, is equivalent to this one.
declarations.statement:
structure RelativeMorphism (Z X Q : (BigFppfOver B S hS)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u) (z : Z ⟶ Q) (x : X ⟶ Q)
    (T : (BigFppfOver B S hS)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u)
declarations.comment: the pair `(a, b)` of the diagram

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.RelativeMorphismDiagram
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 05Y1.** The diagram of a pair at a test presheaf `T`, in the shape the source
displays it: a morphism `a : T ⟶ Q` together with a morphism
`b : T ×_{a, Q} Z ⟶ T ×_{a, Q} X` *over `T`*, that is, commuting with the two projections to
`T`.

This is the first of the source's two descriptions of a pair; the second,
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.RelativeMorphism`, reads `b` instead as a morphism
`T ×_{a, Q} Z ⟶ X` lying over `Q`. The two are the same data —
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.relativeMorphismEquivDiagram`.
declarations.statement:
structure RelativeMorphismDiagram (Z X Q : (BigFppfOver B S hS)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u) (z : Z ⟶ Q)
    (x : X ⟶ Q) (T : (BigFppfOver B S hS)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u)
declarations.comment: the displayed diagram: `b : T ×_{a, B} Z ⟶ T ×_{a, B} X` over `T`

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.relativeHomData
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 05Y2.** The relative morphism functor `Mor_Q(Z, X)` of two morphisms `z : Z ⟶ Q` and
`x : X ⟶ Q` of algebraic spaces over `S`: a small-valued presheaf on the big fppf site of `S`
whose sections over a scheme `T` are the pairs `(a, b)` of Stacks 05Y1, with its projection to `Q`
and with restriction given by base change.

The three algebraicity hypotheses are kept because the source states the functor for algebraic
spaces, but they are not used: smallness of the values comes from essential smallness of the
site (`AlgebraicGeometry.locallySmall_presheaf_bigFppfOver`), not from the existence of an étale
atlas.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def relativeHomData (Z X Q : (BigFppfOver B S hS)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u) (z : Z ⟶ Q)
    (x : X ⟶ Q) (_hZ : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS Z) (_hX : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS X)
    (_hQ : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS Q) : RelativeHomConstruction B S hS Z X Q z x

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.relativeHomEquiv
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 05Y3**, part (2). For a test object `T` — in the source an algebraic space over
`S` — the morphisms `T ⟶ Mor_Q(Z, X)` are canonically the pairs `(a, b)` of Stacks 05Y1 at `T`:
a morphism `a : T ⟶ Q` together with a morphism `b : T ×_{a, Q} Z ⟶ X` over `Q`.

The bijection extends the identification of the sections over a scheme with pairs
(`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.relativeHomEquiv_yoneda`) and is natural in `T`
(`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.relativeHomEquiv_naturality`); the algebraicity of `T` is recorded
because the source states the bijection for algebraic spaces, but it is not used.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def relativeHomEquiv (T : (BigFppfOver B S hS)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u)
    (_hT : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS T) :
    (T ⟶ relativeHom B S hS Z X Q z x hZ hX hQ) ≃ RelativeMorphism B S hS Z X Q z x T
declarations.comment: part (2): the canonical bijection between the morphisms from an algebraic space `T` into `Mor_B(Z, X)` and the pairs `(a, b)` of Stacks 05Y1 at `T`

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isSheaf_relativeHom
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 05Y3**, part (1). For morphisms `z : Z ⟶ Q` and `x : X ⟶ Q` of algebraic spaces
over `S`, the relative morphism functor `Mor_Q(Z, X)` of Stacks 05Y2 is a sheaf on the big fppf
site of `S`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isSheaf_relativeHom (B : BigFppfSite.{u}) (S : Scheme.{u}) (hS : B.Contains S)
    (Z X Q : (BigFppfOver B S hS)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u) (z : Z ⟶ Q) (x : X ⟶ Q)
    (hZ : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS Z) (hX : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS X)
    (hQ : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS Q) :
    Presheaf.IsSheaf (BigFppfOver.topology B S hS)
      (relativeHom B S hS Z X Q z x hZ hX hQ)
declarations.comment: part (1): the relative morphism functor `Mor_B(Z, X)` is a sheaf on the big fppf site of `S`

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.RelativeHomConstruction.isPullback_sheaf_ofBaseChange
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 05Y4.** Let `z : Z ⟶ Q`, `x : X ⟶ Q` and `q : Q' ⟶ Q` be morphisms of algebraic
spaces over `S`, and set `Z' = Q' ×_Q Z` and `X' = Q' ×_Q X`. Then

```text
Mor_{Q'}(Z', X') = Q' ×_Q Mor_Q(Z, X)
```

**in `Sh((Sch/S)_fppf)`**, for arbitrary realizations `H` of `Mor_Q(Z, X)` and `H'` of
`Mor_{Q'}(Z', X')`: the square of fppf sheaves formed by the two projections reading off the first
component of a pair of Stacks 05Y1, the morphism `q` and the morphism forgetting the base change
is cartesian.

Only `Z`, `X`, `Q` and `Q'` are assumed to be algebraic spaces, as in the source. The fibre
products `Z'` and `X'` are algebraic spaces by
`AlgebraicGeometry.isAlgebraicSpace_pullback`, the two relative morphism functors are
sheaves by part (1) of Stacks 05Y3
(`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.RelativeHomConstruction.isSheaf_functor`), and the square is cartesian
by `AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isPullback_sheaf_relativeHomOfBaseChange`.
declarations.statement:
theorem RelativeHomConstruction.isPullback_sheaf_ofBaseChange (q : Q' ⟶ Q)
    (H : RelativeHomConstruction B S hS Z X Q z x)
    (H' : RelativeHomConstruction B S hS (pullback q z) (pullback q x) Q'
      (pullback.fst q z) (pullback.fst q x))
    (hZ : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS Z) (hX : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS X)
    (hQ : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS Q) (hQ' : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS Q') :
    IsPullback
      (ObjectProperty.homMk H'.projection :
        (⟨H'.functor, H'.isSheaf_functor (isAlgebraicSpace_pullback B S hS q z hQ' hZ hQ)
            (isAlgebraicSpace_pullback B S hS q x hQ' hX hQ) hQ'⟩ :
          Sheaf (BigFppfOver.topology B S hS) (Type u)) ⟶ ⟨Q', hQ'.isSheaf⟩)
      (ObjectProperty.homMk (relativeHomOfBaseChange q H H') :
        (⟨H'.functor, H'.isSheaf_functor (isAlgebraicSpace_pullback B S hS q z hQ' hZ hQ)
            (isAlgebraicSpace_pullback B S hS q x hQ' hX hQ) hQ'⟩ :
            Sheaf (BigFppfOver.topology B S hS) (Type u)) ⟶
          ⟨H.functor, H.isSheaf_functor hZ hX hQ⟩)
      (ObjectProperty.homMk q :
        (⟨Q', hQ'.isSheaf⟩ : Sheaf (BigFppfOver.topology B S hS) (Type u)) ⟶ ⟨Q, hQ.isSheaf⟩)
      (ObjectProperty.homMk H.projection :
        (⟨H.functor, H.isSheaf_functor hZ hX hQ⟩ :
          Sheaf (BigFppfOver.topology B S hS) (Type u)) ⟶ ⟨Q, hQ.isSheaf⟩)
declarations.comment: the identification in `Sh((Sch/S)_fppf)`

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isPullback_relativeHomSheafOfBaseChange
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 05Y4** for the relative morphism functor of Stacks 05Y2 and the
fibre products of algebraic spaces of Stacks 02X2: for morphisms `z : Z ⟶ Q`, `x : X ⟶ Q` and
`q : Q' ⟶ Q` of algebraic spaces over `S`,

```text
Mor_{Q'}(Q' ×_Q Z, Q' ×_Q X) = Q' ×_Q Mor_Q(Z, X)
```

**in `Sh((Sch/S)_fppf)`**. This is the source's statement with nothing assumed: the sheaf
property of the two relative morphism functors is part (1) of Stacks 05Y3,
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isSheaf_relativeHom`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isPullback_relativeHomSheafOfBaseChange {Z X Q Q' : AlgebraicSpaces B S hS}
    (z : Z ⟶ Q) (x : X ⟶ Q) (q : Q' ⟶ Q) :
    IsPullback
      (ObjectProperty.homMk
        (relativeHomProjection B S hS (AlgebraicSpaces.fiberProduct B S hS q z).obj
          (AlgebraicSpaces.fiberProduct B S hS q x).obj Q'.obj
          (pullback.fst q.hom z.hom) (pullback.fst q.hom x.hom)
          (AlgebraicSpaces.fiberProduct B S hS q z).property
          (AlgebraicSpaces.fiberProduct B S hS q x).property Q'.property) :
        relativeHomSheaf B S hS (AlgebraicSpaces.fiberProduct B S hS q z).obj
            (AlgebraicSpaces.fiberProduct B S hS q x).obj Q'.obj
            (pullback.fst q.hom z.hom) (pullback.fst q.hom x.hom)
            (AlgebraicSpaces.fiberProduct B S hS q z).property
            (AlgebraicSpaces.fiberProduct B S hS q x).property Q'.property ⟶
          ⟨Q'.obj, Q'.property.isSheaf⟩)
      (ObjectProperty.homMk
        (relativeHomOfBaseChange q.hom
          (relativeHomData B S hS Z.obj X.obj Q.obj z.hom x.hom Z.property X.property Q.property)
          (relativeHomData B S hS (AlgebraicSpaces.fiberProduct B S hS q z).obj
            (AlgebraicSpaces.fiberProduct B S hS q x).obj Q'.obj
            (pullback.fst q.hom z.hom) (pullback.fst q.hom x.hom)
            (AlgebraicSpaces.fiberProduct B S hS q z).property
            (AlgebraicSpaces.fiberProduct B S hS q x).property Q'.property)) :
        relativeHomSheaf B S hS (AlgebraicSpaces.fiberProduct B S hS q z).obj
            (AlgebraicSpaces.fiberProduct B S hS q x).obj Q'.obj
