            (pullback.fst q.hom z.hom) (pullback.fst q.hom x.hom)
            (AlgebraicSpaces.fiberProduct B S hS q z).property
            (AlgebraicSpaces.fiberProduct B S hS q x).property Q'.property ⟶
          relativeHomSheaf B S hS Z.obj X.obj Q.obj z.hom x.hom Z.property X.property Q.property)
      (ObjectProperty.homMk q.hom :
        (⟨Q'.obj, Q'.property.isSheaf⟩ : Sheaf (BigFppfOver.topology B S hS) (Type u)) ⟶
          ⟨Q.obj, Q.property.isSheaf⟩)
      (ObjectProperty.homMk
        (relativeHomProjection B S hS Z.obj X.obj Q.obj z.hom x.hom Z.property X.property
          Q.property) :
        relativeHomSheaf B S hS Z.obj X.obj Q.obj z.hom x.hom Z.property X.property Q.property ⟶
          ⟨Q.obj, Q.property.isSheaf⟩)
declarations.comment: the identification in `Sh((Sch/S)_fppf)` for the functor of Stacks 05Y2 and the fibre products of Stacks 02X2

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isSurjective_relativeHomPostcompose_of_isFiniteLocallyFree
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 05Y5, third conclusion, at the hypotheses of the source.**  Let `z : Z ⟶ Q` and
`x' : X' ⟶ X ⟶ Q` be morphisms of algebraic spaces over `S` with `X' ⟶ X` étale and surjective
and `z` finite locally free.  Then `Mor_Q(Z, X') ⟶ Mor_Q(Z, X)` is surjective.

This is `AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isSurjective_relativeHomPostcompose` with its hypothesis
`h05XQ` discharged by `AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isFibreSectionsSurjective`; it is stated here for
the reason recorded on
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isSurjective_restrictionOfScalarsMap_of_isFiniteLocallyFree`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isSurjective_relativeHomPostcompose_of_isFiniteLocallyFree
    {X' X Z Q : AlgebraicSpaces B S hS} {x' : X' ⟶ Q} {x : X ⟶ Q} {z : Z ⟶ Q}
    (HX' : RelativeHomConstruction B S hS Z.obj X'.obj Q.obj z.hom x'.hom)
    (HX : RelativeHomConstruction B S hS Z.obj X.obj Q.obj z.hom x.hom)
    (g : X' ⟶ X) (hg : g.hom ≫ x.hom = x'.hom)
    (hg_etale : IsEtale B S hS g.hom) (hg_surjective : IsSurjective B S hS g.hom)
    (hz : IsFiniteLocallyFree B S hS z) :
    IsSurjective B S hS (relativeHomPostcompose HX' HX g.hom hg)
declarations.comment:
surjective, given `X' ⟶ X` surjective: at the hypotheses of the source, with
nothing carried

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isRepresentableByAlgebraicSpaces_relativeHomPostcompose_of_isFiniteLocallyFree
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 05Y5, first conclusion, at the hypotheses of the source.** Let `Z → Q` and
`X' → X → Q` be morphisms of algebraic spaces over `S` with `X' → X` étale and `Z → Q` finite
locally free. Then `Mor_Q(Z, X') → Mor_Q(Z, X)` is representable by algebraic spaces.
declarations.statement:
theorem isRepresentableByAlgebraicSpaces_relativeHomPostcompose_of_isFiniteLocallyFree
    {X' X Z Q : AlgebraicSpaces B S hS} {x' : X' ⟶ Q} {x : X ⟶ Q} {z : Z ⟶ Q}
    (HX' : RelativeHomConstruction B S hS Z.obj X'.obj Q.obj z.hom x'.hom)
    (HX : RelativeHomConstruction B S hS Z.obj X.obj Q.obj z.hom x.hom)
    (g : X' ⟶ X) (hg : g.hom ≫ x.hom = x'.hom) (hg_etale : IsEtale B S hS g.hom)
    (hz : IsFiniteLocallyFree B S hS z) :
    IsRepresentableByAlgebraicSpaces B S hS (relativeHomPostcompose HX' HX g.hom hg)
declarations.comment:
representable by algebraic spaces: at the hypotheses of the source, with nothing
carried

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.hasProperty_isEtale_relativeHomPostcompose_of_isFiniteLocallyFree
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 05Y5, second conclusion, at the hypotheses of the source.** In the situation of
`isRepresentableByAlgebraicSpaces_relativeHomPostcompose_of_isFiniteLocallyFree`,
the morphism `Mor_Q(Z, X') → Mor_Q(Z, X)` is étale.
declarations.statement:
theorem hasProperty_isEtale_relativeHomPostcompose_of_isFiniteLocallyFree
    {X' X Z Q : AlgebraicSpaces B S hS} {x' : X' ⟶ Q} {x : X ⟶ Q} {z : Z ⟶ Q}
    (HX' : RelativeHomConstruction B S hS Z.obj X'.obj Q.obj z.hom x'.hom)
    (HX : RelativeHomConstruction B S hS Z.obj X.obj Q.obj z.hom x.hom)
    (g : X' ⟶ X) (hg : g.hom ≫ x.hom = x'.hom) (hg_etale : IsEtale B S hS g.hom)
    (hz : IsFiniteLocallyFree B S hS z) :
    HasProperty B S hS (fun _ _ f => IsEtale B S hS f.hom)
      (relativeHomPostcompose HX' HX g.hom hg)
      (isRepresentableByAlgebraicSpaces_relativeHomPostcompose_of_isFiniteLocallyFree B S hS HX'
        HX g hg hg_etale hz)
declarations.comment: étale: at the hypotheses of the source, with nothing carried

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.relativeHom_representableBy_affine
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 05Y6.** If `Z` and `X` are affine schemes over an affine scheme `S`
and `Γ(Z, 𝒪_Z)` is finite free over `Γ(S, 𝒪_S)`, then the relative morphism
functor `Mor_S(Z, X)` is represented by an affine scheme over `S`.
declarations.statement:
lemma relativeHom_representableBy_affine
    (S Z X : Scheme.{u}) (f : Z ⟶ S) (g : X ⟶ S)
    [IsAffine S] [IsAffine Z] [IsAffine X]
    (hfinite : letI := f.appTop.hom.toAlgebra
      Module.Finite Γ(S, ⊤) Γ(Z, ⊤))
    (hfree : letI := f.appTop.hom.toAlgebra
      Module.Free Γ(S, ⊤) Γ(Z, ⊤)) :
    ∃ W : Over S, IsAffine W.left ∧
      Nonempty
        (((Limits.prod.functor.obj (Over.mk f)).op ⋙
          yoneda.obj (Over.mk g)).RepresentableBy W)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isAlgebraicSpace_relativeHom_of_isFiniteLocallyFree_source
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 05Y7, at the hypotheses of the source.** Let `S` be a scheme contained in a big fppf
site, and let `z : Z ⟶ Q` and `x : X ⟶ Q` be morphisms of algebraic spaces over `S`. If `z` is
finite locally free then the relative morphism functor `Mor_Q(Z, X)` of Stacks 05Y2 is an
algebraic space over `S`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isAlgebraicSpace_relativeHom_of_isFiniteLocallyFree_source
    (Z X Q : (BigFppfOver B S hS)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u) (z : Z ⟶ Q) (x : X ⟶ Q)
    (hZ : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS Z) (hX : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS X)
    (hQ : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS Q)
    (hz : IsFiniteLocallyFree B S hS
      (ObjectProperty.homMk z :
        (⟨Z, hZ⟩ : AlgebraicSpaces B S hS) ⟶ (⟨Q, hQ⟩ : AlgebraicSpaces B S hS))) :
    IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS (relativeHom B S hS Z X Q z x hZ hX hQ)
declarations.comment: at the hypotheses of the source, with nothing carried

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.RestrictionPair
declarations.doc:
A pair `(a, b)` for the restriction of scalars of `x : X ⟶ Z` along
`z : Z ⟶ Q` at a test presheaf `T`: a morphism `a : T ⟶ Q` together with a morphism
`b : T ×_{a, Q} Z ⟶ X` lying over `Z`.

This is a pair of `AlgebraicGeometry.Space.RelativeMorphism` for `z` and `x ≫ z` subject to the
stronger requirement that `b` lie over `Z` and not merely over `Q`; see
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.restrictionPairEquivSubtype`.
declarations.statement:
structure RestrictionPair {X Z Q : AlgebraicSpaces B S hS} (x : X ⟶ Z) (z : Z ⟶ Q)
    (T : (BigFppfOver B S hS)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u)
declarations.comment: the pair (a, b) displayed by the diagram

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.restrictionOfScalars
declarations.doc:
The restriction of scalars `Res_{Z/Q}(X)` of `x : X ⟶ Z` along `z : Z ⟶ Q`: the functor of
points on the big fppf site of `S` whose sections over a scheme `T` are the pairs `(a, b)` of
Stacks 05Y9, with its projection to `Q` and with restriction given by base change.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def restrictionOfScalars {X Z Q : AlgebraicSpaces B S hS} (x : X ⟶ Z)
    (z : Z ⟶ Q) : RestrictionOfScalarsConstruction B S hS x z

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.restrictionOfScalarsHomEquiv
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 05YB.** Morphisms from an algebraic space `T` into the restriction of scalars
`Res_{Z/Q}(X)` of `x : X ⟶ Z` along `z : Z ⟶ Q` are the pairs `(a, b)` of Stacks 05Y9 at `T`:
a morphism `a : T ⟶ Q` together with a morphism `b : T ×_{a, Q} Z ⟶ X` over `Z`.

The bijection is characterized by the two properties recorded with it: its value at `v` base
changes, along every scheme-valued point `i` of `T`, to the pair that Stacks 05YA attaches to
`i ≫ v`; and it is natural in `T`.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def restrictionOfScalarsHomEquiv (x : X ⟶ Z) (z : Z ⟶ Q) :
    {e : ∀ T : AlgebraicSpaces B S hS,
        (T.obj ⟶ (restrictionOfScalars B S hS x z).presheaf) ≃
          RestrictionPair B S hS x z T.obj //
      (∀ (T : AlgebraicSpaces B S hS) (U : BigFppfOver B S hS) (i : yoneda.obj U ⟶ T.obj)
          (v : T.obj ⟶ (restrictionOfScalars B S hS x z).presheaf),
        RestrictionPair.IsPullbackAlong i (e T v)
          ((restrictionOfScalars B S hS x z).pairEquiv U (yonedaEquiv (i ≫ v)))) ∧
      (∀ (T T' : AlgebraicSpaces B S hS) (f : T' ⟶ T)
          (v : T.obj ⟶ (restrictionOfScalars B S hS x z).presheaf),
        RestrictionPair.IsPullbackAlong f.hom (e T v) (e T' (f.hom ≫ v)))}
declarations.comment: the functor of points

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isSheaf_restrictionOfScalars
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 05YB**, part (1). For morphisms `x : X ⟶ Z` and `z : Z ⟶ Q` of algebraic spaces
over `S`, the restriction of scalars `Res_{Z/Q}(X)` of Stacks 05YA is a sheaf on the big fppf
site of `S`.

A pair `(a, b)` of Stacks 05Y9 is a pair of Stacks 05Y1 whose second component lies over `Z`,
and the cartesian square of Stacks 05YE presents `Res_{Z/Q}(X)` as the fibre product of
`Mor_Q(Z, X)` and `Q` over `Mor_Q(Z, Z)`. The descent of pairs the source carries out is
therefore already done: it is part (1) of Stacks 05Y3 for the two relative morphism functors,
and the fibre product of sheaves of types is a sheaf.
declarations.statement:
theorem isSheaf_restrictionOfScalars {X Z Q : AlgebraicSpaces B S hS} (x : X ⟶ Z) (z : Z ⟶ Q) :
    Presheaf.IsSheaf (BigFppfOver.topology B S hS)
      (restrictionOfScalars B S hS x z).presheaf
declarations.comment: part (1): `Res_{Z/B}(X)` is a sheaf on the big fppf site of `S`

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.baseChangeFiberProductMap
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 05YC.** The base change `Q' ×_Q X ⟶ Q' ×_Q Z` of a morphism `x : X ⟶ Z` of
algebraic spaces over `z : Z ⟶ Q` along a morphism `b : Q' ⟶ Q`, for the chosen fibre products
of Stacks 02X2. It is the identity on the first factor and `x` on the second.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def baseChangeFiberProductMap {X Z Q Q' : AlgebraicSpaces B S hS} (x : X ⟶ Z)
    (z : Z ⟶ Q) (b : Q' ⟶ Q) :
    AlgebraicSpaces.fiberProduct B S hS b (x ≫ z) ⟶ AlgebraicSpaces.fiberProduct B S hS b z
declarations.comment: the base-changed morphism

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isPullback_baseChangeFiberProductMap
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 05YC.** The base-changed morphism exhibits `Q' ×_Q X` as `(Q' ×_Q Z) ×_Z X`. This
is the form in which `AlgebraicGeometry.Space.restrictionOfScalars_baseChange` asks for the
base change of `x`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isPullback_baseChangeFiberProductMap :
    IsPullback (baseChangeFiberProductMap B S hS x z b).hom
      (pullback.snd b.hom (x ≫ z).hom) (pullback.snd b.hom z.hom) x.hom
declarations.comment: the base-changed morphism as a fibre product

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.restrictionOfScalars_baseChange
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 05YC.** Let `x : X ⟶ Z` and `z : Z ⟶ Q` be morphisms of algebraic spaces over `S`
and let `b : Q' ⟶ Q` be a morphism of algebraic spaces over `S`. Let `z' : Z' ⟶ Q'`, `c : Z' ⟶ Z`
exhibit `Z'` as the base change `Q' ×_Q Z`, and let `x' : X' ⟶ Z'`, `e : X' ⟶ X` exhibit `X'` as
the base change `Z' ×_Z X`, so that `X' = Q' ×_Q X`. Then

```text
Res_{Z'/Q'}(X')  =  Q' ×_Q Res_{Z/Q}(X)
```

as presheaves on the big fppf site of `S`: there is an isomorphism compatible with the
projections to `Q'`, which on sections carries the pair of Stacks 05Y9 of a section of
`Res_{Z'/Q'}(X')` to its base change
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.RestrictionPair.baseChange`.

For the chosen fibre products of Stacks 02X2 the two hypotheses are
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isPullback_hom_fiberProduct` and
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isPullback_baseChangeFiberProductMap`; that instance is
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.restrictionOfScalars_baseChange_fiberProduct`.
declarations.statement:
theorem restrictionOfScalars_baseChange :
    ∃ i : r'.presheaf ≅ pullback b.hom r.projection,
      i.hom ≫ pullback.fst b.hom r.projection = r'.projection ∧
        ∀ (T : BigFppfOver B S hS) (v : r'.presheaf.obj (op T)),
          r.pairEquiv T ((i.hom ≫ pullback.snd b.hom r.projection).app (op T) v) =
            (r'.pairEquiv T v).baseChange hZ hX
declarations.comment: the base-change identification

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.restrictionOfScalars_baseChange_fiberProduct
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 05YC.** The form of `AlgebraicGeometry.Space.restrictionOfScalars_baseChange` for
the chosen fibre products of Stacks 02X2: with `Z' = Q' ×_Q Z` and `X' = Q' ×_Q X` those fibre
products and `x' : X' ⟶ Z'` the base-changed morphism
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.baseChangeFiberProductMap`,

```text
Res_{Z'/Q'}(X')  =  Q' ×_Q Res_{Z/Q}(X)
```

as presheaves on the big fppf site of `S`, compatibly with the projections to `Q'`.
declarations.statement:
theorem restrictionOfScalars_baseChange_fiberProduct {X Z Q Q' : AlgebraicSpaces B S hS}
    (x : X ⟶ Z) (z : Z ⟶ Q) (b : Q' ⟶ Q)
    (r : RestrictionOfScalarsConstruction B S hS x z)
    (r' : RestrictionOfScalarsConstruction B S hS (baseChangeFiberProductMap B S hS x z b)
      (ObjectProperty.homMk (pullback.fst b.hom z.hom) :
        AlgebraicSpaces.fiberProduct B S hS b z ⟶ Q')) :
    ∃ i : r'.presheaf ≅ pullback b.hom r.projection,
      i.hom ≫ pullback.fst b.hom r.projection = r'.projection ∧
        ∀ (T : BigFppfOver B S hS) (v : r'.presheaf.obj (op T)),
          r.pairEquiv T ((i.hom ≫ pullback.snd b.hom r.projection).app (op T) v) =
            (r'.pairEquiv T v).baseChange (isPullback_hom_fiberProduct B S hS b z)
              (isPullback_baseChangeFiberProductMap B S hS x z b)
declarations.comment: the base-change identification for the chosen fibre products

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isSurjective_restrictionOfScalarsMap_of_isFiniteLocallyFree
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 05YD, third conclusion, at the hypotheses of the source.**  Let
`X' → X → Z → Q` be morphisms of algebraic spaces over `S` with `X' → X` étale and surjective
and `Z → Q` finite locally free.  Then `Res_{Z/Q}(X') → Res_{Z/Q}(X)` is surjective.

This is `AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isSurjective_restrictionOfScalarsMap` with its hypothesis
`h05XQ` discharged by `AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isFibreSectionsSurjective`.  It is stated here
rather than beside that theorem because
`StacksFrontier/AlgebraicGeometry/Spaces/SmallEtaleChartLocalizationBaseChange.lean`, which the
chart comparison of Stacks 03ZU is built on, already imports the file where it lives.
declarations.statement:
theorem isSurjective_restrictionOfScalarsMap_of_isFiniteLocallyFree
    {X' X Z Q : AlgebraicSpaces B S hS} {x' : X' ⟶ Z} {x : X ⟶ Z} (g : X' ⟶ X)
    (hg : g ≫ x = x') (z : Z ⟶ Q)
    (hg_etale : IsEtale B S hS g.hom) (hg_surjective : IsSurjective B S hS g.hom)
    (hz : IsFiniteLocallyFree B S hS z) :
    IsSurjective B S hS (restrictionOfScalarsMap g hg z).1
declarations.comment:
surjective, given `X' ⟶ X` surjective: at the hypotheses of the source, with
nothing carried

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isRepresentableByAlgebraicSpaces_restrictionOfScalarsMap_of_isFiniteLocallyFree
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 05YD, first conclusion, at the hypotheses of the source.** Let `X' → X → Z → Q` be
morphisms of algebraic spaces over `S` with `X' → X` étale and `Z → Q` finite locally free. Then
`Res_{Z/Q}(X') → Res_{Z/Q}(X)` is representable by algebraic spaces.
declarations.statement:
theorem isRepresentableByAlgebraicSpaces_restrictionOfScalarsMap_of_isFiniteLocallyFree
    {X' X Z Q : AlgebraicSpaces B S hS} {x' : X' ⟶ Z} {x : X ⟶ Z} (g : X' ⟶ X)
    (hg : g ≫ x = x') (z : Z ⟶ Q) (hg_etale : IsEtale B S hS g.hom)
    (hz : IsFiniteLocallyFree B S hS z) :
    IsRepresentableByAlgebraicSpaces B S hS (restrictionOfScalarsMap g hg z).1
declarations.comment:
representable by algebraic spaces: at the hypotheses of the source, with nothing
carried

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.hasProperty_isEtale_restrictionOfScalarsMap_of_isFiniteLocallyFree
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 05YD, second conclusion, at the hypotheses of the source.** In the situation of
`isRepresentableByAlgebraicSpaces_restrictionOfScalarsMap_of_isFiniteLocallyFree`,
the morphism `Res_{Z/Q}(X') → Res_{Z/Q}(X)` is étale.
declarations.statement:
theorem hasProperty_isEtale_restrictionOfScalarsMap_of_isFiniteLocallyFree
    {X' X Z Q : AlgebraicSpaces B S hS} {x' : X' ⟶ Z} {x : X ⟶ Z} (g : X' ⟶ X)
    (hg : g ≫ x = x') (z : Z ⟶ Q) (hg_etale : IsEtale B S hS g.hom)
    (hz : IsFiniteLocallyFree B S hS z) :
    HasProperty B S hS (fun _ _ f => IsEtale B S hS f.hom) (restrictionOfScalarsMap g hg z).1
      (isRepresentableByAlgebraicSpaces_restrictionOfScalarsMap_of_isFiniteLocallyFree B S hS g hg
        z hg_etale hz)
declarations.comment: étale: at the hypotheses of the source, with nothing carried

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isPullback_restrictionOfScalars
declarations.doc:
The square

```text
Mor_Q(Z, X) ⟶ Mor_Q(Z, Z)
     ↑              ↑ id_Z
Res_{Z/Q}(X) ⟶     Q
```

of presheaves on the big fppf site of `S` is cartesian: the restriction of scalars of `x : X ⟶ Z`
along `z : Z ⟶ Q` is the fibre product of `Mor_Q(Z, X)` and `Q` over `Mor_Q(Z, Z)`, where the
morphism from `Q` picks out the identity endomorphism of `Z`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isPullback_restrictionOfScalars {X Z Q : AlgebraicSpaces B S hS} {x : X ⟶ Z} {z : Z ⟶ Q}
    (R : RestrictionOfScalarsConstruction B S hS x z)
    (HX : RelativeHomConstruction B S hS Z.obj X.obj Q.obj z.hom (x.hom ≫ z.hom))
    (HZ : RelativeHomConstruction B S hS Z.obj Z.obj Q.obj z.hom z.hom) :
    IsPullback (restrictionOfScalarsToRelativeHom R HX) R.projection
      (relativeHomPostcompose HX HZ x.hom rfl) (relativeHomIdentity HZ)
declarations.comment: the cartesian square of presheaves on the big fppf site

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isPullback_restrictionOfScalars_relativeHomData
declarations.doc:
The square of `AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isPullback_restrictionOfScalars` is cartesian for the
relative morphism functor of Stacks 05Y2 and the restriction of scalars of Stacks 05YA.
declarations.statement:
theorem isPullback_restrictionOfScalars_relativeHomData {X Z Q : AlgebraicSpaces B S hS}
    (x : X ⟶ Z) (z : Z ⟶ Q) :
    IsPullback
      (restrictionOfScalarsToRelativeHom (restrictionOfScalars B S hS x z)
        (relativeHomData B S hS Z.obj X.obj Q.obj z.hom (x.hom ≫ z.hom) Z.property X.property
          Q.property))
      (restrictionOfScalars B S hS x z).projection
      (relativeHomPostcompose
        (relativeHomData B S hS Z.obj X.obj Q.obj z.hom (x.hom ≫ z.hom) Z.property X.property
          Q.property)
        (relativeHomData B S hS Z.obj Z.obj Q.obj z.hom z.hom Z.property Z.property Q.property)
        x.hom rfl)
      (relativeHomIdentity
        (relativeHomData B S hS Z.obj Z.obj Q.obj z.hom z.hom Z.property Z.property Q.property))
declarations.comment: the cartesian square, for the functors of Stacks 05Y2 and 05YA

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isAlgebraicSpace_restrictionOfScalars_of_isFiniteLocallyFree_source
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 05YF, at the hypotheses of the source.** Let `x : X ⟶ Z` and `z : Z ⟶ Q` be
morphisms of algebraic spaces over `S` with `z` finite locally free. Then the restriction of
scalars `Res_{Z/Q}(X)` of Stacks 05YA is an algebraic space over `S`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isAlgebraicSpace_restrictionOfScalars_of_isFiniteLocallyFree_source
    {X Z Q : AlgebraicSpaces B S hS} (x : X ⟶ Z) (z : Z ⟶ Q)
    (hz : IsFiniteLocallyFree B S hS z) :
    IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS (restrictionOfScalars B S hS x z).presheaf
declarations.comment: at the hypotheses of the source, with nothing carried

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.isRepresentableByAlgebraicSpaces_and_isEtale_mapRelative
declarations.doc:
Let `G : 𝒳' ⟶ 𝒳` be a 1-morphism of stacks in groupoids over the big fppf site of `S` which
is representable by algebraic spaces and étale, and let `γ` present `𝒳' ⟶ 𝒴` as the composite of
`G` with `F : 𝒳 ⟶ 𝒴`. Then the canonical 1-morphism `ℋ_d(𝒳'/𝒴) ⟶ ℋ_d(𝒳/𝒴)` of Stacks 05XN is
representable by algebraic spaces and étale.

The conclusion is the shape of `AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.IsRelativelyEtale` at the free universes
of the stacks involved: representability by algebraic spaces, and étaleness over `S` of every
algebraic space representing a fibre over a scheme-valued point. The two halves are
`AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.isRepresentableByAlgebraicSpaces_mapRelative` and
`AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.isEtale_mapRelative`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isRepresentableByAlgebraicSpaces_and_isEtale_mapRelative
    (γ : BasedFunctor.comp F' (𝟙 𝒴.toBasedCategory) ≅ BasedFunctor.comp G F)
    (hGrep : IsRepresentableByAlgebraicSpaces B S hS G)
    (hGet : ∀ (U : BigFppfOver B S hS)
      (z : BigFppfOver B U.left.1 U.left.2 ⥤ 𝒳.toBasedCategory.obj)
      (_hz : z ⋙ 𝒳.toBasedCategory.p = Over.map U.hom)
      (W : (BigFppfOver B U.left.1 U.left.2)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u)
      (hW : IsAlgebraicSpace B U.left.1 U.left.2 W),
      Nonempty (StacksRepresentableCFG.EquivalenceOver
        (TwoFibreProductOver.fst (Over.map U.hom) 𝒳'.toBasedCategory.p 𝒳.toBasedCategory.p z
          G.toFunctor)
        (presheafOfCategories (W ⋙ typeToCat)).p) →
      Space.IsEtale B S hS (algebraicSpaceMap B S hS U
        ((spacesOverSmallerBaseFunctor B U.left.1 S U.left.2 hS U.hom).obj ⟨W, hW⟩)).hom) :
    ∃ _ : IsRepresentableByAlgebraicSpaces B S hS
        (mapRelative B S hS d 𝒳' 𝒴 𝒳 𝒴 F' F G (𝟙 𝒴.toBasedCategory) γ),
      ∀ (U : BigFppfOver B S hS)
        (y : BigFppfOver B U.left.1 U.left.2 ⥤
          (finiteHilbertCategory (B := B) (S := S) (hS := hS) (𝒳 := 𝒳) (𝒴 := 𝒴) (F := F)
            (d := d)).obj)
        (_hy : y ⋙ (finiteHilbertCategory (B := B) (S := S) (hS := hS) (𝒳 := 𝒳) (𝒴 := 𝒴)
          (F := F) (d := d)).p = Over.map U.hom)
        (A : (BigFppfOver B U.left.1 U.left.2)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u)
        (hA : IsAlgebraicSpace B U.left.1 U.left.2 A),
        Nonempty (StacksRepresentableCFG.EquivalenceOver
          (TwoFibreProductOver.fst (Over.map U.hom)
            (finiteHilbertCategory (B := B) (S := S) (hS := hS) (𝒳 := 𝒳') (𝒴 := 𝒴) (F := F')
              (d := d)).p
            (finiteHilbertCategory (B := B) (S := S) (hS := hS) (𝒳 := 𝒳) (𝒴 := 𝒴) (F := F)
              (d := d)).p y
            (mapRelative B S hS d 𝒳' 𝒴 𝒳 𝒴 F' F G (𝟙 𝒴.toBasedCategory) γ).toFunctor)
          (presheafOfCategories (A ⋙ typeToCat)).p) →
        Space.IsEtale B S hS (algebraicSpaceMap B S hS U
          ((spacesOverSmallerBaseFunctor B U.left.1 S U.left.2 hS U.hom).obj ⟨A, hA⟩)).hom
declarations.comment: part (1)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.isSurjectiveOnObjects_mapRelative
declarations.doc:
If `G : 𝒳' ⟶ 𝒳` is representable by algebraic spaces, étale and surjective, then the
canonical 1-morphism `ℋ_d(𝒳'/𝒴) ⟶ ℋ_d(𝒳/𝒴)` is surjective.

By Stacks 06D7 surjectivity of a 1-morphism representable by algebraic spaces is surjectivity of
every algebraic space representing one of its fibres over a scheme-valued point; that algebraic
space is a space of sections of a surjective étale morphism to a finite cover of the point, which
is surjective over the point by Stacks 05XQ.
declarations.statement:
theorem isSurjectiveOnObjects_mapRelative
    (γ : BasedFunctor.comp F' (𝟙 𝒴.toBasedCategory) ≅ BasedFunctor.comp G F)
    (hGrep : IsRepresentableByAlgebraicSpaces B S hS G)
    (hGet : ∀ (U : BigFppfOver B S hS)
      (z : BigFppfOver B U.left.1 U.left.2 ⥤ 𝒳.toBasedCategory.obj)
      (_hz : z ⋙ 𝒳.toBasedCategory.p = Over.map U.hom)
      (W : (BigFppfOver B U.left.1 U.left.2)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u)
      (hW : IsAlgebraicSpace B U.left.1 U.left.2 W),
      Nonempty (StacksRepresentableCFG.EquivalenceOver
        (TwoFibreProductOver.fst (Over.map U.hom) 𝒳'.toBasedCategory.p 𝒳.toBasedCategory.p z
          G.toFunctor)
        (presheafOfCategories (W ⋙ typeToCat)).p) →
      Space.IsEtale B S hS (algebraicSpaceMap B S hS U
        ((spacesOverSmallerBaseFunctor B U.left.1 S U.left.2 hS U.hom).obj ⟨W, hW⟩)).hom)
    (hGsurj : IsSurjectiveOnObjects B S hS 𝒳'.toBasedCategory.p 𝒳.toBasedCategory.p
      G.toFunctor) :
    IsSurjectiveOnObjects B S hS
      (finiteHilbertCategory (B := B) (S := S) (hS := hS) (𝒳 := 𝒳') (𝒴 := 𝒴) (F := F')
        (d := d)).p
      (finiteHilbertCategory (B := B) (S := S) (hS := hS) (𝒳 := 𝒳) (𝒴 := 𝒴) (F := F) (d := d)).p
      (mapRelative B S hS d 𝒳' 𝒴 𝒳 𝒴 F' F G (𝟙 𝒴.toBasedCategory) γ).toFunctor
declarations.comment: part (2)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.isRepresentableByAlgebraicSpacesForgetToProduct_of_diagonal
declarations.doc:
Let `F : 𝒳 ⟶ 𝒴` be a 1-morphism of stacks in groupoids over the big fppf
site of a scheme `S` and let `d` be a natural number. If the diagonal `𝒴 ⟶ 𝒴 × 𝒴` is
representable by algebraic spaces then the 1-morphism

`ℋ_d(𝒳/𝒴) ⟶ ℋ_d(𝒳) × 𝒴`

of Equation 05WD is representable by algebraic spaces, in the sense of Stacks 02ZW.
declarations.statement:
theorem isRepresentableByAlgebraicSpacesForgetToProduct_of_diagonal
    (hΔ : HasRepresentableDiagonal B S hS (targetCFG (𝒴 := 𝒴))) :
    IsRepresentableByAlgebraicSpacesForgetToProduct
      (B := B) (S := S) (hS := hS) (d := d) (𝒳 := 𝒳) (𝒴 := 𝒴) (F := F)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.isRepresentableByAlgebraicSpaces_mapRelative_of_representable
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 05YJ.** Let `G : 𝒳' ⟶ 𝒳` be a 1-morphism of stacks in groupoids over the big fppf
site of `S` which is representable by algebraic spaces, and let `γ` present `𝒳' ⟶ 𝒴` as the
composite of `G` with `F : 𝒳 ⟶ 𝒴`. Then the canonical 1-morphism
`ℋ_d(𝒳'/𝒴) ⟶ ℋ_d(𝒳/𝒴)` of degree-`d` relative finite Hilbert stacks is representable by
algebraic spaces.

The fibre over the universal family of an object `ξ = (U, Z, y, x, α)` is the restriction of
scalars along `Z ⟶ U` of an algebraic space representing the fibre of `G` over `x`, which is an
algebraic space by Stacks 05YF; that is
`AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.FiniteHilbert.Object.exists_isAlgebraicSpace_sectionSpace`. An arbitrary
scheme-valued point reduces to those by the 2-Yoneda normalisation
`AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.isRepresentableByAlgebraicSpaces_of_universalFamilies`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isRepresentableByAlgebraicSpaces_mapRelative_of_representable
    (γ : BasedFunctor.comp F' (𝟙 𝒴.toBasedCategory) ≅ BasedFunctor.comp G F)
    (hG : IsRepresentableByAlgebraicSpaces B S hS G) :
    IsRepresentableByAlgebraicSpaces B S hS
      (mapRelative B S hS d 𝒳' 𝒴 𝒳 𝒴 F' F G (𝟙 𝒴.toBasedCategory) γ)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.FiniteFreeAlgebra.existsUnique_map_universalRingStructure
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 05YM.** For every scheme `T`, every free `d`-dimensional algebra over `Γ(T, 𝒪_T)`
is the extension of the universal algebra `m_univ` along the ring map induced by exactly one
morphism `T ⟶ X = Spec(R_univ)`; and the resulting identification of `X(T)` with free
`d`-dimensional algebras over `Γ(T, 𝒪_T)` commutes with pullback along every morphism of
schemes.
declarations.statement:
theorem existsUnique_map_universalRingStructure :
    (∀ (T : Scheme.{u}) (m : FiniteFreeAlgebra Γ(T, ⊤) d),
      ∃! x : T ⟶ scheme.{u} d, map (classifyingRingHom x) (universalRingStructure d) = m) ∧
    ∀ {T U : Scheme.{u}} (f : T ⟶ U) (x : U ⟶ scheme.{u} d),
      map f.appTop.hom (map (classifyingRingHom x) (universalRingStructure d)) =
        map (classifyingRingHom (f ≫ x)) (universalRingStructure d)
declarations.comment: for every scheme `T`, the point `x : T ⟶ Spec(R_univ)` corresponds to the extension of the universal algebra along the ring map `R_univ → Γ(T, 𝒪_T)` induced by `x`; this is a bijection, natural in `T`

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.FiniteFreeAlgebra.structureConstantsOver
declarations.doc: The scheme of structure constants, as a scheme over the integers.
declarations.statement: noncomputable abbrev structureConstantsOver : Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of (ULift.{u} ℤ)))
declarations.comment: the scheme of structure constants over the integers

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.FiniteFreeAlgebra.structureConstantsBaseChange
declarations.doc:
The scheme `X_S` of structure constants over a scheme `S`, obtained by base change from the
integers.
declarations.statement: noncomputable abbrev structureConstantsBaseChange (S : Scheme.{u}) : Over S
declarations.comment: the scheme of structure constants over a general base

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.FiniteFreeAlgebra.structureConstantsBaseChangePoints
declarations.doc:
The points of `X_S` over a scheme `T` over `S` are the free `d`-dimensional algebras over
`Γ(T, 𝒪_T)`.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def structureConstantsBaseChangePoints (S : Scheme.{u}) (T : Over S) :
    (T ⟶ structureConstantsBaseChange.{u} d S) ≃ FiniteFreeAlgebra Γ(T.left, ⊤) d
declarations.comment: the points of the scheme of structure constants over a general base

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.FiniteFreeAlgebra.structureConstantsBaseChangePoints_naturality
declarations.doc:
`AlgebraicGeometry.FiniteFreeAlgebra.structureConstantsBaseChangePoints` is natural in the
scheme over `S`: restricting a point along `f` extends the scalars of its structure constants
along the induced map of global sections.
declarations.statement:
theorem structureConstantsBaseChangePoints_naturality (S : Scheme.{u}) {T U : Over S}
    (f : T ⟶ U) (x : U ⟶ structureConstantsBaseChange.{u} d S) :
    FiniteFreeAlgebra.map f.left.appTop.hom
        (structureConstantsBaseChangePoints d S U x) =
      structureConstantsBaseChangePoints d S T (f ≫ x)
declarations.comment: the points of the scheme of structure constants over a general base

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.structureConstantsSiteObject
declarations.doc:
The scheme `X_S` of structure constants over `S`, read as an object of the big fppf site
over `S`.
declarations.statement: noncomputable def structureConstantsSiteObject : BigFppfOver 𝒞 S hS
declarations.comment: the scheme of structure constants as an object of the site

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.structureConstantsSpaceOver
declarations.doc:
The algebraic space `B ×_S X_S` over an algebraic space `B` over `S`, as an object of the
slice of presheaves on the big fppf site over `B`.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def structureConstantsSpaceOver (B : (BigFppfOver 𝒞 S hS)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u) :
    Over B
declarations.comment: the scheme of structure constants as an object over an algebraic space

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isAlgebraicSpace_structureConstantsSpaceOver
declarations.doc: The presheaf underlying `B ×_S X_S` is an algebraic space over `S`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isAlgebraicSpace_structureConstantsSpaceOver (B : (BigFppfOver 𝒞 S hS)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u)
    (hB : IsAlgebraicSpace 𝒞 S hS B) :
    IsAlgebraicSpace 𝒞 S hS
      (B ⨯ yoneda.obj (structureConstantsSiteObject 𝒞 S hS d))
declarations.comment: the scheme of structure constants as an object over an algebraic space

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.FiniteFreeAlgebra.presheaf
declarations.doc:
The presheaf in groupoids `FA_d` of free rank-`d` commutative algebra structures and their
isomorphisms.
declarations.statement: noncomputable def presheaf (B : BigFppfSite.{u}) (d : ℕ) [NeZero d] : Presheaf B d

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.FiniteFreeAlgebra.presheaf_actionGroupoid
declarations.doc:
Conjugation defines an action on the scheme of structure constants, and `FA_d` is
naturally isomorphic to its action-groupoid functor, by the representing equivalence on objects
and the inverse matrices on arrows.
declarations.statement:
public theorem presheaf_actionGroupoid
    (B : BigFppfSite.{u}) (d : ℕ) [NeZero d]
    (F : Presheaf B d) :
    ∃ (laws : ConjugationPreservesAlgebraLaws.{u} d)
      (P : ActionGroupoidPresheaf B d laws)
      (η : F.functor ≅ P.toFunctor),
      (∀ (T : B.Schemesᵒᵖ) (x : F.functor.obj T),
        (η.hom.app T).obj x =
          ((representation.{u} d).equiv T.unop.1).symm
            (F.objectEquiv T x)) ∧
      (∀ (T : B.Schemesᵒᵖ) (x y : F.functor.obj T) (e : x ⟶ y),
        (P.arrowEquiv T _ _ ((η.hom.app T).map e)).1.1 =
          (F.arrowEquiv T x y e).matrix⁻¹)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.isAlgebraicStack_finiteCoverFibered
declarations.doc:
The category `ℋ_d` of degree-`d` finite locally free covers over the big fppf site over `S`
is an algebraic stack over `S`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isAlgebraicStack_finiteCoverFibered :
    IsAlgebraicStack.{u, w} 𝒞 S hS (finiteCoverFibered 𝒞 S hS d).val
declarations.comment: the second assertion: `ℋ_d` is an algebraic stack over `S`, transported along the equivalence of the first assertion from the quotient stack `[X/G]` of the conjugation action, which is an algebraic stack by Stacks 04TK

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.FiniteFreeAlgebra.nonempty_isEquivalenceOver_finiteCover_conjugationQuotient
declarations.doc:
The category `ℋ_d` of degree-`d` finite locally free covers is equivalent, over the big fppf
site over `S`, to the quotient stack `[X/G]` of the conjugation action of the unit-fixing subgroup
`G ⊆ GL_d` on the scheme `X` of structure constants of free `d`-dimensional algebras, by the
extension of `AlgebraicGeometry.FiniteFreeAlgebra.specQuotientPrestack` across the stackification
`AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.toQuotientStack`.
declarations.statement:
theorem nonempty_isEquivalenceOver_finiteCover_conjugationQuotient :
    Nonempty (Functor.IsEquivalenceOver
      (Space.structureConstantsQuotientStack 𝒞 S hS d (Space.terminalSpace 𝒞 S hS)).p
      (Functor.uliftHomProj (AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.finiteCoverProjection
        (B := 𝒞) (S := S) (hS := hS) (d := d)))
      (Functor.Stackification.extend
        (AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.isFibredOneMorphism_toQuotientStack
          (conjugationGroupoidInSpaces 𝒞 S hS d (isAlgebraicSpace_conjugationGroup 𝒞 S hS d)
          (isAlgebraicSpace_conjugationObject 𝒞 S hS d)))
        (isFibredOneMorphism_specQuotientPrestack
          (conjugationGroupoidInSpaces 𝒞 S hS d (isAlgebraicSpace_conjugationGroup 𝒞 S hS d)
          (isAlgebraicSpace_conjugationObject 𝒞 S hS d))
          (conjugationGroupoidIso 𝒞 S hS d))
        (AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.isLocallyBijective_toQuotientStack
          (conjugationGroupoidInSpaces 𝒞 S hS d (isAlgebraicSpace_conjugationGroup 𝒞 S hS d)
          (isAlgebraicSpace_conjugationObject 𝒞 S hS d)))
        (isStack_uliftHomProj_finiteCoverProjection 𝒞 S hS d).isMorSheaf
        (AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.essImage_toQuotientStack
          (conjugationGroupoidInSpaces 𝒞 S hS d (isAlgebraicSpace_conjugationGroup 𝒞 S hS d)
          (isAlgebraicSpace_conjugationObject 𝒞 S hS d)))
        (isStack_uliftHomProj_finiteCoverProjection 𝒞 S hS d).hasEffectiveDescent))
declarations.comment: the category of degree-`d` finite locally free covers is equivalent, over the big fppf site over `S`, to the quotient stack `[X/G]` of the conjugation action of the unit-fixing subgroup `G` of `GL_d` on the scheme `X` of structure constants

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.FiniteFreeAlgebra.algEquivCarrierOfIsUnit
declarations.doc:
If one coordinate of the unit becomes invertible in `S`, the base changed algebra `S ⊗[R] A` is
the algebra of a free `d`-dimensional structure over `S`.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def algEquivCarrierOfIsUnit (b : Module.Basis (Fin d) R A) (i : Fin d)
    (hi : IsUnit (algebraMap R S (b.repr 1 i))) :
    (S ⊗[R] A) ≃ₐ[S] Carrier (structureOfIsUnit S b i hi)
declarations.comment: clause (b) of the proof over an affine base: inverting one coordinate of the unit presents the algebra as the algebra of a free `d`-dimensional structure

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.FiniteFreeAlgebra.exists_structure_algEquiv_localizationAway
declarations.doc:
Over each member of the standard open cover of `Spec R` cut out by the coordinates of the unit,
the algebra is the algebra of a free `d`-dimensional structure.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_structure_algEquiv_localizationAway (b : Module.Basis (Fin d) R A) (i : Fin d) :
    ∃ m : FiniteFreeAlgebra (Localization.Away (b.repr 1 i)) d,
      Nonempty ((Localization.Away (b.repr 1 i) ⊗[R] A) ≃ₐ[Localization.Away (b.repr 1 i)]
        Carrier m)
declarations.comment: clause (b) of the proof over an affine base, on the standard open cover cut out by the coordinates of the unit

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.FiniteFreeAlgebra.algEquivCarrierOfBasis
declarations.doc:
An algebra that is free of rank `d` on a basis whose first vector is the unit is isomorphic,
as an `R`-algebra, to the algebra of the structure constants of that basis.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def algEquivCarrierOfBasis (b : Module.Basis (Fin d) R A) (hb : b 0 = 1) :
    A ≃ₐ[R] Carrier (ofBasis b hb)
declarations.comment: transport of the multiplication along a basis whose first vector is the unit, over an affine base

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.FiniteFreeAlgebra.isFiniteLocallyFreeOfRank_specCover
declarations.doc:
The spectrum of the algebra of a free `d`-dimensional structure is finite locally free of
degree `d` over the base.
declarations.statement:
theorem isFiniteLocallyFreeOfRank_specCover (m : FiniteFreeAlgebra R d) :
    Stacks.Morphisms.IsFiniteLocallyFreeOfRank (specCover m).hom d
declarations.comment: the degree-`d` clause for the spectrum of a free `d`-dimensional structure over a ring, in the affine case

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.FiniteFreeAlgebra.structureIsoEquivSpecIso
declarations.doc:
The isomorphisms of two free `d`-dimensional structures over `R` are exactly the
isomorphisms of their spectra as schemes over `Spec R`.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def structureIsoEquivSpecIso (m n : FiniteFreeAlgebra R d) :
    StructureIso m n ≃ (specCover m ≅ specCover n)
declarations.comment: clause (a) of the proof over an affine base: `Isom (m, n)` is `Isom (Spec m, Spec n)` as schemes over the base

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.FiniteFreeAlgebra.Carrier.basis
declarations.doc:
The module underlying the algebra of a free `d`-dimensional structure is free with basis the
`d` standard basis vectors.
declarations.statement: noncomputable def basis (m : FiniteFreeAlgebra R d) : Module.Basis (Fin d) R (Carrier m)
declarations.comment: the module underlying the algebra of a free `d`-dimensional structure is free of rank `d`, the affine core of the degree-`d` clause for the relative spectrum of `m`

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.FiniteFreeAlgebra.structureIsoEquivAlgEquiv
declarations.doc:
The isomorphisms of two free `d`-dimensional structures over a ring are exactly the
`R`-algebra isomorphisms of the two associated algebras.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def structureIsoEquivAlgEquiv (m n : FiniteFreeAlgebra R d) :
    StructureIso m n ≃ (Carrier m ≃ₐ[R] Carrier n)
declarations.comment: clause (a) of the proof, in algebraic form: the isomorphisms of two free `d`-dimensional structures are exactly the algebra isomorphisms of the associated algebras

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.isAlgebraicStack_absoluteHilbertFibered
declarations.doc:
The finite Hilbert stack `ℋ_d(𝒳)` of an algebraic space `𝒳` over `S` is an algebraic
stack.
declarations.statement:
theorem isAlgebraicStack_absoluteHilbertFibered [NeZero d]
    (𝒳 : StackInGroupoids.{w, u, u, u + 1, u + 1} (BigFppfOver B S hS)
      (BigFppfOver.topology B S hS))
    (h𝒳 : IsRepresentableByAlgebraicSpace B S hS
      (CatFiberedInGroupoids.mk 𝒳.toBasedCategory
        𝒳.isStackInGroupoids.isFiberedInGroupoids)) :
    IsAlgebraicStack.{u, w} B S hS (absoluteHilbertFibered 𝒳 d).val
declarations.comment: `NeZero d` restricts nothing: Examples of Stacks, Section 95.18 (Stacks 05WA) introduces `ℋ_d(X)` only `For each integer d ≥ 1`, and the source's proof of this lemma cites Stacks 05YQ, which stands under the `Let d ≥ 1 be an integer` of Section 97.13 (Stacks 05YL)

declarations.name: Stacks.Thickenings.etale_of_isKerBaseChange
declarations.doc:
Let

```
X --f--→ Y
|        |
i        j
↓        ↓
X' -f'-→ Y'
```

be a commutative square of schemes with `i` and `j` closed immersions. If the kernel ideal
sheaf of `j` has square zero, the kernel ideal sheaf of `i` is the base change along `f'` of the
kernel ideal sheaf of `j`, and `f` is étale, then `f'` is étale. The two hypotheses on `j`
together say that `j` is a first-order thickening, `Stacks.Thickenings.IsFirstOrderThickening`;
nothing is assumed about the order of `i`, nor that either closed immersion is surjective on
points.
declarations.comment:
The scheme-level form: on a commutative square of schemes with closed immersions
`i : X ⟶ X'` and `j : Y ⟶ Y'`, square-zero kernel ideal sheaf for `j` and the kernel ideal of
`i` the base change along `f'` of that of `j`, étaleness of `f` gives étaleness of `f'`. The
affine-local content on each pair of affine opens is the lemma itself, which is already proved
for ring maps as `Algebra.Etale.of_ker_sq_eq_bot_of_isBaseChange`; what is proved here is the
reduction of the scheme statement to it.

declarations.name: Algebra.Etale.of_ker_sq_eq_bot_of_isBaseChange
declarations.doc:
Let `A' → A` and `B' → B` be surjective ring maps forming a commutative square with `A' → B'`
and `A → B`, and write `I = ker (A' → A)`, `J = ker (B' → B)`. If `I` has square zero, `A → B` is
étale, and `J` is the base change of `I` along `A' → B'` (`J = I ⊗_A B`), then `A' → B'` is étale.
declarations.statement:
theorem Algebra.Etale.of_ker_sq_eq_bot_of_isBaseChange
    {A' A B' B : Type*} [CommRing A'] [CommRing A] [CommRing B'] [CommRing B]
    [Algebra A' A] [Algebra A' B'] [Algebra A' B] [Algebra A B] [Algebra B' B]
    [IsScalarTower A' A B] [IsScalarTower A' B' B] [Algebra.Etale A B]
    (hA : Function.Surjective (algebraMap A' A)) (hB : Function.Surjective (algebraMap B' B))
    (hI : RingHom.ker (algebraMap A' A) ^ 2 = ⊥)
    (f : RingHom.ker (algebraMap A' A) →ₗ[A'] RingHom.ker (algebraMap B' B))
    (hf : ∀ x, (f x : B') = algebraMap A' B' (x : A')) (hbc : IsBaseChange B' f) :
    Algebra.Etale A' B'
declarations.comment:
The source's `J = I ⊗_A B` is spelled as bijectivity of the canonical map
`B' ⊗[A'] I → J`, i.e. as `IsBaseChange B' f` for the map `f : I → J` induced by `A' → B'`;
tensoring over `A'` rather than `A` avoids the `A`-module structure on `I`, which is unavailable
to typeclass inference, and asks for the same thing (see the module docstring). The source's
hypothesis `J ^ 2 = ⊥` is dropped: it follows from `hI` and the surjectivity half of `hbc`.

declarations.name: Stacks.AffineFromUniversallyClosed.isAffine_of_surjective_universallyClosed
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 05YU].** A scheme admitting a surjective universally closed morphism from an
affine scheme is affine.

By the reduction above the morphism is integral over a separated, quasi-compact and
quasi-separated base, so `f_* 𝒪_X` is an integral quasi-coherent sheaf of `𝒪_S`-algebras.  Part
(1) of [Stacks, Tag 0817] presents it as a directed colimit of finite quasi-coherent
subalgebras, indexed in the universe of the scheme, and the relative spectrum turns that colimit
into an inverse system of schemes finite over `S` whose limit is `X`.  One stage of that system
is affine by [Stacks, Tag 01Z6], and is surjective over `S` because `f` factors through it, so
[Stacks, Tag 01ZT] applies to it.
declarations.statement:
theorem isAffine_of_surjective_universallyClosed [IsAffine X] [Surjective f]
    [UniversallyClosed f] : IsAffine S

declarations.name: Stacks.Thickenings.firstOrderThickening_squareZeroExtension
declarations.doc: Every first-order thickening over a base is obtained from a square-zero extension.
declarations.statement:
public theorem firstOrderThickening_squareZeroExtension {X Y S : Scheme.{u}}
    (i : X ⟶ Y) (g : Y ⟶ S) (hi : Stacks.Thickenings.IsFirstOrderThickening i) :
    ∃ E : SquareZeroExtension (i ≫ g),
      ∃ r : Realization E, r.ambient = Y ∧ HEq r.immersion i ∧ HEq r.toBase g
declarations.comment: converse: every first-order thickening has this form

declarations.name: Stacks.Etale.affineEtalePullback_isEquivalence_of_essSurj_of_h09YZ
declarations.doc:
**Topological invariance of the étale site on affine objects.** Base change along a universal
homeomorphism `f : X ⟶ Y` restricts to an equivalence between the full subcategory of affine
objects of the small étale site of `Y` and the full subcategory of affine objects of the small
étale site of `X`.

The hypothesis `hessSurj` is essential surjectivity of base change on the whole small étale
site, part of Stacks Project, Tag 04DZ, and `h09YZ` is Stacks Project, Tag 09YZ over a
quasi-compact quasi-separated base, the input of Stacks Project, Tag 05YU.
declarations.statement:
theorem affineEtalePullback_isEquivalence_of_essSurj_of_h09YZ
    {X Y : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ Y) [UniversalHomeomorphism f]
    (hessSurj :
      letI : MorphismProperty.HasPullbacksAlong
          (@Etale : MorphismProperty Scheme.{u}) f := ⟨fun _ _ ↦ inferInstance⟩
      letI : MorphismProperty.IsStableUnderBaseChangeAlong
          (@Etale : MorphismProperty Scheme.{u}) f :=
        ⟨fun pb hg ↦ MorphismProperty.IsStableUnderBaseChange.of_isPullback pb hg⟩
      (show Y.Etale ⥤ X.Etale from
        MorphismProperty.Over.pullback
          (@Etale : MorphismProperty Scheme.{u}) ⊤ f).EssSurj)
    (h09YZ : IntegralHasFinitePresentationLimit.{u}) :
    letI : MorphismProperty.HasPullbacksAlong
        (@Etale : MorphismProperty Scheme.{u}) f :=
      ⟨fun _ _ ↦ inferInstance⟩
    letI : MorphismProperty.IsStableUnderBaseChangeAlong
        (@Etale : MorphismProperty Scheme.{u}) f :=
      ⟨fun pb hg ↦
        MorphismProperty.IsStableUnderBaseChange.of_isPullback pb hg⟩
    let F : Y.Etale ⥤ X.Etale :=
      MorphismProperty.Over.pullback
        (@Etale : MorphismProperty Scheme.{u}) ⊤ f
    let PY : ObjectProperty Y.Etale := fun V ↦ IsAffine V.left
    let PX : ObjectProperty X.Etale := fun U ↦ IsAffine U.left
    ∃ (h : ∀ V : PY.FullSubcategory, PX (F.obj V.obj)),
      (PX.lift (PY.ι ⋙ F) h).IsEquivalence
declarations.comment:
assuming essential surjectivity of etale pullback (the content of Stacks 04DZ)
and Stacks 09YZ over a qcqs base

declarations.name: Stacks.Etale.affineEtalePullback_isEquivalence_of_universalHomeomorphism
declarations.doc:
**Topological invariance of the étale site on affine objects.** Let `f : X ⟶ Y` be a universal
homeomorphism. Base change `V ↦ X ×_Y V` along `f` carries an affine scheme étale over `Y` to an
affine scheme étale over `X`, and the induced functor from the full subcategory of affine objects
of the small étale site of `Y` to the full subcategory of affine objects of the small étale site
of `X` is an equivalence.
declarations.statement:
theorem affineEtalePullback_isEquivalence_of_universalHomeomorphism
    {X Y : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ Y) [UniversalHomeomorphism f] :
    letI : MorphismProperty.HasPullbacksAlong
        (@Etale : MorphismProperty Scheme.{u}) f :=
      ⟨fun _ _ ↦ inferInstance⟩
    letI : MorphismProperty.IsStableUnderBaseChangeAlong
        (@Etale : MorphismProperty Scheme.{u}) f :=
      ⟨fun pb hg ↦
        MorphismProperty.IsStableUnderBaseChange.of_isPullback pb hg⟩
    let F : Y.Etale ⥤ X.Etale :=
      MorphismProperty.Over.pullback
        (@Etale : MorphismProperty Scheme.{u}) ⊤ f
    let PY : ObjectProperty Y.Etale := fun V ↦ IsAffine V.left
    let PX : ObjectProperty X.Etale := fun U ↦ IsAffine U.left
    ∃ (h : ∀ V : PY.FullSubcategory, PX (F.obj V.obj)),
      (PX.lift (PY.ι ⋙ F) h).IsEquivalence
declarations.comment:
base change along a universal homeomorphism restricts to an equivalence between
the affine schemes etale over the target and the affine schemes etale over the source

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.presentationPullbackIso
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 05YY.** Let `φ : U ⟶ X` be a morphism of algebraic spaces with `R = U ×_X U` and
`t, s : R ⟶ U` the two projections, as for a presentation of `X` by a surjective étale `φ`. For
a sheaf `ℱ` on the small étale site of `X`, the sheaf `𝒢 = φ⁻¹ℱ` on the small étale site of `U`
carries a canonical isomorphism

`α : t⁻¹𝒢 ⟶ s⁻¹𝒢`,

natural in `ℱ`.

It is the identification of the two iterated inverse images along `(t, φ)` and along `(s, φ)`,
whose composites agree because `R` is the fibre product of `φ` with itself.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def presentationPullbackIso (φ : U ⟶ X) (s t : R ⟶ U)
    (hR : IsPullback t s φ φ) :
    smallEtaleSheafInverseImage B S hS φ ⋙ smallEtaleSheafInverseImage B S hS t ≅
      smallEtaleSheafInverseImage B S hS φ ⋙ smallEtaleSheafInverseImage B S hS s
declarations.comment: the canonical isomorphism and its cocycle condition

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.presentationPullbackIsoApp
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 05YY.** The isomorphism

`α : t⁻¹𝒢 ⟶ s⁻¹𝒢`

canonically attached to the sheaf `𝒢 = φ⁻¹ℱ`, for `φ : U ⟶ X` with `R = U ×_X U` and
`t, s : R ⟶ U` the two projections, as for a presentation of `X` by a surjective étale `φ`.

By construction it is the value at `ℱ` of the natural isomorphism
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.presentationPullbackIso`.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def presentationPullbackIsoApp (φ : U ⟶ X) (s t : R ⟶ U)
    (hR : IsPullback t s φ φ) (F : smallEtaleSheafCat B S hS X) :
    (smallEtaleSheafInverseImage B S hS t).obj
        ((smallEtaleSheafInverseImage B S hS φ).obj F) ≅
      (smallEtaleSheafInverseImage B S hS s).obj
        ((smallEtaleSheafInverseImage B S hS φ).obj F)
declarations.comment: the canonical isomorphism and its cocycle condition

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.presentationPullbackIsoApp_cocycle
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 05YY.** The cocycle condition on `α`. Let `R₂ = R ×_{s, U, t} R` be the fibre
product of `s` and `t`, with projections `pr₀` and `pr₁`, and let `c : R₂ ⟶ R` be the
composition law of the groupoid, so that `c` has the target of the first arrow and the source of
the second. Then the pentagon

`pr₀⁻¹t⁻¹𝒢 → pr₀⁻¹s⁻¹𝒢 = pr₁⁻¹t⁻¹𝒢 → pr₁⁻¹s⁻¹𝒢 = c⁻¹s⁻¹𝒢`,
`pr₀⁻¹t⁻¹𝒢 = c⁻¹t⁻¹𝒢 → c⁻¹s⁻¹𝒢`

commutes: its three arrows are `pr₀⁻¹α`, `pr₁⁻¹α` and `c⁻¹α`, and its three equalities are the
canonical identifications of iterated inverse images along pairs with the same composite.

This is `CategoryTheory.compIsoOfEqApp_cocycle` for the small étale inverse images, whose
associativity coherence is
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.smallToposMorphism_comp_inverseImage_assoc`.
declarations.statement:
theorem presentationPullbackIsoApp_cocycle (φ : U ⟶ X) (s t : R ⟶ U) (hR : IsPullback t s φ φ)
    (pr₀ pr₁ c : R₂ ⟶ R) (hR₂ : IsPullback pr₀ pr₁ s t) (hct : pr₀ ≫ t = c ≫ t)
    (hcs : pr₁ ≫ s = c ≫ s) (F : smallEtaleSheafCat B S hS X) :
    (smallEtaleSheafInverseImage B S hS pr₀).map
          (presentationPullbackIsoApp B S hS φ s t hR F).hom ≫
        (inverseImageCompIsoOfEqApp B S hS pr₀ pr₁ s t hR₂.w
          ((smallEtaleSheafInverseImage B S hS φ).obj F)).hom ≫
        (smallEtaleSheafInverseImage B S hS pr₁).map
          (presentationPullbackIsoApp B S hS φ s t hR F).hom ≫
        (inverseImageCompIsoOfEqApp B S hS pr₁ c s s hcs
          ((smallEtaleSheafInverseImage B S hS φ).obj F)).hom =
      (inverseImageCompIsoOfEqApp B S hS pr₀ c t t hct
          ((smallEtaleSheafInverseImage B S hS φ).obj F)).hom ≫
        (smallEtaleSheafInverseImage B S hS c).map
          (presentationPullbackIsoApp B S hS φ s t hR F).hom
declarations.comment: the canonical isomorphism and its cocycle condition

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.SpacesEtale.isEquivalence_toPresentationDescentData
declarations.doc:
Let `X` be an algebraic space over a scheme `S`, let `φ : U ⟶ X` be a
surjective étale morphism and let `(U, R, s, t, c, e, i)` be the groupoid of the presentation
`X = U/R`, so that `R = U ×_X U` with `t` and `s` the two projections and `c` the composition
law on `R₂ = R ×_{s, U, t} R`. Then the functor taking a sheaf `ℱ` on the small étale site of
`X` to the pair `(𝒢, α)`, where `𝒢 = φ⁻¹ℱ` is a sheaf on the small étale site of `U` and
`α : t⁻¹𝒢 ⟶ s⁻¹𝒢` is the canonical isomorphism, is an equivalence of categories onto the
category of such pairs: pairs of a sheaf on the small étale site of `U` and an isomorphism
`t⁻¹𝒢 ⟶ s⁻¹𝒢` whose pentagon over `R₂` commutes, with morphisms the maps of sheaves commuting
with those isomorphisms.
declarations.statement:
theorem isEquivalence_toPresentationDescentData
    (hsurj : IsSurjective B S hS Uo.obj.hom.hom) :
    (toPresentationDescentData B S hS t s hR pr₀ pr₁ c hR₂ hct hcs).IsEquivalence
declarations.comment: the equivalence of categories

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.existsUnique_spaceHom_twoIso_of_smallEtaleRingedToposIso
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 05YZ.** Let `X` and `Y` be algebraic spaces over `ℤ`, and let
`(g, g♯) : (Sh(X_étale), 𝒪_X) ⟶ (Sh(Y_étale), 𝒪_Y)` be an isomorphism of ringed topoi: its
direct image is an equivalence and `g♯ : 𝒪_Y ⟶ g_*𝒪_X` is an isomorphism.  Then there is a
unique morphism `f : X ⟶ Y` of algebraic spaces such that `(g, g♯)` is 2-isomorphic to
`(f_small, f♯)` — the morphism of small étale ringed topoi
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.smallEtaleRingedToposHom` of Stacks 03G8, a 2-isomorphism being one of
Stacks 04IC — and that morphism is an isomorphism of algebraic spaces.

As in the source, the existence and uniqueness is Stacks 04KL
(`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.existsUnique_spaceHom_twoIso_of_isLocallyRinged`), applicable because
`(g, g♯)` is a morphism of locally ringed topoi
(`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isLocallyRinged_of_smallEtaleRingedToposIso`).  For the last clause,
Stacks 04KL applied to the inverse of `(g, g♯)` and to the inverse of that gives `f'` and `f''`,
and `AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isIso_of_twoIso_of_inverse` shows that `f` is invertible.
declarations.statement:
theorem existsUnique_spaceHom_twoIso_of_smallEtaleRingedToposIso (B : BigFppfSite.{u})
    (hZ : B.Contains (Spec (CommRingCat.of (ULift.{u} ℤ))))
    {X Y : AlgebraicSpaces B (Spec (CommRingCat.of (ULift.{u} ℤ))) hZ}
    (g : RingedToposHom (smallEtaleRingedTopos B (Spec (CommRingCat.of (ULift.{u} ℤ))) hZ X)
      (smallEtaleRingedTopos B (Spec (CommRingCat.of (ULift.{u} ℤ))) hZ Y))
    [g.toToposHom.pushforward.IsEquivalence] [IsIso g.fSharp] :
    (∃! f : X ⟶ Y, Nonempty (RingedToposHom.TwoIso.{u, u + 1, u, u, u + 1, u} g
      (smallEtaleRingedToposHom B (Spec (CommRingCat.of (ULift.{u} ℤ))) hZ f))) ∧
    ∀ f : X ⟶ Y, Nonempty (RingedToposHom.TwoIso.{u, u + 1, u, u, u + 1, u} g
      (smallEtaleRingedToposHom B (Spec (CommRingCat.of (ULift.{u} ℤ))) hZ f)) → IsIso f

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.existsUnique_spaceHom_twoIso_of_smallEtaleRingedToposIso'
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks Project, Tag 05YZ], the clause about `f`.**  If `g` is a morphism of the small
étale ringed topoi of `X` and `Y` whose direct image is an equivalence and whose structure map
is an isomorphism, and `g` is 2-compatible with a pair of structure morphisms `pX : X ⟶ A`,
`pY : Y ⟶ A`, then there is exactly one morphism of algebraic spaces `f : X ⟶ Y` with `g`
2-isomorphic to the morphism of small étale ringed topoi of `f`.

This is `AlgebraicGeometry.Space.IsRecoveredFromSmallEtaleOver` at `A`, supplied by
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isRecoveredFromSmallEtale_holds`, applied to `g`: the hypothesis that
`g` is locally ringed is `AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isLocallyRinged_of_smallEtaleRingedToposIso`,
and the two 2-isomorphisms are read in the opposite direction from
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.InducesSmallEtaleRingedToposHom`.

Only the source's clause about `f` is registered here; its further clause that `f` is an
isomorphism of algebraic spaces lies outside this statement.

The 2-compatibility `hbase` is not optional: the source states Stacks 05YZ for algebraic spaces
over `Spec(ℤ)`, where `f` is an absolute morphism, whereas `f : X ⟶ Y` here is a morphism over
`S`.  Without it the conclusion is false — see the σ-twist counterexample recorded with
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.IsRecoveredFromSmallEtale`.  Since
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.baseSpace` is terminal, `hbase` can always be asked of the structure
morphisms to the base itself.
declarations.statement:
theorem existsUnique_spaceHom_twoIso_of_smallEtaleRingedToposIso' {A : AlgebraicSpaces B S hS}
    (pX : X ⟶ A) (pY : Y ⟶ A)
    (g : RingedToposHom (smallEtaleRingedTopos B S hS X) (smallEtaleRingedTopos B S hS Y))
    [g.toToposHom.pushforward.IsEquivalence] [IsIso g.fSharp]
    (hbase : Nonempty (SmallEtaleTwoIso B S hS
      (smallEtaleComp B S hS (smallEtaleRingedToposHom B S hS pY) g)
      (smallEtaleRingedToposHom B S hS pX))) :
    ∃! f : X ⟶ Y, Nonempty (RingedToposHom.TwoIso.{u, u + 1, u, u, u + 1, u} g
      (smallEtaleRingedToposHom B S hS f))
declarations.comment: the clause about f ALONE: its existence and uniqueness, together with the 2-isomorphism of (g, g sharp) with (f_small, f sharp) (Stacks 04IC). Stacks 04KL over a base, which the existence needs, is isRecoveredFromSmallEtale_holds. The source's further clause that f is an ISOMORPHISM of algebraic spaces lies outside this registration. NARROWER than the source in one further respect: the source states 05YZ for spaces over Spec(Z), where f is an absolute morphism and no compatibility is asked of (g, g sharp), while f here is a morphism over S, so the 2-compatibility hbase is assumed in addition -- it is what Stacks 04SG supplies, and without it the conclusion is FALSE

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.morphismToAffineEquiv
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 05Z1.** Pullback of regular functions is a bijection between morphisms of
algebraic spaces `X ⟶ T` into an affine object of the site and ring homomorphisms
`Γ(T, 𝒪_T) →+* Γ(X, 𝒪_X)`.

The bijection is specified, not merely asserted: its forward map restricts on every étale
scheme chart of `X` to pullback of regular functions along the induced morphism of schemes.
declarations.statement:
def morphismToAffineEquiv (X : AlgebraicSpaces B S hS) (T : BigFppfOver B S hS)
    (hterminal : IsTerminal S) [IsAffine ((BigFppfOver.toScheme B S hS).obj T)] :
    { e : (X ⟶ schemeSpace T) ≃
        (Γ((BigFppfOver.toScheme B S hS).obj T, ⊤) →+* globalFunctions B S hS X.1) //
      ∀ (f : X ⟶ schemeSpace T) (U : SmallEtale B S hS X.1)
        (s : Γ((BigFppfOver.toScheme B S hS).obj T, ⊤)),
        ((e f) s).1 (op U) = Scheme.Γ.map (op ((BigFppfOver.toScheme B S hS).map
          (yoneda.preimage (U.1.hom ≫ f.hom)))) s }

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isSeparated_of_isSurjective_of_universallyClosed
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 05Z2, part (4).** Let `X ⟶ Y ⟶ T` be morphisms of algebraic spaces over `S`, with
`X ⟶ Y` surjective and universally closed. If `X` is separated over `T`, then so is `Y`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isSeparated_of_isSurjective_of_universallyClosed
    (hX : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS X) (hY : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS Y)
    (hT : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS T) (f : X ⟶ Y) (g : Y ⟶ T)
    (hfsurj : IsSurjective B S hS f) (hfclosed : UniversallyClosed B S hS f)
    (hsep : IsSeparated B S hS (f ≫ g)) :
    IsSeparated B S hS g
declarations.comment: part (4): separated over the base

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isQuasiSeparated_of_isSurjective_of_universallyClosed
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 05Z2, part (3).** Let `X ⟶ Y ⟶ T` be morphisms of algebraic spaces over `S`, with
`X ⟶ Y` surjective and universally closed. If `X` is quasi-separated over `T`, then so is `Y`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isQuasiSeparated_of_isSurjective_of_universallyClosed
    (hX : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS X) (hY : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS Y)
    (hT : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS T) (f : X ⟶ Y) (g : Y ⟶ T)
    (hfsurj : IsSurjective B S hS f) (hfclosed : UniversallyClosed B S hS f)
    (hqs : IsQuasiSeparated B S hS (f ≫ g)) :
    IsQuasiSeparated B S hS g
declarations.comment: part (3): quasi-separated over the base

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isAbsolutelyQuasiSeparated_of_isSurjective_of_universallyClosed
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 05Z2, part (1).** Let `X ⟶ Y` be a surjective universally closed morphism of
algebraic spaces over `S`. If `X` is quasi-separated, then so is `Y`.

This is part (3) over the terminal scheme, as the source says: quasi-separatedness of an
algebraic space is quasi-separatedness over `Spec ℤ` of its lower-shriek extension along
`S ⟶ Spec ℤ`, by Stacks 03BS, and that extension of `X ⟶ Y` is again surjective and universally
closed by `AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isSurjective_relocalize` and
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.universallyClosed_relocalize`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isAbsolutelyQuasiSeparated_of_isSurjective_of_universallyClosed
    (hX : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS X) (hY : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS Y) (f : X ⟶ Y)
    (hfsurj : IsSurjective B S hS f) (hfclosed : UniversallyClosed B S hS f)
    (hqs : IsAbsolutelyQuasiSeparated B S hS hZ X) :
    IsAbsolutelyQuasiSeparated B S hS hZ Y
declarations.comment: part (1): quasi-separated

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isAbsolutelySeparated_of_isSurjective_of_universallyClosed
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 05Z2, part (2).** Let `X ⟶ Y` be a surjective universally closed morphism of
algebraic spaces over `S`. If `X` is separated, then so is `Y`.

This is part (4) over the terminal scheme, as the source says: separatedness of an algebraic
space is separatedness over `Spec ℤ` of its lower-shriek extension along `S ⟶ Spec ℤ`, by
Stacks 03BS, and that extension of `X ⟶ Y` is again surjective and universally closed by
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isSurjective_relocalize` and
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.universallyClosed_relocalize`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isAbsolutelySeparated_of_isSurjective_of_universallyClosed
    (hX : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS X) (hY : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS Y) (f : X ⟶ Y)
    (hfsurj : IsSurjective B S hS f) (hfclosed : UniversallyClosed B S hS f)
    (hsep : IsAbsolutelySeparated B S hS hZ X) :
    IsAbsolutelySeparated B S hS hZ Y
declarations.comment: part (2): separated

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.presheaf_universalHomeomorphism_iff
declarations.doc:
A representable morphism of algebraic spaces over `S` has universal
homeomorphy of every one of its represented base changes, which is what being a universal
homeomorphism means for a representable morphism, exactly when it is a universal homeomorphism in
the sense of Stacks 05Z5: every base change of it by an algebraic space over `S` induces a
homeomorphism on the spaces of points.
declarations.statement:
theorem presheaf_universalHomeomorphism_iff
    (hX : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS X) (hY : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS Y) {f : X ⟶ Y}
    (hf : yoneda.relativelyRepresentable f) :
    (MorphismProperty.inverseImage
      (@AlgebraicGeometry.UniversalHomeomorphism.{u} : MorphismProperty Scheme.{u})
      (BigFppfOver.toScheme B S hS)).presheaf f ↔ UniversalHomeomorphism B S hS f

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.UniversalHomeomorphism
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 05Z5.** A morphism of algebraic spaces over `S` is a *universal homeomorphism*
when its base change along every morphism to its target from an algebraic space over `S`
induces a homeomorphism on the spaces of points.
declarations.statement: abbrev UniversalHomeomorphism (f : F ⟶ G) : Prop

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.AffineLineInvolution.nonSeparatedUniversalHomeomorphism_squaringMap
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 05Z6.**  Let `k` be a field in which `2` is invertible, let `B` be a big fppf site
containing `Spec k`, and let `X = 𝐀¹_k/\{x ∼ -x ∣ x ≠ 0\}` be the quotient of the affine line
by the punctured graph of negation.  Then `X` is an algebraic space over `k`, and of the two
morphisms
`𝐀¹_k ⟶ X ⟶ 𝐀¹_k`,
the projection onto the quotient and the morphism descended from squaring the coordinate:

1. the first is surjective and étale;
2. the second is universally injective;
3. their composition is the map `x ↦ x²`;
4. hence that composition is universally closed;
5. therefore the second morphism is a universal homeomorphism;
6. but the second morphism is not separated.

The projection is surjective and étale because the relation is an étale equivalence relation
whose morphism into the self-product of the affine line is affine, which makes the presentation
of Stacks 0265 unconditional here.  Squaring is injective on field-valued points up to the
relation and integral on the affine line, which gives (2) and (4); a universally injective,
universally closed and surjective morphism of algebraic spaces is a universal homeomorphism,
which gives (5).  For (6) the relation is a represented base change of the relative diagonal of
the squaring map and is not a closed immersion, its restriction to the punctured summand
factoring through the split section of the fibre square with components the identity and
negation.
declarations.statement:
theorem nonSeparatedUniversalHomeomorphism_squaringMap (hchar : (2 : k) ≠ 0) :
    IsAlgebraicSpace B (Spec (.of k)) hk (involutionQuotient k B hk).obj ∧
      (MorphismProperty.inverseImage (@Surjective.{u} : MorphismProperty Scheme.{u})
            (BigFppfOver.toScheme B (Spec (.of k)) hk)).presheaf
          (Stacks.Groupoids.toQuotientSheaf (BigFppfOver.topology B (Spec (.of k)) hk)
            (Over.post (X := B.obj hk) B.inclusion) (involutionRelation k)) ∧
      (MorphismProperty.inverseImage (@Etale.{u} : MorphismProperty Scheme.{u})
            (BigFppfOver.toScheme B (Spec (.of k)) hk)).presheaf
          (Stacks.Groupoids.toQuotientSheaf (BigFppfOver.topology B (Spec (.of k)) hk)
            (Over.post (X := B.obj hk) B.inclusion) (involutionRelation k)) ∧
      Space.UniversallyInjective B (Spec (.of k)) hk (squaringMap k B hk) ∧
      Stacks.Groupoids.toQuotientSheaf (BigFppfOver.topology B (Spec (.of k)) hk)
            (Over.post (X := B.obj hk) B.inclusion) (involutionRelation k) ≫
          squaringMap k B hk =
        (Over.post (X := B.obj hk) B.inclusion).op.whiskerLeft
          (yoneda.map (affineLineSquare k)) ∧
      Space.UniversallyClosed B (Spec (.of k)) hk
          (Stacks.Groupoids.toQuotientSheaf (BigFppfOver.topology B (Spec (.of k)) hk)
              (Over.post (X := B.obj hk) B.inclusion) (involutionRelation k) ≫
            squaringMap k B hk) ∧
      Space.UniversalHomeomorphism B (Spec (.of k)) hk (squaringMap k B hk) ∧
      ¬ Space.IsSeparated B (Spec (.of k)) hk (squaringMap k B hk)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.universallyClosed_toQuotientSheaf_comp_squaringMap
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 05Z6.** The composite of the projection onto the quotient of the affine line by
the punctured involution relation with the descended squaring map of Stacks 05VS is
universally closed.

The composite is, through
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.toQuotientSheaf_comp_squaringMap_eq_conj`, the morphism of
represented presheaves induced by squaring of the coordinate. Squaring is an integral morphism
of schemes, hence a universally closed one, so the induced morphism of presheaves is
universally closed after every represented base change, and Stacks 03XD turns that into
universal closedness in the sense of Stacks 03HI. No assumption on the characteristic is
needed.
declarations.statement:
theorem universallyClosed_toQuotientSheaf_comp_squaringMap (hk : B.Contains (Spec (.of k)))
    [HasSheafify (BigFppfOver.topology B (Spec (.of k)) hk) (Type u)] :
    UniversallyClosed B (Spec (.of k)) hk
      (Stacks.Groupoids.toQuotientSheaf (BigFppfOver.topology B (Spec (.of k)) hk)
          (Over.post (X := B.obj hk) B.inclusion) (involutionRelation k) ≫
        squaringMap k B hk)
declarations.comment: closed_squaring

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.universalHomeomorphism_squaringMap
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 05ZI, the last sentence: there is a universal homeomorphism `X ⟶ 𝐀¹_k`, exhibited
directly by `t ↦ t ^ 2` on affine space.**

Here `X` is the quotient of the affine line by the relation identifying `t` with `-t` away from
the origin, the algebraic space of Stacks 05Z6, and the morphism is the one Stacks 05VS
descends from squaring the coordinate. It is universally closed by
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.universallyClosed_squaringMap`, universally injective by Stacks 05VS
part (4), and surjective after every base change by
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isSurjective_pullback_fst_squaringMap`; the criterion is
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.universalHomeomorphism_of_universallyClosed_of_universallyInjective`.

Stacks 05Z6 and Stacks 05ZI state this over an algebraically closed field of characteristic
zero. Only `2 ≠ 0` in `k` is used, and only for universal injectivity.
declarations.statement:
theorem universalHomeomorphism_squaringMap (hchar : (2 : k) ≠ 0)
    (hk : B.Contains (Spec (.of k)))
    [HasSheafify (BigFppfOver.topology B (Spec (.of k)) hk) (Type u)] :
    UniversalHomeomorphism B (Spec (.of k)) hk (squaringMap k B hk)
declarations.comment: universal_homeomorphism: the map X ⟶ 𝐀¹_k is a universal homeomorphism

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isSheafOfDifferentialsMap_comp
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 05Z7**, the characterization: for two stacked commutative squares, the composite
`c_g ∘ g^*c_f` of the comparison maps of the inner squares, read through the comparison
`(g ≫ f)^* ≅ g^*f^*` of inverse images of Stacks 03LU, has the characterizing property of
Stacks 04CX for the outer square.
declarations.statement:
theorem isSheafOfDifferentialsMap_comp (f : X' ⟶ X) (g : X'' ⟶ X') (p : X ⟶ Y) (p' : X' ⟶ Y')
    (p'' : X'' ⟶ Y'')
    {cf : (modulePullback B S hS f).obj (sheafOfDifferentials B S hS p) ⟶
      sheafOfDifferentials B S hS p'}
    {cg : (modulePullback B S hS g).obj (sheafOfDifferentials B S hS p') ⟶
      sheafOfDifferentials B S hS p''}
    (hf : IsSheafOfDifferentialsMap B S hS f p p' cf)
    (hg : IsSheafOfDifferentialsMap B S hS g p' p'' cg) :
    IsSheafOfDifferentialsMap B S hS (g ≫ f) p p''
      ((modulePullbackCompIso B S hS g f).inv.app (sheafOfDifferentials B S hS p) ≫
        (modulePullback B S hS g).map cf ≫ cg)
declarations.comment: the composite satisfies the characterization of `c_{g ≫ f}`

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.eq_comp_of_isSheafOfDifferentialsMap
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 05Z7.**  The comparison maps of Stacks 04CX compose: for two stacked commutative
squares with top edges `g : X'' ⟶ X'` and `f : X' ⟶ X`, the comparison map of the outer square
is the comparison map of the inner right square pulled back along `g`, followed by the
comparison map of the inner left square, the two being composable through the comparison
`(g ≫ f)^* ≅ g^*f^*` of Stacks 03LU.  Each of the three comparison maps appears through its
characterizing property of Stacks 04CX, which determines it uniquely.
declarations.statement:
theorem eq_comp_of_isSheafOfDifferentialsMap (f : X' ⟶ X) (g : X'' ⟶ X') (p : X ⟶ Y)
    (p' : X' ⟶ Y') (p'' : X'' ⟶ Y'')
    {c : (modulePullback B S hS (g ≫ f)).obj (sheafOfDifferentials B S hS p) ⟶
      sheafOfDifferentials B S hS p''}
    {cf : (modulePullback B S hS f).obj (sheafOfDifferentials B S hS p) ⟶
      sheafOfDifferentials B S hS p'}
    {cg : (modulePullback B S hS g).obj (sheafOfDifferentials B S hS p') ⟶
      sheafOfDifferentials B S hS p''}
    (hc : IsSheafOfDifferentialsMap B S hS (g ≫ f) p p'' c)
    (hf : IsSheafOfDifferentialsMap B S hS f p p' cf)
    (hg : IsSheafOfDifferentialsMap B S hS g p' p'' cg) :
    c = (modulePullbackCompIso B S hS g f).inv.app (sheafOfDifferentials B S hS p) ≫
      (modulePullback B S hS g).map cf ≫ cg

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.triangleDifferentials_epi
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 05Z8**, exactness at the right term of the transitivity sequence
`f^*Ω_{Y/B} ⟶ Ω_{X/B} ⟶ Ω_{X/Y} ⟶ 0`: the canonical map `Ω_{X/B} ⟶ Ω_{X/Y}` is an epimorphism.

Two morphisms out of `Ω_{X/Y}` agreeing after it agree on every `d_{X/Y}(t)`, because
`d_{X/B}(t)` is carried to `d_{X/Y}(t)`, so they are equal by the uniqueness half of
Stacks 04CT.
declarations.statement:
theorem triangleDifferentials_epi (f : X ⟶ Y) (g : Y ⟶ Z) :
    Epi (toRelativeDifferentials B S hS f g)
declarations.comment: exactness at the right term: the map to Ω_{X/Y} is an epimorphism

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.triangleDifferentials_exact
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 05Z8**, the two clauses of the transitivity sequence
`f^*Ω_{Y/B} ⟶ Ω_{X/B} ⟶ Ω_{X/Y} ⟶ 0` that concern its left half: the composite of the two maps
is zero, and the resulting short complex is exact at `Ω_{X/B}`.  Together with
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.triangleDifferentials_epi`, which is exactness at `Ω_{X/Y}`, this is
the exactness of the whole sequence.

Both come from `AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isColimitCokernelCoforkToRelativeDifferentials`: the
cokernel cofork carries the vanishing of the composite, and
`CategoryTheory.ShortComplex.exact_of_g_is_cokernel` turns the colimit into exactness in the
middle.  The homology of the short complex is formed in the abelian category of `𝒪_X`-modules;
the instance that makes it abelian is `HasSheafify` for abelian sheaves on the small étale
site, which instance search does not find at the projection
`(AlgebraicGeometry.Space.smallEtaleRingedSite B S hS X.1 X.2).J` of the ringed site, exactly as
for `AlgebraicGeometry.Space.smallEtaleRingedSite_hasWeakSheafify`.
declarations.statement:
theorem triangleDifferentials_exact (f : X ⟶ Y) (g : Y ⟶ Z) :
    ∃ h : pullbackDifferentialsMap B S hS f g ≫ toRelativeDifferentials B S hS f g = 0,
      (ShortComplex.mk _ _ h).Exact
declarations.comment: the composite of the two maps is zero, and exactness at the middle term Ω_{X/B}

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isZero_sheafOfDifferentials_of_isLocallySurjective
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 05Z9**, with local surjectivity of the structure map in place of the hypothesis
that `f` is an immersion.  If `f♯ : f⁻¹𝒪_Y ⟶ 𝒪_X` is locally surjective then `Ω_{X/Y}` is zero.

`Ω_{X/Y}` corepresents the functor of `Y`-derivations, and by
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.derivation_eq_of_isLocallySurjective` that functor takes at most one
value at each sheaf of `𝒪_X`-modules; so the identity and the zero endomorphism of `Ω_{X/Y}`
both factor the same derivation and are therefore equal.

An immersion has locally surjective structure map, by
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isLocallySurjective_structureSharpInverseImage_of_isImmersion`, which is
how `AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isZero_sheafOfDifferentials_of_isImmersion_unconditional` reaches
the source's statement.
declarations.statement:
theorem isZero_sheafOfDifferentials_of_isLocallySurjective (f : X ⟶ Y)
    (hsharp : Presheaf.IsLocallySurjective (SmallEtale.topology B S hS X.1)
      (structureSharpInverseImage B S hS f).hom) :
    IsZero (sheafOfDifferentials B S hS f)
declarations.comment:
the vanishing Ω_{X/Y} = 0, from local surjectivity of `f♯`; the gap to the
  source's hypothesis is that an immersion of algebraic spaces has locally surjective structure
  map, which is the inverse-image form of the surjectivity clause of 03MB

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isZero_sheafOfDifferentials_of_isImmersion
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 05Z9.**  If `f : X ⟶ Y` is an immersion of algebraic spaces over `S` then
`Ω_{X/Y}` is zero.

The hypothesis `hsharp` is the one input not proved in this development: the structure map
`f♯ : f⁻¹𝒪_Y ⟶ 𝒪_X` of an immersion of algebraic spaces is locally surjective.  It is the
inverse-image form of the surjectivity clause of Stacks 03MB, which
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isLocallySurjective_structureSharp` supplies only in the direct-image
form `𝒪_Y ⟶ f_*𝒪_X` and only for closed immersions, and it is carried here universally
quantified over all immersions of algebraic spaces over `S`.

That input is no longer unproved: it is
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isLocallySurjective_structureSharpInverseImage_of_isImmersion` above, so
the hypothesis-free form of this statement is
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isZero_sheafOfDifferentials_of_isImmersion_unconditional`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isZero_sheafOfDifferentials_of_isImmersion
    (hsharp : ∀ (X' Y' : AlgebraicSpaces B S hS) (g : X' ⟶ Y'), IsImmersion B S hS g.hom →
      Presheaf.IsLocallySurjective (SmallEtale.topology B S hS X'.1)
        (structureSharpInverseImage B S hS g).hom)
    (f : X ⟶ Y) (hf : IsImmersion B S hS f.hom) :
    IsZero (sheafOfDifferentials B S hS f)
declarations.comment:
the source's statement, carrying local surjectivity of the structure map of an
  immersion (the inverse-image form of the surjectivity clause of 03MB) as `hsharp`, quantified
  over all immersions of algebraic spaces over `S`

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isZero_sheafOfDifferentials_of_isImmersion_unconditional
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 05Z9.**  If `f : X ⟶ Y` is an immersion of algebraic spaces over `S` then
`Ω_{X/Y}` is zero, with no hypothesis beyond the immersion.

The structure map `f♯ : f⁻¹𝒪_Y ⟶ 𝒪_X` of an immersion is locally surjective
(`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isLocallySurjective_structureSharpInverseImage_of_isImmersion`), and
local surjectivity forces the vanishing
(`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isZero_sheafOfDifferentials_of_isLocallySurjective`).  This is
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isZero_sheafOfDifferentials_of_isImmersion` with its hypothesis
`hsharp` discharged.
declarations.statement:
theorem isZero_sheafOfDifferentials_of_isImmersion_unconditional (f : X ⟶ Y)
    (hf : IsImmersion B S hS f.hom) :
    IsZero (sheafOfDifferentials B S hS f)
declarations.comment: the source's statement: the sheaf of differentials of an immersion of algebraic spaces over `S` is a zero object, with no hypothesis beyond the immersion

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.conormalSequenceFirstMap_comp_pullbackDifferentialsMap
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 05ZA, the composite of the two arrows is zero.**  For a closed subspace `Z` of an
algebraic space `X` over `Bb`, with inclusion `i : Z ⟶ X`, the sequence
```
  𝒞_{Z/X} ⟶ i^*Ω_{X/Bb} ⟶ Ω_{Z/Bb}
```
is a complex.

This is
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.conormalSequenceIdealPullbackMap_comp_pullbackDifferentialsMap` with the
source of the first arrow read as the conormal module, which it is by
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.conormalModule_eq`.
declarations.statement:
theorem conormalSequenceFirstMap_comp_pullbackDifferentialsMap
    (Z : ClosedSubspaces B S hS X.1) (b : X ⟶ Bb) :
    conormalSequenceFirstMap B S hS Z b ≫
        pullbackDifferentialsMap B S hS (subspaceInclusion B S hS X Z) b = 0
declarations.comment: the composite of the two arrows is zero, so the sequence `𝒞_{Z/X} ⟶ i^*Ω_{X/Bb} ⟶ Ω_{Z/Bb}` is a complex, for a closed subspace. Unconditional

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.conormalSequenceFirstMap_comp_pullbackDifferentialsMap_eq_zero
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 05ZA, the composite of the two arrows is zero**, read at
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.conormalSequenceFirstMap`, that is with the source of the first arrow
written as the conormal module `𝒞_{Z/X}` of Stacks 04CN rather than as `i^*𝓘`.  The two readings
are the same morphism, by `AlgebraicGeometry.Space.conormalModule_eq`.

This is the shape in which the clause is consumed: it is the `hzero` hypothesis carried by
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.thickeningConormalSequence_exact` of Stacks 060F and by
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.epi_thickeningConormalFirstMap` of Stacks 060G.
declarations.statement:
theorem conormalSequenceFirstMap_comp_pullbackDifferentialsMap_eq_zero
    (Z : ClosedSubspaces B S hS Y.1) (b : Y ⟶ Bb) :
    conormalSequenceFirstMap B S hS Z b ≫
      pullbackDifferentialsMap B S hS (subspaceInclusion B S hS Y Z) b = 0
declarations.comment: the composite of the two arrows is zero, at a subspace inclusion, with the first arrow read out of the conormal module `𝒞_{Z/X}` of 04CN.
