The same clause at the first arrow of an arbitrary immersion is `conormalSequenceFirstMapOfImmersion_comp_pullbackDifferentialsMap_eq_zero`

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.conormalSequenceIdealDifferential_val_app_apply
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 05ZA, "the first arrow is induced by `d_{X/B}`".**  The first arrow is by definition
the transpose across `i^* ⊣ i_*` of
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.conormalSequenceIdealDifferential`, and that transpose carries a local
section `a` of the defining ideal sheaf of `Z` to `D(a)`, where `D` is `d_{X/B}` followed by the
unit of the adjunction — which is what
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.conormalSequenceUnitDerivation` is, by its definition.  This equation is
the whole of the arrow's dependence on `d_{X/B}`; since the transposition is a bijection, it
determines the arrow.
declarations.statement:
theorem conormalSequenceIdealDifferential_val_app_apply (Z : ClosedSubspaces B S hS X.1)
    (b : X ⟶ Bb) (U : (SmallEtale B S hS X.1)ᵒᵖ)
    (x : (definingIdealSheaf B S hS X Z).toSheafOfModules.val.obj U) :
    ((conormalSequenceIdealDifferential B S hS Z b).val.app U).hom x =
      (conormalSequenceUnitDerivation B S hS Z b).d x.1
declarations.comment: the first arrow is induced by `d_{X/B}`: the transpose of the first arrow across `i^* ⊣ i_*` carries a section of the defining ideal sheaf to the universal differential of that section, followed by the unit

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.conormalSequenceFirstMap
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 05ZA, the canonical first arrow.**  For a subspace `Z` of an algebraic space
`X` over `B`, with inclusion `i : Z ⟶ X`, the arrow
```
  𝒞_{Z/X} ⟶ i^*Ω_{X/B}
```
induced by `d_{X/B}`.  It is `AlgebraicGeometry.Space.conormalSequenceIdealPullbackMap` with its
source read as the conormal module, which it is by
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.conormalModule_eq`.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def conormalSequenceFirstMap (Z : ClosedSubspaces B S hS X.1) (b : X ⟶ Bb) :
    conormalModule B S hS X Z ⟶
      (modulePullback B S hS (subspaceInclusion B S hS X Z)).obj
        (sheafOfDifferentials B S hS b)
declarations.comment: the canonical first arrow `𝒞_{Z/X} ⟶ i^*Ω_{X/B}` induced by `d_{X/B}`, at a subspace inclusion. The same arrow at an arbitrary immersion is `conormalSequenceFirstMapOfImmersion`

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.epi_pullbackDifferentialsMap_of_isLocallySurjective
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 05ZA, exactness at the right term**, under local surjectivity of the structure map
`i♯ : i⁻¹𝒪_X ⟶ 𝒪_Z`.  The comparison map `c_i : i^*Ω_{X/B} ⟶ Ω_{Z/B}` of Stacks 04CX is an
epimorphism, so the conormal sequence of `i` ends in zero.

Left-cancellation is checked directly: given `g, g'` with equal composites,
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.sheafOfDifferentialsMap_comp_eq_iff` makes them agree on the universal
differentials of the sections in the image of `i♯`; local surjectivity makes every local section
of `𝒪_Z` locally of that form, so the two values agree on a covering sieve and hence are equal,
the target being a sheaf; and `AlgebraicGeometry.Space.sheafOfDifferentials_hom_ext` turns that
into `g = g'`.
declarations.statement:
theorem epi_pullbackDifferentialsMap_of_isLocallySurjective (i : X ⟶ Y) (b : Y ⟶ Bb)
    (hsharp : Presheaf.IsLocallySurjective (SmallEtale.topology B S hS X.1)
      (structureSharpInverseImage B S hS i).hom) :
    Epi (pullbackDifferentialsMap B S hS i b)
declarations.comment: exactness at the right term: the second arrow `i^*Ω_{X/B} ⟶ Ω_{Z/B}` is an epimorphism, carrying local surjectivity of `i♯ : i⁻¹𝒪_X ⟶ 𝒪_Z` (the inverse-image form of the surjectivity clause of 03MB) as `hsharp`

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.epi_pullbackDifferentialsMap_of_isImmersion
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 05ZA, exactness at the right term, for an immersion.**  For an immersion
`i : X ⟶ Y` of algebraic spaces over `B` and a structure morphism `b : Y ⟶ B`, the second arrow
`i^*Ω_{Y/B} ⟶ Ω_{X/B}` of the conormal sequence — the comparison map of Stacks 04CX for the
square over the identity of `B` — is an epimorphism.

This is `AlgebraicGeometry.Space.epi_pullbackDifferentialsMap_of_isLocallySurjective` with its
hypothesis `hsharp` discharged by
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isLocallySurjective_structureSharpInverseImage_of_isImmersion`.
declarations.statement:
theorem epi_pullbackDifferentialsMap_of_isImmersion (i : X ⟶ Y) (b : Y ⟶ Bb)
    (hi : IsImmersion B S hS i.hom) :
    Epi (pullbackDifferentialsMap B S hS i b)
declarations.comment: exactness at the right term: the second arrow `i^*Ω_{X/B} ⟶ Ω_{Z/B}` is an epimorphism for an immersion, with no hypothesis beyond the immersion

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.conormalSequenceFirstMapOfImmersion
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 05ZA, the canonical first arrow, for an arbitrary immersion.**  For an immersion
`i : Z ⟶ X` of algebraic spaces over `B` with structure morphism `b : X ⟶ B`, the arrow
```
  𝒞_{Z/X} ⟶ i^*Ω_{X/B}
```
induced by `d_{X/B}`.

It is `AlgebraicGeometry.Space.kernelConormalFirstMap`, the arrow built from the kernel ideal
sheaf of `i` by restricting `d_{X/B}` followed by the unit of `i^* ⊣ i_*` to it, read out of the
conormal module: `AlgebraicGeometry.Space.conormalAlgebra_piece_one` says the source of that
arrow *is* the degree-one piece of the conormal algebra of `i`, and
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.conormalAlgebraOfImmersionPieceIso` identifies that piece with the
conormal module of the immersion.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def conormalSequenceFirstMapOfImmersion (i : Z ⟶ X)
    (hi : IsImmersion B S hS i.hom) (b : X ⟶ Bb) :
    immersionConormalModule B S hS i hi ⟶
      (modulePullback B S hS i).obj (sheafOfDifferentials B S hS b)
declarations.comment: the canonical first arrow `𝒞_{Z/X} ⟶ i^*Ω_{X/B}` induced by `d_{X/B}`, for an arbitrary immersion

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.conormalSequenceFirstMapOfImmersion_comp_pullbackDifferentialsMap_eq_zero
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 05ZA, the composite of the two arrows is zero, for an arbitrary immersion.**  The
first arrow `𝒞_{Z/X} ⟶ i^*Ω_{X/B}` followed by the second arrow `i^*Ω_{X/B} ⟶ Ω_{Z/B}`, the
comparison map of Stacks 04CX for the square over the identity of `B`, is the zero morphism.

The first arrow factors through
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.kernelConormalFirstMap`, for which the clause is
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.kernelConormalFirstMap_comp_pullbackDifferentialsMap_eq_zero`.
declarations.statement:
theorem conormalSequenceFirstMapOfImmersion_comp_pullbackDifferentialsMap_eq_zero (i : Z ⟶ X)
    (hi : IsImmersion B S hS i.hom) (b : X ⟶ Bb) :
    conormalSequenceFirstMapOfImmersion B S hS i hi b ≫
      pullbackDifferentialsMap B S hS i b = 0
declarations.comment: the composite `𝒞_{Z/X} ⟶ i^*Ω_{X/B} ⟶ Ω_{Z/B}` of the two arrows is zero, for an arbitrary immersion

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.conormalSequenceOfImmersion_exact
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 05ZA, exactness at the middle term, for an arbitrary immersion.**  For an immersion
`i : Z ⟶ X` of algebraic spaces over `B` with structure morphism `b : X ⟶ B`, the sequence
```
  𝒞_{Z/X} ⟶ i^*Ω_{X/B} ⟶ Ω_{Z/B}
```
built from the canonical first arrow
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.conormalSequenceFirstMapOfImmersion` and the second arrow
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.pullbackDifferentialsMap` is exact at `i^*Ω_{X/B}`.

**No hypothesis beyond the immersion is carried.**  It is
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.conormalSequenceKernel_exact_of_isImmersion` fed to
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.conormalSequenceOfImmersion_exact_of_kernelConormalFirstMap`, which
reads the first arrow out of the conormal module `𝒞_{Z/X}` of [Stacks Project, Tag 04CN] rather
than out of the kernel ideal sheaf; the two differ by the isomorphism
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.conormalModuleOfImmersionKernelPullbackIso` of the left-hand terms.
declarations.statement:
theorem conormalSequenceOfImmersion_exact (i : Z ⟶ X) (hi : IsImmersion B S hS i.hom)
    (b : X ⟶ Bb) :
    (ShortComplex.mk _ _
      (conormalSequenceFirstMapOfImmersion_comp_pullbackDifferentialsMap_eq_zero
        B S hS i hi b)).Exact
declarations.comment: exactness at the middle term `i^*Ω_{X/B}`: the second arrow is a cokernel of the first, for an arbitrary immersion `i : Z ⟶ X`, at the tag's own first arrow `conormalSequenceFirstMapOfImmersion`. Unconditional: the open-subspace reduction of the tag's own proof is carried out, through the factorisation of 04CE and the comparison of the two first arrows across the étale inclusion of the ambient open

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.epi_pullbackDifferentialsMap_subspaceInclusion
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 05ZA, exactness at the right term, unconditionally for a closed subspace.**  The
second arrow `i^*Ω_{X/Bb} ⟶ Ω_{Z/Bb}` of the sequence of Stacks 05ZA is an epimorphism.

`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.epi_pullbackDifferentialsMap_of_isLocallySurjective` proves this from
local surjectivity of `i♯ : i⁻¹𝒪_X ⟶ 𝒪_Z`, which that module's implementation notes record as
*carried*; it is not carried any more, and for a closed immersion it is proved —
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isLocallySurjective_structureSharpInverseImage` of
`StacksFrontier/AlgebraicGeometry/Spaces/ClosedImmersionStructureSharpInverseImage.lean`, the
inverse-image form of the surjectivity clause of Stacks 03MB — and the inclusion of a closed
subspace is a closed immersion by `Z.2.2`.
declarations.statement:
theorem epi_pullbackDifferentialsMap_subspaceInclusion :
    Epi (pullbackDifferentialsMap B S hS (subspaceInclusion B S hS X Z) b)
declarations.comment: exactness at the right term: the second arrow `i^*Ω_{X/Bb} ⟶ Ω_{Z/Bb}` is an epimorphism. UNCONDITIONAL for a closed subspace: the local surjectivity of `i♯ : i⁻¹𝒪_X ⟶ 𝒪_Z` that `epi_pullbackDifferentialsMap_of_isLocallySurjective` carries as `hsharp` is `isLocallySurjective_structureSharpInverseImage`, the inverse-image form of the surjectivity clause of 03MB, applied to the closed immersion `Z.2.2`

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.conormalSequence_exact
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 05ZA, exactness at the middle term, unconditionally.**  For a subspace
`Z ⊆ X` of an algebraic space over `B` with structure morphism `b : X ⟶ Bb`, the short complex
```
  𝒞_{Z/X} ⟶ i^*Ω_{X/B} ⟶ Ω_{Z/B}
```
built from the canonical first arrow `AlgebraicGeometry.Space.conormalSequenceFirstMap` and the
second arrow `AlgebraicGeometry.Space.pullbackDifferentialsMap` is exact at `i^*Ω_{X/B}`.

**No hypothesis is carried.**  This is
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.conormalSequenceAt_exact_subspaceInclusion`, read with the source of the
first arrow written as the conormal module `𝒞_{Z/X}` of Stacks 04CN rather than as `i^*𝓘`; the
two readings are the same morphism, by `AlgebraicGeometry.Space.conormalModule_eq`.

The transport is through `CategoryTheory.ShortComplex.exact_iff_of_iso`, with every component of
the isomorphism written out, rather than by ascribing the statement directly; the implementation
notes of this file record what each of the other routes costs.
declarations.statement:
theorem conormalSequence_exact (Z : ClosedSubspaces B S hS X.1) (b : X ⟶ Bb) :
    (ShortComplex.mk _ _
      (conormalSequenceFirstMap_comp_pullbackDifferentialsMap_eq_zero B S hS Z b)).Exact
declarations.comment: exactness at the middle term `i^*Ω_{X/B}`: the second arrow is a cokernel of the first, at a subspace inclusion `Z ⊆ X` — the case the tag's own proof reduces the immersion case to. Unconditional: stated at the canonical inclusion and at the registered first arrow `conormalSequenceFirstMap`, with no hypothesis beyond the tag's own data. The general form with the inclusion an explicit parameter is `conormalSequenceAt_exact`, whose three hypotheses this discharges — the two halves of `mem_definingIdealAt_iff` and the closed-immersion clause of 02YU(4); the inclusion is left a parameter there for the reason recorded in `ConormalSequenceInclusionParameter.lean`. The same clause at the first arrow of an arbitrary immersion, over the ambient open of 04CE, is `conormalSequenceOfImmersion_exact`

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.exact_conormalSequence
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 05ZA, exactness at the middle term, unconditionally for a closed subspace.**  The
short complex `𝒞_{Z/X} ⟶ i^*Ω_{X/Bb} ⟶ Ω_{Z/Bb}` of [Stacks Project, Tag 05ZA] is exact at
`i^*Ω_{X/Bb}`.

This is
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.exact_conormalSequence_of_exists_pushforwardDerivation`, whose
hypothesis `hdesc` is `AlgebraicGeometry.Space.exists_conormalPushforwardDerivation_eq` above.
Nothing beyond the inclusion `i` being a closed immersion is used: the one step that used to
carry a thickening hypothesis, the vanishing of the transpose of a derivation on the sections
killed by `i^♯` in inverse-image form, is proved for an arbitrary closed subspace in
`StacksFrontier/AlgebraicGeometry/Spaces/ConormalSequenceThickeningKernelVanishing.lean` from the
fibre-square presentation of the defining ideal sheaf.

Together with `AlgebraicGeometry.Space.epi_pullbackDifferentialsMap_subspaceInclusion`, which is
the clause at the right, this is the whole of 05ZA for the closed immersions this development
models — the source asserts exactness at `i^*Ω_{X/Bb}` and at `Ω_{Z/Bb}` and nothing on the
left.
declarations.statement:
theorem exact_conormalSequence :
    (ShortComplex.mk _ _
      (conormalSequenceFirstMap_comp_pullbackDifferentialsMap B S hS Z b)).Exact
declarations.comment: exactness at the middle term: the short complex `𝒞_{Z/X} ⟶ i^*Ω_{X/Bb} ⟶ Ω_{Z/Bb}` is exact at `i^*Ω_{X/Bb}`, for a closed subspace

registrations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.pullbackDifferentialsMap
registrations.comment:
the canonical second arrow `i^*Ω_{X/B} ⟶ Ω_{Z/B}`, the comparison map of
  04CX for the square over the identity of the base

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.nonempty_conormalSequenceOfImmersion_splitting
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 05ZB, the global clause, at an arbitrary immersion.**  Let `i : Z ⟶ X` be an
immersion of algebraic spaces over `Bb` with structure morphism `b : X ⟶ Bb`, and let `g : X ⟶ Z`
be a left inverse of `i` over `Bb`.  Then the conormal sequence of [Stacks Project, Tag 05ZA]
```
  0 ⟶ 𝒞_{Z/X} ⟶ i^*Ω_{X/Bb} ⟶ Ω_{Z/Bb} ⟶ 0
```
is **split exact**: it admits a `CategoryTheory.ShortComplex.Splitting`, that is a retraction of
the first arrow and a section of the second summing to the identity — so in particular the first
arrow is a monomorphism, the sequence is exact at its middle term and the second arrow is a split
epimorphism.

The sequence is the one the tag states: the first arrow is
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.conormalSequenceFirstMapOfImmersion`, whose source is the conormal
module `𝒞_{Z/X}` of [Stacks Project, Tag 04CN].  Nothing is assumed beyond the immersion and the
left inverse over `Bb`, which are the tag's own data: the splitting at the kernel-ideal reading is
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.nonempty_conormalSequenceKernel_splitting_of_isImmersion`, and the two
short complexes differ by the isomorphism
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.conormalModuleOfImmersionKernelPullbackIso` of their left-hand terms and
nothing else.
declarations.statement:
theorem nonempty_conormalSequenceOfImmersion_splitting (i : Z ⟶ X)
    (hi : IsImmersion B S hS i.hom) (b : X ⟶ Bb) (g : X ⟶ Z) (hg : i ≫ g = 𝟙 Z)
    (hgb : g ≫ i ≫ b = b) :
    Nonempty (ShortComplex.mk _ _
      (conormalSequenceFirstMapOfImmersion_comp_pullbackDifferentialsMap_eq_zero
        B S hS i hi b)).Splitting
declarations.comment: the global clause at an arbitrary immersion `i : Z ⟶ X` having a left inverse over `B`: the conormal sequence of 05ZA is split exact, that is, it admits a `CategoryTheory.ShortComplex.Splitting`, so its first arrow is a monomorphism, it is exact at the middle term `i^*Ω_{X/B}` and its second arrow is a split epimorphism. Stated at the tag's own first arrow `conormalSequenceFirstMapOfImmersion` out of the conormal module of 04CN, with no hypothesis beyond `IsImmersion` and the tag's own left inverse over `B`. The source's open-subspace reduction is carried out: the immersion is factored through the open subspace of 04CE, where it is closed and the restricted left inverse makes `nonempty_conormalSequenceKernel_splitting` apply, and the splitting is transported back along the comparison of the two sequences across the étale inclusion of that open

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.nonempty_conormalSequenceOfImmersion_splitting_of_etale
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 05ZB, the étale-local clause, at an arbitrary immersion.**  Let `i : Zs ⟶ W` be a
morphism of algebraic spaces over `Bb` with structure morphism `b : W ⟶ Bb`, let `φ : W' ⟶ W` be
étale, let `i' : Zs' ⟶ W'` be an arbitrary immersion and `a : Zs' ⟶ Zs` étale with
`i' ≫ φ = a ≫ i`, and let `g' : W' ⟶ Zs'` be a left inverse of `i'` over `Bb`.  Then

* the restricted conormal sequence, the sequence of [Stacks Project, Tag 05ZA] at `i'` over
  `φ ≫ b`, is split exact;
* the inverse image along `a` of the second arrow of the unrestricted sequence is a split
  epimorphism.

Étaleness is assumed of `φ` and of `a` separately rather than `Zs'` being assumed to be the
preimage of `Zs`, which is weaker: in the situation of the source `a` is a base change of `φ`.
**The unrestricted morphism `i` is free**: the split epimorphism clause is
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isSplitEpi_map_pullbackDifferentialsMap_of_etale`, which assumes nothing
of `i` or `i'`, and the restricted sequence's splitting is
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.nonempty_conormalSequenceOfImmersion_splitting` at `i'`.
declarations.statement:
theorem nonempty_conormalSequenceOfImmersion_splitting_of_etale (i : Zs ⟶ W) (b : W ⟶ Bb)
    (φ : W' ⟶ W) (hφ : IsEtale B S hS φ.hom) (i' : Zs' ⟶ W')
    (hi' : IsImmersion B S hS i'.hom) (a : Zs' ⟶ Zs) (ha : IsEtale B S hS a.hom)
    (hsq : i' ≫ φ = a ≫ i) (g' : W' ⟶ Zs') (hg' : i' ≫ g' = 𝟙 Zs')
    (hg'b : g' ≫ i' ≫ φ ≫ b = φ ≫ b) :
    Nonempty (ShortComplex.mk _ _
          (conormalSequenceFirstMapOfImmersion_comp_pullbackDifferentialsMap_eq_zero B S hS i'
            hi' (φ ≫ b))).Splitting ∧
      IsSplitEpi ((modulePullback B S hS a).map (pullbackDifferentialsMap B S hS i b))
declarations.comment: the étale-local clause at an arbitrary immersion: for an étale `φ : W' ⟶ W`, an immersion `i' : Zs' ⟶ W'` and an étale `a : Zs' ⟶ Zs` with `i' ≫ φ = a ≫ i`, the immersion `i'` having a left inverse over `B`, the restricted conormal sequence of 05ZA is split exact — it admits a `CategoryTheory.ShortComplex.Splitting`, so its first arrow is a monomorphism, it is exact at the middle term and its second arrow is a split epimorphism — and the inverse image along `a` of the second arrow of the unrestricted sequence is a split epimorphism too, which is where the étale-localization clause of 04CU is consumed. Stated at the tag's own first arrow `conormalSequenceFirstMapOfImmersion`, with `IsImmersion` of `i'` and the étale-local data of the tag the only hypotheses; the unrestricted `i` is an arbitrary morphism

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.nonempty_map_conormalSequenceOfImmersion_splitting_of_isEtaleCovering
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 05ZB, the étale-local clause in full.**  Let `i : Z ⟶ X` be an immersion of
algebraic spaces over `Bb` with structure morphism `b : X ⟶ Bb`, and assume that `i` étale
locally has a left inverse: there is an étale covering `{φ_k : X_k ⟶ X}` of `X`
(Stacks 041E: every `φ_k` étale, the family jointly surjective) such that, for each `k`, in a
cartesian square
```
Z_k --i_k--→ X_k
 |            |
a_k          φ_k
 ↓            ↓
 Z  ---i---→  X
```
presenting `Z_k` as `Z ×_X X_k`, the immersion `i_k` has a left inverse `g_k` over `Bb`.  Then
for every `k` the restriction to `Z_k` of the conormal sequence of [Stacks Project, Tag 05ZA]
of `i` — the image under `a_k^*` of the whole short complex
```
  𝒞_{Z/X} ⟶ i^*Ω_{X/Bb} ⟶ Ω_{Z/Bb},
```
conormal term and first arrow included — admits a `CategoryTheory.ShortComplex.Splitting`.  So
the restricted first arrow `a_k^*𝒞_{Z/X} ⟶ a_k^*i^*Ω_{X/Bb}` is a monomorphism, the restricted
sequence is exact at its middle term, and its second arrow is a split epimorphism.

Each member is
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.nonempty_map_conormalSequenceOfImmersion_splitting_of_isPullback`.
declarations.statement:
theorem nonempty_map_conormalSequenceOfImmersion_splitting_of_isEtaleCovering (i : Z ⟶ X)
    (hi : IsImmersion B S hS i.hom) (b : X ⟶ Bb) {ι : Type*}
    {Xk Zk : ι → AlgebraicSpaces B S hS} (φ : ∀ k, Xk k ⟶ X)
    (hφ : IsEtaleCovering B S hS (fun k ↦ (Xk k).1) (fun k ↦ (φ k).hom))
    (ik : ∀ k, Zk k ⟶ Xk k) (a : ∀ k, Zk k ⟶ Z) (hpb : ∀ k, IsPullback (ik k) (a k) (φ k) i)
    (g : ∀ k, Xk k ⟶ Zk k) (hg : ∀ k, ik k ≫ g k = 𝟙 (Zk k))
    (hgb : ∀ k, g k ≫ ik k ≫ φ k ≫ b = φ k ≫ b) (k : ι) :
    Nonempty ((ShortComplex.mk _ _
      (conormalSequenceFirstMapOfImmersion_comp_pullbackDifferentialsMap_eq_zero
        B S hS i hi b)).map (modulePullback B S hS (a k))).Splitting
declarations.comment: the étale-local clause in full: if i étale locally has a left inverse (on an étale covering {X_k → X} with Z_k = Z ×_X X_k), the restriction to each Z_k of the whole conormal sequence of i is split exact

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.conormalSequence_splitExact
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 05ZB, the global clause, unconditionally.**  Let `Z ⊆ X` be a closed subspace of an
algebraic space over `Bb` with structure morphism `b : X ⟶ Bb`, and let `g : X ⟶ Z` be a left
inverse over `Bb` of the inclusion of `Z`.  Then the conormal sequence of Stacks 05ZA
```
  𝒞_{Z/X} ⟶ i^*Ω_{X/Bb} ⟶ Ω_{Z/Bb} ⟶ 0
```
is exact at its middle term and its second arrow is a split epimorphism.

**No hypothesis beyond the left inverse is carried**, and the sequence is the one Stacks 05ZA
states: the first arrow is `AlgebraicGeometry.Space.conormalSequenceFirstMap`, whose source is the
conormal module `𝒞_{Z/X}` of Stacks 04CN.  The exactness clause is
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.conormalSequence_exact`, which is
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.conormalSequenceAt_splitExact`'s first component at the canonical
inclusion with its three hypotheses discharged — the two halves of
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.mem_definingIdealAt_iff` and part (4) of Stacks 02YU — and read at
`conormalSequenceFirstMap`; the splitness clause is unchanged by that reading, since
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.pullbackDifferentialsMap` does not mention the first arrow.

The hypothesis is satisfiable: at the top closed subspace the inclusion is an isomorphism, and its
inverse is a left inverse over `Bb`; the retraction is written out in the proof of
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isZero_conormalModule_top` of
`StacksFrontier/AlgebraicGeometry/Spaces/Thickenings/LiftingSheaf.lean`.
declarations.statement:
theorem conormalSequence_splitExact (Z : ClosedSubspaces B S hS X.1) (b : X ⟶ Bb)
    (g : X ⟶ (⟨Z.1.toFunctor, Z.2.1⟩ : AlgebraicSpaces B S hS))
    (hg : subspaceInclusion B S hS X Z ≫ g = 𝟙 (⟨Z.1.toFunctor, Z.2.1⟩ : AlgebraicSpaces B S hS))
    (hgb : g ≫ subspaceInclusion B S hS X Z ≫ b = b) :
    (ShortComplex.mk _ _
          (conormalSequenceFirstMap_comp_pullbackDifferentialsMap_eq_zero B S hS Z b)).Exact ∧
      IsSplitEpi (pullbackDifferentialsMap B S hS (subspaceInclusion B S hS X Z) b)
declarations.comment: the global clause at the inclusion of a bundled subspace `Z ⊆ X` having a left inverse over `B`: the conormal sequence of 05ZA is exact at its middle term `i^*Ω_{X/B}` and its second arrow is a split epimorphism, hence also an epimorphism, which is exactness at the right term; the vanishing of the composite is the short complex itself. Stated at the canonical inclusion and at the registered first arrow `conormalSequenceFirstMap`, with no hypothesis beyond the left inverse, which is the tag's own datum. The injectivity clause at the left end of the sequence is the subject of `nonempty_conormalSequence_splitting_iff_mono`, which shows it equivalent to the full `ShortComplex.Splitting`. The general form with the inclusion an explicit parameter is `conormalSequenceAt_splitExact`, and the same clause at an arbitrary closed immersion, with no bundled subspace anywhere, is `conormalSequenceKernel_splitExact_of_isClosedImmersion`; at the generality the tag is stated at, an arbitrary immersion with a left inverse over `B`, the sequence is split exact in full by `nonempty_conormalSequenceOfImmersion_splitting`

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.conormalSequence_splitExact_of_etale
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 05ZB, the étale-local clause, unconditionally.**  Let `Z ⊆ X` and `Z' ⊆ X'` be closed
subspaces, let `φ : X' ⟶ X` be étale, let `a : Z' ⟶ Z` be étale with `i' ≫ φ = a ≫ i` for the two
inclusions, and let `g' : X' ⟶ Z'` be a left inverse of the inclusion of `Z'` over `Bb`.  Then

* the restricted conormal sequence, the sequence of Stacks 05ZA at `Z' ⊆ X'` over `φ ≫ b`, is
  exact at its middle term, and its second arrow is a split epimorphism;
* the inverse image along `a` of the second arrow of the unrestricted sequence is a split
  epimorphism too.

**No hypothesis beyond the étale-local data of the tag is carried**: `φ`, `a` and the square they
sit in, and the left inverse `g'`.  The first clause is
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.conormalSequence_exact` at `Z' ⊆ X'` over `φ ≫ b`, so it is stated at the
registered first arrow `AlgebraicGeometry.Space.conormalSequenceFirstMap` with the source read as
`𝒞_{Z'/X'}`; the other two are the corresponding clauses of
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.conormalSequenceAt_splitExact_of_etale`, which do not mention the first
arrow.  As there, étaleness is assumed of `φ` and of `a` separately rather than `Z'` being assumed
to be the preimage of `Z`, which is weaker: in the situation of the source `a` is a base change
of `φ`.
declarations.statement:
theorem conormalSequence_splitExact_of_etale (Z : ClosedSubspaces B S hS X.1)
    (Z' : ClosedSubspaces B S hS X'.1) (b : X ⟶ Bb) (φ : X' ⟶ X) (hφ : IsEtale B S hS φ.hom)
    (a : (⟨Z'.1.toFunctor, Z'.2.1⟩ : AlgebraicSpaces B S hS) ⟶
      (⟨Z.1.toFunctor, Z.2.1⟩ : AlgebraicSpaces B S hS))
    (ha : IsEtale B S hS a.hom)
    (hsq : subspaceInclusion B S hS X' Z' ≫ φ = a ≫ subspaceInclusion B S hS X Z)
    (g' : X' ⟶ (⟨Z'.1.toFunctor, Z'.2.1⟩ : AlgebraicSpaces B S hS))
    (hg' : subspaceInclusion B S hS X' Z' ≫ g' =
      𝟙 (⟨Z'.1.toFunctor, Z'.2.1⟩ : AlgebraicSpaces B S hS))
    (hg'b : g' ≫ subspaceInclusion B S hS X' Z' ≫ φ ≫ b = φ ≫ b) :
    (ShortComplex.mk _ _
          (conormalSequenceFirstMap_comp_pullbackDifferentialsMap_eq_zero B S hS Z'
            (φ ≫ b))).Exact ∧
        IsSplitEpi (pullbackDifferentialsMap B S hS (subspaceInclusion B S hS X' Z')
          (φ ≫ b)) ∧
      IsSplitEpi ((modulePullback B S hS a).map
        (pullbackDifferentialsMap B S hS (subspaceInclusion B S hS X Z) b))
declarations.comment: the étale-local clause: for closed subspaces `Z ⊆ X` and `Z' ⊆ X'` joined by an étale `φ : X' ⟶ X` and an étale `a : Z' ⟶ Z` over it, with the inclusion of `Z'` admitting a left inverse over `B`, the restricted conormal sequence of 05ZA is exact at its middle term and its second arrow is a split epimorphism, and so is the inverse image along `a` of the second arrow of the unrestricted sequence — which is where the étale-localization clause of 04CU is consumed. Stated at the two canonical inclusions and at the registered first arrow `conormalSequenceFirstMap`, with no hypothesis beyond the étale-local data of the tag. As in the global clause, the injectivity clause at the left end of the sequence is the subject of `nonempty_conormalSequence_splitting_iff_mono`. The general form with both inclusions explicit parameters is `conormalSequenceAt_splitExact_of_etale`

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.nonempty_conormalSequence_splitting
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 05ZB, the global clause in full.**  Let `Z ⊆ X` be a closed subspace of an algebraic
space over `Bb` with structure morphism `b : X ⟶ Bb`, and let `g : X ⟶ Z` be a left inverse over
`Bb` of its inclusion.  Then the conormal sequence of Stacks 05ZA
```
  0 ⟶ 𝒞_{Z/X} ⟶ i^*Ω_{X/Bb} ⟶ Ω_{Z/Bb} ⟶ 0
```
is **split exact**: it admits a `CategoryTheory.ShortComplex.Splitting`, that is a retraction of
the first arrow and a section of the second summing to the identity — so in particular the first
arrow is a monomorphism, the sequence is exact at its middle term and the second arrow is a split
epimorphism.

The exactness and the splitness of the second arrow are
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.conormalSequence_splitExact`; what completes the tag is the injectivity
of the first arrow, `AlgebraicGeometry.Space.mono_conormalSequenceFirstMap`, which
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.nonempty_conormalSequence_splitting_iff_mono` turns into the full
splitting.
declarations.statement:
theorem nonempty_conormalSequence_splitting (b : X ⟶ Bb)
    (hgb : g ≫ subspaceInclusion B S hS X Z ≫ b = b) :
    Nonempty (ShortComplex.mk _ _
      (conormalSequenceFirstMap_comp_pullbackDifferentialsMap_eq_zero B S hS Z b)).Splitting
declarations.comment: the global clause in full at the inclusion of a bundled subspace `Z ⊆ X` of an algebraic space over `B`, that inclusion having a left inverse over `B`: the conormal sequence of 05ZA is split exact, that is, it admits a `CategoryTheory.ShortComplex.Splitting`: the first arrow `conormalSequenceFirstMap` is a monomorphism, the sequence is exact at the middle term `i^*Ω_{X/B}`, and the second arrow is a split epimorphism. Stated at the canonical inclusion and at the registered first arrow, with no hypothesis beyond the tag's own left inverse over `B`. The same clause at an arbitrary closed immersion, with no bundled subspace anywhere, is `nonempty_conormalSequenceKernel_splitting`, and at the generality the tag is stated at, an arbitrary immersion with a left inverse over `B`, it is `nonempty_conormalSequenceOfImmersion_splitting`

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.nonempty_conormalSequence_splitting_of_etale
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 05ZB, the étale-local clause in full.**  Let `Z ⊆ X` and `Z' ⊆ X'` be closed
subspaces, let `φ : X' ⟶ X` be étale, let `a : Z' ⟶ Z` be étale with `i' ≫ φ = a ≫ i` for the two
inclusions, and let `g' : X' ⟶ Z'` be a left inverse over `Bb` of the inclusion of `Z'`.  Then

* the restricted conormal sequence, the sequence of Stacks 05ZA at `Z' ⊆ X'` over `φ ≫ b`, is
  split exact;
* the inverse image along `a` of the second arrow of the unrestricted sequence is a split
  epimorphism.

As in `AlgebraicGeometry.Space.conormalSequence_splitExact_of_etale`, étaleness is assumed of `φ`
and of `a` separately rather than `Z'` being assumed to be the preimage of `Z`, which is weaker:
in the situation of the source `a` is a base change of `φ`.
declarations.statement:
theorem nonempty_conormalSequence_splitting_of_etale
    (Z' : ClosedSubspaces B S hS X'.1) (b : X ⟶ Bb) (φ : X' ⟶ X) (hφ : IsEtale B S hS φ.hom)
    (a : (⟨Z'.1.toFunctor, Z'.2.1⟩ : AlgebraicSpaces B S hS) ⟶
      (⟨Z.1.toFunctor, Z.2.1⟩ : AlgebraicSpaces B S hS))
    (ha : IsEtale B S hS a.hom)
    (hsq : subspaceInclusion B S hS X' Z' ≫ φ = a ≫ subspaceInclusion B S hS X Z)
    (g' : X' ⟶ (⟨Z'.1.toFunctor, Z'.2.1⟩ : AlgebraicSpaces B S hS))
    (hg' : subspaceInclusion B S hS X' Z' ≫ g' =
      𝟙 (⟨Z'.1.toFunctor, Z'.2.1⟩ : AlgebraicSpaces B S hS))
    (hg'b : g' ≫ subspaceInclusion B S hS X' Z' ≫ φ ≫ b = φ ≫ b) :
    Nonempty (ShortComplex.mk _ _
          (conormalSequenceFirstMap_comp_pullbackDifferentialsMap_eq_zero B S hS Z'
            (φ ≫ b))).Splitting ∧
      IsSplitEpi ((modulePullback B S hS a).map
        (pullbackDifferentialsMap B S hS (subspaceInclusion B S hS X Z) b))
declarations.comment: the étale-local clause in full: for closed subspaces `Z ⊆ X` and `Z' ⊆ X'` joined by an étale `φ : X' ⟶ X` and an étale `a : Z' ⟶ Z` over it, with the inclusion of `Z'` admitting a left inverse over `B`, the restricted conormal sequence of 05ZA is split exact — it admits a `CategoryTheory.ShortComplex.Splitting`, so its first arrow is a monomorphism, it is exact at the middle term and its second arrow is a split epimorphism — and the inverse image along `a` of the second arrow of the unrestricted sequence is a split epimorphism too, which is where the étale-localization clause of 04CU is consumed. Stated at the two canonical inclusions and at the registered first arrow, with no hypothesis beyond the étale-local data of the tag

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isSplitEpi_pullbackDifferentialsMap_of_leftInverse
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 05ZB**, the global clause: a left inverse of `i` over `Bb` makes the second arrow of
the sequence of Stacks 05ZA a split epimorphism, so that sequence is split exact.

The comparison map of Stacks 04CX at the identity square is carried as the parameters `cid`,
`hcid` and `[IsIso cid]`; see the implementation notes.
declarations.statement:
theorem isSplitEpi_pullbackDifferentialsMap_of_leftInverse (i : Z ⟶ X) (b : X ⟶ Bb) (g : X ⟶ Z)
    (hg : i ≫ g = 𝟙 Z) (hgb : g ≫ i ≫ b = b)
    (cid : (modulePullback B S hS (𝟙 Z)).obj (sheafOfDifferentials B S hS (i ≫ b)) ⟶
      sheafOfDifferentials B S hS (i ≫ b)) [IsIso cid]
    (hcid : IsSheafOfDifferentialsMap B S hS (𝟙 Z) (i ≫ b) (i ≫ b) cid) :
    IsSplitEpi (pullbackDifferentialsMap B S hS i b)
declarations.comment: the global clause: a left inverse of `i` over `B` splits the second arrow of the conormal sequence of 05ZA, so that sequence is split exact

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isSplitEpi_pullbackDifferentialsMap_of_retraction
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 05ZB**, the global clause, unconditionally: a left inverse of `i` over `Bb` makes the
second arrow of the sequence of Stacks 05ZA a split epimorphism, so that sequence is split exact.

This is `AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isSplitEpi_pullbackDifferentialsMap_of_leftInverse` with the
comparison map of Stacks 04CX at the identity square supplied rather than carried: it is the unit
law of Stacks 03LU at `Ω_{Z/Bb}`, which is a comparison map by
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isSheafOfDifferentialsMap_modulePullbackIdIso`, and invertible by
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isIso_of_isSheafOfDifferentialsMap_id`.  Nothing is assumed beyond the
left inverse.
declarations.statement:
theorem isSplitEpi_pullbackDifferentialsMap_of_retraction (i : Z ⟶ X) (b : X ⟶ Bb) (g : X ⟶ Z)
    (hg : i ≫ g = 𝟙 Z) (hgb : g ≫ i ≫ b = b) :
    IsSplitEpi (pullbackDifferentialsMap B S hS i b)
declarations.comment: the global clause, unconditionally: a left inverse of `i` over `B` splits the second arrow of the conormal sequence of 05ZA, so that sequence is split exact

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isSplitEpi_map_pullbackDifferentialsMap_of_etaleLeftInverse
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 05ZB**, the étale-local clause: if the restriction of `i` along an étale
`φ : X' ⟶ X` has a left inverse over `Bb`, the inverse image along the induced `a : Z' ⟶ Z` of the
second arrow of the sequence of Stacks 05ZA is a split epimorphism, so the restricted sequence is
split exact.

The section is the chosen section of the global clause at `i'`, conjugated by the two invertible
comparison maps of Stacks 04CU and the composition comparisons of Stacks 03LU.  The comparison
map at the identity square and the étale-localization clause of Stacks 04CU are carried as
parameters and instances; see the implementation notes.
declarations.statement:
theorem isSplitEpi_map_pullbackDifferentialsMap_of_etaleLeftInverse (i : Z ⟶ X) (b : X ⟶ Bb)
    (φ : X' ⟶ X) (i' : Z' ⟶ X') (a : Z' ⟶ Z) (hsq : i' ≫ φ = a ≫ i) (g' : X' ⟶ Z')
    (hg' : i' ≫ g' = 𝟙 Z') (hg'b : g' ≫ i' ≫ φ ≫ b = φ ≫ b)
    (cid' : (modulePullback B S hS (𝟙 Z')).obj
        (sheafOfDifferentials B S hS (i' ≫ φ ≫ b)) ⟶
      sheafOfDifferentials B S hS (i' ≫ φ ≫ b)) [IsIso cid']
    (hcid' : IsSheafOfDifferentialsMap B S hS (𝟙 Z') (i' ≫ φ ≫ b) (i' ≫ φ ≫ b) cid')
    (ca : (modulePullback B S hS a).obj (sheafOfDifferentials B S hS (i ≫ b)) ⟶
      sheafOfDifferentials B S hS (i' ≫ φ ≫ b)) [IsIso ca]
    (hca : IsSheafOfDifferentialsMap B S hS a (i ≫ b) (i' ≫ φ ≫ b) ca)
    [IsIso (pullbackDifferentialsMap B S hS φ b)] :
    IsSplitEpi ((modulePullback B S hS a).map (pullbackDifferentialsMap B S hS i b))
declarations.comment: the étale-local clause: a left inverse of the restriction of `i` along an étale `φ : X' ⟶ X` splits the inverse image along the induced `a : Z' ⟶ Z` of the second arrow of the conormal sequence of 05ZA

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isSplitEpi_map_pullbackDifferentialsMap_of_etaleRetraction
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 05ZB**, the étale-local clause, with the comparison map at the identity square no
longer carried: if the restriction of `i` along an étale `φ : X' ⟶ X` has a left inverse over
`Bb`, the inverse image along the induced `a : Z' ⟶ Z` of the second arrow of the sequence of
Stacks 05ZA is a split epimorphism, so the restricted sequence is split exact.

This is `AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isSplitEpi_map_pullbackDifferentialsMap_of_etaleLeftInverse` with
the unit law of Stacks 04CX supplied rather than carried, by
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isSheafOfDifferentialsMap_modulePullbackIdIso` and
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isIso_of_isSheafOfDifferentialsMap_id`.  So this clause is unconditional
in Stacks 04CX.

It still takes the invertibility of the two comparison maps as the instances `[IsIso ca]` and
`[IsIso (pullbackDifferentialsMap B S hS φ b)]`, which is the conclusion of the
étale-localization clause of Stacks 04CU at `a` and at `φ`; étaleness of `φ` and of `a` is not
assumed, so this applies to any square where those two maps are invertible.
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isSplitEpi_map_pullbackDifferentialsMap_of_etale` is the form that
assumes étaleness and discharges the two instances.
declarations.statement:
theorem isSplitEpi_map_pullbackDifferentialsMap_of_etaleRetraction (i : Z ⟶ X) (b : X ⟶ Bb)
    (φ : X' ⟶ X) (i' : Z' ⟶ X') (a : Z' ⟶ Z) (hsq : i' ≫ φ = a ≫ i) (g' : X' ⟶ Z')
    (hg' : i' ≫ g' = 𝟙 Z') (hg'b : g' ≫ i' ≫ φ ≫ b = φ ≫ b)
    (ca : (modulePullback B S hS a).obj (sheafOfDifferentials B S hS (i ≫ b)) ⟶
      sheafOfDifferentials B S hS (i' ≫ φ ≫ b)) [IsIso ca]
    (hca : IsSheafOfDifferentialsMap B S hS a (i ≫ b) (i' ≫ φ ≫ b) ca)
    [IsIso (pullbackDifferentialsMap B S hS φ b)] :
    IsSplitEpi ((modulePullback B S hS a).map (pullbackDifferentialsMap B S hS i b))
declarations.comment: the étale-local clause, unconditional in 04CX: a left inverse of the restriction of `i` along an étale `φ : X' ⟶ X` splits the inverse image along the induced `a : Z' ⟶ Z` of the second arrow of the conormal sequence of 05ZA

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isSplitEpi_map_pullbackDifferentialsMap_of_etale
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 05ZB**, the étale-local clause, with nothing carried: if `φ : X' ⟶ X` and the
induced `a : Z' ⟶ Z` are étale and the restriction `i' : Z' ⟶ X'` of `i` along `φ` has a left
inverse over `Bb`, then the inverse image along `a` of the second arrow of the sequence of
Stacks 05ZA is a split epimorphism, so the restricted sequence is split exact.

This is `AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isSplitEpi_map_pullbackDifferentialsMap_of_etaleRetraction` with
the two invertible comparison maps supplied rather than carried: the comparison map of
Stacks 04CX along an étale morphism, over a fixed base, is invertible by
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isIso_of_isSheafOfDifferentialsMap_etale`, which is the
étale-localization clause of Stacks 04CU.  So nothing is assumed here beyond the hypotheses of
the source: `φ` is étale, `a` — a base change of `φ` in the situation of the source — is étale,
the square `i' ≫ φ = a ≫ i` commutes, and `i'` has the left inverse `g'` over `Bb`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isSplitEpi_map_pullbackDifferentialsMap_of_etale (i : Z ⟶ X) (b : X ⟶ Bb)
    (φ : X' ⟶ X) (hφ : IsEtale B S hS φ.hom) (i' : Z' ⟶ X') (a : Z' ⟶ Z)
    (ha : IsEtale B S hS a.hom) (hsq : i' ≫ φ = a ≫ i) (g' : X' ⟶ Z')
    (hg' : i' ≫ g' = 𝟙 Z') (hg'b : g' ≫ i' ≫ φ ≫ b = φ ≫ b) :
    IsSplitEpi ((modulePullback B S hS a).map (pullbackDifferentialsMap B S hS i b))
declarations.comment: the étale-local clause, with nothing carried: for étale `φ : X' ⟶ X` and `a`, a left inverse of the restriction of `i` along `φ` splits the inverse image along `a` of the second arrow of the conormal sequence of 05ZA

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isIso_sheafOfDifferentialsMap_of_isPullback
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 05ZC.**  Let `X ⟶ Y` be a morphism of algebraic spaces over `S` and let
`g : Y' ⟶ Y` be a morphism of algebraic spaces over `S`.  Let `X' = X_{Y'}` be the base change
of `X` and let `g' : X' ⟶ X` be the projection.  Then the map
`(g')^*Ω_{X/Y} ⟶ Ω_{X'/Y'}` of Stacks 04CX is an isomorphism.

The base change is presented as a cartesian square `IsPullback g' p' p g` of algebraic spaces,
and the map of Stacks 04CX by the property `AlgebraicGeometry.Space.IsSheafOfDifferentialsMap`
that characterizes it — existence is
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isSheafOfDifferentialsMap_sheafOfDifferentialsMap` and uniqueness
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.eq_of_isSheafOfDifferentialsMap`, so naming the map this way asserts
nothing beyond the square.

The proof is the source's own: the case of a square of schemes, Morphisms, Lemma 01V0, together
with the étale localization of Stacks 04CU.  The scheme case enters as
`AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.Hom.bijective_restrictRelativeDerivation_of_isPullback` through
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.schemeSquareDerivationRestriction`.  The earlier form
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isIso_of_isSheafOfDifferentialsMap_of_isPullback`, which takes that
étale localization as an argument, stays as an untagged lemma.
declarations.statement:
theorem isIso_sheafOfDifferentialsMap_of_isPullback (g' : X' ⟶ X) (p' : X' ⟶ Y') (p : X ⟶ Y)
    (g : Y' ⟶ Y) (h : IsPullback g' p' p g)
    {c : (modulePullback B S hS g').obj (sheafOfDifferentials B S hS p) ⟶
      sheafOfDifferentials B S hS p'}
    (hc : IsSheafOfDifferentialsMap B S hS g' p p' c) : IsIso c
declarations.comment:
the map of 04CX for the base change of X along g is an isomorphism, with the base
  change presented as a cartesian square and the map by the property characterizing it.  The
  étale localization of 04CU and the scheme case 01V0 are both applied as proved

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isIso_biprodDesc_sheafOfDifferentialsMap_of_isPullback
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 05ZD.**  Let `f : X ⟶ T` and `g : Y ⟶ T` be morphisms of algebraic spaces over `S`
with the same target and let `p : W ⟶ X`, `q : W ⟶ Y` be the projections of the fibre product
`W = X ×_T Y`.  Then the maps of Stacks 04CX give an isomorphism
`p^*Ω_{X/T} ⊕ q^*Ω_{Y/T} ⟶ Ω_{W/T}`.

The fibre product is presented as a cartesian square `IsPullback p q f g` and the two summands
by the property `AlgebraicGeometry.Space.IsSheafOfDifferentialsMap` that characterizes the map
of Stacks 04CX for the square they come from, so the conclusion is about those two maps and not
about some decomposition of `Ω_{W/T}`.

The proof is the source's own: the case of schemes, Morphisms, Lemma 01V1, together with the
étale localization of Stacks 04CU, the scheme case entering through
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.schemeSquareDerivationRestriction`.  The earlier form
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isIso_biprodDesc_of_isSheafOfDifferentialsMap`, which takes that
étale localization as an argument, stays as an untagged lemma.
declarations.statement:
theorem isIso_biprodDesc_sheafOfDifferentialsMap_of_isPullback {W T : AlgebraicSpaces B S hS}
    (p : W ⟶ X) (q : W ⟶ Y) (f : X ⟶ T) (g : Y ⟶ T) (h : IsPullback p q f g)
    (a : (modulePullback B S hS p).obj (sheafOfDifferentials B S hS f) ⟶
      sheafOfDifferentials B S hS (p ≫ f))
    (b : (modulePullback B S hS q).obj (sheafOfDifferentials B S hS g) ⟶
      sheafOfDifferentials B S hS (p ≫ f))
    (ha : IsSheafOfDifferentialsMap B S hS p f (p ≫ f) a)
    (hb : IsSheafOfDifferentialsMap B S hS q g (p ≫ f) b) :
    IsIso (biprod.desc a b)
declarations.comment:
the two maps of 04CX out of p^*Omega_{X/T} and q^*Omega_{Y/T} give an
  isomorphism onto Omega_{X x_T Y/T}, with the fibre product presented as a cartesian square and
  each summand by the property characterizing it.  The étale localization of 04CU and the scheme
  case 01V1 are both applied as proved

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isFiniteTypeOnSite_sheafOfDifferentials
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 05ZE**, with the two carried hypotheses in place of "`f` is locally of finite
type".  If `𝒪_X` is étale-locally generated as an `f⁻¹𝒪_Y`-algebra by finitely many sections and
the transition maps of the small étale site of `X` are unramified, then `Ω_{X/Y}` is a finite
type `𝒪_X`-module.

The covering of each object is the one `hft` supplies, presented as the family of all its arrows
indexed by their sources, and on each member the finitely many generators are
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.hasFiniteGlobalGenerators_sheafOfDifferentials_over`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isFiniteTypeOnSite_sheafOfDifferentials (f : X ⟶ Y)
    (hunram : HasUnramifiedChartTransitions B S hS X)
    (hft : HasFiniteTypeChartAlgebras B S hS f) :
    (sheafOfDifferentials B S hS f).IsFiniteTypeOnSite
declarations.comment:
finite type of Ω_{X/Y}, from étale-local finite generation of 𝒪_X over f⁻¹𝒪_Y
  and unramifiedness of the transition maps of the small étale site; the gap to the source's
  hypothesis is the bridge from 03XF(1) to the algebra statement, and 00UU for the sections of
  an arrow of the small étale site

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isFiniteTypeOnSite_sheafOfDifferentials_of_isLocallyOfFiniteType
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 05ZE.**  If `f : X ⟶ Y` is a morphism of algebraic spaces over `S` which is locally
of finite type, then `Ω_{X/Y}` is a finite type `𝒪_X`-module.

The two inputs not proved in this development are carried universally quantified: the bridge
from `AlgebraicGeometry.Space.IsLocallyOfFiniteType` (Stacks 03XF(1), defined through étale
scheme charts) to the statement that `𝒪_X` is étale-locally a finite type `f⁻¹𝒪_Y`-algebra, and
the unramifiedness of the transition maps of a small étale site, which is Algebra, Lemma 00UU
for the ring map of sections of an arrow of that site.
declarations.statement:
theorem isFiniteTypeOnSite_sheafOfDifferentials_of_isLocallyOfFiniteType
    (hunram : ∀ X' : AlgebraicSpaces B S hS, HasUnramifiedChartTransitions B S hS X')
    (hft : ∀ (X' Y' : AlgebraicSpaces B S hS) (g : X' ⟶ Y'),
      IsLocallyOfFiniteType B S hS g.hom → HasFiniteTypeChartAlgebras B S hS g)
    (f : X ⟶ Y) (hf : IsLocallyOfFiniteType B S hS f.hom) :
    (sheafOfDifferentials B S hS f).IsFiniteTypeOnSite
declarations.comment:
the source's statement, carrying the bridge from 03XF(1) to étale-local finite
  generation of 𝒪_X over f⁻¹𝒪_Y as `hft` and unramifiedness of the transition maps of a small
  étale site (00UU) as `hunram`, both quantified over all algebraic spaces over `S`

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isFiniteTypeOnSite_sheafOfDifferentials_of_affineChartAlgebras
declarations.doc:
**Finite type of `Ω_{X/Y}` from the étale-local finite generation of `𝒪_X` over `f⁻¹𝒪_Y`.**
If every object of the small étale site of `X` has a covering by affine charts over which `𝒪_X`
is generated as an `f⁻¹𝒪_Y`-algebra by finitely many sections, then `Ω_{X/Y}` is a finite type
`𝒪_X`-module.

The covering of each object is the one `hft` supplies, and on each of its members the finitely
many generators are
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.hasFiniteGlobalGenerators_sheafOfDifferentials_over_of_isAffine`.
Unramifiedness of the transition maps — Algebra, Lemma 00UU — is *proved*, not assumed:
affineness of the members is what makes
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.subsingleton_kaehlerDifferential_chartRing_of_affineChart` apply.

This is the engine of Stacks 05ZE with no unramifiedness hypothesis; at the source's own
hypothesis `AlgebraicGeometry.Space.IsLocallyOfFiniteType`, and with nothing else assumed, the
statement is
`Space.isFiniteTypeOnSite_sheafOfDifferentials_of_isLocallyOfFiniteType_unconditional`,
in `StacksFrontier/AlgebraicGeometry/Spaces/SheafOfDifferentialsFiniteTypeChartBridge.lean`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isFiniteTypeOnSite_sheafOfDifferentials_of_affineChartAlgebras (f : X ⟶ Y)
    (hft : HasFiniteTypeAffineChartAlgebras B S hS f) :
    (sheafOfDifferentials B S hS f).IsFiniteTypeOnSite
declarations.comment:
finite type of Ω_{X/Y} from étale-local finite generation of 𝒪_X over f⁻¹𝒪_Y on a
  covering by affine charts, which is what 03XF(1) delivers; unramifiedness of the transition
  maps of the small étale site (00UU) is proved, not assumed.  The source's own hypothesis is
  taken in `isFiniteTypeOnSite_sheafOfDifferentials_of_isLocallyOfFiniteType_unconditional`

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isFiniteTypeOnSite_sheafOfDifferentials_of_isLocallyOfFiniteType_unconditional
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 05ZE.**  If `f : X ⟶ Y` is a morphism of algebraic spaces over `S` which is locally
of finite type, then `Ω_{X/Y}` is a finite type `𝒪_X`-module.

The chart-algebra condition of
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.hasFiniteTypeAffineChartAlgebras_of_isLocallyOfFiniteType` feeds
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isFiniteTypeOnSite_sheafOfDifferentials_of_affineChartAlgebras`, which
generates `Ω_{X/Y}` over each member of the covering by the universal differentials of the
generators. Algebra, Lemma 00UU for the transition maps of the small étale site is proved there,
not assumed.
declarations.statement:
theorem isFiniteTypeOnSite_sheafOfDifferentials_of_isLocallyOfFiniteType_unconditional
    (f : X ⟶ Y) (hf : IsLocallyOfFiniteType B S hS f.hom) :
    (sheafOfDifferentials B S hS f).IsFiniteTypeOnSite
declarations.comment:
Ω_{X/Y} is a finite type 𝒪_X-module for f locally of finite type, with no
  further hypothesis

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isFiniteTypeOnSite_sheafOfDifferentials_of_isLocallyOfFiniteType_hom
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 05ZE.** If `f : X ⟶ Y` is a morphism of algebraic spaces over `S` which is locally
of finite type, then the sheaf of differentials `Ω_{X/Y}` is an `𝒪_X`-module of finite type.

The proof is the source's. An atlas `q : V ⟶ Y` lifts, by Stacks 02X1, to a surjective étale
chart `p : U ⟶ X` and a morphism `α : U ⟶ V` of schemes over `q`; `α` is locally of finite type
because `f` is. The pullback of `Ω_{X/Y}` to `U` is the sheaf of differentials of `α`
(Stacks 04CU), which is the small-étale module associated to `Ω_{U/V}`; that is of finite type by
Stacks 01V2 and Stacks 08HD, and finite type descends from the surjective chart.
declarations.statement:
theorem isFiniteTypeOnSite_sheafOfDifferentials_of_isLocallyOfFiniteType_hom
    {X Y : AlgebraicSpaces B S hS} (f : X ⟶ Y) (hf : IsLocallyOfFiniteType B S hS f.hom) :
    (sheafOfDifferentials B S hS f).IsFiniteTypeOnSite

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isFinitePresentationOnSite_sheafOfDifferentials
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 05ZF**, with the two carried hypotheses in place of "`f` is locally of finite
presentation".  If `𝒪_X` is étale-locally generated as an `f⁻¹𝒪_Y`-algebra by finitely many
sections whose universal differentials have étale-locally finitely generated relations, and the
transition maps of the small étale site of `X` are unramified, then `Ω_{X/Y}` is an
`𝒪_X`-module of finite presentation.

The covering of each object is the one `hfp` supplies, presented as the family of all its
arrows indexed by their sources, and on each member the finite presentation is
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.hasFiniteGlobalPresentation_sheafOfDifferentials_over`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isFinitePresentationOnSite_sheafOfDifferentials (f : X ⟶ Y)
    (hunram : HasUnramifiedChartTransitions B S hS X)
    (hfp : HasFinitePresentationChartData B S hS f) :
    (sheafOfDifferentials B S hS f).IsFinitePresentationOnSite
declarations.comment:
finite presentation of Ω_{X/Y}. ASSUMED, not proved: the relations half of
  Descent, Proposition 03DX(2), as the last clause of `hfp` — that the relations among the
  universal differentials of a finite generating family are étale-locally finitely generated.
  Also assumed: the bridge from 03XP(1) to étale-local finite generation of 𝒪_X over f⁻¹𝒪_Y
  (first clause of `hfp`), and unramifiedness of the transition maps of the small étale site
  (`hunram`, 00UU), which `hasUnramifiedChartTransitions_of_forall_isAffine` discharges when
  every étale chart is affine. PROVED here: the generators half and the assembly into 03DL(7)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isFinitePresentationOnSite_sheafOfDifferentials_of_isLocallyOfFinitePresentation
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 05ZF.**  If `f : X ⟶ Y` is a morphism of algebraic spaces over `S` which is
locally of finite presentation, then `Ω_{X/Y}` is an `𝒪_X`-module of finite presentation.

The two inputs not proved in this development are carried universally quantified: the bridge
from `AlgebraicGeometry.Space.IsLocallyOfFinitePresentation` (Stacks 03XP(1), defined through
étale scheme charts) to the étale-local finite presentation data of
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.HasFinitePresentationChartData`, and the unramifiedness of the
transition maps of a small étale site, which is Algebra, Lemma 00UU for the ring map of
sections of an arrow of that site.
declarations.statement:
theorem isFinitePresentationOnSite_sheafOfDifferentials_of_isLocallyOfFinitePresentation
    (hunram : ∀ X' : AlgebraicSpaces B S hS, HasUnramifiedChartTransitions B S hS X')
    (hfp : ∀ (X' Y' : AlgebraicSpaces B S hS) (g : X' ⟶ Y'),
      IsLocallyOfFinitePresentation B S hS g.hom → HasFinitePresentationChartData B S hS g)
    (f : X ⟶ Y) (hf : IsLocallyOfFinitePresentation B S hS f.hom) :
    (sheafOfDifferentials B S hS f).IsFinitePresentationOnSite
declarations.comment:
the source's statement. ASSUMED, not proved: the relations half of Descent,
  Proposition 03DX(2), inside `hfp`; the bridge from 03XP(1) to étale-local finite presentation
  data for 𝒪_X over f⁻¹𝒪_Y, also inside `hfp`; and unramifiedness of the transition maps of a
  small étale site (`hunram`, 00UU), discharged by
  `hasUnramifiedChartTransitions_of_forall_isAffine` when every étale chart is affine. Both
  inputs are quantified over all algebraic spaces over `S`

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isFinitePresentationOnSite_sheafOfDifferentials_of_chartData
declarations.doc:
**Finite presentation of `Ω_{X/Y}` from étale-local presentation data for `𝒪_X` over
`f⁻¹𝒪_Y`.**  If `𝒪_X` is étale-locally generated as an `f⁻¹𝒪_Y`-algebra by finitely many sections
whose universal differentials have étale-locally finitely generated relations, then `Ω_{X/Y}` is
an `𝒪_X`-module of finite presentation.

The covering of each object is the one `hfp` supplies, refined to its members with affine
underlying scheme
(`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.SmallEtale.ofArrows_affineMember_mem_topology`), and on each such
member the finite presentation is
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.hasFiniteGlobalPresentation_sheafOfDifferentials_over`.  Refining to
affine members is what makes Algebra, Lemma 00UU applicable: the only transition maps the proof
differentiates are arrows between affine charts.

The tag itself is
`Space.isFinitePresentationOnSite_sheafOfDifferentials_of_isLocallyOfFinitePresentation`
below, which takes the source's hypothesis on `f`; this is the sectionwise route to the same
conclusion, kept because it reads the presentation off the construction of `Ω_{X/Y}` as a
sheafification rather than off the scheme case.
declarations.statement:
theorem isFinitePresentationOnSite_sheafOfDifferentials_of_chartData (f : X ⟶ Y)
    (hfp : HasFinitePresentationChartData B S hS f) :
    (sheafOfDifferentials B S hS f).IsFinitePresentationOnSite
declarations.comment:
finite presentation of Ω_{X/Y} from étale-local finite presentation data for 𝒪_X
  over f⁻¹𝒪_Y; unramifiedness of the transition maps of the small étale site (00UU) is proved,
  not assumed.  The source's own hypothesis is taken in
  `isFinitePresentationOnSite_sheafOfDifferentials_of_isLocallyOfFinitePresentation_unconditional`

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isFinitePresentationOnSite_sheafOfDifferentials_of_isLocallyOfFinitePresentation_unconditional
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 05ZF.**  If `f : X ⟶ Y` is a morphism of algebraic spaces over `S` which is locally
of finite presentation, then `Ω_{X/Y}` is an `𝒪_X`-module of finite presentation.

The proof is the source's, and it is the finite-presentation refinement of the proof of
Stacks 04CV in `StacksFrontier.AlgebraicGeometry.Spaces.SheafOfDifferentialsQuasicoherent`.  An
atlas `q : V ⟶ Y` of the target lifts, by Stacks 02X1, to a surjective étale chart `p : U ⟶ X`
of the source together with a morphism `α : U ⟶ V` of schemes of the site making the square
commute.  Being locally of finite presentation is a condition on exactly such squares, so `α` is
a morphism of schemes locally of finite presentation and its Zariski sheaf of relative
differentials is of finite presentation by Morphisms, Lemma 01V3.  The identification of
Stacks 04CU reads the pullback of `Ω_{X/Y}` along `p` as the sheaf of differentials of `α`, which
the final sentence of Stacks 04CU — Stacks 04CS, in the form
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.sheafOfDifferentialsSchemeComparison` — identifies with the small-étale
module associated to that Zariski sheaf; the associated module of a module of finite presentation
is of finite presentation by
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isFinitePresentationOnSite_representedAssociatedModule`.  Finally
finite presentation descends from a surjective étale chart by
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isFinitePresentationOnSite_iff_exists_etale_surjective`, the pullback of
modules and étale restriction being matched by Equation 03LW.
declarations.statement:
theorem
  isFinitePresentationOnSite_sheafOfDifferentials_of_isLocallyOfFinitePresentation_unconditional
    (f : X ⟶ Y) (hf : IsLocallyOfFinitePresentation B S hS f.hom) :
    (sheafOfDifferentials B S hS f).IsFinitePresentationOnSite
declarations.comment:
finite presentation of Ω_{X/Y} for a morphism of algebraic spaces locally of
  finite presentation

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isEquivalence_spacesBaseChange_of_isIntegralHom_of_universallyInjective
declarations.doc:
For every integral, universally injective and surjective morphism `f` of algebraic spaces over
`S`, base change `V ↦ X ×_Y V` is an equivalence from the spaces-étale site of `Y` to that of
`X`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isEquivalence_spacesBaseChange_of_isIntegralHom_of_universallyInjective (f : X ⟶ Y)
    (hint : IsIntegralHom B S hS f.hom) (hui : UniversallyInjective B S hS f.hom)
    (hsurj : IsSurjective B S hS f.hom) :
    (spacesBaseChange B S hS f).functor.IsEquivalence
declarations.comment: the equivalence at the tag's own class: integral, universally injective and surjective

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.essSurj_spacesBaseChange_of_isFirstOrderThickening
declarations.doc:
Base change `V ↦ X ×_Y V` is essentially surjective from the spaces-étale site of `Y` to that
of `X`, for the inclusion `f` of a first-order thickening.
declarations.statement:
theorem essSurj_spacesBaseChange_of_isFirstOrderThickening (f : X ⟶ Y) [Mono f.hom]
    (hT : IsFirstOrderThickening B S hS Y (Subfunctor.range f.hom)) :
    (spacesBaseChange B S hS f).functor.EssSurj
declarations.comment: essential surjectivity at a first-order thickening

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isEquivalence_spacesBaseChange_of_isFirstOrderThickening
declarations.doc:
Base change `V ↦ X ×_Y V` is an equivalence from the spaces-étale site of `Y` to that of `X`,
for the inclusion `f` of a first-order thickening.
declarations.statement:
theorem isEquivalence_spacesBaseChange_of_isFirstOrderThickening (f : X ⟶ Y) [Mono f.hom]
    (hT : IsFirstOrderThickening B S hS Y (Subfunctor.range f.hom)) :
    (spacesBaseChange B S hS f).functor.IsEquivalence
declarations.comment: the first-order thickening case, not the integral universally injective one

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.essSurj_spacesBaseChange_of_isThickening
declarations.doc:
Let `G ⊂ Y` be a thickening of algebraic spaces over `S`, of arbitrary order. Base change
along the inclusion, `V ↦ G ×_Y V`, is essentially surjective from the spaces-étale site of `Y`
to that of `G`.
declarations.comment: ESSENTIAL SURJECTIVITY ONLY, at a thickening of ARBITRARY order. This lifts the FIRST-ORDER restriction of `AlgebraicGeometry.Space.essSurj_spacesBaseChange_of_isFirstOrderThickening`, which descends the two maps of the lifted etale equivalence relation by the square-zero lifting property of Stacks 0611; the route here is the source's own, where they are descended by FULLNESS at arbitrary order, `AlgebraicGeometry.Space.full_spacesBaseChange_of_isThickening`, and every uniqueness step is FAITHFULNESS at arbitrary order, `AlgebraicGeometry.Space.faithful_spacesBaseChange_of_isThickening`. Together with `AlgebraicGeometry.Space.fullyFaithfulSpacesBaseChangeOfIsThickening` this gives the EQUIVALENCE at arbitrary order, `AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isEquivalence_spacesBaseChange_of_isThickening`. The source states the tag for an arbitrary INTEGRAL, UNIVERSALLY INJECTIVE and SURJECTIVE morphism, which is a wider class: the library proves only that a thickening inclusion belongs to it (Stacks 05ZL, `AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isIntegralHom_universallyInjective_isSurjective_ι_of_isThickening`) and not the converse, so that wider class is NOT covered

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isEquivalence_spacesBaseChange_of_isThickening
declarations.doc:
Let `G ⊂ Y` be a thickening of algebraic spaces over `S`, of arbitrary order. Base change
along the inclusion, `V ↦ G ×_Y V`, is an equivalence from the spaces-étale site of `Y` to that
of `G`.
declarations.comment: the EQUIVALENCE at a thickening of ARBITRARY order -- all three of faithfulness, fullness and essential surjectivity, with no hypothesis beyond the thickening and no monomorphism hypothesis. What is still NOT covered is the source's wider class of an arbitrary INTEGRAL, UNIVERSALLY INJECTIVE and SURJECTIVE morphism: the library proves only that a thickening inclusion lies in that class (Stacks 05ZL, `AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isIntegralHom_universallyInjective_isSurjective_ι_of_isThickening`), not the converse. The first-order statement `AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isEquivalence_spacesBaseChange_of_isFirstOrderThickening` is subsumed up to the identification of the source of `f` with the range of `f.hom`

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.faithful_spacesBaseChange_of_isSurjective
declarations.doc:
Let `f : X ⟶ Y` be a
morphism of algebraic spaces over `S` which is surjective on points. Base change
`V ↦ X ×_Y V` is faithful from the spaces-étale site of `Y` to that of `X`.
declarations.statement:
theorem faithful_spacesBaseChange_of_isSurjective (f : X ⟶ Y)
    (hf : IsSurjective B S hS f.hom) :
    (spacesBaseChange B S hS f).functor.Faithful
declarations.comment: FAITHFULNESS ONLY, for an arbitrary morphism surjective on points -- so at a thickening of ARBITRARY order, and under a hypothesis weaker than the source's integral, universally injective and surjective. The library's other Stacks 05ZH statements are restricted to a FIRST-ORDER thickening because they go through the square-zero lifting property of Stacks 0611; this one reproduces the source's own route instead. FULLNESS is also available at arbitrary order, at a thickening, as `AlgebraicGeometry.Space.full_spacesBaseChange_of_isThickening`; ESSENTIAL SURJECTIVITY remains first-order, see `AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isEquivalence_spacesBaseChange_of_isFirstOrderThickening`

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.faithful_spacesBaseChange_of_isThickening
declarations.doc:
Let `G ⊂ X` be a thickening of algebraic spaces over `S`, of arbitrary order. Base change
along the inclusion, `V ↦ G ×_X V`, is faithful from the spaces-étale site of `X` to that of
`G`.
declarations.comment: FAITHFULNESS ONLY, at a thickening of ARBITRARY order. FULLNESS at arbitrary order is `AlgebraicGeometry.Space.full_spacesBaseChange_of_isThickening`; ESSENTIAL SURJECTIVITY at arbitrary order is `AlgebraicGeometry.Space.essSurj_spacesBaseChange_of_isThickening`

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.full_spacesBaseChange_of_isThickening
declarations.doc:
Let `G ⊂ Y` be a thickening of algebraic spaces over `S`, of arbitrary order. Base change along
the inclusion, `V ↦ G ×_Y V`, is full from the spaces-étale site of `Y` to that of `G`.
declarations.comment: FULLNESS ONLY, at a thickening of ARBITRARY order. Together with `AlgebraicGeometry.Space.faithful_spacesBaseChange_of_isThickening` this gives FULL FAITHFULNESS at arbitrary order, bundled as `AlgebraicGeometry.Space.fullyFaithfulSpacesBaseChangeOfIsThickening`; ESSENTIAL SURJECTIVITY is not covered here; it is proved at arbitrary order in `AlgebraicGeometry.Space.essSurj_spacesBaseChange_of_isThickening`, and the equivalence in `AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isEquivalence_spacesBaseChange_of_isThickening`. The library's other fullness statement, `AlgebraicGeometry.Space.full_spacesBaseChange_of_isFirstOrderThickening`, is restricted to first order because it goes through the square-zero lifting property of Stacks 0611; this one reproduces the source's graph argument instead, and the source's integrality and universal injectivity hypotheses are not needed beyond what a thickening already gives

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.fullyFaithfulSpacesBaseChangeOfIsThickening
declarations.doc:
Let `G ⊂ Y` be a thickening of algebraic spaces over `S`, of arbitrary order. Base change along
the inclusion, `V ↦ G ×_Y V`, is fully faithful from the spaces-étale site of `Y` to that of
`G`.
declarations.comment: FULL FAITHFULNESS ONLY, at a thickening of ARBITRARY order; ESSENTIAL SURJECTIVITY is not covered here, and is proved at arbitrary order in `AlgebraicGeometry.Space.essSurj_spacesBaseChange_of_isThickening`

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.fullyFaithfulSpacesBaseChangeOfIsFirstOrderThickening
declarations.doc:
Base change `V ↦ X ×_Y V` along the inclusion `f` of a first-order thickening is fully
faithful from the spaces-étale site of `Y` to that of `X`.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def fullyFaithfulSpacesBaseChangeOfIsFirstOrderThickening [Mono f.hom]
    (hT : IsFirstOrderThickening B S hS Y (Subfunctor.range f.hom)) :
    (spacesBaseChange B S hS f).functor.FullyFaithful
declarations.comment: full faithfulness at a first-order thickening

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.faithful_spacesBaseChange_of_mono_of_isThickening
declarations.doc:
Base change along the inclusion
of a thickening — of no prescribed order — is faithful on spaces-étale sites.
declarations.statement:
theorem faithful_spacesBaseChange_of_mono_of_isThickening [Mono f.hom]
    (hT : IsThickening B S hS Y (Subfunctor.range f.hom)) :
    (spacesBaseChange B S hS f).functor.Faithful
declarations.comment: faithfulness at an arbitrary thickening

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.full_spacesBaseChange_of_mono_of_isThickening
declarations.doc:
Base change along the inclusion of a
thickening — of no prescribed order — is full on spaces-étale sites.
declarations.statement:
theorem full_spacesBaseChange_of_mono_of_isThickening [Mono f.hom]
    (hT : IsThickening B S hS Y (Subfunctor.range f.hom)) :
    (spacesBaseChange B S hS f).functor.Full
declarations.comment: fullness at an arbitrary thickening

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.fullyFaithfulSpacesBaseChangeOfMonoOfIsThickening
declarations.doc:
Base change `V ↦ X ×_Y V` is fully faithful from the spaces-étale site of `Y` to that of `X`,
for `f` a monomorphism whose range is a thickening of `Y` of arbitrary order.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def fullyFaithfulSpacesBaseChangeOfMonoOfIsThickening [Mono f.hom]
    (hT : IsThickening B S hS Y (Subfunctor.range f.hom)) :
    (spacesBaseChange B S hS f).functor.FullyFaithful
declarations.comment: full faithfulness at an arbitrary thickening

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.fullyFaithfulSpacesBaseChangeOfIsThickeningRange
declarations.doc:
Base change `V ↦ X ×_Y V` is fully faithful from the spaces-étale site of `Y` to that of `X`,
for the inclusion `f` of a thickening of algebraic spaces — a monomorphism whose range is a
closed subspace with the same points, with no hypothesis on its defining ideal.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def fullyFaithfulSpacesBaseChangeOfIsThickeningRange [Mono f.hom]
    (hT : IsThickening B S hS Y (Subfunctor.range f.hom)) :
    (spacesBaseChange B S hS f).functor.FullyFaithful
declarations.comment: full faithfulness at a thickening of unbounded order, not the integral universally injective case

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.fullyFaithfulSpacesBaseChangeOfIsNthOrderThickening
declarations.doc:
Base change `V ↦ X ×_Y V` is fully faithful from the spaces-étale site of `Y` to that of `X`,
for the inclusion `f` of a thickening of order `n`, whose defining ideal has vanishing `(n+1)`st
power.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def fullyFaithfulSpacesBaseChangeOfIsNthOrderThickening {n : ℕ} [Mono f.hom]
    (hT : IsNthOrderThickening B S hS n Y (Subfunctor.range f.hom)) :
    (spacesBaseChange B S hS f).functor.FullyFaithful
declarations.comment: full faithfulness at a thickening of finite order

registrations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.C1573.isEquivalence_spacesBaseChange_of_isThickeningHom
registrations.comment: the equivalence, for the inclusion of a thickening of arbitrary order

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.isIso_of_isFinite_of_etale_of_connectedSpace
declarations.doc:
Over an algebraically closed field `k` of characteristic zero, a finite étale morphism
`Y ⟶ 𝐀¹_k = Spec k[X]` with `Y` connected is an isomorphism.
declarations.statement:
theorem isIso_of_isFinite_of_etale_of_connectedSpace {k : Type u} [Field k] [IsAlgClosed k]
    [CharZero k] {Y : Scheme.{u}} (f : Y ⟶ Spec (.of k[X])) [IsFinite f] [Etale f]
    [ConnectedSpace Y] : IsIso f
declarations.comment: the input: A^1_k has no nontrivial connected finite étale covering when k is algebraically closed of characteristic 0 (details omitted in the source)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.universalHomeomorphism_squaringMap
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 05ZI, the last sentence: there is a universal homeomorphism `X ⟶ 𝐀¹_k`, exhibited
directly by `t ↦ t ^ 2` on affine space.**

Here `X` is the quotient of the affine line by the relation identifying `t` with `-t` away from
the origin, the algebraic space of Stacks 05Z6, and the morphism is the one Stacks 05VS
descends from squaring the coordinate. It is universally closed by
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.universallyClosed_squaringMap`, universally injective by Stacks 05VS
part (4), and surjective after every base change by
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isSurjective_pullback_fst_squaringMap`; the criterion is
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.universalHomeomorphism_of_universallyClosed_of_universallyInjective`.

Stacks 05Z6 and Stacks 05ZI state this over an algebraically closed field of characteristic
zero. Only `2 ≠ 0` in `k` is used, and only for universal injectivity.
declarations.statement:
theorem universalHomeomorphism_squaringMap (hchar : (2 : k) ≠ 0)
    (hk : B.Contains (Spec (.of k)))
    [HasSheafify (BigFppfOver.topology B (Spec (.of k)) hk) (Type u)] :
    UniversalHomeomorphism B (Spec (.of k)) hk (squaringMap k B hk)
declarations.comment: the remark's own last sentence: there exists a universal homeomorphism X ⟶ 𝐀¹_k, exhibited directly by t ↦ t² on affine spaces. NOT asserted: that this X is the same as the quotient Y/G of the remark's alternative construction, that Y ⟶ X is a nontrivial connected finite étale covering, and that 𝐀¹_k has no nontrivial connected finite étale coverings

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.AffineLineInvolution.whiskerLeft_punctured_comp_toQuotientSheaf
declarations.doc:
**The overlap identity of Stacks 05ZI.** The two maps from the punctured affine line to the
quotient sheaf of Stacks 02Z1, one through the inclusion of the puncture and one through
negation of the coordinate, agree. No hypothesis on the ground field is used.
declarations.statement:
theorem whiskerLeft_punctured_comp_toQuotientSheaf {C : Type v} [Category.{w} C]
    (J : GrothendieckTopology C) [HasSheafify J (Type u)] (F : C ⥤ Over (Spec (.of k))) :
    F.op.whiskerLeft (yoneda.map (puncturedAffineLineInclusion k)) ≫
        Stacks.Groupoids.toQuotientSheaf J F (involutionRelation k) =
      F.op.whiskerLeft (yoneda.map (puncturedAffineLineInclusion k ≫ affineLineNeg k)) ≫
        Stacks.Groupoids.toQuotientSheaf J F (involutionRelation k)
declarations.comment:
a construction input only: the gluing datum of the covering `Y` of the remark,
at the level of points. NEITHER assertion of the remark is asserted -- not that a universal
homeomorphism of algebraic spaces need be non-representable, and not that Tag 05ZH fails for
universal homeomorphisms

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.AffineLineInvolution.yoneda_puncturedChart_comp_quotientChart
declarations.doc:
**The gluing datum of the covering of Stacks 05ZI.** The two maps from the punctured affine
line to the quotient `X` of Stacks 05Z6, one through the inclusion of the puncture and one
through negation of the coordinate, agree as morphisms of presheaves on the site.

This is the assertion that the two charts of the affine line with doubled origin have the same
image in `X` over the overlap of the charts, which is what makes the covering of Stacks 05ZI
well defined. No hypothesis on the ground field is used.
declarations.statement:
theorem yoneda_puncturedChart_comp_quotientChart :
    yoneda.map (puncturedChartInclusion k B hk) ≫ quotientChart k B hk =
      yoneda.map (puncturedChartNeg k B hk) ≫ quotientChart k B hk
declarations.comment:
a construction input only: the two chart maps of the doubled-origin line agree
over the overlap, which is the remark's `these agree on the overlap by construction of X`. The
morphism `Y ⟶ X` itself is not constructed and neither assertion of the remark is asserted

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.connectedSpace_affineSpaceWithDoubledZero
declarations.doc:
**The connectedness input of Stacks 05ZI.** In positive dimension affine `n`-space over a
field with its origin doubled is a connected scheme: its two charts are spectra of a polynomial
ring, hence irreducible, they cover the glued scheme, and their images share the image of the
generic point.
declarations.statement:
theorem connectedSpace_affineSpaceWithDoubledZero (k : Type u) [Field k] (n : ℕ) (hn : 0 < n) :
    ConnectedSpace (affineSpaceWithDoubledZero k n)
declarations.comment:
a construction input only: the doubled-origin affine space is connected. That
`Y ⟶ X` is a nontrivial connected finite etale covering is NOT asserted -- this library has no
notion of a connected algebraic space

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.chartSwapNegationData
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 05ZI, the alternative construction.** The endomorphism of affine space with
doubled origin which negates the coordinates and swaps the two charts, packaged with its
restriction to each chart.

The two chart maps agree over the overlap of the charts because negation preserves the
complement of the origin, so `AlgebraicGeometry.comp_chartInclusion_eq` applies.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def chartSwapNegationData (k : Type u) [Field k] (n : ℕ) :
    { f : affineSpaceWithDoubledZero k n ⟶ affineSpaceWithDoubledZero k n //
      chartInclusion k n 0 ≫ f = negAffineSpace k n ≫ chartInclusion k n 1 ∧
        chartInclusion k n 1 ≫ f = negAffineSpace k n ≫ chartInclusion k n 0 }
declarations.comment:
a construction input only: the involution of `Y` of the remark's alternative
route, negating the coordinate and swapping the two charts. That the induced action of `{+1,-1}`
is free and that `X` is its quotient are NOT asserted

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.chartSwapNegation_comp_self
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 05ZI, the alternative construction.** Negating the coordinates and swapping the
two charts of affine space with doubled origin is an involution, so it makes the group of
order two act on that scheme.
declarations.statement:
theorem chartSwapNegation_comp_self (k : Type u) [Field k] (n : ℕ) :
    chartSwapNegation k n ≫ chartSwapNegation k n = 𝟙 _
declarations.comment: a construction input only: that involution is an involution

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.AffineLineInvolution.isPullback_chartPairToDoubledLine
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 05ZI: the square of the remark is cartesian.** Away from characteristic two a
morphism into `Y` together with a morphism into the chart `𝐀¹_k` of Stacks 05Z6 having the same
image in `X` comes from a unique morphism into `Y₁ ⨿ Y₂`.

Locally on the source the morphism into `Y` factors through one of the two charts of the
doubled line, and there the relation of Stacks 02Z1, being the kernel pair of the chart
`𝐀¹_k ⟶ X`, supplies the lift through
`AlgebraicGeometry.AffineLineInvolution.relationToChartPair`. The local lifts agree because the
two edges of the square are jointly monomorphic, so they glue; and the glued lift is unique for
the same reason.
declarations.statement:
theorem isPullback_chartPairToDoubledLine (hchar : (2 : k) ≠ 0) :
    IsPullback (yoneda.map (chartPairToDoubledLine k B hk))
      (yoneda.map (chartPairToAffineLine k B hk)) (coveringMorphism k B hk)
      (quotientChart k B hk)
declarations.comment: the remark's cartesian square: Y ← Y₁ ⨿ Y₂ over X ← 𝐀¹_k is cartesian

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.AffineLineInvolution.nontrivial_connected_finiteEtale_degreeTwo_coveringMorphism
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 05ZI.** The affine line with its origin doubled is a *nontrivial connected finite
étale covering of degree two* of the algebraic space `X = 𝐀¹_k/\{x ∼ -x ∣ x ≠ 0\}` of
Stacks 05Z6: the morphism `Y ⟶ X` of the remark is representable and finite locally free of
degree two, it is étale, `Y` is a connected scheme, and `Y ⟶ X` admits no section.

The remark states this for `k` algebraically closed of characteristic zero; invertibility of two
in the ground field is all that is used. Nontriviality is expressed by the absence of a section:
a covering which is a finite disjoint union of copies of its base has one, so a covering without
one is not such a disjoint union.
declarations.statement:
theorem nontrivial_connected_finiteEtale_degreeTwo_coveringMorphism (hchar : (2 : k) ≠ 0) :
    ((Stacks.Morphisms.IsFiniteLocallyFreeOfRank.property.{u} 2).inverseImage
        (BigFppfOver.toScheme B (Spec (.of k)) hk)).presheaf (coveringMorphism k B hk) ∧
      (MorphismProperty.inverseImage (@Etale.{u} : MorphismProperty Scheme.{u})
        (BigFppfOver.toScheme B (Spec (.of k)) hk)).presheaf (coveringMorphism k B hk) ∧
      ConnectedSpace (doubledLine k).left ∧
      ¬ ∃ s : (involutionQuotient k B hk).obj ⟶ yoneda.obj (doubledLineSite k B hk),
        s ≫ coveringMorphism k B hk = 𝟙 (involutionQuotient k B hk).obj
declarations.comment: the remark's covering: Y, the affine line with its origin doubled, is a nontrivial connected finite étale covering of X of degree two

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.AffineLineInvolution.doubledLine_freeAction_quotient
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 05ZI, the remark's alternative construction.** Away from characteristic two, the
affine line with its origin doubled carries an action of the group `G = \{+1, -1\} = ℤˣ` in
which `-1` swaps the two charts and negates the coordinate. This action is free in the sense of
condition `(*)` of Stacks 02Z2. The quotient `Y/G` of Spaces, Definition 02Z3, is an algebraic
space, and it is the algebraic space `X` of Stacks 05Z6: an isomorphism `X ≅ Y/G` carries the
